# 1 Introduction

## 1.1 Overview
This hardware register description document lists the programmable registers for the APQ8016 processor chip. It is intended for embedded OEMs or developers who require information about how to program the APQ8016 hardware.

Complementary ICs within this APQ chipset include:
* Audio codec
* Power manager
* WLAN and BT connectivity
<!-- page 12 -->
## 1.2 System memory map

The system memory map is shown in Figure 1-1.

### Table: System Memory Map

## 2.1 BIMC_MISC
BIMC Misc Global

### 2.1.1 BIMC_BIMC_MISC
BIMC Misc Global

### BIMC_CORE_CLK_SEL (0x00400020)
* **Type:** RW
* **Clock:** Config Clock
* **Reset State:** 0x00000000

Control bit in this register enables legacy mode clocking scheme. In this scheme, BIMC block gets a 2x clock input from the clock controller. BIMC locally divides the clock extract 1x clock.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1 | CLK_2X_MODE | 0: bimc_core_clk input is 1x when CLK_2X_MODE_CTRL_EN is 1<br>1: bimc_core_clk input is 2x clock when CLK_2X_MODE_CTRL_EN is 1 |
| 0 | CLK_2X_MODE_CTRL_EN | 0: CLK_2X_MODE select control used from BIMC interface<br>1: CLK_2X_MODE select control used from this register bit 1 (programmed) |

### BIMC_CORE_CLK_PERIOD (0x00400024)
* **Type:** RW
* **Clock:** Config Clock
* **Reset State:** 0x00000000

Core Clock Period Register
<!-- page 15 -->
### BIMC_CORE_CLK_PERIOD (0x00400024) Fields (Cont.)
| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 28 | CLK_PERIOD_RESOLUTION | 1: DDR clock period defined in period field of this register is in 1ps unit.<br>0: DDR clock period is in 100ps unit. |
| 16:0 | PERIOD | value of core clock period defined in unit described by encoding in bit 28. When CLK_PERIOD_RESOLUTION is 100ps, maximum value that can be programmed for the PERIOD is 255 |

### BIMC_SCMOn_LOCAL_CGC_THRESHOLD (0x00400100 + 0x4*n, n=[0..1])
* **Type:** RW
* **Clock:** Config Clock
* **Reset State:** 0x00000000

used to compare with core clk period info from time based feature design for disabling specific SCMO internal core clk CGC(s).

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 28 | THRESHOLD_ENA | 1: enable frequency based clock gating.<br>0: disable frequency based clock gating. |
| 7:0 | THRESHOLD_VAL | value of core clk period in 100ps unit. If the period info from time based module is smaller than the value from these bits, then SCMO internal core clk CGCs will be disabled and clk is not gated.<br>Examples:<br>- 0x00: the minimum value of the setting and the comparator output is always low. This means clk gating will be enabled if THRESHOLD_ENA of this register is also set to 0<br>- 0x01: 100ps = 10GHz<br>- 0x0c: 1200ps = 833MHz<br>- 0xFF: 6553.6ns = 15.25kHz (max. setting) |

### BIMC_CALIBRATION_CFG (0x00400400)
* **Type:** RW
* **Clock:** Config Clock
* **Reset State:** 0x00000000

Calibration configuration

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 28 | RAPID_CAL_ENA | Enable/disable rapid calibration. When rapid calibration is enabled, the calibrate pulses are generated every alternate core clock cycle. |
| 23:0 | COUNT_VAL | Count value used to generate calibrate pulses periodically. The counter is based of XO clock cycles. For example when the COUNT_VAL is 1, the calibrate pulses are generated every alternate XO clock cycle. Note: When the COUNT_VAL is 0, the calibrate pulses aren't generated. |

### 2.2.1 BIMC_BRIC_GLOBAL1

BRIC Global #1

### 0x00401000 BIMC_BRIC_GLOBAL1_COMPONENT_INFO

**Type:** R  
**Clock:** Config Clock  
**Reset State:** 0x00000101  

Component information registers provide discoverability information on the type of component and instance of each component. These registers are always the very first register in each component's configuration address space and allow for a software routine to walk the configuration address space in steps of 4KB to identify the location of each configuration register space and to which component each 4KB configures.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 15:8 | SUB_TYPE | Identifies this configuration space as belonging to global1 configuration registers<br>0x1: GLOBAL1 |
| 7:0 | TYPE | Identifies this configuration space as belonging to a global/common component, that does not specifically connect to a bus master or slave.<br>0x1: GLOBAL |

### 0x00401020 BIMC_BRIC_CONFIGURATION_INFO_0

**Type:** R  
**Clock:** Config Clock  
**Reset State:** 0x00000808  

Configuration information registers provide information on the capability and configuration of the interconnect. See register field descriptions for more details.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:24 | ADDR_WIDTH | Indicates the width of addresses generated by masters connected to the interconnect. |
| 23:16 | BUSID | Indicates the BUSID added to all commands originating from masters that are directly connected to this interconnect. Generally assigned to be a unique value in the SoC. |
<!-- page 23 -->

### BIMC_BRIC_CONFIGURATION_INFO_0 (continued)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 15:8 | NUM_SWAYS | Indicates the number of slaveways in the interconnect. Also includes any internal slaveways that perform controller functionality to on-chip and off-chip memory, including DDR-SDRAM. Each slaveway connected to a single bus slave or another level of interconnect. |
| 7:0 | NUM_MPORTS | Indicates the number of masterports in the interconnect. Each masterport connects to a single bus master or another level of interconnect. |

### 0x00401030 BIMC_BRIC_CONFIGURATION_INFO_1

**Type:** R  
**Clock:** Config Clock  
**Reset State:** 0x00000000  

Configuration information registers provide information on the capability and configuration of the interconnect. See register field descriptions for more details.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:16 | DATA_WIDTH | Indicates the width of read and write data used in the core of the interconnect. |
| 15:8 | TID_WIDTH | Indicates the width of transfer ID in the core of the interconnect. TIDs are made as wide as necessary to accommodate TIDs from all masters and to accommodate any addition transaction tagging required by the interconnect. |
| 7:0 | MID_WIDTH | Indicates the width of master ID in the core of the interconnect, including any bus and port IDs as inserted by different levels of interconnects. |

### 0x00401100 BIMC_BRIC_INTERRUPT_STATUS_0

**Type:** R  
**Clock:** Config Clock  
**Reset State:** 0x00000000  

Interrupt status registers collect interrupts from each component and are part of a central set of interrupt status and control registers to indicate and control interrupts from which components are propagated to the interrupt controller.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 7:0 | MPORT | Indicates interrupts from each masterport. 1-bit per masterport. When set (1), indicates that the corresponding masterport has generated an interrupt that requires servicing. |

### 0x00401108 BIMC_BRIC_INTERRUPT_CLEAR_0

**Type:** W  
**Clock:** Config Clock  
**Reset State:** 0x00000000  

Interrupt clear registers provide the capability to clear an interrupt status, once an interrupt has been acknowledged or serviced. It is part of a central set of interrupt status and control registers to indicate and control interrupts from which components are propagated to the interrupt controller.
<!-- page 26 -->

### BIMC_BRIC_INTERRUPT_CLEAR_0 (continued)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 7:0 | MPORT | Write '1' to specific bits to clear interrupt status. 1-bit per masterport. Only interrupt status that are set are cleared. Writes of '1' to interrupt status that are not set are ignored. Writes of '0' are ignored. |

Interrupt clear registers provide the capability to clear an interrupt status, once an interrupt has been acknowledged or serviced. It is part of a central set of interrupt status and control registers to indicate and control interrupts from which components are propagated to the interrupt controller

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 7:0 | SWAY_1 | Write '1' to specific bits to clear interrupt status. 1-bit per slaveway. Only interrupt status that are set are cleared. Writes of '1' to interrupt status that are not set are ignored. Writes of '0' are ignored. |

### 0x0040112C BIMC_BRIC_INTERRUPT_ENABLE_2

**Type:** RW  
**Clock:** Config Clock  
**Reset State:** 0x00000000

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 7:0 | SWAY_1 | When set (1), configures the corresponding interrupt to be propagated to the interrupt controller. 1-bit per slaveway. |

| :--- | :--- | :--- |

### 0x00401200 BIMC_BRIC_REF_TIMER_INTERVAL

**Type:** RW  
**Clock:** Config & Reference Clocks  
**Reset State:** 0x00000000  

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 15:0 | INTERVAL | Configures the number of clock cycles of implementation specified reference clock to generate a reference timer tick on for use in arbitration and other functions in the interconnect. The reference timer tick defines the time units that arbitration intervals are specified in. A single interval definition allows for this reference time unit to be adjusted on any change in the frequency of the reference clock. When configured with either '0' or '1', indicates an interval of 1-cycle. When configured with values greater than '1', a timer tick is generated once every configured number of reference clock cycles. |

## 2.3 GLOBAL2

BRIC Global #2

### 2.3.1 BIMC_BRIC_GLOBAL2

BRIC Global #2

### 0x00402000 BIMC_BRIC_GLOBAL2_COMPONENT_INFO

**Type:** R  
**Clock:** Config Clock  
**Reset State:** 0x00000201  

Component information registers provide discoverability information on the type of component and instance of each component. These registers are always the very first register in each component's configuration address space and allow for a software routine to walk the configuration address space in steps of 4KB to identify the location of each configuration register space and to which component each 4KB configures.


<!-- page 31 -->

### BIMC_BRIC_GLOBAL2_COMPONENT_INFO (continued)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 15:8 | SUB_TYPE | Identifies this configuration space as belonging to global2 configuration registers<br>0x2: GLOBAL2 |
| 7:0 | TYPE | Identifies this configuration space as belonging to a global/common component, that does not specifically connect to a bus master or slave.<br>0x1: GLOBAL |

### 0x004021F0 BIMC_BRIC_DEFAULT_SEGMENT

**Type:** RW  
**Clock:** Config Clock  
**Reset State:** 0x80060007  

Default segment configuration register defines the slaveways to direct all commands that do not decode to a specific bus slave in the system and commands that request specific routing.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31 | REDIRECT_EN | When set (1), enables redirection of commands that request cacheable/coherent redirection (AREDIRECT=1). When cleared (0), command redirection is ignored and address of command determines the slave to which the command is routed to. |
| 19:16 | REDIRECT | Configures the slaveway to send all commands that request cacheable/coherent redirection. Defaults to the slaveway interfacing to the bus slave capable of handling cachable/coherent commands. |
| 3:0 | DEFAULT | Configures the slaveway to send all commands that do not decode to one of the specified address ranges. Defaults to an internal default slave capable of generating decode error, but can be configured to be any other slaveway. |

### 0x00402200+ BIMC_BRIC_SEGMENTn_ADDR_BASE_A_LOWER, n=[0..7]
**Offset:** 0x80*n

**Type:** RW  
**Clock:** Config Clock  
**Reset State:** 0x00000000  

Segment configuration registers define the address range in the memory map for each bus slave. Each bus slave has three sets of address ranges (A, B, C), with each address range defined with a pair of BASE and MASK registers. Each BASE/MASK pair of registers defines a power-of-2 address range that is at a minimum 1MB in size. For e.g., a BASE of 0x80000000 and MASK of
<!-- page 32 -->

0xF0000000 defines the address range 0x80000000-0x8FFFFFFF. Each BASE and MASK register is broken into UPPER and LOWER to accommodate upto 64-bit address.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:20 | BASE_31_20 | Configures ADDR_BASE[31:20] to match for in address of a command. Used in conjunction with ADDR_MASK[31:20], which controls which bits of ADDR_BASE[31:20] are matched for in address of a command. |
| 10 | BASE_10 | Configures ADDR_BASE[10] to match for in address of a command. Used in conjunction with ADDR_MASK[10], which controls whether ADDR_BASE[10] is matched for in address of a command. |
| 3:2 | RFU | Reserved for future use |
| 1 | TYPE | When cleared (0), identifies BASE_A/MASK_A pair of address range registers as adding to the address space defined for bus slave 'n'. When set (1), identifies BASE_A/MASK_A pair of address range registers as subtracting from the address space defined for bus slave 'n'. For e.g., allows for the address space to be defined as 128MB - 16MB for a total of 114MB. |
| 0 | ENABLE | When set (1), enables use of BASE_A/MASK_A pair of address range registers for determining whether a command decodes to bus slave 'n' or not. When cleared (0), disables use of BASE_A/MASK_A pair of address range registers. |

### 0x00402A00+ BIMC_BRIC_REMAPn_ADDR_BASE_LOWER, n=[0..3]
**Offset:** 0x40*n

**Type:** RW  
**Clock:** Config Clock  
**Reset State:** 0x00000000  

Remap configuration registers define allow for one address range to be remapped to a different address range to facilitate easier decoding in bus slaves and/or allow for multiple disjoint address ranges to be collected together to make them appear to be a single contiguous space for the slave. It is particularly useful in external DRAM access, where a single device could be allowed to be accessed with interleaved addresses for a portion and linear addresses for the remainder. Refer HPG for example configurations.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:28 | BASE_31_28 | Configures ADDR_BASE[31:28] to match for in address of a command. Used in conjunction with ADDR_MASK[31:28], which controls which bits of ADDR_BASE[31:28] are matched for in address of a command. |
| 10 | BASE_10 | Configures ADDR_BASE[10] to match for in address of a command. Used in conjunction with ADDR_MASK[10], which controls whether ADDR_BASE[10] is matched for in address of a command. |
| 3:1 | RFU | Reserved for future use |
| 0 | ENABLE | When set (1), enables use of BASE/MASK pair of address range registers for determining whether a command decodes to a specific address range and enables remapping of matched addresses. |

### 0x00402A20+ BIMC_BRIC_REMAPn_OP0, n=[0..3]
**Offset:** 0x40*n

**Type:** RW  
**Clock:** Config Clock  
**Reset State:** 0x000A0000  

Remap operation configuration registers define the operation to perform on a matched address. Two operations are currently supported, de-interleaving and offset change. Each operation can be independently enabled. When an operation is not enabled, no change is performed on the matched address. Incoming command address is input for remap operation #0. The result of remap operation #0 is fed as input to remap operation #1. The result of remap operation #1 is forwarded to internal slaves.

| Bits | Name | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 23:16 | OPERAND | R | De-interleaving granularity. For eg., when de-interleaving on 1KByte granularity, addr[10] is dropped and bits higher than addr[10] are shifted right. A '0' is shifted into the MSB.<br>0xA: GRANULARITY_1KB |
| 4 | OPCODE | R | De-interleave matched addresses on granularity selected in operand.<br>0x0: DE_INTERLEAVE |
| 0 | OPCODE_ENABLE | RW | When set(1), enables conversion of matched addresses based on opcode selected |

### 0x00402A24+ BIMC_BRIC_REMAPn_OP1, n=[0..3]
**Offset:** 0x40*n

**Type:** RW  
**Clock:** Config Clock  
**Reset State:** 0x00000010  

Remap operation configuration registers define the operation to perform on a matched address. Two operations are currently supported, de-interleaving and offset change. Each operation can be independently enabled. When an operation is not enabled, no change is performed on the matched address. Incoming command address is input for remap operation #0. The result of remap operation #0 is fed as input to remap operation #1. The result of remap operation #1 is forwarded to internal slaves.


<!-- page 41 -->

### BIMC_BRIC_REMAPn_OP1 (continued)

| Bits | Name | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 23:16 | OPERAND | RW | Offset to add or subtract from matched addresses in 256MB granularity. For eg., +1, adds 256MB to matched address, -1 subtracts 256MB from matched address. |
| 4 | OPCODE | R | Change offset of matched addresses, in 256MB granularity.<br>0x1: OFFSET |
| 0 | OPCODE_ENABLE | RW | When set(1), enables conversion of matched addresses based on opcode selected |

### 2.4.1 BIMC_M_APP_MPORT_BRIC_MASTERPORT

#### 0x00408000 BIMC_M_APP_MPORT_COMPONENT_INFO

- **Type**: R
- **Clock**: Config Clock

Component information registers provide discoverability information on the type of component and instance of each component. These registers are always the very first register in each component's configuration address space and allow for a software routine to walk the configuration address space in steps of 4KB to identify the location of each configuration register space and to which component each 4KB configures.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 23:16 | INSTANCE | Indicates the instance number of this masterport. |
| 15:8 | SUB_TYPE | Identifies this configuration space as belonging to a masterport<br>0x1: MASTERPORT |
| 7:0 | TYPE | Identifies this configuration space as belonging to a component that interfaces to a bus master.<br>0x2: MASTERPORT |

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:28 | WR_GATHER_BEATS | Configures the number of write data beats to gather/buffer in write channel buffer before allowing the corresponding write command to be routed to arbiters. When configured to 0, write commands are held until the first beat of write data has been buffered. When configured to 1, write commands are held until two beats of write data have been buffered and so on. When configured with values larger than the number of beats in a write command, the command is held until the last beat has been buffered. When configured with values larger than the depth of write channel buffers, the command is held until all entries in the write channel buffer have been occupied. |
| 19:16 | RD_GATHER_BEATS | Configures the number of read data beats to gather/buffer in read channel buffer before allowing the read data to proceed to the master. When configured to 0, read data is allowed to proceed to the master as soon as the first beat is buffered in the read channel buffer. When configured to 1, read data is allowed to proceed to the master as soon as two beats of read data have been buffered and so on. When configured with values larger than the number of beats in the read burst, read data is held until the last beat has been buffered. When configured with values larger than the depth of read channel buffers, read data is held until all entries in the read channel buffer have been occupied. |

#### 0x00408220 BIMC_M_APP_MPORT_WR_WAY_CROSSING

- **Type**: RW
- **Clock**: Config & Master Clocks
- **Reset State**: 0x00000000


<!-- page 51 -->

Configures the level of strictness or relaxedness of way crossing checks for writes.

### Register: BIMC_M_APP_MPORT_WR_WAY_CROSSING

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 7:0 | REG | 1-bit per slaveway. When 2 or more bits are set (1), allows the corresponding slaveways to be treated as one slaveway when write commands are considered as way crossing, i.e. write commands to these 2 (or more) slaveways are not treated as way crossing when one write command targets one slaveway and the next write command targets the second slaveway. Not treating write commands as way crossing allows the write commands to go to the slaveway ahead of the write data for potentially better overall system performance. When all bits are set (1), disables all way crossing checks. When all bits are cleared (0), way crossing is strict with each way crossing write command held until write data for all previous writes have been routed to their corresponding slaveways. |

### Register: BIMC_M_APP_MPORT_BKE_ENABLE
**Address:** `0x00408300`

- **Clock:** Config & Master Clocks
- **Reset State:** `0x00000000`

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 0 | ENABLE | When set (1), enables the book keeping element (BKE) to determine AREQPRIORITY and APRIORITYLVL of commands from the bus master by comparing the amount of bus traffic from the bus master to a target, and determining a health level for the bus master. The health level determines the relative priority of commands from the bus master to allow the bus master to catch-up if it is not getting serviced, or slow down to allow other bus masters to get their share of system resources. When cleared (0), disables the book keeping element and AREQPRIORTY and APRIORITYLVL from the bus master are propagated downstream. |

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |

### Register: BIMC_M_APP_MPORT_STATUS_2A
**Address:** `0x00408420`

- **Type:** R
- **Clock:** Config, Master & Pipe0 Clocks
- **Reset State:** `0x00000000`

Status registers indicate the state of several elements in the masterport, including the number of transactions outstanding/pending waiting for a response, emptiness, fullness of several buffers, etc. The state information is available only as a debug indication and could be delayed by a few clock cycles from when the state is reached to being reflected in the status registers. One or more of the state registers are read live and could capture intermediate values as they change.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 23:16 | WR_PENDING_PRE_BUF | Indicates the number of write transactions that are outstanding/pending waiting for a response from the slave. This transaction count is from before address channel buffers, which interfaces to frontend of the masterport. |
| 7:0 | RD_PENDING_PRE_BUF | Indicates the number of read transactions that are outstanding/pending waiting for a response from the slave. This transaction count is from before address channel buffers, which interfaces to frontend of the masterport. |

**Type:** R

**Reset State:** 0x00111111

Buffer status register indicate the state of all buffers in the masterport, whether they are empty or full on either side of the buffer. Some buffers carry information from master to core and others carry information from core to master. Both write side and read side status are indicated separately, since they would be not be similar when master clock and core clock are not synchronous to each other.

## 2.5 BIMC_M_APP_PROF
BRIC Traffic Profiling

### 2.5.1 BIMC_M_APP_PROF_BRIC_PROFILING
BRIC Traffic Profiling

### 0x00409000 BIMC_M_APP_PROF_COMPONENT_INFO

**Type:** R
**Clock:** Config Clock
**Reset State:** 0x00000202

Component information registers provide discoverability information on the type of component and instance of each component. These registers are always the very first register in each component's configuration address space and allow for a software routine to walk the configuration address space in steps of 4KB to identify the location of each configuration register space and to which component each 4KB configures.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 23:16 | INSTANCE | Indicates the instance number of this traffic profiling. |
| 15:8 | SUB_TYPE | Identifies this configuration space as belonging to traffic profiling<br>0x2: PROFILING |
| 7:0 | TYPE | Identifies this configuration space as belonging to a component that interfaces to a bus master.<br>0x2: MASTERPORT |

### 0x00409020 BIMC_M_APP_PROF_CONFIGURATION_INFO_0

**Type:** R
**Clock:** Config Clock
**Reset State:** 0x00000000
<!-- page 63 -->

### BIMC_M_APP_PROF_CONFIGURATION_INFO_0 (cont.)

Configuration information registers provide information on the capability and configuration of each traffic profiling instance. See register field descriptions for more details.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:24 | TENURE_WIDTH | Indicates the width of tenures (latencies) measured in traffic profiling. |
| 23:16 | TRACKING_TABLE_DEPTH | Indicates the number of entries in the table that tracks outstanding commands for determining how many commands have larger turnaround latencies that a programmed threshold. |
| 7:0 | SCALING_FACTOR | Indicates how many extra scaling is performed on events generated by traffic profiling if such events have to be synchronized from the tenure clock to the event clock. Any value that is non-power-of-2 is converted to power-of-2 by hardware. When the value read from this register field is used in software, similar conversion of non-power-of-2 values to next higher power-of-2 value is necessary. |

### 0x00409030 BIMC_M_APP_PROF_CONFIGURATION_INFO_1

**Type:** R
**Clock:** Config Clock
**Reset State:** 0x00000000

Configuration information registers provide information on the capability and configuration of each traffic profiling instance. See register field descriptions for more details.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 23:16 | PIPE2_ACH_DEPTH | Indicates the depth of address channel buffer in pipe2 of masterport in which this traffic profiling instance is paired with. Applies only to traffic profiling instances in XR type masterports, which contains three distinct paths to slaves, in pipe0, pipe1, pipe2. In non-XR type masterports, value contained in field does not refer to any actual address channel buffer. |
| 15:8 | PIPE1_ACH_DEPTH | Indicates the depth of address channel buffer in pipe1 of masterport in which this traffic profiling instance is paired with. Applies only to traffic profiling instances in XR type masterports, which contains three distinct paths to slaves, in pipe0, pipe1, pipe2. In non-XR type masterports, value contained in field does not refer to any actual address channel buffer. |
| 7:0 | PIPE0_ACH_DEPTH | Indicates the depth of address channel buffer in pipe0 of masterport in which this traffic profiling instance is paired with. Applies only to traffic profiling instances in XR type masterports, which contains three distinct paths to slaves, in pipe0, pipe1, pipe2. In non-XR type masterports, pipe0 refers to the common address channel buffer used for all slave accesses. |
<!-- page 64 -->

### 0x00409200 BIMC_M_APP_PROF_CLOCK_CTRL

**Type:** RW
**Clock:** Config, Event & Tenure Clocks
**Reset State:** 0x00000003

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1 | TENURE_CLOCK_GATING_EN | When set (1), enables activity based clock gating of all registers clocked by tenure clock. Activity based clock gating uses architectural clock gates to reduce dynamic power consumption by gating clocks during periods of in-activity. When cleared (0), disables all activity based clock gating by forcing all architectural clock gates to not gate clocks even during periods of in-activity. |
| 0 | EVENT_CLOCK_GATING_EN | When set (1), enables activity based clock gating of all registers clocked by event clock. Activity based clock gating uses architectural clock gates to reduce dynamic power consumption by gating clocks during periods of in-activity. When cleared (0), disables all activity based clock gating by forcing all architectural clock gates to not gate clocks even during periods of in-activity. |

### 0x00409210 BIMC_M_APP_PROF_MODE

**Type:** RW
**Clock:** Config, Event & Tenure Clocks
**Reset State:** 0x00000000
<!-- page 65 -->

### BIMC_M_APP_PROF_MODE (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 25:24 | WR_TENURE_MODE | Configures the start and end events for monitoring write latencies/tenures. When configured to WR_CMD_TO_BRESP, starting event is first cycle of write command from bus master as seen by traffic profiling and ending event is first cycle of write response to bus master as seen by traffic profiling. When configured to WR_CMD_TO_BRESP_HANDSHAKE, starting event is first cycle of write command from bus master as seen by traffic profiling and ending event is transfer handshake of write response to bus master as seen by traffic profiling. When configured to WR_CMD_HANDSHAKE, starting event is first cycle of write command from bus master as seen by traffic profiling and ending event is transfer handshake of the same write command with bus master as seen by traffic profiling. When configured to WR_RESP_HANDSHAKE, starting event is first cycle of write response to bus master as seen by traffic profiling and ending event is transfer handshake of write response to bus master as seen by traffic profiling.<br>0x0: WR_CMD_TO_BRESP<br>0x1: WR_CMD_TO_BRESP_HANDSHAKE<br>0x2: WR_CMD_HANDSHAKE<br>0x3: WR_RESP_HANDSHAKE |
| 17:16 | RD_TENURE_MODE | Configures the start and end events for monitoring read latencies/tenures. When configured to RD_CMD_TO_FIRST_RDATA, starting event is first cycle of read command from bus master as seen by traffic profiling and ending event is first cycle of first beat of read data to bus master as seen by traffic profiling. When configured to RD_CMD_TO_LAST_RDATA, starting event is first cycle of read command from bus master as seen by traffic profiling and ending event is transfer handshake of last beat of read data to bus master as seen by traffic profiling. When configured to RD_CMD_HANDSHAKE, starting event is first cycle of read command from bus master as seen by traffic profiling and ending event is transfer handshake of the same read command with bus master as seen by traffic profiling. When configured to RD_DATA_HANDSHAKE, starting event is first cycle of first beat of read data to bus master as seen by traffic profiling and ending event is transfer handshake of last beat of read data to bus master as seen by traffic profiling.<br>0x0: RD_CMD_TO_FIRST_RDATA<br>0x1: RD_CMD_TO_LAST_RDATA<br>0x2: RD_CMD_HANDSHAKE<br>0x3: RD_DATA_HANDSHAKE |
| 0 | PROFILING_EN | When set (1), enables traffic profiling to monitor bus transactions from bus master and generate events for counting in performance monitors. When cleared (0), disables traffic profiling. |

### 0x0040C000 BIMC_M_DSP_MPORT_COMPONENT_INFO

* **Type**: R
* **Clock**: Config Clock
* **Reset State**: 0x00000102

Component information registers provide discoverability information on the type of component and instance of each component. These registers are always the very first register in each component's configuration address space and allow for a software routine to walk the configuration address space in steps of 4KB to identify the location of each configuration register space and to which component each 4KB configures.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 23:16 | INSTANCE | Indicates the instance number of this masterport. |
| 15:8 | SUB_TYPE | Identifies this configuration space as belonging to a masterport.<br>0x1: MASTERPORT |
| 7:0 | TYPE | Identifies this configuration space as belonging to a component that interfaces to a bus master.<br>0x2: MASTERPORT |
<!-- page 79 -->
### 0x0040C020 BIMC_M_DSP_MPORT_CONFIGURATION_INFO_0

* **Type**: R
* **Clock**: Config Clock
* **Reset State**: 0x01000000

Configuration information registers provide information on the capability and configuration of each masterport instance. See register field descriptions for more details.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:24 | SYNC_MODE | Indicates the clock relationship between the clock used in the master side and the clock used in the core side of the masterport.<br>When ASYNC, identifies the master clock and core clock as unrelated and asynchronous to each other.<br>When SYNC, identifies the master clock and core clock as synchronous to each other.<br>When ISOSYNC, identifies the master clock and core clock as related, but of different frequencies, which are of integer ratios, i.e., they are iso-synchronous to each other.<br>0x0: ASYNC<br>0x1: SYNC<br>0x2: ISOSYNC |
| 15:8 | CONNECTION_TYPE | Indicates the type of master connecting to this masterport.<br>When DIRECT, indicates that a bus master is directly connected to this masterport.<br>When CASCADE, indicates that bus masters connect to this masterport through another level of interconnect.<br>0x0: DIRECT<br>0x1: CASCADE |
| 7:0 | FUNCTIONALITY | Indicates the functionality and type of bus traffic handled by this masterport.<br>When INORDER, identifies this masterport as optimized for in-order bus traffic.<br>When OOO_ONLY, identifies this masterport as optimized for out-of-order bus traffic, where a single master is capable of handling responses return in any order.<br>When REORDER, identifies this masterport as having a reorder buffer for re-ordering responses to command order, while allowing bus slaves to return responses in any order they desire.<br>When STUB, identifies this masterport has a stub.<br>0x0: STUB<br>0x1: OOO_ONLY<br>0x2: INORDER<br>0x3: REORDER |

### 0x0040C200 BIMC_M_DSP_MPORT_CLOCK_CTRL

- **Type**: RW
- **Clock**: Config, Core & Master Clocks
- **Reset State**: 0x00000003

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1 | MASTER_CLOCK_GATING_EN | When set (1), enables activity based clock gating of all registers clocked by master clock. Activity based clock gating uses architectural clock gates to reduce dynamic power consumption by gating clocks during periods of in-activity. When cleared (0), disables all activity based clock gating by forcing all architectural clock gates to not gate clocks even during periods of in-activity. |
| 0 | CORE_CLOCK_GATING_EN | When set (1), enables activity based clock gating of all registers clocked by core clock. Activity based clock gating uses architectural clock gates to reduce dynamic power consumption by gating clocks during periods of in-activity. When cleared (0), disables all activity based clock gating by forcing all architectural clock gates to not gate clocks even during periods of in-activity. |

### 0x0040C208 BIMC_M_DSP_MPORT_CDC_CTRL

- **Type**: RW

| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1 | MASTER_CLOCK_DEMETA_SEL | When cleared (0), selects DEMETA synchronizer that requires atleast 3 clock edges (two rising and one falling). When set (1), selects DEMETA synchronizer that requires atleast 2 clock edges (one falling and one rising) to synchronize to master clock in all buffers. |
| 0 | CORE_CLOCK_DEMETA_SEL | When cleared (0), selects DEMETA synchronizer that requires atleast 3 clock edges (two rising and one falling). When set (1), selects DEMETA synchronizer that requires atleast 2 clock edges (one falling and one rising) to synchronize to core clock in all buffers. |

### 0x0040C210 BIMC_M_DSP_MPORT_MODE

- **Type**: RW
- **Clock**: Config, Core & Master Clocks
- **Reset State**: 0x00000012

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:28 | WR_GATHER_BEATS | Configures the number of write data beats to gather/buffer in write channel buffer before allowing the corresponding write command to be routed to arbiters. When configured to 0, write commands are held until the first beat of write data has been buffered. When configured to 1, write commands are held until two beats of write data have been buffered and so on. When configured with values larger than the number of beats in a write command, the command is held until the last beat has been buffered. When configured with values larger than the depth of write channel buffers, the command is held until all entries in the write channel buffer have been occupied. |
| 19:16 | RD_GATHER_BEATS | Configures the number of read data beats to gather/buffer in read channel buffer before allowing the read data to proceed to the master. When configured to 0, read data is allowed to proceed to the master as soon as the first beat is buffered in the read channel buffer. When configured to 1, read data is allowed to proceed to the master as soon as two beats of read data have been buffered and so on. When configured with values larger than the number of beats in the read burst, read data is held until the last beat has been buffered. When configured with values larger than the depth of read channel buffers, read data is held until all entries in the read channel buffer have been occupied. |
| 15 | RCSSH | Redirect Cacheable System SHareable. When set (1), enables redirection of all cacheable transactions that are system shareable to the redirect slaveway. Note: Only masters connecting using AMBA 4 ACE protocol are able to indicate system shareability for transactions. |
| 14 | RCOSH | Redirect Cacheable Outer SHareable. When set (1), enables redirection of all cacheable transactions that are outer shareable to the redirect slaveway. |
| 13 | RCISH | Redirect Cacheable Inner SHareable. When set (1), enables redirection of all cacheable transactions that are inner shareable to the redirect slaveway. |
| 12 | RCNSH | Redirect Cacheable Non-SHareable. When set (1), enables redirection of all cacheable transactions that are non-shareable to the redirect slaveway. |
| 11 | RNCSSH | Redirect Non-Cacheable System SHareable. When set (1), enables redirection of all non-cacheable transactions that are system shareable to the redirect slaveway. Note: Only masters connecting using AMBA 4 ACE protocol are able to indicate system shareability for transactions. |
<!-- page 87 -->

### BIMC_M_DSP_MPORT_MODE (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 10 | RNCOSH | Redirect Non-Cacheable Outer SHareable. When set (1), enables redirection of all non-cacheable transactions that are outer shareable to the redirect slaveway. |
| 9 | RNCISH | Redirect Non-Cacheable Inner SHareable. When set (1), enables redirection of all non-cacheable transactions that are inner shareable to the redirect slaveway. |
| 8 | RNCNSH | Redirect Non-Cacheable Non-SHareable. When set (1), enables redirection of all non-cacheable transactions that are non-shareable to the redirect slaveway. |
| 4 | NARROW_WRITES | When set (1), enables converting of 1-beat bus-width sized writes down to 32-bit ASIZE based on write strobes. It is recommended to be enabled for directly connected CPU masters. When cleared (0), disables conversion and all writes are forwarded downstream as generated by the master. |
| 2 | FIODV | Force In-Order Device. When set (1), forces commands to device memory to be executed one at a time. In other words, commands to device memory are held until all previous commands have completed (responses have been received at the masterport) and all commands after the device command are held until the device completes (response has been received at the masterport.) |
| 1 | FIOSO | Force In-Order Strongly-Ordered. When set (1), forces commands to strongly ordered memory to be executed one at a time. In other words, commands to strongly ordered memory are held until all previous commands have completed (responses have been received at the masterport) and all commands after the strongly ordered command are held until the strongly ordered completes (response has been received at the masterport.) |
| 0 | ORDERING_MODEL | Configures how commands to memories of type Strongly ordered and Device (SoDv) are handled in the masterport. When configured as STRICT, all commands to SoDv memory are held until all previous commands have completed (responses have been received at the masterport) and all commands after the SoDv command are held until the SoDv completes (i.e. response has been received at the masterport.) When configured as RELAXED, all commands to SoDv memory are treated as accessing Normal memory.<br>0x0: RELAXED<br>0x1: STRICT |

### BIMC_M_DSP_MPORT_WR_WAY_CROSSING (cont.)

Configures the level of strictness or relaxedness of way crossing checks for writes.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 7:0 | REG | 1-bit per slaveway. When 2 or more bits are set (1), allows the corresponding slaveways to be treated as one slaveway when write commands are considered as way crossing, ie. write commands to these 2 (or more) slaveways are not treated as way crossing when one write command targets one slaveway and the next write command targets the second slaveway. Not treating write commands as way crossing allows the write commands to go to the slaveway ahead of the write data for potentially better overall system performance. When all bits are set (1), disables all way crossing checks. When all bits are cleared (0), way crossing is strict with each way crossing write command held until write data for all previous writes have been routed to their corresponding slaveways. |

### BIMC_M_DSP_MPORT_BKE_ENABLE
**Address:** `0x0040C300`  
**Type:** RW  
**Clock:** Config & Master Clocks  
**Reset State:** `0x00000000`

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 0 | ENABLE | When set (1), enables the book keeping element (BKE) to determine AREQPRIORITY and APRIORITYLVL of commands from the bus master by comparing the amount of bus traffic from the bus master to a target, and determining a health level for the bus master. The health level determines the relative priority of commands from the bus master to allow the bus master to catch-up if it is not getting serviced, or slow down to allow other bus masters to get their share of system resources. When cleared (0), disables the book keeping element and AREQPRIORTY and APRIORITYLVL from the bus master are propagated downstream. |
<!-- page 92 -->

### BIMC_M_DSP_MPORT_STATUS_2A
**Address:** `0x0040C420`  
**Type:** R  
**Clock:** Config, Master & Pipe0 Clocks  
**Reset State:** `0x00000000`

Status registers indicate the state of several elements in the masterport, including the number of transactions outstanding/pending waiting for a response, emptiness, fullness of several buffers, etc. The state information is available only as a debug indication and could be delayed by a few clock cycles from when the state is reached to being reflected in the status registers. One or more of the state registers are read live and could capture intermediate values as they change.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 23:16 | WR_PENDING_PRE_BUF | Indicates the number of write transactions that are outstanding/pending waiting for a response from the slave. This transaction count is from before address channel buffers, which interfaces to frontend of the masterport. |
| 7:0 | RD_PENDING_PRE_BUF | Indicates the number of read transactions that are outstanding/pending waiting for a response from the slave. This transaction count is from before address channel buffers, which interfaces to frontend of the masterport. |

## 2.7 BIMC_M_DSP_PROF
BRIC Traffic Profiling

### 2.7.1 BIMC_M_DSP_PROF_BRIC_PROFILING
BRIC Traffic Profiling

---

### BIMC_M_DSP_PROF_COMPONENT_INFO
**Address:** `0x0040D000`  
**Type:** R  
**Clock:** Config Clock  
**Reset State:** `0x00000202`

Component information registers provide discoverability information on the type of component and instance of each component. These registers are always the very first register in each component's configuration address space and allow for a software routine to walk the configuration address space in steps of 4KB to identify the location of each configuration register space and to which component each 4KB configures.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 23:16 | INSTANCE | Indicates the instance number of this traffic profiling. |
| 15:8 | SUB_TYPE | Identifies this configuration space as belonging to traffic profiling<br>0x2: PROFILING |
| 7:0 | TYPE | Identifies this configuration space as belonging to a component that interfaces to a bus master.<br>0x2: MASTERPORT |

---

### BIMC_M_DSP_PROF_CONFIGURATION_INFO_0
**Address:** `0x0040D020`  
**Type:** R  
**Clock:** Config Clock  
**Reset State:** `0x00000000`
<!-- page 100 -->

### BIMC_M_DSP_PROF_CONFIGURATION_INFO_0 (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:24 | TENURE_WIDTH | Indicates the width of tenures (latencies) measured in traffic profiling. |
| 23:16 | TRACKING_TABLE_DEPTH | Indicates the number of entries in the table that tracks outstanding commands for determining how many commands have larger turnaround latencies that a programmed threshold. |
| 7:0 | SCALING_FACTOR | Indicates how many extra scaling is performed on events generated by traffic profiling if such events have to be synchronized from the tenure clock to the event clock. Any value that is non-power-of-2 is converted to power-of-2 by hardware. When the value read from this register field is used in software, similar conversion of non-power-of-2 values to next higher power-of-2 value is necessary. |

---

### BIMC_M_DSP_PROF_CONFIGURATION_INFO_1
**Address:** `0x0040D030`  
**Type:** R  
**Clock:** Config Clock  
**Reset State:** `0x00000000`

Configuration information registers provide information on the capability and configuration of each traffic profiling instance. See register field descriptions for more details.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 23:16 | PIPE2_ACH_DEPTH | Indicates the depth of address channel buffer in pipe2 of masterport in which this traffic profiling instance is paired with. Applies only to traffic profiling instances in XR type masterports, which contains three distinct paths to slaves, in pipe0, pipe1, pipe2. In non-XR type masterports, value contained in field does not refer to any actual address channel buffer. |
| 15:8 | PIPE1_ACH_DEPTH | Indicates the depth of address channel buffer in pipe1 of masterport in which this traffic profiling instance is paired with. Applies only to traffic profiling instances in XR type masterports, which contains three distinct paths to slaves, in pipe0, pipe1, pipe2. In non-XR type masterports, value contained in field does not refer to any actual address channel buffer. |
| 7:0 | PIPE0_ACH_DEPTH | Indicates the depth of address channel buffer in pipe0 of masterport in which this traffic profiling instance is paired with. Applies only to traffic profiling instances in XR type masterports, which contains three distinct paths to slaves, in pipe0, pipe1, pipe2. In non-XR type masterports, pipe0 refers to the common address channel buffer used for all slave accesses. |




<!-- page 101 -->

### 0x0040D200 BIMC_M_DSP_PROF_CLOCK_CTRL

* **Type**: RW
* **Clock**: Config, Event & Tenure Clocks
* **Reset State**: `0x00000003`

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1 | TENURE_CLOCK_GATING_EN | When set (1), enables activity based clock gating of all registers clocked by tenure clock. Activity based clock gating uses architectural clock gates to reduce dynamic power consumption by gating clocks during periods of in-activity. When cleared (0), disables all activity based clock gating by forcing all architectural clock gates to not gate clocks even during periods of in-activity. |
| 0 | EVENT_CLOCK_GATING_EN | When set (1), enables activity based clock gating of all registers clocked by event clock. Activity based clock gating uses architectural clock gates to reduce dynamic power consumption by gating clocks during periods of in-activity. When cleared (0), disables all activity based clock gating by forcing all architectural clock gates to not gate clocks even during periods of in-activity. |

* **Clock**: Config, Event & Tenure Clocks
* **Reset State**: `0x00000000`

### BIMC_M_DSP_PROF_MODE (Continued)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 25:24 | WR_TENURE_MODE | Configures the start and end events for monitoring write latencies/tenures. When configured to WR_CMD_TO_BRESP, starting event is first cycle of write command from bus master as seen by traffic profiling and ending event is first cycle of write response to bus master as seen by traffic profiling. When configured to WR_CMD_TO_BRESP_HANDSHAKE, starting event is first cycle of write command from bus master as seen by traffic profiling and ending event is transfer handshake of write response to bus master as seen by traffic profiling. When configured to WR_CMD_HANDSHAKE, starting event is first cycle of write command from bus master as seen by traffic profiling and ending event is transfer handshake of the same write command with bus master as seen by traffic profiling. When configured to WR_RESP_HANDSHAKE, starting event is first cycle of write response to bus master as seen by traffic profiling and ending event is transfer handshake of write response to bus master as seen by traffic profiling.<br>0x0: WR_CMD_TO_BRESP<br>0x1: WR_CMD_TO_BRESP_HANDSHAKE<br>0x2: WR_CMD_HANDSHAKE<br>0x3: WR_RESP_HANDSHAKE |
| 17:16 | RD_TENURE_MODE | Configures the start and end events for monitoring read latencies/tenures. When configured to RD_CMD_TO_FIRST_RDATA, starting event is first cycle of read command from bus master as seen by traffic profiling and ending event is first cycle of first beat of read data to bus master as seen by traffic profiling. When configured to RD_CMD_TO_LAST_RDATA, starting event is first cycle of read command from bus master as seen by traffic profiling and ending event is transfer handshake of last beat of read data to bus master as seen by traffic profiling. When configured to RD_CMD_HANDSHAKE, starting event is first cycle of read command from bus master as seen by traffic profiling and ending event is transfer handshake of the same read command with bus master as seen by traffic profiling. When configured to RD_DATA_HANDSHAKE, starting event is first cycle of first beat of read data to bus master as seen by traffic profiling and ending event is transfer handshake of last beat of read data to bus master as seen by traffic profiling.<br>0x0: RD_CMD_TO_FIRST_RDATA<br>0x1: RD_CMD_TO_LAST_RDATA<br>0x2: RD_CMD_HANDSHAKE<br>0x3: RD_DATA_HANDSHAKE |
| 0 | PROFILING_EN | When set (1), enables traffic profiling to monitor bus transactions from bus master and generate events for counting in performance monitors. When cleared (0), disables traffic profiling. |

### 0x0040D400+0x4\*n BIMC_M_DSP_PROF_RD_STATUS_n, n=[0..0]
- **Type**: R
- **Clock**: Config & Tenure Clocks
- **Reset State**: 0x00000000

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31 | RD_OUTSTANDING_OVERFLOW | Indicates that the number of outstanding reads crossed the maximum supported (255) during when traffic profiling was last enabled. It is recommended that this register be read only after traffic profiling has been disabled. |
| 30 | RD_OUTSTANDING_UNDERFLOW | Indicates that the number of outstanding reads went below 0 during when traffic profiling was last enabled. It indicates that more command completions were seen compared to commands starts. The most likely scenario is an overflow of number of outstanding reads occurred leading to some command starts not being tracked. It is recommended that this register be read only after traffic profiling has been disabled. |
| 7:0 | RD_OUTSTANDING_MAX | Indicates the maximum number of outstanding reads that were seen when traffic profiling was last enabled. Only reads that match the MID filter and slaveway select filter are accounted for. It is recommended that this register be read only after traffic profiling has been disabled. |

## 2.8 BIMC_M_DSP_PROF
### BRIC Traffic Profiling

### 2.8.1 BIMC_M_DSP_PROF_BRIC_PROFILING
### BRIC Traffic Profiling

### 0x0040D000 BIMC_M_DSP_PROF_COMPONENT_INFO
- **Type**: R
- **Clock**: Config Clock
- **Reset State**: 0x00000202

Component information registers provide discoverability information on the type of component and instance of each component. These registers are always the very first register in each component's configuration address space and allow for a software routine to walk the configuration address space in steps of 4KB to identify the location of each configuration register space and to which component each 4KB configures.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 23:16 | INSTANCE | Indicates the instance number of this traffic profiling. |
| 15:8 | SUB_TYPE | Identifies this configuration space as belonging to traffic profiling<br>0x2: PROFILING |
| 7:0 | TYPE | Identifies this configuration space as belonging to a component that interfaces to a bus master.<br>0x2: MASTERPORT |
<!-- page 116 -->
### 0x0040D020 BIMC_M_DSP_PROF_CONFIGURATION_INFO_0
- **Type**: R
- **Clock**: Config Clock
- **Reset State**: 0x00000000

Configuration information registers provide information on the capability and configuration of each traffic profiling instance. See register field descriptions for more details.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:24 | TENURE_WIDTH | Indicates the width of tenures (latencies) measured in traffic profiling. |
| 23:16 | TRACKING_TABLE_DEPTH | Indicates the number of entries in the table that tracks outstanding commands for determining how many commands have larger turnaround latencies that a programmed threshold. |
| 7:0 | SCALING_FACTOR | Indicates how many extra scaling is performed on events generated by traffic profiling if such events have to be synchronized from the tenure clock to the event clock. Any value that is non-power-of-2 is converted to power-of-2 by hardware. When the value read from this register field is used in software, similar conversion of non-power-of-2 values to next higher power-of-2 value is necessary. |

### 0x0040D030 BIMC_M_DSP_PROF_CONFIGURATION_INFO_1
- **Type**: R
- **Clock**: Config Clock
- **Reset State**: 0x00000000

Configuration information registers provide information on the capability and configuration of each traffic profiling instance. See register field descriptions for more details.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 23:16 | PIPE2_ACH_DEPTH | Indicates the depth of address channel buffer in pipe2 of masterport in which this traffic profiling instance is paired with. Applies only to traffic profiling instances in XR type masterports, which contains three distinct paths to slaves, in pipe0, pipe1, pipe2. In non-XR type masterports, value contained in field does not refer to any actual address channel buffer. |
<!-- page 117 -->
### BIMC_M_DSP_PROF_CONFIGURATION_INFO_1 (Continued)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 15:8 | PIPE1_ACH_DEPTH | Indicates the depth of address channel buffer in pipe1 of masterport in which this traffic profiling instance is paired with. Applies only to traffic profiling instances in XR type masterports, which contains three distinct paths to slaves, in pipe0, pipe1, pipe2. In non-XR type masterports, value contained in field does not refer to any actual address channel buffer. |
| 7:0 | PIPE0_ACH_DEPTH | Indicates the depth of address channel buffer in pipe0 of masterport in which this traffic profiling instance is paired with. Applies only to traffic profiling instances in XR type masterports, which contains three distinct paths to slaves, in pipe0, pipe1, pipe2. In non-XR type masterports, pipe0 refers to the common address channel buffer used for all slave accesses. |

### 0x0040D200 BIMC_M_DSP_PROF_CLOCK_CTRL
- **Type**: RW
- **Clock**: Config, Event & Tenure Clocks
- **Reset State**: 0x00000003

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1 | TENURE_CLOCK_GATING_EN | When set (1), enables activity based clock gating of all registers clocked by tenure clock. Activity based clock gating uses architectural clock gates to reduce dynamic power consumption by gating clocks during periods of in-activity. When cleared (0), disables all activity based clock gating by forcing all architectural clock gates to not gate clocks even during periods of in-activity. |
| 0 | EVENT_CLOCK_GATING_EN | When set (1), enables activity based clock gating of all registers clocked by event clock. Activity based clock gating uses architectural clock gates to reduce dynamic power consumption by gating clocks during periods of in-activity. When cleared (0), disables all activity based clock gating by forcing all architectural clock gates to not gate clocks even during periods of in-activity. |

When configured to WR_CMD_TO_BRESP_HANDSHAKE, starting event is first cycle of write command from bus master as seen by traffic profiling and ending event is transfer handshake of write response to bus master as seen by traffic profiling. When configured to WR_CMD_HANDSHAKE, starting event is first cycle of write command from bus master as seen by traffic profiling and ending event is transfer handshake of the same write command with bus master as seen by traffic profiling. When configured to WR_RESP_HANDSHAKE, starting event is first cycle of write response to bus master as seen by traffic profiling and ending event is transfer handshake of write response to bus master as seen by traffic profiling.<br>0x0: WR_CMD_TO_BRESP<br>0x1: WR_CMD_TO_BRESP_HANDSHAKE<br>0x2: WR_CMD_HANDSHAKE<br>0x3: WR_RESP_HANDSHAKE |
| 17:16 | RD_TENURE_MODE | Configures the start and end events for monitoring read latencies/tenures. When configured to RD_CMD_TO_FIRST_RDATA, starting event is first cycle of read command from bus master as seen by traffic profiling and ending event is first cycle of first beat of read data to bus master as seen by traffic profiling. When configured to RD_CMD_TO_LAST_RDATA, starting event is first cycle of read command from bus master as seen by traffic profiling and ending event is transfer handshake of last beat of read data to bus master as seen by traffic profiling. When configured to RD_CMD_HANDSHAKE, starting event is first cycle of read command from bus master as seen by traffic profiling and ending event is transfer handshake of the same read command with bus master as seen by traffic profiling. When configured to RD_DATA_HANDSHAKE, starting event is first cycle of first beat of read data to bus master as seen by traffic profiling and ending event is transfer handshake of last beat of read data to bus master as seen by traffic profiling.<br>0x0: RD_CMD_TO_FIRST_RDATA<br>0x1: RD_CMD_TO_LAST_RDATA<br>0x2: RD_CMD_HANDSHAKE<br>0x3: RD_DATA_HANDSHAKE |
| 0 | PROFILING_EN | When set (1), enables traffic profiling to monitor bus transactions from bus master and generate events for counting in performance monitors. When cleared (0), disables traffic profiling. |

### 0x0040D400 + 0x4*n BIMC_M_DSP_PROF_RD_STATUS_n (n=0..0)

* **Type**: R
* **Clock**: Config & Tenure Clocks
* **Reset State**: 0x00000000

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31 | RD_OUTSTANDING_OVERFLOW | Indicates that the number of outstanding reads crossed the maximum supported (255) during when traffic profiling was last enabled. It is recommended that this register be read only after traffic profiling has been disabled. |
| 30 | RD_OUTSTANDING_UNDERFLOW | Indicates that the number of outstanding reads went below 0 during when traffic profiling was last enabled. It indicates that more command completions were seen compared to commands starts. The most likely scenario is an overflow of number of outstanding reads occurred leading to some command starts not being tracked. It is recommended that this register be read only after traffic profiling has been disabled. |
| 7:0 | RD_OUTSTANDING_MAX | Indicates the maximum number of outstanding reads that were seen when traffic profiling was last enabled. Only reads that match the MID filter and slaveway select filter are accounted for. It is recommended that this register be read only after traffic profiling has been disabled. |

## 2.9 BIMC_M_GPU_PROF
### BRIC Traffic Profiling

### 2.9.1 BIMC_M_GPU_PROF_BRIC_PROFILING
BRIC Traffic Profiling

#### 0x00411000 BIMC_M_GPU_PROF_COMPONENT_INFO

* **Type**: R
* **Clock**: Config Clock
* **Reset State**: 0x00000202

Component information registers provide discoverability information on the type of component and instance of each component. These registers are always the very first register in each component's configuration address space and allow for a software routine to walk the configuration address space in steps of 4KB to identify the location of each configuration register space and to which component each 4KB configures.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 23:16 | INSTANCE | Indicates the instance number of this traffic profiling. |
| 15:8 | SUB_TYPE | Identifies this configuration space as belonging to traffic profiling.<br>0x2: PROFILING |
| 7:0 | TYPE | Identifies this configuration space as belonging to a component that interfaces to a bus master.<br>0x2: MASTERPORT |
<!-- page 132 -->
## Bus Integrated Memory Controller

#### 0x00411020 BIMC_M_GPU_PROF_CONFIGURATION_INFO_0

* **Type**: R
* **Clock**: Config Clock
* **Reset State**: 0x00000000

Configuration information registers provide information on the capability and configuration of each traffic profiling instance. See register field descriptions for more details.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:24 | TENURE_WIDTH | Indicates the width of tenures (latencies) measured in traffic profiling. |
| 23:16 | TRACKING_TABLE_DEPTH | Indicates the number of entries in the table that tracks outstanding commands for determining how many commands have larger turnaround latencies that a programmed threshold. |
| 7:0 | SCALING_FACTOR | Indicates how many extra scaling is performed on events generated by traffic profiling if such events have to be synchronized from the tenure clock to the event clock. Any value that is non-power-of-2 is converted to power-of-2 by hardware. When the value read from this register field is used in software, similar conversion of non-power-of-2 values to next higher power-of-2 value is necessary. |

#### 0x00411030 BIMC_M_GPU_PROF_CONFIGURATION_INFO_1

* **Type**: R
* **Clock**: Config Clock
* **Reset State**: 0x00000000

Configuration information registers provide information on the capability and configuration of each traffic profiling instance. See register field descriptions for more details.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 23:16 | PIPE2_ACH_DEPTH | Indicates the depth of address channel buffer in pipe2 of masterport in which this traffic profiling instance is paired with. Applies only to traffic profiling instances in XR type masterports, which contains three distinct paths to slaves, in pipe0, pipe1, pipe2. In non-XR type masterports, value contained in field does not refer to any actual address channel buffer. |

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 15:8 | PIPE1_ACH_DEPTH | Indicates the depth of address channel buffer in pipe1 of masterport in which this traffic profiling instance is paired with. Applies only to traffic profiling instances in XR type masterports, which contains three distinct paths to slaves, in pipe0, pipe1, pipe2. In non-XR type masterports, value contained in field does not refer to any actual address channel buffer. |
| 7:0 | PIPE0_ACH_DEPTH | Indicates the depth of address channel buffer in pipe0 of masterport in which this traffic profiling instance is paired with. Applies only to traffic profiling instances in XR type masterports, which contains three distinct paths to slaves, in pipe0, pipe1, pipe2. In non-XR type masterports, pipe0 refers to the common address channel buffer used for all slave accesses. |

#### 0x00411200 BIMC_M_GPU_PROF_CLOCK_CTRL

* **Type**: RW
* **Clock**: Config, Event & Tenure Clocks
* **Reset State**: 0x00000003

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1 | TENURE_CLOCK_GATING_EN | When set (1), enables activity based clock gating of all registers clocked by tenure clock. Activity based clock gating uses architectural clock gates to reduce dynamic power consumption by gating clocks during periods of in-activity. When cleared (0), disables all activity based clock gating by forcing all architectural clock gates to not gate clocks even during periods of in-activity. |
| 0 | EVENT_CLOCK_GATING_EN | When set (1), enables activity based clock gating of all registers clocked by event clock. Activity based clock gating uses architectural clock gates to reduce dynamic power consumption by gating clocks during periods of in-activity. When cleared (0), disables all activity based clock gating by forcing all architectural clock gates to not gate clocks even during periods of in-activity. |

When configured to WR_CMD_TO_BRESP, starting event is first cycle of write command from bus master as seen by traffic profiling and ending event is first cycle of write response to bus master as seen by traffic profiling. When configured to WR_CMD_TO_BRESP_HANDSHAKE, starting event is first cycle of write command from bus master as seen by traffic profiling and ending event is transfer handshake of write response to bus master as seen by traffic profiling. When configured to WR_CMD_HANDSHAKE, starting event is first cycle of write command from bus master as seen by traffic profiling and ending event is transfer handshake of the same write command with bus master as seen by traffic profiling. When configured to WR_RESP_HANDSHAKE, starting event is first cycle of write response to bus master as seen by traffic profiling and ending event is transfer handshake of write response to bus master as seen by traffic profiling.<br>0x0: WR_CMD_TO_BRESP<br>0x1: WR_CMD_TO_BRESP_HANDSHAKE<br>0x2: WR_CMD_HANDSHAKE<br>0x3: WR_RESP_HANDSHAKE |
| 17:16 | RD_TENURE_MODE | Configures the start and end events for monitoring read latencies/tenures. When configured to RD_CMD_TO_FIRST_RDATA, starting event is first cycle of read command from bus master as seen by traffic profiling and ending event is first cycle of first beat of read data to bus master as seen by traffic profiling. When configured to RD_CMD_TO_LAST_RDATA, starting event is first cycle of read command from bus master as seen by traffic profiling and ending event is transfer handshake of last beat of read data to bus master as seen by traffic profiling. When configured to RD_CMD_HANDSHAKE, starting event is first cycle of read command from bus master as seen by traffic profiling and ending event is transfer handshake of the same read command with bus master as seen by traffic profiling. When configured to RD_DATA_HANDSHAKE, starting event is first cycle of first beat of read data to bus master as seen by traffic profiling and ending event is transfer handshake of last beat of read data to bus master as seen by traffic profiling.<br>0x0: RD_CMD_TO_FIRST_RDATA<br>0x1: RD_CMD_TO_LAST_RDATA<br>0x2: RD_CMD_HANDSHAKE<br>0x3: RD_DATA_HANDSHAKE |
| 0 | PROFILING_EN | When set (1), enables traffic profiling to monitor bus transactions from bus master and generate events for counting in performance monitors. When cleared (0), disables traffic profiling. |

| 31 | RD_OUTSTANDING_OVERFLOW | Indicates that the number of outstanding reads crossed the maximum supported (255) during when traffic profiling was last enabled. It is recommended that this register be read only after traffic profiling has been disabled. |
| 30 | RD_OUTSTANDING_UNDERFLOW | Indicates that the number of outstanding reads went below 0 during when traffic profiling was last enabled. It indicates that more command completions were seen compared to commands starts. It is recommended that this register be read only after traffic profiling has been disabled. |

Only reads that match the MID filter and slaveway select filter are accounted for. It is recommended that this register be read only after traffic profiling has been disabled. |

## 2.10 BIMC_M_GPU_MPORT (BRIC Masterport)

### 2.10.1 BIMC_M_GPU_MPORT_BRIC_MASTERPORT (BRIC Masterport)

### 0x00410000 BIMC_M_GPU_MPORT_COMPONENT_INFO

- **Type**: R
- **Clock**: Config Clock
- **Reset State**: 0x00000102

Component information registers provide discoverability information on the type of component and instance of each component. These registers are always the very first register in each component's configuration address space and allow for a software routine to walk the configuration address space in steps of 4KB to identify the location of each configuration register space and to which component each 4KB configures.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 23:16 | INSTANCE | Indicates the instance number of this masterport. |
| 15:8 | SUB_TYPE | Identifies this configuration space as belonging to a masterport. <br>0x1: MASTERPORT |
| 7:0 | TYPE | Identifies this configuration space as belonging to a component that interfaces to a bus master. <br>0x2: MASTERPORT |
<!-- page 148 -->

### 0x00410020 BIMC_M_GPU_MPORT_CONFIGURATION_INFO_0

- **Type**: R
- **Clock**: Config Clock
- **Reset State**: 0x01000000

Configuration information registers provide information on the capability and configuration of each masterport instance. See register field descriptions for more details.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:24 | SYNC_MODE | Indicates the clock relationship between the clock used in the master side and the clock used in the core side of the masterport. When ASYNC, identifies the master clock and core clock as unrelated and asynchronous to each other. When SYNC, identifies the master clock and core clock as synchronous to each other. When ISOSYNC, identifies the master clock and core clock as related, but of different frequencies, which are of integer ratios, i.e., they are iso-synchronous to each other.<br>0x0: ASYNC<br>0x1: SYNC<br>0x2: ISOSYNC |
| 15:8 | CONNECTION_TYPE | Indicates the type of master connecting to this masterport. When DIRECT, indicates that a bus master is directly connected to this masterport. When CASCADE, indicates that bus masters connect to this masterport through another level of interconnect.<br>0x0: DIRECT<br>0x1: CASCADE |
| 7:0 | FUNCTIONALITY | Indicates the functionality and type of bus traffic handled by this masterport. When INORDER, identifies this masterport as optimized for in-order bus traffic. When OOO_ONLY, identifies this masterport as optimized for out-of-order bus traffic, where a single master is capable of handling responses return in any order. When REORDER, identifies this masterport as having a reorder buffer for re-ordering responses to command order, while allowing bus slaves to return responses in any order they desire. When STUB, identifies this masterport has a stub.<br>0x0: STUB<br>0x1: OOO_ONLY<br>0x2: INORDER<br>0x3: REORDER |

### 0x00410030 BIMC_M_GPU_MPORT_CONFIGURATION_INFO_1

- **Type**: R
- **Clock**: Config Clock
- **Reset State**: 0x00000000
<!-- page 149 -->

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:0 | SWAY_CONNECTIVITY | Indicates slaveways that this masterport can route commands to. 1-bit per slaveway. When a specific bit is set (1), indicates that commands can be routed to the slaveway corresponding to this bit. When a specific bit is clear (0), indicates that commands are not routed to the slaveway corresponding to this bit. |

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:24 | RCH_DEPTH | Indicates the depth of read channel buffers in this masterport. A beat of read data occupies one entry in the read channel buffer, until accepted by the bus master. |

### 0x00410060 BIMC_M_GPU_MPORT_CONFIGURATION_INFO_4

### 0x00410210 BIMC_M_GPU_MPORT_MODE

**Type**: RW
**Clock**: Config, Core & Master Clocks
**Reset State**: `0x00000012`

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:28 | WR_GATHER_BEATS | Configures the number of write data beats to gather/buffer in write channel buffer before allowing the corresponding write command to be routed to arbiters. When configured to 0, write commands are held until the first beat of write data has been buffered. When configured to 1, write commands are held until two beats of write data have been buffered and so on. When configured with values larger than the number of beats in a write command, the command is held until the last beat has been buffered. When configured with values larger than the depth of write channel buffers, the command is held until all entries in the write channel buffer have been occupied. |
| 19:16 | RD_GATHER_BEATS | Configures the number of read data beats to gather/buffer in read channel buffer before allowing the read data to proceed to the master. When configured to 0, read data is allowed to proceed to the master as soon as the first beat is buffered in the read channel buffer. When configured to 1, read data is allowed to proceed to the master as soon as two beats of read data have been buffered and so on. When configured with values larger than the number of beats in the read burst, read data is held until the last beat has been buffered. When configured with values larger than the depth of read channel buffers, read data is held until all entries in the read channel buffer have been occupied. |
| 15 | RCSSH | Redirect Cacheable System SHareable. When set (1), enables redirection of all cacheable transactions that are system shareable to the redirect slaveway. Note: Only masters connecting using AMBA 4 ACE protocol are able to indicate system shareability for transactions. |
| 14 | RCOSH | Redirect Cacheable Outer SHareable. When set (1), enables redirection of all cacheable transactions that are outer shareable to the redirect slaveway. |
| 13 | RCISH | Redirect Cacheable Inner SHareable. When set (1), enables redirection of all cacheable transactions that are inner shareable to the redirect slaveway. |
| 12 | RCNSH | Redirect Cacheable Non-SHareable. When set (1), enables redirection of all cacheable transactions that are non-shareable to the redirect slaveway. |
| 11 | RNCSSH | Redirect Non-Cacheable System SHareable. When set (1), enables redirection of all non-cacheable transactions that are system shareable to the redirect slaveway. Note: Only masters connecting using AMBA 4 ACE protocol are able to indicate system shareability for transactions. |

### BIMC_M_GPU_MPORT_MODE (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 10 | RNCOSH | Redirect Non-Cacheable Outer SHareable. When set (1), enables redirection of all non-cacheable transactions that are outer shareable to the redirect slaveway. |
| 9 | RNCISH | Redirect Non-Cacheable Inner SHareable. When set (1), enables redirection of all non-cacheable transactions that are inner shareable to the redirect slaveway. |
| 8 | RNCNSH | Redirect Non-Cacheable Non-SHareable. When set (1), enables redirection of all non-cacheable transactions that are non-shareable to the redirect slaveway. |
| 4 | NARROW_WRITES | When set (1), enables converting of 1-beat bus-width sized writes down to 32-bit ASIZE based on write strobes. It is recommended to be enabled for directly connected CPU masters. When cleared (0), disables conversion and all writes are forwarded downstream as generated by the master. |
| 2 | FIODV | Force In-Order Device. When set (1), forces commands to device memory to be executed one at a time. In other words, commands to device memory are held until all previous commands have completed (responses have been received at the masterport) and all commands after the device command are held until the device completes (response has been received at the masterport.) |
| 1 | FIOSO | Force In-Order Strongly-Ordered. When set (1), forces commands to strongly ordered memory to be executed one at a time. In other words, commands to strongly ordered memory are held until all previous commands have completed (responses have been received at the masterport) and all commands after the strongly ordered command are held until the strongly ordered completes (response has been received at the masterport.) |
| 0 | ORDERING_MODEL | Configures how commands to memories of type Strongly ordered and Device (SoDv) are handled in the masterport. When configured as STRICT, all commands to SoDv memory are held until all previous commands have completed (responses have been received at the masterport) and all commands after the SoDv command are held until the SoDv completes (i.e. response has been received at the masterport.) When configured as RELAXED, all commands to SoDv memory are treated as accessing Normal memory.<br>0x0: RELAXED<br>0x1: STRICT |

### 0x00410220 BIMC_M_GPU_MPORT_WR_WAY_CROSSING

**Type**: RW
**Clock**: Config & Master Clocks
**Reset State**: `0x00000000`
<!-- page 157 -->

### BIMC_M_GPU_MPORT_WR_WAY_CROSSING (cont.)

Configures the level of strictness or relaxedness of way crossing checks for writes.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 7:0 | REG | 1-bit per slaveway. When 2 or more bits are set (1), allows the corresponding slaveways to be treated as one slaveway when write commands are considered as way crossing, ie. write commands to these 2 (or more) slaveways are not treated as way crossing when one write command targets one slaveway and the next write command targets the second slaveway. Not treating write commands as way crossing allows the write commands to go to the slaveway ahead of the write data for potentially better overall system performance. When all bits are set (1), disables all way crossing checks. When all bits are cleared (0), way crossing is strict with each way crossing write command held until write data for all previous writes have been routed to their corresponding slaveways. |

### 0x00410300 BIMC_M_GPU_MPORT_BKE_ENABLE

**Type**: RW
**Clock**: Config & Master Clocks
**Reset State**: `0x00000000`

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 0 | ENABLE | When set (1), enables the book keeping element (BKE) to determine AREQPRIORITY and APRIORITYLVL of commands from the bus master by comparing the amount of bus traffic from the bus master to a target, and determining a health level for the bus master. The health level determines the relative priority of commands from the bus master to allow the bus master to catch-up if it is not getting serviced, or slow down to allow other bus masters to get their share of system resources. When cleared (0), disables the book keeping element and AREQPRIORTY and APRIORITYLVL from the bus master are propagated downstream. |

Status registers indicate the state of several elements in the masterport, including the number of transactions outstanding/pending waiting for a response, emptiness, fullness of several buffers, etc. The state information is available only as a debug indication and could be delayed by a few clock cycles from when the state is reached to being reflected in the status registers. One or more of the state registers are read live and could capture intermediate values as they change.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |

| 7:0 | RD_PENDING_PRE_BUF | Indicates the number of read transactions that are outstanding/pending waiting for a response from the slave. This transaction count is from before address channel buffers, which interfaces to frontend of the masterport. |

Status registers indicate the state of several elements in the masterport, including the number of transactions outstanding/pending waiting for a response, emptiness, fullness of several buffers, etc. The state information is available only as a debug indication and could be delayed by a few clock cycles from when the state is reached to being reflected in the status registers. One or more of the state registers are read live and could capture intermediate values as they change.
