## BIMC_M_GPU_MPORT_STATUS_3B (0x00410434)

* **Type**: R
* **Clock**: Config, Master & Pipe0 Clocks
* **Reset State**: 0x00111111

Buffer status register indicate the state of all buffers in the masterport, whether they are empty or full on either side of the buffer. Some buffers carry information from master to core and others carry information from core to master. Both write side and read side status are indicated separately, since they would be not be similar when master clock and core clock are not synchronous to each other.

| 31 | RD_OUTSTANDING_OVERFLOW | Indicates that the number of outstanding reads crossed the maximum supported (255) during when traffic profiling was last enabled. It is recommended that this register be read only after traffic profiling has been disabled. |
| 30 | RD_OUTSTANDING_UNDERFLOW | Indicates that the number of outstanding reads went below 0 during when traffic profiling was last enabled. It is recommended that this register be read only after traffic profiling has been disabled. |
| 7:0 | RD_OUTSTANDING_MAX | Indicates the maximum number of outstanding reads that were seen when traffic profiling was last enabled. Only reads that match the MID filter and slaveway select filter are accounted for. It is recommended that this register be read only after traffic profiling has been disabled. |

### BIMC_M_SYS0_MPORT_COMPONENT_INFO (0x00414000)

* **Type**: R
* **Clock**: Config Clock
* **Reset State**: 0x00000102

Component information registers provide discoverability information on the type of component and instance of each component. These registers are always the very first register in each component's configuration address space and allow for a software routine to walk the configuration address space in steps of 4KB to identify the location of each configuration register space and to which component each 4KB configures.

### 0x00414220 BIMC_M_SYS0_MPORT_WR_WAY_CROSSING

- **Type**: RW
- **Clock**: Config & Master Clocks
- **Reset State**: 0x00000000

Configures the level of strictness or relaxedness of way crossing checks for writes.
<!-- page 180 -->

### BIMC_M_SYS0_MPORT_WR_WAY_CROSSING (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 7:0 | REG | 1-bit per slaveway. When 2 or more bits are set (1), allows the corresponding slaveways to be treated as one slaveway when write commands are considered as way crossing, i.e. write commands to these 2 (or more) slaveways are not treated as way crossing when one write command targets one slaveway and the next write command targets the second slaveway. Not treating write commands as way crossing allows the write commands to go to the slaveway ahead of the write data for potentially better overall system performance. When all bits are set (1), disables all way crossing checks. When all bits are cleared (0), way crossing is strict with each way crossing write command held until write data for all previous writes have been routed to their corresponding slaveways. |

### BIMC_M_SYS0_MPORT_BKE_ENABLE

**Address:** `0x00414300`
**Type:** RW
**Clock:** Config & Master Clocks
**Reset State:** `0x00000000`

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 0 | ENABLE | When set (1), enables the book keeping element (BKE) to determine AREQPRIORITY and APRIORITYLVL of commands from the bus master by comparing the amount of bus traffic from the bus master to a target, and determining a health level for the bus master. The health level determines the relative priority of commands from the bus master to allow the bus master to catch-up if it is not getting serviced, or slow down to allow other bus masters to get their share of system resources. When cleared (0), disables the book keeping element and AREQPRIORTY and APRIORITYLVL from the bus master are propagated downstream. |
<!-- page 184 -->

### BIMC_M_SYS0_MPORT_BKE_GRANT_PERIOD

**Address:** `0x00414304`
**Type:** RW
**Clock:** Config & Reference Clocks
**Reset State:** `0x00000000`

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 9:0 | GRANT_PERIOD | Defines the period over which the book keeping element accumulates grants to the bus master for determining it's health level. Grant period is defined in number of reference timer ticks. Refer configuration of reference timer tick for exact time unit. |

### BIMC_M_SYS0_MPORT_BKE_GRANT_COUNT

**Address:** `0x00414308`
**Type:** RW
**Clock:** Config & Master Clocks
**Reset State:** `0x00000000`

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 15:0 | GRANT_COUNT | Defines the target grant count for the bus master. The target grant count is the number of beats of read and write data the bus master is expected to write and read in the grant period and is used as a reference to determine if the bus master is behind or ahead of where it ought to be at any given time. |

### BIMC_M_SYS0_MPORT_STATUS_2A

**Address:** `0x00414420`
**Type:** R
**Clock:** Config, Master & Pipe0 Clocks
**Reset State:** `0x00000000`

Status registers indicate the state of several elements in the masterport, including the number of transactions outstanding/pending waiting for a response, emptiness, fullness of several buffers, etc. The state information is available only as a debug indication and could be delayed by a few clock cycles from when the state is reached to being reflected in the status registers. One or more of the state registers are read live and could capture intermediate values as they change.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 23:16 | WR_PENDING_PRE_BUF | Indicates the number of write transactions that are outstanding/pending waiting for a response from the slave. This transaction count is from before address channel buffers, which interfaces to frontend of the masterport. |
| 7:0 | RD_PENDING_PRE_BUF | Indicates the number of read transactions that are outstanding/pending waiting for a response from the slave. This transaction count is from before address channel buffers, which interfaces to frontend of the masterport. |

## 2.13 BIMC_M_TCU0_MPORT
**BRIC Masterport**

### 2.13.1 BIMC_M_TCU0_MPORT_BRIC_MASTERPORT
**BRIC Masterport**

### 0x0041C000 BIMC_M_TCU0_MPORT_COMPONENT_INFO

- **Type:** R
- **Clock:** Config Clock
- **Reset State:** 0x00000102

Component information registers provide discoverability information on the type of component and instance of each component. These registers are always the very first register in each component's configuration address space and allow for a software routine to walk the configuration address space in steps of 4KB to identify the location of each configuration register space and to which component each 4KB configures.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 23:16 | INSTANCE | Indicates the instance number of this masterport. |
| 15:8 | SUB_TYPE | Identifies this configuration space as belonging to a masterport<br>0x1: MASTERPORT |
| 7:0 | TYPE | Identifies this configuration space as belonging to a component that interfaces to a bus master.<br>0x2: MASTERPORT |

### 0x0041C020 BIMC_M_TCU0_MPORT_CONFIGURATION_INFO_0

- **Type:** R
- **Clock:** Config Clock
- **Reset State:** 0x01000000
<!-- page 192 -->
### BIMC_M_TCU0_MPORT_CONFIGURATION_INFO_0 (cont.)

Component information registers provide information on the capability and configuration of each masterport instance. See register field descriptions for more details.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:24 | SYNC_MODE | Indicates the clock relationship between the clock used in the master side and the clock used in the core side of the masterport. When ASYNC, identifies the master clock and core clock as unrelated and asynchronous to each other. When SYNC, identifies the master clock and core clock as synchronous to each other. When ISOSYNC, identifies the master clock and core clock as related, but of different frequencies, which are of integer ratios, i.e., they are iso-synchronous to each other.<br>0x0: ASYNC<br>0x1: SYNC<br>0x2: ISOSYNC |
| 15:8 | CONNECTION_TYPE | Indicates the type of master connecting to this masterport. When DIRECT, indicates that a bus master is directly connected to this masterport. When CASCADE, indicates that bus masters connect to this masterport through another level of interconnect.<br>0x0: DIRECT<br>0x1: CASCADE |
| 7:0 | FUNCTIONALITY | Indicates the functionality and type of bus traffic handled by this masterport. When INORDER, identifies this masterport as optimized for in-order bus traffic. When OOO_ONLY, identifies this masterport as optimized for out-of-order bus traffic, where a single master is capable of handling responses return in any order. When REORDER, identifies this masterport as having a reorder buffer for re-ordering responses to command order, while allowing bus slaves to return responses in any order they desire. When STUB, identifies this masterport has a stub.<br>0x0: STUB<br>0x1: OOO_ONLY<br>0x2: INORDER<br>0x3: REORDER |

When a specific bit is set (1), indicates that commands can be routed to the slaveway corresponding to this bit. WHen a specific bit is clear (0), indicates that commands are not routed to the slaveway corresponding to this bit. |

### 0x0041C050 BIMC_M_TCU0_MPORT_CONFIGURATION_INFO_3

- **Type:** R
- **Clock:** Config Clock
- **Reset State:** 0x00000000

Configuration information registers provide information on the capability and configuration of each masterport instance. See register field descriptions for more details.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:24 | RCH_DEPTH | Indicates the depth of read channel buffers in this masterport. A beat of read data occupies one entry in the read channel buffer, until accepted by the bus master. |
| 23:16 | BCH_DEPTH | Indicates the depth of write response channel buffers in this masterport. Each write response occupies one entry in the write response channel buffer, until accepted by the bus master. |

### 0x0041C210 BIMC_M_TCU0_MPORT_MODE

- **Type:** RW
- **Clock:** Config, Core & Master Clocks
- **Reset State:** 0x00000012

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:28 | WR_GATHER_BEATS | Configures the number of write data beats to gather/buffer in write channel buffer before allowing the corresponding write command to be routed to arbiters. When configured to 0, write commands are held until the first beat of write data has been buffered. When configured to 1, write commands are held until two beats of write data have been buffered and so on. When configured with values larger than the number of beats in a write command, the command is held until the last beat has been buffered. When configured with values larger than the depth of write channel buffers, the command is held until all entries in the write channel buffer have been occupied. |
| 19:16 | RD_GATHER_BEATS | Configures the number of read data beats to gather/buffer in read channel buffer before allowing the read data to proceed to the master. When configured to 0, read data is allowed to proceed to the master as soon as the first beat is buffered in the read channel buffer. When configured to 1, read data is allowed to proceed to the master as soon as two beats of read data have been buffered and so on. When configured with values larger than the number of beats in the read burst, read data is held until the last beat has been buffered. When configured with values larger than the depth of read channel buffers, read data is held until all entries in the read channel buffer have been occupied. |
| 15 | RCSSH | Redirect Cacheable System SHareable<br>When set (1), enables redirection of all cacheable transactions that are system shareable to the redirect slaveway. Note: Only masters connecting using AMBA 4 ACE protocol are able to indicate system shareability for transactions. |

| 13 | RCISH | Redirect Cacheable Inner SHareable<br>When set (1), enables redirection of all cacheable transactions that are inner shareable to the redirect slaveway. |

| 11 | RNCSSH | Redirect Non-Cacheable System SHareable<br>When set (1), enables redirection of all non-cacheable transactions that are system shareable to the redirect slaveway. Note: Only masters connecting using AMBA 4 ACE protocol are able to indicate system shareability for transactions. |

| Bits | Name | Description |

It is recommended to be enabled for directly connected CPU masters. When cleared (0), disables conversion and all writes are forwarded downstream as generated by the master. |
| 2 | FIODV | Force In-Order Device<br>When set (1), forces commands to device memory to be executed one at a time. | 1 | FIOSO | Force In-Order Strongly-Ordered<br>When set (1), forces commands to strongly ordered memory to be executed one at a time. In other words, commands to strongly ordered memory are held until all previous commands have completed (responses have been received at the masterport) and all commands after the strongly ordered command are held until the strongly ordered completes (response has been received at the masterport.) |
| 0 | ORDERING_MODEL | Configures how commands to memories of type Strongly ordered and Device (SoDv) are handled in the masterport. When configured as STRICT, all commands to SoDv memory are held until all previous commands have completed (responses have been received at the masterport) and all commands after the SoDv command are held until the SoDv completes (i.e. response has been received at the masterport.) When configured as RELAXED, all commands to SoDv memory are treated as accessing Normal memory.<br>0x0: RELAXED<br>0x1: STRICT |

### 0x0041C220 BIMC_M_TCU0_MPORT_WR_WAY_CROSSING

- **Type:** RW
- **Clock:** Config & Master Clocks
- **Reset State:** 0x00000000




<!-- page 201 -->

Configures the level of strictness or relaxedness of way crossing checks for writes.

### BIMC_M_TCU0_MPORT_WR_WAY_CROSSING

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 7:0 | REG | 1-bit per slaveway. When 2 or more bits are set (1), allows the corresponding slaveways to be treated as one slaveway when write commands are considered as way crossing, ie. write commands to these 2 (or more) slaveways are not treated as way crossing when one write command targets one slaveway and the next write command targets the second slaveway. Not treating write commands as way crossing allows the write commands to go to the slaveway ahead of the write data for potentially better overall system performance. When all bits are set (1), disables all way crossing checks. When all bits are cleared (0), way crossing is strict with each way crossing write command held until write data for all previous writes have been routed to their corresponding slaveways. |

| 0 | ENABLE | When set (1), enables the book keeping element (BKE) to determine AREQPRIORITY and APRIORITYLVL of commands from the bus master by comparing the amount of bus traffic from the bus master to a target, and determining a health level for the bus master. The health level determines the relative priority of commands from the bus master to allow the bus master to catch-up if it is not getting serviced, or slow down to allow other bus masters to get their share of system resources. Status registers indicate the state of several elements in the masterport, including the number of transactions outstanding/pending waiting for a response, emptiness, fullness of several buffers, etc. The state information is available only as a debug indication and could be delayed by a few clock cycles from when the state is reached to being reflected in the status registers. One or more of the state registers are read live and could capture intermediate values as they change.

#### BIMC_M_TCU0_MPORT_STATUS_2A

### 0x0041C430 BIMC_M_TCU0_MPORT_STATUS_3A

* **Type:** R
* **Clock:** Config, Master & Pipe0 Clocks
* **Reset State:** 0x55111111

Status registers indicate the state of several elements in the masterport, including the number of transactions outstanding/pending waiting for a response, emptiness, fullness of several buffers, etc. The state information is available only as a debug indication and could be delayed by a few clock cycles from when the state is reached to being reflected in the status registers. One or more of the state registers are read live and could capture intermediate values as they change.

**Type:** R

Buffer status register indicate the state of all buffers in the masterport, whether they are empty or full on either side of the buffer. Some buffers carry information from master to core and others carry information from core to master. ## 2.14 BIMC_M_SYS1_PROF (BRIC Traffic Profiling)

### 2.14.1 BIMC_M_SYS1_PROF_BRIC_PROFILING (BRIC Traffic Profiling)

### 0x00419000 BIMC_M_SYS1_PROF_COMPONENT_INFO

**Type:** R  
**Clock:** Config Clock  
**Reset State:** 0x00000202  

Component information registers provide discoverability information on the type of component and instance of each component. These registers are always the very first register in each component's configuration address space and allow for a software routine to walk the configuration address space in steps of 4KB to identify the location of each configuration register space and to which component each 4KB configures.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---------- |
| 23:16 | INSTANCE | Indicates the instance number of this traffic profiling. |
| 15:8 | SUB_TYPE | Identifies this configuration space as belonging to traffic profiling<br>0x2: PROFILING |
| 7:0 | TYPE | Identifies this configuration space as belonging to a component that interfaces to a bus master.<br>0x2: MASTERPORT |

### 0x00419020 BIMC_M_SYS1_PROF_CONFIGURATION_INFO_0

**Type:** R  
**Clock:** Config Clock  
**Reset State:** 0x00000000  

Configuration information registers provide information on the capability and configuration of each traffic profiling instance. See register field descriptions for more details.
<!-- page 213 -->
#### BIMC_M_SYS1_PROF_CONFIGURATION_INFO_0 (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---------- |
| 31:24 | TENURE_WIDTH | Indicates the width of tenures (latencies) measured in traffic profiling. |
| 23:16 | TRACKING_TABLE_DEPTH | Indicates the number of entries in the table that tracks outstanding commands for determining how many commands have larger turnaround latencies that a programmed threshold. |
| 7:0 | SCALING_FACTOR | Indicates how many extra scaling is performed on events generated by traffic profiling if such events have to be synchronized from the tenure clock to the event clock. Any value that is non-power-of-2 is converted to power-of-2 by hardware. When the value read from this register field is used in software, similar conversion of non-power-of-2 values to next higher power-of-2 value is necessary. |

### 0x00419030 BIMC_M_SYS1_PROF_CONFIGURATION_INFO_1

**Type:** R  
**Clock:** Config Clock  
**Reset State:** 0x00000000  

Configuration information registers provide information on the capability and configuration of each traffic profiling instance. See register field descriptions for more details.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---------- |
| 23:16 | PIPE2_ACH_DEPTH | Indicates the depth of address channel buffer in pipe2 of masterport in which this traffic profiling instance is paired with. Applies only to traffic profiling instances in XR type masterports, which contains three distinct paths to slaves, in pipe0, pipe1, pipe2. In non-XR type masterports, value contained in field does not refer to any actual address channel buffer. |
| 15:8 | PIPE1_ACH_DEPTH | Indicates the depth of address channel buffer in pipe1 of masterport in which this traffic profiling instance is paired with. Applies only to traffic profiling instances in XR type masterports, which contains three distinct paths to slaves, in pipe0, pipe1, pipe2. In non-XR type masterports, value contained in field does not refer to any actual address channel buffer. |
| 7:0 | PIPE0_ACH_DEPTH | Indicates the depth of address channel buffer in pipe0 of masterport in which this traffic profiling instance is paired with. Applies only to traffic profiling instances in XR type masterports, which contains three distinct paths to slaves, in pipe0, pipe1, pipe2. In non-XR type masterports, pipe0 refers to the common address channel buffer used for all slave accesses. |
<!-- page 214 -->
### 0x00419200 BIMC_M_SYS1_PROF_CLOCK_CTRL

**Type:** RW  
**Clock:** Config, Event & Tenure Clocks  
**Reset State:** 0x00000003  

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---------- |
| 1 | TENURE_CLOCK_GATING_EN | When set (1), enables activity based clock gating of all registers clocked by tenure clock. Activity based clock gating uses architectural clock gates to reduce dynamic power consumption by gating clocks during periods of in-activity. When cleared (0), disables all activity based clock gating by forcing all architectural clock gates to not gate clocks even during periods of in-activity. |
| 0 | EVENT_CLOCK_GATING_EN | When set (1), enables activity based clock gating of all registers clocked by event clock. Activity based clock gating uses architectural clock gates to reduce dynamic power consumption by gating clocks during periods of in-activity. When cleared (0), disables all activity based clock gating by forcing all architectural clock gates to not gate clocks even during periods of in-activity. |

### 0x00419210 BIMC_M_SYS1_PROF_MODE

**Type:** RW  
**Clock:** Config, Event & Tenure Clocks  
**Reset State:** 0x00000000  
<!-- page 215 -->
#### BIMC_M_SYS1_PROF_MODE (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---------- |
| 25:24 | WR_TENURE_MODE | Configures the start and end events for monitoring write latencies/tenures. When configured to WR_CMD_TO_BRESP, starting event is first cycle of write command from bus master as seen by traffic profiling and ending event is first cycle of write response to bus master as seen by traffic profiling. When configured to WR_CMD_TO_BRESP_HANDSHAKE, starting event is first cycle of write command from bus master as seen by traffic profiling and ending event is transfer handshake of write response to bus master as seen by traffic profiling. When configured to WR_CMD_HANDSHAKE, starting event is first cycle of write command from bus master as seen by traffic profiling and ending event is transfer handshake of the same write command with bus master as seen by traffic profiling. When configured to WR_RESP_HANDSHAKE, starting event is first cycle of write response to bus master as seen by traffic profiling and ending event is transfer handshake of write response to bus master as seen by traffic profiling.<br>0x0: WR_CMD_TO_BRESP<br>0x1: WR_CMD_TO_BRESP_HANDSHAKE<br>0x2: WR_CMD_HANDSHAKE<br>0x3: WR_RESP_HANDSHAKE |
| 17:16 | RD_TENURE_MODE | Configures the start and end events for monitoring read latencies/tenures. When configured to RD_CMD_TO_FIRST_RDATA, starting event is first cycle of read command from bus master as seen by traffic profiling and ending event is first cycle of first beat of read data to bus master as seen by traffic profiling. When configured to RD_CMD_TO_LAST_RDATA, starting event is first cycle of read command from bus master as seen by traffic profiling and ending event is transfer handshake of last beat of read data to bus master as seen by traffic profiling. When configured to RD_CMD_HANDSHAKE, starting event is first cycle of read command from bus master as seen by traffic profiling and ending event is transfer handshake of the same read command with bus master as seen by traffic profiling. When configured to RD_DATA_HANDSHAKE, starting event is first cycle of first beat of read data to bus master as seen by traffic profiling and ending event is transfer handshake of last beat of read data to bus master as seen by traffic profiling.<br>0x0: RD_CMD_TO_FIRST_RDATA<br>0x1: RD_CMD_TO_LAST_RDATA<br>0x2: RD_CMD_HANDSHAKE<br>0x3: RD_DATA_HANDSHAKE |
| 0 | PROFILING_EN | When set (1), enables traffic profiling to monitor bus transactions from bus master and generate events for counting in performance monitors. When cleared (0), disables traffic profiling. |

## 2.15 BIMC_M_TCU0_MPORT (BRIC Masterport)

### 2.15.1 BIMC_M_TCU0_MPORT_BRIC_MASTERPORT (BRIC Masterport)

### `0x0041C000` BIMC_M_TCU0_MPORT_COMPONENT_INFO

- **Type**: R
- **Clock**: Config Clock
- **Reset State**: `0x00000102`

Component information registers provide discoverability information on the type of component and instance of each component. These registers are always the very first register in each component's configuration address space and allow for a software routine to walk the configuration address space in steps of 4KB to identify the location of each configuration register space and to which component each 4KB configures.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 23:16 | INSTANCE | Indicates the instance number of this masterport. |
| 15:8 | SUB_TYPE | Identifies this configuration space as belonging to a masterport<br>0x1: MASTERPORT |
| 7:0 | TYPE | Identifies this configuration space as belonging to a component that interfaces to a bus master.<br>0x2: MASTERPORT |
<!-- page 229 -->

### `0x0041C020` BIMC_M_TCU0_MPORT_CONFIGURATION_INFO_0

- **Type**: R
- **Clock**: Config Clock
- **Reset State**: `0x01000000`

Configuration information registers provide information on the capability and configuration of each masterport instance. See register field descriptions for more details.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:24 | SYNC_MODE | Indicates the clock relationship between the clock used in the master side and the clock used in the core side of the masterport. When ASYNC, identifies the master clock and core clock as unrelated and asynchronous to each other. When SYNC, identifies the master clock and core clock as synchronous to each other. When ISOSYNC, identifies the master clock and core clock as related, but of different frequencies, which are of integer ratios, i.e., they are iso-synchronous to each other.<br>0x0: ASYNC<br>0x1: SYNC<br>0x2: ISOSYNC |
| 15:8 | CONNECTION_TYPE | Indicates the type of master connecting to this masterport. When DIRECT, indicates that a bus master is directly connected to this masterport. When CASCADE, indicates that bus masters connect to this masterport through another level of interconnect.<br>0x0: DIRECT<br>0x1: CASCADE |
| 7:0 | FUNCTIONALITY | Indicates the functionality and type of bus traffic handled by this masterport. When INORDER, identifies this masterport as optimized for in-order bus traffic. When OOO_ONLY, identifies this masterport as optimized for out-of-order bus traffic, where a single master is capable of handling responses return in any order. When REORDER, identifies this masterport as having a reorder buffer for re-ordering responses to command order, while allowing bus slaves to return responses in any order they desire. When STUB, identifies this masterport has a stub.<br>0x0: STUB<br>0x1: OOO_ONLY<br>0x2: INORDER<br>0x3: REORDER |

### 0x0041C200 BIMC_M_TCU0_MPORT_CLOCK_CTRL

**Type:** RW

Activity based clock gating uses architectural clock gates to reduce dynamic power consumption by gating clocks during periods of inactivity. When cleared (0), disables all activity based clock gating by forcing all architectural clock gates to not gate clocks even during periods of inactivity. |

### 0x0041C210 BIMC_M_TCU0_MPORT_MODE

**Type:** RW
**Clock:** Config, Core & Master Clocks
**Reset State:** 0x00000012

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:28 | WR_GATHER_BEATS | Configures the number of write data beats to gather/buffer in write channel buffer before allowing the corresponding write command to be routed to arbiters. When configured to 0, write commands are held until the first beat of write data has been buffered. When configured to 1, write commands are held until two beats of write data have been buffered and so on. When configured with values larger than the number of beats in a write command, the command is held until the last beat has been buffered. When configured with values larger than the depth of write channel buffers, the command is held until all entries in the write channel buffer have been occupied. |
| 19:16 | RD_GATHER_BEATS | Configures the number of read data beats to gather/buffer in read channel buffer before allowing the read data to proceed to the master. When configured to 0, read data is allowed to proceed to the master as soon as the first beat is buffered in the read channel buffer. When configured to 1, read data is allowed to proceed to the master as soon as two beats of read data have been buffered and so on. When configured with values larger than the number of beats in the read burst, read data is held until the last beat has been buffered. When configured with values larger than the depth of read channel buffers, read data is held until all entries in the read channel buffer have been occupied. |
| 15 | RCSSH | Redirect Cacheable System SHareable<br>When set (1), enables redirection of all cacheable transactions that are system shareable to the redirect slaveway. Note: Only masters connecting using AMBA 4 ACE protocol are able to indicate system shareability for transactions. |
| 14 | RCOSH | Redirect Cacheable Outer SHareable<br>When set (1), enables redirection of all cacheable transactions that are outer shareable to the redirect slaveway. |
| 13 | RCISH | Redirect Cacheable Inner SHareable<br>When set (1), enables redirection of all cacheable transactions that are inner shareable to the redirect slaveway. |
| 12 | RCNSH | Redirect Cacheable Non-SHareable<br>When set (1), enables redirection of all cacheable transactions that are non-shareable to the redirect slaveway. |
| 11 | RNCSSH | Redirect Non-Cacheable System SHareable<br>When set (1), enables redirection of all non-cacheable transactions that are system shareable to the redirect slaveway. Note: Only masters connecting using AMBA 4 ACE protocol are able to indicate system shareability for transactions. |

#### BIMC_M_TCU0_MPORT_MODE (continued)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 10 | RNCOSH | Redirect Non-Cacheable Outer SHareable<br>When set (1), enables redirection of all non-cacheable transactions that are outer shareable to the redirect slaveway. |
| 9 | RNCISH | Redirect Non-Cacheable Inner SHareable<br>When set (1), enables redirection of all non-cacheable transactions that are inner shareable to the redirect slaveway. |
| 8 | RNCNSH | Redirect Non-Cacheable Non-SHareable<br>When set (1), enables redirection of all non-cacheable transactions that are non-shareable to the redirect slaveway. |
| 4 | NARROW_WRITES | When set (1), enables converting of 1-beat bus-width sized writes down to 32-bit ASIZE based on write strobes. It is recommended to be enabled for directly connected CPU masters. When cleared (0), disables conversion and all writes are forwarded downstream as generated by the master. |
| 2 | FIODV | Force In-Order Device<br>When set (1), forces commands to device memory to be executed one at a time. In other words, commands to device memory are held until all previous commands have completed (responses have been received at the masterport) and all commands after the device command are held until the device completes (response has been received at the masterport.) |
| 1 | FIOSO | Force In-Order Strongly-Ordered<br>When set (1), forces commands to strongly ordered memory to be executed one at a time. In other words, commands to strongly ordered memory are held until all previous commands have completed (responses have been received at the masterport) and all commands after the strongly ordered command are held until the strongly ordered completes (response has been received at the masterport.) |
| 0 | ORDERING_MODEL | Configures how commands to memories of type Strongly ordered and Device (SoDv) are handled in the masterport. When configured as STRICT, all commands to SoDv memory are held until all previous commands have completed (responses have been received at the masterport) and all commands after the SoDv command are held until the SoDv completes (i.e. response has been received at the masterport.) When configured as RELAXED, all commands to SoDv memory are treated as accessing Normal memory.<br>0x0: RELAXED<br>0x1: STRICT |

### 0x0041C220 BIMC_M_TCU0_MPORT_WR_WAY_CROSSING

**Type:** RW
**Clock:** Config & Master Clocks
**Reset State:** 0x00000000
<!-- page 238 -->

#### BIMC_M_TCU0_MPORT_WR_WAY_CROSSING (continued)

Configures the level of strictness or relaxedness of way crossing checks for writes.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 7:0 | REG | 1-bit per slaveway. When 2 or more bits are set (1), allows the corresponding slaveways to be treated as one slaveway when write commands are considered as way crossing, ie. write commands to these 2 (or more) slaveways are not treated as way crossing when one write command targets one slaveway and the next write command targets the second slaveway. Not treating write commands as way crossing allows the write commands to go to the slaveway ahead of the write data for potentially better overall system performance. When all bits are set (1), disables all way crossing checks. When all bits are cleared (0), way crossing is strict with each way crossing write command held until write data for all previous writes have been routed to their corresponding slaveways. |

**Clock:** Config & Master Clocks

| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 9:8 | PRIORITYLVL | Configures the values to override APRIORITYLVL from bus master with when OVERRIDE_PRIORITYLVL is set (1). |
| 0 | OVERRIDE_PRIORITYLVL | When set (1), overrides APRIORITYLVL from the bus master with values configured in PRIORITYLVL register field. When cleared (0), allows APRIORITYLVL from the bus master to be propagated downstream. |

### BIMC_M_TCU0_MPORT_BKE_ENABLE

**Address:** `0x0041C300`  
**Type:** RW  
**Clock:** Config & Master Clocks  
**Reset State:** `0x00000000`  

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 0 | ENABLE | When set (1), enables the book keeping element (BKE) to determine AREQPRIORITY and APRIORITYLVL of commands from the bus master by comparing the amount of bus traffic from the bus master to a target, and determining a health level for the bus master. The health level determines the relative priority of commands from the bus master to allow the bus master to catch-up if it is not getting serviced, or slow down to allow other bus masters to get their share of system resources. When cleared (0), disables the book keeping element and AREQPRIORTY and APRIORITYLVL from the bus master are propagated downstream. |
<!-- page 242 -->
### BIMC_M_TCU0_MPORT_BKE_GRANT_PERIOD

**Address:** `0x0041C304`  
**Type:** RW  
**Clock:** Config & Reference Clocks  
**Reset State:** `0x00000000`  

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 9:0 | GRANT_PERIOD | Defines the period over which the book keeping element accumulates grants to the bus master for determining it's health level. Grant period is defined in number of reference timer ticks. Refer configuration of reference timer tick for exact time unit. |

**Address:** `0x0041C308`

**Reset State:** `0x00000000`  

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 15:0 | GRANT_COUNT | Defines the target grant count for the bus master. The target grant count is the number of beats of read and write data the bus master is expected to write and read in the grant period and is used as a reference to determine if the bus master is behind or ahead of where it ought to be at any given time. |

### BIMC_M_TCU0_MPORT_STATUS_2A

**Address:** `0x0041C420`  
**Type:** R  
**Clock:** Config, Master & Pipe0 Clocks  
**Reset State:** `0x00000000`  

Status registers indicate the state of several elements in the masterport, including the number of transactions outstanding/pending waiting for a response, emptiness, fullness of several buffers, etc. The state information is available only as a debug indication and could be delayed by a few clock cycles from when the state is reached to being reflected in the status registers. One or more of the state registers are read live and could capture intermediate values as they change.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 23:16 | WR_PENDING_PRE_BUF | Indicates the number of write transactions that are outstanding/pending waiting for a response from the slave. This transaction count is from before address channel buffers, which interfaces to frontend of the masterport. |
| 7:0 | RD_PENDING_PRE_BUF | Indicates the number of read transactions that are outstanding/pending waiting for a response from the slave. This transaction count is from before address channel buffers, which interfaces to frontend of the masterport. |

### BIMC_M_TCU0_MPORT_STATUS_2B

**Clock:** Config, Master & Pipe0 Clocks  
**Reset State:** `0x00000000`

| :--- | :--- | :--- |

| 7:0 | RD_PENDING_POST_BUF | Indicates the number of read transactions that are outstanding/pending waiting for a response from the slave. This transaction count is from after address channel buffers, which interfaces to core of the interconnect, i.e., arbiter and slaveway. |

## 2.16 BIMC_M_TCU0_PROF
**BRIC Traffic Profiling**

### 2.16.1 BIMC_M_TCU0_PROF_BRIC_PROFILING
**BRIC Traffic Profiling**

### BIMC_M_TCU0_PROF_COMPONENT_INFO

**Address:** `0x0041D000`  
**Type:** R  
**Clock:** Config Clock  
**Reset State:** `0x00000202`  

Component information registers provide discoverability information on the type of component and instance of each component. These registers are always the very first register in each component's configuration address space and allow for a software routine to walk the configuration address space in steps of 4KB to identify the location of each configuration register space and to which component each 4KB configures.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 23:16 | INSTANCE | Indicates the instance number of this traffic profiling. |
| 15:8 | SUB_TYPE | Identifies this configuration space as belonging to traffic profiling<br>0x2: PROFILING |
| 7:0 | TYPE | Identifies this configuration space as belonging to a component that interfaces to a bus master.<br>0x2: MASTERPORT |

### BIMC_M_TCU0_PROF_CONFIGURATION_INFO_0

**Address:** `0x0041D020`  
**Type:** R  
**Clock:** Config Clock  
**Reset State:** `0x00000000`  
<!-- page 250 -->
### BIMC_M_TCU0_PROF_CONFIGURATION_INFO_0 (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:24 | TENURE_WIDTH | Indicates the width of tenures (latencies) measured in traffic profiling. |
| 23:16 | TRACKING_TABLE_DEPTH | Indicates the number of entries in the table that tracks outstanding commands for determining how many commands have larger turnaround latencies that a programmed threshold. |
| 7:0 | SCALING_FACTOR | Indicates how many extra scaling is performed on events generated by traffic profiling if such events have to be synchronized from the tenure clock to the event clock. Any value that is non-power-of-2 is converted to power-of-2 by hardware. When the value read from this register field is used in software, similar conversion of non-power-of-2 values to next higher power-of-2 value is necessary. |

### BIMC_M_TCU0_PROF_CONFIGURATION_INFO_1

**Address:** `0x0041D030`  
**Type:** R  
**Clock:** Config Clock  
**Reset State:** `0x00000000`  

Configuration information registers provide information on the capability and configuration of each traffic profiling instance. See register field descriptions for more details.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 23:16 | PIPE2_ACH_DEPTH | Indicates the depth of address channel buffer in pipe2 of masterport in which this traffic profiling instance is paired with. Applies only to traffic profiling instances in XR type masterports, which contains three distinct paths to slaves, in pipe0, pipe1, pipe2. In non-XR type masterports, value contained in field does not refer to any actual address channel buffer. |
| 15:8 | PIPE1_ACH_DEPTH | Indicates the depth of address channel buffer in pipe1 of masterport in which this traffic profiling instance is paired with. Applies only to traffic profiling instances in XR type masterports, which contains three distinct paths to slaves, in pipe0, pipe1, pipe2. In non-XR type masterports, value contained in field does not refer to any actual address channel buffer. |
| 7:0 | PIPE0_ACH_DEPTH | Indicates the depth of address channel buffer in pipe0 of masterport in which this traffic profiling instance is paired with. Applies only to traffic profiling instances in XR type masterports, which contains three distinct paths to slaves, in pipe0, pipe1, pipe2. In non-XR type masterports, pipe0 refers to the common address channel buffer used for all slave accesses. |


<!-- page 251 -->
# Bus Integrated Memory Controller

## BIMC_M_TCU0_PROF_CLOCK_CTRL (0x0041D200)

* **Type**: RW
* **Clock**: Config, Event & Tenure Clocks
* **Reset State**: 0x00000003

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1 | TENURE_CLOCK_GATING_EN | When set (1), enables activity based clock gating of all registers clocked by tenure clock. Activity based clock gating uses architectural clock gates to reduce dynamic power consumption by gating clocks during periods of in-activity. When cleared (0), disables all activity based clock gating by forcing all architectural clock gates to not gate clocks even during periods of in-activity. |
| 0 | EVENT_CLOCK_GATING_EN | When set (1), enables activity based clock gating of all registers clocked by event clock. Activity based clock gating uses architectural clock gates to reduce dynamic power consumption by gating clocks during periods of in-activity. When cleared (0), disables all activity based clock gating by forcing all architectural clock gates to not gate clocks even during periods of in-activity. |

## BIMC_M_TCU0_PROF_MODE (0x0041D210)

* **Type**: RW
* **Clock**: Config, Event & Tenure Clocks
* **Reset State**: 0x00000000
<!-- page 252 -->
# Bus Integrated Memory Controller

## BIMC_M_TCU0_PROF_MODE (0x0041D210) (Continued)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 25:24 | WR_TENURE_MODE | Configures the start and end events for monitoring write latencies/tenures. When configured to WR_CMD_TO_BRESP, starting event is first cycle of write command from bus master as seen by traffic profiling and ending event is first cycle of write response to bus master as seen by traffic profiling. When configured to WR_CMD_TO_BRESP_HANDSHAKE, starting event is first cycle of write command from bus master as seen by traffic profiling and ending event is transfer handshake of write response to bus master as seen by traffic profiling. When configured to WR_CMD_HANDSHAKE, starting event is first cycle of write command from bus master as seen by traffic profiling and ending event is transfer handshake of the same write command with bus master as seen by traffic profiling. When configured to WR_RESP_HANDSHAKE, starting event is first cycle of write response to bus master as seen by traffic profiling and ending event is transfer handshake of write response to bus master as seen by traffic profiling.<br>0x0: WR_CMD_TO_BRESP<br>0x1: WR_CMD_TO_BRESP_HANDSHAKE<br>0x2: WR_CMD_HANDSHAKE<br>0x3: WR_RESP_HANDSHAKE |
| 17:16 | RD_TENURE_MODE | Configures the start and end events for monitoring read latencies/tenures. When configured to RD_CMD_TO_FIRST_RDATA, starting event is first cycle of read command from bus master as seen by traffic profiling and ending event is first cycle of first beat of read data to bus master as seen by traffic profiling. When configured to RD_CMD_TO_LAST_RDATA, starting event is first cycle of read command from bus master as seen by traffic profiling and ending event is transfer handshake of last beat of read data to bus master as seen by traffic profiling. When configured to RD_CMD_HANDSHAKE, starting event is first cycle of read command from bus master as seen by traffic profiling and ending event is transfer handshake of the same read command with bus master as seen by traffic profiling. When configured to RD_DATA_HANDSHAKE, starting event is first cycle of first beat of read data to bus master as seen by traffic profiling and ending event is transfer handshake of last beat of read data to bus master as seen by traffic profiling.<br>0x0: RD_CMD_TO_FIRST_RDATA<br>0x1: RD_CMD_TO_LAST_RDATA<br>0x2: RD_CMD_HANDSHAKE<br>0x3: RD_DATA_HANDSHAKE |
| 0 | PROFILING_EN | When set (1), enables traffic profiling to monitor bus transactions from bus master and generate events for counting in performance monitors. When cleared (0), disables traffic profiling. |

### 0x0041D400 + 0x4*n BIMC_M_TCU0_PROF_RD_STATUS_n, n=[0..0]

**Type:** R
**Clock:** Config & Tenure Clocks
**Reset State:** 0x00000000

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31 | RD_OUTSTANDING_OVERFLOW | Indicates that the number of outstanding reads crossed the maximum supported (255) during when traffic profiling was last enabled. It is recommended that this register be read only after traffic profiling has been disabled. |
| 30 | RD_OUTSTANDING_UNDERFLOW | Indicates that the number of outstanding reads went below 0 during when traffic profiling was last enabled. It indicates that more command completions were seen compared to commands starts. The most likely scenario is an overflow of number of outstanding reads occurred leading to some command starts not being tracked. It is recommended that this register be read only after traffic profiling has been disabled. |
| 7:0 | RD_OUTSTANDING_MAX | Indicates the maximum number of outstanding reads that were seen when traffic profiling was last enabled. Only reads that match the MID filter and slaveway select filter are accounted for. It is recommended that this register be read only after traffic profiling has been disabled. |

## 2.17 BIMC_M_TCU1_MPORT

BRIC Masterport

### 2.17.1 BIMC_M_TCU1_MPORT_BRIC_MASTERPORT

BRIC Masterport

### 0x00420000 BIMC_M_TCU1_MPORT_COMPONENT_INFO

**Type:** R
**Clock:** Config Clock
**Reset State:** 0x00000102

Component information registers provide discoverability information on the type of component and instance of each component. These registers are always the very first register in each component's configuration address space and allow for a software routine to walk the configuration address space in steps of 4KB to identify the location of each configuration register space and to which component each 4KB configures.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 23:16 | INSTANCE | Indicates the instance number of this masterport. |
| 15:8 | SUB_TYPE | Identifies this configuration space as belonging to a masterport<br>0x1: MASTERPORT |
| 7:0 | TYPE | Identifies this configuration space as belonging to a component that interfaces to a bus master.<br>0x2: MASTERPORT |
<!-- page 266 -->

### 0x00420020 BIMC_M_TCU1_MPORT_CONFIGURATION_INFO_0

**Type:** R
**Clock:** Config Clock
**Reset State:** 0x01000000

Configuration information registers provide information on the capability and configuration of each masterport instance. See register field descriptions for more details.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:24 | SYNC_MODE | Indicates the clock relationship between the clock used in the master side and the clock used in the core side of the masterport. When ASYNC, identifies the master clock and core clock as unrelated and asynchronous to each other. When SYNC, identifies the master clock and core clock as synchronous to each other. When ISOSYNC, identifies the master clock and core clock as related, but of different frequencies, which are of integer ratios, i.e., they are iso-synchronous to each other.<br>0x0: ASYNC<br>0x1: SYNC<br>0x2: ISOSYNC |
| 15:8 | CONNECTION_TYPE | Indicates the type of master connecting to this masterport. When DIRECT, indicates that a bus master is directly connected to this masterport. When CASCADE, indicates that bus masters connect to this masterport through another level of interconnect.<br>0x0: DIRECT<br>0x1: CASCADE |
| 7:0 | FUNCTIONALITY | Indicates the functionality and type of bus traffic handled by this masterport. When INORDER, identifies this masterport as optimized for in-order bus traffic. When OOO_ONLY, identifies this masterport as optimized for out-of-order bus traffic, where a single master is capable of handling responses return in any order. When REORDER, identifies this masterport as having a reorder buffer for re-ordering responses to command order, while allowing bus slaves to return responses in any order they desire. When STUB, identifies this masterport has a stub.<br>0x0: STUB<br>0x1: OOO_ONLY<br>0x2: INORDER<br>0x3: REORDER |

When a specific bit is clear (0), indicates that commands are not routed to the slaveway corresponding to this bit. |

### 0x00420210 BIMC_M_TCU1_MPORT_MODE

- **Type**: RW

**BIMC_M_TCU1_MPORT_MODE**

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:28 | WR_GATHER_BEATS | Configures the number of write data beats to gather/buffer in write channel buffer before allowing the corresponding write command to be routed to arbiters. When configured to 0, write commands are held until the first beat of write data has been buffered. When configured to 1, write commands are held until two beats of write data have been buffered and so on. When configured with values larger than the number of beats in a write command, the command is held until the last beat has been buffered. When configured with values larger than the depth of write channel buffers, the command is held until all entries in the write channel buffer have been occupied. |
| 19:16 | RD_GATHER_BEATS | Configures the number of read data beats to gather/buffer in read channel buffer before allowing the read data to proceed to the master. When configured to 0, read data is allowed to proceed to the master as soon as the first beat is buffered in the read channel buffer. When configured to 1, read data is allowed to proceed to the master as soon as two beats of read data have been buffered and so on. When configured with values larger than the number of beats in the read burst, read data is held until the last beat has been buffered. When configured with values larger than the depth of read channel buffers, read data is held until all entries in the read channel buffer have been occupied. |
| 15 | RCSSH | Redirect Cacheable System SHareable<br>When set (1), enables redirection of all cacheable transactions that are system shareable to the redirect slaveway. Note: Only masters connecting using AMBA 4 ACE protocol are able to indicate system shareability for transactions. |

| 11 | RNCSSH | Redirect Non-Cacheable System SHareable<br>When set (1), enables redirection of all non-cacheable transactions that are system shareable to the redirect slaveway. Note: Only masters connecting using AMBA 4 ACE protocol are able to indicate system shareability for transactions. |

It is recommended to be enabled for directly connected CPU masters. When cleared (0), disables conversion and all writes are forwarded downstream as generated by the master. |
| 2 | FIODV | Force In-Order Device<br>When set (1), forces commands to device memory to be executed one at a time. In other words, commands to device memory are held until all previous commands have completed (responses have been received at the masterport) and all commands after the device command are held until the device completes (response has been received at the masterport.) |
| 1 | FIOSO | Force In-Order Strongly-Ordered<br>When set (1), forces commands to strongly ordered memory to be executed one at a time. In other words, commands to strongly ordered memory are held until all previous commands have completed (responses have been received at the masterport) and all commands after the strongly ordered command are held until the strongly ordered completes (response has been received at the masterport.) |
| 0 | ORDERING_MODEL | Configures how commands to memories of type Strongly ordered and Device (SoDv) are handled in the masterport. When configured as STRICT, all commands to SoDv memory are held until all previous commands have completed (responses have been received at the masterport) and all commands after the SoDv command are held until the SoDv completes (i.e. response has been received at the masterport.) When configured as RELAXED, all commands to SoDv memory are treated as accessing Normal memory.<br>0x0: RELAXED<br>0x1: STRICT |

### 0x00420220 BIMC_M_TCU1_MPORT_WR_WAY_CROSSING

- **Type**: RW
- **Clock**: Config & Master Clocks
- **Reset State**: 0x00000000
<!-- page 275 -->
**BIMC_M_TCU1_MPORT_WR_WAY_CROSSING (cont.)**

Configures the level of strictness or relaxedness of way crossing checks for writes.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 7:0 | REG | 1-bit per slaveway. When 2 or more bits are set (1), allows the corresponding slaveways to be treated as one slaveway when write commands are considered as way crossing, i.e.. write commands to these 2 (or more) slaveways are not treated as way crossing when one write command targets one slaveway and the next write command targets the second slaveway. Not treating write commands as way crossing allows the write commands to go to the slaveway ahead of the write data for potentially better overall system performance. When all bits are set (1), disables all way crossing checks. When all bits are cleared (0), way crossing is strict with each way crossing write command held until write data for all previous writes have been routed to their corresponding slaveways. |

Status registers indicate the state of several elements in the masterport, including the number of transactions outstanding/pending waiting for a response, emptiness, fullness of several buffers, etc. The state information is available only as a debug indication and could be delayed by a few clock cycles from when the state is reached to being reflected in the status registers. | Properties | Value |

Status registers indicate the state of several elements in the masterport, including the number of transactions outstanding/pending waiting for a response, emptiness, fullness of several buffers, etc. The state information is available only as a debug indication and could be delayed by a few clock
<!-- page 283 -->

cycles from when the state is reached to being reflected in the status registers. One or more of the state registers are read live and could capture intermediate values as they change.

| :--- | :--- | :--- |

| 7:0 | RD_PENDING_POST_BUF | Indicates the number of read transactions that are outstanding/pending waiting for a response from the slave. This transaction count is from after address channel buffers, which interfaces to core of the interconnect, i.e., arbiter and slaveway. |

Buffer status register indicate the state of all buffers in the masterport, whether they are empty or full on either side of the buffer. ## 2.18 BIMC_M_TCU1_PROF

BRIC Traffic Profiling

### 2.18.1 BIMC_M_TCU1_PROF_BRIC_PROFILING

BRIC Traffic Profiling

### 0x00421000 BIMC_M_TCU1_PROF_COMPONENT_INFO

| Properties | Value |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Type** | R |
| **Clock** | Config Clock |
| **Reset State** | 0x00000202 |

Component information registers provide discoverability information on the type of component and instance of each component. These registers are always the very first register in each component's configuration address space and allow for a software routine to walk the configuration address space in steps of 4KB to identify the location of each configuration register space and to which component each 4KB configures.

**BIMC_M_TCU1_PROF_COMPONENT_INFO**

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 23:16 | INSTANCE | Indicates the instance number of this traffic profiling. |
| 15:8 | SUB_TYPE | Identifies this configuration space as belonging to traffic profiling<br>0x2: PROFILING |
| 7:0 | TYPE | Identifies this configuration space as belonging to a component that interfaces to a bus master.<br>0x2: MASTERPORT |

### 0x00421020 BIMC_M_TCU1_PROF_CONFIGURATION_INFO_0

| Properties | Value |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Type** | R |
| **Clock** | Config Clock |
| **Reset State** | 0x00000000 |
<!-- page 287 -->

Configuration information registers provide information on the capability and configuration of each traffic profiling instance. See register field descriptions for more details.

**BIMC_M_TCU1_PROF_CONFIGURATION_INFO_0**

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:24 | TENURE_WIDTH | Indicates the width of tenures (latencies) measured in traffic profiling. |
| 23:16 | TRACKING_TABLE_DEPTH | Indicates the number of entries in the table that tracks outstanding commands for determining how many commands have larger turnaround latencies that a programmed threshold. |
| 7:0 | SCALING_FACTOR | Indicates how many extra scaling is performed on events generated by traffic profiling if such events have to be synchronized from the tenure clock to the event clock. Any value that is non-power-of-2 is converted to power-of-2 by hardware. When the value read from this register field is used in software, similar conversion of non-power-of-2 values to next higher power-of-2 value is necessary. |

### 0x00421030 BIMC_M_TCU1_PROF_CONFIGURATION_INFO_1

| Properties | Value |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Type** | R |
| **Clock** | Config Clock |
| **Reset State** | 0x00000000 |

Configuration information registers provide information on the capability and configuration of each traffic profiling instance. See register field descriptions for more details.

**BIMC_M_TCU1_PROF_CONFIGURATION_INFO_1**

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 23:16 | PIPE2_ACH_DEPTH | Indicates the depth of address channel buffer in pipe2 of masterport in which this traffic profiling instance is paired with. Applies only to traffic profiling instances in XR type masterports, which contains three distinct paths to slaves, in pipe0, pipe1, pipe2. In non-XR type masterports, value contained in field does not refer to any actual address channel buffer. |
| 15:8 | PIPE1_ACH_DEPTH | Indicates the depth of address channel buffer in pipe1 of masterport in which this traffic profiling instance is paired with. Applies only to traffic profiling instances in XR type masterports, which contains three distinct paths to slaves, in pipe0, pipe1, pipe2. In non-XR type masterports, value contained in field does not refer to any actual address channel buffer. |
| 7:0 | PIPE0_ACH_DEPTH | Indicates the depth of address channel buffer in pipe0 of masterport in which this traffic profiling instance is paired with. Applies only to traffic profiling instances in XR type masterports, which contains three distinct paths to slaves, in pipe0, pipe1, pipe2. In non-XR type masterports, pipe0 refers to the common address channel buffer used for all slave accesses. |
<!-- page 288 -->

### 0x00421200 BIMC_M_TCU1_PROF_CLOCK_CTRL

| Properties | Value |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Type** | RW |
| **Clock** | Config, Event & Tenure Clocks |
| **Reset State** | 0x00000003 |

**BIMC_M_TCU1_PROF_CLOCK_CTRL**

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1 | TENURE_CLOCK_GATING_EN | When set (1), enables activity based clock gating of all registers clocked by tenure clock. Activity based clock gating uses architectural clock gates to reduce dynamic power consumption by gating clocks during periods of in-activity. When cleared (0), disables all activity based clock gating by forcing all architectural clock gates to not gate clocks even during periods of in-activity. |
| 0 | EVENT_CLOCK_GATING_EN | When set (1), enables activity based clock gating of all registers clocked by event clock. Activity based clock gating uses architectural clock gates to reduce dynamic power consumption by gating clocks during periods of in-activity. When cleared (0), disables all activity based clock gating by forcing all architectural clock gates to not gate clocks even during periods of in-activity. |

### 0x00421210 BIMC_M_TCU1_PROF_MODE

| Properties | Value |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Type** | RW |
| **Clock** | Config, Event & Tenure Clocks |
| **Reset State** | 0x00000000 |
<!-- page 289 -->

**BIMC_M_TCU1_PROF_MODE**

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 25:24 | WR_TENURE_MODE | Configures the start and end events for monitoring write latencies/tenures. When configured to WR_CMD_TO_BRESP, starting event is first cycle of write command from bus master as seen by traffic profiling and ending event is first cycle of write response to bus master as seen by traffic profiling. When configured to WR_CMD_TO_BRESP_HANDSHAKE, starting event is first cycle of write command from bus master as seen by traffic profiling and ending event is transfer handshake of write response to bus master as seen by traffic profiling. When configured to WR_CMD_HANDSHAKE, starting event is first cycle of write command from bus master as seen by traffic profiling and ending event is transfer handshake of the same write command with bus master as seen by traffic profiling. When configured to WR_RESP_HANDSHAKE, starting event is first cycle of write response to bus master as seen by traffic profiling and ending event is transfer handshake of write response to bus master as seen by traffic profiling.<br>0x0: WR_CMD_TO_BRESP<br>0x1: WR_CMD_TO_BRESP_HANDSHAKE<br>0x2: WR_CMD_HANDSHAKE<br>0x3: WR_RESP_HANDSHAKE |
| 17:16 | RD_TENURE_MODE | Configures the start and end events for monitoring read latencies/tenures. When configured to RD_CMD_TO_FIRST_RDATA, starting event is first cycle of read command from bus master as seen by traffic profiling and ending event is first cycle of first beat of read data to bus master as seen by traffic profiling. When configured to RD_CMD_TO_LAST_RDATA, starting event is first cycle of read command from bus master as seen by traffic profiling and ending event is transfer handshake of last beat of read data to bus master as seen by traffic profiling. When configured to RD_CMD_HANDSHAKE, starting event is first cycle of read command from bus master as seen by traffic profiling and ending event is transfer handshake of the same read command with bus master as seen by traffic profiling. When configured to RD_DATA_HANDSHAKE, starting event is first cycle of first beat of read data to bus master as seen by traffic profiling and ending event is transfer handshake of last beat of read data to bus master as seen by traffic profiling.<br>0x0: RD_CMD_TO_FIRST_RDATA<br>0x1: RD_CMD_TO_LAST_RDATA<br>0x2: RD_CMD_HANDSHAKE<br>0x3: RD_DATA_HANDSHAKE |
| 0 | PROFILING_EN | When set (1), enables traffic profiling to monitor bus transactions from bus master and generate events for counting in performance monitors. When cleared (0), disables traffic profiling. |

### BIMC_M_TCU1_PROF_RD_STATUS_n

**Address**: `0x00421400 + 0x4 * n`, where `n = [0..0]`
**Type**: R
**Clock**: Config & Tenure Clocks
**Reset State**: `0x00000000`

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31 | RD_OUTSTANDING_OVERFLOW | Indicates that the number of outstanding reads crossed the maximum supported (255) during when traffic profiling was last enabled. It is recommended that this register be read only after traffic profiling has been disabled. |
| 30 | RD_OUTSTANDING_UNDERFLOW | Indicates that the number of outstanding reads went below 0 during when traffic profiling was last enabled. It indicates that more command completions were seen compared to commands starts. The most likely scenario is an overflow of number of outstanding reads occurred leading to some command starts not being tracked. It is recommended that this register be read only after traffic profiling has been disabled. |
| 7:0 | RD_OUTSTANDING_MAX | Indicates the maximum number of outstanding reads that were seen when traffic profiling was last enabled. Only reads that match the MID filter and slaveway select filter are accounted for. It is recommended that this register be read only after traffic profiling has been disabled. |

## 2.19 BIMC_S_APP_SWAY BRIC Slaveway

### 2.19.1 BIMC_S_APP_SWAY_BRIC_SLAVEWAY BRIC Slaveway

### BIMC_S_APP_SWAY_COMPONENT_INFO

**Address**: `0x00450000`
**Type**: R
**Clock**: Config Clock
**Reset State**: `0x00000103`

Component information registers provide discoverability information on the type of component and instance of each component. These registers are always the very first register in each component's configuration address space and allow for a software routine to walk the configuration address space in steps of 4KB to identify the location of each configuration register space and to which component each 4KB configures.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 23:16 | INSTANCE | Indicates the instance number of this slaveway. |
| 15:8 | SUB_TYPE | Identifies this configuration space as belonging to a slaveway<br>0x1: SLAVEWAY |
| 7:0 | TYPE | Identifies this configuration space as belonging to a component that interfaces to a bus slave.<br>0x3: SLAVEWAY |
<!-- page 303 -->

### BIMC_S_APP_SWAY_CONFIGURATION_INFO_0

**Address**: `0x00450020`
**Type**: R
**Clock**: Config Clock
**Reset State**: `0x01000001`

Configuration information registers provide information on the capability and configuration of each slaveway instance. See register field descriptions for more details.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:24 | SYNC_MODE | Indicates the clock relationship between the clock used in the core side and the clock used in the slave side of the slaveway. When ASYNC, identifies the master clock and core clock as un-related and asynchronous to each other. When SYNC, identifies the core clock and slave clock as synchronous to each other. When ISOSYNC, identifies the core clock and slave clock as related, but of different frequencies, which are of integer ratios, i.e., they are iso-synchronous to each other.<br>0x0: ASYNC<br>0x1: SYNC<br>0x2: ISOSYNC |
| 7:0 | FUNCTIONALITY | Indicates the functionality and type of bus traffic handled by this slaveway. When DEFAULT_SLAVE, identifies this slaveway as a default slave which responds to all commands with decode error. When SLAVEWAY, identifies this slaveway as interfacing to a bus slave. When STUB, identifies this slaveway has a stub.<br>0x0: STUB<br>0x1: SLAVEWAY |

**Address**: `0x00450030`
**Type**: R
**Clock**: Config Clock
**Reset State**: `0x00000000`

Configuration information registers provide information on the capability and configuration of each slaveway instance. See register field descriptions for more details.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:0 | MPORT_CONNECTIVITY | Indicates which masterports can route commands to this slaveway instance. 1-bit per masterport. When a specific bit is set (1), indicates that the masterport corresponding to this bit can route commands to this slaveway instance. When a specific bit is cleared (0), indicates that the masterport corresponding to this bit does not route commands to this slaveway instance. |

### BIMC_S_APP_SWAY_CLOCK_CTRL

**Address**: `0x00450200`
**Type**: RW
**Clock**: Config, Core & Slave Clocks
**Reset State**: `0x00000003`

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1 | SLAVE_CLOCK_GATING_EN | When set (1), enables activity based clock gating of all registers clocked by slave clock. Activity based clock gating uses architectural clock gates to reduce dynamic power consumption by gating clocks during periods of in-activity. When cleared (0), disables all activity based clock gating by forcing all architectural clock gates to not gate clocks even during periods of in-activity. |
<!-- page 309 -->

### BIMC_S_APP_SWAY_CLOCK_CTRL (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 0 | CORE_CLOCK_GATING_EN | When set (1), enables activity based clock gating of all registers clocked by core clock. Activity based clock gating uses architectural clock gates to reduce dynamic power consumption by gating clocks during periods of in-activity. When cleared (0), disables all activity based clock gating by forcing all architectural clock gates to not gate clocks even during periods of in-activity. |

| 0 | CORE_CLOCK_DEMETA_SEL | When cleared (0), selects DEMETA synchronizer that requires atleast 3 clock edges (two rising and one falling). When set (1), selects DEMETA synchronizer that requires atleast 2 clock edges (one falling and one rising) to synchronize to core clock in all buffers. |

### BIMC_S_APP_SWAY_GATHERING

**Address**: `0x00450230`
**Type**: RW
**Clock**: Config & Slave Clocks
**Reset State**: `0x00000000`

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 3:0 | RD_GATHER_BEATS | Configures the number of read data beats to gather/buffer in read channel buffer before allowing the read data to be routed to masterports. When configured with 0, read data is allowed to proceed as soon as the first beat has been buffered. When configured with 1, read data is allowed to proceed as soon as the second beat has been buffered. When configured with values larger than the number of beats in the read burst, the read data is allowed to proceed as soon as the last beat has been buffered. When configured with values larger than the depth of read channel buffers, the read data is held until all entries in the read channel buffer have been occupied. |

### BIMC_S_APP_SWAY_STATUS_0A

**Address**: `0x00450400`
**Type**: R
**Clock**: Config & Core Clocks
**Reset State**: `0x00000000`

Status registers indicate the state of several elements in the slaveway, including the number of transactions outstanding/pending waiting for a response, emptiness, fullness of several buffers, etc. The state information is available only as a debug indication and could be delayed by a few clock cycles from when the state is reached to being reflected in the status registers. One or more of the state registers are read live and could capture intermediate values as they change.


<!-- page 311 -->

| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 23:16 | WR_PENDING_PRE_BUF | Indicates the number of write transactions that are outstanding/pending waiting for a response from the slave. This transaction count is before address channel buffers, which interfaces to core of the interconnect. |
| 7:0 | RD_PENDING_PRE_BUF | Indicates the number of read transactions that are outstanding/pending waiting for a response from the slave. This transaction count is from PIPE0 of the masterport before address channel buffers, which interfaces to core of the interconnect. |

## 2.20 BIMC_S_SYS_SWAY
### BRIC Slaveway

### 2.20.1 BIMC_S_SYS_SWAY_BRIC_SLAVEWAY
#### BRIC Slaveway
<!-- page 317 -->

### BIMC_S_SYS_SWAY_COMPONENT_INFO
**Address:** `0x00458000`

**Type:** R
**Clock:** Config Clock
**Reset State:** `0x00000103`

Component information registers provide discoverability information on the type of component and instance of each component. These registers are always the very first register in each component's configuration address space and allow for a software routine to walk the configuration address space in steps of 4KB to identify the location of each configuration register space and to which component each 4KB configures.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 23:16 | INSTANCE | Indicates the instance number of this slaveway. |
| 15:8 | SUB_TYPE | Identifies this configuration space as belonging to a slaveway.<br>0x1: SLAVEWAY |
| 7:0 | TYPE | Identifies this configuration space as belonging to a component that interfaces to a bus slave.<br>0x3: SLAVEWAY |

### BIMC_S_SYS_SWAY_CONFIGURATION_INFO_0
**Address:** `0x00458020`

**Type:** R
**Clock:** Config Clock
**Reset State:** `0x01000001`

Configuration information registers provide information on the capability and configuration of each slaveway instance. See register field descriptions for more details.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:24 | SYNC_MODE | Indicates the clock relationship between the clock used in the core side and the clock used in the slave side of the slaveway. When ASYNC, identifies the master clock and core clock as un-related and asynchronous to each other. When SYNC, identifies the core clock and slave clock as synchronous to each other. When ISOSYNC, identifies the core clock and slave clock as related, but of different frequencies, which are of integer ratios, i.e., they are iso-synchronous to each other.<br>0x0: ASYNC<br>0x1: SYNC<br>0x2: ISOSYNC |
<!-- page 318 -->

### BIMC_S_SYS_SWAY_CONFIGURATION_INFO_0 (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 7:0 | FUNCTIONALITY | Indicates the functionality and type of bus traffic handled by this slaveway. When DEFAULT_SLAVE, identifies this slaveway as a default slave which responds to all commands with decode error. When SLAVEWAY, identifies this slaveway as interfacing to a bus slave. When STUB, identifies this slaveway has a stub.<br>0x0: STUB<br>0x1: SLAVEWAY |

When a specific bit is cleared (0), indicates that the masterport corresponding to this bit does not route commands to this slaveway instance. |

## BIMC_S_SYS_SWAY_CLOCK_CTRL

**Address:** 0x00458200
**Type:** RW
**Clock:** Config, Core & Slave Clocks
**Reset State:** 0x00000003

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1 | SLAVE_CLOCK_GATING_EN | When set (1), enables activity based clock gating of all registers clocked by slave clock. Activity based clock gating uses architectural clock gates to reduce dynamic power consumption by gating clocks during periods of in-activity. When cleared (0), disables all activity based clock gating by forcing all architectural clock gates to not gate clocks even during periods of in-activity. |
| 0 | CORE_CLOCK_GATING_EN | When set (1), enables activity based clock gating of all registers clocked by core clock. Activity based clock gating uses architectural clock gates to reduce dynamic power consumption by gating clocks during periods of in-activity. When cleared (0), disables all activity based clock gating by forcing all architectural clock gates to not gate clocks even during periods of in-activity. |

**Type:** RW
**Clock:** Config, Core & Slave Clocks

## BIMC_S_SYS_SWAY_CDC_CTRL

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1 | SLAVE_CLOCK_DEMETA_SEL | When cleared (0), selects DEMETA synchronizer that requires atleast 3 clock edges (two rising and one falling). When set (1), selects DEMETA synchronizer that requires atleast 2 clock edges (one falling and one rising) to synchronize to slave clock in all buffers. |
| 0 | CORE_CLOCK_DEMETA_SEL | When cleared (0), selects DEMETA synchronizer that requires atleast 3 clock edges (two rising and one falling). When set (1), selects DEMETA synchronizer that requires atleast 2 clock edges (one falling and one rising) to synchronize to core clock in all buffers. |

## BIMC_S_SYS_SWAY_GATHERING

**Address:** 0x00458230
**Type:** RW
**Clock:** Config & Slave Clocks
**Reset State:** 0x00000000
<!-- page 325 -->
## BIMC_S_SYS_SWAY_GATHERING

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 3:0 | RD_GATHER_BEATS | Configures the number of read data beats to gather/buffer in read channel buffer before allowing the read data to be routed to masterports. When configured with 0, read data is allowed to proceed as soon as the first beat has been buffered. When configured with 1, read data is allowed to proceed as soon as the second beat has been buffered. When configured with values larger than the number of beats in the read burst, the read data is allowed to proceed as soon as the last beat has been buffered. When configured with values larger than the depth of read channel buffers, the read data is held until all entries in the read channel buffer have been occupied. |

## BIMC_S_SYS_SWAY_STATUS_1A

**Address:** 0x00458410

Status registers indicate the state of several elements in the slaveway, including the number of transactions outstanding/pending waiting for a response, emptiness, fullness of several buffers, etc. The state information is available only as a debug indication and could be delayed by a few clock cycles from when the state is reached to being reflected in the status registers.
