## 2.21 BIMC_S_DEFAULT_SWAY
### BRIC Default Slave

### 2.21.1 BIMC_S_DEFAULT_SWAY_BRIC_SLAVEWAY_DEFAULT
BRIC Default Slave

### 0x00460000 BIMC_S_DEFAULT_SWAY_COMPONENT_INFO

- **Type:** R
- **Clock:** Config Clock
- **Reset State:** 0x00000103

Component information registers provide discoverability information on the type of component and instance of each component. These registers are always the very first register in each component's configuration address space and allow for a software routine to walk the configuration address space in steps of 4KB to identify the location of each configuration register space and to which component each 4KB configures.

#### BIMC_S_DEFAULT_SWAY_COMPONENT_INFO

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 23:16 | INSTANCE | Indicates the instance number of this slaveway. |
| 15:8 | SUB_TYPE | Identifies this configuration space as belonging to a slaveway<br>0x1: SLAVEWAY |
| 7:0 | TYPE | Identifies this configuration space as belonging to a component that interfaces to a bus slave.<br>0x3: SLAVEWAY |
<!-- page 332 -->

### 0x00460020 BIMC_S_DEFAULT_SWAY_CONFIGURATION_INFO_0

- **Type:** R
- **Clock:** Config Clock
- **Reset State:** 0x00000002

Configuration information registers provide information on the capability and configuration of each slaveway instance. See register field descriptions for more details.

#### BIMC_S_DEFAULT_SWAY_CONFIGURATION_INFO_0

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 7:0 | FUNCTIONALITY | Indicates the functionality and type of bus traffic handled by this slaveway. When DEFAULT_SLAVE, identifies this slaveway as a default slave which responds to all commands with decode error. When SLAVEWAY, identifies this slaveway as interfacing to a bus slave. When STUB, identifies this slaveway has a stub.<br>0x2: DEFAULT_SLAVE |

### 0x00460030 BIMC_S_DEFAULT_SWAY_CONFIGURATION_INFO_1

- **Type:** R
- **Clock:** Config Clock
- **Reset State:** 0x00000000

Configuration information registers provide information on the capability and configuration of each slaveway instance. See register field descriptions for more details.

#### BIMC_S_DEFAULT_SWAY_CONFIGURATION_INFO_1

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:0 | MPORT_CONNECTIVITY | Indicates which masterports can route commands to this slaveway instance. 1-bit per masterport. When a specific bit is set (1), indicates that the masterport corresponding to this bit can route commands to this slaveway instance. When a specific bit is cleared (0), indicates that the masterport corresponding to this bit does not route commands to this slaveway instance. |

### 0x00460100 BIMC_S_DEFAULT_SWAY_INTERRUPT_STATUS

- **Type:** R
- **Clock:** Config Clock
- **Reset State:** 0x00000000

Interrupt status registers provide indication of which interrupts from this masterport require servicing.
<!-- page 333 -->

### BIMC_S_DEFAULT_SWAY_INTERRUPT_STATUS (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1 | RFU | Reserved for future use |
| 0 | DECODE_ERROR | When set (1), indicates that a read or write command was responded with decode error. |

### 0x00460108 BIMC_S_DEFAULT_SWAY_INTERRUPT_CLEAR

- **Type:** W
- **Clock:** Config Clock
- **Reset State:** 0x00000000

Interrupt clear registers provide the mechanism to turn off interrupt sources once they have been acknowledged or serviced. A write of '1' to the bits corresponding to the interrupts indicated in interrupt status is required to turn off interrupts.

#### BIMC_S_DEFAULT_SWAY_INTERRUPT_CLEAR

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1 | RFU | Reserved for future use |
| 0 | DECODE_ERROR | When written with '1', clears the decode error interrupt status if it is also set. If decode error interrupt status is not set, the write is ignored. All writes of '0' are ignored. |

### 0x0046010C BIMC_S_DEFAULT_SWAY_INTERRUPT_ENABLE

- **Type:** RW
- **Clock:** Config Clock
- **Reset State:** 0x00000000

Interrupt enable registers provide control over which interrupts are allowed to be propagated to an interrupt controller for servicing.

#### BIMC_S_DEFAULT_SWAY_INTERRUPT_ENABLE

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1 | RFU | Reserved for future use |
| 0 | DECODE_ERROR | When set (1), indicates that any decode errors interrupts are allowed to be propagated to a system wide interrupt controller. When cleared (0), any decode error interrupt is not propagated to the system wide interrupt controller. |
<!-- page 334 -->

### 0x00460400 BIMC_S_DEFAULT_SWAY_DEFAULT_SLAVE_STATUS_0

- **Type:** R
- **Clock:** Config & Core Clocks
- **Reset State:** 0x00000000

Default slave status registers recorded the last read or write command that was responded to with decode error.

#### BIMC_S_DEFAULT_SWAY_DEFAULT_SLAVE_STATUS_0

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:0 | ADDR_LOWER | Indicates ADDR[31:0] of the last read or write command that was responded to with decode error. |

### 0x00460410 BIMC_S_DEFAULT_SWAY_DEFAULT_SLAVE_STATUS_1

- **Type:** R
- **Clock:** Config & Core Clocks
- **Reset State:** 0x00000000

Default slave status registers recorded the last read or write command that was responded to with decode error.

#### BIMC_S_DEFAULT_SWAY_DEFAULT_SLAVE_STATUS_1

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31 | WRITE | When set (1), indicates that the last command responded to with decode error was a write. When cleared (0), indicates that the last command responded to with decode error was a read. |
| 3:0 | ADDR_UPPER | Indicates ADDR[35:32] of the last read or write command that was responded to with decode error. |

### 0x00460420 BIMC_S_DEFAULT_SWAY_DEFAULT_SLAVE_STATUS_2

- **Type:** R
- **Clock:** Config & Core Clocks
- **Reset State:** 0x00000000

Default slave status registers recorded the last read or write command that was responded to with decode error.
<!-- page 335 -->

### BIMC_S_DEFAULT_SWAY_DEFAULT_SLAVE_STATUS_2 (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:16 | TID | Indicates the transfer ID of the last command that was responded to with decode error. |
| 15:0 | MID | Indicates the master ID of the last command that was responded to with decode error. |

- **Type:** R
- **Clock:** Config Clock
- **Reset State:** 0x00000000

#### BIMC_S_APP_ARB_CONFIGURATION_INFO_0

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31 | ARB2SW_PIPELINE_EN | When set (1), indicates that a pipeline stage is present between the arbiter and the slaveway. |

The depth provides an indication on the range of values of WR_GRANTS_AHEAD register field that will have an effect on the performance of the arbiter. |
| 7:0 | FUNCTIONALITY | Indicates that this arbiter instance is capable of using plain or fair round-robin for arbitration of commands.<br>0x0: ROUND_ROBIN<br>0x1: FAIR_ROUND_ROBIN<br>0x2: PRIORITY_RR<br>0x3: PRIORITY_FRR<br>0x4: TIERED_RR |

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |

When a specific bit is set (1), indicates that the masterport corresponding to this bit can route commands to this arbiter instance. When a specific bit is cleared (0), indicates that the masterport corresponding to this bit does not route commands to this arbiter instance. |
<!-- page 337 -->

### 0x00451200 BIMC_S_APP_ARB_CLOCK_CTRL

- **Type:** RW
- **Clock:** Config & Core Clocks
- **Reset State:** 0x00000001

#### BIMC_S_APP_ARB_CLOCK_CTRL

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 0 | CORE_CLOCK_GATING_EN | When set (1), enables activity based clock gating of all registers in this arbiter instance. Activity based clock gating uses architectural clock gates to reduce dynamic power consumption by gating clocks during periods of in-activity. When cleared (0), disables all activity based clock gating by forcing all architectural clock gates to not gate clocks even during periods of in-activity. |

### 0x00451210 BIMC_S_APP_ARB_MODE

- **Type:** RW
- **Clock:** Config & Core Clocks
- **Reset State:** 0x00000000

#### BIMC_S_APP_ARB_MODE

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:28 | WR_GRANTS_AHEAD | Number of write commands that can be granted ahead of the corresponding write data bursts. For each write command granted ahead of the corresponding write data, the source route is stored in 'Write Grants Buffer' for routing write data bursts. Range of values is supported is dependent on the depth of 'Write Grants Buffers', as indicated in WGB_DEPTH in CONFIGURATION_INFO registers. Any setting larger than WGB_DEPTH is treated similar to a setting equal to WGB_DEPTH. |

### 0x00461000 BIMC_S_DEFAULT_ARB_COMPONENT_INFO

**Type:** R  
**Clock:** Config Clock  
**Reset State:** 0x00000203  

Component information registers provide discoverability information on the type of component and instance of each component. These registers are always the very first register in each component's configuration address space and allow for a software routine to walk the configuration address space in steps of 4KB to identify the location of each configuration register space and to which component each 4KB configures.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 23:16 | INSTANCE | Indicates the instance number of this arbiter. |
| 15:8 | SUB_TYPE | Identifies this configuration space as belonging to an arbiter.<br/>0x2: ARBITER |
| 7:0 | TYPE | Identifies this configuration space as belonging to a component that interfaces to a bus slave.<br/>0x3: SLAVEWAY |

## Bus Integrated Memory Controller

### BIMC_S_DDR0_SCMO_ADDR_BASE_CSn

**Address:** `0x00448410 + 0x4*n, n=[0..1]`
**Type:** `RW`
**Clock:** `Config Clock`
**Reset State:** `0x00000000`

Base Address Register for Rank n

This register defines the base address for the memory that associates to chip select n.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 15:10 | RFU_15_10 | Reserved for future use |
| 9:2 | ADDR_BASE | Defines the Base Address decode, in conjunction with the ADDR_MAP_CSn, n = [0,1], to determine the address space of the targeted chip select.<br>The Base Address is compared to the upper AXI address. If the portions of the two addresses match, then the particular CS is accessed. |
| 1:0 | RFU_1_0 | Reserved for future use |

### BIMC_S_DDR0_SCMO_ADDR_MAP_CSn

**Address:** `0x00448420 + 0x4*n, n=[0..1]`
**Type:** `RW`
**Clock:** `Config Clock`
**Reset State:** `0x00000000`

Address Mapping Register for Rank n.

This register defines the way to map AXI system address into rank/bank/row/column address to memory devices.

Once the number of bank, row size and column size are defined, the memory size of the associated rank is defined.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 15 | RANK_EN | Rank has memory devices attached<br>0x0: RANK_NOT_PRESENT<br>0x1: RANK_IS_PRESENT |
| 14:13 | RFU_14_13 | Reserved for future use |
<!-- page 353 -->
## Bus Integrated Memory Controller

### BIMC_S_DDR0_SCMO_ADDR_MAP_CSn (continued)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 12 | ADDR_MODE | Addressing Mode Configuration.<br>Selects the Addressing Mode of the Rank and determines the mapping of the System Address to the Memory Address.<br>Linear addressing mode is configuring as 'Rank,Bank,Row,Column'.<br>Bank interleaved addressing mode is configuring as 'Rank,Row,Bank,Column' mode.<br>RK = Rank, R = Row, B = Bank, C=Column.<br>For high tier products linear addressing mode of RKBRC is not supported<br>0x0: RKRBC<br>0x1: RKBRC |
| 11:9 | RFU_11_9 | Reserved for future use |
| 8 | BANK_SIZE | Specifies the number of banks in the memory device.<br>NOTE: For high tier products only 8 banks are supported.<br>0x0: BANKS_4<br>0x1: BANKS_8 |
| 7:6 | RFU_7_6 | Reserved for future use |
| 5:4 | ROW_SIZE | Specifies the number of bits used for the row address of the external memory<br>0x0: ROWS_13<br>0x1: ROWS_14<br>0x2: ROWS_15<br>0x3: ROWS_16 |
| 3:2 | RFU_3_2 | Reserved for future use |
| 1:0 | COL_SIZE | Specifies the number of bits used for the column address of the external memory<br>0x0: COLS_8<br>0x1: COLS_9<br>0x2: COLS_10<br>0x3: COLS_11 |

## 2.27 BIMC_S_DDR0_DPE_ABHN_DPE

### 0x0044C010 BIMC_S_DDR0_DPE_CONFIG_0

* **Type**: RW
* **Clock**: ACLK
* **Reset State**: 0x00000000

DDR Memory Configuration Register 0.
This register is used to setup the DRAM configuration in the DDR controller.
<!-- page 369 -->

### BIMC_S_DDR0_DPE_CONFIG_0 (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 29:28 | CA_BUS_OE_CTRL | When enabled, the design can indicate to the PHY to tri-state the command address bus. This is required as a shunt resistance is typically used in the command address path for PCDDR3 memory boards and hence will always burn power if the command address bus is always driven. The two scenarios wherein the bus can be tri-stated are (1) when all ranks are in self refresh and the memory clocks are off or (2) when all ranks are in powerdown.<br>0x0: DISABLED (dpe_phy_pad_oe_ca is always driven to 1'b1. The CA bus is always in output mode.)<br>0x1: SR_ONLY (dpe_phy_pad_oe_ca is only driven to 1'b0 when both ranks are in self refresh and the clock to the memory device has been turned off.)<br>0x2: SR_OR_PWR_DN (dpe_phy_pad_oe_ca is driven to 1'b0 when both ranks are in self refresh and the clock to the memory device has been turned off or when both ranks are in powerdown)<br>0x3: RESERVED |
| 24 | RD_BEAT_NDX_OOO | Setting this bit will enable the DPE to return read data beats to the front end out of order. dpe_cmd_rd_reseq will indicate that a transaction will have beats out of order, and the change in order will be reflected on the dpe_rdata_ndx port.<br>This can be enabled for LPDDR2/3. This CSR has no effect on PCDDR3, as the read beat index will return out of order based on the column address by default for that memory type.<br>0x0: IN_ORDER (beats for a read are always returned in incrementing order) (Example: 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7)<br>0x1: OOO (beats for a read can be returned in non-incrementing order) (Example: 0, 1, 6, 7, 2, 3, 4, 5) |
| 20 | DDR_WR_MASK_POLARITY | This bit is used to set the polarity for the write byte mask. LPDDR2/3 and PCDDR3 should use the default value '0'.<br>0x0: ACTIVE_HIGH (a high level will mask the corresponding byte from being written - default for LPDDR2)<br>0x1: ACTIVE_LOW (a low level will mask the corresponding byte from being written) |
| 17:16 | DEVICE_TYPE | Type of memory device<br>0x0: LPDDR2<br>0x1: PCDDR3<br>0x2: LPDDR3<br>0x3: PCDDR4 |
<!-- page 370 -->

### BIMC_S_DDR0_DPE_CONFIG_0 (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 11:10 | DEVICE_CFG_RANK1 | Device Configuration for Rank 1. This is required for SRR in order to update the refresh rate correctly if multiple devices are involved. If all x8 individual memory devices are used, then select '00'. If all x16 individual memory devices are used, then select '01'. If all x32 individual memory devices are used, then select '10'. If all x64 individual memory devices are used, then select '11'.<br>0x0: X8_X8_X8_X8<br>0x1: X16_X16<br>0x2: X32<br>0x3: X64 |
| 9:8 | DEVICE_CFG_RANK0 | Device Configuration for Rank 0. This is required for SRR in order to update the refresh rate correctly if multiple devices are involved. If all x8 individual memory devices are used, then select '00'. If all x16 individual memory devices are used, then select '01'. If all x32 individual memory devices are used, then select '10'. If all x64 individual memory devices are used, then select '11'.<br>0x0: X8_X8_X8_X8<br>0x1: X16_X16<br>0x2: X32<br>0x3: X64 |
| 4 | SHARED_CLK | Rank Clock Configuration.<br>0x0: UNSHARED_CLK<br>0x1: SHARED_CLK (Rank 0 and Rank 1 have the same clock) |
| 0 | DDR_CMD | Specify if Device command bus is Double Data Rate (in addition to the data bus). This needs to be enabled (1) for LPDDR2/3 SDRAM devices and disabled for PCDDR3 SDRAM devices.<br>0x0: SDR_ON_CMD<br>0x1: DDR_ON_CMD |

### 0x0044C014 BIMC_S_DDR0_DPE_CONFIG_1

* **Type**: RW
* **Clock**: ACLK
* **Reset State**: 0x00000000

DDR Memory Configuration Register 1.
This register is used to setup the DRAM configuration in the DDR controller.


<!-- page 371 -->

### BIMC_S_DDR0_DPE_CONFIG_1 (continued)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:24 | PERIOD_BUS_THRESHOLD_POWER_MODE | Indicates the core clock frequency (in 100ps granularity) threshold for the controller to enable low power mode to the PHY. If the current core clock frequency is less than this threshold, then low power mode is enabled for the PHY and the corresponding pads. This value will be considered valid if CONFIG_1[PAD_POWER_MODE] is enabled and CONFIG_1[PAD_POWER_MODE_CTRL] is set to 0. |
| 20 | PAD_POWER_MODE_CTRL | Indicates if HW automatically controls the pad power mode to the PHY based on the current frequency of operation. If set to 1, then SW needs to program the values in DRAM_TIMING_16[PAD_MODE] depending on the current frequency of operation. SW would also be required to setup the new value before a frequency switch event. If set to 0, then HW automatically changes the power mode based on CONFIG_1[PERIOD_BUS_THRESHOLD_POWER_MODE] and the current frequency of operation and also would handle changes in the power mode based on frequency switch events. The value of this CSR is only valid if CONFIG_1[PAD_POWER_MODE] is enabled. If operating in cycle-based mode, the only allowed value is '1'.<br>0x0: HW_CTRL (default)<br>0x1: SW_CTRL |
| 16 | PAD_POWER_MODE | A value of '0' is required for chips which use Gen2 PHY whereas a value of '1' is recommended for chips which use Gen1 PHY.<br>0x0: DISABLED (default, Drive to high power mode)<br>0x1: ENABLED (Power mode is controlled by the memory controller) |
| 12:8 | NUM_BANKS_RANK1 | Number of banks for Rank 1 |
| 4:0 | NUM_BANKS_RANK0 | Number of banks for Rank 0 |

### 0x0044C018 BIMC_S_DDR0_DPE_CONFIG_2

* **Type**: RW
* **Clock**: ACLK
* **Reset State**: 0x00000000

DDR Memory Configuration Register 2.

This register is used to setup the DRAM configuration in the DDR controller.
<!-- page 372 -->

### BIMC_S_DDR0_DPE_CONFIG_2 (continued)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 29:28 | TIMING_MODE | Command Interface timing relative to the chip select. This is necessary to provide an option to guarantee an additional cycle for the command interface signals to propagate to the DRAM device and settle (to meet input setup requirements) before being clocked in. This must be set to 00 for LPDDR2/3 (TM_1T). 1T, 2T and 3T is supported for PCDDR3.<br>0x0: TM_1T (Default: Address and command can be driven in the same cycle as the chip select)<br>0x1: TM_2T (Address and command must be driven at least 1 cycle before chip select is asserted)<br>0x2: TM_3T<br>0x3: RESERVED |
| 24:20 | DDR_BURST_LEN | Specifies the Memory Burst Length. For LPDDR2, only 4 and 8 are valid. LPDDR3 only supports burst length of 8. PCDDR3 supports burst length of 8 only. BL of 16 is not supported.<br>0x4: BL_OF_4<br>0x8: BL_OF_8<br>0x10: BL_OF_16 |
| 16 | WR_DQS_EARLY | Indicates if the DQS needs to toggle one cycle before the write data is driven. This needs to be set based on the specific SDRAM device present. This is to be enabled for LPDDR3 and PCDDR3 devices, and disabled for LPDDR2 devices.<br>0x0: DISABLED (default)<br>0x1: ENABLED |
| 12 | DDR_CK_ON_DBG | Debug mode in which the clock to the memory device will continuously run regardless of the state of the memory (CSPD, Self Refresh).<br>0x0: DISABLED (default)<br>0x1: ENALBLED (Enable Debug Mode) |
| 11:8 | MRR_BURST_LEN | The Memory burst length of a Mode Register Read. This is used for LPDDR2/3 memory only. For LPDDR2, this is 4 beats, while for LPDDR3 this is 8 beats.<br>0x4: BL4<br>0x8: BL8 |
| 5:4 | BURST_RD_START | Specifies the starting column address restrictions for a read operation. This field needs to be set depending on the specific SDRAM device. For LPDDR2/3 use '00'. For PCDDR3, use '01'. This is currently not supported.<br>0x0: ADDRS_0_2_4 (default- addresses of 0,2,4,6 etc)<br>0x1: ADDRS_0_4_8 (addresses of 0,4, etc)<br>0x2: ADDRS_0_ONLY (addresses of 0 only)<br>11: (invalid) |
<!-- page 373 -->

### BIMC_S_DDR0_DPE_CONFIG_2 (continued)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1:0 | BURST_WR_START | Specifies the starting column address restrictions for a write operation. This field needs to be set depending on the specific SDRAM device. For LPDDR2/3 use '00'. For PCDDR3, use '01'. This is currently not supported.<br>0x0: ADDRS_0_2_4 (default- addresses of 0,2,4,6 etc)<br>0x1: ADDRS_0_4_8 (addresses of 0,4, etc)<br>0x2: ADDRS_0_ONLY (addresses of 0 only)<br>11: (invalid) |

### 0x0044C01C BIMC_S_DDR0_DPE_CONFIG_3

* **Type**: RW
* **Clock**: ACLK

DDR Memory Configuration Register 3.

This register is used to setup the DRAM configuration in the DDR controller.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 28 | DIST_LOAD_CTRL | This will enable duplication of cs_n, cke and odt signals in order to ease timing for multi-t by distributing the load of these signals. This is for single rank systems only. | 26:24 | REF_DEFICIT_WTRMRK | Number of refreshes to postpone. This field allows the design to postpone up to 7 refreshes to increase performance. When set to 0, all refreshes are 'urgent' and will be issued immediately. When set to a non-zero value, the controller will postpone this number of refreshes in the presence of RD/WR traffic. Once the controller has postponed REF_DEFICIT_WTRMRK refreshes, each additional outstanding refresh will be treated as 'urgent' and will be issued to the memory device immediately. Typically, for LPDDR, write 3'b001 for up to 8 all-bank refreshes to be permitted in the tREFBW rolling window. For non-LPDDR devices, this field should be disabled by writing all zeros. ### 0x0044C020 BIMC_S_DDR0_DPE_CONFIG_4

* **Type**: W
* **Clock**: ACLK
* **Reset State**: 0x00000000

DDR Memory Configuration Register 4.

This register is used to setup the DRAM configuration in the DDR controller.
<!-- page 376 -->

### BIMC_S_DDR0_DPE_CONFIG_4 (continued)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 4 | RECALC_PS_PARAMS | Writing a 1 to this bit will cause all parameters which are programmed in 100ps units as specified by their corresponding \*_IN_PS bit in CONFIG_5/6 to be recalculated by HW. They will not be loaded into the active registers by writing this bit. After writing this bit, the CYC_CALC_VALID bit in MEMC_STATUS_1 should be polled before writing a '1' to LOAD_ALL_CONFIG. Therefore, RECALC should not be written to this bit in the same write as '1' ('LOAD') is written to LOAD_ALL_CONFIG.<br>0x0: NOP<br>0x1: RECALC (1 will kick off calculation of fields specified in picoseconds) |
| 0 | LOAD_ALL_CONFIG | Setting this will load the DDR configuration registers for use by the controller. DPE maintains 2 sets of configuration registers: one read/write which can be set by software based on frequency requirements or for other reasons. These can be written at anytime and have no affect on current operation. Another shadow set of registers exists which is actively used by the DPE. Software must load the read/write set, then set this bit to propagate the new settings to the controller. After writing this bit, the SHADOW_REGS_STALE bit in MEMC_STATUS_2 will go to 'UP_TO_DATE' until another write is performed to the control registers. See MEMC_STATUS_2 for more details.<br>0x0: NOP (No change in active shadow register set) (default)<br>0x1: LOAD (1 will load the read only active shadow register set with the values in the R/W set) |

### 0x0044C024 BIMC_S_DDR0_DPE_CONFIG_5

* **Type**: RW
* **Clock**: ACLK
* **Reset State**: 0x00000000

DDR Memory Configuration Register 5.

If the timing parameter value is only specified in clock cycles as per the JEDEC specification, then it is recommended to set that specific timing parameter in cycle based mode in the CSR below.

If the timing parameter value is only specified in ns as per the JEDEC specification, then it is recommended to set that specific timing parameter in time based mode in the CSR below.

If the timing parameter value is specified such that it has a minimum cycle time requirement as well as a timing parameter value in ns as per the JEDEC specification, then it is recommended to set that specific timing parameter in time based mode in the CSR below.

Each bit in this register indicates if the value stored in the DRAM_TIMING register is in 100ps intervals, or in DDR clock cycles.

## BIMC_S_DDR0_DPE_MEMC_STATUS_1 (0x0044C0A0)

* **Type**: R
* **Clock**: ACLK
* **Reset State**: `0x00000000`

**DPE Status Register 1.**

This register contains information on the state of the memory controller. When the timing parameters in DRAM_TIMING registers are stored in multiples of 100ps, time is required for the calculation of DDR clock cycles. This register is the status of that calculation. The calculation is kicked off by either a req/ack interface in the DPE I/Os or writing RECALC ('1') to CONFIG_4[RECALC_PS_PARAMS]. The status bit will go to NO ('1') when the calculation has been kicked off and will go to YES ('0') when all cycle calculations for all DRAM_TIMING registers are complete.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 0 | CYC_CALC_VALID | 0x0: YES (The DPE logic is NOT currently calculating DRAM_TIMING values from 100ps intervals into DDR clock cycles)<br>0x1: NO (The DPE logic is currently calculating DRAM_TIMING values from 100ps intervals into DDR clock cycles) |

## BIMC_S_DDR0_DPE_MEMC_STATUS_2 (0x0044C0A4)

* **Type**: R
* **Clock**: ACLK
* **Reset State**: `0x00000000`

**DPE Status Register 2.**

This register contains information on the state of the memory controller. This register indicates if the active shadow set of registers matches the set of Read/Write registers. Any time the Read/Write registers are written, this bit will go to '0' (STALE) to indicate the active shadow registers are stale with respect to the Read/Write registers. The bit will go back to '1' (UP_TO_DATE) once a '1' is written to the LOAD_ALL_CONFIG register in CONFIG_4 or the new values are loaded into the active shadow set due to a frequency switch. It will remain '1' (UP_TO_DATE) until the next time a Read/Write register is written by software.
<!-- page 397 -->
### BIMC_S_DDR0_DPE_MEMC_STATUS_2 (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 0 | SHADOW_REGS_STALE | 0x0: STALE (Active shadow registers are stale)<br>0x1: UP_TO_DATE (Active shadow registers match Read/Write registers) |

* **Type**: RW
* **Clock**: ACLK

**DPE Interrupt Enable Register.**

This register controls the conditions for the interrupt bit to assert. These registers are used for LPDDR2/3 only, and should be set to DISABLED for PCDDR3 devices.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 6:4 | LOW_TEMP_THRESHOLD | The external interrupt will be generated based on the following refresh rate requirements based on low temperature:<br>0x0: DISABLED (default, interrupt for low temp disabled)<br>0x1: TREFI_2X_OR_4X (Interrupt is enabled if temp reaches 2X tREFI, 4X tREFI or LOW_LIMIT level)<br>0x2: TREFI_4X (Interrupt is enabled if temp reaches 4X tREFI or LOW_LIMIT level)<br>0x3: TREFI_2X (Interrupt is enabled if temp reaches 2X tREFI level)<br>0x4: TREFI_1X (Interrupt is enabled if temp reaches 1X tREFI level)<br>0x5: TREFI_0_5X (LPDDR3 only, Interrupt is enabled if temp reaches 0.5X tREFI level, 1X tREFI level, 2X tREFI level, 4X tREFI level, or LOW_LIMIT) |
<!-- page 398 -->
### BIMC_S_DDR0_DPE_INTERRUPT_ENABLE (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 2:0 | HIGH_TEMP_THRESHOLD | The external interrupt will be generated based on the following refresh rate requirements based on high temperature:<br>0x0: DISABLED (default, interrupt for high temp disabled)<br>0x1: TREFI_0_25X_DERATE (Interrupt is enabled if temp reaches 0.25X tREFI, DERATE, or HIGH_LIMIT level)<br>0x2: DERATE (Interrupt is enabled if temp reaches derate or HIGH_LIMIT level)<br>0x3: TREFI_0_25X (Interrupt is enabled if temp reaches 0.25X tREFI level)<br>0x4: TREFI_1X (Interrupt is enabled if temp reaches 1X tREFI level)<br>0x5: TREFI_0_5X (LPDDR3 only, Interrupt is enabled if temp reaches 0.5X tREFI level, 0.25X tREFI level, DERATE level or HIGH_LIMIT level) |

## BIMC_S_DDR0_DPE_INTERRUPT_STATUS (0x0044C0B8)

* **Type**: R
* **Clock**: ACLK
* **Reset State**: `0x00000000`

**DPE Interrupt Status Register.**

Interrupts are enabled in the INTERRUPT_ENABLE register. This register is read to determine which enabled, interrupt events have occurred and are causing an interrupt assertion. Interrupt will remain asserted until cleared via the INTERRUPT_CLR register. These registers are used for LPDDR2/3 only, and are required to remain at '0' (default value) for PCDDR3 devices.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |

## BIMC_S_DDR0_DPE_INTERRUPT_CLR (0x0044C0BC)

* **Type**: W
* **Clock**: ACLK
* **Reset State**: `0x00000000`

**DPE Interrupt Clear Register.**

This register allows control for SW to clear the interrupt. HW will set the interrupt based on the scenarios enabled in INTERRUPT_ENABLE register. Additional information about the interrupt is available via INTERRUPT_STATUS CSRs. The interrupt I/O will remain set (asserted) until SW writes a '1' to the corresponding field in this register. These registers are used for LPDDR2/3 only, and should not be used for PCDDR3 devices.
<!-- page 400 -->
### BIMC_S_DDR0_DPE_INTERRUPT_CLR (cont.)

| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 3 | RANK1_LOW_TEMP | 0x0: NOP<br>0x1: CLR_INT |
| 2 | RANK1_HIGH_TEMP | 0x0: NOP<br>0x1: CLR_INT |
| 1 | RANK0_LOW_TEMP | 0x0: NOP<br>0x1: CLR_INT |
| 0 | RANK0_HIGH_TEMP | 0x0: NOP<br>0x1: CLR_INT |

## BIMC_S_DDR0_DPE_INTERRUPT_SET (0x0044C0C0)

* **Type**: W
* **Clock**: ACLK
* **Reset State**: `0x00000000`

**DPE Interrupt Set Register.**

This register gives SW the capability to force the interrupt to be driven. Writing a '1' to a field in this register will force the interrupt to be driven until cleared by writing the corresponding field in INTERRUPT_CTRL CSR. These registers are used for LPDDR2/3 only, and should be used for PCDDR3 devices.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 3 | RANK1_LOW_TEMP | 0x0: NOP<br>0x1: SET_INT |
| 2 | RANK1_HIGH_TEMP | 0x0: NOP<br>0x1: SET_INT |
| 1 | RANK0_LOW_TEMP | 0x0: NOP<br>0x1: SET_INT |
| 0 | RANK0_HIGH_TEMP | 0x0: NOP<br>0x1: SET_INT |

### BIMC_S_DDR0_DPE_TIMER_1

**Address:** `0x0044C0E8`
**Type:** `RW`
**Clock:** `ACLK`
**Reset State:** `0x00000000`

DPE Clock cycle timer register 1.
This register contains timer values used for frequency independent timing parameters. These are to be programmed in DDR clock cycles.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 13:12 | DERATE_OFFSET | Temperature Derating value for DDR memory timing parameters. TRCD, TRAS, TRP and TRRD will be derated to add DERATE_OFFSET extra clock cycles to the normal value. Not used for PCDDR, must program to 0x0. For LPDDR2/3 this must be programmed based on upcoming frequency prior to frequency switch:<br>set to 0x2 for frequencies > 50 MHz<br>set to 0x0 for frequencies <= 50 MHz<br>(Below 50MHz, the min cycle fields will guarantee the derate requirements are met.) |
| 8 | TDQSS | DDR Timing parameter tDQSS. This is for LPDDR2/3 only.<br>0x0: ZERO (ZERO (0 cycles, default, PCDDR3))<br>0x1: ONE (ONE (1 cycle, LPDDR2/3)) |
| 7:0 | IDLE_PWR_DN_CNT | Minimum number of cycles a Rank must be idle before going into Power Down. If this is set to '0', the device will not wait any idle cycles before going into power down. Setting this to a value greater than zero will put the memory device into power down once a count down from the programmed value expires. (0x0 = 0 cycles, 0x1 = 1 cycle etc) |

### BIMC_S_DDR0_DPE_TIMER_2

**Address:** `0x0044C0EC`
**Type:** `RW`
**Clock:** `ACLK`
**Reset State:** `0x00000000`

DPE Clock cycle timer register 2.
This register contains timer values used for frequency independent timing parameters. It is to be programmed in DDR clock cycles.
<!-- page 404 -->

### BIMC_S_DDR0_DPE_TIMER_2 (Continued)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 16:8 | TRASMAX_XO_DIV_6_CYCLES | This field is used to define the amount of time to allow for tRASMAX for LPDDR2 and LPDDR3. tRASMAX is the maximum row active time. Generally, tRASMAX is specified as 70 usec for both LPDDR2 and LPDDR3 but refer to the device datasheet for actual requirement. The setting for this value will not vary with the frequency of the DPE core clock as the implementation actually uses the XO clock divided by 6.<br>Set to 0x0 to disable tRASMAX. tRASMAX is enforced automatically via refreshes for PCDDR3 so this should be set to 0x0 for PCDDR3.<br>The value programmed for TRASMAX_XO_DIV_6_CYLES is TRASMAX_XO_DIV_6_CYLES = ROUND_DOWN(tRASMAX / (Txo*6)) -6; where Txo = the period of the tcxo clock. tRASMAX = tRAS(max) value specified in uSec in the specification or data sheet.<br>e.g., tRASMAX = 70 uSec, tcxo=19.2 MHz gives RD(70us / 312.5 ns) - 6 = 218 decimal |
| 7:4 | TMRW | Mode register write command period. For LPDDR2 devices, this should be set to tMRW. For LPDDR3 devices, this must be set to 'h15. For PCDDR3, this should be set to tMRD. |
| 2:0 | TMRR | DDR timing parameter tMRR. Mode register read command Period. This is for LPDDR2/3 only. |

### BIMC_S_DDR0_DPE_DRAM_TIMING_0

**Address:** `0x0044C144`
**Type:** `RW`
**Clock:** `ACLK`
**Reset State:** `0x00000000`

This register contains the parameters which are specified by the memory vendor in ns. These values are not used by the design, until they are loaded into the active register DRAM_TIMING_0_ACT by setting CONFIG_4[LOAD_ALL_CONFIG] to '1' or when CONFIG_3[LOAD_TIMING_ON_FREQ_CHNG] is set to '1' and a frequency change occurs.

The value of the parameter contained in the registers can be in DDR clock cycles or in multiples of 100ps, and may vary from one SDRAM vendor to another.

> [!NOTE]
> The following applies to all DRAM_TIMING_* CSRs
>
> If the timing parameter value is only specified in clock cycles as per the JEDEC specification, then it is recommended to set that specific timing parameter in cycle based mode in CONIFG_5 CSR and program the timing parameter field as the cycle value, while the MIN_CYC value for that parameter would be 0 (SW could also program the MIN_CYC value if the parameter has one specified in the JEDEC specification).
>
> If the timing parameter value is only specified in ns as per the JEDEC specification, then it is recommended to set that specific timing parameter in time based mode in CONIFG_5 CSR and to program the timing parameter field in multiples of 100ps and leave the MIN_CYC field (for that timing parameter) as 0.
>
> If the timing parameter value is specified such that it has a minimum cycle time requirement as well as a timing parameter value in ns as per the JEDEC specification, then it is recommended to set that specific timing parameter in time based mode in CONIFG_5 CSR and to program the timing parameter field in multiples of 100ps and program the MIN_CYC field to reflect the minimum cycle time requirement for that timing parameter.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 15:12 | TRASMIN_MIN_CYC | Minimum TRASMIN value in DDR clock cycles. |
| 9:0 | TRASMIN | DDR timing parameter tRASmin. |

### Fields

| Bits | Name | Description |

| 25:24 | IE_WINDOW_START_SUB_CYCLES | Number of clock cycles to subtract from the delay of the start of the pad input enable window. Allows the IE window to start up to 3 cycles sooner than RL cycles beyond the CAS command. For PCDDR3 devices, this is required to be set to 1 as the first DQS edge could arrive slightly before RL expires. |

| 15:12 | IE_WINDOW_END_ADD_CYCLES | Additional clock cycles to extend the pad input enable window. |
| 7:0 | IE_WINDOW_END | Amount of time to extend the DQ/DQS pad input enable window beyond CAS Cycle + Read Latency + burst length/2. This can be set to a minimum of tDQSCKmax + delays in the read data path from memory to the DQ pad (board/package delays) + 500ps. |

### 0x0044C1A0 BIMC_S_DDR0_DPE_DRAM_TIMING_23

* **Type:** RW
* **Clock:** ACLK
* **Reset State:** 0x00000000

This register contains timing values required by the memory vendor in ns. These values are not used by the design until they are loaded in the active register DRAM_TIMING_23_ACT by setting CONFIG_4[LOAD_ALL_CONFIG] to '1' or when CONFIG_3[LOAD_TIMING_ON_FREQ_CHNG] is set to '1' and a frequency change occurs

The value of the parameter contained in the registers can be in DDR clock cycles or in multiples of 100ps and may vary from one SDRAM vendor to another.

Refer to the note in DRAM_TIMING_0 CSR.

| 20:16 | ODTON_MIN | Specifies the ODT on min delay for LPDDR3/PCDDR3. |
| 13:8 | ODTOFF_MAX | Specifies the ODT off max delay for LPDDR3/PCDDR3. |

## BIMC_S_DDR0_DPE_DQCAL_RDATA_RANK1_U (0x0044C240)

| Property | Value |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Type** | R |
| **Clock** | ACLK |
| **Reset State** | 0x00000000 |

DQCAL Read Data Register for Rank1 Upper.

This register contains the upper 32 bits of a x64 DRAM mode register contents for a DQ calibration command triggered via SHKE to Rank1. The contents of this register are only valid for x64 DRAM devices. This is used to capture the read data from the DRAM device's mode register for a read DQ calibration command for LPDDR3 or an MPR read command for PCDDR3. The DQS data bits 0, 8, 16, 24, 32, 40, 48 and 56 are only captured on each DQS edge. The field below will capture the data for the last 2 cycles of DQS (last 4 DQS edges). Eg. DQCAL_RDATA[7:0] will have DQS data bits 0, 8, 16, 24, 32, 40, 48 and 56 for the fifth DQS edge. Hence 32 bits for the first 4 DQS edges.

### BIMC_S_DDR0_DPE_DQCAL_RDATA_RANK1_U Bits

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:0 | DQCAL_RDATA | READ ONLY<br>Upper 32 bits of Data for DQ calibration read for Rank1. The data captures the lowest bit for each byte across the memory burst. For eg. each cycle of memory burst is 16 bytes of data for x64 DRAM- 1 bit for each byte is captured which is 16 bits for every cycle of DQS. |
<!-- page 440 -->

## BIMC_S_DDR0_DPE_DQCAL_RDATA_RANK1_L (0x0044C244)

| Property | Value |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Type** | R |
| **Clock** | ACLK |
| **Reset State** | 0x00000000 |

DQCAL Read Data Register for Rank1 Lower.

This register contains the lower 32 bits of a x64 DRAM or 32 bits of a x32 DRAM mode register contents for a DQ calibration command triggered via SHKE to Rank1. This is used to capture the read data from the DRAM device's mode register for a read DQ calibration command for LPDDR3 or an MPR read command for PCDDR3. The DQS data bits 0, 8, 16 and 24 are only captured on each DQS edge for x32 DRAM device. For x32 LPDDR3 or PCDDR3 DRAM, DQCAL_RDATA[3:0] will have DQS data bits 0, 8, 16 and 24 for the first DQS edge. Hence 32 bits for the 8 DQS edges. For x64 LPDDR3 or PCDDR3 DRAM, the DQS data bits 0, 8, 16, 24, 32, 40, 48 and 56 are only captured on each DQS edge for x64 DRAM device. For x64 LPDDR3 or PCDDR3 DRAM, DQCAL_RDATA[7:0] will have DQS data bits 0, 8, 16, 24, 32, 40, 48 and 56 for every DQS edge (in this case DQS edges 1 - 4) resulting in 32 bits of captured data.

### BIMC_S_DDR0_DPE_DQCAL_RDATA_RANK1_L Bits

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:0 | DQCAL_RDATA | READ ONLY<br>Lower 32 bits of Data for DQ calibration read for Rank1. The data captures the lowest bit for each byte across the memory burst. For eg. each cycle of memory burst is 8 bytes of data for x32 DRAM (or 16 bytes of data for x64 DRAM) - 1 bit for each byte is captured which is 8 bits for every cycle of DQS. |

### BIMC_S_DDR0_DPE_DQCAL_STATUS0_RANK1 (continued)

*Note that the byte numbers below may not correspond to the actual DRAM byte. This is required so as to keep the byte number reference correct between the controller and the PHY (which has no information on the byte swap feature)*

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 7 | DQCAL_COMPARE_BYTE7 | **READ ONLY**<br>This field is only valid for x64 DRAM devices.<br>Indicates whether the DQ calibration command for LPDDR3 or PCDDR3 triggered via SHKE_DRAM_MANUAL_0[RD_DQCAL] resulted in an expected pattern comparison pass/fail. The value in this CSR field is valid when HW deasserts SHKE_DRAM_MANUAL_0[RD_DQCAL] indicating that the command completed. SW also needs to ensure that the number of DQS edges received in DQCAL_STATUS1_RANK1[DQS_PE_BYTE7] and DQCAL_STATUS1_RANK1[DQS_NE_BYTE7] are correct. ### BIMC_S_DDR0_DPE_CGC_CTRL

**Address**: `0x0044C2FC`
**Type**: `RW`
**Clock**: `ACLK`
**Reset State**: `0x00000000`

DPE clock gating control register. This register is used to enable automatic, dynamic gating of clock trees within the DPE. Values written to the CSR_ACCESS and RECALC_TCYC fields take effect immediately, while changes to all other fields become active upon writing a value of '1' to CONFIG_4[LOAD_ALL_CONFIG] or when CONFIG_3[LOAD_TIMING_ON_FREQ_CHNG] is set to '1' and a frequency change occurs.

### 0x0044D020 BIMC_S_DDR0_SHKE_DRAM_MANUAL_0

**Type:** RW
**Clock:** HCLK
**Reset State:** 0x00000000

Manual Command Register 0.

This register enables the software to manually issue commands to the DDR SDRAM interface. A value of '1' should be written in the bit field of the command that the software wants to force the controller to perform. When the controller has finished executing the command, it will clear the bit. Only one bit should be active at any given time in the register below, except for the RANK_SEL field. This limits the SW to have only 1 outstanding SW command for execution by the memory controller. This CSR is typically used for initialization the memory rank along with the DRAM_MANUAL_1 register. During SDRAM device initialization, SW should also program the DRAM_MANUAL_1 register (optional) so HW can maintain timing between the memory commands else, this is SW's responsibility. Once the rank(s) are initialized, it is not typical for SW to trigger commands (except those which are required as part of sequences - eg. Deep Power down). However after rank initialization, the HW will maintain protocol legal timings for SW triggered commands.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 29:28 | RANK_SEL | SW: RW, HW: R<br>Select which chip select should be targeted for the chosen manual command to be executed.<br>0x0: INVALID (Invalid (default))<br>0x1: CS0_ONLY (CS0 only)<br>0x2: CS1_ONLY (CS1 only)<br>0x3: CS0_AND_CS1 (CS0 and CS1) |
| 27 | CK_ON | SW: RW, HW: R<br>Turns on external clock CK, CKN.<br>This bit is self-cleared once the command is executed. Until the rank is initialized, HW would control the clocks based on this setting.<br>0x0: NOP (Nop (default))<br>0x1: EXECUTE (Execute) |
| 26 | CKE_ON | SW: RW, HW: R<br>Turns on clock enable CKE.<br>This bit is self-cleared once the command is executed. Until the rank is initialized, HW would control the CKE based on this setting.<br>0x0: NOP (Nop (default))<br>0x1: EXECUTE (Execute) |

| 24 | CK_OFF | SW: RW, HW: R<br>Turns off external clock CK, CKN.<br>This bit is self-cleared once the command is executed. Until the rank is initialized, HW would control the clocks based on this setting.<br>0x0: NOP (Nop (default))<br>0x1: EXECUTE (Execute) |
| 23 | CKE_OFF | SW: RW, HW: R<br>Turns off clock enable CKE.<br>This bit is self-cleared once the command is executed. Until the rank is initialized, HW would control the CKE based on this setting.<br>0x0: NOP (Nop (default))<br>0x1: EXECUTE (Execute) |
| 22 | RESETN_OFF | SW: RW, HW: R<br>Turns off reset pin to PCDDR3/4 devices only.<br>This bit is self-cleared once the command is executed. Until the rank is initialized, HW would control the SDRAM reset based on this setting.<br>0x0: NOP (Nop (default))<br>0x1: EXECUTE (Execute) |

HW will check to ensure all commands outstanding to the rank have completed before issuing the DPD command. The RANK_SEL field for this command cannot be set to '11'.<br>0x0: NOP (Nop (default))<br>0x1: EXECUTE (Execute) |

The RANK_SEL field for this command cannot be set to '11'. It is SW's responsibility to ensure that the minimum duration of DPD is met. Additionally SW needs to ensure that the clocks are stable before exiting DPD. | 8 | STALL_CMDS | SW: RW, HW: R<br>This allows SW to stop transactions on the DDR bus. Once the transactions are stalled, SW will be required to unstall by executing the RESUME_CMDS command. SW needs to account for the same when setting the RANK_SEL field for this command (e.g. if the other rank is uninitialized or in deep power down). This bit is self-cleared once the command is executed.<br>0x0: NOP (Nop (default))<br>0x1: EXECUTE (Execute) |
| 7 | RESUME_CMDS | SW: RW, HW: R<br>This allows SW to resume transactions on the DDR bus. This feature has been provided for debug. This SW trigger for resume is only supported for all active ranks. SW needs to account for the same when setting the RANK_SEL field for this command (eg. if the other rank is uninitialized or in deep power down). Also, this command is only supported if SW had triggered a stall. The corresponding status can be observed via SHKE_DRAM_STATUS CSR. This bit is self-cleared once the command is executed.<br>0x0: NOP (Nop (default))<br>0x1: EXECUTE (Execute) |

This bit is self-cleared once the command is executed. This bit is only to be used for Mode register writes related to the LPDDR3 CA training sequence as this allows the CA bus to be stable before and after the command to allow for sufficient setup time for the DRAM to sample the command correctly. The RANK_SEL field for this command cannot be set to '11'.<br>0x0: NOP (Nop (default))<br>0x1: EXECUTE (Execute) |

This bit is self-cleared once the command is executed. The RANK_SEL field for this command cannot be set to '11'.<br>0x0: NOP (Nop (default))<br>0x1: EXECUTE (Execute) |
| 4 | RD_DQCAL | SW: RW, HW: RW<br>DQ Calibration Read Command.<br>This relates to LPDDR3 MRR command & PCDDR3 MPR command.<br>This is used for read training and/or rank auto detect. A pre-defined read pattern is sent out by the DRAM and captured by the controller. In case of LPDDR3, this is an MRR commands with SHKE_MREG_ADDR_WDATA_CNTL[MREG_ADDR] specified correctly (valid values are 0x32 & 0x40). In case of PCDDR3 devices, this is an MPR read command and hence SHKE_MREG_ADDR_WDATA_CNTL[MREG_ADDR] is a don't care. This bit is self-cleared once the command is executed. The read data status for the calibration read command is captured in the DPE status registers. The RANK_SEL field for this command cannot be set to '11'.<br>0x0: NOP (Nop (default))<br>0x1: EXECUTE (Execute) |

### 0x0044D024 BIMC_S_DDR0_SHKE_DRAM_MANUAL_1

**Type:** RW
**Clock:** HCLK
**Reset State:** 0x00000000

Manual Command Register 1.

This register can only be used during memory rank initialization. As part of the memory device initialization, certain delays are required between commands. This can be enforced by SW or by setting up the following register before triggering a command to be executed via DRAM_MANUAL_0 CSR. When WAIT_TIMER_BEFORE_HW_CLEAR is set to a non-zero value any SW command issued during memory device initialization will wait the programmable number of timer/xo clock cycles before indicating the command completion response.
<!-- page 469 -->

### BIMC_S_DDR0_SHKE_DRAM_MANUAL_1 (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 16 | WAIT_TIMER_DOMAIN | SW: RW, HW: R<br>Indicates which clock should be used in HW for the down counter.<br>0x0: TIMER_CLOCK (Timer Clock (default))<br>0x1: XO_CLOCK (XO Clock) |
| 15:0 | WAIT_TIMER_BEFORE_HW_CLEAR | SW: RW, HW: R<br>This indicates the amount of time in timer/xo clock cycles required to wait after sending the SW triggered command in SHKE_DRAM_MANUAL_0 CSR before indicating the command completion response. |

### 0x0044D030 BIMC_S_DDR0_SHKE_MREG_ADDR_WDATA_CNTL

**Type:** RW
**Clock:** HCLK

### Register: BIMC_S_DDR0_SHKE_PERIODIC_MRR
- **Address:** `0x0044D0A0`
- **Type:** `RW`
- **Clock:** `HCLK`
- **Reset State:** `0x00000000`

SHKE Periodic MRR Command.
This is typically used to generate periodic LPDDR2/3 MRR commands to monitor the temperature of the memory device and appropriately adjust the refresh rate depending on the SDRAM device temperature.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 27:20 | MRR_ADDR | Specify which mode register to access. For LPDDR2/3 devices, this would typically be set to 0x04. |
| 17:16 | MRR_RANK_SEL | SW: RW, HW: R<br>Specify DRAM rank to which the command goes. The HW will only send the command to a rank which is initialized.<br>0x0: NOT_VALID (Not valid (default))<br>0x1: RANK_0_ONLY (Rank 0 only)<br>0x2: RANK_1_ONLY (Rank 1 only)<br>0x3: BOTH_RANKS_0_AND_1 (Both ranks 0 and 1) |
<!-- page 474 -->
| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 15:0 | MRR_INTERVAL | SW: RW, HW: R<br>Number of timer clock edges between periodic MRR samples. This interval is maintained by the controller on a per-rank basis. The timer clock typically runs at 32 kHz, hence providing a range of 10-2050ms periodic interval. The minimum supported value is ?d4 for 1 rank systems and ?d13 for 2 rank systems.<br>0x0: DISABLED (Disabled (default))<br>0x100: TIME_OF_10MS (Time of 10ms)<br>0x200: TIME_OF_20MS (Time of 20ms)<br>0x400: TIME_OF_30MS (Time of 30ms)<br>0x800: TIME_OF_60MS (Time of 60ms)<br>0x1000: TIME_OF_130MS (Time of 130ms)<br>0x2000: TIME_OF_260MS (Time of 260ms)<br>0x4000: TIME_OF_510MS (Time of 510ms)<br>0x8000: TIME_OF_1030MS (Time of 1030ms)<br>0xFFFF: TIME_OF_2050MS (Time of 2050ms) |

### Register: BIMC_S_DDR0_SHKE_AUTO_REFRESH_CNTL
- **Address:** `0x0044D0F0`
- **Type:** `RW`
- **Clock:** `HCLK`
- **Reset State:** `0x00000000`

This register provides the controls for auto refresh functionality for the SDRAM devices.
<!-- page 477 -->
| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 29 | AUTO_RFSH_ENABLE_RANK1 | SW: RW, HW: R<br>Auto Refresh Enable for Rank1<br>0x0: DISABLE (Disable (default))<br>0x1: ENABLE (Enable) |
| 28 | AUTO_RFSH_ENABLE_RANK0 | SW: RW, HW: R<br>Auto Refresh Enable for Rank0<br>0x0: DISABLE (Disable (default))<br>0x1: ENABLE (Enable) |
| 25:24 | AUTO_REFRESH_MODE | SW: RW, HW: R<br>Specifies the auto refresh mode. Per-bank refresh mode is only supported for LPDDR2/3 8-bank devices.<br>0x0: ALL_BANK_REFRESH (All Bank Refresh (default))<br>0x1: PER_BANK_REFRESH (Per Bank Refresh) |
| 23:22 | AUTO_SWITCH_ALL_BANK_MODE | SW: RW, HW: R<br>If configured in per-bank refresh mode, this setting controls whether HW automatically switches to all-bank refresh mode when a certain high temperature of the memory device is detected which requires a faster refresh rate. When enabled, HW automatically switches back to the configured per-bank refresh mode when the device temperature returns below the threshold specified. When set to '10', HW will automatically switch to all-bank refresh mode when a TREFI multiplier of 0.25 is received and it switches bank to per-bank refresh mode when a multiplier greater than 0.25 is received (eg. 0.5 or 1). It is illegal to change this CSR setting after the rank has been initialized.<br>0x0: DISABLE (Disable (default))<br>0x1: TREFI_0_5X_OR_TREFI_0_25X (TREFI_0.5X_OR_TREFI_0.25X)<br>0x2: TREFI_0_25X (TREFI_0.25X)<br>0x3: NOT_VALID (Not Valid) |
| 16 | DISABLE_AUTO_REFRESH_TEMP_UPDATE | SW: RW, HW: R<br>Disables the refresh rate updates based on SRR based DRAM temperature updates. It is illegal to change this CSR setting after the rank has been initialized.<br>0x0: ENABLE (Enable (default))<br>0x1: DISABLE (Disable) |
| 9:0 | TREFI | SW: RW, HW: R<br>If `SHKE_AUTO_RFSH_CNTL_1[TREFI]` is non-zero, then this field is used as TREFI value for rank0. If `SHKE_AUTO_RFSH_CNTL_1[TREFI]` is zero, then this field is used as TREFI value for both ranks. Number of clock cycle delay (in tcxo clock cycles) between all-bank auto-refresh commands. This is required to be set to the "desired tREFI" -1 tcxo cycles. It is illegal to change this CSR setting after the rank has been initialized. |
<!-- page 478 -->
### Register: BIMC_S_DDR0_SHKE_SELF_REFRESH_CNTL
- **Address:** `0x0044D0F4`
- **Type:** `RW`
- **Clock:** `HCLK`
- **Reset State:** `0x00000000`

This register provides the controls for HW activity based self refresh.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 29 | HW_SELF_RFSH_ENABLE_RANK1 | SW: RW, HW: R<br>Enables HW to look for no activity for rank1 and trigger an idle timer specified based on the value of HW_SELF_RFSH_TIMER. If there is no activity still and the timer expires, the HW will initiate entry to self refresh mode.<br>0x0: DISABLE (Disable (default))<br>0x1: ENABLE (Enable) |
| 28 | HW_SELF_RFSH_ENABLE_RANK0 | SW: RW, HW: R<br>Enables HW to look for no activity for rank0 and trigger an idle timer specified based on the value of HW_SELF_RFSH_TIMER. If there is no activity still and the timer expires, the HW will initiate entry to self refresh mode.<br>0x0: DISABLE (Disable (default))<br>0x1: ENABLE (Enable) |
| 23:12 | HW_SELF_RFSH_IDLE_TIMER | SW: RW, HW: R<br>Count idle tcxo cycles before entering self refresh. The timer is based on XO clock frequency. Valid only when HW_SELF_RFSH_ENABLE_RANK* or CONCURRENT_SELF_RFSH_EN is set. The minimum supported value is 4. |
<!-- page 479 -->
| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 8 | CONCURRENT_SELF_RFSH_EN | SW: RW, HW: R<br>Concurrent Self Refresh Mode. This field is only valid if both the memory ranks are populated with DRAM devices and if only one or none of the individual self refresh enable bits for the ranks are set. (Currently only support this field can be set if and only if the individual self refresh enable bits for the ranks are both off) If the individual self refresh enable bits for both ranks (above) are off and this field is set (only supported mode), then self refresh is only entered when both ranks are idle and the idle timer has expired for both ranks. The above is a recommended setting for PCDDR3 (or LPDDR3) for dual rank ODT configurations wherein the inactive rank is selected to provide termination for a read/write to the other rank. If the concurrent self refresh enable bit is set and only the hardware self refresh enable bit for rank1 is set (not supported), then the controller would enter self refresh for rank1 entirely based on rank1 traffic, however the self refresh enter for rank0 would happen only if rank1 is in self refresh and rank0's idle timer has expired. Rank0 will come out of self refresh if either of the ranks go non-idle. This setting is recommended for LPDDR3 (external) dual rank devices wherein only 1 ODT pin exists.<br>0x0: DISABLE (Disable (default))<br>0x1: ENABLE (Enable) |
<!-- page 480 -->
### Register: BIMC_S_DDR0_SHKE_AUTO_REFRESH_CNTL_1
- **Address:** `0x0044D100`
- **Type:** `RW`
- **Clock:** `HCLK`
- **Reset State:** `0x00000000`

This register provides the controls for auto refresh functionality for Rank1 for the SDRAM devices.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 9:0 | TREFI | SW: RW, HW: R<br>This field is only for Rank1 refresh rate. If the contents of this field are zero, then `SHKE_AUTO_REFRESH_CNTL[TREFI]` is used as the initial value for both ranks, else `SHKE_AUTO_REFRESH_CNTL[TREFI]` is used as the initial value for rank0 and this field is used as the initial value for rank1. Number of clock cycle delay (in tcxo clock cycles) between all-bank auto-refresh commands. This is required to be set to the "desired tREFI" -1 tcxo cycles. It is illegal to change this CSR setting after the rank has been initialized. |

### Register: BIMC_S_DDR0_SHKE_AUTO_REFRESH_CNTL_2
- **Address:** `0x0044D104`
- **Type:** `RW`
- **Clock:** `HCLK`
- **Reset State:** `0x00000000`

This register provides the programmable delay for updating the refresh rate based on SDRAM's device temperature. This register is NOT SUPPORTED if retention based power collapse is used.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:16 | RFSH_UPDATE_TIMER | SW: RW, HW: R<br>Number of timer clock edges to wait before updating the refresh rate. This is only for the refresh rates selected in `DLY_RFSH_CONDN` below. Typically, SW would want to set this to the amount of time it takes to service a high temperature interrupt from DPE indicating high temperature is reached and hence the min. frequency of operation needs to be increased for the design to perform data commands in addition to keeping up with the auto refresh requirements of the device. A value of 0 indicates that the timer is disabled. The minimum supported value for this timer is ?h3. Typically, the value programmed in this timer would be far less than the value in `PERIODIC_MRR[MRR_INTERVAL]`. |


<!-- page 481 -->

### BIMC_S_DDR0_SHKE_AUTO_REFRESH_CNTL_2 (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 0 | DLY_RFSH_CONDN | SW: RW, HW: R<br><br>If the timer above is valid (non-zero), then this CSR field determines at what requested refresh rates should the timer be enabled.<br>0x0: TREFI_0_5X_OR_LESS (TREFI_0.5X_OR_LESS)<br>0x1: TREFI_0_25X (TREFI_0.25X) |

### PCNOC_EPRB0_SPROF_MAINCTL

**Address:** `0x00503008`
**Type:** RW
**Reset State:** `0x00000000`

Register MainCtl contains probe global control bits. The register has seven bit fields:

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 7 | FILTBYTEALWAYSCHAINABLEEN | When set to 0, Filter Byte / ByteEn Cnt will be connected to all statistics counters where odd Stat count are not chainable. When set to 1, Filter Byte / ByteEn Cnt will be connected only to chainable stat counter (even stat counter). |
| 6 | INTRUSIVEMODE | When set to 1, register field IntrusiveMode enables trace operation in Intrusive flow-control mode. When set to 0, the register enables trace operation in Overflow flow-control mode |
| 5 | STATCONDDUMP | When set, register field StatCondDump enables the dump of a statistics frame to the range of counter values set for registers StatAlarmMin, StatAlarmMax, and AlarmMode. This field also renders register StatAlarmStatus inoperative. When parameter statisticsCounterAlarm is set to False, the StatCondDump register bit is reserved. |
| 4 | ALARMEN | When set, register field AlarmEn enables the probe to collect alarm-related information. When the register field bit is null, both TraceAlarm and StatAlarm outputs are driven to 0. |
<!-- page 505 -->

### PCNOC_EPRB0_SPROF_MAINCTL (Continued)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 3 | STATEN | When set to 1, register field StatEn enables statistics profiling. The probe sendS statistics results to the output for signal ObsTx. All statistics counters are cleared when the StatEn bit goes from 0 to 1. When set to 0, counters are disabled. |
| 2 | PAYLOADEN | Register field PayloadEn, when set to 1, enables traces to contain headers and payload. When set to 0, only headers are reported. |
| 1 | TRACEEN | Register field TraceEn enables the probe to send filtered packets (Trace) on the ObsTx observation output. |
| 0 | ERREN | Register field ErrEn enables the probe to send on the ObsTx output any packet with Error status, independently of filtering mechanisms, thus constituting a simple supplementary global filter. |

| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 4:0 | STATPERIOD | Register StatPeriod is a 5-bit register that sets a period, within a range of 2-8 megacycles, during which statistics are collected before being dumped automatically. Setting the register effectively enables automatic mode operation for statistics collection. Note: The configured period is also used for statistics alarm generation. The period is calculated with the formula: N_Cycle = 2**min(23,StatPeriod)When register StatPeriod is set to its default value 0, automatic dump mode is disabled, and register StatGo is activated for manual mode operation. ### PCNOC_TPRB0_SPROF_MAINCTL

**Address:** `0x00504008`  
**Type:** RW  
**Reset State:** `0x00000000`

Register MainCtl contains probe global control bits. The register has seven bit fields:


<!-- page 521 -->
### PCNOC_TPRB0_SPROF_MAINCTL (continued)

| Bits | Name | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 7 | FILTBYTEALWAYSCHAINABLEEN | RW | When set to 0, Filter Byte / ByteEn Cnt will be connected to all statistics counters where odd Stat count are not chainable. When set to 1, Filter Byte / ByteEn Cnt will be connected only to chainable stat counter (even stat counter). |
| 6 | INTRUSIVEMODE | R | When set to 1, register field IntrusiveMode enables trace operation in Intrusive flow-control mode. When set to 0, the register enables trace operation in Overflow flow-control mode |
| 5 | STATCONDDUMP | RW | When set, register field StatCondDump enables the dump of a statistics frame to the range of counter values set for registers StatAlarmMin, StatAlarmMax, and AlarmMode. This field also renders register StatAlarmStatus inoperative. When parameter statisticsCounterAlarm is set to False, the StatCondDump register bit is reserved. |
| 4 | ALARMEN | RW | When set, register field AlarmEn enables the probe to collect alarm-related information. When the register field bit is null, both TraceAlarm and StatAlarm outputs are driven to 0. |
| 3 | STATEN | RW | When set to 1, register field StatEn enables statistics profiling. The probe sendS statistics results to the output for signal ObsTx. All statistics counters are cleared when the StatEn bit goes from 0 to 1. When set to 0, counters are disabled. |
| 2 | PAYLOADEN | RW | Register field PayloadEn, when set to 1, enables traces to contain headers and payload. When set ot 0, only headers are reported. |
| 1 | TRACEEN | RW | Register field TraceEn enables the probe to send filtered packets (Trace) on the ObsTx observation output. |
| 0 | ERREN | RW | Register field ErrEn enables the probe to send on the ObsTx output any packet with Error status, independently of filtering mechanisms, thus constituting a simple supplementary global filter. |

### PCNOC_TPRB0_SPROF_STATPERIOD

* **Address**: `0x00504024`
* **Type**: `RW`
* **Reset State**: `0x00000000`

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 4:0 | STATPERIOD | Register StatPeriod is a 5-bit register that sets a period, within a range of 2-8 megacycles, during which statistics are collected before being dumped automatically. Setting the register effectively enables automatic mode operation for statistics collection. Note: The configured period is also used for statistics alarm generation. The period is calculated with the formula: N_Cycle = 2**min(23,StatPeriod) When register StatPeriod is set to its default value 0, automatic dump mode is disabled, and register StatGo is activated for manual mode operation. Note: When parameter nStatisticsCounter is set to 0, statistics collection is disabled, with the consequence that all statistics collection registers, including StatPeriod, are reserved. |

### PCNOC_TPRB0_SPROF_STATGO

* **Address**: `0x00504028`
* **Type**: `RW`
* **Reset State**: `0x00000000`

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 0 | STATGO | Writing to 1-bit pulse register StatGo generates a statistics dump. The register is active when statistics collection operates in its manual mode, that is, when register StatPeriod is set to 0. |

## Section 3.1: PCNOC_0_BUS_TIMEOUT

### Register: PCNOC_0_ABT_INST_ID
- **Address**: `0x00023004`
- **Type**: `RW`
- **Clock**: `AHB Clock`
- **Reset State**: `0x00000000`

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:0 | INSTID | SW configurable field to provide unique instance number for each of the AHB Timeout Slaves in the chip. |

### Register: PCNOC_0_ABT_NUM_SLAVES
- **Address**: `0x00023008`
- **Type**: `R`
- **Clock**: `AHB Clock`
- **Reset State**: `0x00000005`

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 5:0 | NUMSLAVES | Specifies the number of slaves on the AHB bus excluding the Timeout Slave. Valid values are from 1 to 32. |
<!-- page 546 -->

### Register: PCNOC_0_ABT_TIMER_LOADVAL
- **Address**: `0x0002300C`
- **Type**: `RW`
- **Clock**: `AHB Clock`
- **Reset State**: `0x000000FF`

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 7:0 | LOADVAL | Load the timer with this value, when the timer is in load mode, i.e, MODE field in ABT_TIMER_MODE is 0.<br>Note: LOADVAL of 0 is not valid. |

### Register: PCNOC_0_ABT_TIMER_MODE
- **Address**: `0x00023010`
- **Type**: `RW`
- **Clock**: `AHB Clock`
- **Reset State**: `0x00000000`

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 0 | MODE | If this field is 0, the timer is in load mode and the LOADVAL field value in ABT_TIMER_LOADVAL is loaded into the timer. If this field is 1, the timer is in run mode. |

### Register: PCNOC_0_ABT_INTR_STATUS
- **Address**: `0x00023014`
- **Type**: `R`
- **Clock**: `AHB Clock`
- **Reset State**: `0x00000000`

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 0 | INTRSTATUS | Specifies the timeout interrupt status irrespective of interrupt enable. |

### Register: PCNOC_0_ABT_INTR_CLEAR
- **Address**: `0x00023018`
- **Type**: `W`
- **Clock**: `AHB Clock`
- **Reset State**: `0x00000000`
<!-- page 547 -->

### Register: PCNOC_0_ABT_INTR_CLEAR (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 0 | INTRCLEAR | Clears the pending interrupt. |

### Register: PCNOC_0_ABT_INTR_ENABLE
- **Address**: `0x0002301C`
- **Type**: `RW`
- **Clock**: `AHB Clock`
- **Reset State**: `0x00000000`

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 0 | INTRENABLE | Enable an interrupt generation on timeout event. |

### Register: PCNOC_0_ABT_SYND_VALID
- **Address**: `0x00023020`
- **Type**: `R`
- **Clock**: `AHB Clock`
- **Reset State**: `0x00000000`

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 0 | SYNDVALID | Set when the information in other syndrome registers is valid. |

### Register: PCNOC_0_ABT_SYND_CLEAR
- **Address**: `0x00023024`
- **Type**: `W`
- **Clock**: `AHB Clock`
- **Reset State**: `0x00000000`

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 0 | SYNDCLEAR | Clears the syndrome valid bit and syndrome information (ABT_SYND_ID, ABT_SYND_ADDR, ABT_SYND_HREADY). |
<!-- page 548 -->

### Register: PCNOC_0_ABT_SYND_ID
- **Address**: `0x00023028`
- **Type**: `R`
- **Clock**: `AHB Clock`
- **Reset State**: `0x00000000`

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 15:13 | BID | Bus ID of the transaction that caused bus hang. |
| 12:8 | PID | Port ID of the transaction that caused bus hang. |
| 7:0 | MID | Master ID of the transaction that caused bus hang. |

### Register: PCNOC_0_ABT_SYND_ADDR0
- **Address**: `0x0002302C`
- **Type**: `R`
- **Clock**: `AHB Clock`
- **Reset State**: `0x00000000`

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:0 | SYNDADDR0 | Lower 32-bit address field of the transaction that caused bus hang. |

### Register: PCNOC_0_ABT_SYND_ADDR1
- **Address**: `0x00023030`
- **Type**: `R`
- **Clock**: `AHB Clock`
- **Reset State**: `0x00000000`

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:0 | SYNDADDR1 | Upper 32-bit address field of the transaction that caused bus hang. Reserved for future use. |

### Register: PCNOC_0_ABT_SYND_HREADY
- **Address**: `0x00023034`
- **Type**: `R`
- **Clock**: `AHB Clock`
- **Reset State**: `0xFFFFFFFF`
<!-- page 549 -->

### Register: PCNOC_0_ABT_SYND_HREADY (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:0 | SYNDHREADY | Contains the status of Hready for each slave on the bus during the timeout event. The valid bit fields are [ABT_NUM_SLAVES-1:0]. Each valid bit field corresponds to a physical slave on the bus. |

# 4 Clock Controller

## 4.1 GCC_GLOBAL_CLK_CTL_REG

### GCC_GPLL0_MODE

**Address:** 0x01821000
**Type:** RW
**Clock:** CLK
**Reset State:** 0x00000000

GPLL0_MODE register configures and controls GPLL0.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 21 | PLL_VOTE_FSM_RESET | Resets PLL voting FSM<br>0:Deasserts Reset to PLL voting FSM<br>1:Resets PLL voting FSM |
| 20 | PLL_VOTE_FSM_ENA | Enable PLL voting FSM<br>0:Disabled<br>1:Enabled |
| 19:14 | PLL_BIAS_COUNT | Sets PLL bias count of PLL voting FSM. The count specifies X * 16 PLL reference clock cycles to wait for biasing the PLL during bring up. |
| 13:8 | PLL_LOCK_COUNT | Sets PLL lock time of PLL voting FSM. The count specifies the number of BIAS wait time interval to wait before determining PLL is locked. If lock count is Y, it will wait Y * PLL_BIAS_COUNT * 16 PLL reference clock cycles before declaring PLL is locked. If this value is set to 0, the lock_det output of the PLL is used instead |
| 3 | RESERVED | Reserved |
| 2 | PLL_RESET_N | This bitfield is used for reset of digital logic in PLL. This includes the MND counters and integer divider |
| 1 | PLL_BYPASSNL | Specify the PLL bypass mode<br>0:Bypass PLL<br>1:Use PLL |
<!-- page 585 -->

### GCC_GPLL0_MODE (continued)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 0 | PLL_OUTCTRL | Specify the PLL output control<br>0:Disable PLL output and save power<br>1:Activate PLL outputs |

### GCC_GPLL0_L_VAL

**Address:** 0x01821004
**Type:** RW
**Clock:** CLK
**Reset State:** 0x00000000

Following equation is used to calculate the GPLL0 output frequency

VCO = REF * [L+(M/N)]

Where R represents the pre-divider of 2 and P represents post-divider

The value of GPLL0 register is the given value of L for that equation.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 7:0 | PLL_L | This bitfield contains 8-bit L value. This specifies the PLL VCO feedback divide ratio. |

### GCC_GPLL0_M_VAL

**Address:** 0x01821008
**Type:** RW
**Clock:** CLK
**Reset State:** 0x00000000

Following equation is used to calculate the GPLL0 output frequency

VCO = REF * [L+(M/N)]
Where R represents the pre-divider of 2 and P represents post-divider

The value of GPLL0 register is the given value of M for that equation.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 18:0 | PLL_M | This bitfield contains 19-bit M value. This specifies the PLL M-value for frac-N accumulator. |
<!-- page 586 -->

### GCC_GPLL0_N_VAL

**Address:** 0x0182100C
**Type:** RW
**Clock:** CLK
**Reset State:** 0x00000000

Following equation is used to calculate the GPLL0 output frequency

VCO = REF * [L+(M/N)]

Where R represents the pre-divider of 2 and P represents post-divider

The value of GPLL0 register is the given value of N for that equation.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 18:0 | PLL_N | This bitfield contains 19-bit N value. This specifies the PLL N-value for frac-N accumulator. |

**Address:** 0x01821010
**Type:** RW
**Clock:** CLK
**Reset State:** 0x00000000

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:25 | RESERVE_BITS31_25 | Reserved bits. |
| 24 | MN_EN | PLL fractional mode control.<br>0:Disable<br>1:Enable |
| 23:21 | RESERVE_BITS23_21 | Reserved bits. |
| 20 | VCO_SEL | VCO selection<br>1: Select low freq VCO (100-500 Mhz)<br>0: Select high-freq VCO (400-1400 Mhz) |
| 19:13 | RESERVE_BITS19_13 | Reserved bits. |
| 12 | PRE_DIV_RATIO | Clk_ref pre-divide ratio.<br>0: 1<br>1: 2 |
| 11:10 | RESERVE_BITS11_10 | Reserved bits. |
<!-- page 587 -->

### GCC_GPLL0_USER_CTL (continued)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 9:8 | POST_DIV_RATIO | Output clock Post divide ration.<br>00: 1<br>01: 2<br>10: Reserved<br>11: 4 |
| 7 | OUTPUT_INV | Output invert state.<br>0: Output invert disable<br>1: Output invert enable |
| 6:5 | RESERVED | Reserved |
| 4 | RESERVED | Reserved |
| 3 | PLLOUT_LV_EARLY | Enable or disable of pllout_lv_early output.<br>0: Disable<br>1: Enable |
| 2 | PLLOUT_LV_BIST | Enable or disable of pllout_lv_bist output.<br>0: Disable<br>1: Enable |
| 1 | PLLOUT_LV_AUX | Enable or disable of pllout_lv_aux output.<br>0: Disable<br>1: Enable |
| 0 | PLLOUT_LV_MAIN | Enable or disable of pllout_lv_main output.<br>0: Disable<br>1: Enable |

**Address:** 0x01821014
**Type:** RW
**Clock:** CLK
**Reset State:** 0x00031000

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:30 | RESERVE_BITS31_30 | Reserved bits. |
| 29 | FORCE_PFD_UP | Force PFD Up (force_PFD<1>).<br>0 Normal operation (default).<br>1 Force PFD UP -> 1 |
<!-- page 588 -->

### GCC_GPLL0_CONFIG_CTL (continued)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 28 | FORCE_PFD_DOWN | Force PFD down (force_PFD<0>).<br>0 Normal operation (default).<br>1 Force PFD DN -> 1 |
| 27:26 | NMOSC_FREQ_CTRL | Noise measurement oscillator frequency control.<br>00: Highest (2.8 GHz at TT / 1.05V / 40°C) (default)<br>01: 1/2 highest<br>10: 1/3 highest<br>11: 1/4 highest |
| 25:24 | PFD_DZSEL | PFD reset pulse width adjustment (PFD_dzsel<1:0>).<br>00 1x delay (default)<br>01: 2x delay<br>10: 3x delay<br>11: 4x delay |
| 23 | NMOSC_EN | Noise measurement oscillator control (nmosc_en)<br>0: Disable (default)<br>1: Enable |
| 22 | RESERVE_BIT22 | Reserved bit. |
| 21:20 | ICP_DIV | Charge pump bias mirror multiplication factor(icp_div<1:0>).<br>00: 1 (default)<br>01: 3/2<br>10: 7/4<br>11: 9/4 |
| 19:18 | IREG_DIV | Regulator bias mirror multiplication factor (ireg_div<1:0>).<br>00: 1 (default)<br>01: 7/5<br>10: 9/5<br>11: 11/5 |
| 17:16 | CUSEL | VCO desoupling cap unit size (cusel <1:0>).<br>00: 125 fF<br>01: 250 fF<br>10: 375 fF<br>11: 500 fF (default) |
| 15 | REF_MODE | Reference circuit mode (ref_mode).<br>0: Bandgap Mode: Seed currents source from bandgap circuit and Nwell refernce circuit active. (default)<br>1: Supply-independent mode: Seed currents sourced from supply-independent circuit and Nwell reference pulled to VDDA. |
| 14 | RESERVE_BIT14 | Reserved bit. |
<!-- page 589 -->

### GCC_GPLL0_CONFIG_CTL (continued)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 13:12 | CFG_LOCKDET | Lock detector phase error threshold (cfg_lockdet<1:0>).<br>00: 2pi/2<br>01: 2pi/15 (default)<br>10: 2pi/23<br>11: 2pi/31 |
| 11 | FORCE_ISEED | Seed current control (force_iseed).<br>0: Turn off seed currents when clock is detected. (default)<br>1: Keep seed currents on at all times. |
| 10:0 | RESERVE_BITS10_0 | Reserved bits. |

### 0x01823004 GCC_BIMC_PLL_L_VAL

* **Type**: RW
* **Clock**: CLK
* **Reset State**: 0x00000000

Following equation is used to calculate the BIMC_PLL output frequency:

$$VCO = REF \times [L+(M/N)]$$

Where R represents the pre-divider of 2 and P represents post-divider.

The value of BIMC_PLL register is the given value of L for that equation.

| 7:4 | SLEEP | RW | This bitfield specifies the number of clock cycles till complete sleep where headswitch of the corresponding memories will be opened.<br>0x0: CLOCK0 (Zero cycle)<br>0x1: CLOCK1 (One cycle)<br>0x2: CLOCK2 (Two cycles)<br>0x3: CLOCK3 (Three cycles)<br>0x4: CLOCK4 (Four cycles)<br>0x5: CLOCK5 (Five cycles)<br>0x6: CLOCK6 (Six cycles)<br>0x7: CLOCK7 (Seven cycles)<br>0x8: CLOCK8 (Eight cycles)<br>0x9: CLOCK9 (Nine cycles)<br>0xA: CLOCK10 (Ten cycles)<br>0xB: CLOCK11 (Eleven cycles)<br>0xC: CLOCK12 (Twelve cycles)<br>0xD: CLOCK13 (Thirteen cycles)<br>0xE: CLOCK14 (Fourteen cycles)<br>0xF: CLOCK15 (Fifteen cycles) |

### 0x01874004 GCC_CLOCK_FRQ_MEASURE_CTL

* **Type**: RW
* **Clock**: CLK
* **Reset State**: 0x00000000

The clock frequency measure control register holds the value to load in the XO DIV4 counter. It also contains the enable to turn on both up and down counters for measure frequency for the corresponding debug clock.

> [!NOTE]
> The XO DIV4 counter use the gcc_xo_div4_clk. One must enable the gcc_xo_div4_clk by programming GCC_XO_DIV4_CBCR.
<!-- page 783 -->

### GCC_CLOCK_FRQ_MEASURE_CTL (continued)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 20 | CNT_EN | This bitfield is used to enable both the Up and Down counter.<br>0x1: ENABLE (Enable.)<br>0x0: DISABLE (Disable.) |
| 19:0 | XO_DIV4_TERM_CNT | After being loaded, this value is decremented and used to compare in order to figure out the frequency of the clock being measured. Freq(measure clock) = Freq(XO_DIV4) * (MEASURE_CNT + 1.5) / (XO_DIV4_TERM_CNT + 3.5) |

### 0x01874008 GCC_CLOCK_FRQ_MEASURE_STATUS

* **Type**: R
* **Clock**: CLK
* **Reset State**: 0x00000000

This register is read only register which contains the status of the measurement counter and its value.

It is used to figure out the frequency of the clock being measured at the end.

#### GCC_CLOCK_FRQ_MEASURE_STATUS Bit Fields

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 25 | XO_DIV4_CNT_DONE | This bitfield is automatically set (1) when the XO_DIV4 counter terminates. It can be polled by the microprocessor to determine when the value of the measurement counter is valid |
| 24:0 | MEASURE_CNT | These read only register bits hold the value stored in the measurement counter, which is used to figure out the frequency of the clock being measured. Freq(measure clock) = Freq(XO_DIV4) * (MEASURE_CNT + 1.5) / (XO_DIV4_TERM_CNT + 3.5) |

### 0x01808008 GCC_GP1_CFG_RCGR

* **Clock**: CLK

#### GCC_GP1_CFG_RCGR Bit Fields

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 13:12 | MODE | This bitfield provides SW selection of MN counter mode.<br>0x3: SINGLE_EDGE (Single-edge.)<br>0x2: DUAL_EDGE (Dual-edge.)<br>0x1: SWALLOW (Swallow.)<br>0x0: BYPASS (Bypass.) |
| 10:8 | SRC_SEL | This bitfield selects clock source that will be used to source the RCG output<br>0x0: SRC0 (CXO.)<br>0x1: SRC1 (GPLL0_MAIN.)<br>0x2: SRC2 (Unused(Grounded).)<br>0x3: SRC3 (Unused(Grounded).)<br>0x4: SRC4 (Unused(Grounded).)<br>0x5: SRC5 (Unused(Grounded).)<br>0x6: SRC6 (Unused(Grounded).)<br>0x7: SRC7 (Unused(Grounded).) |
<!-- page 786 -->

### GCC_GP1_CFG_RCGR (continued)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 4:0 | SRC_DIV | This field defines the integer and half integer portion of the divider setting of the RCG. The value specifies is 2N-1 where N is the divide ratio. For example, if the half integer divide ration is 2.5, the src_div should be set at 00100.<br>0x0: BYPASS (Bypsss.)<br>0x1: DIV1 (Divide by 1.)<br>0x2: DIV1_5 (Divide by 1.5.)<br>0x3: DIV2 (Divide by 2.)<br>0x4: DIV2_5 (Divide by 2.5.)<br>0x5: DIV3 (Divide by 3.)<br>0x6: DIV3_5 (Divide by 3.5.)<br>0x7: DIV4 (Divide by 4.)<br>0x8: DIV4_5 (Divide by 4.5.)<br>0x9: DIV5 (Divide by 5.)<br>0xA: DIV5_5 (Divide by 5.5.)<br>0xB: DIV6 (Divide by 6.)<br>0xC: DIV6_5 (Divide by 6.5.)<br>0xD: DIV7 (Divide by 7.)<br>0xE: DIV7_5 (Divide by 7.5.)<br>0xF: DIV8 (Divide by 8.)<br>0x10: DIV8_5 (Divide by 8.5.)<br>0x11: DIV9 (Divide by 9.)<br>0x12: DIV9_5 (Divide by 9.5.)<br>0x13: DIV10 (Divide by 10.)<br>0x14: DIV10_5 (Divide by 10.5.)<br>0x15: DIV11 (Divide by 11.)<br>0x16: DIV11_5 (Divide by 11.5.)<br>0x17: DIV12 (Divide by 12.)<br>0x18: DIV12_5 (Divide by 12.5.)<br>0x19: DIV13 (Divide by 13.)<br>0x1A: DIV13_5 (Divide by 13.5.)<br>0x1B: DIV14 (Divide by 14.)<br>0x1C: DIV14_5 (Divide by 14.5.)<br>0x1D: DIV15 (Divide by 15.)<br>0x1E: DIV15_5 (Divide by 15.5.)<br>0x1F: DIV16 (Divide by 16.) |

### GCC_CCI_CMD_RCGR (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
