# 5 Core Top CSR

## 5.1 TCSR_TCSR_MUTEX
TCSR mutex

### 5.1.1 TCSR_TCSR_MUTEX
TCSR mutex

#### TCSR_MUTEX_REG_n (0x01905000 + 0x1000 * n, n=[0..31])

**Type:** RW
**Clock:** AHB_CLK
**Reset State:** 0x00000000

The MUTEX_REGn register specifies the information regarding the access status of each of the 32 sections of memory, which is denoted by n. Register contents of 0 imply that the respective section of memory is free to use, and therefore unlocked. Non-zero contents would imply that the respective section of memory is in use, and therefore locked

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 7:0 | MUTEX | Mutex register data |

## 5.2 TCSR_TCSR_REGS
TCSR internal

### 5.2.1 TCSR_TCSR_REGS
TCSR internal
<!-- page 950 -->

### TCSR_MUTEX_REG_RESET (0x01939800)

**Type:** RW
**Clock:** AHB_CLK
**Reset State:** 0x00000000

The MUTEX_REG_RESET register resets the MUTEX_REG_%n% blocks. Software has to assert the reset in order to clear the MUTEX_REGn. The reset bit needs to be de-asserted before SW can write to Mutex registers

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 0 | MUTEX_RESET | 0: deasserts reset<br>1: asserts reset |

### TCSR_TCSR_CLK_EN (0x0193B07C)

**Type:** RW
**Clock:** AHB_CLK
**Reset State:** 0x00000001

This register controls HW clock gating logics in core_top_csr block

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 0 | TCSR_CLK_EN | 0: clock gating logic is enabled. clock to TCSR is turned off when there is no AHB transactions.<br>1: Clock gating logic is disabled. clock to TCSR is always on |

Read Only registers for Oxili debug purpose

Contains the following subfields:<br><br>**[15:11]** Reserved<br><br>**[10:8] USB PORT TYPE**<br>- 3'b000 = SDP (500mA HID Grant)<br>- 3'b001 = DCP<br>- 3'b010 = CDP<br>- 3'b011 = ACA-Dock<br>- 3'b100 = ACA-A<br>- 3'b101 = ACA-B<br>- 3'b110 = ACA-C<br>- 3'b111 = None/Unconfigured<br><br>**[7] ABOVE_WEAK_TH**<br>- 1'b0 = VBAT is below the weak (bootable) threshold<br>- 1'b1 = VBAT is above the weak (bootable) threshold<br><br>**[6:5] CHG_PATH**<br>- 2'b00 = None (PMIC is powered from battery, no valid charger attached)<br>- 2'b01 = USB path charger attached<br>- 2'b10 = DCIN path charger attached<br>- 2'b11 = Both USB and DCIN path chargers are attached<br><br>**[4] SKIP**<br>- 1'b0 = Standard PMIC dual stage PON sequence, primary sequence first<br>- 1'b1 = Single stage PON sequence, includes primary followed by secondary sequence without MSM PMIC PON Handshake required.<br><br>**[3] FLCB_PMIC**<br>- 1'b0 = PMIC is non-FLCB compatible or 3rd party PMIC<br>- 1'b1 = PMIC is FLCB compatible<br><br>**[2] BATTERY_PRESENT** (passed from PMIC PBL_ACCESS1 register)<br>- 1'b0 = No Battery<br>- 1'b1 = Battery is present in the system<br><br>**[1:0] Reserved** |

# 7 EBI1 Physical Layer Configuration

## 7.1 DIM_C00_DDRPHY_CA

### 0x00480000 DIM_C00_DIM_CA_TOP_CFG

- **Type:** RW
- **Clock:** HCLK
- **Reset State:** 0x00000031

The DIM_CA_TOP_CFG register configures the following:

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 24 | CA_LB_MODE_SEL | Selects external or internal loop back mode<br>1'b1: internal loop back mode<br>1'b0: external loop back mode (default) |
| 23 | CA_LB_MODE_EN | Enables external or internal loop back mode<br>1'b1: loop back mode enabled<br>1'b0: loop back mode disabled (default) |
| 22 | RESERVED | Reserved |
| 21 | MISR_DATA_CLK_SEL | selects b/w MISR data or SEED and Loopback clock or FF clock<br>1'b1: reserved<br>1'b0: seed from csr ff clk (default) |
| 20 | IOCAL_CTLR_SEL | Select source of PCNT/NCNT/PNCNT_VALID<br>1'b1: external<br>1'b0: internal (default) |
| 16 | SDR_MODE_EN | 1'b1: Enables SDR mode on address bus<br>1'b0: Enables DDR mode on address bus (default) |
| 8 | RESERVED | Reserved |
<!-- page 997 -->
*(Continuation of DIM_C00_DIM_CA_TOP_CFG)*

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 5 | WR_PIPE_EXTEND1 | Write pipe extend select (when hp_mode = 1'b1)<br>1'b1: with pipe extend (default)<br>1'b0: without pipe extend |
| 4 | WR_PIPE_EXTEND0 | Write pipe extend select (when hp_mode = 1'b0)<br>1'b1: with pipe extend (default)<br>1'b0: without pipe extend |
| 0 | WR_CLK_SEL | Write clock select<br>1'b1: With write CDC (default)<br>1'b0: Bypass write CDC, write clock from cdiv2 phi2 output |

### DIM_D00_DIM_DQ_CDC_CTLR_CFG0

**Address:** `0x00480830`
**Type:** RW
**Clock:** HCLK
**Reset State:** `0x02000000`

The DIM_DQ_CDC_CTLR_CFG0 register configures the following:

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 26 | ERROR_CODE_UPDATE_EN | 1'b1: Enable overwriting (default) the error code for subsequent calibrations.<br>1'b0: Disable overwriting the error code during subsequent calibrations |
| 25 | STAGGER_CAL_ENA | 1'b1: Stagger calibration of write and read CDCs once after the other to reduce peak voltage drop.<br>1'b0: Both write and read CDCs calibrated simultaneously<br>This bit is introduced on the x2 core, so not present on x0 and x1 versions of DIM/PHY. |
| 24 | TRACKING_CAL_ENA | 1'b1: Relationship between subunits and oscillator count is learnt and used for tracking calibration.<br>1'b0: Periodic calibration triggers cause full recalibration |
| 23:20 | OSC_COUNT_ERR_TOLERANCE | Magnitude of the difference between oscillator count and target count when the algorithm assumes convergence and stops further search. |
| 19 | TRACK_CALIB_MODE | 1'b0: Tracking calibration uses previous Target_count value.<br>1'b1 Accurate mode: Target_count is recomputed at the start of tracking calibration |
<!-- page 1025 -->

### DIM_D00_DIM_DQ_CDC_CTLR_CFG0 (continued)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 18 | FULL_DELAY | 1'b0: unitstep and subunit caps are from calibration or SW settings<br>1'b1: All unit step and subunit caps are selected for the delay arrays. |
| 17 | HW_AUTOCAL_ENA | 1'b1: Enables periodic auto calibration<br>1'b0: Periodic calibration is disabled |
| 16 | SW_TRIG_FULL_CALIB | A low to high transition on this register bit triggers the CDC calibration statemachine to initiate full calibration of the standby delay array. Also resets tracking mode for the delay arrays. |
| 13:12 | OSC_PRE_DIV | The factor by which the raw oscillator frequency is divided before being given to the counting logic.<br>2'b00 Divide by 1<br>2'b01 Divide by 2<br>2'b10 Divide by 4<br>2'b11 Divide by 8 |
| 10:0 | TMUX_CHAR | Cchar is a characterized constant equal to the ratio of output mux offset delay to average unit step delay. This register is programmed by multiplying the constant with 1024 and rounding to the nearest integer. E.g. if Cchar = 0.67, RO(0.67 * 1024) = 686, hence program TMUX_CHAR = 11'h2AE |

Hardware waits for explicit acknowledgement of delay array switch from CDC.<br>Others: Explicit acknowledgement mode is disabled and the counter is used |

| 25 | CDC_SWITCH_RC_EN | Enablement of CDC power RC (LPF) switch<br>1'b1: Enabled<br>1'b0: Disabled (default) |
| 24 | CDC_SWITCH_BYPASS_OFF | Enablement of CDC power bypass switch<br>1'b1: Disabled<br>1'b0: Enabled (default) |
| 16 | RCW_EN | Enablement of the Read Capture Window<br>1'b1: Enable the RCW<br>1'b0: Disabled (default) |
| 8 | RESERVED | Reserved |
| 5 | WR_PIPE_EXTEND1 | Write pipe extend select (when hp_mode = 1'b1)<br>1'b1: with pipe extend (default)<br>1'b0: without pipe extend |
| 4 | WR_PIPE_EXTEND0 | Write pipe extend select (when hp_mode = 1'b0)<br>1'b1: with pipe extend (default)<br>1'b0: without pipe extend |

### DIM_D01_DIM_DQ_WR_CDC_STATUS0

Desired delay cannot be realized even when all unit-steps are selected.<br>3'b100: Unit-step underflow<br>3'b101: Unit-step overflow: Overflow during coarse calibration. Estimated unit steps needed to realize the desired delay are greater than the total number of unit-steps in design.<br>Note: The CDC_ERROR_CODE is not a sticky register and is updated after each CDC calibration. |
| 23:16 | SW_REF_GATE_COUNT | Number of reference clock cycles in the software generated oscillation gate window doing SW override mode |
| 15:4 | OSC_COUNT | Current value of oscillator count |
| 3 | CURR_SEL_DA | This bit indicates the current active delay array connected to the output.<br>1'b0: DA0 is selected<br>1'b1: DA1 is selected |
| 2 | CTLR_SM_IDLE | 1'b1 Indicates that the calibration state machine is idle<br>1'b0 indicates calibration statemachine is busy |
| 1 | OSC_DONE | This status register is set after oscillations count is finished by CDC. It gets reset when a new oscillator count is started. |
| 0 | CALIBRATION_DONE | 1'b1 indicates that calibration is done and CURR_SUBUNIT_STEPS, CURR_UNIT_STEPS status registers are valid. |

#### DIM_D02_DIM_DQ_CDC_CTLR_CFG0

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 26 | ERROR_CODE_UPDATE_EN | 1'b1: Enable overwriting (default) the error code for subsequent calibrations.<br>1'b0: Disable overwriting the error code during subsequent calibrations |
| 25 | STAGGER_CAL_ENA | 1'b1: Stagger calibration of write and read CDCs once after the other to reduce peak voltage drop.<br>1'b0: Both write and read CDCs calibrated simultaneously<br>This bit is introduced on the x2 core, so not present on x0 and x1 versions of DIM/PHY. |
| 24 | TRACKING_CAL_ENA | 1'b1: Relationship between subunits and oscillator count is learnt and used for tracking calibration.<br>1'b0: Periodic calibration triggers cause full recalibration |
| 23:20 | OSC_COUNT_ERR_TOLERANCE | Magnitude of the difference between oscillator count and target count when the algorithm assumes convergence and stops further search. |
| 19 | TRACK_CALIB_MODE | 1'b0: Tracking calibration uses previous Target_count value.<br>1'b1 Accurate mode: Target_count is recomputed at the start of tracking calibration |

### DIM_D02_DIM_DQ_CDC_CTLR_CFG0 (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 18 | FULL_DELAY | `1'b0`: unitstep and subunit caps are from calibration or SW settings<br>`1'b1`: All unit step and subunit caps are selected for the delay arrays. |
| 17 | HW_AUTOCAL_ENA | `1'b1`: Enables periodic auto calibration<br>`1'b0`: Periodic calibration is disabled |
| 16 | SW_TRIG_FULL_CALIB | A low to high transition on this register bit triggers the CDC calibration statemachine to initiate full calibration of the standby delay array. Also resets tracking mode for the delay arrays. |
| 13:12 | OSC_PRE_DIV | The factor by which the raw oscillator frequency is divided before being given to the counting logic.<br>`2'b00`: Divide by 1<br>`2'b01`: Divide by 2<br>`2'b10`: Divide by 4<br>`2'b11`: Divide by 8 |
| 10:0 | TMUX_CHAR | Cchar is a characterized constant equal to the ratio of output mux offset delay to average unit step delay. This register is programmed by multiplying the constant with 1024 and rounding to the nearest integer. E.g. if Cchar = 0.67, RO(0.67 * 1024) = 686, hence program TMUX_CHAR = 11'h2AE |

### DIM_D02_DIM_DQ_CDC_CTLR_CFG1

* DIM_DQ_CDC_CTLR_CFG1

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 26:24 | OSC_COUNT_DELAY | Number of oscillator cycles from the end of reference gate signal to assertion of oscillation counter done. Legal values are from 0 to 4. |
| 23:20 | STANDBY_DELAY | This is the number of reference clock cycles from when a newly calibrated delay array is made active to when the current active delay array is put into standby mode.<br>`4'b0`: Disables the counter. Hardware waits for explicit acknowledgement of delay array switch from CDC.<br>Others: Explicit acknowledgement mode is disabled and the counter is used |

| Bits | Name | Description |

| 14:12 | OSC_MODE_DELAY | Number of reference clock cycles between putting a delay array in oscillator mode to starting the oscillation counter. This delay is allowed for the oscillations to stabilize through the delay array. The miniumum allowed value is 1 |
| 10:8 | DECODER_DELAY | Number of reference clock cycles allowed for unitstep and subunit counts to be encoded into the unit and finecap select lines on the DDA. The miniumum allowed value is 1. |

| 29 | DQ_LB_MODE_EN | Enables external or internal loop back mode<br>1'b1: loop back mode enabled<br>1'b0: loop back mode disabled (default) |

| 25 | CDC_SWITCH_RC_EN | Enablement of CDC power RC (LPF) switch<br>1'b1: Enabled<br>1'b0: Disabled (default) |
| 24 | CDC_SWITCH_BYPASS_OFF | Enablement of CDC power bypass switch<br>1'b1: Disabled<br>1'b0: Enabled (default) |
| 16 | RCW_EN | Enablement of the Read Capture Window<br>1'b1: Enable the RCW<br>1'b0: Disabled (default) |
| 8 | RESERVED | Reserved |
| 5 | WR_PIPE_EXTEND1 | Write pipe extend select (when hp_mode = 1'b1)<br>1'b1: with pipe extend (default)<br>1'b0: without pipe extend |
| 4 | WR_PIPE_EXTEND0 | Write pipe extend select (when hp_mode = 1'b0)<br>1'b1: with pipe extend (default)<br>1'b0: without pipe extend |

* **Type**: RW
* **Clock**: HCLK

The DIM_DQ_CDC_CTLR_CFG0 register configures the following:
DIM_DQ_CDC_CTLR_CFG0

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 26 | ERROR_CODE_UPDATE_EN | 1'b1: Enable overwriting (default) the error code for subsequent calibrations.<br>1'b0: Disable overwriting the error code during subsequent calibrations |
| 25 | STAGGER_CAL_ENA | 1'b1: Stagger calibration of write and read CDCs once after the other to reduce peak voltage drop.<br>1'b0: Both write and read CDCs calibrated simultaneously<br>This bit is introduced on the x2 core, so not present on x0 and x1 versions of DIM/PHY. |
| 24 | TRACKING_CAL_ENA | 1'b1: Relationship between subunits and oscillator count is learnt and used for tracking calibration.<br>1'b0: Periodic calibration triggers cause full recalibration |
| 23:20 | OSC_COUNT_ERR_TOLERANCE | Magnitude of the difference between oscillator count and target count when the algorithm assumes convergence and stops further search. |
| 19 | TRACK_CALIB_MODE | 1'b0: Tracking calibration uses previous Target_count value.<br>1'b1 Accurate mode: Target_count is recomputed at the start of tracking calibration |
<!-- page 1094 -->
### DIM_D03_DIM_DQ_CDC_CTLR_CFG0 (continued)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 18 | FULL_DELAY | 1'b0: unitstep and subunit caps are from calibration or SW settings<br>1'b1: All unit step and subunit caps are selected for the delay arrays. |
| 17 | HW_AUTOCAL_ENA | 1'b1: Enables periodic auto calibration<br>1'b0: Periodic calibration is disabled |
| 16 | SW_TRIG_FULL_CALIB | A low to high transition on this register bit triggers the CDC calibration statemachine to initiate full calibration of the standby delay array. Also resets tracking mode for the delay arrays. |
| 13:12 | OSC_PRE_DIV | The factor by which the raw oscillator frequency is divided before being given to the counting logic.<br>2'b00 Divide by 1<br>2'b01 Divide by 2<br>2'b10 Divide by 4<br>2'b11 Divide by 8 |
| 10:0 | TMUX_CHAR | Cchar is a characterized constant equal to the ratio of output mux offset delay to average unit step delay. This register is programmed by multiplying the constant with 1024 and rounding to the nearest integer. E.g. if Cchar = 0.67, RO(0.67 * 1024) = 686, hence program TMUX_CHAR = 11'h2AE |

## 7.7 EBI1_AHB2PHY_BROADCAST
AHB2PHY Broadcast Address Space

### 7.7.1 EBI1_AHB2PHY_BROADCAST
AHB2PHY Broadcast Address Space
<!-- page 1112 -->

### 0x0049F800 + 0x4*n: EBI1_AHB2PHY_BROADCAST_ADDRESS_SPACE_n, n=[0..255]

**Type:** RW  
**Clock:** hclk  
**Reset State:** 0x00000000  

A write or read access to this space activates all PHY chip selects that have their broadcast enable bit set to a 1.

#### EBI1_AHB2PHY_BROADCAST_ADDRESS_SPACE_n

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:0 | BROADCAST_SPACE | The entire 1 kB address space for this slave chip select is dedicated to the Broadcast function. If a write or read access is performed in this address space the chip selects of all PHY slaves that have been enabled will be active during the access. A PHY slave is enabled for broadcast by setting the BROADCAST_EN bit in the AHB2PHY_BROADCAST_EN_CFG register. Each PHY slave has a dedicated bit in this register. |

QTMR AC Block

### 0x0B020000 APCS_QTMR_AC_CNTFRQ

**Type:** RW  
**Clock:** SYS_AHB_CLK  
**Reset State:** 0x00000000  
**Security Treatment:** Restricted  

Counter Frequency register.Counter frequency in ticks per second

#### APCS_QTMR_AC_CNTFRQ

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:0 | CNTFRQ | |

### 0x0B020004 APCS_QTMR_AC_CNTSR

**Type:** RW  
**Clock:** SYS_AHB_CLK  
**Reset State:** 0x00000000  
**Security Treatment:** Restricted  

The Counter Secure Register (CNTSR) contains a bit for Secure access to each timer frame, including both views of the timer frame and the access to the associated CNTACR and CNTVOFF registers in the Access Control region.
<!-- page 1114 -->

#### APCS_QTMR_AC_CNTSR (continued)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 6:0 | NSN | Non-secure access to frame N. N lies from 0 to $NUM_FRAME-1 (# of configured frame)<br>0x0: SECURE_ONLY (Secure access only - non-secure access is RAZ/WI)<br>0x1: SECURE_OR_NONSECURE (Secure or Non-secure access) |

### 0x0B020008 APCS_QTMR_AC_CNTTID

**Type:** R  
**Clock:** SYS_AHB_CLK  
**Reset State:** 0x00000000  
**Security Treatment:** Both  

The Counter Timer ID (CNTTID) is 32-bit register that identifies the number of timer frames implemented, which frame have virtual offsets and timers, and which frames have second views

#### APCS_QTMR_AC_CNTTID

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:28 | F7_CFG | Frame 7 configuration (same definition as Frame 0) |
| 27:24 | F6_CFG | Frame 6 configuration (same definition as Frame 0) |
| 23:20 | F5_CFG | Frame 5 configuration (same definition as Frame 0) |
| 19:16 | F4_CFG | Frame 4 configuration (same definition as Frame 0) |
| 15:12 | F3_CFG | Frame 3 configuration (same definition as Frame 0) |
| 11:8 | F2_CFG | Frame 2 configuration (same definition as Frame 0) |
| 7:4 | F1_CFG | Frame 1 configuration (same definition as Frame 0) |
| 3:0 | F0_CFG | Frame 0 configuration<br>0x3: RSVD (Reserved (Read as zero))<br>0x2: FPLO (Frame has second view)<br>0x1: FVI (Virtual frame implemented)<br>0x0: FI (Frame implemented) |

### 0x0B020040 + 0x4*n: APCS_QTMR_AC_CNTACR_n, n=[0..6]

**Type:** RW  
**Clock:** SYS_AHB_CLK  
**Reset State:** 0x00000000  
**Security Treatment:** Controlled by QTMR_AC_CNTSR[n]
<!-- page 1115 -->

#### APCS_QTMR_AC_CNTACR_n (continued)

The Counter Access Control Register (CNTACR) provide access control to the individual elements of timer frame n, including the second view of that timer frame n

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 5 | RWPT | Read/Write access to CNTP_*register<br>0x0: ACCESS_DENIED (Access denied)<br>0x1: ACCESS_ALLOWED (Access allowed) |
| 4 | RWVT | Read/Write access to CNTV_*register<br>0x0: ACCESS_DENIED (Access denied)<br>0x1: ACCESS_ALLOWED (Access allowed) |
| 3 | RVOFF | Read access to CNTVOFF register<br>0x0: ACCESS_DENIED (Access denied)<br>0x1: ACCESS_ALLOWED (Access allowed) |
| 2 | RFRQ | Read access to CNTFRQ register<br>0x0: ACCESS_DENIED (Access denied)<br>0x1: ACCESS_ALLOWED (Access allowed) |
| 1 | RPVCT | Read access to CNTVCT register<br>0x0: ACCESS_DENIED (Access denied)<br>0x1: ACCESS_ALLOWED (Access allowed) |
| 0 | RPCT | Read access to CNTPCT register<br>0x0: ACCESS_DENIED (Access denied)<br>0x1: ACCESS_ALLOWED (Access allowed) |

## APCS_F0_QTMR_V1_CNTV_TVAL (0x0B021038)

**Type:** RW  
**Clock:** SYS_TMR_CLK  
**Reset State:** 0x00000000  
**Security Treatment:** Controlled by QTMR_AC_CNTACR_n[RWVT]

An alternative 32 bit TVAL view to provide read or write CVAL register.

The TVAL reads:
$$\text{TVAL} = (\text{CVAL} - (\text{CNTP} - \text{CNTVOFF}))$$

The TVAL write CVAL with:
$$\text{CVAL} = (\text{CNTP} - \text{CNTVOFF}) + \text{signExtend}(\text{TVAL})$$

This register is implemented if FVI (Virtual Frame implemented) for the Frame n is set in QTMR_AC_CNTTID register.

### APCS_F0_QTMR_V1_CNTV_TVAL Bits

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:0 | CNTV_TVAL | Timer Value in tick per second for Frame |

**Clock:** SYS_TMR_CLK  
**Reset State:** 0x00000000  
**Security Treatment:** Controlled by QTMR_AC_CNTACR_n[RWVT]

The Virtual Timer Control Register which can disable the timer and can mask its interrupt. If the timer is disabled, interrupt are masked, but the timer value continue to count down.

This register is implemented if FVI (Virtual Frame implemented) for the Frame n is set in QTMR_AC_CNTTID register.

### APCS_F0_QTMR_V1_CNTV_CTL Bits

| Bits | Name | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 2 | ISTAT | R | Interrupt Status before masking (Read Only)<br>0x0: INTERRUPT_NOT_PENDING<br>0x1: INTERRUPT_PENDING |
<!-- page 1123 -->
## APCS_F0_QTMR_V1_CNTV_CTL (cont.)

- **Type**: RW
- **Clock**: SYS_TMR_CLK
- **Reset State**: `0x00000000`
- **Security Treatment**: Controlled by `QTMR_AC_CNTACR_n[RWVT]`

An alternative 32 bit TVAL view to provide read or write CVAL register.

The TVAL reads:
`TVAL = (CVAL - (CNTP - CNTVOFF)`

The TVAL write CVAL with:
`CVAL = (CNTP - CNTVOFF) + signExtend(TVAL)`

This register is implemented if FVI (Virtual Frame implemented) for the Frame n is set in QTMR_AC_CNTTID register.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |

### 0x0B02303C APCS_F1_QTMR_V1_CNTV_CTL

- **Type**: RW
- **Clock**: SYS_TMR_CLK
- **Reset State**: `0x00000000`
- **Security Treatment**: Controlled by `QTMR_AC_CNTACR_n[RWVT]`

The Virtual Timer Control Register which can disable the timer and can mask its interrupt. If the timer is disabled, interrupt are masked, but the timer value continue to count down.

This register is implemented if FVI (Virtual Frame implemented) for the Frame n is set in QTMR_AC_CNTTID register.

#### APCS_F1_QTMR_V1_CNTV_CTL
| Bits | Name | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 2 | ISTAT | R | Interrupt Status before masking (Read Only)<br>0x0: INTERRUPT_NOT_PENDING<br>0x1: INTERRUPT_PENDING |
| 1 | IMSK | RW | Mask Interrupt<br>0x0: UNMASK_INTERRUPT<br>0x1: MASK_INTERRUPT |
| 0 | EN | RW | Enable Timer<br>0x0: DISABLED<br>0x1: ENABLED |

| 0 | EN | RW | Enable Timer<br>- 0x0: DISABLED<br>- 0x1: ENABLED |

* **Reset State:** `0x00000000`
* **Security Treatment:** Controlled by `QTMR_AC_CNTACR_n[RWVT]`

The Virtual Timer Compare Value register is compare against the `CNTVCT` counter. The interrupt signal is asserted when the `CNTVCT` counter is greater than equal to `CNTV_CVAL`. This register is implemented if FVI (Virtual Frame implemented) for the Frame n is set in
<!-- page 1168 -->
`QTMR_AC_CNTTID` register.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 23:0 | CNTV_CVAL_HI | Higher bits [31:0] of compare value for interrupt for Frame n |

---

## APCS_F6_QTMR_V1_CNTV_TVAL (0x0B028038)

* **Type:** RW
* **Clock:** `SYS_TMR_CLK`
* **Reset State:** `0x00000000`
* **Security Treatment:** Controlled by `QTMR_AC_CNTACR_n[RWVT]`

An alternative 32 bit TVAL view to provide read or write CVAL register.

The TVAL reads:
$$\text{TVAL} = \text{CVAL} - (\text{CNTP} - \text{CNTVOFF})$$

The TVAL write CVAL with:
$$\text{CVAL} = (\text{CNTP} - \text{CNTVOFF}) + \text{signExtend}(\text{TVAL})$$

This register is implemented if FVI (Virtual Frame implemented) for the Frame n is set in `QTMR_AC_CNTTID` register.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:0 | CNTV_TVAL | Timer Value in tick per second for Frame |

---

## APCS_F6_QTMR_V1_CNTV_CTL (0x0B02803C)

* **Type:** RW
* **Clock:** `SYS_TMR_CLK`
* **Reset State:** `0x00000000`
* **Security Treatment:** Controlled by `QTMR_AC_CNTACR_n[RWVT]`

The Virtual Timer Control Register which can disable the timer and can mask its interrupt. If the timer is disabled, interrupt are masked, but the timer value continue to count down.

This register is implemented if FVI (Virtual Frame implemented) for the Frame n is set in `QTMR_AC_CNTTID` register.
<!-- page 1169 -->
| Bits | Name | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 2 | ISTAT | R | Interrupt Status before masking (Read Only)<br/>0x0: INTERRUPT_NOT_PENDING<br/>0x1: INTERRUPT_PENDING |
| 1 | IMSK | RW | Mask Interrupt<br/>0x0: UNMASK_INTERRUPT<br/>0x1: MASK_INTERRUPT |
| 0 | EN | RW | Enable Timer<br/>0x0: DISABLED<br/>0x1: ENABLED |

---

## 8.11 APCS_KPSS_WDT

### APCS_WDOG_SECURE
**Address:** `0x0B017000`
- **Type:** RW
- **Clock:** SYS_AHB_CLK
- **Reset State:** `0x00000001`
- **Security Treatment:** Restricted

The WDOG_SECURE register is used to enable or disable non-secure bus transactions. The bus security status is signaled by APROTNS pin. When APROTNS is set to '0' the state of the APCS_WDTSECURE register is not considered - a secure transaction is always allowed. When APROTNS is set to '1', the APCS_WDTSECURE register's SECURE bit must be '1' for access to be granted. If the SECURE bit is set to '0', the non-secure (APROTNS = '1') transactions are denied. When access is denied, a write is ignored, and a read will return '0'. No error is signaled.

When reading the APCS_WDTSECURE register, non secure agents will always read '0'. Secure agents will see the actual value of the register. The same is true for the registers or bits each bit in the APCS_WDTSECURE register correspond to.
<!-- page 1173 -->

### APCS_WDOG_SECURE (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 0 | WDT | Controls security treatment for the Watch Dog Timer registers: WDOG_RESET, WDOG_CTL, WDOG_STATUS, WDOG_BARK_TIME, WDOG_BITE_TIME, WDOG_TEST_LOAD_STATUS, WDOG_TEST_LOAD, WDOG_TEST.<br>0x1: NSEC (Non-secure)<br>0x0: SEC (Secure) |

---

### APCS_WDOG_RESET
**Address:** `0x0B017004`
- **Type:** W
- **Clock:** SYS_AHB_CLK
- **Reset State:** `0x00000000`
- **Security Treatment:** Controlled by WDOG_SECURE [WDT]

The WDOG_RESET register resets the watch dog counter. In normal operation, the microprocessor should periodically write this command register to reset the watch dog counter. This command register also disables the watchdog freeze.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 0 | RESET | This bit generates the WDT_STB during the non-sleep mode. A pulse is generated on WDT_STB when this bit is written with a '1'. |

---

### APCS_WDOG_CTL
**Address:** `0x0B017008`
- **Type:** W
- **Clock:** SYS_AHB_CLK
- **Reset State:** `0x00000000`
- **Security Treatment:** Controlled by WDOG_SECURE [WDT]

The WDOG_CTL register controls when the watch dog timer is enabled.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1 | UNMASKED_INT_ENABLE | Enable unmasked interrupt (IRQ or FIQ) to wake up the wdog timer:<br>0x1: ENABLE (Enable)<br>0x0: DISABLE (Disable) |
<!-- page 1174 -->

### APCS_WDOG_CTL (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 0 | ENABLE | Enable wdog timer:<br>0x1: ENABLE (Enable)<br>0x0: DISABLE (Disable) |

---

### APCS_WDOG_STATUS
**Address:** `0x0B01700C`
- **Type:** R
- **Clock:** SYS_AHB_CLK
- **Reset State:** `0x00000000`
- **Security Treatment:** Controlled by WDOG_SECURE [WDT]

The WDOG_STATUS register is the watchdog status register.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31 | FROZEN | This bit indicates whether the or not wdog timer is frozen at count 0.<br>0x1: YES (frozen)<br>0x0: NO (not frozen) |
| 20:1 | COUNT | Counter value [19:0] of the watch dog counter.<br>Note: The sleep counter value is sampled using the AHB clk. Multiple reads are required to determine the value (assuming AHB clk is much faster than sleep clock). |
| 0 | EXPIRED_STATUS | 0x1: YES (expired (wdog timer has expired))<br>0x0: NO (not expired (wdog timer has not expired) |

---

### APCS_WDOG_BARK_TIME
**Address:** `0x0B017010`
- **Type:** RW
- **Clock:** SYS_AHB_CLK
- **Reset State:** `0x0007FFFF`
- **Security Treatment:** Controlled by WDOG_SECURE [WDT]

The WDOG_BARK_TIME register defines the time in sleep_clk when to assert the watchdog ('bark') interrupts. The value can be between 0 and 12787 (the time when the watchdog times out). The default value is 0x3FFF, but this reset value is not readable through the AHB interface. Note that this value is larger than the watchdog timeout of 0x31F3, effectively disabling the watchdog ('bark') interrupt.
<!-- page 1175 -->

### APCS_WDOG_BARK_TIME (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 19:0 | DATA | The WDOG counter value on which to trigger the bark interrupt. |

---

### APCS_WDOG_BITE_TIME
**Address:** `0x0B017014`
- **Type:** RW
- **Clock:** SYS_AHB_CLK
- **Reset State:** `0x000FFFFF`
- **Security Treatment:** Controlled by WDOG_SECURE [WDT]

The WDOG_BITE_TIME register defines the time in sleep_clk when to assert the watchdog ('bark') interrupts. The value can be between 0 and 12787 (the time when the watchdog times out). The default value is 0x3FFF, but this reset value is not readable through the AHB interface. Note that this value is larger than the watchdog timeout of 0x31F3, effectively disabling the watchdog ('bark') interrupt.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 19:0 | DATA | The WDOG bite expiration time [19:0]. |

---

## 8.13 APCS_L2_SAW2

### APCS_L2_SAW2_SECURE
**Address:** `0x0B012000`
- **Type:** RW
- **Clock:** sys_ref_clk
- **Reset State:** `0x00000007`
- **Security Treatment:** Restricted
<!-- page 1179 -->

### APCS_L2_SAW2_SECURE (cont.)

The SAW2_SECURE register is used to enable or disable non-secure bus transactions. The bus security status is signaled by ahb_saw_hprotns pin. When ahb_saw_hprotns is set to '0' the state of the SAW2_SECURE register is not considered - a secure transaction is always allowed. When ahb_saw_hprotns is set to '1', the SAW2_SECURE register security treatment bit of that register must be '1' for access to be granted. If the security treatment bit of the register is set to '0', the non-secure (ahb_saw_hprotns = '1') transactions are denied. When access is denied, a write is ignored, and a read will return '0'. No error is signaled.

When reading the SAW2_SECURE register, non secure agents will always read '0'. Secure agents will see the actual value of the register. The reset value is controlled by CFGNSINIT input pin.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 2 | SAW_CTL | Controls security treatment for SAW2 registers: SAW2_ID, SAW2_CFG, SAW2_STS_0, SAW2_STS_1, SAW2_RST, SAW2_VERSION.<br>0x1: NSEC (Non-secure)<br>0x0: SEC (Secure) |
| 1 | PWR_CTL | Controls security treatment for SPM registers: SAW2_SPM_CTL, SAW2_SPM_PMIC_DLY, SAW2_SPM_PMIC_DATA_0, SAW2_SPM_PMIC_DATA_1, SAW2_SPM_SLP_SEQ_ENTRY_n.<br>0x1: NSEC (Non-secure)<br>0x0: SEC (Secure) |
| 0 | VLT_CTL | 0x1: NSEC (Non-secure)<br>0x0: SEC (Secure) |

---

## 8.14 APCS_BANKED_SAW2

### 0x0B009000 APCS_BANKED_SAW2_SECURE

* **Type**: RW
* **Clock**: sys_ref_clk
* **Reset State**: 0x00000000
* **Security Treatment**: Restricted

The SAW2_SECURE register is used to enable or disable non-secure bus transactions. The bus security status is signaled by ahb_saw_hprotns pin. When ahb_saw_hprotns is set to '0' the state of the SAW2_SECURE register is not considered - a secure transaction is always allowed. When ahb_saw_hprotns is set to '1', the SAW2_SECURE register security treatment bit of that register must be '1' for access to be granted. If the security treatment bit of the register is set to '0', the non-secure (ahb_saw_hprotns = '1') transactions are denied. When access is denied, a write is ignored, and a read will return '0'. No error is signaled.

When reading the SAW2_SECURE register, non secure agents will always read '0'. Secure agents will see the actual value of the register. The reset value is controlled by CFGNSINIT input pin.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 2 | SAW_CTL | 0x1: NSEC (NSEC)<br>0x0: SEC (SEC)<br>Controls security treatment for SAW2 registers: SAW2_ID, SAW2_CFG, SAW2_STS_0, SAW2_STS_1, SAW2_RST, SAW2_VERSION) |
<!-- page 1186 -->
### APCS_BANKED_SAW2_SECURE (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1 | PWR_CTL | 0x1: NSEC (NSEC)<br>0x0: SEC (SEC)<br>Controls security treatment for SPM registers: SAW2_SPM_CTL, SAW2_SPM_PMIC_DLY, SAW2_SPM_PMIC_DATA_0, SAW2_SPM_PMIC_DATA_1, SAW2_SPM_SLP_SEQ_ENTRY_n) |
| 0 | VLT_CTL | 0x1: NSEC (NSEC)<br>0x0: SEC (SEC) |

## 8.16 APCS_ALIAS1_SAW2

### 0x0B099000 APCS_ALIAS1_SAW2_SECURE

* **Type:** RW
* **Clock:** sys_ref_clk
* **Reset State:** 0x00000000
* **Security Treatment:** Restricted

The SAW2_SECURE register is used to enable or disable non-secure bus transactions. The bus security status is signaled by ahb_saw_hprotns pin. When ahb_saw_hprotns is set to '0' the state of the SAW2_SECURE register is not considered - a secure transaction is always allowed. When ahb_saw_hprotns is set to '1', the SAW2_SECURE register security treatment bit of that register must be '1' for access to be granted. If the security treatment bit of the register is set to '0', the non-secure (ahb_saw_hprotns = '1') transactions are denied. When access is denied, a write is ignored, and a read will return '0'. No error is signaled.

When reading the SAW2_SECURE register, non secure agents will always read '0'. Secure agents will see the actual value of the register. The reset value is controlled by CFGNSINIT input pin.

**APCS_ALIAS1_SAW2_SECURE**

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 2 | SAW_CTL | 0x1: NSEC (NSEC)<br>0x0: SEC (SEC)<br>Controls security treatment for SAW2 registers: SAW2_ID, SAW2_CFG, SAW2_STS_0, SAW2_STS_1, SAW2_RST, SAW2_VERSION |
| 1 | PWR_CTL | 0x1: NSEC (NSEC)<br>0x0: SEC (SEC)<br>Controls security treatment for SPM registers: SAW2_SPM_CTL, SAW2_SPM_PMIC_DLY, SAW2_SPM_PMIC_DATA_0, SAW2_SPM_PMIC_DATA_1, SAW2_SPM_SLP_SEQ_ENTRY_n |
| 0 | VLT_CTL | 0x1: NSEC (NSEC)<br>0x0: SEC (SEC) |

## 8.19 APCS_KPSS_GLB

### 0x0B011000 APCS_GLB_SECURE

* **Type:** RW
* **Clock:** SYS_AHB_CLK
* **Reset State:** 0x0000001F
* **Security Treatment:** Restricted

The GLB_SECURE register is used to enable or disable non-secure bus transactions. The bus security status is signaled by A53SS's APROTNS pin. When APROTNS is set to '0' the state of the GLB_SECURE register is not considered - a secure transaction is always allowed. When APROTNS is set to '1', the GLB_SECURE register's SECURE bit must be '1' for access to be granted. If the SECURE bit is set to '0', the non-secure (APROTNS = '1') transactions are denied. When access is denied, a write is ignored, and a read will return '0'. No error is signaled.

When reading the GLB_SECURE register, non secure agents will always read '0'. Secure agents will see the actual value of the register. The same is true for the registers or bits each bit in the GLB_SECURE register correspond to.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 4 | VOTE | Controls security treatment for SPM Vote registers: L2_SPM_VOTE_HLOS<br>0x0: SEC<br>0x1: NSEC |
| 3 | ACP | Controls security treatment for ACP related registers: AINACTS_CNT, MISC_PWR_CTL, MISC_PWR_STS<br>0x0: SEC<br>0x1: NSEC |
| 2 | RESERVED | Reserved |
| 1 | PWR | Controls security treatment for the global sleep control registers: L2_PWR_CTL, L2_PWR_STATUS, DBG_PWR_CTL<br>0x0: SEC<br>0x1: NSEC |
| 0 | STS | Controls security treatment for the global clock control registers: PWR_CTL_OVERRIDE, GLB_CLK_STATUS, APCS_L2_AUX_CLK_SEL<br>0x0: SEC<br>0x1: NSEC |
<!-- page 1215 -->

### APCS_PWR_CTL_OVERRIDE (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 22 | PRESETDBG | When Set, this bit drives PRESETDBGn signal ZERO |
| 21:18 | L1_RAM_COLLAPSE_DIS | When Set, this bit will override the L1 RAM collapse operation by SPM. Instead the L1 rams will be retained in the case where APC voltage is retained |
| 17 | SCU_RAM_COLLAPSE_DIS | When Set, this bit will override the SCU RAM collapse operation by SPM. Instead the SCU rams will be retained in the case where APC voltage is retained |
| 16 | L2_RET_SLP_DIS | When set, this bit will take L2 array out of retention mode. This bit needs to be set before the vdd_mx voltage is lowered. The L2 data will be lost if vdd_mx is lowered to a voltage level such that the internal array voltage is below the retention voltage. |
| 4:0 | CLK_EN | Clock enables for global APCS clocks. This is only to workaround hardware dynamic clock gating problems.<br>0x0: DYNAMICALLY_ENABLED_BY_HARDWARE (dynamically enabled by hardware)<br>0x1: ALWAYS_ENABLED (Always enabled)<br>[5] = SYS_apcsL2Aux_Clk<br>[4] = SYS_apccL2Pll_Clk<br>[3] = SYS_apcsPiSleep_Clk<br>[2] = SYS_apcsRef_Clk<br>[1] = SYS_apcsAhb_Clk<br>[0] = SYS_apcsQsb_Clk |

| 10 | L2_HS_RST | When set, this bit asserts reset to the headswitched L2 logic |
| 9 | L2_HS_EN | When set, this bit closes the switches for the headswitched L2 logic, putting it into an operational state |
| 8 | L2_HS_CLAMP | When set, this bit clamps the outputs from the headswitched L2 logic into the unswitched domain This bit is ORed with SAW outputs before passing to the CPU(resets to 1). |

### APCS_L2_PWR_CTL (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 3:0 | L2_ARRAY_HS | When set, these bits closes the array head switches for 512 KB sections of the L2 cache array. When clear (default reset value), array head switch is open, resulting a lower cache array leakage when data does not need to be retained in the array. This bits is ORed with SAW outputs before passing to the CPU |

## 8.20 APCS_KPSS_CFG

### 0x0B010000 APCS_CFG_SECURE

**Type:** RW  
**Clock:** SYS_AHB_CLK  
**Reset State:** 0x00000001  
**Security Treatment:** Restricted  

The CFG_SECURE register is used to enable or disable non-secure bus transactions. The bus security status is signaled by A53SS's APROTNS pin. When APROTNS is set to '0' the state of the CFG_SECURE register is not considered - a secure transaction is always allowed. When APROTNS is set to '1', the CFG_SECURE register's SECURE bit must be '1' for access to be granted. If the SECURE bit is set to '0', the non-secure (APROTNS = '1') transactions are denied. When access is denied, a write is ignored, and a read will return '0'. No error is signaled.

When reading the CFG_SECURE register, non secure agents will always read '0'. Secure agents will see the actual value of the register. The same is true for the registers or bits each bit in the APCS_GCCSECURE register correspond to.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 0 | GLB_CTL | 0x1: NSEC (NSEC)<br>0x0: SEC (SEC)<br>Controls security treatment for the global control registers: START_ADDR. |

### 0x0B010004 APCS_BOOT_START_ADDR_SEC

**Type:** RW  
**Clock:** SYS_AHB_CLK  
**Reset State:** 0x00100005  
**Security Treatment:** Controlled by CFG_SECURE[CFG_CTL].

The BOOT_START_ADDR_SEC register is used to determine the address to boot from in secure mode. It resets to the value on SYS_apcsCFGRSTADDR[31:16].Reset by SYS_apcsSYSPor_Ares|SYS_apcsSys_Ares

| 1 | VINITHI | 0 = starts exceptions vectors at address 0x00000000<br>1 = starts exception vectors at address 0xFFFF0000 |
| 0 | REMAP_EN | Enable remapping |

| 0 | REMAP_EN | RW | Enable remapping |

## 8.21 APCS_BANKED_KPSS_ACS

### 0x0B008000 APCS_BANKED_APC_SECURE

**Type:** RW  
**Clock:** SYS_AHB_CLK  
**Reset State:** 0x0000000F  
**Security Treatment:** Restricted  

The APC_SECURE register is used to enable or disable non-secure bus transactions. The bus security status is signaled by A53SS's APROTNS pin. When APROTNS is set to '0' the state of the APC_SECURE register is not considered - a secure transaction is always allowed. When APROTNS is set to '1', the APC_SECURE register's SECURE bit must be '1' for access to be granted. If the SECURE bit is set to '0', the non-secure (APROTNS = '1') transactions are denied. When access is denied, a write is ignored, and a read will return '0'. No error is signaled.

When reading the APC_SECURE register, non secure agents will always read '0'. Secure agents will see the actual value of the register. The same is true for the registers or bits each bit in the APC_SECURE register correspond to.
<!-- page 1234 -->

### APCS_BANKED_APC_SECURE (Continued)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 3 | VOTE | Secure bit for SPM Voting by HLOS.<br>0x1: NSEC (NSEC)<br>0x0: SEC (SEC)<br>Controls security treatment for SPM Vote registers: SPM_VOTE_HLOS |
| 2 | RESERVED | Reserved |
| 1 | CLK_CTL | 0x1: NSEC (NSEC)<br>0x0: SEC (SEC)<br>Controls security treatment for the sleep control registers: APC_PWR_STATUS, APC_PWR_GATE_STATUS |
| 0 | SLP_CTL | 0x1: NSEC (NSEC)<br>0x0: SEC (SEC)<br>Controls security treatment for the clock control registers: CPU_PWR_CTL, CPU_TRGTD_DBG_RST, APC_PWR_GATE_CTL, APC_A53_CFG_STS |

### 0x0B008004 APCS_BANKED_CPU_PWR_CTL

**Type:** RW  
**Clock:** SYS_AHB_CLK  
**Reset State:** 0x00000088  
**Security Treatment:** Controlled by APC_SECURE [SLP_CTL].

The CPU_PWR_CTL register is used to control the clamps, reset and array head switches.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 16 | CLK_EN | Clock enables for CORE clock. This is only to workaround hardware dynamic clock gating problems.<br>0x1: ALWAYS_ENABLED (Always enabled)<br>0x0: DYNAMICALLY_ENABLED_BY_HARDWARE (dynamically enabled by hardware [20:18]= SYS_apcNAux_Clk[3:1] [17] = SYS_apcsRef_Clk [16] = SYS_apcNPll_Clk) |
| 10 | CORE_SLEEP_STATE | Report that the CPU is in sleep state |
| 7 | CORE_PWRD_UP | Report that the CPU is powered up. |
<!-- page 1235 -->

### APCS_BANKED_CPU_PWR_CTL (Continued)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 6 | GATE_CLK | When set, this bit forces the CPU clock to be gated off. This control is intended to permit external masters such as the RPM to gate off the CPU clock during sleep modes, when power control is being done by an external master instead of the SPM. The output of this register bit is ORed with a clock gating control output from the SPM, so that if either the SPM asserts the control, or the RPM sets this bit, the CPU clock will be gated off.<br>When set, this bit gate the CPU clock that must be asserted during sleep state. This bit is ORed with a SAW output before passing to the CPU core. |
| 5 | COREPOR_RST | When set, this bit asserts corepor areset to the CPU core. |
| 4 | CORE_RST | When set, this bit asserts core areset to the COPU core. |
| 3 | CORE_MEM_HS | When cleared, this bit opens a head switch to put the Core Memories into a low-leakage, non-data-retaining state. This bit is ORed with a SAW output before passing to the CPU core. |
| 2 | L1_RST_DIS | When set, this bit disables L1 initialization during low power mode exit |
| 1 | CORE_MEM_CLAMP | When set this bit clamps the output from the headswitch Core Memories. This bit is OR'ed with saw outputs before passing to the Core Memories |
| 0 | CLAMP | When set, this bit asserts the clamp signal that must be asserted prior to collapsing CPU voltage, vdd_apc0. This bit is ORed with SAW output before passing to the CPU core. |

The APC_SECURE register is used to enable or disable non-secure bus transactions. The bus security status is signaled by A53SS's APROTNS pin. When APROTNS is set to '0' the state of the APC_SECURE register is not considered - a secure transaction is always allowed. When APROTNS is set to '1', the APC_SECURE register's SECURE bit must be '1' for access to be
<!-- page 1240 -->

### APCS_ALIAS0_APC_SECURE (Continued)

granted. If the SECURE bit is set to '0', the non-secure (APROTNS = '1') transactions are denied. When access is denied, a write is ignored, and a read will return '0'. No error is signaled.

When reading the APC_SECURE register, non secure agents will always read '0'. Secure agents will see the actual value of the register. The same is true for the registers or bits each bit in the APC_SECURE register correspond to.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 3 | VOTE | Secure bit for SPM Voting by HLOS.<br>0x1: NSEC (NSEC)<br>0x0: SEC (SEC)<br>Controls security treatment for SPM Vote registers: SPM_VOTE_HLOS |
| 2 | RESERVED | Reserved |
| 1 | CLK_CTL | 0x1: NSEC (NSEC)<br>0x0: SEC (SEC)<br>Controls security treatment for the sleep control registers: APC_PWR_STATUS, APC_PWR_GATE_STATUS |
| 0 | SLP_CTL | 0x1: NSEC (NSEC)<br>0x0: SEC (SEC)<br>Controls security treatment for the clock control registers: CPU_PWR_CTL, CPU_TRGTD_DBG_RST, APC_PWR_GATE_CTL, APC_A53_CFG_STS |

The CPU_PWR_CTL register is used to control the clamps, reset and array head switches.


<!-- page 1241 -->
### APCS_ALIAS0_CPU_PWR_CTL (Continued)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 16 | CLK_EN | Clock enables for CORE clock. This is only to workaround hardware dynamic clock gating problems.<br>0x1: ALWAYS_ENABLED (Always enabled)<br>0x0: DYNAMICALLY_ENABLED_BY_HARDWARE (dynamically enabled by hardware [20:18]= SYS_apcNAux_Clk[3:1], [17] = SYS_apcsRef_Clk, [16] = SYS_apcNPll_Clk) |
| 10 | CORE_SLEEP_STATE | Report that the CPU is in sleep state |
| 7 | CORE_PWRD_UP | Report that the CPU is powered up. |
| 6 | GATE_CLK | When set, this bit forces the CPU clock to be gated off. This control is intended to permit external masters such as the RPM to gate off the CPU clock during sleep modes, when power control is being done by an external master instead of the SPM. The output of this register bit is ORed with a clock gating control output from the SPM, so that if either the SPM asserts the control, or the RPM sets this bit, the CPU clock will be gated off.<br>When set, this bit gate the CPU clock that must be asserted during sleep state. This bit is ORed with a SAW output before passing to the CPU core. |
| 5 | COREPOR_RST | When set, this bit asserts corepor areset to the CPU core. |
| 4 | CORE_RST | When set, this bit asserts core areset to the COPU core. |
| 3 | CORE_MEM_HS | When cleared, this bit opens a head switch to put the Core Memories into a low-leakage, non-data-retaining state. This bit is ORed with a SAW output before passing to the CPU core. |
| 2 | L1_RST_DIS | When set, this bit disables L1 initialization during low power mode exit |
| 1 | CORE_MEM_CLAMP | When set this bit clamps the output from the headswitch Core Memories. This bit is OR'ed with saw outputs before passing to the Core Memories |
| 0 | CLAMP | When set, this bit asserts the clamp signal that must be asserted prior to collapsing CPU voltage, vdd_apc0. This bit is ORed with SAW output before passing to the CPU core. |

The output of this register bit is ORed with a clock gating control output from the SPM, so that if either the SPM asserts the control, or the RPM sets this bit, the CPU clock will be gated off. <br>When set, this bit gate the CPU clock that must be asserted during sleep state. This bit is ORed with a SAW output before passing to the CPU core. |
| 5 | COREPOR_RST | When set, this bit asserts corepor areset to the CPU core. |
| 4 | CORE_RST | When set, this bit asserts core areset to the COPU core. |
| 3 | CORE_MEM_HS | When cleared, this bit opens a head switch to put the Core Memories into a low-leakage, non-data-retaining state. This bit is ORed with a SAW output before passing to the CPU core. |
| 2 | L1_RST_DIS | When set, this bit disables L1 initialization during low power mode exit |
| 1 | CORE_MEM_CLAMP | When set this bit clamps the output from the headswitch Core Memories. This bit is OR'ed with saw outputs before passing to the Core Memories |
| 0 | CLAMP | When set, this bit asserts the clamp signal that must be asserted prior to collapsing CPU voltage, vdd_apc0. This bit is ORed with SAW output before passing to the CPU core. |

## 8.25 APCS_ALIAS3_KPSS_ACS

### 0x0B0B8000 APCS_ALIAS3_APC_SECURE

* **Type**: RW
* **Clock**: SYS_AHB_CLK
* **Reset State**: 0x0000000F
* **Security Treatment**: Restricted

The APC_SECURE register is used to enable or disable non-secure bus transactions. The bus security status is signaled by A53SS's APROTNS pin. When APROTNS is set to '0' the state of the APC_SECURE register is not considered - a secure transaction is always allowed. When APROTNS is set to '1', the APC_SECURE register's SECURE bit must be '1' for access to be granted. If the SECURE bit is set to '0', the non-secure (APROTNS = '1') transactions are denied. When access is denied, a write is ignored, and a read will return '0'. No error is signaled.

When reading the APC_SECURE register, non secure agents will always read '0'. Secure agents will see the actual value of the register. The same is true for the registers or bits each bit in the APC_SECURE register correspond to.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 3 | VOTE | Secure bit for SPM Voting by HLOS<br>0x1: NSEC (NSEC)<br>0x0: SEC (SEC)<br>Controls security treatment for SPM Vote registers: SPM_VOTE_HLOS) |
| 2 | RESERVED | Reserved |
| 1 | CLK_CTL | 0x1: NSEC (NSEC)<br>0x0: SEC (SEC)<br>Controls security treatment for the sleep control registers: APC_PWR_STATUS, APC_PWR_GATE_STATUS |
| 0 | SLP_CTL | 0x1: NSEC (NSEC)<br>0x0: SEC (SEC)<br>Controls security treatment for the clock control registers: CPU_PWR_CTL, CPU_TRGTD_DBG_RST, APC_PWR_GATE_CTL, APC_A53_CFG_STS |

## 8.26 APCS_QGIC2
<!-- page 1264 -->

### APCS_GICD_ISRn (0x0B000080 + 0x4 * n, n=[0..8])
**Type:** RW  
**Clock:** CLK  
**Reset State:** 0x00000000  
**Security Treatment:** Restricted  
**Description:** Each bit in an GICD_ISR register controls the security state of an interrupt, to be either secure or non-secure. You can only access these registers with secure read or secure write accesses.  
**Note:** The GICD_ISR register at address offset 0x0080 is banked, that is there is one per CPU Interface. It is only accessible from the designated CPU and controls that CPU's PPI and SGI interrupts. The remaining registers control the SPI interrupts.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:0 | INT_NS | 0x0: SEC (Assigns INTID N to the Secure state.)<br>0x1: NS (Assigns INTID N to the Non-secure state.) |

### APCS_GICD_ISENABLERn (0x0B000100 + 0x4 * n, n=[0..8])
**Type:** RW  
**Clock:** CLK  
**Reset State:** 0x00000000  
**Security Treatment:** NS-int Dependant  
**Description:** Each bit in an GICD_ISENABLER register controls the enabling of an interrupt. Reading this register returns the currently enabled interrupts subject to NS-int Dependant access rules.  
**Note:** The GICD_ISENABLER register at address offset 0x0100 is banked, that is there is one per CPU Interface. It is only accessible from the designated CPU and controls that CPU's PPI and SGI interrupts. The remaining registers control the SPI interrupts.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:0 | INT | 0x0: NA (No effect. Use GICD_ICENABLER register.)<br>0x1: SET (Enables INTID N.) |
<!-- page 1265 -->

### APCS_GICD_ICENABLERn (0x0B000180 + 0x4 * n, n=[0..8])
**Type:** RW  
**Clock:** CLK  
**Reset State:** 0x00000000  
**Security Treatment:** NS-int Dependant  
**Description:** Each bit in an GICD_ICENABLER register controls the disabling of an interrupt. Reading this register returns the currently enabled interrupts subject to NS-int Dependant access rules.  
**Note:** The GICD_ICENABLER register at address offset 0x0180 is banked, that is there is one per CPU Interface. It is only accessible from the designated CPU and controls that CPU's PPI and SGI interrupts. The remaining registers control the SPI interrupts.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:0 | INT | 0x0: NA (No effect. Use GICD_ISENABLER register.)<br>0x1: CLR (Disables INTID N.) |

### APCS_GICD_ISPENDRn (0x0B000200 + 0x4 * n, n=[0..8])
**Type:** RW  
**Clock:** CLK  
**Reset State:** 0x00000000  
**Security Treatment:** NS-int Dependant  
**Description:** Each bit in the GICD_ISPENDR register provides the pending status of an interrupt. Writing a 1 to any of these bits will transition the corresponding interrupt to the Pending (or Active and Pending) state.  
**Note:** The GICD_ISPENDR register at address offset 0x0200 is repeated once per CPU Interface. It is only accessible from the designated CPU and controls that CPU's PPI interrupts. SGI interrupt bits are read-only, however the distributor updates these using the GICD_SGIR register. The remaining registers control the SPI interrupts.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:0 | INT | 0x0: NA (No effect. Use GICD_ICPENDR register.)<br>0x1: SET (Sets INTID N to the Pending state.) |
<!-- page 1266 -->

### APCS_GICD_ICPENDRn (0x0B000280 + 0x4 * n, n=[0..8])
**Type:** RW  
**Clock:** CLK  
**Reset State:** 0x00000000  
**Security Treatment:** NS-int Dependant  
**Description:** Each bit in the GICD_ICPENDR register provides the pending status of an interrupt. Writing a 1 to any of these bits will transition the corresponding interrupt out of the Pending (or Active and Pending) state.  
**Note:** The GICD_ICPENDR register at address offset 0x0280 is banked, that is there is one per CPU Interface. It is only accessible from the designated CPU and controls that CPU's PPI interrupts. SGI interrupt bits are read-only, however the distributor updates these using the GICD_SGIR register. The remaining registers control the SPI interrupts.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:0 | INT | 0x0: NA (No effect. Use GICD_ISPENDR register.)<br>0x1: CLR (Clears INTID N from the pending state.) |

### APCS_GICD_ISACTIVERn (0x0B000300 + 0x4 * n, n=[0..8])
**Type:** RW  
**Clock:** CLK  
**Reset State:** 0x00000000  
**Security Treatment:** NS-int Dependant  
**Description:** Each bit in the GICD_ISACTIVER register provides the active status of an interrupt. Writing a 1 to any of these bits will transition the corresponding interrupt to the Active (or Active and Pending) state.  
**Note:** The GICD_ISACTIVER register at address offset 0x0300 is repeated once per CPU Interface. It is only accessible from the designated CPU and provides information for that CPU's PPI and SGI interrupts. The remaining registers control the SPI interrupts.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:0 | INT | 0x0: DO_NOTHING (DO NOTHING)<br>0x1: SET (SET) |
<!-- page 1267 -->

### APCS_GICD_ICACTIVERn (0x0B000380 + 0x4 * n, n=[0..8])
**Type:** RW  
**Clock:** CLK  
**Reset State:** 0x00000000  
**Security Treatment:** NS-int Dependant  
**Description:** Each bit in the GICD_ICACTIVER register provides the active status of an interrupt. Writing a 1 to any of these bits will transition the corresponding interrupt out of the Active (or Active and Pending) state.  
**Note:** The GICD_ICACTIVER register at address offset 0x0300 is repeated once per CPU Interface. It is only accessible from the designated CPU and provides information for that CPU's PPI and SGI interrupts. The remaining registers control the SPI interrupts.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:0 | INT | 0x1: CLR (CLR)<br>0x0: DO_NOTHING (DO NOTHING) |

### APCS_GICD_IPRIORITYRn (0x0B000400 + 0x4 * n, n=[0..71]) - Continued on next page
**Type:** RW  
**Clock:** CLK  
**Reset State:** 0x00000000  
**Security Treatment:** NS-int Dependant  
**Description:** Each field in the GICD_IPRIORITYR registers controls the priority level of an interrupt.  
**Note:** The GICD_IPRIORITYR registers at address offsets 0x0400 to 0x41C are repeated once per CPU Interface. These are only accessible from the designated CPU and control the priority levels for that CPU's PPI and SGI interrupts. The remaining registers control the SPI interrupt priority levels.  
**Note:** This register is byte addressable.  
The GICD_IPRIORITYR register behaves differently depending on the security setting of interrupt associated with the address written (NS-int) and the security of the bus transaction (NS-prot). Figure 26-1 shows how these differences affect different types of access.

#### Figure: Figure 26-1 Summary of the secure and non-secure views of interrupt priority

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:27 | INT3 | |
| 23:19 | INT2 | |
<!-- page 1268 -->

### APCS_GICD_IPRIORITYRn (0x0B000400 + 0x4 * n, n=[0..71]) - Continued

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 15:11 | INT1 | |
| 7:3 | INT0 | All bits cleared (0x0) is the highest priority. All bits set (5'b11111) is the lowest priority.<br>For non-secure write access, the MSB is always set (1). For non-secure read access, the MSB is always clear (0). Non-secure entities can't use the highest priorities without secure software setting such a priority. The highest priorities are typically reserved for secure software.<br>On the other hand, secure software can, if needed, write and read the MSB. Secure entities have access to all priorities. Secure interrupts can use priority numbers 5'b10000-5'b11111 (the lower half of the priority spectrum) if needed.<br>Due to strict 'less than' comparisons used in the CPU interface, setting an interrupt's priority to 5'b11111 effectively disables that interrupt.<br>The number of priorities actually supported is 32. Software can determine this number by writing 0xFF and reading back the result. |

### APCS_GICD_ITARGETSRn (0x0B000800 + 0x4 * n, n=[0..71]) - Continued on next page
**Type:** RW  
**Clock:** CLK  
**Reset State:** 0x00000000  
**Security Treatment:** NS-int Dependant  
**Description:** Each field in the GICD_ITARGETSR registers controls the destination CPU(s) of an interrupt.  
**Note:** The GICD_ITARGETSR registers at address offsets 0x0800 to 0x81C are not actually implemented. (PPI interrupts, being private, only have one destination CPU. SGI interrupts are generated by the GICD_SGIR register only and do not need the GICD_ITARGETSR.) The remaining registers control the SPI interrupt destinations.  
**Note:** This register is byte addressable.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:24 | INT3 | |
| 23:16 | INT2 | |
| 15:8 | INT1 | |

### APCS_GICD_ITARGETSRn (0x0B000800 + 0x4 * n, n=[0..71]) - Continued

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 7:0 | INT0 | Each bit represents one of 8 CPUs. Bit 0 represents the zeroth CPU, bit 7 represents the seventh CPU. Setting this field to 0 will disable the interrupt as no CPU will see it set.<br>For INTIDs < 32 (the SGI and PPI), reads return the bit corresponding to the CPU performing the read (i.e. CPU 0 reads back 0x01010101). Writes are ignored.<br>The number of CPUs actually supported is determined by NUM_CPU generic. Software can determine this number by writing 0xFF and reading back the result. |

### APCS_GICD_ICFGRn (0x0B000C00 + 0x4 * n, n=[0..17]) - Continued on next page
**Type:** RW  
**Clock:** CLK  
**Reset State:** 0x55555555  
**Security Treatment:** NS-int Dependant  
**Description:** Each field in the GICD_ICFGR registers allows:  
- control of type of an SPI: level-sensitive or edge-sensitive  
- reading the type of PPIs and SGIs  
**Note:** The GICD_ICFGR registers at address offsets 0x0C00 to 0xC04 are repeated once per CPU Interface. These are only accessible from the designated CPU and allow read access for that CPU's PPI and SGI interrupts. The remaining registers control the SPI interrupts.  
**Note:** PPI(0) is the maintenance interrupt and must be configured as level type.  
**Note:** This register is not byte addressable, interrupts should be disabled before configuring their type.  
**Note:** Reset state for GICD_ICFGR0 is 0xaaaaaaaa.

| 23:22 | INT11 | |

### APCS_GICH_LRn

**Address:** `0x0B001100 + 0x4*n, n=[0..3]`
* **Type:** RW
* **Clock:** CLK
* **Reset State:** `0x00000000`
* **Security Treatment:** Common

The GICH_LRn provides access to each of the list registers in the Hypervisor Interface.
<!-- page 1272 -->
### APCS_GICH_LRn (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31 | HW | Indicates that this is a Hardware interrupt. When this bit is set, bits 19:10 contain the Physical interrupt number, and when this interrupt is subject to an EOI request, a Deactivate Interrupt request will be sent to the Interrupt Distributor. |
| 30 | GRP | Indicates that this interrupt should be treated as Group1. This means that the interrupt will present as an IRQ if GICV_CTLR[EnableG1] bit is set.<br>If the GRP bit is clear, the interrupt is put into Group0 and will present as either IRQ or FIQ depending on the setting of the GICV_CTLR[FIQen] but only if GICV_CTLR[EnableG0] bit is also set.<br>This bit is also used with GICV_CTLR[CBPR] to determine which Binary Point register is used in GICV for preemption calculations. |
| 29:28 | STATE | 0x0: IDL (INVALID)<br>0x1: PNA (PENDING, NOT ACTIVE)<br>0x2: A (ACTIVE)<br>0x3: PA (PENDING and ACTIVE)<br><br>**NOTE:** For hardware interrupts, the PENDING+ACTIVE state is held in the physical Distributor rather than the VCPUIF. The PENDING+ACTIVE state (11) should only be used for software originated interrupts (Virtual Devices) or SGIs. |
| 27:23 | PRI | Indicates the priority of this interrupt. This is converted to a traditional 8 bit QGIC priority value by appending three zero bits. |
| 19:10 | PHY_ID | The physical ID of the interrupt (which SGI/PPI/SPI is it?).<br>When the HW bit is set this field indicates the physical interrupt ID, which is forwarded to the Distributor when this interrupt is subject to an EOI request. See below for details when the HW bit is clear.<br>If the Physical ID is between 16 and 31 inclusive (PPI space), the Deactivation will apply to the PPI associated with the same physical CPU as the VCPUIF making the request.<br>If the Physical ID is between 0 and 15 inclusive (SGI space), the Deactivation will still apply to SGI associated with the same physical CPU as the VCPUIF making the request but it is expected that the HW bit and Physical ID will NOT be used for SGIs. |
| 9:0 | VIRTL_ID | Indicates the Virtual ID. This ID is returned to the Guest OS when this interrupt is acknowledged via the GICV_IAR (Interrupt Acknowledge register). |

### OCIMEM_PSCGC_M0_M7_CTL

**Address:** `0x0005003C`
* **Type:** RW
* **Reset State:** `0x00000002`

Memory Banks 0 to 7 PSCGC Power Control. This register is used to perform fine-grain sleep control over OCIMEM memory macros.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 2:0 | M0_PSCGC_CTL | Controls the inputs `{async_clk_halt, up_force_core_on, up_force_periph_on}` for the 3 macros in Bank 0 in Elan. These macros are put to sleep/waken together.<br>bit `[2 1 0]`:<br>`0 0 0` = norm_passthru - upstream sleep-controller is in control (default)<br>`0 1 0` = norm_force_core_on - memory core is forced on<br>`0 0 1` = norm_force_periph_on - peripheral controller is forced on<br>`0 1 1` = norm_force_all_on - peripheral controller and core are forced on<br>`1 1 0` = slp_ret - sleep with retention, periph off<br>`1 1 1` = slp_ret_periph_on - sleep with retention, periph on<br>`1 0 0` = slp_nret - sleep without retention<br>other = Not supported<br><br>**Note:**<br>1. Typical sequence from normal to sleep with retention state sequence (one prgm write): `norm_passthru` -> `slp_ret`<br>2. Typical sequence from sleep with retention to normal state sequence (two prgm writes): `slp_ret` -> `norm_force_core_on` -> `norm_passthru`<br>3. Typical sequence from normal to sleep no retention state sequence (one prgm write): `norm_passthru` -> `slp_nret`<br>4. Typical sequence from sleep no retention to normal state sequence (one prgm write): `slp_nret` -> `norm_passthru` |

**Address:** `0x00050060`
* **Type:** R
* **Reset State:** `0x00000000`
<!-- page 1277 -->
### OCIMEM_ERR_ADDRESS (cont.)

The `OCIMEM_ERR_ADDRESS` register contains the lower (from NOC slave port) address of the request that caused the AXI bus error. This register will be updated by hardware upon the detection of an AXI address decode or sleep error. Once set, the register will be locked until bit `OCIMEM_INTC_CLR.AXI_ERR_INT_CLR` is written to clear the error.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:0 | ERROR_ADDRESS | Lower (System NOC Slave port) address of the request that caused the bus error. For Elan 2 MB is reserved so MSB is bit 20:3 are significant |

---

### OCIMEM_AXI_ERR_SYNDROME

**Address:** `0x00050064`
* **Type:** R
* **Reset State:** `0x00000000`

The `OCIMEM_AXI_ERR_SYNDROME` register provides various data about the request that caused the AXI bus error. This register will be updated by hardware upon the detection of an address decode or sleep error. Once set, the register will be locked until bit `OCIMEM_INTC_CLR.AXI_ERR_INT_CLR` is written to clear the error.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:29 | ERROR_ABID | The Bus ID of the request that caused the bus error. |
| 28:24 | ERROR_APID | The Port ID of the request that caused the bus error. |
| 23:16 | ERROR_AMID | The Master ID of the request that caused the bus error. |
| 14:8 | ERROR_ATID | The Transfer ID of the request that caused the bus error |
| 5 | ERROR_ABURST | The ABURST of the request that caused the bus error |
| 4 | ERROR_AWRITE | The awrite of the request that caused bus error |
| 3:0 | ERROR_ALEN | The burst length of the request that caused bus error |

#### WCSS_A_BT_BT_CLOCK_ALU_COMMAND (0x0A3FF02C)

**Type:** RW
**Clock:** PCLK
**Reset State:** 0x00000000

This is the Bluetooth clock ALU command register and issues (writes) the ALU command as programmed in the individual registers. It does not handle long LE packets because of the MOD 5000 operation inside the ALU.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 18:16 | OP_0 | Selects input 0 of the Bluetooth clock ALU<br>0x0: Zeroes<br>0x1: bt_clk operand register<br>0x2: bt_clkn<br>0x3: bt_clka<br>0x4: bt_clk accumulator register<br>0x5: bt_clk_cap and zeroes |
| 14:12 | OP_1 | Selects input 1 of the Bluetooth clock ALU<br>0x0: Zeroes<br>0x1: bt_clk operand register<br>0x2: bt_clkn<br>0x3: bt_clka<br>0x4: bt_clk accumulator register<br>0x5: bt_clk_cap and zeroes |
| 8 | OP | Executed by the Bluetooth clock ALU<br>0x0: Add OP_0 + OP_1<br>0x1: Subtract OP_0 - OP_1 |
| 6 | LR | Load accumulator register with entire ALU result; not affected by update fields.<br>0x0: Do not capture alu result in accumulator register<br>0x1: Update the integer IntgrAcc and fractional FracAcc accumulator registers with the ALU result for read-back or accumulation or both |
<!-- page 1289 -->

#### WCSS_A_BT_BT_CLOCK_ALU_COMMAND (continuation)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 5 | LN | Load ClkN counter with the entire or partial ALU result.<br>0x0: Do not capture ALU result in Bt ClkN<br>0x1: Update the entire or partial integer and fractional Bt ClkN counters with the alu result according to the update fields. Fractional bits stall during the load. |
| 4 | LA | Load ClkA counter with the entire or partial ALU result.<br>0x0: Do not capture ALU result in Bt ClkA<br>0x1: Update the entire or partial integer and fractional Bt ClkA counters with the ALU result according to update fields. Fractional bits stall during load |
| 3 | UU | Update upper Bt Clk field allows bit(27:2) of Bt ClkN or Bt ClkA, or both, to be updated when an LN or LA, or both, ALU command is issued.<br>0x0: Do not update bit 27:2<br>0x1: Update bit 27:2 |
| 2 | U1 | Update Bt Clk (1) field (U1) allows bit(1) of Bt ClkN and/or Bt ClkA to be updated when a LN and/or LA alu command is issued.<br>0x0: Do not update bit 1<br>0x1: Update bit 1 |
| 1 | U0 | Update Bt Clk (0) field allows bit(0) of Bt ClkN and/or Bt ClkA to be updated when a LN and/or LA alu command is issued.<br>0x0: Do not update bit 0<br>0x1: Update bit 0 |
| 0 | UF | Update fractional Bt Clk field allows the 13-bit fractional portion of Bt ClkN and/or Bt ClkA to be updated when an LN and/or LA alu command is issued.<br>0x0: Do not update fractional bits<br>0x1: Update fractional bits |

### WCSS_A_BT_HOP_AFH_CHANNEL_MAP_0 (0x0A3FF07C)

**Type:** RW  
**Clock:** PCLK  
**Reset State:** 0x00000000  

AFH channel map, which is 79 bits long; using 3 consecutive words; shall be set to 0 for LE. The hop kernel indexes this channel map only when adaptive frequency hopping is enabled (AfhEn = 1). Each bit location represents a corresponding channel (bit 0 is channel 0, etc).  
A particular channel can be avoided by setting its corresponding bit location to indicate a bad channel. When the hop kernel calculates a channel that is deemed bad according to this channel map, it substitutes a valid AFH channel.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:0 | AFHMAP_31_0 | Each bit location represents a corresponding channel (bit 0 is channel 0, etc).<br>0: Indicates a bad channel to be avoided.<br>1: Indicates a valid channel |

### WCSS_A_BT_HOP_FREQUENCY (0x0A3FF090)

**Type:** R  
**Clock:** PCLK  
**Reset State:** 0x00000000  

Hop frequency generated for the radio synthesizer; the high-level priority scheme that shows how the other hop registers are used to generate the hop frequency:  
<!-- page 1299 -->
### WCSS_A_BT_HOP_FREQUENCY (Continuation)

```
HopFreq <= HopOffset when (OffsetOnly = 1) else
HopOffset + Bca0Chan when (servicing Cmd0 = RxBca) else
HopOffset + Bca1Chan when (servicing Cmd1 = RxBca) else
HopOffset + calculated channel
```

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 6:0 | HOPFREQ | Valid range = 0x02 (2) to 0x50 (80) Mhz.<br>Values out of range are not restricted. |

| :--- | :--- | :--- |

**Type:** RW  
**Clock:** PCLK  
**Reset State:** 0x00000000  

Link controller command register for halfslot 0. For write, issues the link control command as programmed in the individual registers; processed at the TxCmdTo/RxCmdTo when the selected Bluetooth clock bit(0) = 1; these time-outs precede the first halfslot. For read, returns the last command that was issued.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 7 | MODMODE | Selects between BR/EDR and LE for the next link controller command.<br>0x0: BR/EDR<br>0x1: LE |
| 6 | CAPT0 | Capture field that controls the capturing of the selected Bluetooth clock + 1 and the UAP portion of the BdAddr when this command is issued; capturing takes place at the TxCmdTo/RxCmdTo preceding the first halfslot.<br>0x0: Disable capturing<br>0x1: Enable capturing |
| 5:4 | CALC0 | Calculate field that controls whether the hop calculator runs when this command is issued; decision to run the hop calculator occurs at the TxCmdTo/RxCmdTo preceding the first halfslot.<br>AfhEn = 0: Hop calculator runs when Cmd0 Idle<br>AfhEn = 1: Hop calculator runs when Cmd0 Idle and bt_clk(1) = 1<br>0x0: Link controller automatically runs the hop calculator<br>0x1: Force the hop calculator to run regardless of Cmd0<br>0x2: Force disabling of the hop calculator regardless of Cmd0 |

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 3:0 | CMD0 | Command field that controls what activity will take place during the first halfslot.<br>0x0: Idle do not Tx or Rx<br>0x1: Tx<br>0x2: Rx data<br>0x3: Rx data X scrambler initialized with hop calculator X input<br>0x4: Rx ID<br>0x6: Rx scan data<br>0x7: Rx scan data X scrambler initialized with hop calculator X input<br>0x8: Rx scan ID<br>0x9: Rx BCA bad channel assessment power burst measurement<br>0xA: Continuous Tx test mode configured by transmit buffer<br>0xB: Continuous Rx Test Mod_1 1 Mbps data<br>0xC: Continuous Rx Test Mod_2 2 Mbps data<br>0xD: Continuous Rx Test Mod_3 3 Mbps data<br>0xE: Tx X scrambler initialized with hop calculator X input |

| 7 | MODMODE | Selects between BR/EDR and LE for the next link controller command.<br>0x0: BR/EDR<br>0x1: LE |
| 6 | CAPT1 | Capture field that controls the capturing of the selected Bluetooth clock + 1 and the UAP portion of the BdAddr when this command is issued; capturing takes place at the TxCmdTo/RxCmdTo preceding the first halfslot.<br>0x0: Disable capturing<br>0x1: Enable capturing |
<!-- page 1302 -->
### WCSS_A_BT_LC_COMMAND_HALF_SLOT_1 (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 5:4 | CALC1 | Calculate field that controls whether the hop calculator runs when this command is issued; decision to run the hop calculator occurs at the TxCmdTo/RxCmdTo preceding the first halfslot.<br>AfhEn = 0: Hop calculator runs when Cmd0 Idle<br>AfhEn = 1: Hop calculator runs when Cmd0 Idle and bt_clk(1) = 1<br>0x0: Link controller automatically runs the hop calculator<br>0x1: Force the hop calculator to run regardless of Cmd0<br>0x2: Force disabling of the hop calculator regardless of Cmd0 |
| 3:0 | CMD1 | Command field that controls what activity will take place during the first halfslot.<br>0x0: Idle do not Tx or Rx<br>0x1: Tx<br>0x2: Rx data<br>0x3: Rx data X scrambler initialized with hop calculator X input<br>0x4: Rx ID<br>0x6: Rx scan data<br>0x7: Rx scan data X scrambler initialized with hop calculator X input<br>0x8: Rx scan ID<br>0x9: Rx BCA bad channel assessment power burst measurement<br>0xA: Continuous Tx test mode configured by transmit buffer<br>0xB: Continuous Rx Test Mod_1 1 Mbps data<br>0xC: Continuous Rx Test Mod_2 2 Mbps data<br>0xD: Continuous Rx Test Mod_3 3 Mbps data<br>0xE: Tx X scrambler initialized with hop calculator X input |

### WCSS_A_BT_RX_CONTROL

- **Address**: 0x0A3FF0B0
- **Type**: RW
- **Clock**: PCLK
- **Reset State**: 0x00000000

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 6 | CDWINEN | Enables the carrier detect window<br>0x0: Disable<br>0x1: Enable |
| 5 | HECALL | Controls the checking of the HEC bits. To save power the receiver should be disabled immediately upon detecting a HEC error. However, the entire HEC should be received before aborting if software needs an accurate number of 1/3 FEC errors that occurred during the packet header.<br>0x0: Check the HEC on the fly as the bits are received and abort the receive immediately if a HEC mismatch is detected<br>0x1: Receive all the HEC bits before checking for a possible HEC mismatch |
| 4 | HEC1SLOT | Controls the receive abort of 1-slot packets due to an AM address mismatch. In some cases, it is vital to receive the entire packet header and check the HEC before aborting due to an AM address mismatch. For example: A slave device may not transmit during an Sco frame if the received packet (from the master) was intended for another device. To detect this, the slave device must check the AM address and verify the HEC before deciding to transmit.<br>0x0: Immediately abort receiving a 1-slot packet due to an AM address mismatch<br>0x1: Always check the HEC before aborting the receive of a 1-slot packet due to an AM address mismatch |
<!-- page 1305 -->
### WCSS_A_BT_RX_CONTROL (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 3 | RXAMADIS | Disables the receive AM address filter<br>0x0: Enable the AM address filter; only packets with a valid AM address in the base AM address array to be received; receive of packets with an invalid AM address are aborted and the AmAddrBad status is set.<br>0x1: Disable the AM address filter; packets with any AM address are received and the AmAddrBad status is never set |
| 2 | WININTEN | Enables asserting of the Rx interrupt for a receive window time-out; receive window time-out is generated when servicing any Rx LC command, except Rx Bca<br>0x0: Prevents a receive window time-out from assert Rx interrupt<br>0x1: Enables a receive window time-out to assert Rx interrupt |
| 1 | HDRALIGNEN | Enables slot alignment for receiving non-ID packets; enables capturing of the frame timing error FrameErr right before slot alignment. Slot alignment occurs when a received packet header is deemed valid - when the HEC matches and the number of 1/3 FEC packet header errors is below the specified threshold; the following Bluetooth clock adjustment is made:<br>[Bt ClkA = integer captured clock(27:0) & fractional RxHdrAlign(12:0)]<br>0x0: Disable non-ID packet slot alignment<br>0x1: Enable non-ID packet slot alignment on a valid packet header; first capture the FrameErr before slot alignment |
| 0 | ACDALIGNEN | Enables slot alignment for receiving ID packets. Slot alignment occurs when the receiver detects a valid access code - when the modem correlator matches the sync word; the following Bluetooth clock adjustment is made:<br>[Bt ClkA = integer Bt ClkA(27:2) & 00 & fractional RxAcdAlign(12:0)]<br>0x0: Disable ID packet slot alignment<br>0x1: Enable ID packet slot alignment on a valid access code detect |

## WCSS Registers

### WCSS_A_BT_TX_BUFFER_POINTER (0x0A3FF150)

* **Type**: RW
* **Clock**: PCLK
* **Reset State**: 0x00000000

Pointer to the starting address of the transmit buffer link-list, which with its corresponding buffer are located in the internal RAM Transmit logic accesses this link-list and read from its corresponding buffer while transmitting any packet or continuous pattern As a safety feature, software can write a null pointer to the first entry of the transmit link-list or simply set this pointer to zero. After software configures the transmit data portion of the link-list then the null pointer can be replaced with a valid entry that points the first word of the transmit buffer. This method prevents old data from being transmitted if software does not meet their deadlines; also more robust than inverting the CRC field with TxInvCrc.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 15:2 | TXBUFPTR | Range = 0 to 16k words (the RAM may be sized smaller) |

### WCSS_A_BT_TX_STATUS (0x0A3FF158)

* **Type**: R
* **Clock**: PCLK
* **Reset State**: 0x00000000

Transmit buffer link-list overflow status; the transmit logic is allowed to request one extra read from the transmit buffer after the null pointer has been read from the transmit buffer link-list; always cleared at the beginning of the transmit operation.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1 | TXBUFERR | 0x0: Null pointer has not been encountered, or only one extra read has been requested by the transmit logic<br>0x1: Transmit logic has requested two more reads from the transmit buffer since the null pointer was read from the transmit buffer link-list |

| 7 | COEXEN | Enables the clock to the coexistence logic<br>0x0: Disable by gating the clock<br>0x1: Enable by ungating the clock |

| 3 | POLRFACT | Sets the polarity of the coexistence interface Rf_Active output<br>0x0: Normal; high output indicates that Bluetooth is active<br>0x1: Inverted; low output indicates that Bluetooth is active |
| 2 | POLSTAT | Sets the polarity of the coexistence interface Status output<br>0x0: Normal; high output indicates Bluetooth high priority or Bluetooth Tx<br>0x1: Inverted; low output indicates Bluetooth high priority or Bluetooth Tx |
| 1 | POLFREQ | Sets the polarity of the coexistence interface Freq output<br>0x0: Normal; high output indicates a frequency overlap<br>0x1: Inverted; low output indicates a frequency overlap |
| 0 | POLTXCNFX | Sets the polarity of the coexistence interface Tx_Confx input<br>0x0: Normal; high input indicates that the Bluetooth should be prevented<br>0x1: Inverted; low input indicates that the Bluetooth should be prevented |
