### WCSS_A_BT_HARDWARE_VERIFICATION_STATUS_1 (Continuation)

Accumulates the number of packet header mismatches during continuous hardware verification receive bursts Expected packet header is programmed into EncrKey(31:0) during test mode Once this accumulator reaches its maximum value it does not roll over PyldCrc register is reused during hardware verification modes to generate this result

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 15:0 | RXHDRERR | Range = 0 to 0xFFFF (65,535) bit errors |

### 0x0A3FF198 WCSS_A_BT_HARDWARE_VERIFICATION_STATUS_2

* **Type**: R
* **Clock**: PCLK
* **Reset State**: 0x00000000

Number of payload bit errors received during hardware verification modes Accumulates the number of Prbs-9 or Prbs-15 mismatches during a continuous receive test or during continuous hardware verification receive bursts Once this accumulator reaches its maximum value it does not roll over FecCorCnt and FecDetCnt registers are reused during hardware verification modes to generate this result.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 15:0 | RXPYLDERR | Range = 0 to 0xFFFF (65,535) bit errors |

* **Reset State**: 0x00000000

<!-- page 1334 -->

### WCSS_A_BT_PACKET_CONTROL (Continuation)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 5 | HECCRCCAPT | Controls the checking of the HEC and CRC bits for BR/EDR and the CRC bits for LE; reading the received HEC and CRC field requires that this bit is set<br/>0x0: Timing of the HEC check is based on the HecAll control register; check the CRC on the fly as the bits are received and abort the receive immediately if a CRC mismatch is detected<br/>0x1: Receive all the HEC and CRC bits before checking for possible mismatches |
| 4 | SCRDIS | Disables the scrambling of the packet header, extended header, and payload for both transmit and receive operations<br/>0x0: Enable scrambling of packet header and payload<br/>0x1: Disable all scrambling |
| 2 | SCOCRCEN | Enables the appending (Tx) and checking (Rx) of the CRC at the end of the payload of the following Sco packets:<br/>(Hv3, Hv4, Hv5, 2-Hv3, 2-Hv5, 3-Hv1, 3-Hv3, 3-Hv5)<br/>0x0: Enable<br/>0x1: Disable |
| 1 | AUX1FECEN | Enables the encoding (Tx) and checking (Rx) of the 2/3 FEC coding during the payload portion of an Aux1 packet<br/>0x0: Enable<br/>0x1: Disable |
| 0 | AUX1CRCEN | Enables the appending (Tx) and checking (Rx) of the CRC at the end of the payload portion of an Aux1 packet<br/>0x0: Enable<br/>0x1: Disable |

### 0x0A3FF1BC WCSS_A_BT_BURST_COEXISTENCE_COMMAND

* **Type**: RW
* **Clock**: PCLK
* **Reset State**: 0x00000000

Compare value for generating the coexistence command burst timer (CoexCmdTo); coexistence state machine runs the hop calculator and starts the coexistence signaling at this burst timer if a coexistence command has been issued CoexCmdTo must occur at least 3.5 usec before the TxCmdTo and the RxCmdTo to prevent hop calculator contention (unless Calc0, Calc1 = CoexCalc) SlotTimer(13) determines which halfslot (0 or 1) to use; SlotTimer(12:0) indicates which fractional Bluetooth clock location is to fire the interrupt

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 13:0 | BRSTCOEXCMD | Time during slot = [312.5 usec * SlotTimer(13)] + [62.5 nsec * SlotTimer(12:0)]<br/>Fractional range = 0 to 0x1387 (4999); resolution = 62.5 nsec |

## 10.5 WCSS_A_SSBI2_CFG_SSBI2_CFG

### WCSS_A_SSBI2_CFG_SSBI2_CTL (0x0A4A0000)
Specifies various generic SSBI2 control information. Bits 19:13 comprising of fields SSBI2_DATA_PDEN, FCLK_MODE, FCLK_SW_OVERRIDE and NUM_FCLK are either asynchronously reset or set. This is because they control the signals going directly to a pad. Remaining bits 12:0 are synchronously reset or set.

| Field | Bits | Type | Reset State | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| NUM_FCLK | 19:16 | RW | 0x8 | Indicates a programmable number of active forwarding clock cycles following a SSBI2 'transaction done' for a corresponding SSBI2 request. Unless there is a new SSBI2 transaction request, the forwarding clock is shut off after toggling NUM_FCLK cycles at the PMIC SSBI2 clock frequency. The suggested setting (also the default value) is 8 clock cycles. |
| FCLK_SW_OVERRIDE | 15 | RW | 0x0 | This is a software override bit to control the CGC for forwarding clock. Set this bit to 1 to allow the SSBI2 clock to continue as a forwarding clock through the CGC (provided FLCK_MODE = 1). This override bit is provided to allow continuos toggling clock to SSBI2 slave irrespective of how the HW logic controls the CGC. Set this bit to 0 to enable pure HW control on the forwarding clock CGC. |
| FCLK_MODE | 14 | RW | 0x0 | Set this bit to 1 to activate forwarding clock mode. When this bit is 0, the FCLK_SW_OVERRIDE field has no meaning. Out of reset, the mode is set to 0 indicating that the SSBI2 slave does not work off the forwarding clock. <br/>When FCLK_MODE = 0; no forwarding clock.<br/>When FCLK_MODE = 1; FCLK_SW_OVERRIDE = 1; forwarding clock always toggles.<br/>When FCLK_MODE = 1; FCLK_SW_OVERRIDE = 0; forwarding clock is controlled by HW logic. |
| SSBI2_DATA_PDEN | 13 | RW | 0x1 | Pulldown enable for SSBI2_DATA pad. |

Note: Clock: AHB bus clock. Reset State: 0x00083005.
<!-- page 1358 -->
### WCSS_A_SSBI2_CFG_SSBI2_CTL (0x0A4A0000) (cont.)

| Field | Bits | Type | Reset State | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| PA_CGC_CTRL | 12 | RW | 0x1 | This to control the SSBI2 clock going to this PMIC arbiter. Set this bit to 1 when you want to allow the clock to flow through the CGC. Set this bit to 0 to shut off clock to PMIC arbiter. Out of reset, this bit is set to 1. |
| SSBI2_ADDR_WIDTH | 10:8 | RW | 0x0 | Specifies what is the addressing mode in SSBI2 mode. This field is only applicable in SSBI2 mode and not the old SSBI1 mode.<br/>0x0: ENUM_8_BIT_ADDRESSING_MODE (8-bit addressing mode)<br/>0x1: ENUM_9_BIT_ADDRESSING_MODE_AND_SO_ON (9-bit addressing mode and so on) |
| SSBI2_MODE | 7 | RW | 0x0 | Set this bit to 1 when SW wants to switch to new SSBI2 mode. Set this is 0 when in old SSBI 1 mode. |
| SEL_RD_DATA | 5:4 | RW | 0x0 | Specifies which RD_DATA value to select out of four possible combinations. This signal allows the returned data from the slave to be captured inside the master, 1, 2, or 3 symbols late in order to accommodate a large range of routing delay. Based on this field, the entire read transaction length will increase by SEL_RD_DATA number of symbols. |
| SSBI2_DATA_DEL | 3:2 | RW | 0x1 | Specifies the number of 1/2 clock periods, SSBI2_DATA will be delayed before sampling inside. |
| IDLE_SYMS | 1:0 | RW | 0x1 | The master will ensure there are at least this number of idle symbol periods in between the accesses. The idle time is inserted at the end of the read or write transaction. This supported values are always between 1 - 3. |

### WCSS_A_SSBI2_CFG_SSBI2_INT_ENABLE (0x0A4A0004)

| Field | Bits | Type | Reset State | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| ENABLE_SSBI2_INT | 6:0 | RW | 0x00 | SSBI2 transaction done interrupts for each SW master are generated only when the corresponding bits are set. The Interrupt mapping corresponds to the entries in the VIT. For e.g. if the VMID in VIT index 0 corresponds to the SW master RPM and VMID in index 1 of the VIT corresponds to SW master ARM 11, the bit 0 in the register will enable the interrupt corresponding to RPM, bit 1 will enable interrupt corresponding to ARM11. |

Note: Clock: AHB bus clock. Reset State: 0x00000000.
<!-- page 1359 -->
### WCSS_A_SSBI2_CFG_SSBI2_PRIORITIES (0x0A4A0008)
Specifies the priorities for SSBI2 arbiter ports. The SSBI2 block supports up to maximum of 8 ports for arbitration. Each port has 3 bits to denote its priority. The bits are synchronously reset.

> [!CAUTION]
> Since the reset state value of SSBI2_PRIORITIES is 0, only SW requests (hard-coded to port #0) can get through. SW has to program this register to allow hardware requests through the SSBI2 arbiter.

| Field | Bits | Type | Reset State | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| PRIORITY3 | 11:9 | RW | 0x0 | Specifies the port number of host, with a priority that is 1 less then PRIORITY2. |
| PRIORITY2 | 8:6 | RW | 0x0 | Specifies the port number of host, with a priority that is 1 less then PRIORITY1. |
| PRIORITY1 | 5:3 | RW | 0x0 | Specifies the port number of host, with a priority that is 1 less then PRIORITY0. |
| PRIORITY0 | 2:0 | RW | 0x0 | Specifies the port number of the highest priority host. |

Note: Clock: AHB bus clock. Reset State: 0x00000000.

### WCSS_A_SSBI2_CFG_SSBI2_BANKS_2_3_CTL (0x0A4A000C)
This register specifies whether an access is allowed to banks 2 and 3 of PMIC. The access control to the banks 2 and 3 of PMIC is set per VMID. Bit 0 corresponds to access control for VMID 0 and bit 31 corresponds to access control for VMID 31.

| Field | Bits | Type | Reset State | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| ACCESS_CONTROL | 31:0 | RW | 0xFFFFFFFF | Set each of the 32 bits to 1 if the master corresponding to that VMID wishes to initiate SW requests to banks 2 and 3 of PMIC. |

Note: Clock: AHB bus clock. Reset State: 0xFFFFFFFF.

### WCSS_A_SSBI2_CFG_SSBI2_ILLEGAL_STATUS (0x0A4A0010)

Note: Clock: AHB bus clock. Reset State: 0x00000000.
<!-- page 1360 -->
### WCSS_A_SSBI2_CFG_SSBI2_ILLEGAL_STATUS (0x0A4A0010) (cont.)
Returns status information of the software master that tried to access a SSBI2 command micro register, and failed security through the VIT table.

| Field | Bits | Type | Reset State | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| ILLEGAL_VMID | 5:1 | R | 0x0 | Indicates the VMID of the master that performed the most recent illegal access. The value in this field is only meaningful when the ILLEGAL_ACCESS bit is set. <br/>On software reads, the value is retained unless another illegal access with a different VMID happens. In that case, this field will have the VMID corresponding to the most recent illegal master. |
| ILLEGAL_ACCESS | 0 | R | 0x0 | When set (1) indicates an illegal access. An illegal access is defined as an access that does not find a matching VMID in the SSBI2_VITn registers. This bit is cleared on a software read provided there is no other illegal access in the same clock cycle that a software read happens. |

### WCSS_A_SSBI2_CFG_SSBI2_VITn (0x0A4A0020 + 0x4*n, n=[0..6])
This is the VMID index table(VIT) used for enabling concurrent SSBI2 SW requests among multiple SW masters. Secure entities are expected to assign a VMID for the SW master corresponding to an index. The SSBI2_VIT0 has the VMID associated with index 0, SSBI2_VIT1 has the VMID associated with index 1 and so on.

> [!CAUTION]
> By default, only the SW master with a VMID of '0' has access to registers in SSBI2 command micro space. SROT/RPM has to populate this table before valid SW masters can initiate SSBI2 SW transactions.

| Field | Bits | Type | Reset State | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| VMID | 4:0 | RW | 0x00 | VMID corresponding to index n. |

Note: Clock: AHB bus clock. Reset State: 0x00000000.

### WCSS_A_SSBI2_CFG_SSBI2_PVC_CTL (0x0A4A00A0)

Note: Clock: AHB bus clock. Reset State: 0x00000000.


<!-- page 1361 -->

This register provides the global enable/disable for the PVC interface module, per PVC port enable/disable as well as captures PVC interface busy status.

> [!WARNING]
> In a PMIC arbiter wrapper system having more than 1 PMIC arbiter module; if a PVC port(x) is enabled in one of the PMIC arbiters, the corresponding PVC_port(x) in all the other PMIC arbiters shall be disabled. If multiple PVC_port(x)'s enabled simultaneously, the hardware does not guarantee correct operation.

### WCSS_A_SSBI2_CFG_SSBI2_PVC_CTL

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 8 | PVC_INTF_BUSY | This is a status bit. When set (1) indicates that the PVC interface module is busy (meaning there is atleast one PVC transaction being serviced). Busy line goes high when PVC interface detects a new request on one of the PVC ports and stays high until it samples a done from SSBI2 arbiter.<br>Writes to this bit will not have any effect and will be ignored. |
| 3 | PVC_PORT3_EN | Set this bit to 1 to enable PVC port 3.<br>PVC port 3 maps to SMPSS CPU1 SAW. |
| 2 | PVC_PORT2_EN | Set this bit to 1 to enable PVC port 2.<br>PVC port 2 maps to SMPSS CPU 0 SAW. |
| 1 | PVC_PORT1_EN | Set this bit to 1 to enable PVC port 1.<br>PVC port 1 maps to LPASS Q6 SAW. |
| 0 | PVC_INTF_EN | Set this bit to 1 to enable PVC interface module. |

### 0x0A4A00A4 WCSS_A_SSBI2_CFG_SSBI2_PVC_TABLEn, n=[0..31]

* **Offset:** `+0x4*n`
* **Type:** RW
* **Clock:** AHB bus clock
* **Reset State:** `0x00000000`

This set of registers indicates the full PVC table corresponding to all the PVC ports. For e.g.: there are 4 entries per PVC port(set by RTL generic) and there are 3 PVC ports (set by RTL generic) in 12 entries. Each entry is 15-bit address to the SSBI2 slave registers. This indirect addressing from the PVC ports to the SSBI2 slave registers provides a way to enforce security on hardware SSBI2 requests.

> [!NOTE]
> Though this current document shows 12 entries, the number of entries should scale based on the GENERIC settings for the number of PVC ports and the address index width. Also though 15-bit addresses are supported, 10-bit addressing is all that is expected for current PMICs.

SSBI2_PVC_TABLEn, n=[0...11]
<!-- page 1362 -->

### WCSS_A_SSBI2_CFG_SSBI2_PVC_TABLEn

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 14:0 | ADDR | 15-bit address of the SSBI2 slave registers. |

## 10.6 WCSS_A_SSBI2_CMD_SSBI2_CMD

### 0x0A480000 WCSS_A_SSBI2_CMD_SSBI2_CMD

* **Type:** W
* **Clock:** AHB bus clock
* **Reset State:** `0x00000000`

The SW masters write to this register to initiate either a read or a write SSBI2 transaction. Through this register, the SW can address up to 32 kB of SSBI2 slave register space. However the PMICs only house a maximum of 1024 registers and hence the values on the most significant 5-bits of the REG_ADDR_14_8 field are ignored. The REG_DATA field is only applicable for write transaction and is ignored for reads. The read data returned back from the SSBI2 slave is directed to the SSBI2_RD_STATUS register. Bit 23 is left as a reserved bit to enable slave address to grow to 16-bits in the future.

#### WCSS_A_SSBI2_CMD_SSBI2_CMD

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 24 | RDWRN | Denotes whether the command to perform is a register write (0) or read (1). |
| 22:16 | REG_ADDR_14_8 | Specifies the upper 7 bits, 14:8, of SSBI slave register address. |
| 15:8 | REG_ADDR_7_0 | Lower 8 bits, 7:0, of SSBI slave register address. |
| 7:0 | REG_DATA | Write data for a slave register. |

### 0x0A480004 WCSS_A_SSBI2_CMD_SSBI2_RD_STATUS

* **Type:** R
* **Clock:** AHB bus clock
* **Reset State:** `0x00000000`

This register provides the read data as well as the status of the transaction. This register also returns back information associated with the transaction such as the SSBI2 slave register address and the transaction access type. SW is expected to poll TRANS_DONE and TRANS_DENIED until either of these bits are set to 1.

* **TRANS_DONE = 0, TRANS_DENIED = 1:** indicates to SW that the current transaction was rejected because the master did not have permissions to access the corresponding SSBI2 slave register.
<!-- page 1363 -->

* **TRANS_DONE = 1, TRANS_DENIED = 0:** indicates to SW that the current transaction was completed successfully. For writes, it means that the write data was sent out on the SSBI wire and for reads, it means that the read data is returned back and is now in `SSBI2_RD_STATUS[REG_DATA]`. At this point, the SW is said to have completed one transaction.
* **Both TRANS_DONE and TRANS_DENIED being either 0 or 1** does not happen and is not a valid combination after a transaction has been initiated.

#### WCSS_A_SSBI2_CMD_SSBI2_RD_STATUS

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 27 | TRANS_DONE | When set (1), indicates that the SSBI2 has completed the transaction. If this was a write request, the write has completed. If this was a read request, the read data has returned back.<br>**NOTE:** This bit is cleared on read. |
| 26 | TRANS_DENIED | When set (1), indicates that a SSBI2 transaction was denied because the master did not have access to the particular SSBI2 slave SW register to where the access was intended. For PM8058 banks 2 and 3, this bit is set based on the settings in `SSBI2_BANKS_2_3_CTL` register that blocked the transaction.<br>**NOTE:** This bit is cleared on read. |
| 25 | TRANS_PROG | When set (1), indicates that a SSBI2 transaction is in progress. This signal will be set for the duration from REQ assertion until DONE assertion. |
| 24 | RDWRN | Returns the access type of transaction. A value of 1 implies a read transaction and a value of 0 implies a write transaction. |
| 22:8 | REG_ADDR | Returns the address to which the SSBI2 transaction was performed. |
| 7:0 | REG_DATA | Returned read register data.<br>**NOTE:** The read data is not cleared on reads, however will return all zeroes for a SW master whose transaction was denied or was an illegal SW master. |

| 22 | BW_CONFIG_VALID_BYPASS | RW | When this bit is set, bw_config_tx_valid, bw_config_rx_valid are not used, and PHY takes bw_config_rx and bw_config_tx as static signal, and doesn't synchronize them. Provided for riva backward compatibility. |
| 21 | BW_CONFIG_RX_VALID | RW | RX BW configuration valid. After changing bw_config_rx, SW should write '1' to this bit until PHY synchronizes bw_config_rx to proper clock domain. SW should clear this bit once PHY has done synchronization, usually after PHY configuration is complete. |

## WCSS Registers

### WCSS_A_PMU_OVRD_VAL (0x0A21C00C)
* **Type:** RW
* **Reset State:** 0x00000002
* **Description:** override value of controls

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1 | CCU_PMU_DISABLE_CLK_GATING_OVRD_VAL | override value of ccu_pmu_disable_clk_gating for PMU |
| 0 | DUMMY_OVRD_VAL | override value of disable_clk_gating for PMU |

### WCSS_A_PMU_SLP_TMR_CTL (0x0A21C010)
* **Type:** RW
* **Reset State:** 0x00000000
* **Description:** control for sleep timer

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 8 | ENABLE_SLP_TMR_CLK | enable clocks to slp_tmr |
| 7 | CLK_INT_CLR | Clear slp_clk_int. |
| 6 | TMR_EN_INT_CLR | Clear tmr_en_int. |
| 5 | CLK_INT_EN | Enable interrupt at the next rising edge of sleep clock. Due to synchronization, it may not be the very next rising edge, but could be 1~2 sleep clocks later. |
| 4 | TMR_EN_INT_EN | Enable interrupt when sleep timer is enabled. Interrupt will be asserted at the rising edge of sleep clock when sleep timer starts to increase or decrease. |
| 3 | TMR_ADD | add slp_tmr_val_wr[31:0] to the current sleep timer value. |
| 2 | TMR_LD | load sleep timer with slp_tmr_val_wr[31:0]. |
| 1 | TMR_DEC | 1 : Decrement sleep timer when tmr_en is set. 0 : increment sleep timer when tmr_en is set. |
| 0 | TMR_EN | Enable sleep timer increment or decrement. |
<!-- page 1392 -->
### WCSS_A_PMU_SLP_TMR_STS (0x0A21C014)
* **Type:** R
* **Reset State:** 0x00000000
* **Description:** Status of sleep timer.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 2 | CLK_INT | Status of slp_clk_int. |
| 1 | TMR_EN_INT | Status of tmr_en_int. |
| 0 | TOGGLE | This bit toggles at the every rising edge of sleep clock. |

## 10.8 WCSS_A_AOAHB_AOAHB

### 0x0A21A000 WCSS_A_AOAHB_AOAHB_AOWBR_PL

**Type:** RW
**Reset State:** 0x00000001

aoahb Arbiter arbitration priority level for aowbr master. In the aoahb arbitration scheme the master with highest priority level always wins. Should there be more than one master with the same priority then the winning master will be selected using a round-robin algorithm.

| Bits | Name | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 3:0 | PRIORITY | | Arbitration priority for aowbr master.The lowest priority level is 1 and the highest priority level is 15. A priority level of 0 has a special significance, it means that the master is disabled and stops participating in the arbitration scheme. Note that the aoahb arbiter will prevent a master from disabling itself. |

### 0x0A21A004 WCSS_A_AOAHB_AOAHB_AOA2AB_PL

**Type:** RW
**Reset State:** 0x00000001

aoahb Arbiter arbitration priority level for aoa2ab master. In the aoahb arbitration scheme the master with highest priority level always wins. Should there be more than one master with the same priority then the winning master will be selected using a round-robin algorithm.

| Bits | Name | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 3:0 | PRIORITY | | Arbitration priority for aoa2ab master.The lowest priority level is 1 and the highest priority level is 15. A priority level of 0 has a special significance, it means that the master is disabled and stops participating in the arbitration scheme. Note that the aoahb arbiter will prevent a master from disabling itself. |

NOTE: Writing anything beyond the 4 R/W bits will cause the entire write to be discarded.<br>0x0: DMY (Grant ownership to aoahb dummy master)<br>0x1: AOWBR (Grant ownership to aoahb aowbr master)<br>0x2: AOA2AB (Grant ownership to aoahb aoa2ab master) |

## 10.9 WCSS_A_SAW2_SAW2

### 0x0A219000 WCSS_A_SAW2_SAW2_SECURE

**Type:** RW
**Clock:** sys_ref_clk
**Reset State:** 0x00000000
**Security Treatment:** Restricted

The SAW2_SECURE register is used to enable or disable non-secure bus transactions. The bus security status is signaled by ahb_saw_hprotns pin. When ahb_saw_hprotns is set to '0' the state of the SAW2_SECURE register is not considered - a secure transaction is always allowed. When ahb_saw_hprotns is set to '1', the SAW2_SECURE register security treatment bit of that register must be '1' for access to be granted. If the security treatment bit of the register is set to '0', the non-secure (ahb_saw_hprotns = '1') transactions are denied. When access is denied, a write is ignored, and a read will return '0'. No error is signaled.

When reading the SAW2_SECURE register, non secure agents will always read '0'. Secure agents will see the actual value of the register. The reset value is controlled by CFGNSINIT input pin.

| Bits | Name | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 2 | SAW_CTL | | 0x1: NSEC (NSEC)<br>0x0: SEC (SEC)<br>Controls security treatment for SAW2 registers: SAW2_ID, SAW2_CFG, SAW2_STS_0, SAW2_STS_1, SAW2_RST, SAW2_VERSION) |
| 1 | PWR_CTL | | 0x1: NSEC (NSEC)<br>0x0: SEC (SEC)<br>Controls security treatment for SPM registers: SAW2_SPM_CTL, SAW2_SPM_PMIC_DLY, SAW2_SPM_PMIC_DATA_0, SAW2_SPM_PMIC_DATA_1, SAW2_SPM_SLP_SEQ_ENTRY_n) |
| 0 | VLT_CTL | | 0x1: NSEC (NSEC)<br>0x0: SEC (SEC) |

### WCSS_A_QTMR_AC_QTMR_AC_CNTTID (cont.)

The Counter Timer ID (CNTTID) is 32-bit register that identifies the number of timer frames implemented, which frame have virtual offsets and timers, and which frames have second views.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:28 | F7_CFG | Frame 7 configuration (same definition as Frame 0) |
| 27:24 | F6_CFG | Frame 6 configuration (same definition as Frame 0) |
| 23:20 | F5_CFG | Frame 5 configuration (same definition as Frame 0) |
| 19:16 | F4_CFG | Frame 4 configuration (same definition as Frame 0) |
| 15:12 | F3_CFG | Frame 3 configuration (same definition as Frame 0) |
| 11:8 | F2_CFG | Frame 2 configuration (same definition as Frame 0) |
| 7:4 | F1_CFG | Frame 1 configuration (same definition as Frame 0) |
| 3:0 | F0_CFG | Frame 0 configuration<br>0x3: RSVD (Reserved (Read as zero))<br>0x2: FPLO (Frame has second view)<br>0x1: FVI (Virtual frame implemented)<br>0x0: FI (Frame implemented) |

### 0x0A211040 + 0x4 * n WCSS_A_QTMR_AC_QTMR_AC_CNTACR_n, n=[0..4]

**Type:** RW  
**Clock:** SYS_AHB_CLK  
**Reset State:** 0x00000000

The Counter Access Control Register (CNTACR) provide access control to the individual elements of timer frame n, including the second view of that timer frame n.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 5 | RWPT | Read/Write access to CNTP_* register<br>0x0: ACCESS_DENIED (Access denied)<br>0x1: ACCESS_ALLOWED (Access allowed) |
| 4 | RWVT | Read/Write access to CNTV_* register<br>0x0: ACCESS_DENIED (Access denied)<br>0x1: ACCESS_ALLOWED (Access allowed) |
| 3 | RVOFF | Read access to CNTVOFF register<br>0x0: ACCESS_DENIED (Access denied)<br>0x1: ACCESS_ALLOWED (Access allowed) |
| 2 | RFRQ | Read access to CNTFRQ register<br>0x0: ACCESS_DENIED (Access denied)<br>0x1: ACCESS_ALLOWED (Access allowed) |

# WCSS

## 0x0A212028 WCSS_A_QTMR_V1_T0_QTMR_V1_CNTP_TVAL

**Type:** RW  
**Clock:** SYS_TMR_CLK  
**Reset State:** 0x00000000  

**Security Treatment:** Controlled by QTMR_AC_CNTACR_n[RWPT] An alternative 32 bit TVAL view to provide read or write CVAL register.

The TVAL reads:
```
TVAL = (CVAL - CNTP)
```
The TVAL write CVAL with:
```
CVAL = (CNTP + signExtend(TVAL))
```

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:0 | CNTP_TVAL | Timer Value in tick per second for Frame |

## 0x0A21202C WCSS_A_QTMR_V1_T0_QTMR_V1_CNTP_CTL

**Type:** RW  
**Clock:** SYS_TMR_CLK  
**Reset State:** 0x00000000  

**Security Treatment:** Controlled by QTMR_AC_CNTACR_n[RWPT] The Physical Timer Control Register which can disable the timer and can mask its interrupt. If the timer is disabled, interrupt are masked, but the timer value continue to count down.

| Bits | Name | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 2 | ISTAT | R | Interrupt Status before masking (Read Only)<br>0x0: INTERRUPT_NOT_PENDING<br>0x1: INTERRUPT_PENDING |
| 1 | IMSK | RW | Mask Interrupt<br>0x0: UNMASK_INTERRUPT<br>0x1: MASK_INTERRUPT |
| 0 | EN | RW | Enable Timer<br>0x0: DISABLED<br>0x1: ENABLED |
<!-- page 1422 -->

**Type:** RW  
**Clock:** SYS_TMR_CLK  
**Reset State:** 0x00000000  

**Security Treatment:** Controlled by QTMR_AC_CNTACR_n[RWVT]  
The Virtual Timer Compare Value register is compare against the CNTVCT counter. The interrupt signal is asserted when the CNTVCT counter is greater than equal to CNTV_CVAL. This register is implemented if FVI (Virtual Frame implemented) for the Frame n is set in QTMR_AC_CNTTID register.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:0 | CNTV_CVAL_L0 | Lower bits [31:0] of compare value for interrupt for Frame n |

| :--- | :--- | :--- |

The Virtual Timer Control Register which can disable the timer and can mask its interrupt. If the timer is disabled, interrupt are masked, but the timer value continue to count down.This register is implemented if FVI (Virtual Frame implemented) for the Frame n is set in QTMR_AC_CNTTID register.

**Type:** RW  
**Clock:** SYS_TMR_CLK  
**Reset State:** 0x00000000  
**Security Treatment:** Controlled by QTMR_AC_CNTACR_n[RWPT] An alternative 32 bit TVAL view to provide read or write CVAL register.

The TVAL reads:
```
TVAL = (CVAL - CNTP)
```
The TVAL write CVAL with:
```
CVAL = (CNTP + signExtend(TVAL))
```

## 0x0A21302C WCSS_A_QTMR_V1_T1_QTMR_V1_CNTP_CTL

**Type:** RW  
**Clock:** SYS_TMR_CLK  
**Reset State:** 0x00000000  
**Security Treatment:** Controlled by QTMR_AC_CNTACR_n[RWPT]  

The Physical Timer Control Register which can disable the timer and can mask its interrupt. If the timer is disabled, interrupt are masked, but the timer value continue to count down.

| Bits | Name | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 2 | ISTAT | R | Interrupt Status before masking (Read Only)<br>0x0: INTERRUPT_NOT_PENDING<br>0x1: INTERRUPT_PENDING |
| 1 | IMSK | RW | Mask Interrupt<br>0x0: UNMASK_INTERRUPT<br>0x1: MASK_INTERRUPT |
| 0 | EN | RW | Enable Timer<br>0x0: DISABLED<br>0x1: ENABLED |

**Type:** RW

**Reset State:** 0x00000000  
**Security Treatment:** Controlled by QTMR_AC_CNTACR_n[RWVT]  

The Virtual Timer Compare Value register is compare against the CNTVCT counter. The interrupt signal is asserted when the CNTVCT counter is greater than equal to CNTV_CVAL. This register is implemented if FVI (Virtual Frame implemented) for the Frame n is set in QTMR_AC_CNTTID register.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:0 | CNTV_CVAL_L0 | Lower bits [31:0] of compare value for interrupt for Frame n |

**Clock:** SYS_TMR_CLK  
**Reset State:** 0x00000000  
**Security Treatment:** Controlled by QTMR_AC_CNTACR_n[RWVT]  

An alternative 32 bit TVAL view to provide read or write CVAL register. The TVAL reads:
```
TVAL = (CVAL - (CNTP - CNTVOFF))
```
The TVAL write CVAL with:

CVAL = (CNTP - CNTVOFF) + signExtend(TVAL)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:0 | CNTV_TVAL | Timer Value in tick per second for Frame |

## 10.16 WCSS_A_QGIC2_QGIC2

### WCSS_A_QGIC2_GICD_CTLR (0x0A20A000)

**Type:** RW  
**Clock:** CLK  
**Reset State:** 0x00000000  
**Security Treatment:** Banked

The GICD_CTLR register controls if the Distributor responds to external interrupt stimulus changes. Non-secure access Distributor provides access to the enable_ns register in bit 0. Secure access Distributor provides access to the enable_s register in bit 0, and the enable_ns register in bit 1.
<!-- page 1450 -->
| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1 | ENABLE_NS | This bit is an alias of the enable_ns bit. This bit is only usable by Secure software.<br>0x0: CLR (CLR)<br>0x1: SET (SET) |
| 0 | ENABLE | This bit is the enable bit for both Secure and Non-secure software. Secure software accesses enable_s at this location. Non-secure software accesses enable_ns.<br>0x0: CLR (CLR)<br>0x1: SET (SET) |

### WCSS_A_QGIC2_GICD_TYPER (0x0A20A004)

**Type:** R  
**Clock:** CLK  
**Reset State:** Undefined  
**Security Treatment:** Common

The GICD_TYPER register provides information about the configuration of the QGIC2.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 15:11 | LSPI | Returns the number of Lockable Shared Peripheral Interrupts (LSPIs) that the QGIC2 contains. QGIC2 does not support lockable SPIs, always reads back 0x0. |
| 10 | TZ | TrustZone support. QGIC2 supports TrustZone, always reads back 0x1. |
| 9:8 | RESERVED_BITS9_TO_8 | |
| 7:5 | CPU_NUM | Returns the number of CPU interfaces that the GIC provides. The GIC provides either:<br>0b 000 = one CPU interface<br>0b 001 = two CPU interfaces<br>0b 010 = three CPU interfaces<br>0b 011 = four CPU interfaces<br>0b 100 = five CPU interfaces<br>0b 101 = six CPU interfaces<br>0b 110 = seven CPU interfaces<br>0b 111 = eight CPU interfaces. |


<!-- page 1451 -->
### WCSS_A_QGIC2_GICD_TYPER (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 4:0 | IT_LINES | Returns the number of INTIDs, to the nearest 32, that the Distributor provides.<br>Read as:<br>0b 00000 = the Distributor is configured for up to 32 INTIDs<br>0b 00001 = the Distributor is configured for up to 64 INTIDs<br>0b 00010 = the Distributor is configured for up to 96 INTIDs<br>0b 00011 = the Distributor is configured for up to 128 INTIDs<br>0b 11110 = the Distributor is configured for up to 992 INTIDs<br>0b 11111 = the Distributor is configured for up to 1020 INTIDs. |

## WCSS_A_QGIC2_GICD_IIDR (0x0A20A008)
* **Type**: R
* **Clock**: CLK
* **Reset State**: 0x00001070
* **Security Treatment**: Common

The GICD_IIDR register provides the implementor of the Distributor and the revision of the Distributor.

### WCSS_A_QGIC2_GICD_IIDR Bits

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 15:12 | REVISION | Returns the revision number of the Distributor, 0x1 |
| 11:0 | IMPLEMENTOR | Returns Qualcomm's JEP106 ID number, 0b 01110000 |

## WCSS_A_QGIC2_GICD_ANSACR (0x0A20A020)
* **Type**: RW
* **Clock**: CLK
* **Reset State**: 0x00000000
* **Security Treatment**: Restricted

The auxiliary non-secure access control register (GICD_ANSACR) is used to control non-secure access to GICD_CGCR.

### WCSS_A_QGIC2_GICD_ANSACR Bits

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 0 | GICD_CGCR | 0x0: SEC (SEC (Dis-allows non-secure access.))<br>0x1: NS (NS (Allows non-secure access.)) |
<!-- page 1452 -->
## WCSS_A_QGIC2_GICD_CGCR (0x0A20A024)
* **Type**: RW
* **Clock**: CLK
* **Reset State**: 0x00000000
* **Security Treatment**: Restricted

The clock gate control register (GICD_CGCR) is used to control localized clock gating over-ride logic. Setting bits in GICD_CGCR disables the corresponding local clock gating logic. The local clock gating logic normally turns off a local (small subset) clock tree automatically if there is no need for the clock. If any error is found in the gating logic, these bits can be used to over-ride it.

### WCSS_A_QGIC2_GICD_CGCR Bits

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:17 | RESERVED_31_TO_17 | |
| 16 | TOP | 0x1: DISABLE (DISABLE)<br>0x0: ENABLE (ENABLE)<br>Controls the top level clock gate (which gates entire QGIC2). |
| 15:4 | RESERVED_15_TO_4 | |
| 3 | DI_SGI_STATE | 0x1: DISABLE (DISABLE)<br>0x0: ENABLE (ENABLE)<br>Controls the clock gate for Distributor interrupt state data base registers for SGI interrupts. |
| 2 | DI_PPI_SPI_STATE | 0x1: DISABLE (DISABLE)<br>0x0: ENABLE (ENABLE)<br>Controls the clock gate for Distributor interrupt state data base registers for PPI and SPI interrupts. |
| 1 | DI_DEMET | 0x1: DISABLE (DISABLE)<br>0x0: ENABLE (ENABLE)<br>Controls the clock gate for Distributor interrupt input demet registers. |
| 0 | DI_RD | 0x1: DISABLE (DISABLE)<br>0x0: ENABLE (ENABLE)<br>Controls the clock gate for Distributor CRIF Read Data. |

## WCSS_A_QGIC2_GICD_ISRn (0x0A20A080 + 0x4*n, n=[0..8])
* **Type**: RW
* **Clock**: CLK
* **Reset State**: 0x00000000
* **Security Treatment**: Restricted

Each bit in an GICD_ISR register controls the security state of an interrupt, to be either secure or non-secure. You can only access these registers with secure read or secure write accesses.
<!-- page 1453 -->
> [!NOTE]
> The GICD_ISR register at address offset 0x0080 is banked, that is there is one per CPU Interface. It is only accessible from the designated CPU and controls that CPU's PPI and SGI interrupts. The remaining registers control the SPI interrupts.

### WCSS_A_QGIC2_GICD_ISRn (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:0 | INT_NS | 0x0: SEC (SEC (Assigns INTID N to the Secure state.))<br>0x1: NS (NS (Assigns INTID N to the Non-secure state.)) |

## WCSS_A_QGIC2_GICD_ISENABLERn (0x0A20A100 + 0x4*n, n=[0..8])
* **Type**: RW
* **Clock**: CLK
* **Reset State**: 0x00000000
* **Security Treatment**: NS-int Dependant

Each bit in an GICD_ISENABLER register controls the enabling of an interrupt.
Reading this register returns the currently enabled interrupts subject to NS-int Dependant access rules.

> [!NOTE]
> The GICD_ISENABLER register at address offset 0x0100 is banked, that is there is one per CPU Interface. It is only accessible from the designated CPU and controls that CPU's PPI and SGI interrupts. The remaining registers control the SPI interrupts.

### WCSS_A_QGIC2_GICD_ISENABLERn Bits

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:0 | INT | 0x0: NA (NA (No effect. Use GICD_ICENABLER register.))<br>0x1: SET (SET (Enables INTID N.)) |

## WCSS_A_QGIC2_GICD_ICENABLERn (0x0A20A180 + 0x4*n, n=[0..8])
* **Type**: RW
* **Clock**: CLK
* **Reset State**: 0x00000000
* **Security Treatment**: NS-int Dependant

Each bit in an GICD_ICENABLER register controls the disabling of an interrupt.

Reading this register returns the currently enabled interrupts subject to NS-int Dependant access rules.

> [!NOTE]
> The GICD_ICENABLER register at address offset 0x0180 is banked, that is there is one per CPU Interface. It is only accessible from the designated CPU and controls that CPU's PPI and SGI interrupts. The remaining registers control the SPI interrupts.
<!-- page 1454 -->
### WCSS_A_QGIC2_GICD_ICENABLERn (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:0 | INT | 0x0: NA (NA (No effect. Use GICD_ISENABLER register.))<br>0x1: CLR (CLR (Disables INTID N.)) |

## WCSS_A_QGIC2_GICD_ISPENDRn (0x0A20A200 + 0x4*n, n=[0..8])
* **Type**: RW
* **Clock**: CLK
* **Reset State**: 0x00000000
* **Security Treatment**: NS-int Dependant

Each bit in the GICD_ISPENDR register provides the pending status of an interrupt. Writing a 1 to any of these bits will transition the corresponding interrupt to the Pending (or Active and Pending) state

> [!NOTE]
> The GICD_ISPENDR register at address offset 0x0200 is repeated once per CPU Interface. It is only accessible from the designated CPU and controls that CPU's PPI interrupts. SGI interrupt bits are read-only, however the distributor updates these using the GICD_SGIR register. The remaining registers control the SPI interrupts.

### WCSS_A_QGIC2_GICD_ISPENDRn Bits

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:0 | INT | 0x0: NA (NA (No effect. Use GICD_ICPENDR register.))<br>0x1: SET (SET (Sets INTID N to the Pending state.)) |

## WCSS_A_QGIC2_GICD_ICPENDRn (0x0A20A280 + 0x4*n, n=[0..8])
* **Type**: RW
* **Clock**: CLK
* **Reset State**: 0x00000000
* **Security Treatment**: NS-int Dependant

Each bit in the GICD_ICPENDR register provides the pending status of an interrupt. Writing a 1 to any of these bits will transition the corresponding interrupt out of the Pending (or Active and Pending) state

> [!NOTE]
> The GICD_ICPENDR register at address offset 0x0280 is banked, that is there is one per CPU Interface. It is only accessible from the designated CPU and controls that CPU's PPI interrupts. SGI interrupt bits are read-only, however the distributor updates these using the GICD_SGIR register. The remaining registers control the SPI interrupts.
<!-- page 1455 -->
### WCSS_A_QGIC2_GICD_ICPENDRn (cont.)

## WCSS_A_QGIC2_GICD_ISACTIVERn (0x0A20A300 + 0x4*n, n=[0..8])
* **Type**: RW
* **Clock**: CLK
* **Reset State**: 0x00000000
* **Security Treatment**: NS-int Dependant

Each bit in the GICD_ISACTIVER register provides the active status of an interrupt. Writing a 1 to any of these bits will transition the corresponding interrupt to the Active (or Active and Pending) state

> [!NOTE]
> The GICD_ISACTIVER register at address offset 0x0300 is repeated once per CPU Interface. It is only accessible from the designated CPU and provides information for that CPU's PPI and SGI interrupts. The remaining registers control the SPI interrupts.

### WCSS_A_QGIC2_GICD_ISACTIVERn Bits

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:0 | INT | 0x0: DO_NOTHING (DO NOTHING)<br>0x1: SET (SET) |

## WCSS_A_QGIC2_GICD_ICACTIVERn (0x0A20A380 + 0x4*n, n=[0..8])
* **Type**: RW

* **Security Treatment**: NS-int Dependant

Each bit in the GICD_ICACTIVER register provides the active status of an interrupt. Writing a 1 to any of these bits will transition the corresponding interrupt out of the Active (or Active and Pending) state

> [!NOTE]
> The GICD_ICACTIVER register at address offset 0x0300 is repeated once per CPU Interface. It is only accessible from the designated CPU and provides information for that CPU's PPI and SGI interrupts. The remaining registers control the SPI interrupts.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:0 | INT | 0x1: CLR (CLR)<br>0x0: DO_NOTHING (DO NOTHING) |

## WCSS_A_QGIC2_GICD_IPRIORITYRn (0x0A20A400 + 0x4*n, n=[0..71])
* **Type**: RW
* **Clock**: CLK
* **Reset State**: 0x00000000
* **Security Treatment**: NS-int Dependant

Each field in the GICD_IPRIORITYR registers controls the priority level of an interrupt.

> [!NOTE]
> The GICD_IPRIORITYR registers at address offsets 0x0400 to 0x41C are repeated once per CPU Interface. These are only accessible from the designated CPU and control the priority levels for that CPU's PPI and SGI interrupts. The remaining registers control the SPI interrupt priority levels.

> [!NOTE]
> This register is byte addressable.

The GICD_IPRIORITYR register behaves differently depending on the security setting of interrupt associated with the address written (NS-int) and the security of the bus transaction (NS-prot). Figure 26-1 shows how these differences affect different types of access.

#### Figure 26-1: Summary of the secure and non-secure views of interrupt priority
*(No image extracted)*

### WCSS_A_QGIC2_GICD_IPRIORITYRn Bits

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:27 | INT3 | |
| 23:19 | INT2 | |
| 15:11 | INT1 | |
<!-- page 1457 -->
### WCSS_A_QGIC2_GICD_IPRIORITYRn (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 7:3 | INT0 | All bits cleared (0x0) is the highest priority. All bits set (5'b11111) is the lowest priority.<br>For non-secure write access, the MSB is always set (1). For non-secure read access, the MSB is always clear (0). Non-secure entities can't use the highest priorities without secure software setting such a priority. The highest priorities are typically reserved for secure software.<br>On the other hand, secure software can, if needed, write and read the MSB. Secure entities have access to all priorities. Secure interrupts can use priority numbers 5'b10000-5'b11111 (the lower half of the priority spectrum) if needed.<br>Due to strict 'less than' comparisons used in the CPU interface, setting an interrupt's priority to 5'b11111 effectively disables that interrupt.<br>The number of priorities actually supported is 32. Software can determine this number by writing 0xFF and reading back the result. |

## WCSS_A_QGIC2_GICD_ITARGETSRn (0x0A20A800 + 0x4*n, n=[0..71])
* **Type**: RW
* **Clock**: CLK
* **Reset State**: 0x00000000
* **Security Treatment**: NS-int Dependant

Each field in the GICD_ITARGETSR registers controls the destination CPU(s) of an interrupt.

> [!NOTE]
> The GICD_ITARGETSR registers at address offsets 0x0800 to 0x81C are not actually implemented. (PPI interrupts, being private, only have one destination CPU. SGI interrupts are generated by the GICD_SGIR register only and do not need the GICD_ITARGETSR.) The remaining registers control the SPI interrupt destinations.

> [!NOTE]
> This register is byte addressable.

### WCSS_A_QGIC2_GICD_ITARGETSRn Bits

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:24 | INT3 | |
| 23:16 | INT2 | |
| 15:8 | INT1 | |
<!-- page 1458 -->
### WCSS_A_QGIC2_GICD_ITARGETSRn (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 7:0 | INT0 | Each bit represents one of 8 CPUs. Bit 0 represents the zeroth CPU, bit 7 represents the seventh CPU. Setting this field to 0 will disable the interrupt as no CPU will see it set.<br>For INTIDs < 32 (the SGI and PPI), reads return the bit corresponding to the CPU performing the read (i.e. CPU 0 reads back 0x01010101). Writes are ignored.<br>The number of CPUs actually supported is determined by NUM_CPU generic. Software can determine this number by writing 0xFF and reading back the result. |

## WCSS_A_QGIC2_GICD_ICFGRn (0x0A20AC00 + 0x4*n, n=[0..17])
* **Type**: RW
* **Clock**: CLK
* **Reset State**: 0x55555555
* **Security Treatment**: NS-int Dependant

Each field in the GICD_ICFGR registers allows:
* control of type of an SPI:
  * level-sensitive
  * edge-sensitive
* reading the type of PPIs and SGIs

> [!NOTE]
> The GICD_ICFGR registers at address offsets 0x0C00 to 0xC04 are repeated once per CPU Interface. These are only accessible from the designated CPU and allow read access for that CPU's PPI and SGI interrupts. The remaining registers control the SPI interrupts.

> [!NOTE]
> PPI(0) is the maintenance interrupt and must be configured as level type.

> [!NOTE]
> This register is not byte addressable, interrupts should be disabled before configuring their type.

> [!NOTE]
> Reset state for GICD_ICFGR0 is 0xaaaaaaaa.

## WCSS_A_QGIC2_GICD_SGIR (0x0A20AF00)
* **Type**: W
* **Clock**: CLK
* **Reset State**: 0x00000000
* **Security Treatment**: Banked

The GICD_SGIR register provides the method by which software may cause interrupts to become pending for designated target CPU(s). The QGIC2 maintains an internal database of all outstanding software interrupt requests pended to each CPU Interface and rotates through them in Round Robin fashion. Signaling the same interrupt a second time before it is serviced will result in only one interrupt from the source CPU to the target CPU(s).

### WCSS_A_QGIC2_GICD_SGIR Bits

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:26 | RESERVED_BITS31_TO_26 | |
<!-- page 1460 -->
### WCSS_A_QGIC2_GICD_SGIR (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 25:24 | T_FILTER | Target Filter<br>0x0: LIST (LIST (Use the T_LIST as is))<br>0x1: OTHERS (OTHERS (Send to all CPUs accept the CPU MID making the request, ignoring T_LIST))<br>0x2: MID (MID (Send to only the CPU MID making the request, ignoring T_LIST))<br>0x3: NA (NA (Reserved)) |
| 23:16 | T_LIST | Target List. Each bit set represents a CPU target for the INT_ID, subject to the T_FILTER field.<br>0x1: CPU0 (CPU0)<br>0x2: CPU1 (CPU1)<br>0x4: CPU2 (CPU2)<br>0x8: CPU3 (CPU3)<br>0x10: CPU4 (CPU4)<br>0x20: CPU5 (CPU5)<br>0x40: CPU6 (CPU6)<br>0x80: CPU7 (CPU7) |
| 15 | SATT | Security ATTribute. This bit is only programmable by secure Software.<br>0x0: SECURE (SECURE (Secure interrupt is issued))<br>0x1: NONSECURE (NONSECURE (Non-secure interrupt is issued).) |
| 14:4 | RESERVED_BITS14_TO_4 | |
| 3:0 | INT_ID | The INT ID number (0-15) of the SGI to be set as pending. See Table 26-3 SGI pending truth table for security (SATT vs. NS-prot) on page 14 for information on the conditions that allow an SGI to be set pending. |

### WCSS_A_QGIC2_GICH_VMCR

**Address:** `0x0A20B008`

**Type:** RW

**Clock:** CLK

**Reset State:** `0x004C0000`

**Security Treatment:** Common

The GICH_VMCR contains read/write aliases of all the Virtual Machine accessible state (aliases from the GICV_* registers). This alias allows the Hypervisor to easily save and restore this state with a single read or write, and without needing to map in the Virtual Machine registers.

> [!NOTE]
> Various bits of this register include the terms group 0 or group 1 in their names. This is purely for compatibility with the physical GIC interface and does not pertain to actual TrustZone security.

| 31:27 | VMPMR | Alias of the GICV_PMR bits 7:3 in GICV |
| 23:21 | VMG0BP | Alias of the group0 GICV_BPR bit in GICV |
| 20:18 | VMG1BP | Alias of the group1 GICV_ABPR bit in GICV |
| 9 | VEM | Alias of the GICV_CTLR[EOIMode] bit in GICV |
| 4 | VMGBPR | Alias of the GICV_CTLR[GBPR] bit in GICV |

### WCSS_A_QGIC2_GICH_MISR

**Address:** `0x0A20B010`

**Type:** R

**Clock:** CLK

**Reset State:** `0x00000000`

**Security Treatment:** Common

The GICH_MISR is the Maintenance interrupt syndrome register in the Hypervisor Interface. This register indicates which Maintenance Interrupts are currently asserted. This takes into account the individual Maintenance Interrupt Enable bits in GICH_HCR. However, the global enable in GICH_HCR (EN) is not factored in to these bits. Therefore the maintenance interrupt is asserted if and only if at least one bit is set in this register and the EN bit in GICH_HCR is set.

| 5 | VDSI | |
| 4 | VESI | |
| 3 | NPI | |
| 2 | SKIDI | |
| 1 | UI | |
| 0 | EI | |

### WCSS_A_QGIC2_GICH_LRn (continued)

The GICH_LRn provides access to each of the list registers in the Hypervisor Interface.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31 | HW | Indicates that this is a Hardware interrupt. When this bit is set, bits 19:10 contain the Physical interrupt number, and when this interrupt is subject to an EOI request, a Deactivate Interrupt request will be sent to the Interrupt Distributor. |
| 30 | GRP | Indicates that this interrupt should be treated as Group1. This means that the interrupt will present as an IRQ if GICV_CTLR[EnableG1] bit is set.<br>If the GRP bit is clear, the interrupt is put into Group0 and will present as either IRQ or FIQ depending on the setting of the GICV_CTLR[FIQen] but only if GICV_CTLR[EnableG0] bit is also set.<br>This bit is also used with GICV_CTLR[CBPR] to determine which Binary Point register is used in GICV for preemption calculations. |
| 29:28 | STATE | 0x0: IDL (IDL (INVALID))<br>0x1: PNA (PNA (PENDING, NOT ACTIVE))<br>0x2: A (A (ACTIVE))<br>0x3: PA (PA (PENDING and ACTIVE)<br>NOTE: for hardware interrupts, the PENDING+ACTIVE state is held in the physical Distributor rather than the VCPUIF. The PENDING+ACTIVE state (11) should only be used for software originated interrupts (Virtual Devices) or SGIs.) |
| 27:23 | PRI | Indicates the priority of this interrupt. This is converted to a traditional 8 bit QGIC priority value by appending three zero bits. |
| 19:10 | PHY_ID | The physical ID of the interrupt (which SGI/PPI/SPI is it?). When the HW bit is set this field indicates the physical interrupt ID, which is forwarded to the Distributor when this interrupt is subject to an EOI request. See below for details when the HW bit is clear. If the Physical ID is between 16 and 31 inclusive (PPI space), the Deactivation will apply to the PPI associated with the same physical CPU as the VCPUIF making the request. If the Physical ID is between 0 and 15 inclusive (SGI space), the Deactivation will still apply to SGI associated with the same physical CPU as the VCPUIF making the request but it is expected that the HW bit and Physical ID will NOT be used for SGIs. |
| 9:0 | VIRTL_ID | Indicates the Virtual ID. This ID is returned to the Guest OS when this interrupt is acknowledged via the GICV_IAR (Interrupt Acknowledge register). |


<!-- page 1471 -->
### 0x0A20B120 WCSS_A_QGIC2_GICH_SW_LR

| Properties | Value |
|---|---|
| Type | RW |
| Clock | CLK |
| Reset State | 0x00000000 |
| Security Treatment | Common |

This register is not a real physical register or address in the design. It is placed here in the Software Manual to describe the alternate meanings for bits 19:10 in the LRn registers. Adding it here allows SW to pick up defines for these alternate meanings and use them in LRn accesses.

The HW uses these alternate definitions when bit 31 (HW) is set to 0 - indicating a (a pure virtual interrupt) written directly to this Hypervisor interface or an interrupt generated due to an SGI that originated in the Distributor. Bits 31:20 and 9:0 retain the normal GICH_LRn meanings.

#### WCSS_A_QGIC2_GICH_SW_LR Bits
| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 19 | EI | Indicates that this interrupt should trigger an EOI Interrupt. When this bit is set, a maintenance interrupt will be asserted whenever this interrupt becomes INVALID. |
| 12:10 | CPUID | If this interrupt is an SGI, indicates the requesting CPU ID. This will appear in the relevant field of the VM Interrupt Acknowledge register. If the interrupt is not an SGI, software must set this field to 0. |

### 0x0A20C000 WCSS_A_QGIC2_GICC_CTLR

| Properties | Value |
|---|---|
| Type | RW |
| Clock | CLK |
| Reset State | 0x00000000 |
| Security Treatment | Banked |

The GICC_CTLR configures the QGIC2 CPU interface.

Non-secure access Access is granted only to bits 0, 5,6 and 9.
Secure access Access is granted to all register bits. Non-secure bits 0,5,6, and 9 are aliased into bits 1, 7, 8, and 10 for access by secure software. Modifying these aliased bits will modify the non-secure settings. Bits 0, 5, 6, 9 are physically banked into Secure and Non-secure space.

#### WCSS_A_QGIC2_GICC_CTLR Bits
| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 10 | EOIMODENS | For secure software, a read/writable alias of Non-Secure EOImode. |
<!-- page 1472 -->
#### WCSS_A_QGIC2_GICC_CTLR Bits (cont.)
| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 9 | EOIMODE | For secure software, controls the behavior of secure access to GICC_EOI and GICC_DIR. <br>For non-secure software, controls the behavior of non-secure access to GICC_EOI and GICC_DIR.<br>0x0: PD_AND_DI (PD_AND_DI (Both Priority Drop and Deactivate Interrupt, GICC_DIR does not function))<br>0x1: PD (PD(GICC_EOI performs Priority Drop, GICC_DIR performs deactivate interrupt function)) |
| 8 | IRQBYPDISABLENS | For secure software, a read/writable alias of Non-secure version of IRQBypDisable. |
| 7 | FIQBYPDISABLENS | For secure software, a read/writable alias of Non-secure version of FIQBypDisable |
| 6 | IRQBYPDISABLE | For Non-secure software, when CPU Interface is disabled, prevents the legacy bypass IRQ signal from being forwarded to the CPU (if IRQ is under Non-secure control). For secure software, prevents bypass if FIQ is under secure control.<br>0x0: CLR (CLR)<br>0x1: SET (SET) |
| 5 | FIQBYPDISABLE | For Non-secure software, when CPU Interface is disabled, prevents the legacy bypass FIQ signal from being forwarded to the CPU (if FIQ is under Non-secure control). For secure software, prevents bypass if FIQ is under secure control.<br>0x0: CLR (CLR)<br>0x1: SET (SET) |
| 4 | SBPR | Controls which binary point register is used to calculate preemption.<br>0x0: BANKED (BANKED (secure interrupts use the secure Binary Point Register, non-secure interrupts use the non-secure Binary Point Register))<br>0x1: RESTRICTED (RESTRICTED (all interrupts use the secure Binary Point Register)) |
| 3 | S_DEST | Controls destination of secure interrupts.<br>0x0: IRQ (IRQ)<br>0x1: FIQ (FIQ) |
<!-- page 1473 -->
#### WCSS_A_QGIC2_GICC_CTLR Bits (cont.)
| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 2 | ACKCTL | Controls the side effect behavior of a secure read request to the Interrupt Acknowledge Register in the case where the highest priority pending interrupt is non-secure. <br>If AckCtl is set to 0, a secure read request to the Interrupt Acknowledge Register returns an Interrupt ID value of 1022, and the read request does not cause the interrupt to be acknowledged (that is the Pending status of the interrupt remains unchanged).<br>If AckCtl is set to 1, a secure read request to the Interrupt Acknowledge Register returns the Interrupt ID value of the non-secure interrupt, and causes the interrupt to be acknowledged (that is the interrupt becomes Active, or Active and Pending).<br>0x0: DISABLE_ACK_OF_NS_PENDING (DISABLE ACK OF NS PENDING)<br>0x1: ENABLE_ACK_OF_NS_PENDING (ENABLE ACK OF NS PENDING) |
| 1 | ENABLE_NS | For secure software, a read/writable alias of non secure software's enable bit (bit 0 of this same register in non secure space).<br>0x0: CLR (CLR)<br>0x1: SET (SET) |
| 0 | ENABLE | For non-secure software, this bit enables/disables non secure interrupts.<br>For secure software, this bit enables/disables secure interrupts.<br>0x0: CLR (CLR)<br>0x1: SET (SET) |

### 0x0A20C004 WCSS_A_QGIC2_GICC_PMR

| Properties | Value |
|---|---|
| Type | RW |
| Clock | CLK |
| Reset State | 0x00000000 |
| Security Treatment | Banked |

The GICC_PMR register configures the QGIC2 CPU interface Priority Mask. The Priority Mask can be used to limit the interrupts that can cause an interrupt request to the CPU based on priority levels.

Non-secure access Write access is granted only if bit 7 is 0x1, writes are ignored otherwise. Reads are always granted, however, bit 7 is always set in the data returned. Bit 0 is always zero.

Secure access Access is granted to all register bits.
<!-- page 1474 -->
#### WCSS_A_QGIC2_GICC_PMR Bits
| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 7:3 | LEVEL | Set the Priority Mask Level. The CPU interface asserts an interrupt request to CPU if the priority of the highest Pending interrupt sent by the interrupt Distributor is strictly higher than at least the mask set in Priority Mask Register. |

### 0x0A20C008 WCSS_A_QGIC2_GICC_BPR

| Properties | Value |
|---|---|
| Type | RW |
| Clock | CLK |
| Reset State | 0x00000002 |
| Security Treatment | Banked |

The GICC_BPR register configures the QGIC2 CPU interface Binary Point. The Binary Point is used to limit interrupts that can cause an interrupt request to the CPU based on the interrupt's priority and the interrupt priority that currently being serviced by the CPU (if there is one). If the CPU is not servicing an interrupt, the Binary Point register is not used.

Non-secure access Provides access to the non-secure Binary Point register.

Secure access Provides access to the secure Binary Point register. Secure software may access the non secure Binary Point register at offset 0x001C.

#### WCSS_A_QGIC2_GICC_BPR Bits
| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 2:0 | VAL | The VAL setting is used to determine the priority bits used for preemption according to Table 26-6. |

### 0x0A20C00C WCSS_A_QGIC2_GICC_IAR

| Properties | Value |
|---|---|
| Type | R |
| Clock | CLK |
| Reset State | 0x000003FF |
| Security Treatment | Banked |

The GICC_IAR register is used by the CPU to obtain the ID of the interrupt which caused the assertion if IRQn or FIQn.

Performing this read has the side effect of causing the Distributor to change the interrupt from the Pending state to the Active or Active and Pending state according the description below:
Using three bits defined by AHB bus security state (1=non-secure), security of the HPPI(1=non-secure) and the value of GICC_CTLR[AckCtl]:
<!-- page 1475 -->
#### WCSS_A_QGIC2_GICC_IAR (cont.)

The side effects of performing this read are based on a 3-bit value: [AHB bus security state (1=non-secure), security of the HPPI (1=non-secure), GICC_CTLR[AckCtl]]:

* **00x**: Respond with the true interrupt number, transitioning to active (secure request to secure interrupt, ACKCTL is don't care).
* **010**: Respond with 1022 (secure request to non-secure interrupt but ACKCTL=0 disabling secure handling of non-secure interrupts).
* **011**: Respond with the true interrupt number, transitioning to active (secure request to non-secure interrupt with ACKCTL=1).
* **10x**: Respond with 1023 (non-secure request to secure interrupt).
* **11x**: Respond with the true interrupt number, transitioning to active (non-secure request to non-secure interrupt).

#### WCSS_A_QGIC2_GICC_IAR Bits
| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 12:10 | CPU_ID | CPU Source ID value is only valid if the interrupt is a Software Interrupt, in which case it contains the ID of the CPU which requested the Interrupt. <br>For PPIs and SPIs the CPU source ID field is read as zero and should be ignored. |
| 9:0 | INT_ID | Interrupt Identifier. The value returned in this field is dependent on the security state of the access to the register, the security state of any outstanding interrupts, the value of GICC_CTLR[AckCtl] as defined in the description above. |

### 0x0A20C010 WCSS_A_QGIC2_GICC_EOIR

| Properties | Value |
|---|---|
| Type | W |
| Clock | CLK |
| Reset State | 0x00000000 |
| Security Treatment | Banked |

Unlike QGIC1, GICC_EOIR (End Of Interrupt) register has two possible behaviors. By default it acts as it did in QGIC1, that is, it can be written to indicate when software has finished handling an interrupt.

In QGIC2, if GICC_CTLR[EOImode] is set (1), writing this register has the 'priority drop' (PD) effect. The PD effect is when the active priority bit for the highest priority active interrupt is cleared. The key difference, when EOImode is one, is that the Distributor is not notified that this happened - that is, the interrupt itself does not become inactive.

When EOImode is zero, writing to this register will, in addition to the PD effect described above, set the interrupt to Inactive or Pending (if prior to writing to this register, the interrupt was both Active and Pending it becomes just pending) in the Distributor.

In either case, the value written must be the interrupt ID, and the CPU Source ID for SGIs, of the interrupt that is being completed.
<!-- page 1476 -->
#### WCSS_A_QGIC2_GICC_EOIR (cont.)

The security status of the write to this register (NS-prot) must match the security status (NS-int) of the interrupt ID, according to Table 26-7 for the interrupt to be successfully cleared.

#### WCSS_A_QGIC2_GICC_EOIR Bits
| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 12:10 | CPU_ID | CPU Source ID value is only valid if the interrupt is a Software Interrupt, in which case it must match the ID of the CPU which requested the Interrupt. As described in Table 26-7, the CPU Source ID must match an active interrupt in order for the GICC_EOIR to take effect. The CPU_ID is written must match that delivered to software when GICC_IAR is read. <br>For PPIs and SPIs the CPU source ID field is ignored. |
| 9:0 | INT_ID | Interrupt Identifier. The value must match the interrupt ID that software received when reading the GICC_IAR register. If the security settings match (see Table 26-7) a write will cause the priority drop effect and if EOImode=0, the Active state in the Distributor for the corresponding interrupt will also be cleared. |

### 0x0A20C014 WCSS_A_QGIC2_GICC_RPR

| Properties | Value |
|---|---|
| Type | R |
| Clock | CLK |
| Reset State | 0x000000F8 |
| Security Treatment | Banked |

The GICC_RPR (Running Priority) register provides access to the highest priority of all the Active interrupts on this CPU. The priority value returned is sensitive to the security status (NS-int) of the interrupt currently running and the NS-prot.

Non-secure access If the currently interrupt is secure (NS-int = 0), and a non-secure read of the Running Priority register is attempted (NS-prot = 1), then the value 0 (maximum priority) is returned.

Secure access Returns the true value in the register.

#### WCSS_A_QGIC2_GICC_RPR Bits
| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 7:3 | VAL | Running Priority |

### 0x0A20C018 WCSS_A_QGIC2_GICC_HPPIR

| Properties | Value |
|---|---|
| Type | R |
| Clock | CLK |
| Reset State | 0x000003FF |
| Security Treatment | Banked |
<!-- page 1477 -->
#### WCSS_A_QGIC2_GICC_HPPIR (cont.)

The GICC_HPPIR register provides access to the highest priority pending interrupt to the CPU Interface.

> [!NOTE]
> Interrupts that are Active and Pending in the Distributor are not considered candidates to become the highest priority pending interrupt.

The returned values are based on three bits defined by AHB bus security state (1=non-secure), security of the HPPI (1=non-secure) and the value of GICC_CTLR[AckCtl]:

* **00x**: Respond with the true interrupt number (secure request to secure interrupt, ACKCTL is don't care).
* **010**: Respond with 1022 (secure request to non-secure interrupt but ACKCTL=0 disabling secure handling of non-secure interrupts).
* **011**: Respond with the true interrupt number (secure request to non-secure interrupt with ACKCTL=1).
* **10x**: Respond with 1023 (non-secure request to secure interrupt).
* **11x**: Respond with the true interrupt number (non-secure request to non-secure interrupt).

#### WCSS_A_QGIC2_GICC_HPPIR Bits
| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 12:10 | CPU_ID | CPU Source ID value is only valid if the interrupt is a Software Interrupt, in which case it contains the ID of the CPU which requested the Interrupt. <br>For PPIs and SPIs the CPU source ID field is read as zero and should be ignored. |
| 9:0 | INT_ID | Interrupt Identifier. The value returned in this field is dependent on the security state of the access to the register, and the security state of any outstanding interrupts, as described above. |

|---|---|
| Type | RW |
| Clock | CLK |
| Reset State | 0x00000003 |
| Security Treatment | Restricted |

The GICC_ABPR register provides a copy of the non-secure binary point register for use by secure software. See the definition of the GICC_BPR register for details on the use of this register.

Non-secure access No access.

Secure access Access granted, updates are reflected to non-secure software at the GICC_BPR register at address offset 0x08.

### 0x0A20C020 WCSS_A_QGIC2_GICC_AIAR

| Properties | Value |
|---|---|
| Type | R |
| Clock | CLK |
| Reset State | 0x000003FF |
| Security Treatment | Restricted |

The GICC_AIAR register is used by the CPU to obtain the ID of the interrupt which caused the assertion of IRQn or FIQn. This is a secure only register used to read non-secure interrupts by Secure Software.

Performing this read has the side effect of causing the Distributor to change the interrupt from the Pending state to the Active or Active and Pending state.

Non-secure access No access. Read as zero.

Secure access See description below.

Based on the 2 bits defined by the AHB Security of the request (1=non-secure) and the security of the interrupt (1=non-secure):
* **00**: Respond with 1023 (secure request that behaves as if it is a non-secure request, to secure interrupt)
* **01**: Respond with the true interrupt number, transitioning to active (secure request that behaves as if it is a non-secure request, to non-secure interrupt)
* **1x**: RAZ/WI (non-secure request cannot access this register)

| 9:0 | INT_ID | Interrupt Identifier. |

### 0x0A20C024 WCSS_A_QGIC2_GICC_AEOIR

| Properties | Value |
|---|---|
| Type | W |
| Clock | CLK |
| Reset State | 0x00000000 |
| Security Treatment | Restricted |

A secure write to this register has an identical effect to a non-secure write to GICC_EOIR, with the exception of the EOImode bit; the value of the secure EOImode bit (bit 9) in GICC_CTLR is used to determine whether the interrupt is deactivated or just priority dropped rather than the non-secure EOImode bit (bit 10).

This register must be used by secure software to signal completion of non-secure interrupts when GICC_CTLR AckCtl bit is set to 0; GICC_EOIR cannot be used for this purpose since it would affect GICC_APRn rather than GICC_NSAPRn.

Non-secure access Ignored

Secure access Signal completion of non-secure interrupt

The CPU Source ID must match an active interrupt in order for the GICC_AEOIR to take effect. The CPU_ID is written must match that delivered to software when GICC_IAR is read. <br>For PPIs and SPIs the CPU source ID field is ignored. |
| 9:0 | INT_ID | Interrupt Identifier. The value must match the interrupt ID that software received when reading the GICC_IAR register. Interrupt Identifier. A write will cause the priority drop effect and if EOImode=0, the Active state in the Distributor for the corresponding interrupt will also be cleared. |

### WCSS_A_QGIC2_GICC_DIR (0x0A20D000)

**Type:** W  
**Clock:** CLK  
**Reset State:** 0x00000000  
**Security Treatment:** Banked  
<!-- page 1482 -->

*(Continuation of WCSS_A_QGIC2_GICC_DIR from page 1481)*

The GICC_DIR register provides the mechanism by which Software can Deactivate a specific interrupt.

Secure writes can deactivate secure and non-secure interrupts.

Non-secure writes can only deactivate non-secure interrupts.

Note that unlike GICC_EOIR and GICC_IAR, there is no restriction of the Deactivation of Non-Secure interrupts with Secure accesses. The AckCtl bit does not affect the behaviour of GICC_DIR. This is because unlike GICC_IAR there is no chance of the access affecting an interrupt from an unexpected security state, and unlike GICC_EOIR there is no effect on GICC_APRn or GICC_NSAPRn, so there is no need to indicate which register should be affected.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 12:10 | CPU_ID | CPU Source ID value is only valid if the interrupt is a Software Interrupt, in which case it contains the ID of the CPU which requested the Interrupt.<br>For PPIs and SPIs the CPU source ID field is read as zero and should be ignored. |
| 9:0 | INT_ID | Interrupt Identifier. INT_ID written should match value returned from GICC_IAR read. |

| 4 | GBPR | Controls which binary point register is used to calculate preemption, GICV_BPR or the GICV_ABPR.<br>0x0: BANKED (Group 0 interrupts use the Group 0 Binary Point Register, Group 1 interrupts use the Group 1 Binary Point Register)<br>0x1: G0 (all interrupts use the Group 0 Binary Point Register) |

**Type:** RW  
**Clock:** CLK  
**Reset State:** 0x00000002  
**Security Treatment:** Common  

The GICV_BPR register configures the QGIC2 Virtual CPU interface Binary Point. The Binary Point is used to limit interrupts that can cause an interrupt request to the CPU based on the interrupt's priority and the interrupt priority that currently being serviced by the CPU (if there is one). If the CPU is not servicing an interrupt, the Binary Point register is not used.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 2:0 | VAL | The VAL setting is used to determine the priority bits used for preemption according to Table 26-6. |

---

### WCSS_A_QGIC2_GICV_IAR (0x0A20E00C)

**Type:** R  
**Clock:** CLK  
**Reset State:** 0x000003FF  
**Security Treatment:** Common  

The GICV_IAR register is used by the CPU to obtain the ID of the interrupt which caused the assertion if IRQn or FIQn.

Performing this read has the side effect of causing the GICH to change the interrupt from the Pending state to the Active or Active and Pending state according to the rules below:

Using the 2 bits defined by Security of the HPPI(1=non-secure) and the value of GICV_CTLR[AckCtl]:
* **0x** - respond with the true interrupt number, transitioning to active (ignore APROTNS and consider as a secure request to secure interrupt, ACKCTL is don't care)
* **10** - respond with 1022 (ignore APROTNS and consider as secure request to non-secure interrupt but ACKCTL=0 disabling secure handling of non-secure interrupts)
* **11** - respond with the true interrupt number, transitioning to active (ignore APROTNS and consider as secure request to non-secure interrupt with ACKCTL=1)
<!-- page 1485 -->

*(Continuation of WCSS_A_QGIC2_GICV_IAR from page 1484)*

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 12:10 | CPU_ID | CPU Source ID value is only valid if the interrupt is a Software Interrupt, in which case it contains the ID of the CPU which requested the Interrupt.<br>For PPIs and SPIs the CPU source ID field is read as zero and should be ignored. |
| 9:0 | INT_ID | Interrupt Identifier - a virtual interrupt number determined by the Hypervisor SW. |

---

### WCSS_A_QGIC2_GICV_EOIR (0x0A20E010)

**Type:** W  
**Clock:** CLK  
**Reset State:** 0x00000000  
**Security Treatment:** Common  

GICV_EOIR (End Of Interrupt) register has two possible behaviors. By default it can be written to to indicate when software has finished handling an interrupt.

If GICV_CTLR[EOImode] is set (1), writing this register has the 'priority drop' (PD) effect. The PD effect is when the active priority bit for the highest priority active interrupt is cleared. The key difference, when EOImode is (1), is the interrupt itself does not become inactive.

When EOImode is (0), writing to this register will, in addition to the PD effect described above, set the interrupt to Inactive or Pending (if prior to writing to this register, the interrupt was both Active and Pending it becomes just pending). However, if GICV_CTLR[EOImode] is (0), then the CPU_ID and INT_ID must match an active interrupt for a state change to occur.

In either case, the value written must be the interrupt ID, and the CPU Source ID for SGIs, of the interrupt that is being completed.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 12:10 | CPU_ID | CPU Source ID value is only valid if the interrupt is a Software Interrupt, in which case it must match the ID of the CPU which requested the Interrupt. The CPU_ID is written must match that delivered to software when GICV_IAR is read.<br>For PPIs and SPIs the CPU source ID field is ignored. |
| 9:0 | INT_ID | Interrupt Identifier. The value must match the interrupt ID that software received when reading the GICV_IAR register. |
<!-- page 1486 -->

### WCSS_A_QGIC2_GICV_RPR (0x0A20E014)

**Type:** R  
**Clock:** CLK  
**Reset State:** 0x000000F8  
**Security Treatment:** Common  

The GICV_RPR (Running Priority) register provides access to the highest priority of all the Active interrupts on this Virtual CPU.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 7:3 | VAL | Running Priority |

---

### WCSS_A_QGIC2_GICV_HPPIR (0x0A20E018)

**Type:** R  
**Clock:** CLK  
**Reset State:** 0x000003FF  
**Security Treatment:** Common  

The GICV_HPPIR register provides access to the highest priority pending interrupt to the Virtual CPU Interface. If no interrupt is pending, responds with 0x3FF.

NOTE Interrupts that are Active and Pending in the GICH (hypervisor) are not considered candidates to be come the highest priority pending interrupt.

Using 2 bits defined by the value of GICV_CTLR[AckCtl] and the NS bit of the HPPI (1=non-secure):
* **1x** - respond with the virtual interrupt number
* **00** - respond with the virtual interrupt number
* **01** - respond with 1022

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 12:10 | CPU_ID | CPU Source ID value is only valid if the interrupt is a Software Interrupt, in which case it contains the ID of the CPU which requested the Interrupt.<br>For PPIs and SPIs the CPU source ID field is read as zero and should be ignored. |
| 9:0 | INT_ID | Interrupt Identifier. |
<!-- page 1487 -->

### WCSS_A_QGIC2_GICV_ABPR (0x0A20E01C)

**Type:** RW  
**Clock:** CLK  
**Reset State:** 0x00000003  
**Security Treatment:** Common  

The GICV_ABPR register provides access to the non-secure binary point register used by non-secure interrupts when GICV_CTRL[GBPR]=0. See the definition of the GICV_BPR register for details on the use of this register.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 2:0 | VAL | Same as the GICV_BPR register - affects only non-secure interrupts. |

---

### WCSS_A_QGIC2_GICV_AIAR (0x0A20E020)

**Type:** R  
**Clock:** CLK  
**Reset State:** 0x000003FF  
**Security Treatment:** Common  

The GICV_AIAR register is used by the CPU to obtain the ID of the interrupt which caused the assertion if IRQn or FIQn.

Performing this read has the side effect of causing the GICH to change the interrupt from the Pending state to the Active or Active and Pending state according to the rules below:

Using the security state of the pending interrupt:
* **0** - respond with 1023
* **1** - respond with the true interrupt number, transitioning to active

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 12:10 | CPU_ID | CPU Source ID value is only valid if the interrupt is a Software Interrupt, in which case it contains the ID of the CPU which requested the Interrupt.<br>For PPIs and SPIs the CPU source ID field is read as zero and should be ignored. |
| 9:0 | INT_ID | Interrupt Identifier - a virtual interrupt number determined by the Hypervisor SW. |
<!-- page 1488 -->

### WCSS_A_QGIC2_GICV_AEOIR (0x0A20E024)

**Type:** W  
**Clock:** CLK  
**Reset State:** 0x00000000  
**Security Treatment:** Common  

This register presents the same programmers model as GICC_AEOIR.

The effect of writing to this register is identical to the effect of writing the same value to the GICV_EOIR register. This alias is provided for compatibility with the Physical CPU Interface, where the two registers have a different effect due to the provision of separate Secure and Non-Secure Active Priority Registers.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 12:10 | CPU_ID | CPU Source ID value is only valid if the interrupt is a Software Interrupt, in which case it must match the ID of the CPU which requested the Interrupt. The CPU_ID is written must match that delivered to software when GICV_IAR is read.<br>For PPIs and SPIs the CPU source ID field is ignored. |
| 9:0 | INT_ID | Interrupt Identifier. The value must match the interrupt ID that software received when reading the GICV_IAR register. |

---

### WCSS_A_QGIC2_GICV_AHPPIR (0x0A20E028)

**Type:** R  
**Clock:** CLK  
**Reset State:** 0x000003FF  
**Security Treatment:** Common  

This register presents the same programmers model as GICC_AHPPIR.

This register returns the interrupt ID of the highest priority PENDING interrupt if it has an NS value of 1. Reading this interrupt has no side effects and simply returns the highest priority PENDING interrupt among the list registers or a status code according to the following table:

Using the NS bit of the HPPI (1=non-secure):
* **0** - 1023
* **1** - respond with the virtual interrupt number

Note that in some cases the returned value may not be strictly accurate if interrupts are currently paged out in software.
<!-- page 1489 -->

*(Continuation of WCSS_A_QGIC2_GICV_AHPPIR from page 1488)*

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 12:10 | CPU_ID | CPU Source ID value is only valid if the interrupt is a Software Interrupt, in which case it contains the ID of the CPU which requested the Interrupt.<br>For PPIs and SPIs the CPU source ID field is read as zero and should be ignored. |
| 9:0 | INT_ID | Interrupt Identifier. |

---

### WCSS_A_QGIC2_GICV_APR (0x0A20E0D0)

**Type:** RW  
**Clock:** CLK  
**Reset State:** 0x00000000  
**Security Treatment:** Common  

Each bit in the GICV_APR is an alias of GICH_APR. The data and access control are one and the same.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:0 | PRI | 0x1: A (ACTIVE)<br>0x0: NA (NOT ACTIVE) |

---

### WCSS_A_QGIC2_GICV_IIDR (0x0A20E0FC)

**Type:** R  
**Clock:** CLK  
**Reset State:** 0x00020070  
**Security Treatment:** Common  

The GICV_IIDR register provides information about the QGIC2 Virtual CPU Interface version and device implementor information.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:20 | PART_NUM | Part Number: 0x390 |
| 19:16 | ARCH_VERSION | Architecture Version : 0x2 |
| 15:12 | REVISION | Revision number: 0x0 |
<!-- page 1490 -->

*(Continuation of WCSS_A_QGIC2_GICV_IIDR from page 1489)*

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 11:0 | IMPLEMENTOR | Bits[11:8] contain the implementor's JEP106 continuation code, 0x0<br>Bit[7] is always 0<br>Bits[6:0] contain bits [6:0] of the implementor's JEP106 code |

---

### WCSS_A_QGIC2_GICV_DIR (0x0A20F000)

**Type:** W  
**Clock:** CLK  
**Reset State:** 0x00000000  
**Security Treatment:** Banked  

The GICV_DIR register provides the mechanism by which Software can Deactivate a specific interrupt.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 12:10 | CPU_ID | CPU Source ID value is only valid if the interrupt is a Software Interrupt, in which case it contains the ID of the CPU which requested the Interrupt. |
| 9:0 | INT_ID | Interrupt Identifier. The value should match the INT_ID returned from the read of GICV_IAR. |
