### WCSS_A_DXE_0_CH3_DADRL
**Address:** `0x0A2024D4`
**Type:** `RW`
**Reset State:** `0x00000000`

The channel destination address register specifies either the destination address in flat internal or external memory, or else the BMU queue ID, UIF RX endpoint ID, or EIF outbound FIFO ID for the transfer. The register must be programmed directly by software before the channel is enabled, then, once the DMA channel is enabled, the register is updated after each atomic chunk transfer (read+write) with the number of bytes transferred. (except when using a UIF/EIF queue) and also after loading a new descriptor When using flat memory as the destination, addresses can have arbitrary byte-alignment. When using a BMU queue, UIF endpoint or EIF fifo as a destination, the software is responsible for programming a valid queue ID and correct base address for the queue. The layout of bitfields in this register depends on the setting of the `CH_CSR[DIQ]` bit. When this bit is clear then the register has no bitfields and the full 32-bits are interpreted as the physical address of a location in flat memory, and when the bit is set this register has two bitfields: The DQID bitfield used to specify the queue ID, and the BASE bitfield used to provide the base address for the UIF or EIF destination endpoint/FIFO.

For H2B or B2B transfers, when using a BMU queue as the destination (`CH_CSR[DIQ]` = 1 and DQID matches BMU), the DXE will push the index of the BD of the packet into the specified queue at the end of the packet transfer. Therefore, software is responsible for programming a valid BMU Queue ID.

Else, when the destination is an index (`CH_CSR[DIQ]` = 0), the BD will be written to the address obtained by adding the provided index to the BMU_BASE, again, the software must ensure that said address is legal and known to BMU. That is, software must preallocate the BD (get the BD from BMU via GET BD/PDU cmd) for the BD before starting the transfer. For B2H or H2H transfers, if the destination is a UIF endpoint or EIF FIFO (`CH_CSR[DIQ]` = 1 and DQID matches UIF/EIF), SW should program the SAHB base address of the UIF destination endpoint in the
<!-- page 1608 -->
### WCSS_A_DXE_0_CH3_DADRL (cont.)

... BASE bitfield and the queue ID to match in the `DQID` bitfield, then the DXE will use the base address given to generate the physical address and write the data over the SAHB bus and also use the appropriate sideband signals as specified by the `DQID` field to communicate with the selected UIF endpoint. SW should make sure that the BASE and `DQID` fields are consistent and refer to the same endpoint else hangs or unpredictable behavior might occur. On the other hand, when the destination is just a location in flat memory space, (`CH_CSR[DIQ]` = 0), be it internal or external, the bitfields lose their special meaning and DXE will just use the full 32-bits programmed into the register as the address to write the data. For this case, SW should make sure that the address maps to the intended destination interface (Internal memory, USB, PCI, PCIe) by conforming to the address map specified for the SAHB bus.

To summarize, for H2B and B2B transfers the address must conform to the following format:

For index of BD mode (`CH_CSR[DIQ]` = 0):
```c
ADDR[31:7] = BMU_BASE + BD_INDEX[15:0]
ADDR[ 6:0] = 7'd0
```

For BMU Queue ID mode (`CH_CSR[DIQ]` = 1 & DQID matching one of the BMU queues):
```c
ADDR[31:5] = Any value will do but zero preferred
ADDR[ 4:0] = Any BMU Queue ID as specified in description of QID field
```

For B2H and H2H transfers the address must conform to the following format:

For destinations in flat memory space (`CH_CSR[DIQ]` = 0):
```c
ADDR[31:0] = address mapping to destination interface
```

For UIF RX endpoints or EIF FIFOs (`CH_CSR[DIQ]` = 1 & DQID matching UIF or EIF):
```c
ADDR[31:5] = UIF RX endpoint base or EIF inbound FIFO base
ADDR[ 4:0] = Queue ID matching UIF or EIF as specified in description of DQID field
```

| Bits | Name | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:7 | BASE | RW | Base Address. Valid only when the `CH_CSR[DIQ]` bit is set. For this case, this bitfield provides the base address of the destination UIF RX endpoint or EIF outbound FIFO (for BMU SW may use any value can be used but zero is suggested).<br>Consult the appropriate interface uarch for the offset within the interface's address space. When `CH_CSR[SIQ]` (sic, probably `DIQ`) bit is not set this field loses its special meaning and is interpreted only as part of the full 32-bit source (sic, probably destination) address. |
<!-- page 1609 -->

### WCSS_A_DXE_0_CH3_DESCL
**Address:** `0x0A2024DC`
**Type:** `RW`
**Reset State:** `0x00000000`

The Channel 3 Linked List Descriptor Pointer register contains the 32 lower bits of the address of the next descriptor to be loaded in the linked list. This address must be dword (32-bit) aligned (`addr[1:0]`=0 if `CH_CTRL[PIQ]`=0). Each complete transfer descriptor consists of 7 32-bit values arranged contiguously in memory. The value of this register will be overwritten with the address of the start of the next descriptor set in the list after the current descriptor has been fetched. The meaning of the value in this register depends on the value of the `CH_CTRL[PIQ]` bitfield similar to the way in which `SADRL` and `DADRL` are depending in `SIQ` and `DIQ` respectively. For `CH_CTRL[PIQ]`=0 then this register has no bitfields and the value is just interpreted as an address in flat memory space. When `CH_CTRL[PIQ]` is set then the descriptor will be read from FIFO type memory in UIF and the register has 2 bitfields: BASE, and SQID. BASE specifies the base address of the UIF Tx queue (derived from the start of the UIF address space in SAHB plus the internal UIF offset).


<!-- page 1611 -->

### WCSS_A_DXE_0_CH3_DESCL

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:7 | BASE | This bitfield only exists and has meaning when the descriptor needs to be read from a UIF TX queue (and therefore CH_CTRL[PIQ]=1), then it serves to specify the base address of the UIF endpoint to use as the source of the descriptor. Refer to the Nova address map document and to the UIF architecture document for guaranteed correct values to use here. For convenience but without a guarantee of accuracy, the base value to use for both the Tx data and management endpoints is the following:<br>base = UIF base + TD_and_TM_offset = 0x0E02_5000 + x100 = 0x0E02_5100>>7 = 0x1C_04A2 |
| 6:0 | SQID | This bitfield only exists and has meaning when the descriptor needs to be read from a UIF TX queue (and therefore CH_CTRL[PIQ]=1), then it serves to specify which of the two UIF TX queues to use. Note that in this case SW also needs to program the correct base address of the source UIF endpoint in the BASE bitfield.<br>0x0: UIF_TX_DATA_EP (Descriptor to be read from UIF TX Data Endpoint)<br>0x1: UIF_TX_MGMT_EP (Descriptor to be read from UIF TX Management Endpoint) |

**Address:** 0x0A202500

The BD template base store is pointed at by the DXE BD_TMPLT(H/L) registers and the address used to read the template data is calculated as follows:<br>BD_TMPLT_ADRR = BD_TMPLT_BASE + (128 * CH_CTRL[BDT_IDX]) The corresponding bitfield in the control word of the external descriptor is mapped to bits[19:18] |

### WCSS_A_DXE_0_CH4_CTRL (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 27 | ABORT | RW | Writing a one to this bit will cause the channel to stop its current transfer and set the ERR bit and ERR_CODE fields in CH_STATUS. Note that if the channel is currently disabled or if it is about to be disabled because it has just finished its programmed transfer, then the abort request will be ignored and the error bit and error codes won't be set. If the channel is currently masked by the arbiter then setting this bit will forcibly unmask it so that the transfer can be aborted the next time the channel is selected by the internal arbiter. The abort request is automatically cleared by hw once the channel has aborted the transfer. Also note that since the DXE will not attempt to do any cleanup when a transfer is aborted, software might need to do so. For example, for H2B transfers, SW should manually release the BD and any PDUs currently in use by the partial transfer or else a BD/PDU leak will result. |
| 26 | ENDIANNESS | RW | Specifies the endianness of the master generating the data. Affects alignment of valid bytes for non-dword aligned reads/writes. | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 7 | PIQ | RW | next descriptor Pointer address Is Queue. When set the source of the descriptor address is interpreted as a queue ID instead of just the address of a flat memory location. The only valid source queues for descriptors are the UIF Tx data and Tx management endpoints. Any other IDs will result the channel aborting the transfer with an invalid source queue error. Therefore, when this bit is set, SW must ensure that the CH_DESCL[QID] bitfield is set to a valid queue ID and that the CH_DESCL[BASE] bitfield is set to the base address of the source UIF endpoint. This base address is formed by taking the base address for the UIF block in the SAHB bus which can be found in the Nova address map document and then adding the internal UIF offset for the correct source endpoint. This offsets can be obtained from the UIF specification document. For convenience, the current internal UIF offsets are provided in the description of the QID bitfield in the CH_DESCL register description.<br>0x0: FLAT (Source address maps to regular flat memory)<br>0x1: QUEUE (Source address maps to FIFO type memory (UIF Tx endpoints)) |
| 6 | DIQ | RW | Destination Is Queue. When set the destination address is interpreted as a queue ID instead of just the address of a flat memory location. The queue could be either a BMU queue, one of the UIF RX endpoints or and EIF outbound FIFO. When this bit is set, SW must ensure that the DADR[QID] bitfield is set to a valid queue ID and that the DADR[BASE] bitfield is set to the base address of the destination queue for UIF or EIF, or to zero for a BMU queue. endpoint.<br>0x0: FLAT (Destination address maps to regular flat memory)<br>0x1: QUEUE (Destination address maps to a BMU queue or FIFO type memory) |
| 5 | SIQ | RW | Source Is Queue. When set the source address is interpreted as a queue ID instead of just the address of a flat memory location. The queue could be either a BMU queue, one of the UIF TX endpoints or and EIF inbound FIFO. When this bit is set, SW must ensure that the SADR[QID] bitfield is set to a valid queue ID and that the SADR[BASE] bitfield is set to the base address of the source queue for UIF or EIF, or to zero for a BMU queue. endpoint.<br>0x0: FLAT (Source address maps to regular flat memory)<br>0x1: QUEUE (Source address maps to a BMU queue or FIFO type memory) |

### WCSS_A_DXE_0_CH4_CTRL (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 4 | BDH | RW | BD Handling bit. The behavior depends on the setting of XTYPE.<br>If XTYPE is:<br>H2B: Then if BDH is:<br>0: Use first 128 bytes of packet as BD.<br>1: Create BD from BD template (Up to 4 supported. Also see desc for BDT_IDX).<br>B2H: Then if BDH is:<br>0: Insert BD in front of payload.<br>1: Discard BD.<br>For XTYPE values of H2H and B2B the value of this bit is ignored. |
| 3 | EOP | RW | End of Packet bit. For H2B transfers marks the end of a packet. Note that when not using external descriptors DXE cannot support the gather functionality and therefore the EOP bit must be set. For XTYPE values of H2H, B2B and B2H the value of this bit is ignored. |
| 2:1 | XTYPE | RW | Transfer Type. Specifies the type of transfer to perform:<br>00: H2H. Host space to Host space transfer.<br>01: B2B. BMU space to BMU space transfer.<br>10: H2B. Host space to BMU translation.<br>11: B2H. BMU space to Host space translation.<br>For cross-space transfers (H2B and B2H) the DMA engine will also perform the required data format translation. The format translation behavior can be modified by the setting of the BDH and PAD bits.<br>0x0: H2H (Host space to Host space transfer)<br>0x1: B2B (BMU space to BMU space transfer)<br>0x2: H2B (Host space to BMU space transfer)<br>0x3: B2H (BMU space to Host space transfer) |
<!-- page 1620 -->

### WCSS_A_DXE_0_CH4_CTRL (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 0 | EN | RW | Channel Enable or Restart. Writing this bit with a one either starts a new DMA transfer according to the parameters programmed in the channel's configuration registers and clears the DONE bit or, if the channel is already enabled but the STOP bit is set, then it restarts channel processing and also clears the STOP bit. This bit is automatically cleared when a single transfer completes or, if the channel is configured to use linked list descriptors, when the last transfer in the descriptor linked list completes (DESC_NXT is NULL or/and DESC_CSR[VALID]=0). The channel is also disabled and this bit cleared if a channel error is encountered. Reading this bit indicates whether a channel is currently enabled or disabled:.<br>0: Channel Disabled.<br>1: Channel Enabled.<br>The Channel Enable bit status can also be found by reading the DMA_ENCH register which aggregates the EN bits of all channels. Note: Software must take care to not disable the channel while it is busy or data could be lost. |

### 0x0A202508 WCSS_A_DXE_0_CH4_SZ

**Type:** RW  
**Reset State:** 0x00000000  

The transfer size register specifies the total, remaining, and burst or 'chunk' transfer sizes for each channel. The maximum total transfer size is 16K-1 bytes. The chunk size control can be useful to control the relative bandwidth used by each channel as the dma engine will change channels, release the AHB bus, and rearbitrate for access after transferring chunk size bytes.

#### WCSS_A_DXE_0_CH4_SZ

| Bits | Name | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:28 | CHK_SZ | RW | Chunk transfer size. Specifies the number of bytes (in multiples of 8) to be transferred at one given time (not implying they are buffered but that they will be transferred for each start event in one bus request cycle). If chunk size is zero the DMA engine will always perform maximum chunk size transfers. Maximum chunk size is 128 bytes. |
| 27:14 | REM_SZ | R | Remaining transfer size. Specifies the number of bytes that remain to be transferred to complete the current operation. |
<!-- page 1623 -->

### WCSS_A_DXE_0_CH4_SZ (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 13:0 | TOT_SZ | RW | Total Transfer Size. Specifies the number of bytes to be transferred. Maximum total transfer size is (4K-1) bytes.<br>Note: This field is unnecessary and will be ignored for B2H or B2B transfers, when the source of the transfer is in BMU space (either BMU queue or direct pointer to BD). This is because the size of the transfer will be the packet length encoded in the BD at offset 0x0c bits [11:0]. |

### 0x0A20250C WCSS_A_DXE_0_CH4_SADRL

**Type:** RW  
**Reset State:** 0x00000000  

The channel source address register specifies either the source address in flat internal or external memory, or else the BMU queue ID, UIF TX endpoint ID, or EIF inbound FIFO ID for the transfer. The register must be programmed directly by software before the channel is enabled, then, once the DMA channel is enabled, the register is updated after each atomic chunk transfer (read+write) with the number of bytes transferred (except when using a UIF/EIF queue) and also after loading a new descriptor. When using flat memory as the source, addresses can have arbitrary byte-alignment. When using a BMU queue, UIF endpoint or EIF fifo as a source, the software is responsible for programming a valid queue ID and correct base address for the queue. The layout of bitfields in this register depends on the setting of the CH_CSR[SIQ] bit. When CH_CSR[SIQ] is clear then the register has no bitfields and the full 32-bits are interpreted as the physical address of a location in flat memory, and when it is set this register has two bitfields: The SQID bitfield used to specify the queue ID, and the BASE bitfield used to provide the base address for the UIF or EIF source endpoint/FIFO.

For B2H or B2B transfers, when the source is a BMU Queue ID (CH_CSR[SIQ] = 1 and SWQID matches BMU), the DXE will issue a BMU POPWQ command to pop the specified queue and obtain the BD index of the source packet. Else, when the source is an address (CH_CSR[SIQ] = 0), the DXE will interpret the address as the index of the packet BD and will add it to the BMU_BASE to obtain the physical addresss to use to fetch it directly from memory.

For H2B or H2H transfers, if the source is a UIF endpoint or EIF FIFO (CH_CSR[SIQ] = 1 and SQID matches UIF/EIF), SW should program the SAHB base address of the UIF source endpoint in the BASE bitfield and the queue ID to match in the SWQID bitfield, then the DXE will use the base address given to generate the physical address and read the data over the SAHB bus and also use the appropriate sideband signals as specified by the SQID field to communicate with the selected UIF endpoint. SW should make sure that the BASE and SQID fields are consistend and refer to the same endpoint or else hangs or unpredictable behavior might occur. Else, when the source is just a location in flat memory space, (CH_CSR[SIQ] = 0), the bitfields lose their special meaning and DXE will just use the full 32-bits programmed into the register as the physical address to use to fetch the data. For this case, SW should make sure that the provided address maps to the intended source interface (Internal memory, USB, PCI, PCIe) by conforming to the address map specified for the SAHB bus.

To summarize, for B2H and B2B transfers the address must conform to the following format:
<!-- page 1624 -->

For index of BD mode (`CH_CSR[SIQ]` = 0):
```
ADDR[31:7] = BMU_BASE + BD_INDEX[15:0]
ADDR[ 6:0] = 7'd0
```

For BMU Queue ID mode (`CH_CSR[SIQ]` = 1 & SQID matching one of the BMU queues):
```
ADDR[31:7] = Any value will do but zero preferred
ADDR[ 6:0] = Any BMU Queue ID as specified in description of SQID field
```

For H2B and H2H transfers the address must conform to the following format:

* For sources in flat memory space (`CH_CSR[SIQ]` = 0): `ADDR[31:0]` = address mapping to source interface
* For UIF RX endpoints or EIF FIFOs (`CH_CSR[SIQ]` = 1 & QID matching UIF or EIF):
  ```
  ADDR[31:7] = UIF RX endpoint base or EIF inbound FIFO base
  ADDR[ 6:0] = Queue ID matching UIF or EIF as specified in description of SQID field
  ```

#### WCSS_A_DXE_0_CH4_SADRL

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:7 | BASE | Base Address.<br>Valid only when the `CH_CSR[SIQ]` bit is set. For this case, this bitfield provides the base address of the source UIF TX endpoint or EIF inbound FIFO.<br>Consult the appropriate interface uarch for the offset within the interface's address space. When `CH_CSR[SIQ]` bit is not set this field loses its special meaning and is interpreted only as part of the full 32-bit source address. |
<!-- page 1625 -->

When `CH_CSR[SIQ]` bit is not set this field loses its special meaning and is interpreted only as part of the full 32-bit source address.<br>0x0: UIF_TX_DATA_EP (UIF TX Data Endpoint)<br>0x1: UIF_TX_MGMT_EP (UIF TX Management Endpoint)<br>0x2: BMU_2 (BMU Work Queue 2)<br>0x3: BMU_3 (BMU Work Queue 3)<br>0x4: BMU_4 (BMU Work Queue 4)<br>0x5: BMU_5 (BMU Work Queue 5)<br>0x6: BMU_6 (BMU Work Queue 6)<br>0x7: BMU_7 (BMU Work Queue 7)<br>0x8: BMU_8 (BMU Work Queue 8)<br>0x9: BMU_9 (BMU Work Queue 9)<br>0xA: BMU_10 (BMU Work Queue 10)<br>0xB: BMU_11 (BMU Work Queue 11)<br>0xC: BMU_12 (BMU Work Queue 12)<br>0xD: BMU_13 (BMU Work Queue 13)<br>0xE: BMU_14 (BMU Work Queue 14)<br>0xF: BMU_15 (BMU Work Queue 15)<br>0x10: BMU_16 (BMU Work Queue 16)<br>0x11: BMU_17 (BMU Work Queue 17)<br>0x12: BMU_18 (BMU Work Queue 18)<br>0x13: BMU_19 (BMU Work Queue 19)<br>0x14: BMU_20 (BMU Work Queue 20)<br>0x15: BMU_21 (BMU Work Queue 21)<br>0x16: BMU_22 (BMU Work Queue 22)<br>0x17: BMU_23 (BMU Work Queue 23)<br>0x18: BMU_24 (BMU Work Queue 24)<br>0x19: RSVD_25 (Reserved)<br>0x1A: RSVD_26 (Reserved)<br>0x1B: RSVD_27 (Reserved)<br>0x1C: RSVD_28 (Reserved)<br>0x1D: RSVD_29 (Reserved)<br>0x1E: RSVD_30 (Reserved)<br>0x1F: RSVD_31 (Reserved) |

### 0x0A202514 WCSS_A_DXE_0_CH4_DADRL

**Type:** RW  
**Reset State:** 0x00000000  

The channel destination address register specifies either the destination address in flat internal or external memory, or else the BMU queue ID, UIF RX endpoint ID, or EIF outbound FIFO ID for the transfer. The register must be programmed directly by software before the channel is enabled, then, once the DMA channel is enabled, the register is updated after each atomic chunk transfer (read+write) with the number of bytes transferred (except when using a UIF/EIF queue) and also after loading a new descriptor. When using flat memory as the destination, addresses can have arbitrary byte-alignment. When using a BMU queue, UIF endpoint or EIF fifo as a destination, the software is responsible for programming a valid queue ID and correct base address for the queue. The layout of bitfields in this register depends on the setting of the `CH_CSR[DIQ]` bit. When this bit is clear then the register has no bitfields and the full 32-bits are interpreted as the physical address of a location in flat memory, and when the bit is set this register has two bitfields: The DQID bitfield used to specify the queue ID, and the BASE bitfield used to provide the base address for the UIF or EIF destination endpoint/FIFO.

For H2B or B2B transfers, when using a BMU queue as the destination (`CH_CSR[DIQ]` = 1 and DQID matches BMU), the DXE will push the index of the BD of the packet into the specified queue at the end of the packet transfer. Therefore, software is responsible for programming a valid BMU Queue ID.

Else, when the destination is an index (`CH_CSR[DIQ]` = 0), the BD will be written to the address obtained by adding the provided index to the BMU_BASE, again, the software must ensure that said address is legal and known to BMU. That is, software must preallocate the BD (get the BD from BMU via GET BD/PDU cmd) for the BD before starting the transfer. For B2H or H2H transfers, if the destination is a UIF endpoint or EIF FIFO (`CH_CSR[DIQ]` = 1 and DQID matches UIF/EIF), SW should program the SAHB base address of the UIF destination endpoint in the
<!-- page 1627 -->

... BASE bitfield and the queue ID to match in the `DQID` bitfield, then the DXE will use the base address given to generate the physical address and write the data over the SAHB bus and also use the appropriate sideband signals as specified by the `DQID` field to communicate with the selected UIF endpoint. SW should make sure that the BASE and DQID fields are consistent and refer to the same endpoint else hangs or unpredictable behavior might occur. On the other hand, when the destination is just a location in flat memory space, (`CH_CSR[DIQ]` = 0), be it internal or external, the bitfields lose their special meaning and DXE will just use the full 32-bits programmed into the register as the address to write the data. For this case, SW should make sure that the address maps to the intended destination interface (Internal memory, USB, PCI, PCIe) by conforming to the address map specified for the SAHB bus. To summarize, for H2B and B2B transfers the address must conform to the following format:

For index of BD mode (`CH_CSR[DIQ]` = 0):
```
ADDR[31:7] = BMU_BASE + BD_INDEX[15:0]
ADDR[ 6:0] = 7'd0
```

For BMU Queue ID mode (`CH_CSR[DIQ]` = 1 & DQID matching one of the BMU queues):
```
ADDR[31:5] = Any value will do but zero preferred
ADDR[ 4:0] = Any BMU Queue ID as specified in description of QID field
```

For B2H and H2H transfers the address must conform to the following format:

* For destinations in flat memory space (`CH_CSR[DIQ]` = 0): `ADDR[31:0]` = address mapping to destination interface
* For UIF RX endpoints or EIF FIFOs (`CH_CSR[DIQ]` = 1 & DQID matching UIF or EIF):
  ```
  ADDR[31:5] = UIF RX endpoint base or EIF inbound FIFO base
  ADDR[ 4:0] = Queue ID matching UIF or EIF as specified in description of DQID field
  ```

#### WCSS_A_DXE_0_CH4_DADRL

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:7 | BASE | Base Address.<br>Valid only when the `CH_CSR[DIQ]` bit is set. For this case, this bitfield provides the base address of the destination UIF RX endpoint or EIF outbound FIFO (for BMU SW may use any value can be used but zero is suggested).<br>Consult the appropriate interface uarch for the offset within the interface's address space. When `CH_CSR[SIQ]` (sic, probably DIQ) bit is not set this field loses its special meaning and is interpreted only as part of the full 32-bit source (sic, probably destination) address. |
<!-- page 1628 -->

### WCSS_A_DXE_0_CH4_DADRL (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 6:0 | DQID | Destination Queue ID.<br>Valid only when the `CH_CSR[SIQ]` (sic, probably `DIQ`) bit is set. For this case, this bitfield provides the ID for the destination BMU WQ, UIF RX endpoint or EIF outbound queue to be used for the transfer. When `CH_CSR[SIQ]` (sic, probably `DIQ`) bit is not set this field loses its special meaning and is interpreted only as part of the full 32-bit source (sic, probably destination) address.<br>0x0: RSVD_0 (Reserved)<br>0x1: RSVD_1 (Reserved)<br>0x2: BMU_2 (BMU Work Queue 2)<br>0x3: BMU_3 (BMU Work Queue 3)<br>0x4: BMU_4 (BMU Work Queue 4)<br>0x5: BMU_5 (BMU Work Queue 5)<br>0x6: BMU_6 (BMU Work Queue 6)<br>0x7: BMU_7 (BMU Work Queue 7)<br>0x8: BMU_8 (BMU Work Queue 8)<br>0x9: BMU_9 (BMU Work Queue 9)<br>0xA: BMU_10 (BMU Work Queue 10)<br>0xB: BMU_11 (BMU Work Queue 11)<br>0xC: BMU_12 (BMU Work Queue 12)<br>0xD: BMU_13 (BMU Work Queue 13)<br>0xE: BMU_14 (BMU Work Queue 14)<br>0xF: BMU_15 (BMU Work Queue 15)<br>0x10: BMU_16 (BMU Work Queue 16)<br>0x11: BMU_17 (BMU Work Queue 17)<br>0x12: BMU_18 (BMU Work Queue 18)<br>0x13: BMU_19 (BMU Work Queue 19)<br>0x14: BMU_20 (BMU Work Queue 20)<br>0x15: BMU_21 (BMU Work Queue 21)<br>0x16: BMU_22 (BMU Work Queue 22)<br>0x17: BMU_23 (BMU Work Queue 23)<br>0x18: BMU_24 (BMU Work Queue 24)<br>0x19: BMU_25 (BMU Work Queue 25)<br>0x1A: BMU_26 (BMU Work Queue 26)<br>0x1B: BMU_SINK_WQ (BMU_SINK (WQ255))<br>0x1C: UIF_RX_1_EP (UIF RX 1 endpoint)<br>0x1D: UIF_RX_2_EP (UIF RX 2 endpoint)<br>0x1E: UIF_RX_3_EP (UIF RX 3 endpoint)<br>0x1F: UIF_RX_4_EP (UIF RX 4 endpoint) |

### 0x0A20251C WCSS_A_DXE_0_CH4_DESCL

**Type:** RW  
**Reset State:** 0x00000000  

The Channel 4 Linked List Descriptor Pointer register contains the 32 lower bits of the address of the next descriptor to be loaded in the linked list. This address must be dword (32-bit) aligned (addr[1:0]=0 if `CH_CTRL[PIQ]`=0). Each complete transfer descriptor consists of 7 32-bit values arranged contiguously in memory. The value of this register will be overwritten with the address of the start of the next descriptor set in the list after the current descriptor has been fetched. The meaning of the value in this register depends on the value of the `CH_CTRL[PIQ]` bitfield similar to the way in which `SADRL` and `DADRL` are depending in `SIQ` and `DIQ` respectively. For `CH_CTRL[PIQ]`=0 then this register has no bitfields and the value is just intrepreted as an address in flat memory space. When `CH_CTRL[PIQ]` is set then the descriptor will be read from FIFO type memory in UIF and the register has 2 bitfields: BASE, and SQID. BASE specifies the base address of the UIF Tx queue (derived from the start of the UIF address space in SAHB plus the internal UIF offset).
<!-- page 1630 -->

### WCSS_A_DXE_0_CH4_DESCL (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:7 | BASE | This bitfield only exists and has meaning when the descriptor needs to be read from a UIF TX queue (and therefore `CH_CTRL[PIQ]`=1), then it serves to specify the base address of the UIF endpoint to use as the source of the descriptor. Refer to the Nova address map document and to the UIF architecture document for guaranteed correct values to use here. For convenience but without a guarantee of accuracy, the base value to use for both the Tx data and management endpoints is the following:<br>base = UIF base + TD_and_TM_offset = 0x0E02_5000 + x100 = 0x0E02_5100>>7 = 0x1C_04A2 |
| 6:0 | SQID | This bitfield only exists and has meaning when the descriptor needs to be read from a UIF TX queue (and therefore `CH_CTRL[PIQ]`=1), then it serves to specify which of the two UIF TX queues to use. Note that in this case SW also needs to program the correct base address of the source UIF endpoint in the BASE bitfield.<br>0x0: UIF_TX_DATA_EP (Descriptor to be read from UIF TX Data Endpoint)<br>0x1: UIF_TX_MGMT_EP (Descriptor to be read from UIF TX Management Endpoint) |

Writing this bit with a one either starts a new DMA transfer according to the parameters programmed in the channel's configuration registers and clears the DONE bit or, if the channel is already enabled but the STOP bit is set, then it restarts channel processing and also clears the STOP bit. This bit is automatically cleared when a single transfer completes or, if the channel is configured to use linked list descriptors, when the last transfer in the descriptor linked list completes (DESC_NXT is NULL or/and DESC_CSR[VALID]=0). The channel is also disabled and this bit cleared if a channel error is encountered. Reading this bit indicates whether a channel is currently enabled or disabled:.<br>0: Channel Disabled.<br>1: Channel Enabled.<br>The Channel Enable bit status can also be found by reading the DMA_ENCH register which aggregates the EN bits of all channels. ### WCSS_A_DXE_0_CH5_SZ
**Address:** 0x0A202548
**Type:** RW
**Reset State:** 0x00000000

The transfer size register specifies the total, remaining, and burst or 'chunk' transfer sizes for each channel. The maximum total transfer size is 16K-1 bytes. The chunk size control can be useful to control the relative bandwidth used by each channel as the dma engine will change channels, release the AHB bus, and rearbitrate for access after transferring chunk size bytes.

| Bits | Name | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:28 | CHK_SZ | RW | Chunk transfer size. Specifies the number of bytes (in multiples of 8) to be transferred at one given time (not implying they are buffered but that they will be transferred for each start event in one bus request cycle). If chunk size is zero the DMA engine will always perform maximum chunk size transfers. Maximum chunk size is 128 bytes. |
| 27:14 | REM_SZ | R | Remaining transfer size. Specifies the number of bytes that remain to be transferred to complete the current operation. |
<!-- page 1642 -->
### WCSS_A_DXE_0_CH5_SZ (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 13:0 | TOT_SZ | RW | Total Transfer Size. Specifies the number of bytes to be transferred. Maximum total transfer size is (4K-1) bytes.<br>Note: This field is unnecessary and will be ignored for B2H or B2B transfers, when the source of the transfer is in BMU space (either BMU queue or direct pointer to BD). This is because the size of the transfer will be the packet length encoded in the BD at offset 0x0c bits [11:0]. |

### WCSS_A_DXE_0_CH5_SADRL
**Address:** 0x0A20254C
**Type:** RW
**Reset State:** 0x00000000

The channel source address register specifies either the source address in flat internal or external memory, or else the BMU queue ID, UIF TX endpoint ID, or EIF inbound FIFO ID for the transfer. The register must be programmed directly by software before the channel is enabled, then, once the DMA channel is enabled, the register is updated after each atomic chunk transfer (read+write) with the number of bytes transferred. (except when using a UIF/EIF queue) and also after loading a new descriptor. When using flat memory as the source, addresses can have arbitrary byte-alignment. When using a BMU queue, UIF endpoint or EIF fifo as a source, the software is responsible for programming a valid queue ID and correct base address for the queue. The layout of bitfields in this register depends on the setting of the CH_CSR[SIQ] bit. When CH_CSR[SIQ] is clear then the register has no bitfields and the full 32-bits are interpreted as the physical address of a location in flat memory, and when it is set this register has two bitfields: The SQID bitfield used to specify the queue ID, and the BASE bitfield used to provide the base address for the UIF or EIF source endpoint/FIFO.

For B2H or B2B transfers, when the source is a BMU Queue ID (CH_CSR[SIQ] = 1 and SWQID matches BMU), the DXE will issue a BMU POPWQ command to pop the specified queue and obtain the BD index of the source packet. Else, when the source is an address (CH_CSR[SIQ] = 0), the DXE will interpret the address as the index of the packet BD and will add it to the BMU_BASE to obtain the physical addresss to use to fetch it directly from memory.

For H2B or H2H transfers, if the source is a UIF endpoint or EIF FIFO (CH_CSR[SIQ] = 1 and SQID matches UIF/EIF), SW should program the SAHB base address of the UIF source endpoint in the BASE bitfield and the queue ID to match in the SWQID bitfield, then the DXE will use the base address given to generate the physical address and read the data over the SAHB bus and also use the appropriate sideband signals as specified by the SQID field to communicate with the selected UIF endpoint. SW should make sure that the BASE and SQID fields are consistent and refer to the same endpoint or else hangs or unpredictable behavior might occur. Else, when the source is just a location in flat memory space, (CH_CSR[SIQ] = 0), the bitfields lose their special meaning and DXE will just use the full 32-bits programmed into the register as the physical address to use to fetch the data. For this case, SW should make sure that the provided address maps to the intended source interface (Internal memory, USB, PCI, PCIe) by conforming to the address map specified for the SAHB bus.

To summarize, for B2H and B2B transfers the address must conform to the following format:
<!-- page 1643 -->
For index of BD mode (CH_CSR[SIQ] = 0):
* ADDR[31:7] = BMU_BASE + BD_INDEX[15:0]
* ADDR[6:0] = 7'd0

For BMU Queue ID mode (CH_CSR[SIQ] = 1 & SQID matching one of the BMU queues):
* ADDR[31:7] = Any value will do but zero preferred
* ADDR[6:0] = Any BMU Queue ID as specified in description of SQID field

For H2B and H2H transfers the address must conform to the following format:
* For sources in flat memory space (CH_CSR[SIQ] = 0): ADDR[31:0] = address mapping to source interface
* For UIF RX endpoints or EIF FIFOs (CH_CSR[SIQ] = 1 & QID matching UIF or EIF):
    * ADDR[31:7] = UIF RX endpoint base or EIF inbound FIFO base
    * ADDR[6:0] = Queue ID matching UIF or EIF as specified in description of SQID field

### WCSS_A_DXE_0_CH5_DADRL
**Address:** 0x0A202554
**Type:** RW
**Reset State:** 0x00000000

The channel destination address register specifies either the destination address in flat internal or external memory, or else the BMU queue ID, UIF RX endpoint ID, or EIF outbound FIFO ID for the transfer. The register must be programmed directly by software before the channel is enabled, then, once the DMA channel is enabled, the register is updated after each atomic chunk transfer (read+write) with the number of bytes transferred (except when using a UIF/EIF queue) and also after loading a new descriptor. When using flat memory as the destination, addresses can have arbitrary byte-alignment. When using a BMU queue, UIF endpoint or EIF fifo as a destination, the software is responsible for programming a valid queue ID and correct base address for the queue. The layout of bitfields in this register depends on the setting of the CH_CSR[DIQ] bit. When this bit is clear then the register has no bitfields and the full 32-bits are interpreted as the physical address of a location in flat memory, and when the bit is set this register has two bitfields: The DQID bitfield used to specify the queue ID, and the BASE bitfield used to provide the base address for the UIF or EIF destination endpoint/FIFO.

For H2B or B2B transfers, when using a BMU queue as the destination (CH_CSR[DIQ] = 1 and DQID matches BMU), the DXE will push the index of the BD of the packet into the specified queue at the end of the packet transfer. Therefore, software is responsible for programming a valid BMU Queue ID.

Else, when the destination is an index (CH_CSR[DIQ] = 0), the BD will be written to the address obtained by adding the provided index to the BMU_BASE, again, the software must ensure that said address is legal and known to BMU. That is, software must preallocate the BD (get the BD from BMU via GET BD/PDU cmd) for the BD before starting the transfer. For B2H or H2H transfers, if the destination is a UIF endpoint or EIF FIFO (CH_CSR[DIQ] = 1 and DQID matches UIF/EIF), SW should program the SAHB base address of the UIF destination endpoint in the
<!-- page 1646 -->
...BASE bitfield and the queue ID to match in the DQID bitfield, then the DXE will use the base address given to generate the physical address and write the data over the SAHB bus and also use the appropriate sideband signals as specified by the DQID field to communicate with the selected UIF endpoint. SW should make sure that the BASE and DQID fields are consistent and refer to the same endpoint else hangs or unpredictable behavior might occur. On the other hand, when the destination is just a location in flat memory space, (CH_CSR[DIQ] = 0), be it internal or external, the bitfields lose their special meaning and DXE will just use the full 32-bits programmed into the register as the address to write the data. For this case, SW should make sure that the address maps to the intended destination interface (Internal memory, USB, PCI, PCIe) by conforming to the address map specified for the SAHB bus.

To summarize, for H2B and B2B transfers the address must conform to the following format:
* For index of BD mode (CH_CSR[DIQ] = 0):
  * ADDR[31:7] = BMU_BASE + BD_INDEX[15:0]
  * ADDR[6:0] = 7'd0
* For BMU Queue ID mode (CH_CSR[DIQ] = 1 & DQID matching one of the BMU queues):
  * ADDR[31:5] = Any value will do but zero preferred
  * ADDR[4:0] = Any BMU Queue ID as specified in description of QID field

For B2H and H2H transfers the address must conform to the following format:
* For destinations in flat memory space (CH_CSR[DIQ] = 0): ADDR[31:0] = address mapping to destination interface
* For UIF RX endpoints or EIF FIFOs (CH_CSR[DIQ] = 1 & DQID matching UIF or EIF):
  * ADDR[31:5] = UIF RX endpoint base or EIF inbound FIFO base
  * ADDR[4:0] = Queue ID matching UIF or EIF as specified in description of DQID field

### WCSS_A_DXE_0_CH5_DESCL
**Address:** 0x0A20255C
**Type:** RW
**Reset State:** 0x00000000

The Channel 5 Linked List Descriptor Pointer register contains the 32 lower bits of the address of the next descriptor to be loaded in the linked list. This address must be dword (32-bit) aligned (addr[1:0]=0 if CH_CTRL[PIQ]=0). Each complete transfer descriptor consists of 7 32-bit values arranged contiguously in memory. The value of this register will be overwritten with the address of the start of the next descriptor set in the list after the current descriptor has been fetched. The meaning of the value in this register depends on the value of the CH_CTRL[PIQ] bitfield similar to the way in which SADRL and DADRL are depending in SIQ and DIQ respectively. For CH_CTRL[PIQ]=0 then this register has no bitfields and the value is just interpreted as an address in flat memory space. When CH_CTRL[PIQ] is set then the descriptor will be read from FIFO type memory in UIF and the register has 2 bitfields: BASE, and SQID. BASE specifies the base address of the UIF Tx queue (derived from the start of the UIF address space in SAHB plus the internal UIF offset).
<!-- page 1649 -->
### WCSS_A_DXE_0_CH5_DESCL (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:7 | BASE | This bitfield only exists and has meaning when the descriptor needs to be read from a UIF TX queue (and therefore CH_CTRL[PIQ]=1), then it serves to specify the base address of the UIF endpoint to use as the source of the descriptor. Refer to the Nova address map document and to the UIF architecture document for guaranteed correct values to use here. For convenience but without a guarantee of accuracy, the base value to use for both the Tx data and management endpoints is the following:<br>base = UIF base + TD_and_TM_offset = 0x0E02_5000 + x100 = 0x0E02_5100>>7 = 0x1C_04A2 |
| 6:0 | SQID | This bitfield only exists and has meaning when the descriptor needs to be read from a UIF TX queue (and therefore CH_CTRL[PIQ]=1), then it serves to specify which of the two UIF TX queues to use. Note that in this case SW also needs to program the correct base address of the source UIF endpoint in the BASE bitfield.<br>0x0: UIF_TX_DATA_EP (Descriptor to be read from UIF TX Data Endpoint)<br>0x1: UIF_TX_MGMT_EP (Descriptor to be read from UIF TX Management Endpoint) |

---

#### WCSS_A_DXE_0_CH6_CTRL (0x0A202580)
* **Type:** RW
* **Reset State:** 0x11800708
* **Description:** Serves to configure channel 6 operation

| Bits | Name | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31 | SWAP | RW | Endian Byte Swap Enable. When high instructs DXE to perform an endian swap of the incoming byte stream. The corresponding bitfield in the DXE descriptor control word is located at DXE_DESC_CTRL[20] |
| 30:29 | BDT_IDX | RW | BD Template Index. When XTYPE=H2B and BDH=1, DXE supports creating a BD by using template data from one of up to 4 different BD templates. The BD template base store is pointed at by the DXE BD_TMPLT(H/L) registers and the address used to read the template data is calculated as follows: BD_TMPLT_ADRR = BD_TMPLT_BASE + (128 * CH_CTRL[BDT_IDX]) The corresponding bitfield in the control word of the external descriptor is mapped to bits[19:18] |
| 28 | DFMT | RW | Descriptor Format. This bitfield is used to select between long and short descriptor formats. When using the short descriptor format, the high part of the source, destination and descriptor addresses will be taken from the SADRH_DFLT, DADRH_DFLT or DESCH_DFLT registers respectively. Default is to use the long descriptor format.<br>0x0: SHORT (Short descriptor format (5 dwords))<br>0x1: LONG (Long descriptor format (8 dwords)) |
<!-- page 1654 -->
#### WCSS_A_DXE_0_CH6_CTRL (cont.)
| Bits | Name | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 27 | ABORT | RW | Writing a one to this bit will cause the channel to stop its current transfer and set the ERR bit and ERR_CODE fields in CH_STATUS. Note that if the channel is currently disabled or if it is about to be disabled because it has just finished its programmed transfer, then the abort request will be ignored and the error bit and error codes won't be set. If the channel is currently masked by the arbiter then setting this bit will forcibly unmask it so that the transfer can be aborted the next time the channel is selected by the internal arbiter. The abort request is automatically cleared by hw once the channel has aborted the transfer. Also note that since the DXE will not attempt to do any cleanup when a transfer is aborted, software might need to do so. For example, for H2B transfers, SW should manually release the BD and any PDUs currently in use by the partial transfer or else a BD/PDU leak will result. |
| 26 | ENDIANNESS | RW | Specifies the endianness of the master generating the data. Affects alignment of valid bytes for non-dword aligned reads/writes. The corresponding field in the DXE descriptor control word is located in DXE_DESC_CTRL[21].<br>0x0: BIGEND (System is Big-Endian)<br>0x1: LTLEND (System is Little-Endian) |
| 25:22 | CTR_SEL | RW | Counter Select. If the event counters are enabled (DMA_CSR[ECTR_EN]=1) then this bitfield selects the counter that will be incremented at the end of the transfer. By default the value in this bitfield is the same as the channel number so that after reset channel 0 increments counter 0, channel 1 increments counter 1 and so on. |
| 21 | EDVEN | RW | When set, the DMA engine will clear the VAL bit in the DESC_CSR word of the current descriptor once it has completed processing it. This is useful for implementing a descriptor "ring" (see the description of the VALID bit in Table 3.1) |
| 20 | EDEN | RW | External Descriptor Enable. Use External Descriptor Linked List |
| 19 | INE_DONE | RW | Enable Channel Interrupt when Channel is Done. The corresponding interrupt source bit is INT_DONE |
| 18 | INE_ERR | RW | Enable Channel Interrupt on Errors. The corresponding interrupt source bit is INT_ERR |
| 17 | INE_ED | RW | Enable External Descriptor Interrupt. When this bit is set, an interrupt will be generated after processing a descriptor item that has the INT bit set in its DESC_CTRL word (see Table 3.1). The corresponding interrupt source bit is INT_ED |

| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |

| 15:13 | PRIO | RW | This field sets the channel priority.<br>7: Highest Priority.<br>0: Lowest Priority. |

The value of this bitfield is only meaningful for transfer types that involve the BMU and therefore its value will be ignored for H2H transfers.<br>0x0: RSVD0 (Reserved)<br>0x1: RSVD1 (Reserved)<br>0x2: THLD2 (Use BD/PDU threshold 2)<br>0x3: THLD3 (Use BD/PDU threshold 3)<br>0x4: THLD4 (Use BD/PDU threshold 4)<br>0x5: THLD5 (Use BD/PDU threshold 5)<br>0x6: THLD6 (Use BD/PDU threshold 6)<br>0x7: THLD7 (Use BD/PDU threshold 7)<br>0x8: THLD8 (Use BD/PDU threshold 8)<br>0x9: THLD9 (Use BD/PDU threshold 9)<br>0xA: THLD10 (Use BD/PDU threshold 10)<br>0xB: RSVD11 (Reserved)<br>0xC: RSVD12 (Reserved)<br>0xD: RSVD13 (Reserved)<br>0xE: RSVD14 (Reserved)<br>0xF: RSVD15 (Reserved) |

#### WCSS_A_DXE_0_CH6_CTRL (cont.)
| Bits | Name | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 7 | PIQ | RW | next descriptor Pointer address Is Queue. When set the source of the descriptor address is interpreted as a queue ID instead of just the address of a flat memory location. The only valid source queues for descriptors are the UIF Tx data and Tx management endpoints. Any other IDs will result the channel aborting the transfer with an invalid source queue error. Therefore, when this bit is set, SW must ensure that the CH_DESCL[QID] bitfield is set to a valid queue ID and that the CH_DESCL[BASE] bitfield is set to the base address of the source UIF endpoint. This base address is formed by taking the base address for the UIF block in the SAHB bus which can be found in the Nova address map document and then adding the internal UIF offset for the correct source endpoint. This offsets can be obtained from the UIF specification document. For convenience, the current internal UIF offsets are provided in the description of the QID bitfield in the CH_DESCL register description.<br>0x0: FLAT (Source address maps to regular flat memory)<br>0x1: QUEUE (Source address maps to FIFO type memory (UIF Tx endpoints)) |
| 6 | DIQ | RW | Destination Is Queue. When set the destination address is interpreted as a queue ID instead of just the address of a flat memory location. The queue could be either a BMU queue, one of the UIF RX endpoints or and EIF outbound FIFO. When this bit is set, SW must ensure that the DADR[QID] bitfield is set to a valid queue ID and that the DADR[BASE] bitfield is set to the base address of the destination queue for UIF or EIF, or to zero for a BMU queue. endpoint.<br>0x0: FLAT (Destination address maps to regular flat memory)<br>0x1: QUEUE (Destination address maps to a BMU queue or FIFO type memory) |
| 5 | SIQ | RW | Source Is Queue. When set the source address is interpreted as a queue ID instead of just the address of a flat memory location. The queue could be either a BMU queue, one of the UIF TX endpoints or and EIF inbound FIFO. When this bit is set, SW must ensure that the SADR[QID] bitfield is set to a valid queue ID and that the SADR[BASE] bitfield is set to the base address of the source queue for UIF or EIF, or to zero for a BMU queue. endpoint.<br>0x0: FLAT (Source address maps to regular flat memory)<br>0x1: QUEUE (Source address maps to a BMU queue or FIFO type memory) |

#### WCSS_A_DXE_0_CH6_CTRL (cont.)
| Bits | Name | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 4 | BDH | RW | BD Handling bit. The behavior depends on the setting of XTYPE.<br>If XTYPE is:<br>H2B: Then if BDH is:<br>0: Use first 128 bytes of packet as BD.<br>1: Create BD from BD template (Up to 4 supported. Also see desc for BDT_IDX).<br>B2H: Then if BDH is:<br>0: Insert BD in front of payload.<br>1: Discard BD.<br>For XTYPE values of H2H and B2B the value of this bit is ignored. |

| 2:1 | XTYPE | RW | Transfer Type. Specifies the type of transfer to perform:<br>00: H2H. Host space to Host space transfer.<br>01: B2B. BMU space to BMU space transfer.<br>10: H2B. Host space to BMU translation.<br>11: B2H. BMU space to Host space translation.<br>For cross-space transfers (H2B and B2H) the DMA engine will also perform the required data format translation. The format translation behavior can be modified by the setting of the BDH and PAD bits.<br>0x0: H2H (Host space to Host space transfer)<br>0x1: B2B (BMU space to BMU space transfer)<br>0x2: H2B (Host space to BMU space transfer)<br>0x3: B2H (BMU space to Host space transfer) |
<!-- page 1658 -->
#### WCSS_A_DXE_0_CH6_CTRL (cont.)
| Bits | Name | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 0 | EN | RW | Channel Enable or Restart. Writing this bit with a one either starts a new DMA transfer according to the parameters programmed in the channel's configuration registers and clears the DONE bit or, if the channel is already enabled but the STOP bit is set, then it restarts channel processing and also clears the STOP bit. This bit is automatically cleared when a single transfer completes or, if the channel is configured to use linked list descriptors, when the last transfer in the descriptor linked list completes (DESC_NXT is NULL or/and DESC_CSR[VALID]=0). The channel is also disabled and this bit cleared if a channel error is encountered. Reading this bit indicates whether a channel is currently enabled or disabled:<br>0: Channel Disabled.<br>1: Channel Enabled.<br>The Channel Enable bit status can also be found by reading the DMA_ENCH register which aggregates the EN bits of all channels. Note: Software must take care to not disable the channel while it is busy or data could be lost. |

#### WCSS_A_DXE_0_CH6_SZ (0x0A202588)
* **Type:** RW
* **Reset State:** 0x00000000
* **Description:** The transfer size register specifies the total, remaining, and burst or 'chunk' transfer sizes for each channel. The maximum total transfer size is 16K-1 bytes. The chunk size control can be useful to control the relative bandwidth used by each channel as the dma engine will change channels, release the AHB bus, and rearbitrate for access after transferring chunk size bytes.

| Bits | Name | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |

Specifies the number of bytes (in multiples of 8) to be transferred at one given time (not implying they are buffered but that they will be transferred for each start event in one bus request cycle). If chunk size is zero the DMA engine will always perform maximum chunk size transfers. Maximum chunk size is 128 bytes. |
| 27:14 | REM_SZ | R | Remaining transfer size. Specifies the number of bytes that remain to be transferred to complete the current operation. |

### WCSS_A_DXE_0_CH6_SADRL (0x0A20258C)

* **Type:** RW
* **Reset State:** 0x00000000

The channel source address register specifies either the source address in flat internal or external memory, or else the BMU queue ID, UIF TX endpoint ID, or EIF inbound FIFO ID for the transfer. The register must be programmed directly by software before the channel is enabled, then, once the DMA channel is enabled, the register is updated after each atomic chunk transfer (read+write) with the number of bytes transferred (except when using a UIF/EIF queue) and also after loading a new descriptor. When using flat memory as the source, addresses can have arbitrary byte-alignment. When using a BMU queue, UIF endpoint or EIF fifo as a source, the software is responsible for programming a valid queue ID and correct base address for the queue. The layout of bitfields in this register depends on the setting of the `CH_CSR[SIQ]` bit. When `CH_CSR[SIQ]` is clear then the register has no bitfields and the full 32-bits are interpreted as the physical address of a location in flat memory, and when it is set this register has two bitfields: The `SQID` bitfield used to specify the queue ID, and the `BASE` bitfield used to provide the base address for the UIF or EIF source endpoint/FIFO.

For B2H or B2B transfers, when the source is a BMU Queue ID (`CH_CSR[SIQ]` = 1 and `SWQID` matches BMU), the DXE will issue a BMU POPWQ command to pop the specified queue and obtain the BD index of the source packet. Else, when the source is an address (`CH_CSR[SIQ]` = 0), the DXE will interpret the address as the index of the packet BD and will add it to the `BMU_BASE` to obtain the physical address to use to fetch it directly from memory.

For H2B or H2H transfers, if the source is a UIF endpoint or EIF FIFO (`CH_CSR[SIQ]` = 1 and `SQID` matches UIF/EIF), SW should program the SAHB base address of the UIF source endpoint in the `BASE` bitfield and the queue ID to match in the `SWQID` bitfield, then the DXE will use the base address given to generate the physical address and read the data over the SAHB bus and also use the appropriate sideband signals as specified by the `SQID` field to communicate with the selected UIF endpoint. SW should make sure that the `BASE` and `SQID` fields are consistent and refer to the same endpoint or else hangs or unpredictable behavior might occur. Else, when the source is just a location in flat memory space, (`CH_CSR[SIQ]` = 0), the bitfields lose their special meaning and DXE will just use the full 32-bits programmed into the register as the physical address to use to fetch the data. For this case, SW should make sure that the provided address maps to the intended source interface (Internal memory, USB, PCI, PCIe) by conforming to the address map specified for the SAHB bus.

To summarize, for B2H and B2B transfers the address must conform to the following format:
<!-- page 1662 -->

For index of BD mode (`CH_CSR[SIQ]` = 0):
* `ADDR[31:7] = BMU_BASE + BD_INDEX[15:0]`
* `ADDR[ 6:0] = 7'd0`

For BMU Queue ID mode (`CH_CSR[SIQ]` = 1 & `SQID` matching one of the BMU queues):
* `ADDR[31:7]` = Any value will do but zero preferred
* `ADDR[ 6:0]` = Any BMU Queue ID as specified in description of `SQID` field

For H2B and H2H transfers the address must conform to the following format:
* For sources in flat memory space (`CH_CSR[SIQ]` = 0): `ADDR[31:0]` = address mapping to source interface
* For UIF RX endpoints or EIF FIFOs (`CH_CSR[SIQ]` = 1 & `QID` matching UIF or EIF):
  * `ADDR[31:7]` = UIF RX endpoint base or EIF inbound FIFO base
  * `ADDR[ 6:0]` = Queue ID matching UIF or EIF as specified in description of `SQID` field

### WCSS_A_DXE_0_CH6_SADRL (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:7 | BASE | Base Address.<br><br>Valid only when the `CH_CSR[SIQ]` bit is set. For this case, this bitfield provides the base address of the source UIF TX endpoint or EIF inbound FIFO. Consult the appropriate interface uarch for the offset within the interface's address space. When `CH_CSR[SIQ]` bit is not set this field loses its special meaning and is interpreted only as part of the full 32-bit source address. |

### WCSS_A_DXE_0_CH6_SADRH (0x0A202590)

* **Type:** RW

The channel source address high register holds the high bits of the source address for a transfer. See the description of `CH_SADRL` for more info.
<!-- page 1664 -->

### WCSS_A_DXE_0_CH6_SADRH (cont.)

### WCSS_A_DXE_0_CH6_DADRL (0x0A202594)

* **Type:** RW
* **Reset State:** 0x00000000

The channel destination address register specifies either the destination address in flat internal or external memory, or else the BMU queue ID, UIF RX endpoint ID, or EIF inbound FIFO ID for the transfer. The register must be programmed directly by software before the channel is enabled, then, once the DMA channel is enabled, the register is updated after each atomic chunk transfer (read+write) with the number of bytes transferred (except when using a UIF/EIF queue) and also after loading a new descriptor. When using flat memory as the destination, addresses can have arbitrary byte-alignment. When using a BMU queue, UIF endpoint or EIF FIFO as a destination, the software is responsible for programming a valid queue ID and correct base address for the queue. The layout of bitfields in this register depends on the setting of the `CH_CSR[DIQ]` bit. When this bit is clear then the register has no bitfields and the full 32-bits are interpreted as the physical address of a location in flat memory, and when the bit is set this register has two bitfields: The `DQID` bitfield used to specify the queue ID, and the `BASE` bitfield used to provide the base address for the UIF or EIF destination endpoint/FIFO.

For H2B or B2B transfers, when using a BMU queue as the destination (`CH_CSR[DIQ]` = 1 and `DQID` matches BMU), the DXE will push the index of the BD of the packet into the specified queue at the end of the packet transfer. Therefore, software is responsible for programming a valid BMU Queue ID.

Else, when the destination is an index (`CH_CSR[DIQ]` = 0), the BD will be written to the address obtained by adding the provided index to the `BMU_BASE`, again, the software must ensure that said address is legal and known to BMU. That is, software must preallocate the BD (get the BD from BMU via GET BD/PDU cmd) for the BD before starting the transfer.

For B2H or H2H transfers, if the destination is a UIF endpoint or EIF FIFO (`CH_CSR[DIQ]` = 1 and `DQID` matches UIF/EIF), SW should program the SAHB base address of the UIF destination endpoint in the
<!-- page 1665 -->

... `BASE` bitfield and the queue ID to match in the `DQID` bitfield, then the DXE will use the base address given to generate the physical address and write the data over the SAHB bus and also use the appropriate sideband signals as specified by the `DQID` field to communicate with the selected UIF endpoint. SW should make sure that the `BASE` and `DQID` fields are consistent and refer to the same endpoint else hangs or unpredictable behavior might occur. On the other hand, when the destination is just a location in flat memory space, (`CH_CSR[DIQ]` = 0), be it internal or external, the bitfields lose their special meaning and DXE will just use the full 32-bits programmed into the register as the address to write the data. For this case, SW should make sure that the address maps to the intended destination interface (Internal memory, USB, PCI, PCIe) by conforming to the address map specified for the SAHB bus. To summarize, for H2B and B2B transfers the address must conform to the following format:

For index of BD mode (`CH_CSR[DIQ]` = 0):
* `ADDR[31:7] = BMU_BASE + BD_INDEX[15:0]`
* `ADDR[ 6:0] = 7'd0`

For BMU Queue ID mode (`CH_CSR[DIQ]` = 1 & `DQID` matching one of the BMU queues):
* `ADDR[31:5]` = Any value will do but zero preferred
* `ADDR[ 4:0]` = Any BMU Queue ID as specified in description of `QID` field

For B2H and H2H transfers the address must conform to the following format:
* For destinations in flat memory space (`CH_CSR[DIQ]` = 0): `ADDR[31:0]` = address mapping to destination interface
* For UIF RX endpoints or EIF FIFOs (`CH_CSR[DIQ]` = 1 & `DQID` matching UIF or EIF):
  * `ADDR[31:5]` = UIF RX endpoint base or EIF inbound FIFO base
  * `ADDR[ 4:0]` = Queue ID matching UIF or EIF as specified in description of `DQID` field

| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:7 | BASE | Base Address.<br><br>Valid only when the `CH_CSR[DIQ]` bit is set. For this case, this bitfield provides the base address of the destination UIF RX endpoint or EIF outbound FIFO (for BMU SW may use any value but zero is suggested). Consult the appropriate interface uarch for the offset within the interface's address space. When `CH_CSR[DIQ]` bit is not set this field loses its special meaning and is interpreted only as part of the full 32-bit destination address. |

| 1:0 | ADDRH | RW | This register holds bits 33 and 32 of the address. With the current address mapping these high order bits determine where the transfer is routed and whether the lower 32 bits of the address (the ones held in `CH_DADRL`) go untranslated through PIF or XIF or if they use the PIF and XIF address translation windows. See the bitfield encoding descriptions for an explanation.<br><br>* 0x0: `ADDR_XTLN` (If address in PIF or XIF address space then address goes through translation in PIF or XIF)<br>* 0x1: `PIF_NO_XTLN` (Always maps to PIF and full 32-bits in `CH_DADRL` goes through PIF untranslated)<br>* 0x2: `XIF_NO_XTLN` (Always maps to XIF and full 32-bits in `CH_DADRL` goes through XIF untranslated)<br>* 0x3: `RSVD` (Reserved. Maps to default slave. Reads return error, writes are ignored) |

### WCSS_A_DXE_0_CH6_DESCL (0x0A20259C)

* **Type:** RW
* **Reset State:** 0x00000000

The Channel 6 Linked List Descriptor Pointer register contains the 32 lower bits of the address of the next descriptor to be loaded in the linked list. This address must be dword (32-bit) aligned (`addr[1:0]=0` if `CH_CTRL[PIQ]=0`). Each complete transfer descriptor consists of 7 32-bit values arranged contiguously in memory. The value of this register will be overwritten with the address of the start of the next descriptor set in the list after the current descriptor has been fetched.

The meaning of the value in this register depends on the value of the `CH_CTRL[PIQ]` bitfield similar to the way in which `SADRL` and `DADRL` are dependent on `SIQ` and `DIQ` respectively. For `CH_CTRL[PIQ]=0` then this register has no bitfields and the value is just interpreted as an address in flat memory space. When `CH_CTRL[PIQ]` is set then the descriptor will be read from FIFO type memory in UIF and the register has 2 bitfields: `BASE`, and `SQID`. `BASE` specifies the base address of the UIF TX queue (derived from the start of the UIF address space in SAHB plus the internal UIF offset).
<!-- page 1668 -->

### WCSS_A_DXE_0_CH6_DESCL (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:7 | BASE | This bitfield only exists and has meaning when the descriptor needs to be read from a UIF TX queue (and therefore `CH_CTRL[PIQ]=1`), then it serves to specify the base address of the UIF endpoint to use as the source of the descriptor. Refer to the Nova address map document and to the UIF architecture document for guaranteed correct values to use here. For convenience but without a guarantee of accuracy, the base value to use for both the TX data and management endpoints is the following:<br><br>`base = UIF base + TD_and_TM_offset = 0x0E02_5000 + 0x100 = 0x0E02_5100 >> 7 = 0x1C_04A2` |
| 6:0 | SQID | This bitfield only exists and has meaning when the descriptor needs to be read from a UIF TX queue (and therefore `CH_CTRL[PIQ]=1`), then it serves to specify which of the two UIF TX queues to use. Note that in this case SW also needs to program the correct base address of the source UIF endpoint in the `BASE` bitfield.<br><br>* 0x0: `UIF_TX_DATA_EP` (Descriptor to be read from UIF TX Data Endpoint)<br>* 0x1: `UIF_TX_MGMT_EP` (Descriptor to be read from UIF TX Management Endpoint) |

### WCSS_A_DXE_0_CH7_CTRL
**Address:** `0x0A2025C0`
**Type:** RW
**Reset State:** `0x11C00708`

Serves to configure channel 7 operation

| Bits | Name | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31 | SWAP | RW | Endian Byte Swap Enable. When high instructs DXE to perform an endian swap of the incoming byte stream. The corresponding bitfield in the DXE descriptor control word is located at DXE_DESC_CTRL[20] |
| 30:29 | BDT_IDX | RW | BD Template Index. When XTYPE=H2B and BDH=1, DXE supports creating a BD by using template data from one of up to 4 different BD templates. The BD template base store is pointed at by the DXE BD_TMPLT(H/L) registers and the address used to read the template data is calculated as follows: BD_TMPLT_ADRR = BD_TMPLT_BASE + (128 * CH_CTRL[BDT_IDX]) The corresponding bitfield in the control word of the external descriptor is mapped to bits[19:18] |
| 28 | DFMT | RW | Descriptor Format. This bitfield is used to select between long and short descriptor formats. When using the short descriptor format, the high part of the source, destination and descriptor addresses will be taken from the SADRH_DFLT, DADRH_DFLT or DESCH_DFLT registers respectively. Default is to use the long descriptor format<br>0x0: SHORT (Short descriptor format (5 dwords))<br>0x1: LONG (Long descriptor format (8 dwords)) |

| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 27 | ABORT | RW | Writing a one to this bit will cause the channel to stop its current transfer and set the ERR bit and ERR_CODE fields in CH_STATUS. Note that if the channel is currently disabled or if it is about to be disabled because it has just finished its programmed transfer, then the abort request will be ignored and the error bit and error codes won't be set. If the channel is currently masked by the arbiter then setting this bit will forcibly unmask it so that the transfer can be aborted the next time the channel is selected by the internal arbiter. The abort request is automatically cleared by hw once the channel has aborted the transfer. When this bit is set, SW must ensure that the SADR[QID] bitfield is set to a valid queue ID and that the SADR[BASE] bitfield is set to the base address of the source queue for UIF or EIF, or to zero for a BMU queue. endpoint.<br>0x0: FLAT (Source address maps to regular flat memory)<br>0x1: QUEUE (Source address maps to a BMU queue or FIFO type memory) |

### WCSS_A_DXE_0_CH7_CTRL (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 0 | EN | RW | Channel Enable or Restart. Writing this bit with a one either starts a new DMA transfer according to the parameters programmed in the channel's configuration registers and clears the DONE bit or, if the channel is already enabled but the STOP bit is set, then it restarts channel processing and also clears the STOP bit. This bit is automatically cleared when a single transfer completes or, if the channel is configured to use linked list descriptors, when the last transfer in the descriptor linked list completes (DESC_NXT is NULL or/and DESC_CSR[VALID]=0). The channel is also disabled and this bit cleared if a channel error is encountered. Reading this bit indicates whether a channel is currently enabled or disabled:<br>0: Channel Disabled.<br>1: Channel Enabled.<br>The Channel Enable bit status can also be found by reading the DMA_ENCH register which aggregates the EN bits of all channels. Note: Software must take care to not disable the channel while it is busy or data could be lost. |

### WCSS_A_DXE_0_CH7_SZ
**Address:** `0x0A2025C8`
**Type:** RW
**Reset State:** `0x00000000`

The transfer size register specifies the total, remaining, and burst or 'chunk' transfer sizes for each channel. The maximum total transfer size is 16K-1 bytes. The chunk size control can be useful to control the relative bandwidth used by each channel as the dma engine will change channels, release the AHB bus, and rearbitrate for access after transferring chunk size bytes.

| Bits | Name | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:28 | CHK_SZ | RW | Chunk transfer size. Specifies the number of bytes (in multiples of 8) to be transferred at one given time (not implying they are buffered but that they will be transferred for each start event in one bus request cycle). If chunk size is zero the DMA engine will always perform maximum chunk size transfers. Maximum chunk size is 128 bytes. |
| 27:14 | REM_SZ | R | Remaining transfer size. Specifies the number of bytes that remain to be transferred to complete the current operation. |
<!-- page 1680 -->
### WCSS_A_DXE_0_CH7_SZ (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 13:0 | TOT_SZ | RW | Total Transfer Size. Specifies the number of bytes to be transferred. Maximum total transfer size is (4K-1) bytes. Note: This field is unnecessary and will be ignored for B2H or B2B transfers, when the source of the transfer is in BMU space (either BMU queue or direct pointer to BD). This is because the size of the transfer will be the packet length encoded in the BD at offset 0x0c bits [11:0]. |

### WCSS_A_DXE_0_CH7_SADRL
**Address:** `0x0A2025CC`
**Type:** RW
**Reset State:** `0x00000000`

The channel source address register specifies either the source address in flat internal or external memory, or else the BMU queue ID, UIF TX endpoint ID, or EIF inbound FIFO ID for the transfer. The register must be programmed directly by software before the channel is enabled, then, once the DMA channel is enabled, the register is updated after each atomic chunk transfer (read+write) with the number of bytes transferred (except when using a UIF/EIF queue) and also after loading a new descriptor. When using flat memory as the source, addresses can have arbitrary byte-alignment. When using a BMU queue, UIF endpoint or EIF fifo as a source, the software is responsible for programming a valid queue ID and correct base address for the queue. The layout of bitfields in this register depends on the setting of the CH_CSR[SIQ] bit. When CH_CSR[SIQ] is clear then the register has no bitfields and the full 32-bits are interpreted as the physical address of a location in flat memory, and when it is set this register has two bitfields: The SQID bitfield used to specify the queue ID, and the BASE bitfield used to provide the base address for the UIF or EIF source endpoint/FIFO.

For B2H or B2B transfers, when the source is a BMU Queue ID (CH_CSR[SIQ] = 1 and SWQID matches BMU), the DXE will issue a BMU POPWQ command to pop the specified queue and obtain the BD index of the source packet. Else, when the source is an address (CH_CSR[SIQ] = 0), the DXE will interpret the address as the index of the packet BD and will add it to the BMU_BASE to obtain the physical addresses to use to fetch it directly from memory.

For H2B or H2H transfers, if the source is a UIF endpoint or EIF FIFO (CH_CSR[SIQ] = 1 and SQID matches UIF/EIF), SW should program the SAHB base address of the UIF source endpoint in the BASE bitfield and the queue ID to match in the SWQID bitfield, then the DXE will use the base address given to generate the physical address and read the data over the SAHB bus and also use the appropriate sideband signals as specified by the SQID field to communicate with the selected UIF endpoint. SW should make sure that the BASE and SQID fields are consistent and refer to the same endpoint or else hangs or unpredictable behavior might occur. Else, when the source is just a location in flat memory space, (CH_CSR[SIQ] = 0), the bitfields lose their special meaning and DXE will just use the full 32-bits programmed into the register as the physical address to use to fetch the data. For this case, SW should make sure that the provided address maps to the intended source interface (Internal memory, USB, PCI, PCIe) by conforming to the address map specified for the SAHB bus.

To summarize, for B2H and B2B transfers the address must conform to the following format:


<!-- page 1681 -->

For index of BD mode (CH_CSR[SIQ] = 0):

ADDR[31:7] = BMU_BASE + BD_INDEX[15:0]
ADDR[ 6:0] = 7'd0

For BMU Queue ID mode (CH_CSR[SIQ] = 1 & SQID matching one of the BMU queues):

ADDR[31:7] = Any value will do but zero preferred

ADDR[ 6:0] = Any BMU Queue ID as specified in description of SQID field

For H2B and H2H transfers the address must conform to the following format:

For sources in flat memory space (CH_CSR[SIQ] = 0): ADDR[31:0] = address mapping to source interface

For UIF RX endpoints or EIF FIFOs (CH_CSR[SIQ] = 1 & QID matching UIF or EIF):
ADDR[31:7] = UIF RX endpoint base or EIF inbound FIFO base

ADDR[ 6:0] = Queue ID matching UIF or EIF as specified in description of SQID field

Consult the appropriate interface uarch for the offset within the interface's address space. When CH_CSR[SIQ] bit is not set this field loses its special meaning and is interpreted only as part of the full 32-bit source address. |

### WCSS_A_DXE_0_CH7_DADRL

**Address:** `0x0A2025D4`
**Type:** RW
**Reset State:** `0x00000000`

The channel destination address register specifies either the destination address in flat internal or external memory, or else the BMU queue ID, UIF RX endpoint ID, or EIF outbound FIFO ID for the transfer. The register must be programmed directly by software before the channel is enabled, then, once the DMA channel is enabled, the register is updated after each atomic chunk transfer (read+write) with the number of bytes transferred. (except when using a UIF/EIF queue) and also after loading a new descriptor When using flat memory as the destination, addresses can have arbitrary byte-alignment. When using a BMU queue, UIF endpoint or EIF fifo as a destination, the software is responsible for programming a valid queue ID and correct base address for the queue. The layout of bitfields in this register depends on the setting of the CH_CSR[DIQ] bit. When this bit is clear then the register has no bitfields and the full 32-bits are interpreted as the physical address of a location in flat memory, and when the bit is set this register has two bitfields: The DQID bitfield used to specify the queue ID, and the BASE bitfield used to provide the base address for the UIF or EIF destination endpoint/FIFO.

For H2B or B2B transfers, when using a BMU queue as the destination (CH_CSR[DIQ] = 1 and DQID matches BMU), the DXE will push the index of the BD of the packet into the specified queue at the end of the packet transfer. Therefore, software is responsible for programming a valid BMU Queue ID.
Else, when the destination is an index (CH_CSR[DIQ] = 0), the BD will be written to the address obtained by adding the provided index to the BMU_BASE, again, the software must ensure that said address is legal and known to BMU. That is, software must preallocate the BD (get the BD from BMU via GET BD/PDU cmd) for the BD before starting the transfer. For B2H or H2H transfers, if the destination is a UIF endpoint or EIF FIFO (CH_CSR[DIQ] = 1 and DQID matches UIF/EIF), SW should program the SAHB base address of the UIF destination endpoint in the
<!-- page 1684 -->

BASE bitfield and the queue ID to match in the DQID bitfield, then the DXE will use the base address given to generate the physical address and write the data over the SAHB bus and also use the appropriate sideband signals as specified by the DQID field to communicate with the selected UIF endpoint. SW should make sure that the BASE and DQID fields are consistent and refer to the same endpoint else hangs or unpredictable behavior might occur. On the other hand, when the destination is just a location in flat memory space, (CH_CSR[DIQ] = 0), be it internal or external, the bitfields lose their special meaning and DXE will just use the full 32-bits programmed into the register as the address to write the data. For this case, SW should make sure that the address maps to the intended destination interface (Internal memory, USB, PCI, PCIe) by conforming to the address map specified for the SAHB bus. To summarize, for H2B and B2B transfers the address must conform to the following format:

For index of BD mode (CH_CSR[DIQ] = 0):

ADDR[31:7] = BMU_BASE + BD_INDEX[15:0]
ADDR[ 6:0] = 7'd0

For BMU Queue ID mode (CH_CSR[DIQ] = 1 & DQID matching one of the BMU queues):

ADDR[31:5] = Any value will do but zero preferred
ADDR[ 4:0] = Any BMU Queue ID as specified in description of QID field

For B2H and H2H transfers the address must conform to the following format:

For destinations in flat memory space (CH_CSR[DIQ] = 0):

ADDR[31:0] = address mapping to destination interface

For UIF RX endpoints or EIF FIFOs (CH_CSR[DIQ] = 1 & DQID matching UIF or EIF):

ADDR[31:5] = UIF RX endpoint base or EIF inbound FIFO base
ADDR[ 4:0] = Queue ID matching UIF or EIF as specified in description of DQID field

| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:7 | BASE | Base Address.<br>Valid only when the CH_CSR[DIQ] bit is set. For this case, this bitfield provides the base address of the destination UIF RX endpoint or EIF outbound FIFO (for BMU SW may use any value can be used but zero is suggested). Consult the appropriate interface uarch for the offset within the interface's address space. When CH_CSR[SIQ] bit is not set this field loses its special meaning and is interpreted only as part of the full 32-bit source address. |

When CH_CSR[SIQ] bit is not set this field loses its special meaning and is interpreted only as part of the full 32-bit source address.<br>0x0: RSVD_0 (Reserved)<br>0x1: RSVD_1 (Reserved)<br>0x2: BMU_2 (BMU Work Queue 2)<br>0x3: BMU_3 (BMU Work Queue 3)<br>0x4: BMU_4 (BMU Work Queue 4)<br>0x5: BMU_5 (BMU Work Queue 5)<br>0x6: BMU_6 (BMU Work Queue 6)<br>0x7: BMU_7 (BMU Work Queue 7)<br>0x8: BMU_8 (BMU Work Queue 8)<br>0x9: BMU_9 (BMU Work Queue 9)<br>0xA: BMU_10 (BMU Work Queue 10)<br>0xB: BMU_11 (BMU Work Queue 11)<br>0xC: BMU_12 (BMU Work Queue 12)<br>0xD: BMU_13 (BMU Work Queue 13)<br>0xE: BMU_14 (BMU Work Queue 14)<br>0xF: BMU_15 (BMU Work Queue 15)<br>0x10: BMU_16 (BMU Work Queue 16)<br>0x11: BMU_17 (BMU Work Queue 17)<br>0x12: BMU_18 (BMU Work Queue 18)<br>0x13: BMU_19 (BMU Work Queue 19)<br>0x14: BMU_20 (BMU Work Queue 20)<br>0x15: BMU_21 (BMU Work Queue 21)<br>0x16: BMU_22 (BMU Work Queue 22)<br>0x17: BMU_23 (BMU Work Queue 23)<br>0x18: BMU_24 (BMU Work Queue 24)<br>0x19: BMU_25 (BMU Work Queue 25)<br>0x1A: BMU_26 (BMU Work Queue 26)<br>0x1B: BMU_SINK_WQ (BMU_SINK (WQ255))<br>0x1C: UIF_RX_1_EP (UIF RX 1 endpoint)<br>0x1D: UIF_RX_2_EP (UIF RX 2 endpoint)<br>0x1E: UIF_RX_3_EP (UIF RX 3 endpoint)<br>0x1F: UIF_RX_4_EP (UIF RX 4 endpoint) |
