### WCSS_A_DXE_0_CH7_DESCL

**Address:** `0x0A2025DC`
**Type:** RW
**Reset State:** `0x00000000`

The Channel 7 Linked List Descriptor Pointer register contains the 32 lower bits of the address of the next descriptor to be loaded in the linked list. This address must be dword (32-bit) aligned (addr[1:0]=0 if CH_CTRL[PIQ]=0). Each complete transfer descriptor consists of 7 32-bit values arranged contiguously in memory. The value of this register will be overwritten with the address of the start of the next descriptor set in the list after the current descriptor has been fetched. The meaning of the value in this register depends on the value of the CH_CTRL[PIQ] bitfield similar to the way in which SADRL and DADRL are depending in SIQ and DIQ respectively. For CH_CTRL[PIQ]=0 then this register has no bitfields and the value is just intrepreted as an address in flat memory space. When CH_CTRL[PIQ] is set then the descriptor will be read from FIFO type memory in UIF and the register has 2 bitfields: BASE, and SQID. BASE specifies the base address of the UIF Tx queue (derived from the start of the UIF address space in SAHB plus the internal UIF offset).
<!-- page 1687 -->

### WCSS_A_DXE_0_CH7_DESCL

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:7 | BASE | This bitfield only exists and has meaning when the descriptor needs to be read from a UIF TX queue (and therefore CH_CTRL[PIQ]=1), then it serves to specify the base address of the UIF endpoint to use as the source of the descriptor. Refer to the Nova address map document and to the UIF architecture document for guaranteed correct values to use here. For convenience but without a guarantee of accuracy, the base value to use for both the Tx data and management endpoints is the following:<br>base = UIF base + TD_and_TM_offset = 0x0E02_5000 + x100 = 0x0E02_5100>>7 = 0x1C_04A2 |
| 6:0 | SQID | This bitfield only exists and has meaning when the descriptor needs to be read from a UIF TX queue (and therefore CH_CTRL[PIQ]=1), then it serves to specify which of the two UIF TX queues to use. Note that in this case SW also needs to program the correct base address of the source UIF endpoint in the BASE bitfield.<br>0x0: UIF_TX_DATA_EP (Descriptor to be read from UIF TX Data Endpoint)<br>0x1: UIF_TX_MGMT_EP (Descriptor to be read from UIF TX Management Endpoint) |

## 10.21 WCSS_A_CCAHB_CCAHB

### WCSS_A_CCAHB_CCAHB_BT_PL

* **Address:** `0x0A200000`
* **Type:** RW
* **Reset State:** `0x00000005`

ccahb Arbiter arbitration priority level for bt master. In the ccahb arbitration scheme the master with highest priority level always wins. Should there be more than one master with the same priority then the winning master will be selected using a round-robin algorithm.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 3:0 | PRIORITY | Arbitration priority for bt master.The lowest priority level is 1 and the highest priority level is 15. A priority level of 0 has a special significance, it means that the master is disabled and stops participating in the arbitration scheme. Note that the ccahb arbiter will prevent a master from disabling itself. |

## 10.22 WCSS_A_FM_SSBI2_CFG_SSBI2_CFG

### WCSS_A_FM_SSBI2_CFG_SSBI2_CTL

* **Address:** `0x0A1E0000`
* **Type:** RW
* **Clock:** AHB bus clock
* **Reset State:** `0x00083005`

Specifies various generic SSBI2 control information. Bits 19:13 comprising of fields SSBI2_DATA_PDEN, FCLK_MODE, FCLK_SW_OVERRIDE and NUM_FCLK are either
<!-- page 1707 -->

### WCSS_A_FM_SSBI2_CFG_SSBI2_CTL (continued)

asynchronously reset or set. This is because they control the signals going directly to a pad. Remaining bits 12:0 are synchronously reset or set.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 19:16 | NUM_FCLK | Indicates a programmable number of active forwarding clock cycles following a SSBI2 'transaction done' for a corresponding SSBI2 request. Unless there is a new SSBI2 transaction request, the forwarding clock is shut off after toggling NUM_FCLK cycles at the PMIC SSBI2 clock frequency. The suggested setting (also the default value) is 8 clock cycles. |
| 15 | FCLK_SW_OVERRIDE | This is a software override bit to control the CGC for forwarding clock. Set this bit to 1 to allow the SSBI2 clock to continue as a forwarding clock through the CGC (provided FLCK_MODE = 1). This override bit is provided to allow continuos toggling clock to SSBI2 slave irrespective of how the HW logic controls the CGC. Set this bit to 0 to enable pure HW control on the forwarding clock CGC. |
| 14 | FCLK_MODE | Set this bit to 1 to activate forwarding clock mode. When this bit is 0, the FCLK_SW_OVERRIDE field has no meaning. Out of reset, the mode is set to 0 indicating that the SSBI2 slave does not work off the forwarding clock.<br>When FCLK_MODE = 0; no forwarding clock.<br>When FCLK_MODE = 1; FCLK_SW_OVERRIDE = 1; forwarding clock always toggles.<br>When FCLK_MODE = 1; FCLK_SW_OVERRIDE = 0; forwarding clock is controlled by HW logic. |
| 13 | SSBI2_DATA_PDEN | Pulldown enable for SSBI2_DATA pad. |
| 12 | PA_CGC_CTRL | This is to control the SSBI2 clock going to this PMIC arbiter. Set this bit to 1 when you want to allow the clock to flow through the CGC. Set this bit to 0 to shut off clock to PMIC arbiter. Out of reset, this bit is set to 1. |
| 10:8 | SSBI2_ADDR_WIDTH | Specifies what is the addressing mode in SSBI2 mode. This field is only applicable in SSBI2 mode and not the old SSBI1 mode.<br>0x0: ENUM_8_BIT_ADDRESSING_MODE (8-bit addressing mode)<br>0x1: ENUM_9_BIT_ADDRESSING_MODE_AND_SO_ON (9-bit addressing mode and so on) |
| 7 | SSBI2_MODE | Set this bit to 1 when SW wants to switch to new SSBI2 mode. Set this is 0 when in old SSBI 1 mode. |
| 5:4 | SEL_RD_DATA | Specifies which RD_DATA value to select out of four possible combinations. This signal allows the returned data from the slave to be captured inside the master, 1, 2, or 3 symbols late in order to accommodate a large range of routing delay. Based on this field, the entire read transaction length will increase by SEL_RD_DATA number of symbols. |
| 3:2 | SSBI2_DATA_DEL | Specifies the number of 1/2 clock periods, SSBI2_DATA will be delayed before sampling inside. |
<!-- page 1708 -->

### WCSS_A_FM_SSBI2_CFG_SSBI2_CTL (continued)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1:0 | IDLE_SYMS | The master will ensure there are at least this number of idle symbol periods in between the accesses. The idle time is inserted at the end of the read or write transaction. This supported values are always between 1 - 3. |

### WCSS_A_FM_SSBI2_CFG_SSBI2_INT_ENABLE

* **Address:** `0x0A1E0004`
* **Type:** RW
* **Clock:** AHB bus clock
* **Reset State:** `0x00000000`

Provides control on whether the TRANSACTION-DONE interrupts can be generated or not (per SW master).

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 6:0 | ENABLE_SSBI2_INT | SSBI2 transaction done interrupts for each SW master are generated only when the corresponding bits are set. The Interrupt mapping corresponds to the entries in the VIT . For e.g. if the VMID in VIT index 0 corresponds to the SW master RPM and VMID in index 1 of the VIT corresponds to SW master ARM 11, the bit 0 in the register will enable the interrupt corresponding to RPM , bit 1 will enable interrupt corresponding to ARM11. |

### WCSS_A_FM_SSBI2_CFG_SSBI2_PRIORITIES

* **Address:** `0x0A1E0008`
* **Type:** RW
* **Clock:** AHB bus clock
* **Reset State:** `0x00000000`

Specifies the priorities for SSBI2 arbiter ports. The SSBI2 block supports up to maximum of 8 ports for arbitration. Each port has 3 bits to denote its priority. The bits are synchronously reset.

> [!CAUTION]
> Since the reset state value of SSBI2_PRIORITIES is 0, only SW requests (hard-coded to port #0) can get through. SW has to program this register to allow hardware requests through the SSBI2 arbiter.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 11:9 | PRIORITY3 | Specifies the port number of host, with a priority that is 1 less then PRIORITY2. |
<!-- page 1709 -->

### WCSS_A_FM_SSBI2_CFG_SSBI2_PRIORITIES (continued)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 8:6 | PRIORITY2 | Specifies the port number of host, with a priority that is 1 less then PRIORITY1. |
| 5:3 | PRIORITY1 | Specifies the port number of host, with a priority that is 1 less then PRIORITY0. |
| 2:0 | PRIORITY0 | Specifies the port number of the highest priority host. |

### WCSS_A_FM_SSBI2_CFG_SSBI2_BANKS_2_3_CTL

* **Address:** `0x0A1E000C`
* **Type:** RW
* **Clock:** AHB bus clock
* **Reset State:** `0xFFFFFFFF`

This register specifies whether an access is allowed to banks 2 and 3 of PMIC. The access control to the banks 2 and 3 of PMIC is set per VMID. Bit 0 corresponds to access control for VMID 0 and bit 31 corresponds to access control for VMID 31.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:0 | ACCESS_CONTROL | Set each of the 32 bits to 1 if the master corresponding to that VMID wishes to initiate SW requests to banks 2 and 3 of PMIC. |

### WCSS_A_FM_SSBI2_CFG_SSBI2_ILLEGAL_STATUS

* **Address:** `0x0A1E0010`
* **Type:** R
* **Clock:** AHB bus clock
* **Reset State:** `0x00000000`

Returns status information of the software master that tried to access a SSBI2 command micro register, and failed security through the VIT table.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 5:1 | ILLEGAL_VMID | Indicates the VMID of the master that performed the most recent illegal access. The value in this field is only meaningful when the ILLEGAL_ACCESS bit is set. On software reads, the value is retained unless another illegal access with a different VMID happens. In that case, this field will have the VMID corresponding to the most recent illegal master. |
<!-- page 1710 -->

### WCSS_A_FM_SSBI2_CFG_SSBI2_ILLEGAL_STATUS (continued)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 0 | ILLEGAL_ACCESS | When set (1) indicates an illegal access. An illegal access is defined as an access that does not find a matching VMID in the SSBI2_VITn registers. This bit is cleared on a software read provided there is no other illegal access in the same clock cycle that a software read happens. |

### WCSS_A_FM_SSBI2_CFG_SSBI2_VITn (n=[0..6])

* **Address:** `0x0A1E0020 + 0x4*n`
* **Type:** RW
* **Clock:** AHB bus clock
* **Reset State:** `0x00000000`

This is the VMID index table (VIT) used for enabling concurrent SSBI2 SW requests among multiple SW masters. Secure entities are expected to assign a VMID for the SW master corresponding to an index. The SSBI2_VIT0 has the VMID associated with index 0, SSBI2_VIT1 has the VMID associated with index 1 and so on.

> [!CAUTION]
> By default, only the SW master with a VMID of '0' has access to registers in SSBI2 command micro space. SROT/RPM has to populate this table before valid SW masters can initiate SSBI2 SW transactions.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 4:0 | VMID | VMID corresponding to index n. |

### WCSS_A_FM_SSBI2_CFG_SSBI2_PVC_CTL

* **Address:** `0x0A1E00A0`
* **Type:** RW
* **Clock:** AHB bus clock
* **Reset State:** `0x00000000`

This register provides the global enable/disable for the PVC interface module, per PVC port enable/disable as well as captures PVC interface busy status.

> [!WARNING]
> In a PMIC arbiter wrapper system having more than 1 PMIC arbiter module; if a PVC port(x) is enabled in one of the PMIC arbiters, the corresponding PVC_port(x) in all the other PMIC arbiters shall be disabled. If multiple PVC_port(x)'s enabled simultaneously, the hardware does not guarantee correct operation.


<!-- page 1711 -->

### WCSS_A_FM_SSBI2_CFG_SSBI2_PVC_CTL
| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 8 | PVC_INTF_BUSY | This is a status bit. When set (1) indicates that the PVC interface module is busy (meaning there is atleast one PVC transaction being serviced). Busy line goes high when PVC interface detects a new request on one of the PVC ports and stays high until it samples a done from SSBI2 arbiter.<br>Writes to this bit will not have any effect and will be ignored. |
| 3 | PVC_PORT3_EN | Set this bit to 1 to enable PVC port 3.<br>PVC port 3 maps to SMPSS CPU1 SAW. |
| 2 | PVC_PORT2_EN | Set this bit to 1 to enable PVC port 2.<br>PVC port 2 maps to SMPSS CPU 0 SAW. |
| 1 | PVC_PORT1_EN | Set this bit to 1 to enable PVC port 1.<br>PVC port 1 maps to LPASS Q6 SAW. |
| 0 | PVC_INTF_EN | Set this bit to 1 to enable PVC interface module. |

### WCSS_A_FM_SSBI2_CFG_SSBI2_PVC_TABLEn (n=0..31)
- **Address**: `0x0A1E00A4 + 0x4 * n`
- **Type**: `RW`
- **Clock**: `AHB bus clock`
- **Reset State**: `0x00000000`

This set of registers indicates the full PVC table corresponding to all the PVC ports. For e.g.: there are 4 entries per PVC port(set by RTL generic) and there are 3 PVC ports (set by RTL generic). Each entry is 15-bit address to the SSBI2 slave registers. This indirect addressing from the PVC ports to the SSBI2 slave registers provides a way to enforce security on hardware SSBI2 requests.

> [!NOTE]
> Though this current document shows 12 entries, the number of entries should scale based on the GENERIC settings for the number of PVC ports and the address index width. Also though 15-bit addresses are supported, 10-bit addressing is all that is expected for current PMICs.

SSBI2_PVC_TABLEn, n=[0...11]

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 14:0 | ADDR | 15-bit address of the SSBI2 slave registers. |
<!-- page 1712 -->

## 10.23 WCSS_A_FM_SSBI2_CMD_SSBI2_CMD

### WCSS_A_FM_SSBI2_CMD_SSBI2_CMD
- **Address**: `0x0A1C0000`
- **Type**: `W`
- **Clock**: `AHB bus clock`
- **Reset State**: `0x00000000`

The SW masters write to this register to initiate either a read or a write SSBI2 transaction. Through this register, the SW can address up to 32 kB of SSBI2 slave register space. However the PMICs only house a maximum of 1024 registers and hence the values on the most significant 5-bits of the REG_ADDR_14_8 field are ignored. The REG_DATA field is only applicable for write transaction and is ignored for reads. The read data returned back from the SSBI2 slave is directed to the SSBI2_RD_STATUS register. Bit 23 is left as a reserved bit to enable slave address to grow to 16-bits in the future.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 24 | RDWRN | Denotes whether the command to perform is a register write (0) or read (1). |
| 22:16 | REG_ADDR_14_8 | Specifies the upper 7 bits, 14:8, of SSBI slave register address. |
| 15:8 | REG_ADDR_7_0 | Lower 8 bits, 7:0, of SSBI slave register address. |
| 7:0 | REG_DATA | Write data for a slave register. |

### WCSS_A_FM_SSBI2_CMD_SSBI2_RD_STATUS
- **Address**: `0x0A1C0004`
- **Type**: `R`
- **Clock**: `AHB bus clock`
- **Reset State**: `0x00000000`

This register provides the read data as well as the status of the transaction. This register also returns back information associated with the transaction such as the SSBI2 slave register address and the transaction access type. SW is expected to poll TRANS_DONE and TRANS_DENIED until either of these bits are set to 1.

* **TRANS_DONE = 0, TRANS_DENIED = 1**; indicates to SW that the current transaction was rejected because the master did not have permissions to access the corresponding SSBI2 slave register.
* **TRANS_DONE = 1, TRANS_DENIED = 0**; indicates to SW that the current transaction was completed successfully. For writes, it means that the write data was sent out on the SSBI wire and for reads, it means that the read data is returned back and is now in `SSBI2_RD_STATUS[REG_DATA]`. At this point, the SW is said to have completed one transaction.
<!-- page 1713 -->

* Both TRANS_DONE and TRANS_DENIED being either 0 or 1 does not happen and is not a valid combination after a transaction has been initiated.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 27 | TRANS_DONE | When set (1), indicates that the SSBI2 has completed the transaction. If this was a write request, the write has completed. If this was a read request, the read data has returned back.<br>NOTE: This bit is cleared on read. |
| 26 | TRANS_DENIED | When set (1), indicates that a SSBI2 transaction was denied because the master did not have access to the particular SSBI2 slave SW register to where the access was intended. |
| 25 | TRANS_PROG | When set (1), indicates that a SSBI2 transaction is in progress. This signal will be set for the duration from REQ assertion until DONE assertion. |
| 24 | RDWRN | Returns the access type of transaction. A value of 1 implies a read transaction and a value of 0 implies a write transaction. |
| 22:8 | REG_ADDR | Returns the address to which the SSBI2 transaction was performed. |
| 7:0 | REG_DATA | Returned read register data.<br>NOTE: The read data is not cleared on reads, however will return all zeroes for a SW master whose transaction was denied or was an illegal SW master. |

The TX_EN register is to control Riva-FM TX functionality.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 11:10 | AUDIO_IN_SHIFT_CTRL | Used for rounding the left and right audio input. The TX_AUDIO_IN_SHIFT_CTRL register is used for controlling the rounding operation of the audio input data stream.<br>0x0: ROUND_2 (2 bit round)<br>0x1: ROUND_3 (3 bit round)<br>0x2: ROUND_4 (4 bit round)<br>0x3: ROUND_5 (5 bit round) |

### WCSS_A_FM_TX_CONTROL (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 9:5 | PRE_EMPH_CONST | 0x13 for 50u pre-emph<br>0x1D for 75u pre-emph<br>The PRE_EMPH_CONST is to set the TX pre-emphasis value. |
| 4:3 | DC_BLOCK | # of bits to truncate from the DC blocking accumulator. The TX_DC_BLOCK register is used to select the number of bits for dc blocking feedback. The DC Blocking accumulation registers are AUDIO_D+9 bits wide, and the 2-bit DC_BLOCK_SEL input is used to select 1-of-4 truncation bit sizes (no-feedback, 9-bit, 10-bit and 11-bit truncation), for selectable AUDIO_D-2-bit-width feedback data<br>0x0: DISABLE (no DC blocking)<br>0x1: TRUNC_9 (truncate 9 bit from feedback)<br>0x2: TRUNC_10 (truncate 10 bit from feedback)<br>0x3: TRUNC_11 (truncate 11 bit from feedback) |
| 2 | PRE_EMPH_EN | This is a debugging mode register only. For normal operation should be set to 1 at all times.<br>0x1: ENABLE (Enables pre-emphasis)<br>0x0: DISABLE (Disables pre-emphasis) |
| 1 | STEREO | 0x1: STEREO (Enables Tx Stereo Mode)<br>0x0: MONO (The TX_STEREO register is to enable the stereo mode. Incase of disable the stereo mode mono modulation should be increased. Mono mode modulation mono should be increased.) |
| 0 | TX_EN | Active high<br>0x1: ENABLE (Enables TX. For proper operation, this register should be set as the last programmed register for TX.)<br>0x0: DISABLE (Disables TX and gates off all clocks, except for Tx Registers.) |

| 9:5 | DROP_THRESHOLD | Peak index difference threshold to drop bit. This is 5 bit signed value. This register is used only in non-coherent mode. The register is used to set the peak index difference threshold to drop bits. If the current peak index minus previous peak index is less than RX_RDS_DROP_BIT_THRESHOLD value the current received bit will be dropped |
| 4:0 | REPEAT_THRESHOLD | Peak index difference threshold to add bit. This is 5 bit signed value. This register is used only in non-coherent mode. The register is used to set the peak index difference threshold to add bits. So if the current peak index minus previous index is greater than RX_RDS_REPEAT_BIT_THRESHOLD value the current received bit will be repeated. |

* **Type**: R

16 bit RDS peak index output from the bit synchronizer. In case of detection of repeat/drop demod bit inside the rds physical layer this register will reflect the peak indexes that cause the repeat/drop to happen. This register stores the last 4 peak indexes that cause repeat/drop to happen. This register could be considered as 4 deep FIFO for the peak index but only store values at the event of adding or dropping bits

## WCSS_A_FM_RX_ROT_CTRL_0 (0x0A1900D4)

* **Type**: RW
* **Clock**: APB
* **Reset State**: 0x00000000

This register is to control the spur rotator and removal block.

The idea behind the spur removal block is to rotate the signal such that the spur will move to DC. Then you remove a DC value representing the level of the spur. There are two options for that DC value. The first is to use a DC tracking filter to estimate it. The second is to use a predetermined value in spur_comp_i/q registers.

To use this register, the ROT3_SEL bit must be managed properly. The first write to this register must set ROT3_SEL=1, to select new rotator and to activate the fields defined in this register. Subsequent writes must be used to set the other fields in this register.

For legacy mode, set ROT3_SEL=0 and the register fields will be as defined as in legacy register RX_ROT_CTRL, where the field definitions are different than in RX_ROT_CTRL_0.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---------- |
| 31 | ROT3_SEL | Select for legacy (LUT-based) or new (CORDIC-based) rotator.<br>0x0: LEGACY (One Spur Removal block with a LUT based rotator and 1kHz resolution)<br>0x1: CORDIC (Up to 3 Spur Removal blocks with CORDIC based Rotators and 0.228 Hz resolution in 240kHz sampling rate) |
<!-- page 1737 -->
### WCSS_A_FM_RX_ROT_CTRL_0 (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---------- |
| 27 | BYPASS_IN_G1G2G3 | When Legacy_based Rotator is selected, this field is located at bit 15.<br>0x0: NORMAL (NORMAL)<br>0x1: BYPASS_IN_G1G2G3 (BYPASS_IN_G1G2G3 (bypass in any non zero gain state)) |
| 26:7 | ROT_FREQ | Rotation Frequency. When Legacy_based Rotator is selected, this field is located at bits [14:7] and has 1kHz resolution. When CORDIC_based Rotator is selected, the 20 bits [26:7] represents the spur frequency normalized by the sampling rate (240kHz). The resolution is 0.228 Hz. |
| 6 | FORCE_DC_TRACK | 0x0: USE_DC (USE_DC (enable built in DC tracking logic in spur rotator))<br>0x1: USE_SPUR (USE_SPUR (use spur_comp_I/Q registers value as dc level to be subtracted from signal after rotation)) |
| 5 | SPUR_DC_DELAY | 0x0: DELAY_2048 (DELAY_2048 (enable dc tracking circuit after 2048 240kHz cycles))<br>0x1: DELAY_4096 (DELAY_4096 (enable dc tracking circuit after 4096 240kHz cycles)) |
| 4 | SPUR_1K_ROT_ENABLE | 0x0: DISABLE (DISABLE (disable and bypass spur rotator))<br>0x1: ENABLE (ENABLE (enable spur rotator)) |
| 3:2 | SPUR_DC_IIR_RND | Set the rounding position for DC tracking.<br>0x0: ROUND_3 (Recommended)<br>0x1: ROUND_4<br>0x2: ROUND_5<br>0x3: ROUND_6 |
| 1:0 | SPUR_INT_SETTING | Set the DC tracking integration period. Number of cycles below in 240kHz period<br>0x0: INTEGRATE_256 (Recommended)<br>0x1: INTEGRATE_512<br>0x2: INTEGRATE_1024<br>0x3: INTEGRATE_2048 |

## WCSS_A_FM_DEMOD_DC_IF_OFFSET (0x0A1900E0)

* **Type**: RW
* **Clock**: APB
* **Reset State**: 0x00000000

This is 16bit register contains fm_demod 16 bit dc offset. This register should be calculated based on the rotator freq. This register is used by fm_demod value to subtract FM DC offset after demodulation.

DEMOD_DC_IF_OFFSET = (429 * (-rot_freq + 100)) / 4

## WCSS_A_FM_RX_ROT_CTRL_1 (0x0A190120)

* **Type**: RW
* **Clock**: APB
* **Reset State**: 0x00000000

This register is to control the second spur removal block.

The idea behind the spur removal block is to rotate the signal such that the spur will move to DC. Then you remove a DC value representing the level of the spur. There are two options for that DC value. The first is to use a DC tracking filter to estimate it. The second is to use a predetermined value in spur_comp_i/q registers.

The second spur removal block should only be enabled when first spur removal block is enabled.
<!-- page 1740 -->

| :--- | :--- | :---------- |
| 27 | BYPASS_IN_G1G2G3 | 0x0: NORMAL (NORMAL)<br>0x1: BYPASS_IN_G1G2G3 (BYPASS_IN_G1G2G3 (bypass in any non zero gain state)) |
| 26:7 | ROT_FREQ | Rotation Frequency. Available only when CORDIC_based Rotator is selected. The 20 bits [26:7] represents the spur frequency normalized by the sampling rate (240kHz). The resolution is 0.228 Hz. |
| 6 | FORCE_DC_TRACK | 0x0: USE_DC (USE_DC (enable built in DC tracking logic in spur rotator))<br>0x1: USE_SPUR (USE_SPUR (use spur_comp_I/Q registers value as dc level to be subtracted from signal after rotation)) |
| 5 | SPUR_DC_DELAY | 0x0: DELAY_2048 (DELAY_2048 (enable dc tracking circuit after 2048 240kHz cycles))<br>0x1: DELAY_4096 (DELAY_4096 (enable dc tracking circuit after 4096 240kHz cycles)) |

### WCSS_A_FM_RX_ROT_CTRL_2

* **Address:** `0x0A19012C`
* **Type:** RW
* **Clock:** APB
* **Reset State:** `0x00000000`

This register is to control the third spur removal block.

The idea behind the spur removal block is to rotate the signal such that the spur will move to DC. The Then you remove a DC value representing the level of the spur. There are two options for that DC value. The first is to use a DC tracking filter to estimate it. The second is to use a predetermined value in spur_comp_i/q registers.

The third spur removal block should only be enabled when the first 2 spur removal blocks are enabled.
<!-- page 1742 -->

| 26:7 | ROT_FREQ | Rotation Frequency. Aavailable only when CORDIC_based Rotator is selected. The 20 bits [26:7] represents the spur frequency normalized by the sampling rate (240kHz). The resolution is 0.228 Hz. |
| 6 | FORCE_DC_TRACK | 0x0: USE_DC (USE_DC (enable built in DC tracking logic in spur rotator))<br>0x1: USE_SPUR (USE_SPUR (use spur_comp_I/Q registers value as dc level to be subtracted from signal after rotation)) |
| 5 | SPUR_DC_DELAY | 0x0: DELAY_2048 (DELAY_2048 (enable dc tracking circuit after 2048 240kHz cycles))<br>0x1: DELAY_4096 (DELAY_4096 (enable dc tracking circuit after 4096 240kHz cycles)) |
| 4 | SPUR_1K_ROT_ENABLE | 0x0: DISABLE (DISABLE (disable and bypass spur rotator))<br>0x1: ENABLE (ENABLE (enable spur rotator)) |
| 3:2 | SPUR_DC_IIR_RND | Set the rounding position for DC tracking.<br>0x0: ROUND_3 (Recommended)<br>0x1: ROUND_4<br>0x2: ROUND_5<br>0x3: ROUND_6 |
| 1:0 | SPUR_INT_SETTING | Set the DC tracking integration period. Number of cycles below in 240kHz period.<br>0x0: INTEGRATE_256 (Recommended)<br>0x1: INTEGRATE_512<br>0x2: INTEGRATE_1024<br>0x3: INTEGRATE_2048 |

## 10.25 WCSS_A_A2XB_A2XB

### WCSS_A_A2XB_A2XB_CFG

**Address:** `0x0A100400`
**Type:** RW
**Reset State:** `0x00000020`

Description: This register's value configures general A2XB features.

| Bits | Name | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 21:16 | MSTR_SPLIT_TIMEOUT | R | Shows the split timeout status of each of the CDAHB masters (one bit per master). When set signifies that the master has been split for longer than the timeout limit and therefore has seen a split timeout. The bits are sticky so that if more than one timeout happen the new timed out masters get OR-ed in with the previous value. |
| 15:10 | MSTR_SPLIT_STAT | R | Shows the split status of each of the CDAHB masters (one bit per master). When set signifies that the master has been split by A2XB.<br>There are four reasons for a master being split:<br>1. Command Queue is full so request could not be accepted<br>2. Write data Queue is full so write data could not be accepted<br>3. Read request is pending and A2XB is waiting on AXI read completion<br>4. A write by another master is pending due to <2> so a new write command cannot be accepted |
| 9:2 | SPLIT_LIMIT | RW | configures the split timeout limit in the AHB slave in thousands of cycles. If a master is split for more than the configured limit a split timeout error interrupt will be generated. |
<!-- page 1754 -->

### WCSS_A_A2XB_A2XB_CFG (continued)

| Bits | Name | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1 | BUSY_OFF | RW | Purely a debug feature. A bug in the busy generation logic has the potential to hang every master in Riva. Should this type of bug be encountered, setting this bit to 1 will ensure that busy is always low, thereby preventing masters from getting hung waiting for completion of writes. Note that this will likely cause data coherency issues between masters. |
| 0 | ENABLE | R | Set to enable the A2XB bridge functionality. This register is actually on the PMU and this read only bit just reflects the status of the corresponding PMU register.<br>When set to zero all rd/wr requests not destined to internal A2XB registers will generate an AHB error response. |

| 2 | A2XB_SPLIT_TIMEOUT_ERR_INT_MSK | When clear it masks off the a2xb_split_timeout_err interrupt request. |
| 1 | A2XB_RD_ERR_INT_MSK | When clear it masks off the a2xb_rd_err interrupt request. |
| 0 | A2XB_WR_ERR_INT_MSK | When clear it masks off the a2xb_wr_err interrupt request. |

### WCSS_A_A2XB_INT_SRC

**Address:** `0x0A10040C`
**Type:** R
**Reset State:** `0x00000000`

Description: The value of this register is the interrupt source.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 3 | A2XB_AXI_HALT_REQ_SET_INT | This field is only set when A2XB receives a halt request from the AXI NOC (visible through halt[haltreq_external]=1) It is NOT set for internally driven halt requests (halt[haltreq_internal]=1) Upon receiving the halt request, the A2XB will complete all pending AXI transfers but will from then on return error responses to any AHB transaction destined to the AXI master port. Local access to A2XB CSRs will still work normally. |
| 2 | A2XB_SPLIT_TIMEOUT_ERR_INT | This field is set when the A2XB GAS detects that a master has been split for longer than the timeout limit. This is a fatal error that will require at least a full A2XB reset to recover. On occurrence, A2XB will immediately unsplit any split masters, will flush all its buffers, will discard any data incoming on its AXI port side and will from then on return error responses to any AHB transaction destined to the fabric. Local access to A2XB CSRs will still work normally. |
| 1 | A2XB_RD_ERR_INT | This field is set when A2XB receives an error response from the AXI fabric on any data beat of a read transaction. Data following the first beat with an error and belonging to the same transfer will be discarded and when the AHB master returns to complete its read it will be able to complete only as many beats as completed without an AXI error (if any) and will then receive an AHB error response on the beat that incurred the AXI error. |
<!-- page 1756 -->

### WCSS_A_A2XB_INT_SRC (continued)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 0 | A2XB_WR_ERR_INT | This field is set when A2XB receives an error response from the AXI fabric for a write transaction. Since the AHB protocol provides no way to notify the originating master of errors incurred on posted writes, this interrupt will be the only indication that a write error occurred. |

### WCSS_A_A2XB_HALT

**Address:** `0x0A100428`
**Type:** RW
**Reset State:** `0x00000008`

Description: This register contains control and status bits related to the haltreq/haltack interface.

| Bits | Name | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 3 | MASTER_IDLE | R | This bit is only set when there are no pending AXI transfers so the AXI master interface is idle. |
| 2 | HALTACK | R | Reflects the status of the haltack WCSS output signal. This bit can be set if either internal or external halt requests are asserted and only after the interface has completed all pending AXI transfers and is idle. |
| 1 | HALTREQ_EXTERNAL | R | Reflects the status of the external haltreq input signal to the WCSS subsystem. The triggered behavior when set is identical to the one described for the haltreq_internal bit. |
| 0 | HALTREQ_INTERNAL | RW | Internal haltreq request. When set this bit triggers the haltreq/haltack protocol. When set, the A2XB interface will finish all pending AXI transfers but will not accept any new AXI-bound requests from any master returning an AHB error response instead. Once set this bit is set it can only be cleared by resetting the A2XB interface. Accesses to A2XB csr registers are not affected by this bit. |
<!-- page 1759 -->

### WCSS_A_A2XB_AXI_SB_CFG

**Address:** `0x0A10042C`
**Type:** RW
**Reset State:** `0x000000DB`

Description: This register serves to configure the values used to drive the AXI sideband signals that are not used within WCSS and for which otherwise constant values would be driven.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 8:6 | AMEMTYPE_HW_MASTERS | This bitfield contains the value that will be used to drive the AXI amemtype[2:0] signal for ALL transfers originated by (non-cpu) all other hardware masters. HW modules only access packet memory in DDR and so its default value should not be changed. |
| 5:3 | AMEMTYPE_CPU_BURST | This bitfield contains the value that will be used to drive the AXI amemtype[2:0] signal for burst transfers originated by the internal WCSS cpu, such accesses are always used for cacheable regions (HPROT[3]=1) |
| 2:0 | AMEMTYPE_CPU_SINGLE | This bitfield contains the value that will be used to drive the AXI amemtype[2:0] signal for single beat transfers originated by the internal WCSS cpu. The concern was that using a memtype of NORMAL to access locations with potential sideffects (FIFOs, registers) could result in corruption in certain scenarios. This field provides a way to use a type of strongly-ordered or device for this type of transfers. This is because cacheable access always use burst transfers while non-cacheable accesses will always be mapped to single transfers. So, HPROT[3:2]=01 (non-cacheable, bufferable) which is roughly equivalent to AMEMTYPE=DEVICE, can be inferred when the bridge sees a cpu initiated single-beat 32-bit transfer.<br>Also, Note that HPROT[3:2]=01 (non-cacheable, bufferable), even if available to the bridge and used to automatically set amemtype=DEVICE, would not guarantee the requirement of the NOC team that a DEVICE type never go to the DDR. This is because DDR memory locations shared or used by WCSS ARM9 SW to communicate with other processors need to be marked as non-cacheable because no mechanism exists to synchronize the Pronto ARM9 caches when the contents of the shared memory are changed by other processors in the system. I really don't see a way to simultaneously guarantee the dual requirement that CSR accesses always use DEVICE while DDR accesses always use NORMAL without building a non-portable (if hardwired) or expensive (if programmable) linkage of the WCSS subsystem to a target MSM's memory map simply to map to the required amemtype. This is not a failure of the WCSS subsystem but rather a consequence of the system using non-standard ARM signals which our stock ARM9 CPU obviously does not support |
<!-- page 1760 -->

## 10.26 WCSS_A_ADU_ADU

### WCSS_A_ADU_CONTROL

**Address:** `0x0A082800`
**Type:** RW
**Reset State:** `0x0BFF0002`

Description: Contains configuration information for the adu

| Bits | Name | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:24 | NEXT_WQ | RW | This field indicates the WQ that the ADU will push the frames to after they have been processed. This field is only used when 'push_wq_selection_mode' is set to '1'. |
| 23:16 | WOW_WQ | RW | This field indicates the WQ that the ADU will push the frames during WOW mode. This field is only used when 'push_wq_selection_mode' is set to '1'. |
| 15 | REG_REINIT_ERR_STATE_CFG | RW | When set, ADU reg reinit FSM will go back to idle instead of staying in error state. |
| 13 | REG_REINIT_GOTO_IDLE | RW | When set, ADU reg reinit FSM (BPS, MIMO) will go to idle. |
| 8 | CLEAR_TIMEOUT_CNT | W | Writing a '1' will reset the timeout counter and clear timeout error interrupt. Always read 0. |
| 7 | DISABLE_LENGTH_CHECK | RW | When set, the ADU will not check the subframe length error |
| 6 | PUSH_WQ_SELECTION_WOW_MODE | RW | This field controls where the ADU finds the index for the WQ to which the processed frames need to be pushed to in WOW mode. This bit should be set (a 0->1 transition) prior to WOW mode to select the WOW_WQ. Upon the assertion of dpu_wakeuphost, ADU will push to the normal WQ. 0: ADU will push the frame to the WQ that is selected by the push_wq_selection_mode 1: ADU will push the frame to the WQ that is indicate in the 'WOW_WQ' field in this register |
| 5 | ADU_ERROR_EXIT | W | Writing a '1' will clear the interrupts and ADU will go back to IDLE from ERROR_STATE. Always read 0 |


<!-- page 1761 -->
### WCSS_A_ADU_CONTROL (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 4 | ADU_BYPASS_OPTION_ENABLE | RW | When set, ADU will immediately forward the frame and NOT check if the frame is AMSDU |
| 3 | CLEAR_COUNTERS | RW | When set, the ADU packet counters are cleared To re-enable the counters, this bit needs to be cleared again |
| 2 | DISABLE_HT_FIELD_DETECTION | RW | When set, the ADU will NOT check for the presence of the HT control field |
| 1 | PUSH_WQ_SELECTION_MODE | RW | This field controls where the ADU finds the index for the WQ to which the processed frames need to be pushed to.<br>0: ADU will push the frame to the WQ that is indicated in the 'ADU/DPU routing flag' in the BD descriptor.<br>1: ADU will push the frame to the WQ that is indicated in the 'Next WQ' field in this register |
| 0 | ADU_ENABLE | RW | When set, the ADU is enabled. When the adu gets disabled in the middle of a transfer, it will finish the ongoing transfer. |

## 10.27 WCSS_A_AGC_AGC

### WCSS_A_AGC_AGC_RESET

* **Address:** `0x0A013C00`
* **Type:** RW
* **Reset State:** `0x0001`

Soft reset of the AGC state machine.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 0 | RESET | Reset bit.<br>0x0: NORMAL (Normal operation)<br>0x1: RESET (Reset AGC state machine) |

### WCSS_A_AGC_DIS_MODE

* **Address:** `0x0A013C04`
* **Type:** RW
* **Reset State:** `0x0000`

Disables detection of OFDM (11a,11g)/OFDM-MIMO, Barker/CCK (11b) packets or double bandwidth 11a/MIMO packets. Useful to reduce misdetect probability in a pure 11a or 11b environment.


<!-- page 1781 -->

### WCSS_A_AGC_DIS_MODE (continued)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 3 | DISABLE_11AC80 | Disable quadruple bandwidth bit for 11ac80 MHz packets.<br>0x0: ENABLE (Enable 11ac 80MHz detection.)<br>0x1: DISABLE (Disable 11ac 80MHz packet detection.) |
| 2 | DISABLE_11N40 | Disable double bandwidth bit for 11n40 MHz packets.<br>0x0: ENABLE (Enable 11n 40MHz detection.)<br>0x1: DISABLE (Disable 11n 40MHz packet detection.) |
| 1 | DISABLE_11B | Disable 11b bit.<br>0x0: ENABLE (Enable 11b packet detection.)<br>0x1: DISABLE (Disable 11b packet detection.) |
| 0 | DISABLE_11AG | Disable 11a/g bit.<br>0x0: ENABLE (Enable 11a/g packet detection.)<br>0x1: DISABLE (Disable 11a/g packet detection.) |

### 0x0A013C08 WCSS_A_AGC_RX_OVERRIDE

**Type:** RW  
**Reset State:** 0x0000

This register allows the EN_RX (Receive Enable) outputs of the BBIC, the standby input and the powerdown inputs of the built-in ADC to be software-controlled. These outputs are used to enable the AD converters and RF ASICs for debugging and calibration purposes. The power down bits are used to put all of the ADCs in power down mode (for instance in beacon power save mode) or part of its ADCs to be powered down (for instance a product not using all of the antenna).

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 4 | ENRX_VAL | Enable values for receive chain 0 to 0. For these values to take effect, the corresponding override bits should be set. |
| 0 | STBY_VAL | ADC standby values for receive chain 0 to 0. Note that the standby values are asserted low, and de-asserted high. For these values to take effect, the corresponding override bits should be set. |

### 0x0A013C0C WCSS_A_AGC_PHY_LOOPBACK

**Type:** RW  
**Reset State:** 0x0008

Configures support for PHY loopback.
<!-- page 1782 -->

### WCSS_A_AGC_PHY_LOOPBACK (continued)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 3 | DIG_LOOPBACK | Enables the loopback digitally. |
| 2 | PMI_EN | Enables loop backed data to go out the PMI to the MAC. |
| 1:0 | MODE | Sets the PHY loopback mode. PHY loopback can be enabled statically, where it is always in loopback mode, or dynamically where it only enters loopback mode when we're transmitting.<br>0x0: DISABLED (Disabled)<br>0x1: STATIC_EN (Always enabled)<br>0x2: DYN_EN (Only enabled during packet transmission) |

### 0x0A013C10 WCSS_A_AGC_CONFIG_XBAR

**Type:** RW  
**Reset State:** 0x0000

Sets the configuration for the digital / analog crossbar. This will configure how a particular analog receive chain is mapped to a particular digital RX processing chain. In addition, it will also configure how a particular digital TX processing chain is connected to a particular analog transmit chain. An analog chain includes the baseband analog + the corresponding RF chain. Although there are separate controls for txxbar and rxxbar, for normal mode of operation, they should be set the same. Refer to the System Engineering Specification on the edge portal for the configuration and connectivity of xbar. Note that no analog chain other than analog chain 2 can feed the digital chain 2 and hence there is no xbar functionality on digital chain 2

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 15 | PHYDBG_SEL | PHYDBG input select. Used for playing PHYDBG data into RX ADC path. |
| 14 | IQSWAP_EN | Enables swapping of the I and Q rails of the ADC. |

### 0x0A013C14 WCSS_A_AGC_CW_DETECT

**Type:** RW  
**Reset State:** 0x000B

At packet detection, the PHY detects narrowband interference to avoid false alarms caused by narrowband interference. This type of interference could arise as the result of LO leakage, LO interference of other IEEE802.11 devices in the vicinity of the receiver and other, intentional radiators, such as Bluetooth devices. of factors the explanation of which is beyond the scope of this guide. When CW is found the packet detection is ignored since it is most likely that the packet detectors triggered on the CW interference. The CW frequency is used to set a CW notchfilter
<!-- page 1783 -->

### WCSS_A_AGC_CW_DETECT (continued)

...inside the RXFIR to cancel out that interferer in the future, until a different CW interferer is found or until a timer expires.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 7 | TXLO_DIS | Disables the use of the Rxfir with a TX LO notch.<br>0x0: ENABLE (Enable TX LO Notch Filter.)<br>0x1: DISABLE (Disable TX LO Notch Filter.) |
| 6 | CW_EN_RXB_DATA | Enables CW notch processing when the AGC is in states 9 or 11.<br>0x0: DISABLE (Disable CW Notch Filter when processing RXB data.)<br>0x1: ENABLE (Enable CW Notch Filter when processing RXB data.) |
| 5 | CW_EN_RXB | Enables CW notch processing when the AGC is in states 2,3 or 7.<br>0x0: DISABLE (Disable CW Notch Filter when processing RXB preamble.)<br>0x1: ENABLE (Enable CW Notch Filter when processing RXB preamble.) |
| 4 | CW_EN_RXA_DATA | Enables CW notch processing when the AGC is in states 8 or 10.<br>0x0: DISABLE (Disable CW Notch Filter when processing RXA data.)<br>0x1: ENABLE (Enable CW Notch Filter when processing RXA data.) |
| 3 | CW_EN_RXA | Enables CW notch processing when the AGC is in states 2,3 or 6.<br>0x0: DISABLE (Disable CW Notch Filter when processing RXA preamble.)<br>0x1: ENABLE (Enable CW Notch Filter when processing RXA preamble.) |
| 2 | DC_DIS | Disables the use of the Rxfir with a DC notch. Note that this bitfield should be set in conjunction with the RACTL's rxfir_scaling_coeff register.<br>0x0: ENABLE (Enable DC Notch Filter.)<br>0x1: DISABLE (Disable DC Notch Filter.) |
| 1 | RADAR_DETECT_DIS | 0x1: DISABLE (Disable use of CW detector during radar detection.)<br>0x0: ENABLE (Enable use of CW detector during radar detection .) |
| 0 | PKT_DETECT_DIS | 0x1: DISABLE (Disable use of CW detects to abort packet detects.)<br>0x0: ENABLE (Enable use of CW detects to abort packet detects..) |

### 0x0A013C18 WCSS_A_AGC_CW_NOTCH_TIMEOUT

**Type:** RW  
**Reset State:** 0x0064
<!-- page 1784 -->

### WCSS_A_AGC_CW_NOTCH_TIMEOUT (continued)

The CW notch filter applies a notch to the receiver input signal at a frequency as measured by the CW detector. The notch is applied until the CW detector passes a different value to the notch filter, or until the notch filter's built-in timer expires. When this timer expires the input signal bypasses the notch filter altogether. The timeout value of the timer is defined in this register.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 8 | DIS | Setting this field to 1 is equivalent to setting an infinite timeout value. When set, the cw notch index will remain the same until is set to a different value. |
| 7:0 | VAL | Timeout value. This value is multiplied by 2^19 to get the number of 80 MHz clock cycles that make up the timeout time.<br>0x1: MINIMUM (100 * 2^19 = 0.65 seconds)<br>0x64: DEFAULT (1 * 2^19 = 6.5 milliseconds)<br>0xFF: MAXIMUM (255 * 2^19 = 1.67 seconds) |

### 0x0A013C1C WCSS_A_AGC_GAIN_MODE

**Type:** RW  
**Reset State:** 0x0000

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1 | MULT_STEP | This bit defines if only a single COARSE_STEP or SAT_STEP is made or if multiple steps are possible.<br>0x0: SING (Single sat/coarse gain step)<br>0x1: MULT (Multiple sat/coarse gain steps) |
| 0 | USE_RXFIR_PWR | Setting this field to 1 will cause the gain computation to come from the power measured in the RXFIR power detector instead of the ADC power detector. |

### 0x0A013C24 WCSS_A_AGC_GAINSET0

**Type:** RW  
**Reset State:** 0x0000

Allows to break AGC gain setting loop and manually override AGC setting of chain 0. For debugging purposes.
<!-- page 1785 -->

### WCSS_A_AGC_GAINSET0 (continued)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 7 | OVERRIDE | Override bit.<br>0x0: NORMAL (automatic gain control)<br>0x1: OVERRIDE (manual gain setting) |
| 6:0 | GAIN | Gain setting. |

### 0x0A013C28 WCSS_A_AGC_GAINSET_WRITE

**Type:** W  
**Reset State:** 0x0000

When a 1 is written to this register, the gain registers of the RFIC(s) are loaded with the values stored in bit [3:0] of registers GAINSET0. 0, provided that the override bit [4] these registers is set. At the moment that these registers are written, the gain that is programmed in the RFIC receivers will remain at its previously programmed value. Writing to this register enforces a write of the gain values to the RFIC gain registers, which would otherwise happen only when the AGC decides to change gain when a packet is received or a strong signal clips the RF frontend, or when the AGC is reset (through RX_RESET signal, SLEEP signal, packet transmission or by writing to AGC_RESET register. On the chains on which the override bit is not set, the current gain remains unchanged. This register is provided for debugging purposes. This register cannot be read back

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 0 | OVERRIDE | Gain write pulse bit.<br>0x0: NORMAL (Idle)<br>0x1: OVERRIDE (Write gain settings to the RFIC) |

**Type:** RW

This stores the channel frequency in MHz is stored used to calculate resampler offset for 11b operation. This register needs to be reprogrammed every time the MAC switches to a different RF channel. Width is 13 bits, so 11b mode can also operate in 5 GHz band, if the need arises.

### 0x0A013C38 WCSS_A_AGC_N_ACTIVE

### WCSS_A_AGC_SAT_STEP (0x0A013CD4)
**Type:** RW  
**Reset State:** 0x0072  

The sat_step field is used to specify the step used to gain the RF Frontend down if the RF is saturated. The same value is used to step up the gain if the signal energy is below TH_NO_SIGNAL. This gain step is specified in multiples of 2dB from 0 dB to 128 dB. The enable field is used to switch this functionality on or off.




<!-- page 1801 -->
### WCSS_A_AGC_SAT_STEP (Continued)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 7 | IGNORE_ADC_CLIP | Normally, a sat step is only taken if a digital (or ADC) clip is also seen at the same time, but if you set this bit to 1, then only the RF sat flag is used. |
| 6 | SAT_STEP_EN | Allow AGC to make gain step when in Vega mode RF frontend is in saturation.<br>0x0: DISABLE (Saturated gain step disabled)<br>0x1: ENABLE (Saturated gain step enabled) |
| 5:0 | SAT_STEP | Coarse gain step. Default value is 25, or 50dB step for Vega mode |

| :--- | :--- | :--- |

| 13 | VHT_STS_COARSE_GAIN_SET_DIS | Enable VHT-STS coarse gain setting<br>0x1: DISABLE (Disable WCSS_A_AGC_COARSE_STEP_HT coarse gain setting.)<br>0x0: ENABLE (Enable WCSS_A_AGC_COARSE_STEP_HT coarse gain setting) |
| 12 | HT_STS_GAIN_SET_DIS | Enable HT-STS gain setting<br>0x1: DISABLE (Disable HT-STS gain setting.)<br>0x0: ENABLE (Enable HT-STS gain setting) |
| 11:6 | VHTSTS_STEP | Coarse gain step for 2nd STF in mixed mode packets. |
| 5:0 | HTSTS_STEP | Coarse gain step. |

### WCSS_A_AGC_MAX_POWER_DIFF

**Address:** `0x0A013CE0`
**Type:** `RW`
**Reset State:** `0x0004`

The value in this register specifies maximum power difference. If the received power on all any antenna is this much less than the power on the strongest antenna, then the AGC limits the gain for the chain with the less power to that corresponding with a power of the strongest power minus the value in this register. This threshold avoids gaining up receive chains with weak signal and thereby blowing up noise. antenna.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 3:0 | DIFFERENCE | Maximum power difference in 4 dB steps. From 0 .. 14*4=56 dB |

**Address:** `0x0A013CE4`
**Type:** `RW`
**Reset State:** `0x0020`

Target Backoff for Listen chains. The gain is set this amount of dBs below the gain that would fully saturate the receiver. The backoff is specified in 0.5 dB steps.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 5:0 | BACK_OFF | Backoff value. Default backoff is 32, or 16 dB. |

### WCSS_A_AGC_TARGET_BO_INACTIVE

**Address:** `0x0A013CE8`
**Type:** `RW`
**Reset State:** `0x0024`

### WCSS_A_AGC_TARGET_BO_INACTIVE (Continued)

Target Backoff for Receive chains, that are not listen chains. The gain is set this amount of dBs below the gain that would fully saturate the receiver. This backoff is typically higher than that of listen antennas to accommodate the unknown upfading on the inactive receive chains. The backoff is specified in 0.5 dB steps.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 5:0 | BACK_OFF | Backoff value. Default backoff is 36, i.e. 18 dB. |

**Type:** `RW`

| :--- | :--- | :--- |

| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 10:0 | THRESHOLD | Clip threshold in offset binary. Example: if the 2's complement threshold is -400, then the 11-bit offset binary code is -400 + 1024 = 624. -800 corresponds to 224 |

### WCSS_A_AGC_TH_D0_B_TF_EST

**Address:** `0x0A013D3C`
**Type:** `RW`
**Reset State:** `0x0050`

This registers sets the correlation threshold above which the AGC decides an 802.11b packet is being received during the timing and frequency estimation state. This is a reconfirmation test which reduces the false alarm rate of the AGC for 11b packets. It is generally set lower than the initial threshold for 11b packets since the correlator is to allow margin for a low correlation value which can occur at the moment the correlator output is sampled (at the end of the 10 us tf(time and frequency)-estimation interval).

### 0x0A013DC8 WCSS_A_AGC_SIFS_TIME_A
* **Type:** RW
* **Reset State:** 0x0028

This register specifies the time in 25 ns increments, that the receiver is insensitive after the reception of an IEEE802.11a packet. This value may be set to zero which increases false detection probability of ACK packets, but which allows receptions of packets with a non-standard interframe spacing.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 9:0 | SIFS_A | SIFS time. Default value is 40, or 1 micro seconds (16 us as per 11a standard - 4us CCA hangover time).<br>0x0: MIN (0 ns, minimum value.)<br>0x1: STEP (25 ns, step size value.)<br>0x3FF: MAX (25.57 us, maximum value.) |

### 0x0A013DCC WCSS_A_AGC_SIFS_TIME_B
* **Type:** RW
* **Reset State:** 0x0028

This register specifies the time in 25 ns increments, that the receiver is insensitive after the reception of an IEEE802.11b packet. This value may be set to zero which increases false detection probability of ACK packet, but which allows receptions of packets with a non-standard interframe spacing.
<!-- page 1820 -->
| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 9:0 | SIFS_B | SIFS time. Default value is 40, or 1 micro seconds.<br>0x0: MIN (0 ns, minimum value.)<br>0x1: STEP (25 ns, step size value.)<br>0x3FF: MAX (25.57 us, maximum value.) |

### 0x0A013DD0 WCSS_A_AGC_MAX_RX_TIME_A
* **Type:** RW
* **Reset State:** 0x01AD

Max receive time of an 11a packet in 12.8 us increments. Used to prevent lockup of the AGC state machine when it is unable to determine end of packet in the case of a corrupted length field when no end of packet level drop is detected.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 11:0 | MAX_RX_TIME | Max RX time. Default value 20+4096*8/6=5482 (6 Mbit/s packet of 4096 bytes plus OFDM preamble) and 429*12.8=5491.2) |

### 0x0A013DD4 WCSS_A_AGC_MAX_RX_TIME_B
* **Type:** RW
* **Reset State:** 0x0A10

Max receive time of an 11b packet in 25.6 us increments. Used to prevent lockup of the AGC state machine when it is unable to determine end of packet in the case of a corrupted length field when no end of packet level drop is detected.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 11:0 | MAX_RX_TIME | Max RX time. Default value 192+4096*8=32960 (1 Mbit/s packet of 4096 bytes plus long preamble) and 2576*12.8=32973) |

### WCSS_A_AGC_RDET_RSSI_THRESHOLD

**Address:** `0x0A013DFC`
**Type:** RW
**Reset State:** `0x007F`

If the maximum of the N_LISTEN RSSI inputs as calculated by the power block in the AGC exceeds the value in the up threshold field of this register, a start of pulse is flagged to the pulse train detector. When the max RSSI sinks below the value of the down threshold field, the end of pulse is flagged. If both thresholds are set to 0, the analog pulse detector (in the Mars RF ASIC) is used instead. The start of the pulse is detected on the rising edge of this signal. The end of the pulse is detected on the falling edge.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 13:7 | DET_THLD_DN | Pulse detection threshold. |
| 6:0 | DET_THLD_UP | Pulse detection threshold. |
<!-- page 1824 -->
### WCSS_A_AGC_RDET_MIN_IAT_WRITE

**Address:** `0x0A013E00`
**Type:** RW
**Reset State:** `0x6F7C`

This register defines the maximum inter-arrival time between radar pulses, measured in multiples of 128 samples. Pulse that arrive after the previous pulse within a time less than the value in this register are ignored by the radar pulse train detector. If set equal to max_iat, then this register has no effect on the operation of the radar detector. This value gets written to the appropriate train detector selected by det_sel, with the write itself enabled using det_write (see register rdet_reset).

| Bits | Name | Description |

### WCSS_A_AGC_RDET_PULSE_WIDTH_MARGIN_WRITE

**Address:** `0x0A013E08`
**Type:** RW
**Reset State:** `0x0005`

When the first pulse of a train arrives, its duration is stored. Subsequent pulses' durations are compared to this first one. If a pulse of a different length is encountered, the pulse train ends. The comparison uses a margin as defined by this register. The check performed is if abs (current_pulse_duration - first_pulse_duration) <= this register then the current pulse does not break the train, and the pulse counter is increased. This value gets written to the appropriate train detector selected by det_sel, with the write itself enabled using det_write (see register rdet_reset).

### WCSS_A_AGC_RDET_MEASUREMENT_DELAY

* **Address:** `0x0A013E58`
* **Type:** RW
* **Reset State:** `0x0020`

This register configures the time interval (measured in rssi samples) after which the radar detector measures rssi level after it returns to the CORR state after a gain set due to a clip event. It can not evaluate RSSI immediately since the RSSI circuit comes out of reset when the CORR state is entered. Therefore it takes time for the RSSI to ramp up (about 32 samples). The time programmed in this register should be larger than the RSSI rampup time.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 8 | CORR_FLAG_BYPASS | Correlation flag function bypass. If asserted, the correlation flag function in the RDET pulse detector (used to delay transition of the main state machine from IDLE to CLIP_S1) will be bypassed.<br>Default setting = 1'b0. |
| 7:0 | TIME | Measurement delay. |

* **Type:** W
* **Reset State:** `0x0000`

This register contains 2 bits that control the operation of the radar detector.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 0 | DFLAG_RST | Reset detector flag. While the detector flag is set further radar detects are ignored and the num_detected and pulse width registers are not updated. By writing a 1 to this register, the detector flag is reset and will be set when the next radar burst is detected.<br>0x0: NORMAL (Normal)<br>0x1: RESET (Reset detector flag) |

### WCSS_A_AGC_CW_PULSE_WIDTH

* **Address:** `0x0A013E64`
* **Type:** RW
* **Reset State:** `0x0019`

When the radar detector's pulse detector detects a radar pulse it monitors the CW detect flag. When this flag is set the pulse detector sets a local flag called cw_detected. When at the end of the radar pulse, the cw_detected flag is still not set, the in the pulse is discounted as a radar pulse (which should be narrow-band) and the pulse_cancel output is asserted. Some pulses are too short to perform a cw detection on. The cw detection time is the sum of the sample data gathering time (which is programmed in CSR cw_radar_delay) and the fft and cw detect calculation time. If the pulse duration is less than the number in this register, then the radar detector'S pulse detector assumes that the detected pulse is a radar pulse. The radar detector's train detectors may still reject is because it is not in between the minimum and maximum radar pulse width.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 7:0 | VAL | Duration of data gathering and calculation time for cw detection, specified in multiples of 0.8 us (16 20 Mhz sample). |

### WCSS_A_AGC_CW_RADAR

* **Address:** `0x0A013E68`
* **Type:** RW
* **Reset State:** `0x007D`

This register configures if and with what delay the radar detector can start the CW detector.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 9 | DET_DIS | Disables control of the CW detector by the radar detector. |
| 8:0 | DELAY | Amount of delay in 40 MHz samples between start pulse of the radar detector and the time that the CW detector starts calculating. |
<!-- page 1835 -->

### WCSS_A_AGC_ACI_DETECT_TH

* **Address:** `0x0A013E6C`
* **Type:** RW
* **Reset State:** `0x0148`

When detecting a radar pulse, the radar detector's pulse detector calculates the difference between the total (pre FIR) RSSI and the in-band (post FIR) RSSI. If this difference exceeds the threshold programmed in this register, the aci_detect flag is asserted. If, during a radar pulse, the ratio of the total time that this flag is asserted and the pulse's duration exceeds the second threshold specified in this register, then the radar deector decides that this pulse was in the adjacent channel. The rain detector will then ignored this pulse. This mechanism help to avoid false triggers on packet traffic, interference and radar pulses in the adjacent channel. This type of false triggers would have the adverse effect that the radar detector would vacate a clean channel because a noisy neighbor.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 12 | DETECT_DIS | 0x1: DISABLE (Disable use of ACI detector during radar detection.)<br>0x0: ENABLE (Enable use of ACI detector during radar detection.) |
| 11:4 | TH_RSSI_ACI | This register field specifies the RSSI delta which the pre and post FIR RSSI should differ by, to be considered adjacent channel power. |
| 3:0 | ACI_FRACTION | This register field specifies the fractional threshold that the pre and post FIR RSSI difference should exceed to be counted as ACI (Adjacent Channel Interference). This threshold is specified in integer multiples of 1/16-ths. For example, a value of 8 means that the RSSI should differ by more than th_rss_aci for more than 50% of the duration of the detected radar pulse for it to ruled ACI. |

### WCSS_A_AGC_NOISE_HIST_CTRL (0x0A013ED4)

**Type:** RW
**Reset State:** 0x0001

Controls various modes of operation of the noise histogram module. It can be reset and stopped, it can be read out and reset, it can read out without being reset, and it can be read out, reset and stopped.
<!-- page 1844 -->
| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 2 | READ_AND_CLEAR | When this bit is set and the read_pulse bit is written to, the current noise histogram bin counter values are latched into the rssi status registers, the noise histogram counters are reset and noise histogram collection continues. |
| 1 | READOUT | When this bit is set and the read_pulse bit is written to, the current noise histogram bin counter values are latched into to the rssi status registers. Noise histogram collection continues. |
| 0 | RESET | When this bit is set the current noise histogram bin counter values are written to the rssi status registers, the noise histogram collection is halted and the counters are reset. |

## WCSS_A_AGC_WATCHDOG_MASK (0x0A013F38)

**Type:** RW  
**Reset State:** 0x0001  

This register is used to mask the watchdog-driven reset of the AGC state machine. When the reset is not masked, an expiry of the AGC watchdog timer will set the timeout state register, generate an interrupt and reset the AGC state machine. When the reset is masked, an expiry of the AGC watchdog timer will set the timeout state register, generate an interrupt, but will not reset the AGC state machine. This functionality is intended for debugging purposes when the AGC state machine needs to remain in the hanging state so the various conditions that may have lead to the hangup can be studied before they are automatically reset by the watchdog timer.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 0 | MASK | 0x0: UNMASKED (watchdog-driven reset enabled)<br>0x1: MASKED (watchdog-driven reset disabled) |

## WCSS_A_AGC_TIMEOUT_STATE (0x0A013F3C)

**Type:** R  
**Reset State:** 0x00000000  

AGC state in which watchdog timer expired.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 4:0 | STATE | AGC State. |

## WCSS_A_AGC_AGC_WATCHDOG_TIMEOUT_WAIT_DCO_A20 (0x0A013F40)

**Type:** RW  
**Reset State:** 0x0000  

This register configures the watchdog timer for the WAIT_DCO_A state of the AGC state machine. The watchdog timer is reset when the AGC state machine transitions from one state to another. When its value exceeds the threshold programmed in this register it resets the AGC state
<!-- page 1852 -->

machine as well as the RXA and RXB modules. A value of zero disables the watchdog timer in this state.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 7:0 | TIME | Timeout delay. This value is multiplied by 2 to arrive at the number of 40 MHz clock cycles after which the watchdog timer expires. This results in a maximum delay of 255 * 2 * 12.5 ns = 6.375 us. |

When its value exceeds the threshold programmed in this register it resets the AGC state machine as well as the RXA and RXB modules. A value of zero disables the watchdog timer in this state.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 7:0 | TIME | Timeout delay. This value is multiplied by 4 (2^2) to arrive at the number of 40 MHz clock cycles after which the watchdog timer expires. This results in a maximum delay of 255 * 2^2 * 25 ns = 25.5 us. |
<!-- page 1857 -->

## 10.28 WCSS_A_BBANA_BBANA

### `0x0A014000 WCSS_A_BBANA_ADC_CTRL`

This set of registers are used to control ADC operations.

* **Type**: RW
* **Reset State**: 0x0000

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 9 | OFFSET_MEAS | Enable ADCs to do offset calibration. |
| 8:7 | INTLV_CTRL | Used to control ADC interleaving. |
| 6 | ADC_PWR_DOWN_N | Power down I & Q reference, clock and output (active low). Not currently used.<br>0x0: PWR_DOWN (Disables both I & Q, reference, clock and output)<br>0x1: ENABLED (ADC I & Q, reference, clock and outputs enabled) |
| 5 | OUTPUT_DISABLE_Q | Output disable control for ADC Q data rail.<br>0x0: NORMAL (Normal ADC output level)<br>0x1: MID (Mid level AC output) |
| 4 | EN_Q_OVERRIDE | Enable override control for ADC Q data rail.<br>0x0: NO_OVERRIDE (Signal in bit 3 is not used to control ADC enable signal)<br>0x1: OVERRIDE (Signal in bit 3 is used to control ADC enable signal) |
| 3 | EN_Q | Enable ADC for Q data rail.<br>0x0: DISABLED (ADC Q data rail disabled)<br>0x1: ENABLED (ADC Q data rail enabled) |
| 2 | OUTPUT_DISABLE_I | Output disable control for ADC I data rail.<br>0x0: NORMAL (Normal ADC output level)<br>0x1: MID (Mid level AC output) |
<!-- page 1865 -->

### `WCSS_A_BBANA_ADC_CTRL` (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |

| 0 | EN_I | Enable ADC for I data rail.<br>0x0: DISABLED (ADC I data rail disabled)<br>0x1: ENABLED (ADC I data rail enabled) |

### `0x0A014004 WCSS_A_BBANA_ADC_CLK_CTRL`

| 2 | CLKEDGE_SEL | Setting used to select the edge of the clock to be used by the ADCs<br>0x0: POSEDGE (Positive edge of clock is used)<br>0x1: NEGEDGE (Negative edge of clock is used) |

## 10.29 WCSS_A_BMU_BMU

### `0x0A080000 WCSS_A_BMU_CONTROL`

Sets the valid range of BD and PDU indexes in the BMU.

* **Type**: RW
* **Reset State**: 0x03FE03FE

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:16 | MAX_PDU_INDEX_NR | Typically the MAX PDU index is greater then the MAC BD index. In that case BDs can not be used as PDUs and vice versa. When MAX_BD_Index and MAX_PDU_index are programmed to the same value, the BMU is set in a special mode: Mixed mode. Each PDU can be used as a BD or each BD used as a PDU. At initialization the PDU idle list does not need to be created, just the BD idle list. When PDUs are requested, they will be taken from the BD idle list. During operation BD and PDU idle lists will both be maintained, but all released PDUs will automatically get moved back to the BD idle list. In this mode, the MAX BD and PDU index number can not be greater then the MAX BD index number that the HW allows. Note that before the WQs get enabled, this value must be programmed accordingly to the amount of packet memoryavailable. This is similar to have to program the bd_pbu_base_address in the MCU. In Volans, the BMU should be configured to only operate in Mixed Mode. |
| 10:0 | MAX_BD_INDEX_NR | Virgo can maximum support 2K BDs. The maximum value that can therefor be programmed is 2047. Where as Libra and Volans can support only 1023 BDs Note that before the WQs get enabled, this value must be programmed accordingly to the amount of packet memoryavailable. This is similar to have to program the bd_pbu_base_address in the MCU. |

### `0x0A080004 WCSS_A_BMU_ERR_INTR_STATUS`

* **Type**: R
* **Reset State**: 0x00000000


<!-- page 1871 -->

This register indicates the BMU Error Interrupt Status When one of these errors occur, the status will always reflect this. The Err_Intr_ENABLE register is used to indicate which error bits will cause an interrupt to be generated. Writing a 1'b1 to a particular bit will clear the error status bit. Most of these errors are generated when the BMU receives a command. In this case the command will be stored in the 'err_int_addr' and 'err_int_wdata' registers.

### WCSS_A_BMU_ERR_INTR_STATUS

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31 | BMU_ACCESS_DIRECTION | When one of the error indications below gets set, this bit will indicate if this happened on a read or write BMU access. 1'b1 indicates write access 1'b0 indicates read access On a write access, register err_int_wdata will contain the write data |
| 30 | BMU_INTERRUPT_STATUS | Status of the BMU err interrupt status signal going to the mcu. This is the OR of all interrupts enabled in this registers and bmu_idle_bd_pdu_threshold_interrupt_status bit from register: bmu_idle_bd_pdu_status. |
| 28 | BTQM_ERR | This is the OR of all the enabled bits from btqm_err_status register Set when the btqm detects an error or some other operational related interrupt in the btqm_err_status register. The details on which btqm error happened can be found in register 'btqm_err_int_status' |
| 27 | DOUBLE_RELEASE_PDU_ERR | Error set when head or tail of a list of linked PDUs that is being released is equal to the head or tail pointer of the idle PDU list. Note that there can be a delay between the release command and the detection of this problem due to buffering |
| 26 | DOUBLE_RELEASE_BD_ERR | Error set when head or tail of a list of linked BDs that is being released is equal to the head or tail pointer of the idle BD list. Note that there can be a delay between the release command and the detection of this problem due to buffering |
| 25 | DOUBLE_PUSH_ERR | Error set when a push command contains a BD index equal to the head or tail pointer of the WQ it is pushed to. |
| 24 | RELEASE_FRAG_BD_INDEX_ERR | When BMU starts releasing defragmentation BD, if a fragment contains invalid BD index this error will be set |
| 23 | MULTIPLE_READY_ERR | Error set when multiple modules in the bmu indicate ready. That should not happen. |
| 22 | RELEASE_INTEGRITY_CHECK_PDU_LINK_ERR | Error set when on a release command, the integrity check failed. The pdu links were incorrect |
| 21 | PUSH_INTEGRITY_CHECK_PDU_LINK_ERR | Error set when on a push bd command, the integrity check failed. The pdu links were incorrect |
| 20 | PUSH_INTEGRITY_CHECK_HEAD_TAIL_PDU_ERR | Error set when on a push bd command, the integrity check failed. The head/tail/entries part in the BD was incorrect |
| 19 | PUSH_INTEGRITY_CHECK_PREV_PDU_ERR | Error set when on a push bd command, the integrity check failed. The prev. pdu pointer in the BD was incorrect |
| 18 | PREV_PDU_INDEX_ERR | Error set when on a release of BD with linked PDUs, and the A-MSDU feature is enabled and the prev PDU pointer has an invalid index. |
<!-- page 1872 -->

### WCSS_A_BMU_ERR_INTR_STATUS (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 17 | NR_OF_PDU_OVERFLOW_ERR | Error set when on a release of PDUs, the number of idle PDUs would gone over the theoretical amount as determined by the MAX BD index and MAX PDU index from the BMU control register |
| 16 | NR_OF_BD_OVERFLOW_ERR | Error set when on a release of BDs, the number of idle BDs would gone over the theoretical amount as determined by the MAX BD index from the BMU control register |
| 15 | WRGAM_ERR | Set when the write GAM indicated an internal error |
| 14 | RDGAM_ERR | Set when the read GAM indicated an internal error |
| 13 | TIME_OUT_ERR | Set when the BMU internally detected is has been hanging There is a timeout counter in the BMU, which tracks the length of each transaction. The timeout count value can be programmed in register: bmu_watchdog_timout_time For this error the 'err_int_addr' and 'err_int_wdata' registers are updated so it is recorded which bmu command caused this error. |
| 12 | IDLE_PDU_LIST_TAIL_ERR | The pdu idle list is corrupted. In the PDU idle list the PDU prefetch unit has read the PDU pointer index from the one but last PDU in the PDU idle list. It was expected that this PDU index pointer points to the PDU indicated in the idle_pdu_tail register. This was however not the case. THis is a serious error as it indicates that the idle PDU list is corrupted. |
| 11 | IDLE_PDU_LIST_CNT_ERR | The pdu idle list is corrupted. In the PDU idle list the PDU prefetch unit has found an PDU who was pointing to the PDU tail index, which would indicate that the end of the idle PDU list has been reached. But this does not correspond with the idle PDU count in the idle_pdu_count register. This error indicates that more PDUs were expected to be in the idle PDU list. THis is a serious error as it indicates that the idle PDU list is corrupted. |
| 10 | PDU_INDEX_FROM_BD_ERR | When a BD with linked PDUs was released, the BMU detected that in the BD the number of linked PDUs was non zero, but the head or tail PDU pointer index in the BD was greater then the MAX PDU index range. This is an indication that the Idle PDU list is broken and is a serious error. |
| 9 | RELEASE_FIFO_FULL_WARNING | Set when the BMU release fifo got full. This will not break BMU operation, but still should not occur as it can effect latency on the AHB bus. This however is minimized due to the split transaction generated by the BMU GAS if the release takes too long. |
| 8 | BD_LINKED_LIST_ERR | Set when in the bd idle list a pointer to a bd index was found that is outside of the valid bd index ranges. This is a serious error and the only way to recover is to soft reset the BMU or generate a bmu module reset |
| 7 | PDU_LINKED_LIST_ERR | Set when in the pdu idle list a pointer to a pdu index was found that is outside of the valid pdu index ranges. This is a serious error and the only way to recover is to soft reset the BMU or generate a bmu module reset |
<!-- page 1873 -->

### WCSS_A_BMU_ERR_INTR_STATUS (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 6 | OUT_OF_MODULE_RANGE_ERR | Set when a BMU command with module index that was out of allowed range was used The valid module index is less than or equal to BMU_HIGHEST_VALID_MASTER_INDEX For this error the 'err_int_addr' and 'err_int_wdata' registers are updated so it is recorded which bmu command caused this error. |
| 5 | OUT_OF_PDU_RANGE | Set when a BMU command with PDU index that was out of allowed range was used For this error the 'err_int_addr' and 'err_int_wdata' registers are updated so it is recorded which bmu command caused this error. |
| 4 | OUT_OF_BD_RANGE | Set when a BMU command with BD index that was out of allowed range was used For this error the 'err_int_addr' and 'err_int_wdata' registers are updated so it is recorded which bmu command caused this error. |
| 3 | UNDEFINED_CMD | Set when an undefined BMU command was given to the BMU For this error the 'err_int_addr' and 'err_int_wdata' registers are updated so it is recorded which bmu command caused this error. |
| 2 | WQ_INVALID | Set when an unenabled or undefined WQ was used in a BMU command In Volans, the valid WQs are "2 to 16 and 23 to 26" For this error the 'err_int_addr' and 'err_int_wdata' registers are updated so it is recorded which bmu command caused this error. |
| 1 | WQ_FULL | This is set with push command when the WQ entries are greater/equal to highest_valid_bd_index value. This shouldn't happen in the system For this error the 'err_int_addr' and 'err_int_wdata' registers are updated so it is recorded which bmu command caused this error. |
| 0 | NOT_ENOUGH_BD_PDU_WARNING | Set when a request for BD_PDUs came in when they were notavailable. The modules should be able to handle this and resubmit their request at a later time. This is not an error, but is given for informational purposes |

This register gives inside into how many BDs and PDUs have been set aside to this master. This number will decrement each time the module gets a BD or PDU.

### WCSS_A_BMU_WQ_ENABLE
* **Address:** `0x0A08006C`
* **Type:** RW
* **Reset State:** `0x00000000`

Controls which WQ will be enabled. These WQs should be enabled during initialization, after the BD and PDU idle lists have been created and all head an tail pointers for the to be enabled WQs have been configured. The number of WQs to be enabled need to be decided at that time. Once enabled, a WQ should never be disable again, as this can cause BD and PDU leaks. Bit 0 corresponds to WQ0, Bit 26 corresponds to WQ 26.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 27:0 | WQ_ENABLE | WQ Enable bits. Bit 0 corresponds to WQ0, Bit 27 corresponds to WQ27. See below for WQ assignments. |

**WQ Assignments:**
* **WQ0:** Assigned for Idle BD from DDR/Ext Memory.
* **WQ1:** Assigned for Idle PDU.
* **WQ2:** Assigned for mCPU RX WQ.
* **WQ3:** Can be assigned to DPU, DXE or mCPU.
* **WQ4:** Can be assigned to DPU, DXE or mCPU.
* **WQ5:** Can be assigned to DPU, DXE or mCPU.
* **WQ6:** Can be assigned to DPU, DXE or mCPU.
* **WQ7:** Can be assigned to DPU, DXE or mCPU.
