### WCSS_A_BMU_CONTROL2
* **Address:** `0x0A080088`
* **Type:** RW
* **Reset State:** `0x00000001`
<!-- page 1888 -->

This register can be used to control bmu A-MSDU support BD/PDU integrity checking by the BMU To enable rxp_bmu_dxe_datalength for DXE wq byte count To enable enhanced reserve all command To enable priority based BD/PDU reservation

### WCSS_A_BMU_CONTROL2 (Continued)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31 | FREEZE_ONE_ERROR_LESS_STRICKED_ENABLE | When bit 'freeze_one_error' is set, and this bit is set, and an error is detected in the BMU, the BMU will freeze, but in a little less rigorous way then when this bit is not set. Get commands will still go through, and the BD/PDU available signals to the RXP and DPU will not be masked off. This will prevent DPU and RXP getting into some error state. |
| 7 | BLOCK_RXP_PUSH_INTEGRITY_CHECK | When set, and 'push_data_integrity_check' is also set, the push integrity will be performed on all WQs except WQ 2. That is the WQ that RXP is pushing to. |
| 6 | FREEZE_ONE_ERROR_ENABLE | When set, and an error is detected in the BMU, the BMU will freeze. That is, release commands are thrown away, get bd/dpu commands will not be successful anymore, and reservation request will return unsuccessful. All wq signals and bd/pdu available signals will be set to low. |
| 5 | RELEASE_INTEGRITY_CHECK | When set, and a release command is received by the BMU, the BMU will check the integrity of the BD and linked PDUs. If a problem is found with the linked DPU pointers, an error is reported and the frame is not pushed into the WQ, so that the contents remains available for debugging |
| 4 | PUSH_DATA_INTEGRITY_CHECK | When set, and a push command is received by the BMU, the BMU will check the integrity of the BD and linked PDUs. If a problem is found with the BD/DPU pointers, an error is reported and the frame is not pushed into the WQ, so that the contents remains available for debugging. The index of the BD that caused the problem can be read in register: `bmu_push_integrity_err_bd_index` |
| 3 | RXP_BMU_DXE_DATALEN_ENABLE | When set, any packet push from Rxp to Dxe, rxp_bmu_dxe_datalen is taken to calculate dxe data length |
| 2 | ENHANCED_RESERVE_ALL_ENABLE | When set, reserve all command checks for TX memory threshold if tx_threshold is greater than BTQM memory size then it reserves min of (tx_threshold - BTQM memory size, idle Packet memory size - requested module threshold) |
| 1 | PRIORITY_BASED_RES_ENABLE | When set, enables priority based BD/PDU reservation command |
| 0 | AMSDU_RELEASE_SUPPORT_ENABLE | When set, the A-MSDU support for releasing PDUs from BDs is enabled. This means that the BMU will evaluate the setting of the PREV PDU index field in the BD. If this field is zero, the PDUs are released according to the head/tail and PDU count linked to the BD. When the PREV PDU index field is unequal to zero, the BMU will use this index as the 'tail' index of the list of PDUs to release. The amount of PDUs to release is set equal to PDU count minus 1. |
<!-- page 1889 -->

### WCSS_A_BMU_DISABLE_WQ_DA
* **Address:** `0x0A08008C`
* **Type:** RW
* **Reset State:** `0x00000000`

This register can be used to disable the `wq_da_available` signals. In that case, modules will think that their WQ is empty.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 26:2 | DISABLE_WQ_DA | Bit 2 corresponds with WQ 2, bit 3 with WQ 3 etc. When set, the `wq_da_available` signal to a WQ will always indicate that the WQ is empty. This overwrites any real amount of frames buffered in a WQ. |

### WCSS_A_BMU_DISABLE_BD_PDU_AVAIL
* **Address:** `0x0A080090`
* **Type:** RW
* **Reset State:** `0x00000000`

This register can be used to disable the `bd_pdu_available` signals. In that case, modules will think that no more BDs or PDUs are available, and will stall their operation.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 10:0 | DISABLE_BD_PDU_AVAIL | Bit 0 corresponds with master 0, bit 1 with master 1 etc. When set, the `bd_pdu_available` signal to a master will always indicate that no BDs and PDUs are available. This overwrites any real amount of BDs or PDUs being available for that module. |

The BD indexes returned for the last 4 pop commands that were issued for the specified WQ, are captured in the registers: `pop_cmd_trace_bd_index0`, `pop_cmd_trace_bd_index1`, `pop_cmd_trace_bd_index2` and `pop_cmd_trace_bd_index3`. ### 0x0A0800E0 WCSS_A_BMU_CONTROL4

| Type | Reset State |
| :--- | :--- |
| RW | 0x00000F28 |

This register can be used to control the generation of the 'priority' signal to the DAHB arbiter who passes this on to the MIF. This priority setting will help BMU getting faster 'prioritized' access to the MIF memory over other (SYS, mCPU) interfaces to the MIF.
<!-- page 1897 -->

| Bits | Name | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31 | PREFETCH_FIFO_ACCESS_PRIORITY_SET | R | When set, the prefetch fifo priority signal is set, resulting in the MIF giving priority to the DAHB accesses. |
| 30 | RELEASE_FIFO_ACCESS_PRIORITY_SET | R | When set, the release fifo priority signal is set, resulting in the MIF giving priority to the DAHB accesses. |
| 29 | PDU_PREFETCH_ACCESS_PRIORITY_SET | R | When set, the pdu based prefetch priority signal is set, resulting in the MIF giving priority to the DAHB accesses. |
| 28 | BD_PREFETCH_ACCESS_PRIORITY_SET | R | When set, the bd based prefetch priority signal is set, resulting in the MIF giving priority to the DAHB accesses. |
| 22:16 | NR_OF_PREFETCH_ENTRIES | R | The number of entries in the PDU prefetch fifo |
| 11:8 | PREFETCH_FIFO_ACCESS_PRIORITY_THRESHOLD | RW | The 'priority' signal is set when the number of used PDU entries in the prefetch fifo gets below this threshold, and there are still PDUs left that can be prefetched When BMU is operating in the special mode where every 128 byte memory segment can be BD or PDU, the amount of the 'priority' signal is set when the prefetched BDs are below the threshold, and the PDU prefetch fifo has less then this threshold number of used entries. |
| 6:0 | RELEASE_FIFO_ACCESS_PRIORITY_THRESHOLD | RW | The 'priority signal is set when the release fifo gets filled above this threshold |

| 17 | REGISTER_PSPOLL_TRIGGER_WHEN_DA_AVAIL | RW | When set, and Data Null transmission is NOT enabled as response to a PSPoll, the pspoll trigger will only be registered when there is data in a transmit queue |

### WCSS_A_BMU_BTQM_STA_ENABLE_DISABLE_CONTROL

**Address:** 0x0A0800FC
**Type:** RW
**Reset State:** 0x00000000

Controls the enable-ing or disable-ing of a STA Whenever a value is written into this register, the BTQM will process the STA settings that came with it. A status bit will indicate if the BTQM is still processing an 'update' command. The next update command should not be issued till the status bit has been cleared. Note that this can sometimes take quite a while. If for example just before a STA-disable command, a transmit exchange sequence with that STA had started, that transmit exchange sequence will be allowed to finish first. This is done to prevent abnormal abortion of sequences.

| Bits | Name | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31 | STA_UPDATE_STATUS | R | When set to one, BTQM is processing the last STAid configuration command written to this register. |
| 10:8 | STA_CONFIGURATION_COMMAND | RW | <ul><li>000: Enable the transmit queues, but do NOT enable transmission</li><li>001: Enable the transmit queues, AND enable transmission</li><li>010: Disable the transmit queues AND disable transmission</li><li>011: Disable the transmit queues AND disable transmission AND cleanup any data left in the transmit queues</li><li>100: Clear the fields related to control frames (ps-poll bit, apsd trigger bit, data null sent bit, qos null sent bit, remaining apsd frame count and eosp sent bit)</li><li>101: Disable transmission, but leave transmit queues enabled AND clear the fields related to control frames (ps-poll bit, apsd trigger bit, data null sent bit, qos null sent bit, remaining apsd frame count and eosp sent bit)</li><li>110: Disable transmission, but leave transmit queues enabled</li></ul> |
| 3:0 | STAID | RW | The STAid for which the STA operation is intended. |

### 0x0A080178 WCSS_A_BMU_STA_CONFIG_STATUS2

* **Type:** RW
* **Reset State:** 0x00000000

Provides the STA information corresponding to the 'staid' programmed in the 'sta_config_status1' register This register only has valid contents when the 'read_write_status' bit in the 'sta_config_status1' register is NOT set

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 22 | EOSP_SENT_STATUS | When set to one, the BTQM has sent a QoS frame for which the EOSP bit in the QoS field was set. This field is used by the BTQM to track the sending of this indicating in case APSD in combination with AMPDU aggregation is used |
| 21 | QOS_NULL_SENT_ONCE_STATUS | When set to one, the BTQM has sent a QoS Null frame. This field is used to be able to indicate that the previous transmission was not successfull, and the next time around the QoS Null will be resent one more time |
| 20 | DATA_NULL_SENT_ONCE_STATUS | When set to one, the BTQM has sent a Data Null frame. This field is used to be able to indicate that the previous transmission was not successfull, and the next time around the Data Null will be resent one more time |
| 18:16 | CURRENT_REMAINING_TX_FRAME_CNT | This value will be taken as the 'current remaining tx frame count'. Typically this value should be set to zero, and access here is only provided for backup or testing purposes When set to a non zero value, it will only be used when also 'current_apsd_trig_received_setting' has been set, and the 'sta_u_apsd_enable' has been set. |
| 14 | CURRENT_APSD_TRIG_RECEIVED_SETTING | When set to one, the BTQM will assume that an apsd trigger frame has just been received |
| 13 | CURRENT_PS_POLL_RECEIVED_SETTING | When set to one, the BTQM will assume that a ps_poll frame has just been received |
| 12 | CURRENT_PWR_STATE_SETTING | When set to one, the BTQM will assume that the STA is in power save mode. |
<!-- page 1916 -->

### WCSS_A_BMU_STA_CONFIG_STATUS2 (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 10:8 | INITIAL_REMAINING_TX_FRAME_CNT | After receiving an APSD trigger frame, the value in this register will represent the number of response frames that will be sent to the STA. A value of 7 indicates, to drain the complete transmit queue |
| 6 | QOS_NULL_RESP_ENABLE | When set, and an apsd trigger is received and all APSD delivery enabled queues are empty, the BTQM will indicate to the TPE to transmit a QoS null frame |
| 5 | U_DATA_NULL_RESP_ENABLE | When set, and a ps-poll apsd trigger is received and all the (non APSD deliver enabled) queues are empty, the BTQM will indicate to the TPE to transmit a Data null frame |
| 4 | STA_U_APSD_TRACK_ENABLE | When set to one, the BTQM will the reception and handling of APSD trigger frames |
| 1 | STA_TX_ENABLE | When set, transmission for this sta is enabled |
| 0 | STA_ENABLE | When set, the STAid is enabled |

### WCSS_A_BMU_BMU_PKT_MEMORY_CONFIG_MODE (0x0A08025C)

* **Type:** RW
* **Reset State:** 0x00000000

To configure each module operational mode i.e to use local/external memory as packet memory to get BD/PDUs:
* 00: External Memory Only -> Defined master gets BD/PDUs from External (DDR) memory only
* 01: Local Memory Only -> Defined master gets BD/PDUs from Local Memory (cMem) only
* 10: Local/Ext -> Defined master gets from cMem and when available BD/PDUs falls below the threshold level BMU gives out BD/PDUs for DDR memory
* 11: Reserved

| Bits | Name | Description |

| 21:20 | MASTER10 | To configure Master10 module operational mode |
| 19:18 | MASTER9 | To configure Master9 module operational mode |
| 17:16 | MASTER8 | To configure Master8 module operational mode |
| 15:14 | MASTER7 | To configure Master7 module operational mode |
| 13:12 | MASTER6 | To configure Master6 module operational mode |
| 11:10 | MASTER5 | To configure Master5 module operational mode |

## 10.31 WCSS_A_CAHB_CAHB

### WCSS_A_CAHB_CAHB_RXP_PL (0x0A082C00)

**Type:** RW

**Reset State:** 0x00000005

cahb Arbiter arbitration priority level for rxp master. In the cahb arbitration scheme the master with highest priority level always wins. Should there be more than one master with the same priority then the winning master will be selected using a round-robin algorithm.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 3:0 | PRIORITY | Arbitration priority for rxp master.The lowest priority level is 1 and the highest priority level is 15. A priority level of 0 has a special significance, it means that the master is disabled and stops participating in the arbitration scheme. Note that the cahb arbiter will prevent a master from disabling itself. |

## 10.32 WCSS_A_CAL_CAL

### WCSS_A_CAL_CALMODE (0x0A008000)

**Type:** RW

**Reset State:** 0x00000000

Determines the calibration mode and generates calibration enables during these modes The Enable_Measure bit in the MSB of the register is used to enable the measurement of the value. For instance, in DC offset initial calibration mode, the CPU writes to the DC offset DAC n the RF ASIC through the SPI interface. The CPU then has to command the DC offset calibration module in the PHY to measure the DC offset (at the ADC output) after the new DAC output (in the RF ASIC) can be observed at the ADC output (typically after 0.5 us after the DAC is written to in the RF ASIC). Hence, once the CPU writes to the SPI interface, it then waits for a specific period of time (1 us) after the SPI write completes, and then asserts this bit to command the DC offset module to start the measurement. Once the measurement is done (as indicated by the CAL_STATUS) register, this bit has to be disabled so as to setup for the next measurement.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 2:0 | MODE | Sets the calibration mode value 3'b101 to 3'b111 are unused<br>0x0: NORMAL (Normal Mode, No calibration being done)<br>0x1: INITDCCAL (DC Offset Initial Calibration Mode (In this mode we correct for the DC offset in all of the receive chains (3x2) by writing to the DC offset correction DAC in the respective RF Ics. This offset measurement is done serially (one receive chain at a time).)<br>0x2: RESDCCAL (Digital/Residual DC Offset Calibration Mode. In this mode we measure the DC offset (to account for any drift in DC offset due to temperature and/or gain settings) and correct for it digitally at the output of the ADCs for all the receive chains (3x2). This of fset measurement is done in parallel.)<br>0x3: IQCAL (I/Q Amplitude Phase Imbalance Calibration Mode. In this mode we measure the amplitude and phase imbalance between the I and Q for each receive chain)<br>0x4: TXLOCAL (TX LO Leakage Measurement mode. In this mode we measure the transmit chain local oscillator leakage by connecting the transmit path to the receive path and measuring the DC offset introduced by the transmit path at the output of the ADCs in the receive chain. T he transmit DACs are then adjusted to minimize this measured DC offset) |

### WCSS_A_CAL_MEASURE (0x0A008004)

**Type:** W

**Reset State:** 0x0000
<!-- page 1946 -->
### WCSS_A_CAL_MEASURE (continued)

By writing to this register, in calibration modes other than normal mode, a measure pulse is pulsed to the calibration module. Originally, this was a level signal called Enable_Measure. With the wr_Pulse register type being supported, it was decided to add this, so that software does not have to disable and then enable for the cal module to detect a pulse

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |

### WCSS_A_CAL_CHAIN_SEL (0x0A008008)

**Type:** RW

**Reset State:** 0x00000000

Determines which transmit/receive channel is being calibrated. If Bit 2 is 0, then the I channel of the transmit/receive chain is selected. If Bit 2 is 1, then the Q chain of the transmit/receive chain is selected. CS1 and CS0 determine which of the receive chains 0,1,2 or the transmit chains 0,1 are being calibrated as shown in table below.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 2 | IQSEL | Selects I/Q inputs for the inputs specified in chain<br>0x0: ISEL (I input Select)<br>0x1: QSEL (Q input Select) |
| 1:0 | CHAIN | Selects receive chain output<br>0x0: CHAIN0 (Chain 0 Select)<br>0x1: CHAIN1 (Chain 1 Select)<br>0x2: CHAIN2 (Chain 2 Select)<br>0x3: CHAIN3 (Chain 3 Select) |

### WCSS_A_CAL_DCO_THRESHOLD (0x0A00801C)

**Type:** RW

**Reset State:** 0x004C

Threshold value for the digital DC offset measured on a per-packet basis. If the measured digital DC offset is more than this threshold, the DC offset module sets the CAL_ATTENTION register to request CPU to recalibrate. Default is 150 mV (= 76 LSBs of a 10-bit ADC with a -1V to +1V swing) =0x4C

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 10:0 | VALUE | |

### WCSS_A_CAL_DCTIMER1 (0x0A008020)

**Type:** RW

**Reset State:** 0x2C24

When the DC offset module is commanded to measure the digital DC offset either by the CPU or the AGC module (the AGC module does so on every packet), the DC offset module terminates all the RFICs inputs and waits for the time (number for 80MHz clocks) specified in the CAL_DC_TIMER1 register. This allows for the terminated input to be observed at the ADC outputs. This time is typically in the order if 0.5 us = 20 40MHz clocks = = 40 80 MHz clocks = 0x28 - 1 POR. Note that this number should always be an odd number (to be a multiple of 40 MHz clocks)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 15:8 | VALUE_RSB | |
| 7:0 | VALUE_RSA | |
<!-- page 1949 -->
### WCSS_A_CAL_DCTIMER2 (0x0A008024)

**Type:** RW

**Reset State:** 0x2000

When the DC offset module is commanded to measure the digital DC offset either by the CPU or the AGC module (the AGC module does so on every packet), the DC offset module terminates all the RFICs inputs and waits for the time (number for 80MHz clocks) specified in the CAL_DC_TIMER1 register. This allows for the terminated input to be observed at the ADC outputs. This time is typically in the order if 0.5 us = 20 40MHz = 40 80 MHz clocks = 0x28-1. Now when the DC offset measurement is done, the DC offset module switches the RF frontend back in. After switching the RF FE in, the DC offset module waits for CAL_DC_TIMER2 time before it can assert a data valid signal to the rest of the blocks. The reason there are two different timer registers for turning on and turning off the RF FE is so as to support any asymmetry in turning on/turning off the RF FE. If this saves clocks, then it allows data to be sampled earlier which may be particularly useful in per-packet calibration. Presently, the default value is 0.5us.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 15:8 | VALUE_RSB | |
| 7:0 | VALUE_RSA | |

### WCSS_A_CAL_DCOFFSET (0x0A008028)

**Type:** W

Usually the last measured DC offset is held for the next packet as well until a new dco measurement is commanded by the AGC. Since, DC offset can change with time, when the AGC comes out of reset (like after beacon power save modes), software may decide to clear the DC offset register.

| :--- | :--- | :--- |

Non-listed encodings default to centre tap selection.<br>0x0: C0_IN_DATA_TAP (Through tap selects input data (no delay))<br>0x1: C0_IN_DATA_DLY1 (Through tap selects input data delayed by 1 cycle)<br>0x2: C0_IN_DATA_DLY2 (Through tap selects input data delayed by 2 cycles (centre tap))<br>0x3: C0_IN_DATA_DLY3 (Through tap selects input data delayed by 3 cycles)<br>0x4: C0_IN_DATA_DLY4 (Through tap selects input data (final tap)) |

### 0x0A206008 WCSS_A_CCU_CCU_MB0_CONTROL

**Type:** RW
**Reset State:** 0x00000000

General purpose Mailbox register, which can be used to generate interrupts to the ccpu or to the msm.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:2 | MAILBOX_VALUE | A 30 bit value from sender to receiver |
| 1 | INT_DIRECTION | Interrupt direction: When set to zero: cCPU to msm When set to one: msm to cCPU Hard Coded to Zero: ReadOnly |
| 0 | MB_RESET | When set, all to this MB related parameters, including the counters, are cleared. |

### 0x0A20600C WCSS_A_CCU_CCU_MB0_CONTROL_COUNTERS

**Type:** R
**Reset State:** 0x00000000

Access counters for tracking the usage and handling of the MB interrupt

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 18:16 | WRITE_CNT | A 3 bit value indicating the number of times a none reset write operation has been performed on the mb0_control register. This value gets cleared on a mb0 reset. |
| 2:0 | READ_CNT | A 3 bit value indicating the number of times a read operation has been performed on the control register of this mailbox This value gets cleared on a MB reset. |

### 0x0A2060B0 WCSS_A_CCU_CCU_MUTEX0

**Type:** RW
**Reset State:** 0x00000101

General purpose semaphore and/or mutex register

| Bits | Name | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31 | RESET | RW | When set, both Current Count and MaxCount fields get initialized with the value written to the MAXcount field. This bit will not get set on a write operation. |
| 15:8 | MAXCOUNT | RW | THe Max count of semaphoresavailable. Can only be set when the Reset bit is written with value 1. |
| 7:0 | CURRENTCOUNT | R | Current count of the semaphore. On a read, the current value of the Semaphore is returned and if the CurrentCount > 0, the CurrentCount value is decreased by one. On a write, the current value of the Semaphore is increased by one if the CurrentCount < MaxCount |

| 31 | RESET | RW | When set, both Current Count and MaxCount fields get initialized with the value written to the MAXcount field. This bit will not get set on a write operation. |
| 15:8 | MAXCOUNT | RW | THe Max count of semaphoresavailable. Can only be set when the Reset bit is written with value 1. |
| 7:0 | CURRENTCOUNT | R | Current count of the semaphore. On a read, the current value of the Semaphore is returned and if the CurrentCount > 0, the CurrentCount value is decreased by one. On a write, the current value of the Semaphore is increased by one if the CurrentCount < MaxCount |

## 10.35 WCSS_A_CDAHB_CDAHB

### WCSS_A_CDAHB_CDAHB_RRI_PL

* **Address:** `0x0A100000`
* **Type:** `RW`
* **Reset State:** `0x00000002`

**Description:** cdahb Arbiter arbitration priority level for rri master. In the cdahb arbitration scheme the master with highest priority level always wins. Should there be more than one master with the same priority then the winning master will be selected using a round-robin algorithm.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 3:0 | PRIORITY | Arbitration priority for rri master. The lowest priority level is 1 and the highest priority level is 15. A priority level of 0 has a special significance, it means that the master is disabled and stops participating in the arbitration scheme. Note that the cdahb arbiter will prevent a master from disabling itself. |

| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 3:0 | DFT_MST | Default Master ID number register. The default master is the master that is granted by the bus when no master has requested ownership. NOTE: Writing anything beyond the 4 R/W bits will cause the entire write to be discarded.<br/>0x0: DMY (Grant ownership to cdahb dummy master)<br/>0x1: RRI (Grant ownership to cdahb rri master)<br/>0x2: FDBR (Grant ownership to cdahb fdbr master)<br/>0x3: CCPU (Grant ownership to cdahb ccpu master)<br/>0x4: DBR (Grant ownership to cdahb dbr master)<br/>0x5: A2AB (Grant ownership to cdahb a2ab master)<br/>0x6: DXE (Grant ownership to cdahb dxe master) |

### WCSS_A_CFG_CFG_STALL_TIMEOUT

* **Address:** `0x0A141844`
* **Type:** `RW`
* **Reset State:** `0x00000A00`

**Description:** Stall timeout functionality - allows CFG to return to idle if PMI interface stalls.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 16 | STALL_TIMEOUT_EN | Enable stall timeout functionality on the MPI. |
| 11:0 | STALL_TIMEOUT_TIME | Number of cycles of no activity during PMI transaction before stall timeout occurs. |

### WCSS_A_CFG_CFG_CONFIG

* **Address:** `0x0A141848`
* **Type:** `RW`
* **Reset State:** `0x00150000`

**Description:** gives some configurations for CFG

| Bits | Name | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31 | CSIPROC_REGACCESS_FAIL | RW | when set indicates template is being updates internally hence read or write access failed this needs to be cleared by SW |
| 30 | CSIPROC_BUSY | R | when set indicates template is being updates internally |
| 29 | CSIPROC_TEMPLATE_READY | R | when set indicates template is ready |
| 28:24 | LOCAL_CLKGATE_DIS | RW | local clock gate disable for all clk gates in cfg bit0 - gas/config modules bit1 - async fifo bit2 - phy_rxif bit3 - csi_proc bit4 - memif |
| 23:16 | CFG_11AC_VHCB_CATEGORY | RW | VHTCB frame is a management Action frame which has category field which is not decided in IEEE spec hence it is made programmable Program VHTCB category field here |
<!-- page 2007 -->

### WCSS_A_CFG_CFG_CONFIG (continued)

| Bits | Name | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 12:11 | RESERVED | | reserved |
| 10:8 | RESERVED | | reserved |
| 3 | SW_TEMPLATE_READY | RW | This is done only for debug purpose. SW can first write to bit 2 in this register to ignore PHY transfers, then write the VHT-CB frame or CSI frame to memory when it is finished creating template, write 1'b1 to bit 3 indicating to TPE frame is ready for transfer |
| 2 | IGNORE_PHY_XFERS_EN | RW | when this bit is set any phy transfer is ignored and only SW will do the writes, this is for debug purpose. |
| 1 | SOFT_PMI_ABORT_EN | RW | Soft PMI abort enable. this is basically to create phy abort thro' sw in this case need to make sure stall timeout is enabled |
| 0 | CFG_CSI_EN | RW | Enables the CSI functionality, by default it is disabled |

* **Type:** `RW`
* **Reset State:** `0x00000004`

**Description:** dahb Arbiter arbitration priority level for dpuw master. In the dahb arbitration scheme the master with highest priority level always wins. Should there be more than one master with the same priority then the winning master will be selected using a round-robin algorithm.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 3:0 | PRIORITY | Arbitration priority for dpuw master. The lowest priority level is 1 and the highest priority level is 15. A priority level of 0 has a special significance, it means that the master is disabled and stops participating in the arbitration scheme. Note that the dahb arbiter will prevent a master from disabling itself. |

| 0 | WQ_ARB_MODE | RW | Setting this bit selects the arbitration scheme of the Work Queues (WQ). 0: Arbitration priority is ordered RX0->RX7 followed by TX0->TX7 i.e. RX WQ's have higher priority than TX WQ's 1: Arbitration priority is ordered RX0,TX0,RX1,TX1,RX2,TX2,etc i.e. RX WQ 0 has higher priority than TX WQ 0 which has higher priority than RX WQ 1 and so on. |

### 0x0A081820 WCSS_A_DPU_DPU_INTERRUPT_MASK

**Type:** RW
**Reset State:** 0x00000000

Enables/Disables the DPU interrupts

| Bits | Name | Description |

| 31 | EGR_WR_ERROR | Setting this bit enables the EGR State Machine Error interrupt. The interrupt occurs when the DPU egress state-machine enters the error state. Such errors are triggered by errors on the Write AHB bus, which should not happen. The DPU does not handle these errors and may result in a DPU lock up. 0: Disabled 1: Enabled |

WCSS_A_DPU_DPU_INTERRUPT_MASK (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 30 | EGR_GBI_ERROR | Setting this bit enables the EGR State Machine Error interrupt. The interrupt occurs when the DPU egress state-machine enters the error state. Such errors are triggered by errors on the Command AHB bus, which should not happen. The DPU does not handle these errors and may result in a DPU lock up. 0: Disabled 1: Enabled |
| 29 | IGR_ERROR | Setting this bit enables the IGR State Machine Error interrupt. The interrupt occurs when the DPU ingress state-machine enters the error state. Such errors are triggered by errors on the Read AHB bus, which should not happen. The DPU does not handle these errors and may result in a DPU lock up. 0: Disabled 1: Enabled |
| 28 | PDUBD_STALL | Setting this bit enables the PDU/BD Stalled interrupt. The interrupt occurs when the DPU requires BD/PDU's but none areavailable. 0: Disabled 1: Enabled |
| 27 | WATCHDOG_TIMER | Setting this bit enables the Watchdog Timer interrupt. The interrupt occurs when the Watchdog timer reaches is programmable threshold. 0: Disabled 1: Enabled |
| 24 | DPU_WAKEUPHOST_EN | Setting this bit enables the wake-up host interrupt In WoWL mode whenever it detects magic packet the interrupt bit is set 0: Disabled 1: Enabled |
| 23 | MIC_ERR_EN | Setting this bit enables the MIC error interrupt. The interrupt occurs when a TKIP MIC is detected as errored. 0: Disabled 1: Enabled |
| 20:0 | PKT_ERR_EN | The state of each bit enables/disables an interrupt for the corresponding Packet Error Code. The interrupt occurs when a packet Error is detected. 0: Disabled (per-bit) 1: Enabled (per-bit) |

### 0x0A081848 WCSS_A_DPU_DPU_WATCHDOG

**Type:** RW
**Reset State:** 0xFFFF0000

This value represents the DPU watch dog timer and controls. The watchdog self resets to 0 when the DPU is idle and increments by 1 at 128 micro-second intervals when the DPU is not idle.
NOTE: The Watchdog does not stop/change the operation of the DPU.

| Bits | Name | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:16 | WATCHDOG_THRES | RW | This is the value that if reached the DPU will issue a timeout interrupt. Writing to this register resets the watchdog timer |
| 15:0 | WATCHDOG_VALUE | R | This is the current value of the DPU watchdog timer. |

**Reset State:** 0x00000110

If the reservation fails the TX/RX 3 to 10 WQ's are disabled from selection until there enough BD/PDU's to satisfy the reservation request. The BD/PDU reservation values must be less than TX/RX 4 WQ reservation values.

### 0x0A081874 WCSS_A_DPU_DPU_ERROR_WQ

* **Type**: RW
* **Reset State**: 0x0000FF08

This register is used to define two Work Queues to which error packets can be routed. By default, both of these error work queues are set to 0xFF, which is intended to be a 'junk' work queue where data is discarded.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 15:8 | ERR_WQ_B | This indicates the work queue number for work queue B. |
| 7:0 | ERR_WQ_A | This indicates the work queue number for work queue A. |

### 0x0A081878 WCSS_A_DPU_DPU_ERROR_WQ_SELECT

* **Type**: RW
* **Reset State**: 0x00000000

This register is used to select the work queue routing for error packet with particular error codes. Each error code is represented by a single bit in this register; for example bit 3 is used for selecting routing of packets with error code 3. A set bit will direct error packets with that error code to work queue B. A cleared bit will direct error packets with that error code to work queue A. By default all errors are routed to error work queue A.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 18:1 | ERR_WQ_SELECT | If bit n is set in this field then error packets with error code n are sent to error work queue B; if the bit is clear then they are sent to work queue A. All bit numbers other than valid error codes are reserved and should be left zero. |

## 10.39 WCSS_A_FDAHB_FDAHB

### 0x0A140000 WCSS_A_FDAHB_FDAHB_RXP_PL

**Type:** RW

**Reset State:** 0x00000004

fdahb Arbiter arbitration priority level for rxp master. In the fdahb arbitration scheme the master with highest priority level always wins. Should there be more than one master with the same priority then the winning master will be selected using a round-robin algorithm.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 3:0 | PRIORITY | Arbitration priority for rxp master. The lowest priority level is 1 and the highest priority level is 15. A priority level of 0 has a special significance, it means that the master is disabled and stops participating in the arbitration scheme. Note that the fdahb arbiter will prevent a master from disabling itself. |

Note that the fdahb arbiter will prevent a master from disabling itself. |

### 0x0A140048 WCSS_A_FDAHB_FDAHB_DFLT_MST

**Type:** RW

**Reset State:** 0x00000000

This register identifies the default master for the fdahb

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 3:0 | DFT_MST | Default Master ID number register. The default master is the master that is granted by the bus when no master has requested ownership. NOTE: Writing anything beyond the 4 R/W bits will cause the entire write to be discarded.<br>0x0: DMY (Grant ownership to fdahb dummy master)<br>0x1: RXP (Grant ownership to fdahb rxp master)<br>0x2: TXP (Grant ownership to fdahb txp master)<br>0x3: TPE (Grant ownership to fdahb tpe master)<br>0x4: FDBR (Grant ownership to fdahb fdbr master)<br>0x5: RPE (Grant ownership to fdahb rpe master) |

## 10.41 WCSS_A_MCU_MCU

### 0x0A080C00 WCSS_A_MCU_BD_PDU_BASE_ADDR

**Type:** RW

**Reset State:** 0x00000000

Sets the memory base address of the BDs and PDUs in external memory.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:7 | BD_PDU_BASE_ADDRESS | Base address of the BDs and PDUs in external memory. Note that the lowest 8 bits can not be programmed as these bits will always have to be zero. BDs and PDUs are in units of 128 bytes. |

### 0x0A080C04 WCSS_A_MCU_MLC_CONTROL

**Type:** RW

**Reset State:** 0x00330000

MAC Loop back Control register
<!-- page 2039 -->

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31 | MLC_LOOPBACK_ENABLE | When set to 1'b1, the MLC loopback functionality is enabled |
| 30 | MLC_SNOOPING_ENABLE | When set to 1'b1, the MLC snooping functionality is enabled |
| 29 | MLC_ADDRESS_SWAP_ENABLE | When set to 1'b1, the MLC will swap address 1 and address2 of the frame received from the TXP |
| 23:16 | BYTE_FORWARDING_INTERVAL | The number of 160MHz clock cycles in between each data byte requested from the TXP and forwarded to the RXP. A value of 8'd3 corresponds with 315 Mbps. A value of 8'd7 corresponds with 100 mbps. This setting is only used in MLC loopback functionality mode, not snooping mode. bits [17:16] are read only and are always tied to 2'b11 since this is the minimum value that you can program. It is tied to this value preventing user from programming it anything other |

### 0x0A080C0C WCSS_A_MCU_DBR_STATUS

**Type:** RW

**Reset State:** 0x00000000

Status register of the DBR

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 5 | DBR_GAM_ERROR | When set to 1'b1, the gam inside the DBR reported an error to overcome some rtl issue, please write to this bit to clear DBR_incorrect_length_error |
| 4 | DBR_INCORRECT_LENGTH_ERROR | When set to 1'b1, the DBR reported an error: a module tried an access that was larger then 1 word to overcome some rtl issue, please write to this bit to clear DBR_GAM_error |

### WCSS_A_MCU_MUTEX0 (cont.)

| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 7:0 | CURRENTCOUNT | Current count of the semaphore. On a read, the current value of the Semaphore is returned and if the CurrentCount > 0, the CurrentCount value is decreased by one. On a write, the current value of the Semaphore is increased by one if the CurrentCount < MaxCount |

### 0x0A080CD8 WCSS_A_MCU_MAC_MODULES_GOTO_IDLE_CONTROL

**Type:** RW  
**Reset State:** 0x00000000  

The statemachines in the MAC modules can be forced to go back to idle by setting these signals. This resembles somewhat the softreset functionality, accept that the configuration registers maintain their settings. It is therefor less intrusive then a soft reset, and might achieve restoring the modules into a known state

| :--- | :--- | :--- |

| 10 | TPE_GOTO_IDLE | When set, the TPE HW state machines will return to idle |
| 9 | RPE_GOTO_IDLE | When set, the RPE HW state machines will return to idle |
| 8 | PHY_AHB_2_APB_GOTO_IDLE | When set, the PHY AHB to APB interface HW state machines will return to idle |
| 7 | DPU_GOTO_IDLE | When set, the DPU HW state machines will return to idle |
| 6 | BMU_GOTO_IDLE | When set, the BMU HW state machines will return to idle |
| 5 | MTU_GOTO_IDLE | When set, the MTU (MAC Timing Unit) HW state machines will return to idle |
| 4 (inferred) | RXP_GOTO_IDLE | When set, the RXP HW state machines will return to idle |
| 2 | DBR_GOTO_IDLE | Reserved |
| 0 | MLC_GOTO_IDLE | When set, the MLC (MAC Loopback Controller) HW state machines will return to idle |

| 3 | TSF_TIMER3_INT_SELECT | When set, in all interrupt related registers indicating mtu timer3/tsf_timer3 interrupt, the interrupt source is set to TSF. When NOT set, the interrupt source is set to mtu timer 3 |
| 2 | TSF_TIMER2_INT_SELECT | When set, in all interrupt related registers indicating mtu timer2/tsf_timer2 interrupt, the interrupt source is set to TSF. When NOT set, the interrupt source is set to mtu timer 2 |
| 1 | TSF_TIMER1_INT_SELECT | When set, in all interrupt related registers indicating mtu timer1/tsf_timer1 interrupt, the interrupt source is set to TSF. When NOT set, the interrupt source is set to mtu timer 1 |
| 0 | TSF_TIMER0_INT_SELECT | When set, in all interrupt related registers indicating mtu timer0/tsf_timer0 interrupt, the interrupt source is set to TSF. When NOT set, the interrupt source is set to mtu timer 0 |

**Type:** RW
**Reset State:** `0x1C1C2525`

AIFS limit register for 0 to 3 back off engines. The value is in micro seconds Though the name is DIFS, it is used for bothe DIFS,AIFS. It is up to s/w to select the value.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:24 | SW_MTU_DIFS_LIMIT_3 | AIFS value in micro seconds for the back-off engine 3 |
| 23:16 | SW_MTU_DIFS_LIMIT_2 | AIFS value in micro seconds for the back-off engine 2 |
| 15:8 | SW_MTU_DIFS_LIMIT_1 | AIFS value in micro seconds for the back-off engine 1 |
| 7:0 | SW_MTU_DIFS_LIMIT_0 | AIFS value in micro seconds for the back-off engine 0 |

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:24 | SW_MTU_DIFS_LIMIT_7 | AIFS value in micro seconds for the back-off engine 7 |
| 23:16 | SW_MTU_DIFS_LIMIT_6 | AIFS value in micro seconds for the back-off engine 6 |
| 15:8 | SW_MTU_DIFS_LIMIT_5 | AIFS value in micro seconds for the back-off engine 5 |

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |

| 15:8 | SW_PIFS_LIMIT | PIFS value in micro seconds |
| 7:0 | SW_MTU_SLOT_LIMIT | slot limit value in micro seconds for all the back-off engines |

### WCSS_A_MTU_SW_MTU_BCN_SLOT_USEC_SIFS_LIMIT

**Address:** `0x0A08140C`
**Type:** RW
**Reset State:** `0x20007714`

This register contains the limits for beacon slot usec pulse generation sifs.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:24 | SW_MTU_EARLY_PKT_DET_MISS_LIMIT | sw_mtu_early_pkt_det_miss_limit-- this is used in respons_to(ack_to) logic if the system is expecting a response and if the early pkt_det is HIGH for this limit, an interrupt is generated (old name is cca_miss_limit) |
| 15:8 | SW_MTU_ONE_USEC_LIMIT | limit value to be programmed to get one usec pulse. Basically this is number of clk cycles. this value is loaded into a counter and keep getting decremented at every clk. |
| 7:0 | SW_MTU_BCN_SLOT_LIMIT | slot limit value in micro seconds for all the back-off engines |

### WCSS_A_MTU_SW_MTU_MISC_LIMITS

**Address:** `0x0A081410`
**Type:** RW
**Reset State:** `0x0C20091E`

This register contains the limits for one usec puls and for programmable pulse generation the programmable pulse is sued by the timers in one of the modes and the sw delay limits.
<!-- page 2119 -->

### WCSS_A_MTU_SW_MTU_MISC_LIMITS (continued)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:24 | SW_MTU_PUSH_MISS_LIMIT | Limit to control the missing_push interrupt. If pkt_det goes high and we don't get a packet from the rxp before this limit, the interrupt will go. |
| 21:16 | SW_MTU_TXP_DELAY_LIMIT | TXP is indicated earlier indication of transmission of a pkt. The number in this register indicates the delay between the indication to s/w and the corresponding flag set that goes to txp The actual delay is the number programmed mulltiplied by the sw_mtu_txp_delay_pulse_limit multiplied by 8ns. |
| 11:8 | SW_MTU_TXP_DELAY_PULSE_LIMIT | This number dictates the resolution of the delay between the s/w interrupt and the corresponding txp flag. |
| 7:0 | TIMER_RESOLUTION_LIMIT | A pulse is generated at the end of "this limit" number of 120mhz pulses. This pulse represents the resolution in timers. |

### 0x0A081440 WCSS_A_MTU_TIMER_CONTROL

- **Type**: RW
- **Reset State**: 0x00000000

This register contains all the controls for the timers.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:16 | SW_MTU_BASIC_UNIT_SELECT | 2 bit for each timer is provided. bit [1:0] for timer 0, bit [3:2] for timer 1... To make these timers more flexible, 3 basic units are provided. if the control =0, the timer will be stopped (this is the only way to disable the counters if the control =01, timer is ++ at every clk if the control =10, timer is ++ at every one us if the control =11, timer is ++ at every programmable pulse. Basically in this mode, the period of the pulse is also controlled by s/w. Note that this programmable pulse is only one for all the timers |
| 11:0 | SW_MTU_TIMER_UP_DOWN_CNTRL | 1 bit for each timer is provided. bit 0 for timer 0, bit 1 for timer 1... This controls the up/down functionality of the timers. 1-> up, 0->down. |

### 0x0A081464 WCSS_A_MTU_BKOF_CONTROL

- **Type**: RW
- **Reset State**: 0xFF000000

This register contains all the controls for the back-off engines.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:24 | SW_MTU_SUPPRESS_COLLISION_INT | 1 bit for each back off is provided. bit 0 for back 0, bit 1 for back 1... If this bit is set to 1, the back off will not send interrupt to s/w for collision case (int status = 2'b11) warm up also will not be generated. |
| 23:16 | SW_MTU_QUEUE_DATA_AVAIL | 1 bit for each back is provided. bit 0 for back 0, bit 1 for back 1... data avail bits from the s/w. Unless this bit is set, s/w won't get interrupt (irrespective of the status of back-off. |
| 15:8 | SW_MTU_STALL_BKOF | 1 bit for each back is provided. bit 0 for back 0, bit 1 for back 1... if this bit is set, the corresponding back-off will be stalled. Basically the back-off counter -- will be stopped. This is used to stall all the back-offs while beacon is supposed to be sent or for any other reasons. |
| 7:0 | SW_MTU_USE_SW_BKOF_COUNTER | 1 bit for each back is provided. bit 0 for back 0, bit 1 for back 1... if this bit is set, the back_off counter is set by sw. Otherwise, HW will use the cw_reg & lfsdr. |

This register contains the cw_reg value that needs to be used by hw. For backoff engine_0 This register also has the control bit that initiates the back-off after the hw issued an interrupt to s/w for its attention.

| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 19 | SW_MTU_CW_UPDATE_VALID | this is write only register. The `sw_mtu_cw_reg` will be updated only when this bit is set. Otherwise the hw update will take place. |

| 16 | SW_MTU_WAIT_DONE_P_0 | This bit is write only. The HW will be waiting for this signal to start the next back-off after issuing the interrupt by the back-off engine. |

### WCSS_A_MTU_MTU_INTERRUPT_STATUS

**Address:** `0x0A081488`
**Type:** RW
**Reset State:** `0x00000000`

This register contains the status of all the interrupts that are generated by MTU. Basically, every interrupt has a corresponding register bit which will be set on sending the interrupt pulse to the interrupt module and this bit is reset by writing '1' to it. S/W has higher priority over HW.
<!-- page 2132 -->

### WCSS_A_MTU_MTU_INTERRUPT_STATUS (continued)

| Bits | Name | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31 | SECONDARY_CCA_TO | R | The secondary_cca_to is sampled and S/W can read its status through this register. |
| 30 | SIFS_TO | R | The sifs_to is sampled and S/W can read its status through this register. |
| 29 | PIFS_TO | R | The pifs_to is sampled and S/W can read its status through this register. |
| 28 | MTU_MCU_WATCH_DOG_ENABLE_DISABL_ERROR | RW | If S/W tries to write wrong combinations to the watchdog enable/disable bits, this interrupt will be generated. |
| 27 | MTU_MCU_WATCH_DOG_PROTECTION_ERROR | RW | If S/W tries to write to the watchdog register and if the protection vector matches, this interrupt will be generated. |
| 26:24 | MTU_MCU_WATCH_DOG_TIMER_FLAG | RW | Watchdog interrupt flags. Bit 24 is for thr0, bit 25 is for thr1, bit 26 is for thr3. |
| 23:16 | MTU_MCU_TSF_INT_FLAG | RW | 8 registers for 8 TSF-based match register interrupts. Bit 0 for match 0, 1 for match 1, ... |
| 15:8 | MTU_MCU_BKOF_INT_FLAG | RW | 8 registers for 8 back-off interrupts. Bit 0 for timer 0, 1 for timer 1, ... |
| 7:0 | MTU_MCU_TIMER_INT_FLAG | RW | 8 registers for 8 timer interrupts. Bit 0 for timer 0, 1 for timer 1, ... |

### WCSS_A_MTU_SW_MATCH_REGISTER_0

**Address:** `0x0A08148C`
**Type:** RW
**Reset State:** `0x00000EFF`

This register contains the match value for TSF-based interrupts. Basically, whenever the TSF is equal to this register, the corresponding interrupt will be generated. This register is also used by timer 0 in up mode. Basically, when the timer is operated in up mode, when the Timer 0 reaches this value, an interrupt is generated.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:30 | SW_TSF_SEL_0 | Lower bits to select the TSF that will trigger the interrupt when the timer value reaches: <br> `3'b000` (implied `3'b00`): BSS TSF; <br> `3'b011` (implied `3'b01`): IBSS TSF; <br> `3'b010` (implied `3'b10`): P2P group owner TSF; <br> `3'b011` (implied `3'b11`): P2P client TSF; <br> `3'b100`: BSS2 TSF. |
| 29 | SW_TSF_SEL_0_HI | Upper bit to select the TSF that will trigger the interrupt when the timer value reaches. |
| 23:0 | SW_MATCH_REGISTER_0 | This register contains the match value for TSF-based counter interrupt 0, timer 0 (in up mode). |
<!-- page 2133 -->

### 0x0A0814D8 WCSS_A_MTU_WATCH_DOG_TIMER

* **Type:** RW
* **Reset State:** 0x00000000

This is watch dog timer register. Basically, when the watch dog timer is enabled, this timer keeps ++ at every us. Once it reaches watch dog thr0, an interrupt is generated when it reaches thr1 another interrupt is generated (higher priority). On reaching thr3, another higher priority interrupt is generated. Typically this is used to reset the chip.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:30 | WATCH_DOG_TIMER_ENABLE_DISABLE | Watch dog timer and the corresponding interrupts are enabled only when these bits are 10. 01 is disable. Any other combination will not be accepted and if sw writes 00 or 11, the status is maintained. We may have an interrupt to this condition as well as for any writes to the watch dog register without protection vector match |
| 29:24 | WATCH_DOG_TIMER_PROTECTION_VECTOR | This is write only register. when it is read ZEROs are returned. Writes to the watch dog register can happen (including the enable/disable) only when this field matches the watch_dog_thr0[25:24],thr1[25:24],thr2[25:24] |
| 23:0 | WATCH_DOG_TIMER | if it is enabled, it keeps ++ at every us. S/W can write to it only when the protection vector matches the concat of the 2 bit protection bits from the watch dog threshold register. The protection vector can't be 00 or 3f |

### 0x0A0814E8 WCSS_A_MTU_BKOF_SW_INT_TYPE

* **Type:** RW
* **Reset State:** 0x00000000

this register contains the status of the interrupt type for the back off engines
<!-- page 2143 -->
#### WCSS_A_MTU_BKOF_SW_INT_TYPE (continued)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 15:0 | BKOF_SW_INT_TYPE | contains the type of the interrupt rom the back off engines. 1:0 is bkoff 0, 3:2 for bkoff 1 and so on. Value 2'b00: No interrupt pending, or cleared by SW Value 2'b01: Backoff engine expired successfully (no collision with a higher priority backoff engine) Value 2'b10: There was in internal collision between this and a higher priority backoff engine. SW needs to re-initialize the backoff engine. Value 2'b11: Dataavailable got programmed after the backoff engine had already run and reached the BKOFF_DONE state. At the moment of programming Dataavailable, the CCA was low. SW needs to re-program the backoff engine. This is read only register. But any write 1 to this register will clear the status for the corresponding back-off. For ex. write of a 1 to bit 0 will clear 1:0, write of a 1 to bit 1 clears the 3:2 and so on. Only 11:0 are enabled for write operation, but will also automatically clear on a write. Corresponds to reset_bkof_sw_int_type_p in RTL |

So a programmability is provided for this also. if bit[30] = 0, 00 selects primary cca, 01 selects secondary cca, 10 selects combined cca (basically and of both primary and secondary) 11 select the sw_mtu_cca_flag which is sw config register bit. if bit[30] = 1, 00 selects tertiary cca, 01 selects quaternary cca, 10 selects all cca (basically and of primary, secondary, tertiary and quaternary) Final cca selection is done based on the next 3 bits-- sw_mtu_pifs_final_cca_sel |

| 19:8 | SW_MTU_CONTINUOUS_VALID | One bit for timer. if this bit is set, the timer will be loaded either with zero or the corresponding match register(depending on up/down). Basically if this bit is set the timer works as divided by N |
<!-- page 2150 -->
#### WCSS_A_MTU_TIMER_CONTROL11TO8 (continued)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 7:0 | SW_MTU_BASIC_UNIT_SELECT11TO8 | 2 bits for each timer is provided. bit [1:0] for timer 8 (manual says 0), bit [3:2] for timer 9 (manual says 1), bit [5:4] for timer 10, bit [7:6] for timer 11. To make these timers more flexible, 3 basic units are provided. if the control = 00, the timer will be stopped (this is the only way to disable the counters). If the control = 01, timer is ++ at every clk. If the control = 10, timer is ++ at every one us. If the control = 11, timer is ++ at every programmable pulse. Basically in this mode, the period of the pulse is also controlled by s/w. Note that this programmable pulse is only one for all the timers |

### WCSS_A_MTU_MTU_GLOBAL_CONTROL2

**Address:** `0x0A081558`  
**Type:** `RW`  
**Reset State:** `0x000000EE`  

Contains the global controls for mtu

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 15:12 | SW_MTU_RTS_NAV_TO_LIMIT_U | The upper bits of sw_mtu_rts_nav_to_limit |
| 11 | SW_MTU_IGNORE_NAV_FOR_EIFS_FCS | Set to 1 to ignore the nav_greater-than-64 check. Whenever rxp indicates that fcs error, the eifs selection will be set regardless of the nav count. |
| 10 | SW_MTU_CONSIDER_SKIP_DIFS | If this bit is set, the skip_difs from the rxp is used.. to take care of any bug in other module. Since this is not a main line function, better to have a protection |
| 9 | SW_MTU_SELECT_LATE_PKT_DET_FOR_ACK_TO | If this bit is set, the late pkt_det is used for ack_to. By default the early_pkt-det should be used. This bit should never be set in the system. The configuration is provided for unknown flexibility.. Should be removed in the next spin atleast |
| 8 | SW_MTU_NAV_BASED_ON_RTS_VALID | The shadow_nav_cnt logic is enabled only when this bit is set. The nav update for RTS is done irrespective of this bit but the rts_nav_to logic is not enabled if this bit is set |
| 7:0 | SW_MTU_RTS_NAV_TO_LIMIT | This register represents the timeout count in the following On receiving an RTS based NAV, a shadow NAV counter will keep running the previous NAV setting. The RTS NAV will be used to set the NAV. A (Programmable) timeout counter is started. If no pkdet_n is detected before the timeout count expires, the shadow NAV will be used again to set the NAV. If a pktdet_n is seen before the timeout expires, the RTS based NAV will continue. The 'shadow' NAV can now be discarded. The default is a randomly chosen.Any suggested value is welcome |

The sw_mtu_early_sw_int_limit_clks is used to provide a resolution of one clk. Since the one_usec counter is a down counter the programming should be in terms of delay. ## 10.44 WCSS_A_PHYINT_PHYINT

### 0x0A015C00 WCSS_A_PHYINT_STATUS

**Type:** RW
**Reset State:** 0x0000

This register consolidates all the interrupt requests on Phy. All interrupt requests are active high. Interrupt bitfields ending in "_P" can be cleared by writing a "1" to the corresponding bit in this register. Interrupt bitfields not ending in "_P" must be cleared at source.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 14 | AGC_WATCHDOG_EXP | AGC FSM watchdog timer expired |
| 13 | PHYDBG_CAPTURE_DONE_P | Pronto2: When Phydbg completes a capture, it sets this interrupt. Useful for RTT3 channel-capture indication. Was: Txa header processor found a bad rate field from mpi data *** This interrupt does not exist in Gen5/6 *** |
| 12 | PMI_ALARM_P | The alarm condition in PMI |
| 11 | RACTL_ALARM_P | The alarm condition in RACTL |
| 10 | RBHPC_SOFEOFATN_P | The sof/eof interrupt from the RXB |
| 9 | TXCTL_ALARM_P | The interrupt from overall Tx Controller indicating error condition inside Phy TX |
| 8 | TACTL_ALARM_P | The interrupt from TACTL indicating error condition inside Phy Txa |
| 7 | MPI_MAXREQATN_P | The interrupt from MAC-Phy Interface (MPI) block indicating too many requests from txa or txb controller engines The threshold is configurable in mpi.reg |
<!-- page 2177 -->

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 6 | MPI_WATCHDOG_P | The interrupt from MAC-Phy Interface (MPI) block indicating expiry of watchdog timer |
| 5 | MPI_TXPABORT_P | The interrupt from MAC-Phy Interface (MPI) block indicating Txp abort |
| 4 | TPC_ATN_P | The interrupt from Transmit Power Control (TPC) block signifying error in tpc loop convergence. |
| 3 | CAL_ATN_P | The interrupt from the Calibration (CAL) block signifying calibration failure. |
| 2 | AGC_RADARDET_P | Set whenever the AGC detects radar. *** This interrupt does not exist in Libra *** |
| 1 | AGC_CLRCHAN_P | Set whenever the channel is clear, i.e. CCA is high. |
| 0 | RFIF_CALIB_DONE_P | Interrupt from Iris on calibration completion. ** NOTE ** this bit is used for agc_pktdet_n interrupt in Virgo ** ** NOTE ** this bit was used for indicating vswr overload in Libra and Volans ** |

### 0x0A080FC0 WCSS_A_QTA_INTR

**Type:** RW

#### WCSS_A_QTA_INTR (continued)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 26 | RX_FIFO_UFLOW_INTR | Receive FIFO Underflow interrupt status bit. Software must write a 1 to this bit to clear it. |
| 25 | RX_FIFO_OFLOW_INTR | Receive FIFO Overflow interrupt status bit. Software must write a 1 to this bit to clear it. |
| 24 | RX_FIFO_RDY_INTR | Receive FIFO Ready interrupt status bit: Indicates when the Receive FIFO is ready to be drained of software characters. This interrupt is set every clock cycle while the FIFO fill level is greater than the Receive FIFO Trigger Level (rx_trig_level). Software must write a 1 to this bit to clear it. |
| 17 | TX_FIFO_OFLOW_INTR | Transmit FIFO Overflow interrupt status bit. Software must write a 1 to this bit to clear it. |
| 16 | TX_FIFO_RDY_INTR | Transmit FIFO Ready interrupt status bit: Indicates when the Transmit FIFO is ready to accept more software characters for transmission. This interrupt is set every clock cycle while the FIFO fill level is less than or equal to the Transmit FIFO Trigger Level (tx_trig_level). Software must write a 1 to this bit to clear it. |
| 8 | RX_HW_CHAR_INTR | Received Hardware Character interrupt status bit. Software must write a 1 to this bit to clear it. |
| 1 | PARITY_ERR_INTR | UART Parity Error interrupt status bit. Software must write a 1 to this bit to clear it. |
| 0 | FRAME_ERR_INTR | UART Frame Error interrupt status bit. Software must write a 1 to this bit to clear it. |

### 0x0A080FC8 WCSS_A_QTA_UART_CTRL

**Type:** RW
**Reset State:** 0x03280060

UART control register.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:24 | BAUD_RATE_NUMERATOR | Sets the numerator for the ratio of the system clock frequency to the baud rate. |
| 23:16 | BAUD_RATE_DENOMINATOR | Sets the denominator for the ratio of the system clock frequency to the baud rate. |
| 6 | TX_INV_EN | When set, enables the UART's serial TX output inverter. |
| 5 | RX_INV_EN | When set, enables the UART's serial RX input inverter. |
| 4 | POWER_DOWN | When set, puts the UART into power-down mode. The UART transmitter will complete its current transmission and then disable all further transmissions. The UART receiver will discard the current character being received and then ignore all further receptions. |
| 3 | PARITY_EN | Enables parity bit generation in the UART transmitter, and parity checking in the UART receiver. |
| 2 | PARITY_ODD | When parity is enabled, this bit specifies whether the parity is odd or even. When 1, the parity is odd; when 0, it is even. |
| 1:0 | NUM_STOPS | Specifies the number of stop bits (1-4) at the end of each character. The number of stop bits per character = num_stops + 1. |

### 0x0A080FCC WCSS_A_QTA_HW_CTRL

**Type:** RW
**Reset State:** 0x00000014

Hardware layer control register.
<!-- page 2190 -->

#### WCSS_A_QTA_HW_CTRL (continued)

| Bits | Name | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:24 | LAST_RX_HW_CHAR | R | This field captures the last received hardware character that was passed on to the Signaling layer. |
| 15 | TX_BUFFER_STATE | R | State of the 1-character-deep Hardware TX Buffer. When 1, the buffer is full; when 0, the buffer is empty. |
| 14:8 | TX_BUFFER_CONTENTS | R | This field captures the hardware character presently stored in the TX Buffer. Resend bit excluded as only non-Resend-Requests are stored in this buffer. |
| 7 | RESEND_REQ_FLAG | R | Indicates the present state of the Resend Request flag. When set, it indicates that a Resend Request is pending transmission. |
| 4 | EXCLUSIVE_RESEND_EN | RW | Exclusive Resend Enable: When set, the QTA module will treat Signal State bits within Resend Request characters as invalid. When clear, the Signal State bits are valid regardless of whether the character is a Resend Request. |
| 3 | RESEND_REQ_PASSTHRU_EN | RW | Resend Request Pass-Through Enable: When set, the QTA module will pass received Resend Request characters through to the Signaling layer for processing. NB: This feature is unsupported for the WLAN version of the QTA module, because the Signaling interface for the WLAN version does not support Resend signaling. |
| 2 | RESEND_RESP_EN | RW | Resend Response Enable: When this bit is set, the QTA module will automatically respond to received Resend Requests by resending its last (non-Resend-Request) hardware character. Otherwise, the QTA module will not respond to Resend Requests received from the peer device. |
| 1 | RETRANSMIT | W | Retransmit TX Buffer contents: Writing a 1 to this bit causes the last (non-Resend-Request) hardware character to be re-transmitted. This bit is self-clearing. |
| 0 | RESEND_REQUEST | W | Send a Resend Request: Writing a 1 to this bit causes a Resend Request character to be queued for transmission. This bit is self-clearing. |

## 10.47 WCSS_A_RACTL_RACTL

### 0x0A00F000 WCSS_A_RACTL_PTC_LOOP_EN

**Type:** RW  
**Reset State:** 0x003F  

This registers provides the enable signals for the amplitude, frequency and channel tracking functions within the RXA PTC module. When each bit is asserted, the corresponding tracking loop is enabled.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 9 | PTCPHASETRK_DSBL | Disables VHTLTF phase-tracking functionality |
| 5 | TIME_ADJ_EN | TDC timing adjustment enable. |
| 4 | PH_ADJ_EN | TDC phase adjustment enable. |
| 3 | CHAN_EN | Channel tracking enable. If asserted, PTC channel tracking loop will detect channel phase changes and modify the channel estimate samples received from the channel estimator module. |
| 2 | FREQ_EN | Frequency tracking enable. If asserted, PTC frequency tracking loop will track reference oscillator frequency drift and modify the phase of the incoming samples received from the phase imbalance corrector module. |
| 1 | AMP_EN_MIMO | Amplitude tracking enable for mimo symbols. If asserted, PTC amplitude tracking loop will track and modify the amplitude of the incoming samples received from the phase imbalance corrector module (mimo symbols only) |
| 0 | AMP_EN_SIMO | Amplitude tracking enable for simo symbols. If asserted, PTC amplitude tracking loop will track and modify the amplitude of the incoming samples received from the phase imbalance corrector module (simo symbols only) |
<!-- page 2193 -->

### 0x0A00F004 WCSS_A_RACTL_PTC_LOOP_GAIN

**Type:** RW  
**Reset State:** 0x002A  

This registers provides the gain factors for the ampiltude, frequency and channel tracking functions within the RXA PTC module.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 7:4 | CHAN_GAIN | Channel tracking loop gain.<br>0x0: CGAIN_2 (gain = 2)<br>0x1: CGAIN_3 (gain = 3)<br>0x2: CGAIN_4 (gain = 4)<br>0x3: CGAIN_4TOO (gain = 4) |
| 3:2 | FREQ_GAIN | Frequency tracking loop gain.<br>0x0: FGNO_AVG (No averaging)<br>0x1: FGAIN_2 (gain = 2)<br>0x2: FGAIN_3 (gain = 3)<br>0x3: FGAIN_4 (gain = 4) |
| 1:0 | AMP_GAIN | Amplitude tracking loop gain.<br>0x0: AGNO_AVG (No averaging)<br>0x1: AGAIN_3 (gain = 3)<br>0x2: AGAIN_4 (gain = 4)<br>0x3: AGAIN_5 (gain = 5) |

### 0x0A00F008 WCSS_A_RACTL_PTC_CHAN_FREQ

**Type:** RW  
**Reset State:** 0x087E  

This value represents the ratio of sampling frequency to RF channel frequency using 10-bit quantisation

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 11:0 | PTC_CHAN_FREQ | Default setting = 12'd2174 |

### 0x0A00F00C WCSS_A_RACTL_RACTL_CFG

**Type:** RW  
**Reset State:** 0x7D35  
<!-- page 2194 -->

### WCSS_A_RACTL_RACTL_CFG (continued)

This register contains all the controls to enable various packet conditioning/decoding parameters

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 14 | UNSUPP_CHK_11AC_PAID GIDMISM_EN | *** Added in Pronto2 *** When enabled and when unsupported conditions in 11ac happens either from gid and/or paid mismatch, MAC will get a new level signal indicating Ractl has entered deferral mode. |
| 13 | UNSUPP_CHK_11N11AC_GENERAL_EN | *** Added in Pronto2 *** When enabled and when general unsupported conditions in 11n and 11ac happens (-except- gid and/or paid mismatch), MAC will get a new level signal indicating Ractl has entered deferral mode. |
| 12 | NDP_EN_11N | This bit enables the checking of NDP(ZLF) packets in 11n |
| 11 | AC_DEMOD_EN | Enables reception of AC packets |
| 10 | SERVFLD_OLVD_EN | This bit enables service-field-overloading for bw-capability exchange in legacy rts/cts frames. Default enabled, pmi byte5[6:4] gets data from de-scrambler input. |
| 9 | BEHAV_11N_EN | When enabled, the signal-field check of 11ac will be similar to 11n, i.e. the crc failure will be treated as a packet-abort condition. Any other condition will qualify for unsupported packet and deferral will be based on lsig. If this bit is 0, irrespective of unsupported or crc-failed vhtsiga, deferral will be done based on lsig. |
| 8 | AC_QAM256_SUPP_EN | This bit enables declaration of 256 QAM as supported rate in 11AC |
| 7 | BW_MSB_CHECK_EN | Asserted to indicate the vhtsiga bits [2:0] will be checked against agc bw [2:0] settings. 0 => vhtsiga bits [1:0] will be checked against agc bw [1:0] settings. Note default changed in Pronto assuming the msb has been changed in the latest 11ac spec to be reserved and so should not be checked. |
| 6 | SU_AID_CHECK_EN | Asserted high to indicate that when SU VHTSIGA is received, the pAID bits will be checked against the PROG_P_AID register contents to deicide whether the packet weas meant for this SU station Default 0 => vhtsiga bits [21:13] 9 bits will NOT be checked against PROG_P_AID reg settings. |
| 5 | AC_VHTB_CHK_EN_MU | This bit enables the 11ac VHTSIGB checking in MU mode Note that the contents of VHTSIGB are used by RACTL/RAHDR in MU mode so checking CRC is preferable. Unlike SU where contents of VHTSIGB are ignored and thus an invalid-CRC VHTSIGB is not indicative of a faulty packet, A CRC-faled VHTSIGB in MU-case can be indicative of a faulty packet. |
| 4 | AC_MU_RXPSHUTOFF_EN | This bit enables the 11ac MU packets to be terminated by packet-completion-indication from RXP. By default, the min of effective length computed from lsig and vhtsigb is used to signal completion within Phy itself. |
| 3 | AC_VHTB_CHK_EN | This bit enables the 11ac VHTSIGB checking in SU mode |
| 2 | SERVICE_EN | This bit enables the SERVICE field content check in non-11ac packets |
<!-- page 2195 -->

| 0 | LSIG_BIT3_CHK_EN | This bit enables checking the LSIG[3] bit which must be 1 for legacy packets, 11n mm and 11ac packets |

### WCSS_A_RACTL_RACTL_INTR_EN (0x0A00F0DC)

* **Type:** RW
* **Reset State:** 0x0060

The enables to report the interrupts to Phyint. Bit 0 is for enabling interrupt from rahdr and the other ones are in sequence corresponding to register RACTL_STATUS. By default, only watchdog-expiry and unsupported configuration-related interrupts are enabled.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 7 | UNSUPHTSIG_INTRMASKEN | Interrupt mask for unsupported HT-SIG |
| 6 | UNSUPCFG_INTRMASKEN | Interrupt mask for unsupported configuration |
| 5 | WATCHDOGEXP_INTRMASKEN | Interrupt mask for watchdog expiry |
| 4 | SERVINVALID_INTRMASKEN | Interrupt mask for invalid service |
| 3 | NOTAVALID_INTRMASKEN | Interrupt mask for not a valid |
| 2 | HTSIG_INVALID_INTRMASKEN | Interrupt mask for invalid HT-SIG |
| 1 | SSF_INVALID_INTRMASKEN | Interrupt mask for invalid SSF |
| 0 | RAHDR_INTRMASKEN | Interrupt mask for RA header |

### WCSS_A_RACTL_RACTL_SUPP_BWMISMCOUNT (0x0A00F0E0)

* **Type:** R
* **Reset State:** 0x00000000

RACTL counter to count the number of times rxa demodulated a packet at a lower bandwidth compared to that specified by agc. Note that counter is in hardware and the slave is only a readonly.

| Bits | Name | Description |

### WCSS_A_RACTL_LMAP_DUPCOMB (0x0A00F108)

* **Type:** RW
* **Reset State:** 0x0000

This register holds 2 bits - one (bit 1) is applicable till the header is demodulated and the other (bit 0) for the data symbols in general. The value in bit 0 of this bit register specifies whether duplicate tones need to be combined in the RXA before simo slicer function in the data portions of the symbol Note that the contents of this register is modified by ractl's mode detection logic such that HT-duplicate packets should always do MRC over duplicate tones irrespective of this setting. Stated otherwise, this register only affects legacy duplicate mode packets.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1 | DUPTONE_COMB_EN_SF | Off by default. When high, duplicate tones combining will take place only for signal fields (legacy or htsig) duplicate symbols. Note that due to hardware processing latencies, the settings of this bit will affect the duplicate combining of the service-data symbol of the legacy duplicate packet. |
| 0 | DUPTONE_COMB_EN | Off by default. When high, duplicate tones combining will take place only for legacy duplicate symbols. Note that due to hardware processing latencies, the settings of this bit will _not_ affect the duplicate combining of the service-data symbol of the legacy duplicate packet. |

### WCSS_A_RACTL_RACTL_SPL (0x0A00F110)

* **Type:** RW
* **Reset State:** 0x0006

This register holds some configuration bits to handle ractl-agc signalling of txop signal (only for MM packets and when LSIG and HTSIG both pass) and ractl-rahdr signalling to steer transfer of data to pmi.
<!-- page 2216 -->
| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 15 | RESET_TXOP | Off by default. When high, the txop signal from ractl will be cleared. This clearing mechanism is devised since the txop signal is not cleared with regular clearing mechanism in ractl like agc_start and agc_abort |
| 2 | NDP_PMI_XFER | ON by default. When high, the command-word and statistics bytes go to pmi. When low, nothing goes. |
| 1 | TXOP_SIG_NDP | On by default. When low, specifies that txop signal need not be toggled at all for ndp (zlf) packets |
| 0 | TXOP_SIG_SUPPHTSIG | Off by default. When high, specifies that txop calculation to be done for supported htsig Note that txop calculation is always done on unsupported htsig. |

### WCSS_A_RACTL_MCSFBSNRTH1
**Address:** 0x0A00F180
**Type:** RW
**Reset State:** 0x00C8

The estimated SNR obtained from combination of LMAP min-SNR [and optionally beamforming gain] are compared against this threshold to determine the MCS value that is suitable for reception by this client receiver. The thresholds provided by Allert are in are in dBs. And they have an offset of 22 dBs. The values here are (Allert's values -22 ) * 4. Multiplication by 4 is to get 0.25dB resolution in comparison. Also note that the values are actually signed 2's complement numbers represented as unsigned numbers, i.e. a value of 255 is -1.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 7:0 | VALUE | |

The thresholds provided by Allert are in are in dBs. And they have an offset of 22 dBs. The values here are (Allert's values -22 ) * 4. Multiplication by 4 is to get 0.25dB resolution in comparison. Also note that the values are actually signed 2's complement numbers represented as unsigned numbers, i.e. a value of 255 is -1.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 7:0 | VALUE | |

### 0x0A01440C WCSS_A_RBAPB_IGN_ILL_PLCP

* **Type**: RW
* **Reset State**: 0x00FB

This register is used to enable checking of the following fields of the PLCP header: CRC16, Rate field and Service Field. These correctness check are all described in standard IEEE802.11b. The CRC16 should check, the service field should have its reserved bits set to zero and the rate field should contain one of the supported rates (in multiples of 100 kbit/s): 8'd10, 8'd20, 8'd55 or 8'd110.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 10 | IGN_SIG | Used to ignore check for valid signal fields and pass packets with signal field errors Valid rate fields conents are 10, 20, 55 and 110 (decimal), denoting 1,2, 5.5 and 11 Mbit/s.<br>0x0: ENABLE (Enable signal field check)<br>0x1: IGNORE (Ingnore signal field check) |
<!-- page 2236 -->

### WCSS_A_RBAPB_IGN_ILL_PLCP (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 9 | IGN_SVC | Used to ignore check for valid service fields and pass packets with signal field errors A valid service fields has all bits equal to zero for 1, 2 and 5.5 Mbit/s mode. The most significant bit may be non-zero in 11 Mbits/s mode.<br>0x0: ENABLE (Enable service field check)<br>0x1: IGNORE (Ingnore service field check) |
| 8 | IGN_CRC | Used to ignore CRC check and pass packets with PLCP CRC errors.<br>0x0: ENABLE (Enable CRC16 check)<br>0x1: IGNORE (Ingnore CRC16 check) |
| 7:0 | SVC_MASK | Service Field Mask. The field is applied using a logical 'and' to the service field before the illegal service field check is applied. By default the 'coupled clocks' bit is masked out, in order not to reject packets tranmsitted by products with uincoupled clocks or products which couple clocks only for higher bit rates. |

SFD Detetction threshold is specified in microseconds. Power-on reset value is 125 decimal. Includes demodulation and descrambling delay.
