## 10.49 WCSS_A_RFIF_RFIF

### 0x0A015000 WCSS_A_RFIF_RF_BUS_CONTROL

**Type:** RW  
**Reset State:** 0x0209  

This set of registers are used to adjust timing parameters used, and to issue special commands, over the RF bus interface.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 11:8 | IRIS_ASYNC_CAP_DLY | Iris begins driving asynchronous signals to Riva at the completion of an RF command. This field is used to delay the sampling of this data after a command has completed. The default value represents a delay of approx. 25 ns ((2+1) x 120M clocks - spec requirement) when bit 3 of this register is 0. The delay changes to be in units of 60M clocks after completion of a register read command when bit 3 in this register is 1. |
<!-- page 2244 -->

### WCSS_A_RFIF_RF_BUS_CONTROL (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 7 | ENABLE_80M_IRIS_CLK_OVERRIDE | This bit is used to override the control of the 80M clock used for RF calibration mode. When disabled, the clock enable for the 80M Iris clock is automatically disabled when we observe a calibration done signal from Iris (software must still enable the clock via bit 6 below). If there are any issues with this automatic clock disabling feature, this override bit can be enabled to re-activate manual control of disabling the 80M clock via bit 6 below.<br>0x0: OVERRIDE_DISABLED (RF 80M calibration clock override is disabled)<br>0x1: OVERRIDE_ENABLED (RF 80M calibration clock override is enabled) |
| 6 | ENABLE_80M_IRIS_CLK | This bit is used to enable/disable the 80M clock used for RF calibration mode. During RF calibration mode, an 80 MHz clock must be fed out on the cmd_clk signal, and it is this bit that is used to enable/disable that clock. Bit 2 in this register is used to select this clock as the source to Iris. Bit 2 must be set first, followed by this bit. And after RF calibration, this bit must be disabled first, followed by bit 2.<br>0x0: DISABLED (RF 80M calibration clock is disabled)<br>0x1: ENABLED (RF 80M calibration clock is enabled) |
| 5:4 | SET_RF_BUS_RD_DELAY | Controls the delay value used by the RF bus interface state machine for register reads. By default (2'b00), the RF bus interface state machine inserts 3 cmd_clk cycles before it samples the read data (on the 4th cmd_clk cycle). Each value set in this register increases the delay inserted by the RF bus interface state machine before it samples the read data, by 1/2 cmd_clk cycle - i.e. 2'b01 causes the insertion of 3.5 cmd_clk cycles, and 2'b10 causes the insertion of 4 cmd_clk cycles.<br>0x0: DEFAULT (Default 3 cmd_clk RF bus interface read delay)<br>0x1: HALF_CYCLE (Extra half cmd_clk cycle RF bus interface read delay)<br>0x2: ONE_CYCLE (Extra one cmd_clk cycle RF bus interface read delay)<br>0x3: INVALID (Invalid setting - defaults to 3 cmd_clk cycle read delay mode) |
| 3 | SET_RF_BUS_FREQ | Controls the frequency setting of the RF bus interface cmd_clk signal. For Riva, two RF bus frequency values are supported - 60 MHz (default) and 30 MHz. When set to 1, this bit sets the RF bus frequency to be 30 MHz. When 0, the default mode of 60 MHz is selected.<br>0x0: V_60M_MODE (RF bus interface frequency set to 60 MHz)<br>0x1: V_30M_MODE (RF bus interface frequency set to 30 MHz) |
<!-- page 2245 -->

### WCSS_A_RFIF_RF_BUS_CONTROL (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 2 | ENABLE_RF_CALIBRATION | This bit is used to enable/disable the RF calibration mode. During RF calibration mode, an 80 MHz clock must be fed out on the cmd_clk signal, and it is this bit that is used to enable the selection of the 80 MHz clock onto cmd_clk. The entire RF calibration mode is under software control - software needs to set this bit when the 80 MHz clock is required, and disable this bit when calibration is complete.<br>0x0: DISABLED (RF calibration mode disabled)<br>0x1: ENABLED (RF calibration mode enabled) |
| 1 | RESERVED | reserved |
| 0 | ENABLE_RF_BUS | This bit enables/disables access to the RF bus. When this bit is 0 (disabled), the RF bus pins are not driven by internal RFIF logic, but may be used to drive debug data over the RF bus. The ENABLE_DEBUG_MODE bit must be set for the debug mode to be in effect. To avoid any pin conflict, debug data is only driven on the RF bus pins, when both ENABLE_DEBUG_MODE is set and ENABLE_RF_BUS is disabled.<br>0x0: DISABLED (RF bus interface access disabled)<br>0x1: ENABLED (RF bus interface access enabled) |

### 0x0A015004 WCSS_A_RFIF_RF_BUS_STATUS

**Type:** R  
**Reset State:** 0x0000  

These registers capture the status of the RF bus interface state machine and controlling logic.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 4 | CALIB_DONE | Holds the current state of the Iris calibration mode done signal. When calibration mode is selected, this signal will reset to 0. On completion of calibration, this signal will capture the done signal returned from Iris. |
| 3:0 | RF_BUS_SM_STATE | Current state of the RF bus interface state machine. |

### 0x0A015008 WCSS_A_RFIF_ARB_CONTROL

**Type:** RW  
**Reset State:** 0x000F  

This set of registers are used by the arbitration module to enable/disable data path access to the RF bus interface.
<!-- page 2246 -->

### WCSS_A_RFIF_ARB_CONTROL (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 3 | ENABLE_TXGAIN_COMMANDS | Enables/disables the Tx gain commands coming from the TXFIR.<br>0x0: DISABLED (TX Gain commands issued to RF bus interface are disabled)<br>0x1: ENABLED (TX Gain commands issued to RF bus interface are enabled) |
| 2 | ENABLE_RXGAIN_COMMANDS | Enables/disables the Rx gain commands coming from the AGC.<br>0x0: DISABLED (RX Gain commands issued to RF bus interface are disabled)<br>0x1: ENABLED (RX Gain commands issued to RF bus interface are enabled) |
| 1 | ENABLE_PHYHW_COMMANDS | This bit enables/disables accesses by PHY H/W over the RF bus interface.<br>0x0: DISABLED (PHY H/W sourced accesses to/from RF bus interface are disabled)<br>0x1: ENABLED (PHY H/W sourced accesses to/from RF bus interface are enabled) |
| 0 | ENABLE_RFAPB_COMMANDS | This bit enables/disables accesses by the RFAPB interface over the RF bus interface.<br>0x0: DISABLED (RFAPB sourced accesses to/from RF bus interface are disabled)<br>0x1: ENABLED (RFAPB sourced accesses to/from RF bus interface are enabled) |

### 0x0A01500C WCSS_A_RFIF_ARB_COMMAND

**Type:** RW  
**Reset State:** 0x000F  

This set of registers are used by the arbitration module to issue RF commands requested by software over the RF interface bus.
<!-- page 2247 -->

### WCSS_A_RFIF_ARB_COMMAND (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 6:4 | RF_CMD_DATA_WRD1 | This field holds the first data word of the software requested RF command. Currently the only commands with data supported are the RF clock enable command, and the RF reset command, of which both require only a single data word. The encoding definitions provided are for the clock enable command only. The RF reset command data word should be set to all zero.<br>0x0: DISABLE_19P2 (Disables Iris clock and selects 19.2M input from PMIC)<br>0x1: ENABLE_19P2 (Enables Iris clock and selects 19.2M input from PMIC)<br>0x2: DISABLE_38P4 (Disables Iris clock and selects 38.4M input from PMIC)<br>0x3: ENABLE_38P4 (Enables Iris clock and selects 38.4M input from PMIC)<br>0x4: RESERVED_WRD4 (Reserved)<br>0x5: RESERVED_WRD5 (Reserved)<br>0x6: DISABLE_48 (Disables Iris clock and selects 48M XO input)<br>0x7: ENABLE_48 (Enables Iris clock and selects 48M XO input) |
| 3:1 | RF_CMD | This field holds the RF_CMD to be issued. Default command is set to RF_RESET command.<br>0x0: CLOCK_ENABLE_CMD (Iris clock enable command. Used to enable/disable clocks and set frequency)<br>0x1: MODE_CMD (Iris mode command. Used to control TX and RX enable.)<br>0x2: RESERVED_CMD2 (Command not supported.)<br>0x3: RESERVED_CMD3 (Command not supported.)<br>0x4: RESERVED_CMD4 (Command not supported.)<br>0x5: RESERVED_CMD5 (Command not supported.)<br>0x6: RESERVED_CMD6 (Command not supported.)<br>0x7: RESET_CMD (Iris reset command. Resets Iris.) |
| 0 | ISSUE_RF_CMD | This bit is used to initiate an RF command over the RF bus interface. Writing a 1 to this bit requests the arbiter to issue the command loaded in the RF_CMD field. Note that only RF commands with 1 data word are currently supported by this means. When issuing a command (by writing a 1 to this bit), the value in this bit will clear to zero to indicate that the current command is in progress. When the command has completed, the value of this bit will return to 1. Reading this bit returns the status described in the encoding section.<br>0x0: CMD_IN_PROGRESS (RF command has been requested and the command is in progress.)<br>0x1: IDLE (RF command is complete, or waiting for new RF command.) |
<!-- page 2248 -->

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:0 | CFG_BASEADDR | Base address for the RPE data descriptor memory |

* **Address:** `0x0A082404`
* **Type:** RW
* **Reset State:** `0x00080006`

This register indicates the max number of stations we are associated with and the max number of Queues per station
<!-- page 2255 -->

### WCSS_A_RPE_FULLSTATE_STATIONS_QUEUES (continued)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 19:16 | CFG_FULLSTATE_QUEUES | Max number of Queues per station default value 8 indicates 8 queues qids 0-7 |
| 4:0 | CFG_FULLSTATE_STATIONS | The number here indicates the number of stations default value 6 indicates station ids 0- 5 |

* **Address:** `0x0A082408`

The register has the time out value used by RPE when any statemachine hangs

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 11:0 | SM_STUCK_CNT_VALUE | This value indicates the timeout value in terms of number of clock cycles for pronto it is 40Mhz |

### WCSS_A_RPE_RPE_CONFIG

* **Address:** `0x0A08240C`
* **Type:** RW
* **Reset State:** `0x00000080`

gives some configurations for RPE

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 27 | RPE_CLEAR_COUNTERS | writing 1 will clear all counters, HW will make it zero |
| 19:16 | RESERVED | reserved |
| 14:8 | RSRC_ENTRY_DIS | This field controls the number of resorces used for fragmentation. one resource is always used. (for only 2 resources are used only bit 0 is useful here) These seven bits can be used to turn of any resource table entry for fragment gathering. Each bit indicates the resource table entry number. bit 8 is for resource table 1, resource table 0 is always on. Resource entries should be on/off sequentially only, not randomly. for example 7'b0001111 is okay 7'b0101011 is not okay |
<!-- page 2256 -->

### WCSS_A_RPE_RPE_CONFIG (continued)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 7 | OUOFORD_PKT_FWD | Whenever a window moves due to one of internal flushing events (internal events described in bitfield 1) then the BA bitmap does not change but reorder bitmap changes if any packets that arrive in reorder for the holes then those packets need to be forwarded when this bit is set else they are dropped 1: Drop out of order packets arriving in reorder 0: Forward out of order packets packets arriving in reorder |
| 5 | NONFRAG_FLUSH_DIS | 1'b1: When set resource entries for frag pkts are not flushed when non-frag packets are received for a staid/qid which has valid entry 1'b0: When non-frag pkts are received for a staid/qid which has valid resource entry then that resource is flushed |
| 4 | HOST_BAR_DROP_DIS | 1'b1: when set then the BAR packets which have same sequence number as next expected packet will be dropped by RPE and not host 1'b0: The BAR packet which has same sequence number as next expected packet will be sent to host with opcode DROP_CUR and host will drop the packet |
| 3 | BDPDU_NOTAVAIL_DROP_DIS | THis is mostly relevant fragmented packets since we create frag BD. set to 1'b1: the packets will not be dropped when bmu indicates no bdpdu is avail, then we will wait for it to beavailable and will not drop the packet. 1'b0: default we will drop the packets when bdpdu is notavailable |
| 2 | REORDER_DIS | when set the h/w buffer reordering support is disabled(Feature that was in Libra also) |
| 0 | LRU_OR_RR | This register should always be set to Zero Inittiall it was reserved for LRU which was not implemented. No one should touch this register. If it is set to 1-> RPE will not work |

| 7:0 | ROUTING_GOOD_PACKET | All good packets will be forwarded to WQ programmed in this feild Defalut WQ is DPU |

### 0x0A082478 WCSS_A_RPE_ERR_INT_ENABLE

* **Type:** RW
* **Reset State:** 0x00000000

This register allows you to enable any error interrupt.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 8 | B_2K_JUMP_SN_IN_BASESSION_INT_EN | When a 1 is written to this bit will enable interrupt whenever AMPDU packet is received whose SN has 2k jump |
| 7 | B_2K_JUMP_SSN_IN_BAR_INT_EN | When a 1 is written to this bit will enable interrupt whenever BAR frame whose SSN has 2k jump |
| 6 | BAR_IN_NON_BASESSION_INT_EN | When a 1 is written to this bit will enable interrupt whenever BAR frames are received in BA session |
| 5 | FRAGPKT_IN_BASESSION_INT_EN | When a 1 is written to this bit will enable interrupt whenever fragmented packets are received in BA session |
| 4 | BU_SM_STUCK_ERR_INT_EN | When a 1 is written to this bit will enable interrupt when bitmap update state machine is hung |
| 3 | DD_SM_STUCK_ERR_INT_EN | When a 1 is written to this bit will enable interrupt when duplicate detect state machine is hung |
| 2 | BMU_BD_AVAIL_ERR_INT_ENABLE | When a 1 is written to this bit will enable interrupt due to noavailable Bd/PDU in BMU |
| 1 | GBI_ERR_INT_EN | When a 1 is written to this bit will enable interrupt due to gbi error |
| 0 | GAM_ERR_INT_EN | When a 1 is written to this bit will enable interrupt due to gam error |

### 0x0A08247C WCSS_A_RPE_ERR_INT_STATUS

* **Type:** RW
* **Reset State:** 0x00000000

This register status of error interrupt.
<!-- page 2262 -->
| Bits | Name | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:28 | REASON_CODE | R | Gives the reason for which the above 4 BA session related interrupts have occured:<br>4'b0000 : No error<br>4'b0001 : Fragmented packets received in BA session<br>4'b0010 : BAR frame received in NON BA session<br>4'b0100 : BAR frame received with a 2k jump in SSN<br>4'b1000 : AMPDU frame received with 2k jump in Seq Number |
| 24:21 | INT_QID | RW | gives QID of for which above interrupt occured, if two interrupts happen one after another later one will overwrite the old one. Reason code will indicate which one of the interrupt was caused by this qid |
| 20:16 | INT_STAID | RW | gives STAID of for which above interrupt occured, if two interrupts happen one after another later one will overwrite the old one. Reason code will indicate which interrupt was caused by this STAID |
| 8 | B_2K_JUMP_SN_IN_BASESSION_INT_STATUS | RW | When this bit is set it indicates that a AMPDU packet is received whose SN has 2k jump Writing a 1 will clear this interrupt and the reason code |
| 7 | B_2K_JUMP_SSN_IN_BAR_INT_STATUS | RW | When this bit is set it indicates that a BAR frame is received whose SSN has 2k jump Writing a 1 will clear this interrupt and the reason code |
| 6 | BAR_IN_NON_BASESSION_INT_STATUS | RW | When this bit is set it indicates that a BAR frame is received in a non BA session. Writing a 1 will clear this interrupt and the reason code |
| 5 | FRAGPKT_IN_BASESSION_INT_STATUS | RW | When this bit is 1 it will indicate that fragmented packets are received in BA session. Writing a 1 will clear this interrupt and the reason code |
| 4 | BU_SM_STUCK_ERR_INT_STATUS | RW | When this bit is 1 indicates bitmap update state machine is hung writing a 1 to this bit will clear the interrupt |
| 3 | DD_SM_STUCK_ERR_INT_STATUS | RW | When this bit is 1 indicates duplicate detect state machine is hung writing a 1 to this bit will clear the interrupt |
| 2 | BMU_BD_AVAIL_ERR_INT_STATUS | RW | When this bit is 1 indicates BMU has ran out of BDs writing a 1 to this bit will clear the interrupt |
| 1 | GBI_ERR_INT_STATUS | RW | When this bit is 1 indicates gbi error interrupt has occured writing a 1 to this bit will clear the interrupt |
| 0 | GAM_ERR_INT_STATUS | RW | When this bit is 1 indicates gam error interrupt has occured writing a 1 to this bit will clear the interrupt |

### 0x0A016010 WCSS_A_RXACLKCTRL_MAIN1_FAST_CLK_CTRL

* **Type:** RW
* **Reset State:** 0x0152

Control for the auxiliary fast clock coming to Phy from external clock control logic.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 12 | DBG_FORCE_FAST_ALWAYS | This is a debug-only mode configuration. Should always be left at 0 for normal purposes. When high, forces the fast_clk to be the source of clock for ALL 11AC packet types. |
| 11 | COMPLIANT_BEHAV | This bit when set to 1 enforces phy-mac interface signalling (related to 256qam processing) to comply with other modes (11a, 11n and 11ac) at the cost of increased latency in 20M and 40M modes depending on tx_bw setting. The following applies to how the clkdivratio for 20M packets is decided in compliant_behav case: *** The design forces this value to 1 when tx_bw_config is 1 or more. *** The value is forced to 0 when tx_bw_config is 0. The following applies to how the clkdivratio for 40M packets is decided- *** The design forces the value to 1 if tx_bw_config is 1. Otherwise a value of 1 or 2 can be used. When this bit is set to 0, all 256QAM STBC 20M packets will get 160MHz fastclk; all 256QAM STBC 40M packets will get either 160 or 320 MHz clock depending on extnclkdivmode40 above. |
<!-- page 2270 -->
| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 10:5 | CLKCHGDLY | Specifies the delay (in number of 80MHz clocks) between assertion of fast_clk_en in ractl (in main2 domain) to when the processing of MCS 8 and 9 STBC data-symbols is going to start. This delay is required so as to allow multi-cycle operation of the enable. This delay should include CDC delays inside PHY as well as clock-generation delay. Tune this to the minimum required delay. |
| 4:3 | EXTNCLKDIVMODE40 | This divmode determines the frequency of the clock being used by functional logic to demodulate 40MHz MCS8 and 9 STBC pkts. A value of 2 implies the clk used has same freq as that of the input fast clk. A value of 1 implies the clk used has one-half freq as that of the input fast clk. A value of 0 implies the clk used has one-quarter freq as that of the input fast clk. Compare this with the clock-division mechanism based on channel bandwidth configuration. Note that setting the value to < 2 will increase the latency of 40M packets to > 11 usec. |
| 2:1 | EXTNCLKDIVMODE20 | This divmode determines the frequency of the clock being used by functional logic to demodulate 20MHz MCS8 and 9 STBC pkts. A value of 2 implies the clk used has same freq as that of the input fast clk. A value of 1 implies the clk used has one-half freq as that of the input fast clk. A value of 0 implies the clk used has one-quarter freq as that of the input fast clk. Compare this with the clock-division mechanism based on channel bandwidth configuration. Note that setting the value to 0 will increase the latency of 20M packets to > 12 usec so a value of 0 should never be used. A value of 2 is usable at the expense of power consumption penalty. *** NOT actually used *** |
| 0 | FORCE_CLK_DISABLE | When high, forcefully disables the clock to save power. When low, the functional logic decides the duration of the enable. Note that functional logic will ensure this clock is enabled only when STBC data symbols in 11AC MCS8 and MCS9 packets mode are being demodulated by RX. |

## 10.53 WCSS_A_RXP_RXP

### WCSS_A_RXP_CONFIG
* **Address**: `0x0A080800`
* **Type**: `RW`
* **Reset State**: `0x09000100`

It contains RXP Configuration registers. These configurations (with the exception of soft abort and mask_subsq_fcs_err_within_ampdu) can be changed at any time by SW but HW will only take effect during the gap of packets so that SW will not corrupt packets during configuration.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:24 | PHY_CMD_MIN_SIZE | RXP requires atleast minimum of 9 cmd bytes for processing packet if it is not 9 then packets will be dropped, but it can be configured to whatever value |
<!-- page 2275 -->
### WCSS_A_RXP_CONFIG (continued)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 23:19 | RESERVED | reserved for future use |
| 18 | CFG_BDPDU_CLEAN_DIS | When gam error occurs it is catastrophic so we will reset the system But just to be safe RXP will clean up all BD/PDUs, this needs some extra state machine check. when this bit is set it will disable the BD/PDU cleanup and SW can go ahead and clean it after reset |
| 17 | CFG_MPR_IE_LENCHK_DIS | For the newly added IE parsing of channel switch and quiet element there is a lenchk done to make sure Channel switch is indeed 3bytes and quite element is indeed 6 bytes seting this bit to 1 this check can be disabled |
| 16 | CFG_FLT_UNPROT_ACTION_RMF_DIS | All action frames are supposed to be RMF frames(encrypted management frames) But some action frames can be unprotected, in those cases RXP sets RMF bit in BD to 0 so DPU can bypass the decryption and pass it to host SW by writing 1 to this bit this feature can be disabled, so that all action frames will have RMF set to 1 and DPU can drop the umprotected RMF frames and firmware can process these packets from Error WQ. |
| 15 | CFG_11AC_AMPDU_EOP_INDICATION_EN | If set, RXP will generate 11ac ampdu end of packet signal to PHY. By default, it will NOT generate this eop signal. If 11ac_eop is generated to PHY, PHY will stop receiving the current packet. This is used to save power in case of MU-MIMO packets |
| 14 | CFG_MPR_DISABLE_WAIT_FOR_FILTER_IDLE | When set, this will disable the 'wait for filter to finish, when eop is received' function. This is a bug fix. This configuration bit will allow the bug fix to be disabled and the rxp logic to be reverted to the original implementation. This allows for backwards compatibility. |
| 13 | RRI_CLEAR_ON_FCS_FAIL | If set, this will enable RRI regeneration when the first RRI got followed by and FCS err. |
| 12 | MASK_SUBSQ_FCS_ERR_WITHIN_AMPDU | If set, this will mask out fcs error notification to the MTU after an MPDU within an AMPDU passes FCS check. This is to prevent doing EIFS in this case. |
| 11 | SOFT_PMI_ABORT_EN | Soft PMI abort enable. |
| 10 | CFG_HAS_FCS_EN | If set, RXP will enable writing 4-byte fcs into BD/PDU and RXP flag has_fcs flag will be set to 1. By default, the RXP DMA will NOT write fcs into BD/PDU and MPDU length does not include the 4-byte fcs. |
<!-- page 2276 -->
### WCSS_A_RXP_CONFIG (continued)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 9 | CFG_RSV_BMU_EN | If set, RXP will enable sending reservation command to BMU. By default, the RXP DMA will NOT send reservation command to BMU at start of packet. |
| 8 | CFG_HAS_PHY_CMD | If set, RXP will write PHY Command into BD. By default, the PHY Command will not be put into BD so that SW can adjust the "mpdu_header_start_offset" to save the BD space for MPDU data. Note that the TimeStamp will be in BD in any case. |
| 7 | CFG_PHY_PROTOCOL_CHK_DIS | When set it disables RXP from doing any PHY protocol check Like checking PHY cmd length and stats length |
| 6 | CFG_DISABLE_DLM_PROC | If set to disable, the Delimiter Processing is disabled for A-MPDU packets and the whole A-MPDU packet will be sent to mCPU without MPDU Processing. The byp_dlm_proc and byp_mpdu_proc will be asserted for A-MPDU packets. By default, Delimiter Processing is enabled. Note: This cfg_disable_dlm_proc will affect only A-MPDU packets, but not MPDU packets. |
| 5 | CFG_DISABLE_MPDU_PROC | If set to disable, the MPDU Processing is disabled for MPDU packets and the MPDU packets will be sent to mCPU without MPDU processing. This means NO FCS check, NO address filtering, and NO binary search. The packets are assumed passing MPDU processing. By default, MPDU Prcessing is enabled. Note: This cfg_disable_mpdu_proc will affect only MPDU packets, but not A-MPDU packets. This means MPDU within A-MPDU will be processed normally (without bypass) if cfg_disable_dlm_proc is not asserted for A-MPDU packets. |
| 4 | CFG_DISABLE_FCS_CHECK | If set to disable, the FCS Check is disabled and all packets will be treated as passing FCS Check. By default, it is enabled and RXP will check FCS on MPDU packets. The counter associated with this config is fcs_err_cnt. If not disabled, this counter will increment if a packet has FCS error. |
| 3 | CFG_MAX_PKTLEN_CHECK_EN | The max packet length check enable bit. By default, the max_pktlen check is disabled. If set, it will check MPDU packet length against max_pktlen register and check A-MPDU packet length against max_len_ampdu register. But it will not affect max_len_mpdu_in_ampdu which is checked in delimiter processing and can be disabled by asserting cfg_disable_dlm_proc. |
| 2 | CFG_ADDR_FILTER_EN | If set, the Address Filter will be enabled. By default, it is disabled and all packets will be treated as passing Address Filtering. |
<!-- page 2277 -->
### WCSS_A_RXP_CONFIG (continued)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1 | CFG_GEN_SHUTOFF_EN | If set, RXP will generate shutoff signal to PHY. By default, it will NOT generate shutoff signal. If shutoff is generated to PHY, PHY will stop receiving the current packet. This is used to save power. |
| 0 | CFG_RXP_EN | If enabled, RXP will receive packets from PHY. By default, the RXP is disabled and will not receive any packet from PHY. This bit can be changed at any time, but will only take effect when there is start pulse from PHY. |

### WCSS_A_RXP_MPDU_HEADER_START_OFFSET
* **Address**: `0x0A080810`
* **Type**: `RW`
* **Reset State**: `0x00000040`
<!-- page 2278 -->
### WCSS_A_RXP_MPDU_HEADER_START_OFFSET (continued)

The MPDU header start offset in BD which is in the unit of data word (4-byte).

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 7:2 | MPDU_HEADER_START_OFFSET | MPDU header start offset in BD. Note that the programmable bits are [7:2] and the lower [1:0] bits are always 2'b00 to guarantee the offset address is 4-byte aligned. If bit[7] is 0, the MPDU header starts at BD, but if bit[7] is 1, the MPDU header starts at PDU. Note that It is not valid to have the value of 6'h3f for bit[7:2] (or 8'hfc for bit[7:0]). The default value is 6'ha which means the offset address of 8'h28. In this case, the PHY Cmd bytes will not be written in BD so that the MPDU header can start right after TimeStamp field. However, for diagnostic purpose, the PHY Cmd can be written into BD by setting cfg_has_phy_cmd bit in config register so that this offset value will be adjusted to 6'h10 which means the offset address of 8'h40. |

### WCSS_A_RXP_SEARCH_TABLE_CMD
* **Address**: `0x0A080838`
* **Type**: `RW`
* **Reset State**: `0x00000000`

This is action register for indirect access to Binary Search Table. When SW writes to this action register, it will trigger the interaction between Search_Table_Data[0-1] registers and Binary Search Table. For writing data into memory table, it is important for SW to write into Search_Table_Data[0-1] registers before Search_Table_Cmd. For reading data from memory table, SW only needs to write into Search_Table_Cmd and the read data will be available in Search_Table_Data[0-1] registers.
<!-- page 2280 -->
### WCSS_A_RXP_SEARCH_TABLE_CMD (continued)

| Bits | Name | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 9 | STATUS | R | read only: If set to 1 a binary search table read or write is ongoing. SW should read and make sure this bit is 0 before issuing another cmd write into this register. |
| 8 | WRITE | RW | Indicate write/read. If 1, write. If 0, read. |
| 7:5 | — | — | Reserved |
| 4:0 | TABLE_PTR | RW | Indicate the action should take effect on this entry number in Binary Search Table. |

---

### WCSS_A_RXP_DMA_BURST_THRESHOLD

**Address:** 0x0A080850
**Type:** RW
**Reset State:** 0x00000008

The data word threshold that RXP DMA control can start burst MPDU data to MIF. The data unit is 1 word (or 4 bytes). By default, the threshold is 8 words (or 32 bytes). RXP MPDU data is accumulated in DMA FIFO. The DMA control will not send data to MIF if the number of data word in DMA FIFO does not reach the threshold. This is to used to control the burstness of RXP data on AHB.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 5:0 | BURST_THRESHOLD | The data word threshold that DMA can start burst MPDU data to MIF. |

### 0x0A0808EC WCSS_A_RXP_CFG_FLT_NAV_CONTROL_RESPONSE_REQ

* **Type**: RW
* **Reset State**: 0x00000000

NAV control register and response requested register. The NAV PHY delay compensation can be programmed here. Also the control of how the NAV needs to be updated, or not at all, when the CCA was not asserted when a frame got received (and dropped) is configured here.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 25 | CFG_FLT_RESPONSE_REQ_WITH_HT_CONTROL | When set and the Reponse interrupt is generated, and the incoming frame has an HT control field (this is: incoming frame is QoS data frame and has the 'order' bit in the frame control field set), the response interrupt is only generated after the HT control field has been fully received and will be located in the reponse_header_info5 field. ### 0x0A080900 WCSS_A_RXP_FRAME_FILTER_CONFIG

* **Type**: RW
* **Reset State**: 0x00000000

This is a register set of 64 sequential word addresses: Each of these 64 words represent the filter configuration for a incoming frame type/subtype The register programming address per type/subtype is created as follows: ("This registers address" + {Type [b3, b2], Subtype [b7,b6,b5,b4], 2'b00}) where 'Type [b3,b2]' and 'Subtype [b7,b6,b5,b4]' are the IEEE standard encodings for the frames. A summary of the bit funtions is as follows:

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 21 | G5_DROP_AT_DMA | When set, the RXP will drop the incoming frame (even when the CRC and filter function passes) at the RXP DMA engine. This feature is usefull to prevent that control frames like the TRS, ACK etc, get unnecessarily written into memory |
| 20 | NONHT_BW_INDICATION_ENABLE | when set then the this particular type/subtype will need to be checked for bw information. If bit 0 of TA is checked to see if BW information is valid. |
| 19 | ROUTING_FLAG_SEL | when set : rxp will use dpu routing flag that is programmed in config3 bits 29:24 when not set : rxp will use dpu routing flag that is programmed in config3 bits 21:16 |
| 18 | FRAME_TRANSLATION_REQ_EN | When set Frame translation by UMA is enabled |
| 17 | PM_BIT_EVAL_REQUIRED_ENABLE | when this bit is set the pm bit is evaluated for this type/subtype packet |
| 16 | RESERVED3 | It is reserved for future use, it is read writable |
| 15 | ADDR3_ACCEPT_REMAINING_ENABLE | when enabled, and no hit was found for the Addr3 binary search, the incoming frame for this type/subtype will pass the Addr3 filter. The ADDR3 index code returned is 255 for multicast/broadcast and 254 for unicast. |
| 14 | ADDR3_BINARY_SEARCH_FILTER_ENABLE | When enabled, Addr3 is submitted to the RXP Addr3 binary search filter. When not enabled, Addr3 filtering is NOT done, The returned ADDR3 index code is 253 and the 'Addr3_index_invalid' bit in the RXP status flags in the BD will be set |
<!-- page 2299 -->

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 13 | ADDR2_ACCEPT_REMAINING_ENABLE | when enabled, and no hit was found for the Addr2 binary search, the incoming frame for this type/subtype will pass the Addr2 filter. The ADDR2 index code returned is 255 for multicast/broadcast and 254 for unicast. |
| 12 | ADDR2_BINARY_SEARCH_FILTER_ENABLE | When enabled, Addr2 is submitted to the RXP Addr2 binary search filter. When not enabled, Addr2 filtering is NOT done, The returned ADDR2 index code is 253 and the 'Addr2_index_invalid' bit in the RXP status flags in the BD will be set |
| 11 | ADDR1_ACCEPT_REMAINING_UNICAST_ENABLE | when enabled, and no hit was found for the unicast address in the Addr1 binary search, the incoming unicast frame for this type/subtype will pass the Addr1 filter. The index code returned is: 254 |
| 10 | ADDR1_ACCEPT_REMAINING_MULTICAST_ENABLE | when enabled, and no hit was found for the multicast/broadcast address in the Addr1 binary search, the incoming multicast/broadcast frame for this type/subtype will pass the Addr1 filter. The index code returned is: 255. |
| 9 | ADDR1_BINARY_SEARCH_FILTER_ENABLE | When enabled, Addr1 is submitted to the RXP Addr1 binary search filter. When not enabled, Addr1 filtering is NOT done, The returned ADDR1 index code is 253 and the 'Addr1_index_invalid' bit in the RXP status flags in the BD will be set |
| 8 | ADDR1_BLOCK_UNICAST_ENABLE | when enabled, a unicast frame for this type/subtype will not pass the filter. |
| 7 | ADDR1_BLOCK_MULTICAST_ENABLE | when enabled, a multicast frame for this type/subtype will not pass the filter. |
| 6 | ADDR1_BLOCK_BROADCAST_ENABLE | when enabled, a broadcast frame for this type/subtype will not pass the filter. |
| 5 | RESERVED4 | It is reserved for future use, it is read writable |
| 4 | RESERVED5 | It is reserved for future use, it is read writable |
| 3 | RESERVED6 | It is reserved for future use, it is read writable |
| 2 | RESERVED7 | It is reserved for future use, it is read writable |
<!-- page 2300 -->

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1 | BLOCK_RECEPTION_ENABLE | When enabled, all frames of this type/subtype will be blocked and will NOT pass the type/subtype/address filter check. |
| 0 | RESERVED8 | It is reserved for future use, it is read writable |

| 8 | CFG_FLT_HW_SW_BASED_RESPONSE_SELECTION_ENABLE | When set, the response generation path: SW based or HW based is controlled based on programming in the type/subtype configuration table, done through register "frame_filter_config". Note that if this control is required, the 'cfg_flt_generate_hw_response_enabled' should be cleared, otherwise this programming is overruled. When 'cfg_flt_hw_sw_based_response_selection_enable' is set, 'cfg_flt_generate_hw_response_enabled' is clear and 'G5_generate_HW_Response' for an incoming frame is set, the RXP will generate a pulse to the TPE to generate a response frame if also the following conditions are met: addr1 is a unicast address, caused a hit in the addr. lookup table AND incoming frame is a: Management frame OR data frame OR QoS data frame with ack policy set to normal OR RTS frame OR PSPOLL frame OR BAR_frame. When 'cfg_flt_hw_sw_based_response_selection_enable' is set, 'cfg_flt_generate_hw_response_enabled' is clear and 'G5_generate_SW_RRI' for an incoming frame is set, the RXP will generate the RRI interrupt, so that SW can start generating the response frame, if also the following conditions are met: addr1 is a unicast address, caused a hit in the addr. lookup table AND incoming frame is a: Management frame OR data frame OR QoS data frame with ack policy set to normal OR RTS frame OR PSPOLL frame OR BAR_frame. |

| 2 | BMU_PWR_UPDATE_ENABLED | When set, enables the rxp interface with the BMU for power management updates related to PWR Mgt bit in frame control field, PS POLL reception and APSD trigger frame reception. |

## Register: WCSS_A_RXP_BEACON_TSF_TIM_EXTRACT_CTRL

* **Address:** `0x0A080A5C`
* **Type:** `RW`
* **Reset State:** `0x00000003`

This is controls what information needs to be extracted from the beacon and under what condition.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31 | BSS2_BEACON_PARSE_EN | when this bit is set it indicates that we can receive a client2 bss beacons so the beacon parsing checks whether received beacon is for BSS,P2P or BSS2(BSS CLient2) mode and accordingly TSF comparison and update is done 1'b0: no BSS beacons for client2 allowed 1'b1: BSS beacons for client2 allowed |
| 30 | EARLY_TIM_PROCESS | when this bit is set then the tim not set interrupt is generated immediatly after TIM bit is received and will not wait for the FCS complete |
| 29 | P2P_BEACON_PARS_EN | when this bit is set then the system is indicating that we can receive p2p beacons so the beacon parsing checks whether received beacon is for P2P or BSS mode and accordingly TSF comparison and update is done 1'b0: no P2P beacons allowed, only BSS beacons allowed 1'b1: P2P/BSS beacons allowed |
| 28 | SIM_IBSS_BSS_BEACON_PARS_EN | when this bit is set then the system is indicating that there is IBSS/BSS co-existance so the beacon parsing checks whether received beacon is for IBSS or BSS mode and accordingly TSF comparison and update is done 1'b1: IBSS/BSS beacons allowed 1'b0: no IBSS beacons allowed only BSS beacons allowed NOTE: when bit[29:28] = 2'b11 P2P/IBSS/BSS beacons allowed |
| 27 | BEACON_CFP_AWARENESS_ENABLE | When set, and beacon processing is enabled, the beacon will also be evaluated for the presence of the CF parameter set. If present, the CFP remaining duration period is extracted and the NAV is set to that value. |
| 26:16 | ASSOCIATION_ID | The association id of the station. This field is used to know which tim bit from the TIM element is related to this station |
<!-- page 2305 -->
### WCSS_A_RXP_BEACON_TSF_TIM_EXTRACT_CTRL (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 15:8 | CFG_MPR_SSID_LENGTH | When 'enable_beacon_ssid_check' is set and 'enable_beacon_partial_ssid_check_ok' is NOT set, RXP will check the SSID length field of the received beacon. That length field will need to have the same value as this register, otherwise the the beacon filter will indicate a mismatch. When 'enable_beacon_ssid_check' is set and 'enable_beacon_partial_ssid_check_ok' is set as well, this length field indicates how many sequenctial bytes in a row of the beacon SSID field, starting from the first byte of the SSID field recieved, will have to match the programmed SSID bytes, in order for the beacon to pass the filter. Note that in this case, the SSID length field itself does not necessarily need to match, except that the length field in the beacon needs to be larger then the value programmed here. |
| 5 | ENABLE_BEACON_SSID_CHECK | When set, the tsf update (based on IBSS of BSS rules) or tim field extraction will only happen if the incoming beacon has an SSID 3 field which matches the contents of the 'SSID_field' register, and 'SSID_length' field in this register |
| 2 | DISABLE_BEACON_DTIM_PARSING | WHen set, RXP will not generate wkeup pulse if broadcast packets are pending |
| 1 | ENABLE_BEACON_TIM_PARSING | WHen set, beacon tim field extraction and TIM field interrupt pulse generation is enabled |
| 0 | ENABLE_BEACON_TSF_PARSING | WHen set, beacon timestamp extraction and TSF update are enabled |

| 25 | P2P_BEACON_CTWIN_CHNG_DETECT_INT | when set enables this interrupt The NOA CTWin value is compared with the value programmed in p2p_parsing_control2 register if there is any change then this interrupt is generated Writing 1 to this bit will clear this interrupt this interrupt goes to firmware only |
| 24 | P2P_BEACON_OPPPS_CHNG_DETECT_INT_EN | when set enables this interrupt The NOA OppPS value is compared with the value programmed in p2p_parsing_control2 register if there is any change then this interrupt is generated this interrupt goes to firmware only --NOTE---- This interrupt is overloaded with NDPA received interrupt for ECO as partial fix for addr3 issue in VHTCB, to enable NDPA interrupt set bit 17 in spare_and_clkgate_dis register. |
| 23 | P2P_TIM_BIT_CLEAR_INT | When set, p2p beacon has tim bit clear this interrupt goes to firmware only |

| 21 | P2P_TIM_BEACON_CRC_ERR_INT | When set, p2p beacon has CRC error this interrupt goes to firmware only |
| 20 | P2P_TIM_BASED_BROADCAST_FRAMES_PENDING_INT | When set, indicates tim bit indicates broadcast frames are pending from a p2p beacon this interrupt goes to firmware only |
| 19 | P2P_BEACON_NOA_ABSENT_INT_EN | When set, P2P beacon which has no NOA element interrupt will be enabled this interrupt goes to firmware only |

| 17 | P2P_BEACON_NOA_INDX_CHNG_DETECT_INT_EN | The NOA, index feild is compared with the index value programmed in p2p_parsing_control register if there is any change the this interrupt is generated When set, P2p Beacon NOA index value change detect interrupt is enabled this interrupt goes to firmware only |
| 16 | RXP_RADAR_INTERRUPT | When set, radar detect interrupt will be generated |

### WCSS_A_RXP_RXP_GROUPED_INTERRUPT_STATUS

**Address:** `0x0A080B24`

**Type:** RW

**Reset State:** `0x00000000`

RXP combined interrupt status, writing 1 to any bit will clear the corresponding interrupt

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31 | DROP_RPE_FIFO_FULL | whenever a frame is dropped due to system out of memory this bit will indicate if there was a rpe fifo full that caused this packet drop. 1: if syste_out_of memory is set and this bit is one packet dropped due RPE fifo full. 0: if syste_out_of memory is set and this bit is zero then there may BMU BD/PDU issue. Writing 1 to this bit will clear this status |
| 30 | PACKET_PRIORITY | whenever a frame is dropped due to system out of memory this bt will indicate what was the priority of the frame that was dropped. 1: high priority frame dropped. 0: Low priority frame dropped. Writing 1 to this bit will clear this status |
| 27 | DMA_GAM_ERROR | when set indicates there is error on the AHB bus (gam error). writing 1 to this bit will clear the interrupt |
| 26 | RXP_SYSTEM_OUT_OF_MEMORY_FIRMWARE_INT | when set it indicates system is running out of memory, which allows software to indicate to AP to back off on sending frmaes by sending frames with PM bit set. Writing 1 to this bit will clear this interrupt. this interrupt goes to firmware only |
| 25 | P2P_BEACON_CTWIN_CHNG_DETECT_INT | The NOA CTWin value is compared with the value programmed in p2p_parsing_control2 register if there is any change then this interrupt is generated. Writing 1 to this bit will clear this interrupt. this interrupt goes to firmware only |
| 24 | P2P_BEACON_OPPPS_CHNG_DETECT_INT | The NOA OppPS value is compared with the value programmed in p2p_parsing_control2 register if there is any change then this interrupt is generated. this interrupt goes to firmware only |
| 23 | P2P_TIM_BIT_CLEAR_INT | When set, p2p beacon has tim bit clear. Writing 1 to this bit will clear this interrupt. this interrupt goes to firmware only |
| 22 | P2P_TIM_BIT_SET_INT | When set, tim bit set in p2p beacon. Writing 1 to this bit will clear this interrupt. this interrupt goes to firmware only |
| 21 | P2P_TIM_BEACON_CRC_ERR_INT | When set, p2p beacon has CRC error. Writing 1 to this bit will clear this interrupt. this interrupt goes to firmware only |
| 20 | P2P_TIM_BASED_BROADCAST_FRAMES_PENDING_INT | When set, indicates tim bit in p2p beacon indicates broadcast frames are pending. Writing 1 to this bit will clear this interrupt. this interrupt goes to firmware only |
| 19 | P2P_BEACON_NOA_ABSENT_INT | When set, P2P beacon which has no NOA element interrupt is generated. Writing 1 to this bit will clear this interrupt. this interrupt goes to firmware only |
| 18 | P2P_BEACON_NOA_INDX_EQ_ONE_DETECT_INT | when set, indicates P2P beacon NOA index value equal to one interrupt is generated. Writing 1 to this bit will clear this interrupt. this interrupt goes to firmware only |

### WCSS_A_RXP_PMU_INTERFACE_CONTROL

**Address:** `0x0A080B48`

**Type:** RW

**Reset State:** `0x00000000`

Controls the PMU interfacing for Beacon Mode Power Save.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 10 | PMU_SLEEP_PULSE_GENERATED | When set, a sleep pulse has been generated to the PMU. Write 0 to clear this bit |
| 9 | WAKEUP_ON_BC_TIM_SET_PULSE_GENERATED | When set, a wakeup pulse has been generated to the PMU indicating a beacon is received with the broadcast tim bit set. Write 0 to clear this bit |
| 8 | WAKEUP_ON_STA_TIM_SET_PULSE_GENERATED | When set, a wakeup pulse has been generated to the PMU indicating a beacon is received with the STA tim bit set. Write 0 to clear this bit |
| 3 | SLEEP_ON_BC_TIM_CLEAR | When set, a sleep pulse will be generated to the PMU when a beacon is received with the broadcast tim bit clear. NOTE: when both 'pmu_sleep_on_sta_tim_clear' and 'sleep_on_bc_tim_clear' are set, both requirements need to be met in order to generate the sleep pulse |
| 2 | PMU_SLEEP_ON_STA_TIM_CLEAR | When set, a sleep pulse will be generated to the PMU when a beacon is received with the sta tim bit clear |

### 0x0A080B6C WCSS_A_RXP_CONFIG4

| 27 | WLAN_RX_GRANT_ENABLE | This bit is used to enable the wlan_rx grant feature.<br>0: disable the WLAN_RX_Grants control of WLAN RX<br>1: enable the WLAN_RX_Grants control of WLAN RX |

| 10 | MANAGEMENT_PRIORITY | This bit gives priority for management frames this is used in support for Better Qos.<br>1: High priority<br>0: Low priority |
| 9 | NONQOS_PRIORITY | This bit gives priority for non qos frames this is used in support for Better Qos.<br>1: High priority<br>0: Low priority |
| 8:1 | UNKNOWN_MC_STAID | when bit 0 is set then that means we are continuing address2 look up for an unknown multicast so the staid assigned for these types of packet should be set here |

## 10.54 WCSS_A_RXP_RXP

### 0x0A080800 WCSS_A_RXP_CONFIG

**Type:** RW  
**Reset State:** 0x09000100

It contains RXP Configuration registers. These configurations (with the exception of soft abort and mask_subsq_fcs_err_within_ampdu) can be changed at any time by SW but HW will only take effect during the gap of packets so that SW will not corrupt packets during configuration.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:24 | PHY_CMD_MIN_SIZE | RXP requires at least minimum of 9 cmd bytes for processing packet if it is not 9 then packets will be dropped, but it can be configured to whatever value |
| 23:19 | RESERVED | Reserved for future use |
| 18 | CFG_BDPDU_CLEAN_DIS | When GAM error occurs it is catastrophic so we will reset the system. But just to be safe RXP will clean up all BD/PDUs, this needs some extra state machine check. When this bit is set it will disable the BD/PDU cleanup and SW can go ahead and clean it after reset |
| 17 | CFG_MPR_IE_LENCHK_DIS | For the newly added IE parsing of channel switch and quiet element there is a lenchk done to make sure Channel switch is indeed 3 bytes and quiet element is indeed 6 bytes. Setting this bit to 1 this check can be disabled |
<!-- page 2340 -->
### WCSS_A_RXP_CONFIG (Continued)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 16 | CFG_FLT_UNPROT_ACTION_RMF_DIS | All action frames are supposed to be RMF frames (encrypted management frames). But some action frames can be unprotected, in those cases RXP sets RMF bit in BD to 0 so DPU can bypass the decryption and pass it to host SW. By writing 1 to this bit this feature can be disabled, so that all action frames will have RMF set to 1 and DPU can drop the unprotected RMF frames and firmware can process these packets from Error WQ. |
| 15 | CFG_11AC_AMPDU_EOP_INDICATION_EN | If set, RXP will generate 11ac AMPDU end of packet signal to PHY. By default, it will NOT generate this EOP signal. If 11ac_eop is generated to PHY, PHY will stop receiving the current packet. This is used to save power in case of MU-MIMO packets |
| 14 | CFG_MPR_DISABLE_WAIT_FOR_FILTER_IDLE | When set, this will disable the 'wait for filter to finish, when eop is received' function. This is a bug fix. This configuration bit will allow the bug fix to be disabled and the RXP logic to be reverted to the original implementation. This allows for backwards compatibility. |
| 13 | RRI_CLEAR_ON_FCS_FAIL | If set, this will enable RRI regeneration when the first RRI got followed by an FCS err. |
| 12 | MASK_SUBSQ_FCS_ERR_WITHIN_AMPDU | If set, this will mask out FCS error notification to the MTU after an MPDU within an AMPDU passes FCS check. This is to prevent doing EIFS in this case. |
| 11 | SOFT_PMI_ABORT_EN | Soft PMI abort enable. |
| 10 | CFG_HAS_FCS_EN | If set, RXP will enable writing 4-byte FCS into BD/PDU and RXP flag has_fcs flag will be set to 1. By default, the RXP DMA will NOT write FCS into BD/PDU and MPDU length does not include the 4-byte FCS. |
| 9 | CFG_RSV_BMU_EN | If set, RXP will enable sending reservation command to BMU. By default, the RXP DMA will NOT send reservation command to BMU at start of packet. |
| 8 | CFG_HAS_PHY_CMD | If set, RXP will write PHY Command into BD. By default, the PHY Command will not be put into BD so that SW can adjust the "mpdu_header_start_offset" to save the BD space for MPDU data. Note that the TimeStamp will be in BD in any case. |


<!-- page 2341 -->
### WCSS_A_RXP_CONFIG (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 7 | CFG_PHY_PROTOCOL_CHK_DIS | When set it disables RXP from doing any PHY protocol check Like checking PHY cmd length and stats length. |
| 6 | CFG_DISABLE_DLM_PROC | If set to disable, the Delimiter Processing is disabled for A-MPDU packets and the whole A-MPDU packet will be sent to mCPU without MPDU Processing. The byp_dlm_proc and byp_mpdu_proc will be asserted for A-MPDU packets. By default, Delimiter Processing is enabled. Note: This cfg_disable_dlm_proc will affect only A-MPDU packets, but not MPDU packets. |
| 5 | CFG_DISABLE_MPDU_PROC | If set to disable, the MPDU Processing is disabled for MPDU packets and the MPDU packets will be sent to mCPU without MPDU processing. This means NO FCS check, NO address filtering, and NO binary search. The packets are assumed passing MPDU processing. By default, MPDU Processing is enabled. Note: This cfg_disable_mpdu_proc will affect only MPDU packets, but not A-MPDU packets. This means MPDU within A-MPDU will be processed normally (without bypass) if cfg_disable_dlm_proc is not asserted for A-MPDU packets. |
| 4 | CFG_DISABLE_FCS_CHECK | If set to disable, the FCS Check is disabled and all packets will be treated as passing FCS Check. By default, it is enabled and RXP will check FCS on MPDU packets. The counter associated with this config is fcs_err_cnt. If not disabled, this counter will increment if a packet has FCS error. |
| 3 | CFG_MAX_PKTLEN_CHECK_EN | The max packet length check enable bit. By default, the max_pktlen check is disabled. If set, it will check MPDU packet length against max_pktlen register and check A-MPDU packet length against max_len_ampdu register. But it will not affect max_len_mpdu_in_ampdu which is checked in delimiter processing and can be disabled by asserting cfg_disable_dlm_proc. |
| 2 | CFG_ADDR_FILTER_EN | If set, the Address Filter will be enabled. By default, it is disabled and all packets will be treated as passing Address Filtering. |
| 1 | CFG_GEN_SHUTOFF_EN | If set, RXP will generate shutoff signal to PHY. By default, it will NOT generate shutoff signal. If shutoff is generated to PHY, PHY will stop receiving the current packet. This is used to save power. |
| 0 | CFG_RXP_EN | If enabled, RXP will receive packets from PHY. By default, the RXP is disabled and will not receive any packet from PHY. This bit can be changed at any time, but will only take effect when there is start pulse from PHY. |
<!-- page 2342 -->

### WCSS_A_RXP_MPDU_HEADER_START_OFFSET

**Address:** `0x0A080810`  
**Type:** `RW`  
**Reset State:** `0x00000040`  

The MPDU header start offset in BD which is in the unit of data word (4-byte).
<!-- page 2343 -->
### WCSS_A_RXP_MPDU_HEADER_START_OFFSET (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 7:2 | MPDU_HEADER_START_OFFSET | MPDU header start offset in BD. Note that the programmable bits are [7:2] and the lower [1:0] bits are always 2'b00 to guarantee the offset address is 4-byte aligned. If bit[7] is 0, the MPDU header starts at BD, but if bit[7] is 1, the MPDU header starts at PDU. Note that It is not valid to have the value of 6'h3f for bit[7:2] (or 8'hfc for bit[7:0]). The default value is 6'ha which means the offset address of 8'h28. In this case, the PHY Cmd bytes will not be written in BD so that the MPDU header can start right after TimeStamp field. However, for diagnostic purpose, the PHY Cmd can be written into BD by setting cfg_has_phy_cmd bit in config register so that this offset value will be adjusted to 6'h10 which means the offset address of 8'h40. |

---

### WCSS_A_RXP_SEARCH_TABLE_CMD

**Address:** `0x0A080838`  
**Type:** `RW`  
**Reset State:** `0x00000000`  

This is action register for indirect access to Binary Search Table. When SW writes to this action register, it will trigger the interaction between Search_Table_Data[0-1] registers and Binary Search Table. For writing data into memory table, it is important for SW to write into Search_Table_Data[0-1] registers before Search_Table_Cmd. For reading data from memory table, SW only needs to write into Search_Table_Cmd and the read data will be available in Search_Table_Data[0-1] registers.
<!-- page 2345 -->
### WCSS_A_RXP_SEARCH_TABLE_CMD (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 9 | STATUS | R | read only: If set to 1 a binary search table read or write is ongoing. SW should read and make sure this bit is 0 before issuing another cmd write into this register. |
| 8 | WRITE | RW | Indicate write/read. If 1, write. If 0, read. |
| 4:0 | TABLE_PTR | RW | Indicate the action should take effect on this entry number in Binary Search Table. |

---

**Address:** `0x0A08083C`

This is data register 0 for indirect access to Binary Search Table. There are totally 3 Data registers for Binary Search address Table.

| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:0 | MAC_ADDR | MAC_Addr[31:0] portion of MAC_Addr[47:0]. Note: The order is Little Endian: MAC_Addr[31:0] = {Byte_3, Byte_2, Byte_1, Byte_0} |

| 26 | RMF | Set when robust management frames require BIP or decryption. |
| 25 | FRAME_TRANSLATION | This bit is used to decide if a per station frame translation is required. When this bit is set and the bit in type/subtype is set then those packets for that station will require frame translation, so FT bit in BD will be set. |
| 24 | DROP | When set, on an address hit, the frame will be dropped. The setting of this bit is only valid when 'valid configuration' is set. |
| 23:16 | ADDR_ID | The addr_id[7:0]. |

### WCSS_A_RXP_DMA_BURST_THRESHOLD

**Address:** `0x0A080850`  
**Type:** `RW`  
**Reset State:** `0x00000008`  

The data word threshold that RXP DMA control can start burst MPDU data to MIF. The data unit is 1 word (or 4 bytes). By default, the threshold is 8 words (or 32 bytes). RXP MPDU data is accumulated in DMA FIFO. The DMA control will not send data to MIF if the number of data word in DMA FIFO does not reach the threshold. This is used to control the burstiness of RXP data on AHB.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 5:0 | BURST_THRESHOLD | The data word threshold that DMA can start burst MPDU data to MIF. |

### WCSS_A_RXP_DMA_DROP_CNT

**Address:** `0x0A080884`
**Type:** R
**Reset State:** `0x00000000`

The number of packets are dropped by RXP Write DMA. This could increment due to:
* Failed filter
* PHY Abort AFTER the 9th command word
* BD/PDU errors
* If packet with command phase shorter or longer than actual command length specified is sent, the RXP will increment dma_drop_cnt instead of phy_err_drop_cnt (unless actual command phase < 9 words, in which case phy_err_drop_cnt will be incremented)
* Will NOT increment if end of psdu (as defined in psdu length by PHY command) occurs during search for next delimiter in AMPDU; this is because a new packet is not found, so there should not be a drop)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 15:0 | DMA_DROP_CNT | The number of packets are dropped by RXP Write DMA. Drop due to filter error, packet len error or Get bmu error any packet dropped at DMA due to any of above errors, these can be drop at DMA marked packets which may have filter fail errors |

**Address:** `0x0A0808B8`
**Type:** R
**Reset State:** `0x00000000`

The number of packets are dropped by RXP PHY Processing because of some apparent PHY protocol errors, such as:
* PHY Cmd Len is smaller than 9 bytes
* PHY Cmd Len is larger than 28 bytes
* PHY Stats Len is not equal to 8 bytes
* *Exception:* if packet with command phase shorter/longer than actual command length is sent, the RXP will increment `dma_drop_cnt` instead (however, if actual command length is < 9, this will be counted as a `phy_err_drop`)

*Note:* The packets are dropped before reaching RXP Write DMA.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |

| Bits | Name | Description |

| 10 | CFG_FLT_REGISTER_CCA_AT_START_OF_OBSERVE_TIME | When NOT set: no action. <br>When set: The RXP filter samples the setting of the primary cca signal at the start of the cca observe time. This sampled CCA is later used to determine if an NAV update is needed or NOT. The cca observe time is configured with other bits in this register. |
| 9 | CFG_FLT_REGISTER_CCA_AT_END_OF_OBSERVE_TIME | When NOT set: no action. <br>When set: The RXP filter samples the setting of the primary cca signal at the end of the cca observe time. This sampled CCA is later used to determine if an NAV update is needed or NOT. The cca observe time is configured with other bits in this register. |

If the cca goes low anywhere during this time, this is recorded and fixed. In that case, even if the CCA went high a little later, the sampled CCA value that is later used to determine if an NAV update is needed or NOT, will have a low value. The cca observe time is configured with other bits in this register. |
| 7 | CFG_FLT_REGISTER_CCA_LEVEL_DURING_DATA_TIME | When NOT set: no action. <br>When set: The 'data reception time' as indicated by pktdet_n being low, is part of the cca observe time. |

| 4 | CFG_FLT_NO_NAV_UPDATE_ON_DROP_AND_BELOW_CCA | When NOT set: no action. <br>When set: When the RXP filter drops a frame due to any reason, AND the cca at the sample point was high, the RXP will NOT generate a NAV update based on the dropped frame. |
| 3 | CFG_FLT_NO_NAV_UPDATE_ON_EXPLICIT_DROP_AND_BELOW_CCA | When NOT set: no action. <br>When set: When the RXP filter drops a frame due to an explicit drop configuration in the address table, AND the cca at the sample point was high, the RXP will NOT generate a NAV update based on the dropped frame. |
| 2 | CFG_FLT_NO_NAV_UPDATE_ON_EXPLICIT_DROP | When NOT set: no action. <br>When set: When the RXP filter drops a frame due to an explicit drop configuration in the address table, the RXP will not generate a NAV update based on the dropped frame. The setting of the CCA is NOT taken into account |

### WCSS_A_RXP_FRAME_FILTER_CONFIG
* **Address**: `0x0A080900`
* **Type**: RW
* **Reset State**: `0x00000000`

This is a register set of 64 sequential word addresses: Each of these 64 words represent the filter configuration for an incoming frame type/subtype. The register programming address per type/subtype is created as follows: ("This registers address" + {Type [b3, b2], Subtype [b7,b6,b5,b4], 2'b00}) where 'Type [b3,b2]' and 'Subtype [b7,b6,b5,b4]' are the IEEE standard encodings for the frames. A detailed description of the RXP filter specification can be found in the NOVA MAC architecture document. A summary of the bit functions is as follows:

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 21 | G5_DROP_AT_DMA | When set, the RXP will drop the incoming frame (even when the CRC and filter function passes) at the RXP DMA engine. This feature is useful to prevent that control frames like the TRS, ACK etc, get unnecessarily written into memory. |
| 20 | NONHT_BW_INDICATION_ENABLE | When set, this particular type/subtype will need to be checked for bw information. If bit 0 of TA is checked to see if BW information is valid. |
| 19 | ROUTING_FLAG_SEL | When set: RXP will use DPU routing flag that is programmed in config3 bits 29:24.<br>When not set: RXP will use DPU routing flag that is programmed in config3 bits 21:16. |
| 18 | FRAME_TRANSLATION_REQ_EN | When set, Frame translation by UMA is enabled. |
| 17 | PM_BIT_EVAL_REQUIRED_ENABLE | When this bit is set, the pm bit is evaluated for this type/subtype packet. |
| 16 | RESERVED3 | It is reserved for future use, it is read writable. |
| 15 | ADDR3_ACCEPT_REMAINING_ENABLE | When enabled, and no hit was found for the Addr3 binary search, the incoming frame for this type/subtype will pass the Addr3 filter. The ADDR3 index code returned is 255 for multicast/broadcast and 254 for unicast. |
| 14 | ADDR3_BINARY_SEARCH_FILTER_ENABLE | When enabled, Addr3 is submitted to the RXP Addr3 binary search filter. When not enabled, Addr3 filtering is NOT done. The returned ADDR3 index code is 253 and the 'Addr3_index_invalid' bit in the RXP status flags in the BD will be set. |
<!-- page 2364 -->
### WCSS_A_RXP_FRAME_FILTER_CONFIG (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 13 | ADDR2_ACCEPT_REMAINING_ENABLE | When enabled, and no hit was found for the Addr2 binary search, the incoming frame for this type/subtype will pass the Addr2 filter. The ADDR2 index code returned is 255 for multicast/broadcast and 254 for unicast. |
| 12 | ADDR2_BINARY_SEARCH_FILTER_ENABLE | When enabled, Addr2 is submitted to the RXP Addr2 binary search filter. When not enabled, Addr2 filtering is NOT done. The returned ADDR2 index code is 253 and the 'Addr2_index_invalid' bit in the RXP status flags in the BD will be set. |
| 11 | ADDR1_ACCEPT_REMAINING_UNICAST_ENABLE | When enabled, and no hit was found for the unicast address in the Addr1 binary search, the incoming unicast frame for this type/subtype will pass the Addr1 filter. The index code returned is: 254 |
| 10 | ADDR1_ACCEPT_REMAINING_MULTICAST_ENABLE | When enabled, and no hit was found for the multicast/broadcast address in the Addr1 binary search, the incoming multicast/broadcast frame for this type/subtype will pass the Addr1 filter. The index code returned is: 255. |
| 9 | ADDR1_BINARY_SEARCH_FILTER_ENABLE | When enabled, Addr1 is submitted to the RXP Addr1 binary search filter. When not enabled, Addr1 filtering is NOT done. The returned ADDR1 index code is 253 and the 'Addr1_index_invalid' bit in the RXP status flags in the BD will be set. |
| 8 | ADDR1_BLOCK_UNICAST_ENABLE | When enabled, a unicast frame for this type/subtype will not pass the filter. |
| 7 | ADDR1_BLOCK_MULTICAST_ENABLE | When enabled, a multicast frame for this type/subtype will not pass the filter. |
| 6 | ADDR1_BLOCK_BROADCAST_ENABLE | When enabled, a broadcast frame for this type/subtype will not pass the filter. |
| 5 | RESERVED4 | It is reserved for future use, it is read writable. |
| 4 | RESERVED5 | It is reserved for future use, it is read writable. |
| 3 | RESERVED6 | It is reserved for future use, it is read writable. |
| 2 | RESERVED7 | It is reserved for future use, it is read writable. |
<!-- page 2365 -->
### WCSS_A_RXP_FRAME_FILTER_CONFIG (cont.)

| 11 | CFG_FLT_PHY_ABORT_DIS | By default phy abort is enabled. When this bit is set, it is disabled. By default, PHY RX will be aborted (shutdown) when the frame does not pass the type/subtype/address filter. This will save extra power. |
| 10 | CFG_FLT_NAV_SET_ENABLE_ON_ABORT | When enabled and the incoming frame does not pass the type/subtype/address filter and is aborted before the FCS is calculated, update the NAV. |
| 9 | CFG_FLT_NAV_CLEAR_ENABLE_ON_ABORT | When enabled, and the incoming frame does not pass the type/subtype/address filter and is aborted before the FCS is calculated, the NAV will be cleared. |
| 8 | CFG_FLT_HW_SW_BASED_RESPONSE_SELECTION_ENABLE | When set, the response generation path: SW based or HW based is controlled based on programming in the type/subtype configuration table, done through register "frame_filter_config". Note that if this control is required, the 'cfg_flt_generate_hw_response_enabled' should be cleared, otherwise this programming is overruled. <br><br>When 'cfg_flt_hw_sw_based_response_selection_enable' is set, 'cfg_flt_generate_hw_response_enabled' is clear and 'G5_generate_HW_Response' for an incoming frame is set, the RXP will generate a pulse to the TPE to generate a response frame if also the following conditions are met: addr1 is a unicast address, caused a hit in the addr. lookup table AND incoming frame is a: Management frame OR data frame OR QoS data frame with ack policy set to normal OR RTS frame OR PSPOLL frame OR BAR_frame. <br><br>When 'cfg_flt_hw_sw_based_response_selection_enable' is set, 'cfg_flt_generate_hw_response_enabled' is clear and 'G5_generate_SW_RRI' for an incoming frame is set, the RXP will generate the RRI interrupt, so that SW can start generating the response frame, if also the following conditions are met: addr1 is a unicast address, caused a hit in the addr. lookup table AND incoming frame is a: Management frame OR data frame OR QoS data frame with ack policy set to normal OR RTS frame OR PSPOLL frame OR BAR_frame. |
| 7 | CFG_FLT_FILTER_GO_TO_IDLE_ON_CLEAR_ENABLED | Gen 4 workaround: When set, and the MPDU PROC statemachine signals 'clear' to the filter, the filter will return to its idle state, forcing it to break off all interaction with other modules. |
| 6 | CFG_MPR_BMU_BA_UPDATE_ENABLED | When set, enables the RXP interface with the BMU for Block Ack update. |
| 5 | CFG_MPDU_PROC_WAIT_FOR_IDLE_FILTER_ENABLED | When set, enables bug fix from gen 4. This forces the MPDU PROC statemachine to wait for the RXP filter to get into an idle state before aborting a frame. |
<!-- page 2368 -->
### WCSS_A_RXP_CONFIG2 (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 4 | CFG_MPR_TPE_INTERFACE_ENABLED | When set to 1 the interface to the TPE is enabled. |
| 3 | CFG_FLT_GENERATE_HW_RESPONSE_ENABLED | When set to 1 the global hw response generation logic within the RXP filter is enabled for the following conditions: addr1 is a unicast address, caused a hit in the addr. lookup table AND incoming frame is a: Management frame OR data frame OR QoS data frame with ack policy set to normal OR RTS frame OR PSPOLL frame OR BAR_frame. |
| 2 | BMU_PWR_UPDATE_ENABLED | When set, enables the RXP interface with the BMU for power management updates related to PWR Mgt bit in frame control field, PS POLL reception and APSD trigger frame reception. |
| 1 | CFG_BD_DPU_SOFTMACFIELDS_UPDATE_ENABLE | When you write a 1 the DPU related fields that softmac updates is enabled. |
| 0 | CFG_RPE_INTERFACE_ENABLE | When you write a 1 RPE interface is enabled. That means duplicate detect interface function from the RXP filter is enabled as well as the bitmap update function from the RXP dma controller. |

### WCSS_A_RXP_SEARCH_TABLE_DATA2
* **Address**: `0x0A080A58`
* **Type**: RW
* **Reset State**: `0x00000000`

This is data register 2 for indirect access to Binary Search Table. It contains all the DPU related configurations that the RXP will insert into the BD. There are totally 3 Data registers for Binary Search address Table.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:29 | DPU_MC_BC_TAG | The DPU routing flag that will be inserted in the BD. |
| 28:21 | DPU_MAN_MC_BC_DESCRIPTOR_INDEX | The DPU descriptor index that will be inserted in the BD for mc/bc management packets. |
| 20 | DPU_NE | When set, the RXP will set the 'ne' field in the bd to 1'b1. |
| 19 | WEP_KEY_ID_EXTRACT_ENABLE | When set, the RXP filter will extract the Key id from encrypted frames (assuming that the encryption is wep). |
| 18:16 | DPU_TAG | The DPU routing flag that will be inserted in the BD. |
| 15:8 | DPU_MC_BC_DPU_DESC | This field contains dpu descriptor index for BC/MC QoS/NonQoS frames. RXP will insert this field in the DPU descriptor field in the BD. |
| 7:0 | DPU_DESCRIPTOR_INDEX | The DPU descriptor index that will be inserted in the BD for unicast data or unicast robust management frames (RMF). |

### WCSS_A_RXP_BEACON_TSF_TIM_EXTRACT_CTRL
* **Address**: `0x0A080A5C`
* **Type**: RW
* **Reset State**: `0x00000003`
<!-- page 2370 -->
### WCSS_A_RXP_BEACON_TSF_TIM_EXTRACT_CTRL (cont.)

This controls what information needs to be extracted from the beacon and under what condition.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31 | BSS2_BEACON_PARSE_EN | When this bit is set it indicates that we can receive a client2 bss beacons. The beacon parsing checks whether received beacon is for BSS, P2P or BSS2 (BSS Client2) mode and accordingly TSF comparison and update is done. <br>1'b0: no BSS beacons for client2 allowed.<br>1'b1: BSS beacons for client2 allowed. |
| 30 | EARLY_TIM_PROCESS | When this bit is set then the tim not set interrupt is generated immediately after TIM bit is received and will not wait for the FCS complete. |
| 29 | P2P_BEACON_PARS_EN | When this bit is set then the system is indicating that we can receive p2p beacons. The beacon parsing checks whether received beacon is for P2P or BSS mode and accordingly TSF comparison and update is done.<br>1'b0: no P2P beacons allowed, only BSS beacons allowed.<br>1'b1: P2P/BSS beacons allowed. |
| 28 | SIM_IBSS_BSS_BEACON_PARS_EN | When this bit is set then the system is indicating that there is IBSS/BSS co-existence. The beacon parsing checks whether received beacon is for IBSS or BSS mode and accordingly TSF comparison and update is done. <br>1'b1: IBSS/BSS beacons allowed.<br>1'b0: no IBSS beacons allowed, only BSS beacons allowed.<br>NOTE: when bit[29:28] = 2'b11, P2P/IBSS/BSS beacons allowed. |
| 27 | BEACON_CFP_AWARENESS_ENABLE | When set, and beacon processing is enabled, the beacon will also be evaluated for the presence of the CF parameter set. If present, the CFP remaining duration period is extracted and the NAV is set to that value. |
| 26:16 | ASSOCIATION_ID | The association id of the station. This field is used to know which tim bit from the TIM element is related to this station. |
| 15:8 | CFG_MPR_SSID_LENGTH | When 'enable_beacon_ssid_check' is set and 'enable_beacon_partial_ssid_check_ok' is NOT set, RXP will check the SSID length field of the received beacon. That length field will need to have the same value as this register, otherwise the beacon filter will indicate a mismatch.<br>When 'enable_beacon_ssid_check' is set and 'enable_beacon_partial_ssid_check_ok' is set as well, this length field indicates how many sequential bytes in a row of the beacon SSID field, starting from the first byte of the SSID field received, will have to match the programmed SSID bytes, in order for the beacon to pass the filter. Note that in this case, the SSID length field itself does not necessarily need to match, except that the length field in the beacon needs to be larger than the value programmed here. |


<!-- page 2371 -->

### WCSS_A_RXP_BEACON_TSF_TIM_EXTRACT_CTRL (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 5 | ENABLE_BEACON_SSID_CHECK | When set, the TSF update (based on IBSS of BSS rules) or TIM field extraction will only happen if the incoming beacon has an SSID field which matches the contents of the 'SSID_field' register, and 'SSID_length' field in this register |
| 2 | DISABLE_BEACON_DTIM_PARSING | When set, RXP will not generate wakeup pulse if broadcast packets are pending |
| 1 | ENABLE_BEACON_TIM_PARSING | When set, beacon TIM field extraction and TIM field interrupt pulse generation is enabled |
| 0 | ENABLE_BEACON_TSF_PARSING | When set, beacon timestamp extraction and TSF update are enabled |

interrupt Enables for RXP errors

### WCSS_A_RXP_RXP_GROUPED_INTERRUPT_ENABLE (Continued)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 27 | DMA_GAM_ERROR | Write 1 to enable this interrupt, so that whenever there is error on the AHB bus (gam error) an interrupt will be generated to firmware. |

| 6:0 | NOA_CTWIN_VALUE | Client Traffic window of value 0-6 is programmed in this register RXP will parse the beacon for this n CTWin of NOA element and if there is any change in value an interrupt is generated. ### WCSS_A_RXP_BSS2_BEACON_PARSE_CONTROL

| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:24 | IE_EID1 | These bits can be programmed to any IE(except zero length IEs) in the beacon that needs to be parsed By default it is "Quiet" IE. Also the programmed in this register can not be same as IE_eid0 |
| 23:16 | IE_EID0 | These bits can be programmed to any IE(except zero length IE) in the beacon that needs to be parsed By default it is "Channel Switch" IE.Also the programmed in this register can not be same as IE_eid1 |

| 12 | IE_EID0_PARSE_ENABLE | SW need to set this bit whenever SW wants to enable the parsing of the IE programmed in bits [23:16] |
| 10:0 | BSS2_ASSOCIATION_ID | The association id of the station for bss2 beacons. This field is used to know which tim bit from the TIM element is related to this station |

### WCSS_A_RXP_RXP_QBOOST_CONTROL

**Address:** `0x0A080BBC`
**Type:** `RW`
**Reset State:** `0x00000000`

Qboost control register

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 15:8 | QBOOST_STAID | When Qboost is enabled the STAID programmed here is staid of the address2 we are associated with |
| 4 | QBOOST_QOS_ACK_POL_NORMAL | when this bit is set and the incoming frame is a QoS frame, the ACK policy shall be set to Normal (or implicit BA request) in order for the frame to be considered as a Qboost candidate trigger frame |
| 3 | QBOOST_PWR_STATE_CHK_EN | when this bit is set, the Power State bit in the incoming shall NOT be set, in order for the frame to be considered as a Qboost candidate trigger frame |
| 2 | QBOOST_QOSNULL_PKT_EN | when this bit is set qos NULL packets will be subject to Qboost |
| 1 | QBOOST_BAR_PKT_EN | when this bit is set bar packets will be subject to Qboost |
| 0 | QBOOST_QOSDATA_PKT_EN | when this bit is set qos data packets will be subject to Qboost |

## 10.56 WCSS_A_TBAPB_TBAPB

### 0x0A012800 WCSS_A_TBAPB_CRC16_CTRL

**Type:** RW
**Reset State:** 0x0000

Controls CRC16 generator operation that calculates IEEE802.11b PLCP header CRC. For debugging purposes.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 0 | DIS | When set disables CRC16 calculation. Should be 0 (enabled) for normal operation.<br>0x0: ENABLE (CRC16 calculation enabled)<br>0x1: DISABLE (CRC16 calculation disabled) |

### 0x0A012804 WCSS_A_TBAPB_SCRAMBLE_CTRL

**Type:** RW
**Reset State:** 0x0000
<!-- page 2412 -->

### WCSS_A_TBAPB_SCRAMBLE_CTRL (continued)

Controls data scrambler operation that scrambled IEEE802.11b frame. For debugging purposes.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 0 | DIS | When set disables data scrambling by bypassing scrambler. Should be 0 (enabled) for normal operation.<br>0x0: ENABLE (scrambler enabled)<br>0x1: DISABLE (scrambler bypassed) |

### 0x0A01280C WCSS_A_TBAPB_LINEAR_DELAY_ANT1

**Type:** RW
**Reset State:** 0x0002

Stores the select for the delay diversity value to be applied to txb chain2 samples in barker and cck modulated data

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 7:6 | CCK11DIVDLY | 0 implies no delay to chain2 cck11 modulated data. 1 implies 1 delay (1 20MHz sample) to chain2 cck11 modulated data. 2 implies 2 delays. 3 implies 3 delays. |
| 5:3 | CCK5DIVDLY | 0 implies no delay to chain2 cck5 modulated data. 1 implies 1 delay (1 20MHz sample) to chain2 cck5 modulated data. 2 implies 2 delays. 3 implies 3 delays. 4 implies 4 delays. 5 implies 5 delays. 6 implies 6 delays. 7 implies 7 delays. |
| 2:0 | BRKDIVDLY | 0 implies no delay to chain2 barker modulated data. 1 implies 1 delay (1 20MHz sample) to chain2 barker modulated data. 2 implies 2 delays. 3 implies 3 delays. 4 implies 4 delays. 5 implies 5 delays. 6 implies 6 delays. 7 implies 7 delays. |

### 0x0A012810 WCSS_A_TBAPB_LINEAR_DELAY_ANT2

**Type:** RW
**Reset State:** 0x0004

Stores the select for the delay diversity value to be applied to txb chain3 samples in barker and cck modulated data
<!-- page 2413 -->

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |

**Type:** RW
**Reset State:** 0x0003

controls the power gain mode.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 2 | FIXED_RF_GAIN | fixed_rf_gain and en (clpc_en) are used to set the tpc mode. When fixed_rf_gain is set, a single rf gain value is used for the tx power control. CLPC Modes 1 and 2 require fixed_rf_gain be set. In Mode 1, rf gain will be static, in Mode 2, the gain value will be adjusted based on feadback from the PDADC. |
| 1 | OVERRIDE | When set the rf and digital gain values from the TXPWR_OVERRIDE register are used for all transmit power values. |
| 0 | EN | en (clpc_en) and fixed_rf_gain are used to set the tpc mode. When en is set, the gain LUTs will be updated based on the feedback from the PDADC. CLPC Modes 2 and 3 require en be set. |

### 0x0A082014 WCSS_A_TPE_SW_TPE_HW_CONTROL_REG

* **Type**: RW
* **Reset State**: 0x01840A01

This register contains all the h/w control config registers. s/w needs to set them as per h/w requirements. These may be either config for bug fixes or for future feature expansion or ...

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31 | IGNORE_TXP_ERROR_INT_ECO | Set '1' to ignore the txp_mim_internal_error_int_p, so tpe won't issue soft reset because of the assertion of the interrupt |
| 30:25 | RESERVED | Reserved spare register bit |
| 24:16 | SW_11G_DUPLICATE_CTRL_INDEX_OFFSET | This is same as sw_11g_ctrl_index_offset but is used only for (40Mhz) pkts If 11b stations are in, in 11g protection This sw_11g_duplicate_ctrl_index_offset + 11G Rate index of the ctrl pkt from rate table is used to derive the actual ctrl rate index -- used for RTS,CTS,BAR there is no separate valid bit for duplicate rate. sw_11g_ctrl_index_offset_valid is used |
| 15:12 | — | Reserved |
| 11 | SW_DTIM_TERMINATE_VALID | when set, dtim will be terminated when p2p/bt/lte termination happened. When cleared, same behavior as in Volans. |
| 10 | SW_P2P_TX_BOUNDARY_TERMINATE_VALID | when set, TPE will terminate the current transmission when p2p tx boundary txop reaches 0. |
| 9 | SW_GEN6_3WIRE_VALID | when set, the gen6 bt functionality is enabled to generate wlan_Active |
| 8 | SW_11G_OFDM_VALID | If this bit is set, the compensation reg is added to duration Also the sifs value in duration calculation is made 10 |
| 7:4 | SW_11G_OFDM_COMPENSATION | In the case of 11G OFDM, we add 6usec to duration. The value is given in Register for flexibility |
| 3:2 | — | Reserved |
| 1:0 | SW_COMP_DIV_DELAY_REG | The div function delay is specified in this register. Actual MCP is = sw_comp_div_delay_reg+2. By default 1+2=3 cycles |
