### 0x0A082018 WCSS_A_TPE_SW_SOFTWARE_TX_CONTROL_REG1

**Type:** RW

**Reset State:** 0x00300000

This register contains the controlls needed for s/w triggered transmission

| Bits | Name | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 29:24 | SW_WAIT_COMMAND2 | RW | This register contains the wait command2. This command is used by TXP while sending pkt in the case of TXOP burst, it is used only first time and later onwards follows the station parameters |
| 21:16 | SW_WAIT_COMMAND1 | RW | This register contains the wait command1. The tpe main waits as per this wait command before the request is considered for arbitration. The definition is as per TXP wait command. Any value beyound 21Hex is treated as no wait. by default it is no wait |
| 10 | SW_TX_GAM_SELECT | RW | When set, TPE will read the sw template from FDAHB. This is only used to send the beamform report from CFG memory in 11n sw assist mode When clear, TPE will read the sw template from CAHB. |
| 9:7 | SW_TX_SESSION_CONTROL | RW | This register contains the type of transmission s/w wants<br>000 --> nothing<br>001 --> data and use back-off index provided by s/w<br>010 --> data and use the staid, Qid given by s/w<br>011 --> template transmission, addr given by template addr |
| 6 | SW_TX_RAW_PKT_VALID_NEED_11AC_DELIMITER | RW | if this bit is set the transmission is done in raw pkt mode, but TPE will add delimiter/ofdm paddings if the rate is 11ac |
| 5 | SW_TX_RAW_PKT_VALID | RW | if this bit is set the transmission is done in raw pkt mode |

### 0x0A082040 WCSS_A_TPE_RATE_TABLE_SRAM_CONTROL

**Type:** RW

**Reset State:** 0x80000000

controls sw operations on TPE rate table. To start a read transaction, check first if bit 31 is 1. If 1, then proceed, writing 0 to bit 31, address to [29:21], 0 to bit 1, and 1 to bit 0. When bit 31 turns 1, then read the data bits. To start a write operation, check first if bit 31 is 1. If 1, then proceed, write 0 to bit 31, address to [29:21], data to [20:4], 1 to bit 1, and 1 to bit 0. When bit 31 turns 1, then write is done.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31 | RATE_SRAM_XACT_DONE | 1 indicates transaction complete - write to 0 at start of operation |
| 29:21 | RATE_SRAM_XACT_ADDR | address for SW rate table sram read/write |
| 20:3 | RATE_SRAM_XACT_DATA | rate table sram data:<br>[3] - ctrl resp lpe bit ([26] in rate table)<br>[7:4] - ctrl rate index ([17:14] in rate table)<br>[12:8] - cntrl rep tx power ([31:27] in rate table)<br>[16:13] - resp rate index ([35:32] in rate table)<br>[20:17] - 11g cntrl rate index minus 11b base offset ([61:58] in rate table) |
| 1 | RATE_SRAM_XACT_WRITE_READZ | 1 indicates write operation, 0 indicates read operation |
| 0 | RATE_SRAM_XACT_START | Write only bit that initiates SW rate sram transaction |

| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 0 | SW_TERMINATE_CURRENT_TX_VALID | If this bit is set, tpe will terminate the current transmission. Basically this needs to be used by s/w when the chip is in station mode. Though we lived with this in earlier chips, it is realized that we might occupy the channel such that the AP might delay the beacons which is not good for the power save of other stations. ### 0x0A082160 WCSS_A_TPE_BEAMFORM_CTRL

* **Type**: RW

Contains the control signals for calibration and beamform

| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:26 | RESERVED | Move to ndp_beamform_ctrl.sounding_frame_response_rate_index due to bit-width increased because of new rate. |
| 25 | CLEAR_WAITING_FOR_SENDING_QOSNULL | In SW controlled implicit beamform, SW has to write this bit so new qosnull request will be accepted SW can also use this to clear the waiting if anything goes wrong |
| 24 | ENABLE_MPI_CSI_EN | The mcfg_phycsxi_xfercsi_nonndp will be always on (as a backup if anything goes wrong). |
| 23 | CLEAR_WAITING_FOR_SENDING_CSI | In SW controlled calibration/explicit beamform, SW has to write this bit so new csi request will be accepted SW can also use this to clear the waiting if anything goes wrong |
| 22 | EXPLICIT_IMMIDIATE_CTS_RSP_EN | When set, the 'cts response' explicit beamform will be acked with immidiate cts and later ack+csi feedback, regardless the setting in bit19. This is not currently implemented. When cleared, delayed feedback will be used if bit19 is set. |
| 21 | EXPLICIT_IMMIDIATE_ACK_RSP_EN | When set, the ack 'response ' explicit beamform will be acked with immediate ack/ba+csi feedback, regardless the setting in bit19. When cleared, delayed feedback will be used if bit19 is set. |
| 20 | EXPLICIT_IMMIDIATE_NO_RSP_EN | When set, the 'no response' explicit beamform will be acked with immediate csi feedback, regardless the setting in bit19. When cleared, delayed feedback will be used if bit19 is set. |
| 19 | HW_EXPLICIT_BEAMFORM_DELAY_FEEDBACK | Set to '1' to enable the hw control csi delayed feedback for explicit beamform (when the support is enabled, and not ruled by the immediate feedback bits). |

### WCSS_A_TPE_BEAMFORM_CTRL (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 18 | EXPLICIT_BEAMFORM_EN | Set to '1' to enable the CSI explicit beamform support. |
| 17:14 | SENDING_BKOF_QOSNUL_RETRY_THRSHLD | To setup the retry threshold when sending the bkof qosnull in hw-controlled implicit beamform mode. |
| 13:10 | SENDING_BKOF_CSI_RETRY_THRSHLD | To setup the retry threshold when sending the bkof csi in hw-controlled calibration and explicit beamform mode. |
| 7 | SW_NONCOMPRESSED_EXPLICIT_BEAMFORM_EN | When set, sw control noncompressed explicit beamform is enabled. Note no hw support for this mode. |
| 6 | SW_COMPRESSED_EXPLICIT_BEAMFORM_EN | When set, sw control compressed explicit beamform is enabled. Note no hw support for this mode. |
| 5 | HW_CONTROLLED_IMPLICIT_BEAMFORM_EN | When set, implicit is under hw control. If a qosnull is waiting to be sent and bakoff 6 expires. the qosnull will be sent. |
| 4 | HW_CONTROLLED_CALIBRATION_EN | When set, calibration is under hw control. If a csi is waiting to be sent and bakoff 7 expires. the csi will be sent. |
| 3 | IGNORE_CSI_FIELD_FOR_CAL_START_NDP | Set to '1' to ignore the csi field for ndp based calibration cal start frame |
| 2 | SW_SEND_NDP2_VALID | Set to '1' to force the HW to send the ndp frame to responded to the ndp frame in the ndp based calibration. The first response for this frame exchange will be a normal ack/cts. Clear to '0' so no ndp is sent. The first response for the ndp based calibration will be a sounding frame. |
| 1 | IMPLICIT_BEAMFORM_EN | Set to '1' to enable implicit beamform support |
| 0 | SW_CALIBRATION_FRAME_EXCHANGE_ENABLED | Set to '1' to enable calibration support |

### WCSS_A_TPE_INTERRUPT_STATUS (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 12 | RTT3_T2_CAPTURE_INT_STATUS | When set, indicates that ack is send in responded to the received TMF so SW can stop the channel capture Write '1' to clear the interrupt. |
| 11 | RTT3_T4_CAPTURE_INT_STATUS | When set, indicates that (t4-t1) and absolute t1 value is ready in the register Write '1' to clear the interrupt. |
| 10 | SW_TEMPLATE_WRONG_CMD_INT_STATUS | When set, indicates that there's an invalid sw template command Write '1' to clear the interrupt. |
| 9 | EXPLICITBF_QOSNULL_INT_STATUS | When set, indicates that explicit bf qosdata+ndp frame exchange is received Write '1' to clear the interrupt. |
| 8 | SW_TEMPLATE_SENT_INT_STATUS | When set, indicates that sw template transmit is completed Write '1' to clear the interrupt. |
| 7 | GOT_ACK_FOR_BACK_INT_STATUS | When set, indicates that when expecting ba but received ack Write '1' to clear the interrupt. |
| 6 | ERROR_VALID_INT_STATUS | When set, indicates the mproc error state, or when enabled by sw, the txp timeout or internal error interrupts Write '1' to clear the interrupt. |
| 5 | WRONG_SSN_OR_TID_ERROR_INT_STATUS | When set, indicates that bar is sent and the tid/ssn of the received ba are not matched Write '1' to clear the interrupt. |
| 4 | NONCOMPRESSED_EXPLICIT_BEAMFORM_INT_STATUS | When set, indicates the noncompressed explicit beamform frame request is received. SW has to control the non compressed explicit beamform transmission Write '1' to clear the interrupt. |
| 3 | COMPRESSED_EXPLICIT_BEAMFORM_INT_STATUS | When set, indicate the compressed explicit beamform frame req is received. SW has to control the compressed explicit beamform transmission Write '1' to clear the interrupt. |
| 2 | CSI_EXPLICIT_BEAMFORM_INT_STATUS | When set, indicates the explicit beamform frame is received. SW has to control the delayed csi explicit beamform transmission Write '1' to clear the interrupt. |
| 1 | IMPLICIT_BEAMFORM_INT_STATUS | When set, indicates the implicit beamform frame is received. SW has to send the non-SIFS sounding frame transmission at bkof Write '1' to clear the interrupt. |
| 0 | CALIBRATION_INT_STATUS | When set, indicates the calibration frame exchnage step1 is done. SW has to control the CSI frame transmission Write '1' to clear the interrupt. |

### WCSS_A_TPE_SW_RTT3_CTRL

**Address:** `0x0A0821D4`

| 31:16 | RTT3_VALIDATE_TA_HI | RW | The upper bits of the TA of TMF to be validate |
| 4 | RTT3_RESP_TO_TMF_EN | W | When bit3 is set, SW has to write 1 to this bit field so HW will send ack for TMF. Once an ack is sent for a TMF, no more ack will be sent when tmf is received until this bit has been set to 1. Always read 0. |
<!-- page 2465 -->
### WCSS_A_TPE_SW_RTT3_CTRL (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 3 | RTT3_ENABLE_NO_ACK_TO_TMF | RW | when clear to 0, the ack will always be sent for TMF regardless bit4 setting when set to 1, enable the feature of not sending ack to TMF. SW has to write 1 to bit4 so ack will be sent in response to TMF. No further ack will be sent to TMF afterwards and SW has to re-enable bit4 so the ack will be sent. |
| 2 | RTT3_NONHT_RESP_RATE_EN | RW | Set to 1 to enable ht/vht response rate to TMF/TMRF |
| 1 | RTT3_RESPONDER_EN | RW | Set to 1 to enable rtt3 feature as responder |
| 0 | RTT3_INITIATOR_EN | RW | Set to 1 to enable rtt3 feature as initiator |

## 10.61 WCSS_A_TXCTL_TXCTL

### WCSS_A_TXCTL_FIR_MODE

**Address:** `0x0A012000`
**Type:** RW
**Reset State:** `0x00C4`
<!-- page 2468 -->
### WCSS_A_TXCTL_FIR_MODE (cont.)

This register is used to switch in a test waveform feed to the TX FIR instead of the normal packet data stream and to manually enable the DACs and RF chains during the test mode. !! NOTE : the user must also appropriately program the DAC_SHUTDOWN register to ensure that the DAC standby and shutdown registers are configured correctly

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 9:8 | RESERVED | reserved |
| 7 | DIS_11MBPS | When set disables secondary antennae (i.e. all antennae except ant0) for 11 Mbps mode. Should be 1 (antennae disabled) for normal operation.<br>0x0: ENABLE (secondary antennae enabled for 11 Mbps mode)<br>0x1: DISABLE (secondary antennae disabled for 11 Mbps mode) |
| 6 | DIS_5MBPS | When set disables secondary antennae (i.e. all antennae except ant0) for 5.5 Mbps mode. Should be 1 (antennae disabled) for normal operation.<br>0x0: ENABLE (secondary antennae enabled for 5.5 Mbps mode)<br>0x1: DISABLE (secondary antennae disabled for 5.5 Mbps mode) |
| 2 | ANT_EN | 4'bxxx0 -> none (No DAC/RF chains enabled)<br>4'bxxx1 -> zero (DAC/RF chain 0 enabled)<br>This field defines which TX CHAINS (DAC and RF) are enabled in the waveform (test) mode of operation and also for packets that request the default TX enable configuration. Default 1'b1, ie Chain 0 enabled. |
| 1 | RESERVED | reserved |
| 0 | SELECT_FIRMODE | This bit selects the input to the TX FIR, 0=Normal, 1=WFM generator. Default 0<br>0x0: NORMAL (Normal operation, packet data fed to TX FIR)<br>0x1: GENERATOR (Waveform operation, waveform generator output fed to TX FIR) |

### WCSS_A_TXCTL_PA_GUARD

**Address:** `0x0A012004`
**Type:** RW
**Reset State:** `0x0000`

Specifies guard interval duration before enabling PAs. Delay between assertion of T/R and assertion of PA enable to protect PAs from transients.
<!-- page 2469 -->
### WCSS_A_TXCTL_PA_GUARD (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 9:0 | TIMER | Specifies the time that the TX takes between enabling T/R switch and enabling PAs. Measured in increments of 6.25 ns for Spica (12.5 ns for Libra) from 0 to 6.4 us (12.8us for Libra). Default 20, ie 0.125us in Gen5, 0.25uS in Libra<br>0x0: MIN (0 ns)<br>0x1: STEP (6.25 ns for Spica, 12.5 ns for Libra)<br>0x3FF: MAX (6.4 us for Spica, 12.8 us for Libra) |

### WCSS_A_TXCTL_RAMP_UP_11A

**Address:** `0x0A012008`
**Type:** RW
**Reset State:** `0x004C`

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |

Measured in increments of 6.25 ns for Spica (12.5 ns for Libra) from 0 to 6.4 us (12.8us for Libra). Default 40, ie 0.25us in Gen5, 0.5uS in Libra<br>0x0: MIN (0 ns)<br>0x1: STEP (6.25 ns for Spica, 12.5 ns for Libra)<br>0x3FF: MAX (6.4 us for Spica, 12.8 us for Libra) |

### WCSS_A_TXCTL_DAC_STDBY

**Address:** `0x0A01201C`
**Type:** RW
**Reset State:** `0x0181`

This register controls the timing of DAC STANDBY signals.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 8:0 | TIMING | Each bit corresponds to one of the possible states of the TXCTL state machine. The states are as follows:<br>Bit 0 = TXCTL_IDLE<br>Bit 1 = TXCTL_RFWARM<br>Bit 2 = TXCTL_START<br>Bit 3 = reserved (unused)<br>Bit 4 = TXCTL_RAMPUP<br>Bit 5 = TXCTL_TX<br>Bit 6 = TXCTL_SHUTOFF<br>Bit 7 = TXCTL_TPC<br>Bit 8 = TXCTL_OVERRIDE |

### WCSS_A_TXCTL_FSHIFT

**Address:** `0x0A012024`
**Type:** RW
**Reset State:** `0x0017`

When enabled, this register defines the value of the frequency shift applied to quarter and half-bandwidth packets. For instance, a 20MHz packet in an 80MHz channel is considered as a quarter-bandwidth packet and its frequency shift would be defined by the bw14 field. Similarly, the frequency shift for a 20MHz packet in a 40MHz channel or 40MHz packet in an 80MHz channel would be defined by the bw12 field.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 4:2 | BW14 | 0x0: ZERO (No shift)<br>0x1: P10 (+10MHz shift)<br>0x2: P20 (+20MHz shift)<br>0x3: P30 (+30MHz shift)<br>0x4: RESERVED (No shift)<br>0x5: M30 (-30MHz shift)<br>0x6: M20 (-20MHz shift)<br>0x7: M10 (-10MHz shift) |
| 1:0 | BW12 | 0x0: ZERO (No shift)<br>0x1: P20 (+static_BW/4 shift)<br>0x2: RESERVED (No shift)<br>0x3: M20 (-static_BW/4 shift) |

---

| 15:0 | CYCLES | Allowed period of time in this state = (Register value * 128 * 12.5)ns. The state machine automatically adjusts for 20/40/80MHz bandwidth settings. Setting a value of 0 disables the watchdog. |

### 0x0A0120A8 WCSS_A_TXCTL_ALARMS

* **Type**: R
* **Reset State**: 0x0000

Monitor of all contributors to TXA abort

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 6:0 | VALUE | Abort contributors:<br>- Bit[0] = TXCTL watchdog timed out<br>- Bit[1] = Incorrect bandwidth field in command word<br>- Bit[2] = Invalid 11b packet parameters error<br>- Bit[3] = TX enable not asserted during active transmission<br>- Bit[4] = RF_WARMUP signal not asserted for sufficient length of time<br>- Bit[5] = Abort received from TACTL<br>- Bit[6] = Abort received from MPI |

### 0x0A0120AC WCSS_A_TXCTL_RESET_ALARMS

* **Type**: W
* **Reset State**: 0x0000

Resets the alarm flags

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 0 | RESET_ALARMS | When this register is written to with any value, an active high pulse is generated which will reset all alarm flags in the TACTL alarms register. |
<!-- page 2483 -->

## 10.62 WCSS_A_TXFIR_TXFIR

### 0x0A018000 WCSS_A_TXFIR_CFG

* **Type**: RW
* **Reset State**: 0x003E

Sets the various modes for the Tx-FIR

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 6 | TVWS_EN | When this field is set, new filtering logic to support TV white space channels is enabled |
| 5 | PEAK_BYPASS_OVERRIDE_EN | When this field is set, dynamic bypass of the smart clipping logic will be disabled (low power) and the peak_bypass field will be used to either statically bypass or not bypass this logic |
| 4 | PEAK_BYPASS | When this field is set, the smart clipping logic is bypassed (as long as the peak_bypass_override_en field is also set) |
| 3 | DPD_BYPASS | When this field is set, the digital pre-distorter logic is bypassed |
| 2 | LOLEAKAGE_BYPASS | When this field is set, the LO leakage correction logic is bypassed |
| 1 | IQIMB_BYPASS | When this field is set, the IQ imbalance correction logic is bypassed |
| 0 | CHAIN0FIRBYPASS | When set bypasses the upsampling and filtering for chain 0 The output of the actual filter is 12-bits and hence drops the LSB of the inputs to present 9-bits at the output |

### 0x0A018004 WCSS_A_TXFIR_LOLEAKAGE_SHIFT

* **Type**: RW
* **Reset State**: 0x0000

This register defines the number of left shifts applied to the LO leakage value derived from the gain-based look-up table in the TXFIR

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1:0 | CH0 | |

## 10.63 WCSS_A_TXP_TXP

### WCSS_A_TXP_TXP_CMDF_DIN

**Address**: `0x0A080400`
**Type**: `W`
**Reset State**: `0x00000000`

Command write port of TXP FIFO.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:0 | TXP_CMDF_WDATA | Write-only, 32-bit bitfield for commands from the software to the TXP. |
<!-- page 2583 -->
### WCSS_A_TXP_TXP_CMDF_CONTROL

**Address**: `0x0A080404`
**Type**: `RW`
**Reset State**: `0x00010024`

TXP command FIFO control register.

| Bits | Name | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 16 | TPE_CAHBZ | RW | This bit controls where the TXP commands will come from. 1 for TPE, 0 for CAHB (i.e. from SW). |
| 7:0 | FREE_ENTRIES | R | Read-only field that shows free entries remaining in TXP command FIFO |

### WCSS_A_TXP_TXP_TIMEOUT_TIMER

**Address**: `0x0A080408`
**Type**: `RW`
**Reset State**: `0x00000000`

TXP Timeout Timer - will interrupt cpu if TXP state machines do not return to idle within prespecified time.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31 | TIMER_EN | Timeout timer enable bit. |
| 23:0 | TIMEOUT_TIMER_VAL | Timeout timer value - in microseconds |

### WCSS_A_TXP_TXP_STATUS

**Address**: `0x0A08040C`
**Type**: `R`
**Reset State**: `0x00000000`

Shows status of TXP.
<!-- page 2584 -->
### WCSS_A_TXP_TXP_STATUS (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 18:17 | GAS_STATUS | Status of GAS in TXP. |
| 16 | GAM_BUSY | Shows whether GAM in TXP is busy. |
| 15:8 | ERROR_CODE | Read-only field that shows TXP error code (0 if no error).<br><ul><li>**Command FIFO - Over flow**: `8'b0001_0000`</li><li>**GAM control - AHB error returned from GAM**: `8'b0010_0000`</li><li>**Invalid BD header**: `8'b0010_0001`</li><li>**tx_size with 0 bytes**: `8'b0010_0010`</li><li>**MPDU Header longer than 1st pdu**: `8'b0010_0011`</li><li>**Data starts outside 1st pdu**: `8'b0010_0100`</li><li>**MPDU header longer than MPDU**: `8'b0010_0101`</li><li>**MPDU data_offset < MPDU hdr_off**: `8'b0010_0110`</li><li>**PINF - PHY sends abort/BTC Active**: `8'b0011_0000`</li><li>**FIFO underrun**: `8'b0011_0001`</li><li>**New transmission with no PHY clkstart**: `8'b0011_0010`</li><li>**New transmission, but PHY not idle**: `8'b0011_0011`</li><li>**PHY goes idle prematurely**: `8'b0011_0100`</li><li>**FCS - Two consecutive FCS Starts received**: `8'b0100_0000`</li><li>**Two consecutive FCS Stops received (last was FCS32)**: `8'b0100_0001`</li><li>**FCS8 Start followed by FCS8 Start**: `8'b0100_0010`</li><li>**Two consecutive FCS Stops received (last was FCS8)**: `8'b0100_0011`</li><li>**FCS32 Start followed by FCS8 Start**: `8'b0100_0100`</li><li>**FCS32 Start followed by FCS8 Stop**: `8'b0100_0101`</li><li>**FCS8 Start followed by FCS32 Start**: `8'b0100_0110`</li><li>**FCS8 Start followed by FCS32 Stop**: `8'b0100_0111`</li><li>**Main FSM - Invalid command type**: `8'b0101_0000`</li><li>**PHY command with 0 bytes**: `8'b0101_0001`</li><li>**tx_sw with 0 bytes**: `8'b0101_0010`</li></ul> |
| 7:0 | LAST_CMD_NR | Read-only field that shows last command number successfully completed by TXP. TXP extracts the last 8 bits of the command and blindly copies it to this register This is the CMD index nr field supplied by s/w. |

# 11 PMIC Arbiter

## 11.1 SPMI_CFG_TOP

### 11.1.1 SPMI_GENI_CFG

### SPMI_GENI_CLK_CTRL

**Address**: `0x0200A000`
**Type**: `RW`
**Clock**: `AHB_CLK`
**Reset State**: `0x00000000`

GENI clock control register.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 0 | SER_CLK_SEL | Serial clock select.<br><ul><li>When clear(0), GENI PROGRAM RAM, and other serial clock domain logic is connected to AHB clock, this is required for the configuration phase.</li><li>When set(1), GENI PROGRAM RAM, and other serial clock domain logic is connected to Serial clock, this is required for the command execution phase.</li></ul> |

### SPMI_GENI_FW_REVISION

**Address**: `0x0200A008`
**Type**: `RW`
**Clock**: `AHB_CLK`
**Reset State**: `0x0000FFFF`

GENI FW revision register.

In the full-duplex mode, the TX and RX protocols might be not the same.

For example, the same Geni instance might support RC-5 protocol for TX and RC-6 for RX. Therefore there are 2 FW Revision registers, one for TX and one for RX (if needed).
<!-- page 2589 -->
### SPMI_GENI_FW_REVISION (cont.)

For half-duplex protocols (SPMI, RFFE, SSBI2, ...) both FW revision registers will contains the same value.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 15:6 | PROTOCOL | TX protocol implemented. |
| 5:0 | VERSION | TX FW version. |

### SPMI_GENI_S_FW_REVISION

**Address**: `0x0200A00C`
**Type**: `RW`
**Clock**: `AHB_CLK`
**Reset State**: `0x0000FFFF`

GENI secondary FW revision register.

In the full-duplex mode, the TX and RX protocols might be not the same.

For example, the same Geni instance might support RC-5 protocol for TX and RC-6 for RX. Therefore there are 2 FW Revision registers, one for TX and one for RX (if needed).

For half-duplex protocols (SPMI, RFFE, SSBI2, ...) both FW revision registers will contains the same value.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 15:6 | PROTOCOL | RX protocol implemented. |
| 5:0 | VERSION | RX FW version. |

### SPMI_GENI_FORCE_DEFAULT_REG

**Address**: `0x0200A010`
**Type**: `W`
**Clock**: `AHB_CLK`
**Reset State**: `0x00000000`

GENI force default register. Writing '1' to this register forces default values on GENI's outputs to pads. The default values are part of the GENI image (i.e. GENI_CFG_REG)
<!-- page 2590 -->
### SPMI_GENI_FORCE_DEFAULT_REG (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 0 | FORCE_DEFAULT | force default bit. |

### SPMI_GENI_OUTPUT_CTRL

**Address**: `0x0200A014`
**Type**: `RW`
**Clock**: `AHB_CLK`
**Reset State**: `0x00000000`

GENI output control register.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 2 | SOE2_EN | forces geni_soe02 to be 0 when set, i.e. geni_sout2 is high-Z. |
| 1 | SOE1_EN | forces geni_soe1 to be 0 when set, i.e. geni_sout1 is high-Z. |
| 0 | SOE0_EN | forces geni_soe0 to be 0 when set, i.e. geni_sout0 is high-Z. |

### SPMI_GENI_CGC_CTRL

**Address**: `0x0200A018`
**Type**: `RW`
**Clock**: `AHB_CLK`
**Reset State**: `0x00000078`

GENI clock gating control register.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 9 | PROG_RAM_SCLK_OFF | When set, SCLK to program RAM is turned off. Should be used only when SCLK_CGC_ON bit is set, otherwise the clock is turned off automatically by HW when not required. |
| 8 | PROG_RAM_HCLK_OFF | When set, HCLK to program RAM is turned off |
| 6 | EXT_CLK_CGC_ON | When set, HW controls the CGC. When cleared, the CGC is always enabled. |
| 5 | RX_CLK_CGC_ON | When set, HW controls the CGC. When cleared, the CGC is enabled taking into consideration clock division |
| 4 | TX_CLK_CGC_ON | When set, HW controls the CGC. When cleared, the CGC is enabled taking into consideration clock division |


<!-- page 2591 -->

### `SPMI_GENI_CGC_CTRL` (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 3 | SCLK_CGC_ON | When set, HW controls the CGC. When cleared, the CGC is always enabled. This bit might be cleared only in half-duplex mode and when the SCLK isn't divided internally; use RX_CLK_ON and TX_CLK_ON to control CGCs in that cases. |
| 2 | DATA_AHB_CLK_CGC_ON | When set, HW controls the CGC. When cleared, the CGC is always enabled. |
| 1 | CFG_AHB_WR_CLK_CGC_ON | When set, HW controls the CGC. When cleared, the CGC is always enabled. |
| 0 | CFG_AHB_CLK_CGC_ON | When set, HW controls the CGC. When cleared, the CGC is always enabled. |

## PMIC Arbiter Registers

### 0x0200AF00 SPMI_MID_REG
* **Type:** RW
* **Clock:** AHB_CLK
* **Reset State:** 0x00000000

This register defines the MID (master ID) of the SPMI master on the bus.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1:0 | MID | This register contains the SPMI master MID. |

### 0x0200AF04 SPMI_CFG_REG
* **Type:** RW
* **Clock:** AHB_CLK
* **Reset State:** 0x00000020

This register holds different configuration of the SPMI-controller.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 16:12 | ARBITER_CTRL | Reserved bits for arbiter control need. |
| 11 | ASYNC_SSC_DET_INT_DIS | when '0'(default) mean the spmi_m async_ssc_detect use the internal indication for SSC,this can be used also for multi master (unlike ssc_detect). |
| 10 | SSC_Q1_DELAY_DIS | when set,disable the delay that placed between Q1 to Q2 regs in the SSC_DETECT |
| 9 | ARB_UNKNOWN_EN | when '0'(default) mean that if ssc_window_en='1',ssc will be detect only when master_win\|slave_win (suitable for single master) if it set to '1'ssc will be detected when master_win\|slave_win\|arb_unknown(suitable for multi master).if ssc_window_en='0' arb_unknown_en is dont_care. |
| 8 | SSC_WINDOW_EN | when set ,SSC is detected only in specific window when it is expected in order to reduce glitch risk |
| 7 | SSC_DET_INT_DIS | when '0'(default) mean the spmi_m use the internal indication for SSC (suitable for single master ,when set use the external bus for ssc detection suitable for multi master). |
| 6 | FORCE_MPM_CLK_REQ_IMM | When set request clock for cofiguration, to enable transferring the values to the ser_clock domain |
| 5 | FORCE_ARB_AFTER_MASTER_TO | When set, BOM starts an arbitration after false master arbitration (i.e. SSC hasn't been asserted within 64 us after an arbitration win. |
<!-- page 2622 -->
### SPMI_CFG_REG (continued)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 4 | BUS_IDLE_CONN_MODE | When asserted, sdata is deasserted on a rising edge when connecting on bus idle. When deasserted, sdata is deasserted on the falling edge. |
| 3 | FORCE_MASTER_WRITE_ON_ERROR | When set, the arbiter will treat a slave command as master write in case of a parity error in a command frame. |
| 2 | FORCE_MPM_CLK_REQ | When set, the mpm_clk_req is high. |
| 1 | ARBITER_BYPASS | Set to enable bypass of SPMI bus arbitration. Used in case where SPMI-controller is a single master and there are no RCS slaves on the bus. Clear to disable the bypass. |
| 0 | ARBITER_ENABLE | Set to enable arbitration process (MID must be valid at time of assertion). All other bits in SPMI_CFG_REG are allowed to change value only while ARBITER_ENABLE bit remains low. Deassertion of this bit must be followed by arst to avoid errors |

### 0x0200B000 SPMI_PROTOCOL_IRQ_STATUS
* **Type:** R
* **Clock:** AHB_CLK
* **Reset State:** 0x00000000

SPMI-protocol interrupt status register. The bits in this register are sticky. In order to clear some bit in this register, corresponding bit should be set in the SPMI_PROTOCOL_IRQ_CLEAR register.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 11 | ARBITER_DISCONNECTED | Disconnection was detected. |
| 10 | ARBITER_CONNECTED | Connection was detected. |
| 9 | PERIH_IRQ_LOST | A Peripheral interrupt was lost. |
| 8 | UNEXPECTED_SSC | Unexpected SSC was detected. |
| 7 | NO_RESPONSE_DATA_FRAME_DETECTED | No response data-frame was detected. |
| 6 | NO_RESPONSE_CMD_FRAME_DETECTED | No response frame was detected. |
| 5 | FALSE_MASTER_ARBITRATION_WIN | Master has won the arbitration but didn't initiate any command sequence within TBT. |
| 4 | FALSE_BUS_REQUEST | Bus arbitration request was asserted but no master/slave won. |
| 3 | UNSUPPORTED_COMMAND | Unsupported SPMI command was detected. |
| 2 | DATA_ADDR_FRAME_PARITY_ERROR | A parity error was detected in a data or address frame driven by an external master/slave. |
| 1 | SLAVE_CMD_FRAME_PARITY_ERROR | A parity error was detected in a command-frame driven by a slave. |
| 0 | MASTER_CMD_FRAME_PARITY_ERROR | A parity error was detected in a command-frame driven by an external master. |

* **Clock:** AHB_CLK

## 11.3 PMIC_ARB_CORE

The PMIC arbiter core are used to configure the PMIC arbiter itself and for software environments to issue commands over the SPMI bus.

### 11.3.1 PMIC_ARB_CORE_SW

The PMIC arbiter core are used to configure the PMIC arbiter itself and for software environments to issue commands over the SPMI bus.

### 0x0200F004 PMIC_ARB_MISC_CONFIG
* **Type:** RW
* **Clock:** HCLK
* **Reset State:** 0x00000002


<!-- page 2631 -->

This register provides a master switch to globally enable/disable transaction done interrupts.

### PMIC_ARB_MISC_CONFIG

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1 | CLK_GATE_EN | Enable/disable dynamic hardware clock gating for the PMIC arbiter.<br>1: Enable<br>0: Disable |
| 0 | DONE_IRQ_EN | Globally enable/disable all transaction done interrupts.<br>1: Enable<br>0: Disable |

### 0x0200F008 PMIC_ARB_PVC_INTF_CTL

**Type:** RW
**Clock:** HCLK
**Reset State:** 0x00000000

This register is used to configure aspects of the PMIC arbiter's PVC interfaces. Global and per-port enable/disable control over PVC ports is provided.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 0 | PVC_INTF_EN | Global enable/disable for all PVC ports. |

### 0x0200F00C PMIC_ARB_PVC_INTF_STATUS

**Type:** R
**Clock:** HCLK
**Reset State:** 0x00000000

This register is used to provide status of the PMIC arbiter's PVC interface as a whole. Provides status as to whether any PVC port has a request that has been received and is not yet complete.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 0 | PVC_INTF_BUSY | Status bit indicating whether or not there is a currently outstanding PMIC command on a PVC interface. |
<!-- page 2632 -->

### 0x0200F100 + 0x4*n PMIC_ARB_PRIORITIESn, n=[0..5]

**Type:** RW
**Clock:** HCLK
**Reset State:** 0x00000000

This register specifies which arbiter port has priority n. Priority 0 is the highest priority, priority 1 is the next highest, and so on.

Arbiter ports are numbered as follows: software is port 0, PVC ports are numbered from 1 to the total number of PVC ports.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 2:0 | PORT | Number of the port with priority n. |

### 0x0200F200 + 0x4*n PMIC_ARB_PVC_PORTn_CTL, n=[0..4]

**Type:** RW
**Clock:** HCLK
**Reset State:** 0x00000000

This register controls the settings for individual PVC ports. The SPMI priority of commands from this port and whether or not the port is enabled are controlled by this register.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1 | SPMI_PRIORITY | The priority the SPMI master should use when executing SPMI commands that are requested by this port. Note that this is not priority for the PMIC arbiter, but priority on the SPMI bus in the event that other (off-chip) devices are also trying to use the SPMI bus.<br>1: High priority<br>0: Low priority |
| 0 | PVC_PORT_EN | Enables/disables this particular PVC port.<br>1: Enable<br>0: Disable |

### 0x0200F280 + 0x4*n PMIC_ARB_PVC_PORTn_STATUS, n=[0..4]

**Type:** R
**Clock:** HCLK
**Reset State:** 0x00000000
<!-- page 2633 -->

This register provides per-port status on the PMIC arbiter's PVC interface.

### PMIC_ARB_PVC_PORTn_STATUS (Continued)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1 | PVC_PORT_FAILURE | Status bit indicating whether or not a PMIC command has failed due to an SPMI protocol error. This bit is cleared on a read of this register. |
| 0 | PVC_PORT_BUSY | Status bit indicating a PMIC command is in progress. |

**Type:** RW
**Clock:** HCLK
**Reset State:** 0x00000000

A write to this register triggers an SPMI command. This register is responsible for specifying all of the information needed to define the command to be performed (except for write data). The SPMI opcode, slave ID, address, and byte count are all written to this register and need to be set with a single write.

*NOTE:* A write to this register will queue up an SPMI command and until that command finished, further writes to this register will be ignored.

*NOTE:* The command register is write-only for PMIC arbiter 1.0.0 (will always read as zero).

| Bits | Name | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:27 | OPCODE | RW | SPMI opcode, as defined by the SPMI master. See the SPMI master documents for further details.<br>0x0: EXTENDED_REG_WRITE_LONG<br>0x1: EXTENDED_REG_READ_LONG<br>0x2: EXTENDED_REG_WRITE<br>0x3: RESET<br>0x4: SLEEP<br>0x5: SHUTDOWN<br>0x6: WAKEUP<br>0x7: AUTHENTICATE<br>0x8: MASTER_READ<br>0x9: MASTER_WRITE<br>0xA: TRANSFER_BUS_OWNERSHIP<br>0xB: DEVICE_DESC_BLOCK_MASTER<br>0xC: DEVICE_DESC_BLOCK_SLAVE<br>0xD: EXTENDED_REGISTER_READ<br>0xE: REGISTER_WRITE<br>0xF: REGISTER_READ<br>0x10: REGISTER_0_WRITE |
| 26 | PRIORITY | W | Controls whether the SPMI command should be sent with high or low priority.<br>1: High priority<br>0: Low priority |
<!-- page 2635 -->

### PMIC_ARBq_CHNLn_CMD (Continued)

| Bits | Name | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 11:4 | ADDRESS | W | 8 LSB bits of address for the register the SPMI command is to access. |
| 2:0 | BYTE_CNT | W | Indicates the number of bytes to read or write for operations that span multiple bytes. For single-byte operations, as well as operations other than read/write operations, this should be set to zero.<br>111: Eight bytes<br>110: Seven bytes<br>101: Six bytes<br>100: Five bytes<br>011: Four bytes<br>010: Three bytes<br>001: Two bytes<br>000: One byte |

### 0x02400004 + 0x01000*q + 0x08000*n PMIC_ARBq_CHNLn_CONFIG, q=[0..5], n=[0..127]

**Type:** RW
**Clock:** HCLK
**Reset State:** 0x00000000

Configuration register for software channels: provides the ability to enable/disable interrupts indicating transactions are done on a per-channel basis.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 0 | IRQ_EN | Enable/disable transaction done interrupt for channel n.<br>1: Enable<br>0: Disable |

### 0x02400008 + 0x01000*q + 0x08000*n PMIC_ARBq_CHNLn_STATUS, q=[0..5], n=[0..127]

**Type:** R
**Clock:** HCLK
**Reset State:** 0x00000001

Provides status of the most recent SPMI command issued to channel n.
<!-- page 2636 -->

### PMIC_ARBq_CHNLn_STATUS (Continued)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 3 | DROPPED | Resets to 0 upon the issue of the new command.<br>1: Indicates that a write to this channel illegally occurred during handling of the last command and was subsequently dropped.<br>0: Indicates that no writes to the channel occurred while the most recent command was being handled. |
| 2 | DENIED | Resets to 0 upon the issue of a new command. This bit should only be considered when DONE=1.<br>1: Indicates that the most recent command was denied by the SPMI master.<br>0: Indicates that the most recent command was not denied. |
| 1 | FAILURE | Resets to 0 upon the issue of a new command. This bit should only be considered when DONE=1.<br>1: Indicates that the most recent command has failed.<br>0: Indicates that the most recent command has completed successfully. |
| 0 | DONE | Resets to 0 upon the issue of a new command. This bit indicates completion, but not necessarily success, and should be observed in conjunction with DENIED and FAILED to determine the status of an operation.<br>1: Indicates that the most recent command is finished.<br>0: Indicates that the most recent command is still pending. |

### 0x02400010 + 0x01000*q + 0x08000*n PMIC_ARBq_CHNLn_WDATA0, q=[0..5], n=[0..127]

| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:0 | DATA | Data to write to PMIC. |

| 2 | STMTRANENAB2 | RW | Enables STM Burst Translator on STMAWID2[7:0]. A one means STM Burst Translator on STMAWID2[7:0] is enabled. |
| 1 | STMTRANENAB1 | RW | Enables STM Burst Translator on STMAWID1[7:0]. A one means STM Burst Translator on STMAWID1[7:0] is enabled. |
| 0 | STMTRANENAB0 | RW | Enables STM Burst Translator on STMAWID0[7:0]. A one means STM Burst Translator on STMAWID0[7:0] is enabled. |

### Register: `QDSS_CS_QDSSCSR_USBBAMCTRL`
* **Address**: `0x00801030`
* **Type**: `RW`
* **Clock**: `PDBGCLK`
* **Reset State**: `0x00000000`

**USB NDP BAM Control Register**

| Bits | Name | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:3 | RFU | R | Reserved for Future Use. |
| 2 | USBENAB | RW | USB trace sink enable. BLKSIZE and USBENAB must be configured before ETR and NDP BAM are configured. A one means USB trace sinking enabled once ETR and NDP BAM blocks have been configured. |
| 1:0 | BLKSIZE | RW | Configures the number of bytes that will be allowed to be written by the ETR between successive EOB indications. This is an average value over time so the EOB descriptors could deviate from this size by plus or minus 15*8 bytes.<br>0x3: ENUM_3 (2048 bytes)<br>0x2: ENUM_2 (1024 bytes)<br>0x1: ENUM_1 (512 bytes)<br>0x0: ENUM_0 (256 bytes) |

QDSS ETR Byte Counter Interrupt Control Register

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:0 | IRQBYTECNTVAL | This 32 bit value defines the number of bytes that, when moved by the ETR AXI interface, causes an interrupt that may be used by an EE to know how much data is present in memory requiring copy to some other location. ## 12.1.3 CXSTM_2_32_32_TRUE

The CoreSight CXSTM is instrumentation trace macrocell with software and hardware stimulus ports that generates trace according to MIPI STPv2 protocol.

### 12.1.3.1 QDSS_CXSTM_2_32_32_TRUE

## 12.1.4 CTI0_CSCTI

The CTI allows mapping a trigger on the Trigger interface to a signal on the Channel interface and vice versa. The mapping is user-programmable. When the CTI receives a channel event it maps this onto a trigger output. This enables subsystems to cross trigger with each other. The receiving and transmitting of triggers is performed through the trigger interface.
<!-- page 2699 -->

### 12.1.4.1 QDSS_CTI0_CSCTI

The CTI allows mapping a trigger on the Trigger interface to a signal on the Channel interface and vice versa. The mapping is user-programmable. ### Register: QDSS_CTI0_CLAIMSET
- **Address**: `0x00810FA0`
- **Type**: RW
- **Reset State**: `0x0000000F`

This is used in conjunction with Claim Tag Clear Register, CLAIMCLR. This register forms one half of the Claim Tag value. This location allows individual bits to be set, write, and returns the number of bits that can be set, read.

| Bits | Name | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 3:0 | CLAIMSET_W | W | Each bit is considered separately: 0 = no effect, 1 = set this bit in the claim tag. |
| 3:0 | CLAIMSET_R | R | This claim tag bit is implemented.<br>0xF: CLAIM_TAG_IMPLEMENTED_BITS (These bits are present within the claim tag field) |

### Register: QDSS_CTI0_CLAIMCLR
- **Address**: `0x00810FA4`
- **Type**: RW
- **Reset State**: `0x00000000`

This register is used in conjunction with Claim Tag Set Register, CLAIMSET. This register forms one half of the Claim Tag value. This location enables individual bits to be cleared, write, and returns the current Claim Tag value, read.

| Bits | Name | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 3:0 | CLAIMCLR_W | W | Each bit is considered separately: 0 = no effect, 1 = clear this bit in the claim tag. |
<!-- page 2709 -->
### Register: QDSS_CTI0_CLAIMCLR (continued)

| Bits | Name | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 3:0 | CLAIMCLR_R | R | The value present reflects the current setting of the Claim Tag. |

### Register: QDSS_CTI0_LAR
- **Address**: `0x00810FB0`
- **Type**: W
- **Reset State**: `Undefined`

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:0 | ACCESS_W | A write of 0xC5ACCE55 enables further write access to this device. A write of any value other than 0xC5ACCE55 will have the affect of removing write access.<br>0xC5ACCE55: UNLOCK (Unlock the protection register to enable write access) |

### Register: QDSS_CTI0_LSR
- **Address**: `0x00810FB4`
- **Type**: R
- **Reset State**: `0x00000003`

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 2 | LOCKTYPE | Indicates if the Lock Access Register (0xFB0) is implemented as 8-bit or 32-bit<br>0x0: ENUM_32_BIT (This component implements a 32-bit Lock Access Register) |
| 1 | LOCKGRANT | Returns the current status of the Lock. This bit reads as 0 when read from an external debugger (PADDRDBG31 = 1) since external debugger accesses are not subject to Lock Registers.<br>0x0: ACCESS_PERMITTED (Write access is permitted to this device)<br>0x1: DEVICE_LOCKED (Write access to the component is blocked. All writes to control registers are ignored. Reads are permitted) |
| 0 | LOCKEXIST | Indicates that a lock control mechanism exists for this device. This bit reads as 0 when read from an external debugger (PADDRDBG31 = 1) since external debugger accesses are not subject to Lock Registers.<br>0x0: LOCK_NOT_PRESENT (No lock control mechanism exists, writes to the Lock Access register (0xFB0) will be ignored)<br>0x1: LOCK_PRESENT (Lock control mechanism is present) |

| 1:0 | NSID | Indicates the security level for non-secure invasive debug<br>0x2: ENUM_2_B10 (Non-secure Invasive debug functionality currently disabled.)<br>0x3: ENUM_2_B11 (Non-secure Invasive debug functionality currently enabled.) |

## 12.1.5 CTI1_CSCTI

The CTI allows mapping a trigger on the Trigger interface to a signal on the Channel interface and vice versa. The mapping is user-programmable. When the CTI receives a channel event it maps this onto a trigger output. This enables subsystems to cross trigger with each other. The receiving and transmitting of triggers is performed through the trigger interface.

### 12.1.5.1 QDSS_CTI1_CSCTI

The CTI allows mapping a trigger on the Trigger interface to a signal on the Channel interface and vice versa. The mapping is user-programmable. When the CTI receives a channel event it maps this onto a trigger output. This enables subsystems to cross trigger with each other. The receiving and transmitting of triggers is performed through the trigger interface.

### 0x00811FA0 QDSS_CTI1_CLAIMSET

* **Type:** RW
* **Reset State:** 0x0000000F

This is used in conjunction with Claim Tag Clear Register, CLAIMCLR. This register forms one half of the Claim Tag value. This location allows individual bits to be set, write, and returns the number of bits that can be set, read.

| Bits | Name | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 3:0 | CLAIMSET_W | W | Each bit is considered separately: 0 = no effect, 1 = set this bit in the claim tag. |
| 3:0 | CLAIMSET_R | R | This claim tag bit is implemented<br>0xF: CLAIM_TAG_IMPLEMENTED_BITS (These bits are present within the claim tag field) |

### 0x00811FA4 QDSS_CTI1_CLAIMCLR

* **Type:** RW
* **Reset State:** 0x00000000

This register is used in conjunction with Claim Tag Set Register, CLAIMSET. This register forms one half of the Claim Tag value. This location enables individual bits to be cleared, write, and returns the current Claim Tag value, read.

| Bits | Name | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 3:0 | CLAIMCLR_W | W | Each bit is considered separately: 0 = no effect, 1 = clear this bit in the claim tag. |
| 3:0 | CLAIMCLR_R | R | The value present reflects the current setting of the Claim Tag. |

| 1 | LOCKGRANT | Returns the current status of the Lock. This bit reads as 0 when read from an external debugger (PADDRDBG31 = 1) since external debugger accesses are not subject to Lock Registers.<br>0x0: ACCESS_PERMITTED (Write access is permitted to this device)<br>0x1: DEVICE_LOCKED (Write access to the component is blocked. All writes to control registers are ignored. Reads are permitted) |
| 0 | LOCKEXIST | Indicates that a lock control mechanism exists for this device. This bit reads as 0 when read from an external debugger (PADDRDBG31 = 1) since external debugger accesses are not subject to Lock Registers.<br>0x0: LOCK_NOT_PRESENT (No lock control mechanism exists, writes to the Lock Access register (0xFB0) will be ignored)<br>0x1: LOCK_PRESENT (Lock control mechanism is present) |

## 12.1.6 CTI2_CSCTI

The CTI allows mapping a trigger on the Trigger interface to a signal on the Channel interface and vice versa. The mapping is user-programmable. When the CTI receives a channel event it maps this onto a trigger output. This enables subsystems to cross trigger with each other. The receiving and transmitting of triggers is performed through the trigger interface.

### 12.1.6.1 QDSS_CTI2_CSCTI

The CTI allows mapping a trigger on the Trigger interface to a signal on the Channel interface and vice versa. The mapping is user-programmable. This bit reads as 0 when read from an external debugger (PADDRDBG31 = 1) since external debugger accesses are not subject to Lock Registers.<br>0x0: ACCESS_PERMITTED (Write access is permitted to this device)<br>0x1: DEVICE_LOCKED (Write access to the component is blocked. ## 12.1.7 CTI3_CSCTI

The CTI allows mapping a trigger on the Trigger interface to a signal on the Channel interface and vice versa. The mapping is user-programmable. When the CTI receives a channel event it maps this onto a trigger output. This enables subsystems to cross trigger with each other. The receiving and transmitting of triggers is performed through the trigger interface.

### 12.1.7.1 QDSS_CTI3_CSCTI

### QDSS_CTI3_CLAIMSET
**Address:** `0x00813FA0`
**Type:** RW
**Reset State:** `0x0000000F`

This is used in conjunction with Claim Tag Clear Register, CLAIMCLR. This register forms one half of the Claim Tag value. This location allows individual bits to be set, write, and returns the number of bits that can be set, read.

| Bits | Name | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 3:0 | CLAIMSET_W | W | Each bit is considered separately: 0 = no effect, 1 = set this bit in the claim tag. |
| 3:0 | CLAIMSET_R | R | This claim tag bit is implemented.<br>0xF: CLAIM_TAG_IMPLEMENTED_BITS (These bits are present within the claim tag field) |

### QDSS_CTI3_CLAIMCLR
**Address:** `0x00813FA4`
**Type:** RW
**Reset State:** `0x00000000`

This register is used in conjunction with Claim Tag Set Register, CLAIMSET. This register forms one half of the Claim Tag value. This location enables individual bits to be cleared, write, and returns the current Claim Tag value, read.

| Bits | Name | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 3:0 | CLAIMCLR_W | W | Each bit is considered separately: 0 = no effect, 1 = clear this bit in the claim tag. |
| 3:0 | CLAIMCLR_R | R | The value present reflects the current setting of the Claim Tag. |

## 12.1.8 CTI4_CSCTI
The CTI allows mapping a trigger on the Trigger interface to a signal on the Channel interface and vice versa. The mapping is user-programmable. When the CTI receives a channel event it maps this onto a trigger output. This enables subsystems to cross trigger with each other. The receiving and transmitting of triggers is performed through the trigger interface.

### 12.1.8.1 QDSS_CTI4_CSCTI
The CTI allows mapping a trigger on the Trigger interface to a signal on the Channel interface and vice versa. The mapping is user-programmable. When the CTI receives a channel event it maps this onto a trigger output. This enables subsystems to cross trigger with each other. The receiving and transmitting of triggers is performed through the trigger interface.

### QDSS_CTI4_CLAIMSET
* **Address**: `0x00814FA0`
* **Type**: RW
* **Reset State**: `0x0000000F`

This is used in conjunction with Claim Tag Clear Register, CLAIMCLR. This register forms one half of the Claim Tag value. This location allows individual bits to be set, write, and returns the number of bits that can be set, read.

| Bits | Name | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 3:0 | CLAIMSET_W | W | Each bit is considered separately: 0 = no effect, 1 = set this bit in the claim tag. |
| 3:0 | CLAIMSET_R | R | This claim tag bit is implemented.<br>0xF: CLAIM_TAG_IMPLEMENTED_BITS (These bits are present within the claim tag field) |

### QDSS_CTI4_CLAIMCLR
* **Address**: `0x00814FA4`
* **Type**: RW
* **Reset State**: `0x00000000`

This register is used in conjunction with Claim Tag Set Register, CLAIMSET. This register forms one half of the Claim Tag value. This location enables individual bits to be cleared, write, and returns the current Claim Tag value, read.

| Bits | Name | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 3:0 | CLAIMCLR_W | W | Each bit is considered separately: 0 = no effect, 1 = clear this bit in the claim tag. |
| 3:0 | CLAIMCLR_R | R | The value present reflects the current setting of the Claim Tag. |

### QDSS_CTI4_LSR
* **Address**: `0x00814FB4`
* **Type**: R
* **Reset State**: `0x00000003`

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 2 | LOCKTYPE | Indicates if the Lock Access Register (0xFB0) is implemented as 8-bit or 32-bit.<br>0x0: ENUM_32_BIT (This component implements a 32-bit Lock Access Register) |
| 1 | LOCKGRANT | Returns the current status of the Lock. This bit reads as 0 when read from an external debugger (PADDRDBG31 = 1) since external debugger accesses are not subject to Lock Registers.<br>0x0: ACCESS_PERMITTED (Write access is permitted to this device)<br>0x1: DEVICE_LOCKED (Write access to the component is blocked. All writes to control registers are ignored. Reads are permitted) |
| 0 | LOCKEXIST | Indicates that a lock control mechanism exists for this device. This bit reads as 0 when read from an external debugger (PADDRDBG31 = 1) since external debugger accesses are not subject to Lock Registers.<br>0x0: LOCK_NOT_PRESENT (No lock control mechanism exists, writes to the Lock Access register (0xFB0) will be ignored)<br>0x1: LOCK_PRESENT (Lock control mechanism is present) |

## 12.1.9 CTI5_CSCTI

The CTI allows mapping a trigger on the Trigger interface to a signal on the Channel interface and vice versa. The mapping is user-programmable. When the CTI receives a channel event it maps this onto a trigger output. This enables subsystems to cross trigger with each other. The receiving and transmitting of triggers is performed through the trigger interface.

### 12.1.9.1 QDSS_CTI5_CSCTI

The CTI allows mapping a trigger on the Trigger interface to a signal on the Channel interface and vice versa. The mapping is user-programmable. When the CTI receives a channel event it maps this onto a trigger output. This enables subsystems to cross trigger with each other. The receiving and transmitting of triggers is performed through the trigger interface.

### 0x00815FA0 QDSS_CTI5_CLAIMSET

* **Type:** RW
* **Reset State:** `0x0000000F`

This is used in conjunction with Claim Tag Clear Register, CLAIMCLR. This register forms one half of the Claim Tag value. This location allows individual bits to be set, write, and returns the number of bits that can be set, read.

| Bits | Name | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 3:0 | CLAIMSET_W | W | Each bit is considered separately: 0 = no effect, 1 = set this bit in the claim tag. |
| 3:0 | CLAIMSET_R | R | This claim tag bit is implemented<br>0xF: CLAIM_TAG_IMPLEMENTED_BITS (These bits are present within the claim tag field) |

### 0x00815FA4 QDSS_CTI5_CLAIMCLR

* **Type:** RW
* **Reset State:** `0x00000000`

This register is used in conjunction with Claim Tag Set Register, CLAIMSET. This register forms one half of the Claim Tag value. This location enables individual bits to be cleared, write, and returns the current Claim Tag value, read.

| Bits | Name | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 3:0 | CLAIMCLR_W | W | Each bit is considered separately: 0 = no effect, 1 = clear this bit in the claim tag. |
| 3:0 | CLAIMCLR_R | R | The value present reflects the current setting of the Claim Tag. |

| 1 | LOCKGRANT | Returns the current status of the Lock. This bit reads as 0 when read from an external debugger (PADDRDBG31 = 1) since external debugger accesses are not subject to Lock Registers.<br>0x0: ACCESS_PERMITTED (Write access is permitted to this device)<br>0x1: DEVICE_LOCKED (Write access to the component is blocked. All writes to control registers are ignored. Reads are permitted) |
| 0 | LOCKEXIST | Indicates that a lock control mechanism exists for this device. This bit reads as 0 when read from an external debugger (PADDRDBG31 = 1) since external debugger accesses are not subject to Lock Registers.<br>0x0: LOCK_NOT_PRESENT (No lock control mechanism exists, writes to the Lock Access register (0xFB0) will be ignored)<br>0x1: LOCK_PRESENT (Lock control mechanism is present) |

## 12.1.10 CTI6_CSCTI

The CTI allows mapping a trigger on the Trigger interface to a signal on the Channel interface and vice versa. The mapping is user-programmable. When the CTI receives a channel event it maps this onto a trigger output. This enables subsystems to cross trigger with each other. The receiving and transmitting of triggers is performed through the trigger interface.

<!-- page 2810 -->
### QDSS_CTI6_CLAIMSET
**Address:** `0x00816FA0`
**Type:** RW
**Reset State:** `0x0000000F`

This is used in conjunction with Claim Tag Clear Register, CLAIMCLR. This register forms one half of the Claim Tag value. This location allows individual bits to be set, write, and returns the number of bits that can be set, read.

| Bits | Name | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 3:0 | CLAIMSET_W | W | Each bit is considered separately:<br>0 = no effect<br>1 = set this bit in the claim tag. |
| 3:0 | CLAIMSET_R | R | This claim tag bit is implemented<br>0xF: CLAIM_TAG_IMPLEMENTED_BITS (These bits are present within the claim tag field) |

### QDSS_CTI6_CLAIMCLR
**Address:** `0x00816FA4`
**Type:** RW
**Reset State:** `0x00000000`

This register is used in conjunction with Claim Tag Set Register, CLAIMSET. This register forms one half of the Claim Tag value. This location enables individual bits to be cleared, write, and returns the current Claim Tag value, read.

| Bits | Name | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 3:0 | CLAIMCLR_W | W | Each bit is considered separately:<br>0 = no effect<br>1 = clear this bit in the claim tag. |
| 3:0 | CLAIMCLR_R | R | The value present reflects the current setting of the Claim Tag. |

### QDSS_CTI6_LAR

| Bits | Name | Description |

| 31:0 | ACCESS_W | A write of 0xC5ACCE55 enables further write access to this device. A write of any value other than 0xC5ACCE55 will have the affect of removing write access.<br>0xC5ACCE55: UNLOCK (Unlock the protection register to enable write access) |

### 0x00816FB4 QDSS_CTI6_LSR

* **Type**: R
* **Reset State**: 0x00000003

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 2 | LOCKTYPE | Indicates if the Lock Access Register (0xFB0) is implemented as 8-bit or 32-bit<br>0x0: ENUM_32_BIT (This component implements a 32-bit Lock Access Register) |
| 1 | LOCKGRANT | Returns the current status of the Lock. This bit reads as 0 when read from an external debugger (PADDRDBG31 = 1) since external debugger accesses are not subject to Lock Registers.<br>0x0: ACCESS_PERMITTED (Write access is permitted to this device)<br>0x1: DEVICE_LOCKED (Write access to the component is blocked. All writes to control registers are ignored. Reads are permitted) |
| 0 | LOCKEXIST | Indicates that a lock control mechanism exists for this device. This bit reads as 0 when read from an external debugger (PADDRDBG31 = 1) since external debugger accesses are not subject to Lock Registers.<br>0x0: LOCK_NOT_PRESENT (No lock control mechanism exists, writes to the Lock Access register (0xFB0) will be ignored)<br>0x1: LOCK_PRESENT (Lock control mechanism is present) |

### 0x00816FEC QDSS_CTI6_PERIPHID3

* **Type**: R
* **Reset State**: 0x00000000

Part of the set of Peripheral Identification registers. Contains the RevAnd and Customer Modified fields.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 7:4 | REVAND | This field indicates minor errata fixes specific to this design, for example metal fixes after implementation. In most cases this field is zero. It is recommended that component designers ensure this field can be changed by a metal fix if required, for example by driving it from registers that reset to zero.<br>0x0: NO_MODIFICATION (Indicates that there have been no metal fixes to this component) |
| 3:0 | CMOD | Where the component is reusable IP, this value indicates if the customer has modified the behavior of the component. In most cases this field is zero.<br>0x0: NO_MODIFICATION (Indicates that there have been no modifications made) |

If a component only requires the standard 4KB then this should read as 0x0, 4KB only, for 8KB set to 0x1, 16KB == 0x2, 32KB == 0x3, and so on.<br>0x0: ENUM_4KB (Indicates that the device only occupies 4kB of memory) |

## 12.1.11 CTI7_CSCTI

The CTI allows mapping a trigger on the Trigger interface to a signal on the Channel interface and vice versa. The mapping is user-programmable. When the CTI receives a channel event it maps this onto a trigger output. This enables subsystems to cross trigger with each other. The receiving and transmitting of triggers is performed through the trigger interface.

### 12.1.11.1 QDSS_CTI7_CSCTI

The CTI allows mapping a trigger on the Trigger interface to a signal on the Channel interface and vice versa. The mapping is user-programmable. When the CTI receives a channel event it maps this onto a trigger output. This enables subsystems to cross trigger with each other. The receiving and transmitting of triggers is performed through the trigger interface.

### 0x00817FA0 QDSS_CTI7_CLAIMSET

**Type**: RW
**Reset State**: 0x0000000F

This is used in conjunction with Claim Tag Clear Register, CLAIMCLR. This register forms one half of the Claim Tag value. This location allows individual bits to be set, write, and returns the number of bits that can be set, read.

| Bits | Name | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 3:0 | CLAIMSET_W | W | Each bit is considered separately: 0 = no effect, 1 = set this bit in the claim tag. |
| 3:0 | CLAIMSET_R | R | This claim tag bit is implemented.<br>0xF: CLAIM_TAG_IMPLEMENTED_BITS (These bits are present within the claim tag field) |

### 0x00817FA4 QDSS_CTI7_CLAIMCLR

**Type**: RW
**Reset State**: 0x00000000

This register is used in conjunction with Claim Tag Set Register, CLAIMSET. This register forms one half of the Claim Tag value. This location enables individual bits to be cleared, write, and returns the current Claim Tag value, read.

| Bits | Name | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 3:0 | CLAIMCLR_W | W | Each bit is considered separately: 0 = no effect, 1 = clear this bit in the claim tag. |
| 3:0 | CLAIMCLR_R | R | The value present reflects the current setting of the Claim Tag. |

### 0x00817FB0 QDSS_CTI7_LAR

**Type**: W
**Reset State**: Undefined
<!-- page 2828 -->
### QDSS_CTI7_LAR

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:0 | ACCESS_W | A write of 0xC5ACCE55 enables further write access to this device. A write of any value other than 0xC5ACCE55 will have the affect of removing write access.<br>0xC5ACCE55: UNLOCK (Unlock the protection register to enable write access) |

### 0x00817FB4 QDSS_CTI7_LSR

**Type**: R
**Reset State**: 0x00000003

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 2 | LOCKTYPE | Indicates if the Lock Access Register (0xFB0) is implemented as 8-bit or 32-bit.<br>0x0: ENUM_32_BIT (This component implements a 32-bit Lock Access Register) |
| 1 | LOCKGRANT | Returns the current status of the Lock. This bit reads as 0 when read from an external debugger (PADDRDBG31 = 1) since external debugger accesses are not subject to Lock Registers.<br>0x0: ACCESS_PERMITTED (Write access is permitted to this device)<br>0x1: DEVICE_LOCKED (Write access to the component is blocked. All writes to control registers are ignored. Reads are permitted) |
| 0 | LOCKEXIST | Indicates that a lock control mechanism exists for this device. This bit reads as 0 when read from an external debugger (PADDRDBG31 = 1) since external debugger accesses are not subject to Lock Registers.<br>0x0: LOCK_NOT_PRESENT (No lock control mechanism exists, writes to the Lock Access register (0xFB0) will be ignored)<br>0x1: LOCK_PRESENT (Lock control mechanism is present) |

### 0x00817FEC QDSS_CTI7_PERIPHID3

**Type:** R
**Reset State:** 0x00000000

Part of the set of Peripheral Identification registers. Contains the RevAnd and Customer Modified fields.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 7:4 | REVAND | This field indicates minor errata fixes specific to this design, for example metal fixes after implementation. In most cases this field is zero. It is recommended that component designers ensure this field can be changed by a metal fix if required, for example by driving it from registers that reset to zero.<br>0x0: NO_MODIFICATION (Indicates that there have been no metal fixes to this component) |
| 3:0 | CMOD | Where the component is reusable IP, this value indicates if the customer has modified the behavior of the component. In most cases this field is zero.<br>0x0: NO_MODIFICATION (Indicates that there have been no modifications made) |

**Reset State:** 0x00000004

### QDSS_CTI7_PERIPHID4 (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 7:4 | SIZE | This is a 4-bit value that indicates the total contiguous size of the memory window used by this component in powers of 2 from the standard 4KB. If a component only requires the standard 4KB then this should read as 0x0, 4KB only, for 8KB set to 0x1, 16KB == 0x2, 32KB == 0x3, and so on.<br>0x0: ENUM_4KB (Indicates that the device only occupies 4kB of memory) |
| 3:0 | DES_2 | JEDEC continuation code indicating the designer of the component (along with the identity code)<br>0x4: ARM_JEP106_CONTINUATION_CODE (Indicates that ARM's JEDEC identity code is on the 5th bank) |

## 12.1.12 CTI8_CSCTI

The CTI allows mapping a trigger on the Trigger interface to a signal on the Channel interface and vice versa. The mapping is user-programmable. When the CTI receives a channel event it maps this onto a trigger output. This enables subsystems to cross trigger with each other. The receiving and transmitting of triggers is performed through the trigger interface.

### 12.1.12.1 QDSS_CTI8_CSCTI

The CTI allows mapping a trigger on the Trigger interface to a signal on the Channel interface and vice versa. The mapping is user-programmable. When the CTI receives a channel event it maps this onto a trigger output. This enables subsystems to cross trigger with each other. The receiving and transmitting of triggers is performed through the trigger interface.

### QDSS_CTI8_CLAIMSET

* **Address:** 0x00818FA0
* **Type:** RW
* **Reset State:** 0x0000000F

This is used in conjunction with Claim Tag Clear Register, CLAIMCLR. This register forms one half of the Claim Tag value. This location allows individual bits to be set, write, and returns the number of bits that can be set, read.

| Bits | Name | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 3:0 | CLAIMSET_W | W | Each bit is considered separately: 0 = no effect, 1 = set this bit in the claim tag. |
| 3:0 | CLAIMSET_R | R | This claim tag bit is implemented.<br>0xF: CLAIM_TAG_IMPLEMENTED_BITS (These bits are present within the claim tag field) |

### QDSS_CTI8_CLAIMCLR

* **Address:** 0x00818FA4
* **Type:** RW
* **Reset State:** 0x00000000

This register is used in conjunction with Claim Tag Set Register, CLAIMSET. This register forms one half of the Claim Tag value. This location enables individual bits to be cleared, write, and returns the current Claim Tag value, read.

| Bits | Name | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 3:0 | CLAIMCLR_W | W | Each bit is considered separately: 0 = no effect, 1 = clear this bit in the claim tag. |
| 3:0 | CLAIMCLR_R | R | The value present reflects the current setting of the Claim Tag. |

## 12.1.13 CSTPIU_CSTPIU

The TPIU acts as a bridge between the on-chip trace data, with separate IDs, to a data stream, encapsulating IDs where required, that is then captured by a Trace Port Analyzer (TPA). The internal formatter inserts source ID signals into the data packet stream so that trace data can be re-associated with its trace source. It contains an Asynchronous FIFO that enables trace data to be driven out at a speed that is not dependent on the on-chip bus clock. The internal trace-out block serializes formatted data before it goes off-chip. The TPIU includes a pattern generator unit that provides a simple set of defined bit sequences or patterns that can be output over the Trace Port and be detected by the TPA or other associated Trace Capture Device (TCD). The TCD can use these patterns to indicate if it is possible to increase or to decrease the trace port clock speed.

## 12.1.14 IN_FUN0_CXATBFUNNEL_128W8SP

The Funnel is used when there is more than one trace source.

### 12.1.14.1 QDSS_IN_FUN0_CXATBFUNNEL_128W8SP

The Funnel is used when there is more than one trace source.

### 0x00821000 QDSS_IN_FUN0_CTRL_REG

* **Type**: RW
* **Reset State**: 0x00000300

The Funnel Control Register enables the slave ports and defines the hold time of the slave ports. Hold time refers to the number of transactions that are output on the funnel master port from the same slave while that slave port atvalidsx is HIGH. Hold time does not refer to clock cycles in this context
<!-- page 2869 -->

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 11:8 | HT | The formatting scheme can easily become inefficient if fast switching occurs, so, where possible, this must be minimized. If a source has nothing to transmit, then another source is selected irrespective of the minimum number of transactions.<br>The maximum value that can be entered is 0xE and this equates to 15 cycles.<br>0xF is reserved.<br>0x0: HOLD_TIME_1 (1 transactions hold time)<br>0x1: HOLD_TIME_2 (2 transactions hold time)<br>0x2: HOLD_TIME_3 (3 transactions hold time)<br>0x3: HOLD_TIME_4 (4 transactions hold time)<br>0x4: HOLD_TIME_5 (5 transactions hold time)<br>0x5: HOLD_TIME_6 (6 transactions hold time)<br>0x6: HOLD_TIME_7 (7 transactions hold time)<br>0x7: HOLD_TIME_8 (8 transactions hold time)<br>0x8: HOLD_TIME_9 (9 transactions hold time)<br>0x9: HOLD_TIME_10 (10 transactions hold time)<br>0xA: HOLD_TIME_11 (11 transactions hold time)<br>0xB: HOLD_TIME_12 (12 transactions hold time)<br>0xC: HOLD_TIME_13 (13 transactions hold time)<br>0xD: HOLD_TIME_14 (14 transactions hold time)<br>0xE: HOLD_TIME_15 (15 transactions hold time) |
| 7 | ENS7 | Setting this bit enables this input, or slave, port. If the bit is not set then this has the effect of excluding the port from the priority selection scheme. The reset value is all clear, that is, all ports disabled.<br>0x1: ENABLE (Slave port enabled)<br>0x0: DISABLE (Slave port disabled) |

### 0x00821004 QDSS_IN_FUN0_PRIORITY_CTRL_REG

* **Type**: RW
* **Reset State**: 0x00000000

The Priority Control Register defines the order in which inputs are selected. Each 3-bit field represents a priority for each particular slave interface. Location 0 has the priority value for the first slave port. Location 1 is the priority value for the second slave port, Location 2 is the third, down to location 7, which has the priority value of the eighth slave port. Values represent the priority value for each port number. If you want to give highest priority to a particular slave port, the corresponding port must be programmed with the lowest value. Typically this is likely to be a port that has more important data or that has a small FIFO and is therefore likely to overflow.

If you want to give lowest priority to a particular slave port, the corresponding slave port must be programmed with the highest value. Typically this is likely to be a device that has a large FIFO that is less likely to overflow or a source that has information that is of lower importance.


<!-- page 2871 -->

| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 23:21 | PRIPORT7 | Priority value of the eighth port. The value written into this location is the value that you want to assign the eighth slave port. If a priority value has been entered for multiple different slave ports then the arbitration logic selects the lowest port number of them.<br>0x0: PRORITY_LEVEL_0 (This value represents the highest priority.)<br>0x1: PRORITY_LEVEL_1 (2nd highest priority)<br>0x2: PRORITY_LEVEL_2 (3rd highest priority)<br>0x3: PRORITY_LEVEL_3 (4th highest priority)<br>0x4: PRORITY_LEVEL_4 (5th highest priority)<br>0x5: PRORITY_LEVEL_5 (6th highest priority)<br>0x6: PRORITY_LEVEL_6 (7th highest priority)<br>0x7: PRORITY_LEVEL_7 (This value represents the lowest priority.) |

### QDSS_IN_FUN0_ITCTRL

**Address:** `0x00821F00`  
**Type:** `RW`  
**Reset State:** `0x00000000`  

This register is used to enable topology detection. This register enables the component to switch from a functional mode, the default behavior, to integration mode where the inputs and outputs of the component can be directly controlled for the purpose of integration testing and topology solving.

> [!NOTE]  
> When a device has been in integration mode, it might not function with the original behavior. After performing integration or topology detection, you must reset the system to ensure correct behavior of CoreSight and other connected system components that are affected by the integration or topology detection.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 0 | INTEGRATION_MODE | Allows the component to switch from functional mode to integration mode or back. If no integration functionality is implemented, this register must read as zero.<br>0x1: INTEGRATION_MODE (Enable integration mode)<br>0x0: FUNCTIONAL_MODE (Disable integration mode) |

---

### QDSS_IN_FUN0_CLAIMSET

**Address:** `0x00821FA0`  
**Type:** `RW`  
**Reset State:** `0x0000000F`  
<!-- page 2874 -->

### QDSS_IN_FUN0_CLAIMSET (continued)

This is used in conjunction with Claim Tag Clear Register, CLAIMCLR. This register forms one half of the Claim Tag value. This location allows individual bits to be set, write, and returns the number of bits that can be set, read.

| Bits | Name | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 3:0 | CLAIMSET_W | W | Each bit is considered separately: 0 = no effect, 1 = set this bit in the claim tag. |
| 3:0 | CLAIMSET_R | R | This claim tag bit is implemented.<br>0xF: CLAIM_TAG_IMPLEMENTED_BITS (These bits are present within the claim tag field) |

---

### QDSS_IN_FUN0_CLAIMCLR

**Address:** `0x00821FA4`  
**Type:** `RW`  
**Reset State:** `0x00000000`  

This register is used in conjunction with Claim Tag Set Register, CLAIMSET. This register forms one half of the Claim Tag value. This location enables individual bits to be cleared, write, and returns the current Claim Tag value, read.

| Bits | Name | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 3:0 | CLAIMCLR_W | W | Each bit is considered separately: 0 = no effect, 1 = clear this bit in the claim tag. |
| 3:0 | CLAIMCLR_R | R | The value present reflects the current setting of the Claim Tag. |

**Address:** `0x00821FEC`  
**Type:** `R`  
**Reset State:** `0x00000000`

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 7:4 | REVAND | This field indicates minor errata fixes specific to this design, for example metal fixes after implementation. In most cases this field is zero. It is recommended that component designers ensure this field can be changed by a metal fix if required, for example by driving it from registers that reset to zero.<br>0x0: NO_MODS (Indicates that there have been no metal fixes to this component) |
| 3:0 | CUSTOMER_MODIFIED | Where the component is reusable IP, this value indicates if the customer has modified the behavior of the component. In most cases this field is zero.<br>0x0: NO_MODS (Indicates that there have been no modifications made) |

## QDSS_REPL64_ITATBCTR0

* **Address:** `0x00824EFC`
* **Type:** W
* **Reset State:** Undefined

Controls the value of the ATVALIDM0, ATVALIDM1 and ATREADYS outputs in integration mode.

### QDSS_REPL64_ITATBCTR0 Bits
| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 4 | ATREADYS_W | Sets the value of the ATREADYS output:<br>0x1: HIGH (Drive logic 1 on the ATREADYS output.)<br>0x0: LOW (Drive logic 0 on the ATREADYS output.) |
| 2 | ATVALIDM1_W | Sets the value of the ATVALIDM1 output:<br>0x1: HIGH (Drive logic 1 on the ATVALIDM1 output.)<br>0x0: LOW (Drive logic 0 on the ATVALIDM1 output.) |
| 0 | ATVALIDM0_W | Sets the value of the ATVALIDM0 output:<br>0x1: HIGH (Drive logic 1 on the ATVALIDM0 output.)<br>0x0: LOW (Drive logic 0 on the ATVALIDM0 output.) |

## QDSS_REPL64_ITATBCTR1

* **Address:** `0x00824EF8`
* **Type:** R
* **Reset State:** Undefined

Returns the value of the ATREADYM0, ATREADYM1 and ATVALIDS inputs in integration mode.

### QDSS_REPL64_ITATBCTR1 Bits
| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 3 | ATVALIDS_R | Reads the value of the ATVALIDS input:<br>0x1: HIGH (Pin is at logic 1.)<br>0x0: LOW (Pin is at logic 0.) |
| 1 | ATREADYM1_R | Reads the value of the ATREADYM1 input:<br>0x1: HIGH (Pin is at logic 1.)<br>0x0: LOW (Pin is at logic 0.) |
| 0 | ATREADYM0_R | Reads the value of the ATREADYM0 input:<br>0x1: HIGH (Pin is at logic 1.)<br>0x0: LOW (Pin is at logic 0.) |

### QDSS_ETFETB_FFSR (0x00825300)

* **Type**: R
* **Reset State**: 0x00000002

This register indicates the status of the Formatter and the status of Flush request.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---------- |
| 1 | FTSTOPPED | Formatter stopped status.<br/>0x0: LOW (Trace capture has not yet completed.)<br/>0x1: HIGH (Trace capture has been completed and all captured trace data has been written to the trace memory.) |
| 0 | RESERVED | Reserved |

### QDSS_ETFETB_FFCR (0x00825304)

* **Type**: RW
* **Reset State**: 0x00000000

| Bits | Name | Access Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---------- | :---------- |
| 14 | RESERVED | W | Reserved |
| 13 | STOPONTRIGEVT | RW | Stop formatting on trigger event.<br/>0x0: LOW (Formatting is not stopped when trigger event is observed.)<br/>0x1: HIGH (Formatting is stopped when trigger event is observed.) |
| 12 | STOPONFL | RW | Stop formatting on flush completed.<br/>0x0: LOW (Formatting is not stopped when FLUSH is completed.)<br/>0x1: HIGH (Formatting is stopped when FLUSH is completed. Any part-completed packets are drained off into the trace memory with a post-amble.) |
<!-- page 2894 -->

### QDSS_ETFETB_FFCR (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Access Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---------- | :---------- |
| 10 | TRIGONFL | RW | 0x0: LOW (A trigger is not indicated on the trace stream when AFREADYS is returned HIGH.)<br/>0x1: HIGH (A trigger is indicated on the trace stream when AFREADYS is returned HIGH.) |
| 9 | TRIGONTRIGEVT | RW | 0x0: LOW (A trigger is not indicated on the trace stream when a Trigger Event occurs.)<br/>0x1: HIGH (A trigger is indicated on the trace stream when a Trigger event occurs.) |
| 8 | TRIGONTRIGIN | RW | 0x0: LOW (A trigger is not indicated on the trace stream when a rising edge is detected on the TRIGIN input.)<br/>0x1: HIGH (A trigger is indicated on the trace stream when a rising edge is detected on the TRIGIN input.) |
| 6 | FLUSHMAN_R | R | Manually generate a flush of the system. Setting this bit causes a flush to be generated. If TraceCaptEn bit in CTL register is 0, then writes to this bit are ignored. In Circular buffer mode and Hardware-FIFO mode, this bit is cleared automatically when AFREADYS is sampled HIGH. In Software-FIFO mode, this bit is cleared when the flush data is written to trace memory. This bit is clear on reset.<br/>0x0: LOW (Manual Flush is not initiated)<br/>0x1: HIGH (Manual Flush is initiated) |
| 6 | FLUSHMAN_W | W | Manually generate a flush of the system. Setting this bit causes a flush to be generated. If TraceCaptEn bit in CTL register is 0, then writes to this bit are ignored. In Circular buffer mode and Hardware-FIFO mode, this bit is cleared automatically when AFREADYS is sampled HIGH. In Software-FIFO mode, this bit is cleared when the flush data is written to trace memory. This bit is clear on reset.<br/>0x0: LOW (Manual Flush is not initiated)<br/>0x1: HIGH (Manual Flush is initiated) |
| 5 | FONTRIGEVT | RW | 0x0: LOW (Flush-on-trigger-event disabled)<br/>0x1: HIGH (Flush-on-trigger-event enabled) |
| 4 | FONFLIN | RW | Setting this bit enables the detection of transitions on the FLUSHIN input by the TMC. If this bit is set and the Formatter has not already stopped, a rising edge on FLUSHIN initiates a flush request. This bit is clear on reset.<br/>0x0: LOW (Flush-on-FLUSHIN feature is disabled)<br/>0x1: HIGH (Flush-on-FLUSHIN feature is enabled) |
<!-- page 2895 -->

### QDSS_ETFETB_FFCR (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Access Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---------- | :---------- |
| 1 | ENTI | RW | Enable trigger insertion.<br/>Setting this bit enables the insertion of triggers in the formatted trace stream. A trigger is indicated by inserting one byte of data 8'h00 with ATID 7'h7D in the trace stream. Trigger indication on the trace stream is additionally controlled by the register bits TrigOnFl, TrigOnTrigEvt and TrigOnTrigIn in the FFCR register, 0x304. This bit can only be changed when TMCReady=1 and TraceCaptEn=0. This bit takes effect only when the EnFt register bit in this register is set. If EnTI bit is set to 1 when EnFt is 0, it results in formatting being enabled. This bit is clear on reset.<br/>0x0: TRIGGER_INSERTION_DISABLED (Triggers are not embedded into the formatted strace stream)<br/>0x1: TRIGGER_INSERTION_ENABLED (Embed triggers into formatted trace stream) |
| 0 | ENFT | RW | Enable formatting.<br/>0x0: LOW (Formatting disabled.)<br/>0x1: HIGH (Formatting enabled) |

### QDSS_ETFETB_CLAIMSET (0x00825FA0)

* **Type**: RW
* **Reset State**: 0x0000000F




<!-- page 2901 -->

This is used in conjunction with Claim Tag Clear Register, CLAIMCLR. This register forms one half of the Claim Tag value. This location allows individual bits to be set, write, and returns the number of bits that can be set, read.

### QDSS_ETFETB_CLAIMSET

| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 3:0 | CLAIMSET_W | W | Each bit is considered separately: 0 = no effect, 1 = set this bit in the claim tag. |
| 3:0 | CLAIMSET_R | R | This claim tag bit is implemented<br>0xF: CLAIM_TAG_IMPLEMENTED_BITS (These bits are present within the claim tag field) |

### 0x00825FA4 QDSS_ETFETB_CLAIMCLR

**Type:** RW  
**Reset State:** 0x00000000  

This register is used in conjunction with Claim Tag Set Register, CLAIMSET. This register forms one half of the Claim Tag value. This location enables individual bits to be cleared, write, and returns the current Claim Tag value, read.
