### 0x00826110 QDSS_ETR_AXICTL

* **Type**: RW
* **Reset State**: 0x00000000

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 11:8 | WRBURSTLEN | |
| 7 | SCATTERGATHERMODE | This bit indicates whether trace memory is accessed as a single buffer in system memory or as a linked-list based scatter-gather memory. This is ignored when the TMC is in Disabled state (TraceCaptEn=0 and TMCReady=1).<br>0x0: SINGLE_BUFFER (Trace memory is a single contiguous block of system memory)<br>0x1: SCATTER_GATHER (Trace memory is spread over multiple blocks of system memory based on a linked-list mechanism.) |
| 5 | CACHECTRLBIT3 | This bit controls the value driven on the ARCACHEM[3]/AWCACHEM[3] signal on the AXI interface when performing AXI transfers. If CacheCtrlBit1 is 0, then this bit must also be 0 to comply with AXI protocol. Setting this bit to 1 when the CacheCtrlBit1 is 0 will result in Unpredictable behavior.<br>0x0: DO_NOT_CACHE_ALLOCATE_ON_WRITES (Do not cache allocate on writes)<br>0x1: CACHE_ALLOCATE_ON_WRITES (If the transfer is a write and it misses in the cache then it should be allocated.) |
| 4 | CACHECTRLBIT2 | This bit controls the value driven on the ARCACHEM[2]/AWCACHEM[2] signal on the AXI interface when performing AXI transfers. If CacheCtrlBit1 is 0, then this bit must also be 0 to comply with AXI protocol. Setting this bit to 1 when the CacheCtrlBit1 is 0 will result in Unpredictable behavior.<br>0x0: DO_NOT_CACHE_ALLOCATE_ON_READS (Do not cache allocate on reads)<br>0x1: CACHE_ALLOCATE_ON_READS (If the transfer is a read and it misses in the cache then it should be allocated.) |
<!-- page 2913 -->

### QDSS_ETR_AXICTL (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 3 | CACHECTRLBIT1 | This bit controls the value driven on the ARCACHEM[1]/AWCACHEM[1] signal on the AXI interface when performing AXI transfers.<br>0x0: NON_CACHEABLE (Non-cacheable)<br>0x1: CACHEABLE (Cacheable. The transaction at the final destination does not have to match the characteristics of the original transaction. For reads this means that a location can be pre-fetched or can be fetched just once for multiple read transactions. For writes this means that a number of different writes can be merged together. To determine if a transaction should be cached this bit should be used in conjunction with the Read Allocate (RA) and Write Allocate (WA) bits.) |
| 2 | CACHECTRLBIT0 | This bit controls the value driven on the ARCACHEM[0]/AWCACHEM[0] signal on the AXI interface when performing AXI transfers.<br>0x0: NON_BUFFERABLE (Non-bufferable)<br>0x1: BUFFERABLE (Bufferable) |
| 1 | PROTCTRLBIT1 | 0x0: SECURE_ACCESS (Secure access)<br>0x1: NON_SECURE_ACCESS (Non-secure access) |
| 0 | PROTCTRLBIT0 | 0x0: NORMAL_ACCESS (Normal access)<br>0x1: PRIVILEGED_ACCESS (Privileged access. A privileged processing mode might have a greater level of access within a system.) |

* **Type**: RW
* **Reset State**: 0x00000000

| Bits | Name | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 13 | STOPONTRIGEVT | RW | 0x0: LOW (Formatting is not stopped when trigger event is observed.)<br>0x1: HIGH (Formatting is stopped when trigger event is observed.) |
| 12 | STOPONFL | RW | 0x0: LOW (Formatting is not stopped when FLUSH is completed.)<br>0x1: HIGH (Formatting is stopped when FLUSH is completed. Any part-completed packets are drained off into the trace memory with a post-amble.) |
| 10 | TRIGONFL | RW | 0x0: LOW (A trigger is not indicated on the trace stream when AFREADYS is returned HIGH.)<br>0x1: HIGH (A trigger is indicated on the trace stream when AFREADYS is returned HIGH.) |

### QDSS_ETR_FFCR (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 9 | TRIGONTRIGEVT | RW | 0x0: LOW (A trigger is not indicated on the trace stream when a Trigger Event occurs.)<br>0x1: HIGH (A trigger is indicated on the trace stream when a Trigger event occurs.) |
| 8 | TRIGONTRIGIN | RW | 0x0: LOW (A trigger is not indicated on the trace stream when a rising edge is detected on the TRIGIN input.)<br>0x1: HIGH (A trigger is indicated on the trace stream when a rising edge is detected on the TRIGIN input.) |
| 6 | FLUSHMAN_R | R | Manually generate a flush of the system. Setting this bit causes a flush to be generated. If TraceCaptEn bit in CTL register is 0, then writes to this bit are ignored. In Circular buffer mode and Hardware-FIFO mode, this bit is cleared automatically when AFREADYS is sampled HIGH. In Software-FIFO mode, this bit is cleared when the flush data is written to trace memory. This bit is clear on reset.<br>0x0: LOW (Manual Flush is not initiated)<br>0x1: HIGH (Manual Flush is initiated) |
| 6 | FLUSHMAN_W | W | Manually generate a flush of the system. Setting this bit causes a flush to be generated. If TraceCaptEn bit in CTL register is 0, then writes to this bit are ignored. In Circular buffer mode and Hardware-FIFO mode, this bit is cleared automatically when AFREADYS is sampled HIGH. In Software-FIFO mode, this bit is cleared when the flush data is written to trace memory. This bit is clear on reset.<br>0x0: LOW (Manual Flush is not initiated)<br>0x1: HIGH (Manual Flush is initiated) |
| 5 | FONTRIGEVT | RW | 0x0: LOW (Flush-on-trigger-event disabled)<br>0x1: HIGH (Flush-on-trigger-event enabled) |
| 4 | FONFLIN | RW | Setting this bit enables the detection of transitions on the FLUSHIN input by the TMC. If this bit is set and the Formatter has not already stopped, a rising edge on FLUSHIN initiates a flush request. This bit is clear on reset.<br>0x0: LOW (Flush-on-FLUSHIN feature is disabled)<br>0x1: HIGH (Flush-on-FLUSHIN feature is enabled) |
<!-- page 2916 -->

### QDSS_ETR_FFCR (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1 | ENTI | RW | Setting this bit enables the insertion of triggers in the formatted trace stream. A trigger is indicated by inserting one byte of data 8'h00 with ATID 7'h7D in the trace stream. Trigger indication on the trace stream is additionally controlled by the register bits TrigOnFl, TrigOnTrigEvt and TrigOnTrigIn in the FFCR register, 0x304. This bit can only be changed when TMCReady=1 and TraceCaptEn=0. This bit takes effect only when the EnFt register bit in this register is set. If EnTI bit is set to 1 when EnFt is 0, it results in formatting being enabled. This bit is clear on reset.<br>0x1: TRIGGER_INSERTION_ENABLED (Embed triggers into formatted trace stream)<br>0x0: TRIGGER_INSERTION_DISABLED (Triggers are not embedded into the formatted strace stream) |
| 0 | ENFT | RW | 0x1: HIGH (Formatting enabled)<br>0x0: LOW (Formatting disabled.) |

### 0x00826FA0 QDSS_ETR_CLAIMSET

* **Type**: RW

This is used in conjunction with Claim Tag Clear Register, CLAIMCLR. This register forms one half of the Claim Tag value. This location allows individual bits to be set, write, and returns the number of bits that can be set, read.

| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |

### 0x00826FA4 QDSS_ETR_CLAIMCLR

* **Type**: RW
* **Reset State**: 0x00000000

This register is used in conjunction with Claim Tag Set Register, CLAIMSET. This register forms one half of the Claim Tag value. This location enables individual bits to be cleared, write, and returns the current Claim Tag value, read.

| Bits | Name | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 3:0 | CLAIMCLR_W | W | Each bit is considered separately: 0 = no effect, 1 = clear this bit in the claim tag. |
| 3:0 | CLAIMCLR_R | R | The value present reflects the current setting of the Claim Tag. |

- **Type**: RW
- **Clock**: bam_clk

This Register holds the BAM Trusted configurations.

This register cannot be reset by any SW reset. Only HW reset applies.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 12:8 | RESERVED | Reserved |
| 7:3 | BAM_P_SUP_GROUP | Super-Group is the upper division of the pipes compared to the pipe-group division.<br>When any pipe locks or unlocks the BAM, all the pipes which are in a different super-group will NOT be affected. Only the pipes within the same super-group of the locker are affected.<br>Usually pipes which belongs to different peripherals which share the same BAM, would be in a different super-groups |

## QDSS_NDPBAM_BAM_BAM_P_TRUST_REGn (continued)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 2:0 | BAM_P_EE | This Field Indicates the EE # (0-7) to which the Pipe Interrupt belongs to. The BAM interrupt will fire to the EE # set at BAM_P_TRUST_REGn registers.<br>The number of supported EEs is reflect in the NUM_EES field in the BAM_REVISION register.<br>3'b000 - EE0<br>3'b001 - EE1<br>3'b010 - EE2<br>3'b011 - EE3<br>3'b100 - EE4<br>3'b101 - EE5<br>3'b110 - EE6<br>3'b111 - EE7 |

### 0x00887000 + 4096*n QDSS_NDPBAM_BAM_BAM_IRQ_SRCS_EEn, n=[0..7]

- **Type**: R
- **Clock**: bam_clk
- **Reset State**: 0x00000000

This Interrupt Status Register provides a single interrupt bit per each pipe in the BAM and a single bit for the BAM (not pipe related) interrupt. This register is read only and provides fast indication for the software to decide which pipe triggered the interrupt. After checking this register, SW reads the BAM_P_IRQ_STTSn register for the pipe interrupt reason and BAM_IRQ_STTS for the BAM interrupt reason.

This register has an alias - BAM_IRQ_SRCS register.

Registers with n=[1..7] exist only when the BAM supports multiple EEs (NUM_EES field in the BAM_REVISION register).

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31 | BAM_IRQ | BAM Global interrupt |
| 30:0 | P_IRQ | An interrupt bit per each pipe in the BAM. |

### 0x00887004 + 4096*n QDSS_NDPBAM_BAM_BAM_IRQ_SRCS_MSK_EEn, n=[0..7]

- **Type**: RW
- **Clock**: bam_clk
- **Reset State**: 0x00000000
<!-- page 2929 -->
## QDSS_NDPBAM_BAM_BAM_IRQ_SRCS_MSK_EEn (continued)

Interrupt Sources Mask register allows to mask the interrupts by their source, whether BAM or a specific pipe.

This register has an alias - BAM_IRQ_SRCS_MSK register.

Registers with n=[1..7] exist only when the BAM supports multiple EEs (NUM_EES field in the BAM_REVISION register).

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31 | BAM_IRQ_MSK | BAM Global Interrupt Mask<br>0x1: ENABLE_BAM_INTERRUPT (Enable BAM interrupt)<br>0x0: DISABLE_BAM_INTERRUPT (Disable BAM interrupt) |
| 30:0 | P_IRQ_MSK | An Interrupt Mask bit per each pipe in the BAM.<br>0x1: ENABLE_PIPE_INTERRUPT (Enable Pipe interrupt)<br>0x0: DISABLE_PIPE_INTERRUPT (Disable Pipe interrupt) |

The reset value written above is true only if EE>0. For BAM_PIPE_ATTR_EE0 the default value is: Bits [MAX_PIPES-1:0] = 1, Bits [31: MAX_PIPES] = 0.

### 0x00897000 + 4096*n QDSS_NDPBAM_BAM_BAM_P_CTRLn, n=[0..30]

- **Type**: RW
- **Clock**: bam_clk
- **Reset State**: 0x00000000

Pipe Control register provides various controls for the pipe.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 20:16 | P_LOCK_GROUP | Pipe's lock group.<br>Upon a lock request on this pipe, all pipes related to different pipe group and different EE (see PIPE_TRUST_REG) will be locked. |
| 11 | P_WRITE_NWD | BAM-Lite feature.<br>Applicable to BAM2BAM producer pipes only.<br>When this bit is set for producer B2B pipe, NWD bit (bit number 28 in the second word of descriptor) will be written with EOT into the generated descriptor for the consumer usage.<br>This bit is not applicable in pipes belong to a Peripheral which uses messaging_only (e.g. USB2). |
| 10:9 | P_PREFETCH_LIMIT | Bam Lite feature<br>Selects the number of bytes to be prefetched by the Bam Lite, once a peripheral requests to read data from a pipe.<br>This feature is relevant for Consumer modes only.<br>2'b00 - 32 bytes at most (INCR8)<br>2'b01 - 16 bytes at most (INCR4)<br>2'b10 - 4 bytes at most (SINGLE)<br>Available in BAM-Lite only |


<!-- page 2931 -->
### QDSS_NDPBAM_BAM_BAM_P_CTRLn (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 8:7 | P_AUTO_EOB_SEL | Bam Lite feature.<br>Selects the number of bytes to be processed before creating End Of Block indication internally by the BAM. See P_AUTO_EOB.<br>Descriptors generated by this feature (bam to bam producer mode) will always be of the chosen size, unless an End Of Transfer, causes a smaller descriptor to be created.<br>2'b00 - 512 Bytes<br>2'b01 - 256 Bytes<br>2'b10 - 128 Bytes<br>2'b11 - 64 Bytes<br>Available in BAM-Lite only |
| 6 | P_AUTO_EOB | BAM Lite feature.<br>When Enabled, the BAM Lite will ignore any incoming End Of Block indications from the peripheral (if any). Instead, the BAM Lite will generate it's own End Of Block indications internally, every P_AUTO_EOB_SEL bytes.<br>This feature is relevant for Producer Bam 2 Bam modes only.<br>It is a must for peripherals which are not able to produce End Of Block indications.<br>1'b1 - Enable<br>1'b0 - Disable<br>Available in BAM-Lite only |
| 5 | P_SYS_MODE | This bit sets the pipe to work in System Mode, where the Software is the second side of the pipe.<br>1'b1 - System mode.<br>1'b0 - BAM to BAM mode. |
| 4 | P_SYS_STRM | Streaming Enable. Relevant to System Producer BAM mode only. When enabled, BAM will not close descriptors with End Of Transfer notifications received from peripheral, but continue writing the data to the same descriptor.<br>1'b1 - Enable Streaming Mode<br>1'b0 - None-Streaming Mode.<br>This field is NOT supported in BAM-NDP (i.e. no streaming mode in NDP). |
| 3 | P_DIRECTION | This bit denotes pipe direction.<br>1'b1 - The pipe can be written (producer mode)<br>1'b0 - The pipe can be read (consumer mode) |
| 1 | P_EN | 1'b1 - Enable Pipe<br>1'b0 - Disable Pipe |
<!-- page 2932 -->
## QDSS_NDPBAM_BAM_BAM_P_RSTn, n=[0..30]

**Address:** `0x00897004 + 4096 * n`  
**Type:** `W`  
**Clock:** `bam_clk`  
**Reset State:** `0x00000000`  

Pipe Reset register provides Pipe Reset ability. Software needs to write 1 to this register to make the Pipe Reset. Writing 0 to this register will finish the Pipe Reset. Writing zero is needed prior to Peripheral reconfiguration for the same pipe.

*Note:* Software can invoke pipe reset only after it make sure that the pipe is 'quiet'. ('quiet' - No data transaction or command-descriptor is active at the time.)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 0 | P_SW_RST | This resets the pipe and it's registers, (Both Flip-Flops and RAM).<br>Software can invoke pipe reset only after it make sure that the pipe is 'quiet'.<br>1'b1 - Reset<br>1'b0 - Do Nothing |

## QDSS_NDPBAM_BAM_BAM_P_HALTn, n=[0..30]

**Address:** `0x00897008 + 4096 * n`  
**Type:** `RW`  
**Clock:** `bam_clk`  
**Reset State:** `0x00000000`  

Pipe Halt register Enables/Disables the Halt Sequence. Refer to the Software Procedures chapter for the Halt Sequence Procedure.

This is a self-modifying register.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1 | P_PROD_HALTED | This bit is used to inform the Consumer about the Producer being in Halt mode now. This is a part of the Halt procedure. See the Software Procedures chapter.<br>1'b1 - Sets this bit to 1<br>1'b0 - Does Nothing<br>This bit will be cleared by the HW. |
<!-- page 2933 -->
### QDSS_NDPBAM_BAM_BAM_P_HALTn (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 0 | P_HALT | When Enabled, the Pipe will enter Halt Mode.<br>1'b1 - Enable Halt<br>1'b0 - Disable Halt<br>For B2B Producer pipes, this bit is self modifying. It doesn't need the SW to clear it. See the Software Procedure chapter for the detailed flow. |

## QDSS_NDPBAM_BAM_BAM_P_IRQ_STTSn, n=[0..30]

**Address:** `0x00897010 + 4096 * n`  
**Type:** `R`  
**Clock:** `bam_clk`  
**Reset State:** `0x00000000`

| 5 | P_TRNSFR_END_IRQ | For producer this interrupt happens whenever the last AHB burst of a transfer happens. For Consumer when `ack_on_success` closes a transfer. |
| 4 | P_ERR_IRQ | Pipe Error interrupt indicates that an error has happened.<br>TBD: Error reason is not yet defined. Interrupt not in use. |
| 3 | P_OUT_OF_DESC_IRQ | Out of descriptors interrupt has several meanings depending on the operation mode:<br>Producer - no free space in the descriptors fifo for adding a descriptor<br>Consumer - no descriptors in the descriptors fifo for processing<br>IO Vectors Producer - No descriptors to read (and therefore no space for data to write to the pipe)<br>IO Vectors Consumer - No descriptors to read (and therefore no data to read from pipe) |

## QDSS_NDPBAM_BAM_BAM_P_TIMER_CTRLn, n=[0..30]

**Address:** `0x00897020 + 4096 * n`  
**Type:** `RW`  
**Clock:** `bam_clk`  
**Reset State:** `0x00000000`  

This register sets various controls and the threshold of the inactivity for interrupt triggering after long idle time.

The resolution of the pipe inactivity timers are in units set by a common counter. This common counter is controlled by a PARAMETER value of the BAM, and uses a separate clock, the `inactivity_timers_clk`. This clock can be slower than the `bam_clk`. The intent of the design is to use the `sleep_clk`, which is an always on 32kHz clock. This allows the `bam_clk` to be turned-off, while the base counter keeps counting. The width of this counter, as well of the rollover value are set using BAM PARAMETER. These values, taking the `inactivity_timers_clk` frequency define the pulse frequency that the base counter gives, and the threshold value can be calculated and set to interrupt after a specific time, regardless of the `bam_clk` frequency, and independent of clock power save features of the `bam_clk`. The timers continue counting even if the clock is turned off due to BAM dynamic hardware clock request voting.

The timer configuration is based on the `inactivity_timers_clk` period and the `INACTIVITY_TIMER_WIDTH` parameter constant. These parameters should be taken into account when setting this register. For example: for `inactivity_timer_clk` period of 1us and parameter is 3 and `P_TIMER_THRSHLD` is 10 will indicate the 2^3 * 1us * 10 which is 80us of inactivity in a pipe before sending an interrupt.
The general formula is: $2^{\text{INACTIVITY\_TIMER\_WIDTH}} \times \text{clock\_period} \times \text{P\_TIMER\_TRSHLD}$.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31 | P_TIMER_RST | To begin using the inactivity timer the SW should write the threshold and write 1 to this bit. Writing the value 0 will hold the timer reset until value 1 is written again. Then the timer will start down counting from the `P_TIMER_THRESOLD` value.<br>1'b1 - Active<br>1'b0 - Reset |
| 30 | P_TIMER_RUN | Will be used along with P_TIMER_MODE.<br>Not implemented at this time. Set to zero(0) |
| 29 | P_TIMER_MODE | Not implemented at this time. Set to zero(0) |
<!-- page 2937 -->
### QDSS_NDPBAM_BAM_BAM_P_TIMER_CTRLn (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 15:0 | P_TIMER_TRSHLD | Inactivity timer threshold for interrupt generation. |

## QDSS_NDPBAM_BAM_BAM_P_SW_OFSTSn, n=[0..30]

**Address:** `0x00897800 + 4096 * n`  
**Type:** `RW`  
**Clock:** `bam_clk`  
**Reset State:** `0x00000000`  

This register denotes the pointer Offset of the first Not Acknowledged Descriptor. Meaning all Descriptors prior to this one have been processed by the BAM. This register is only used by the Software. After receiving an interrupt, software reads this register in order to know what descriptors has been processed.

When the BAM works as Producer, Software will usually read this value after Descriptor Processed Interrupt or after the End of Transfer Interrupt.  
When the BAM works as Consumer, Software will usually read this value after Descriptor Processed Interrupt.

*NOTE:* This is non relevant in BAM to BAM modes.  
*NOTE:* Although being Writable, Software should never write to this register.  
*NOTE:* When using 2 pipes BAM, REVISION 0x03, this registers is Read Only.
<!-- page 2939 -->
### QDSS_NDPBAM_BAM_BAM_P_SW_OFSTSn (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:16 | SW_OFST_IN_DESC | Offset inside the Descriptor. This value is used by the Software only when a BAM is working as System Producer. Then the SW can read this value to know how many Bytes were written to the current descriptor if it was not closed down.<br>This is useful for Streaming mode.<br>This Field is NOT available in BAM-NDP |
| 15:0 | SW_DESC_OFST | Descriptor FIFO offset. |

## QDSS_NDPBAM_BAM_BAM_P_EVNT_REGn, n=[0..30]

**Address:** `0x00897818 + 4096 * n`  
**Type:** `RW`  
**Clock:** `bam_clk`  
**Reset State:** `0x00000000`  

This Register is where Read/Write events are sent to. If current BAM works as Producer, it will receive Read events into this register from the Consumer. If the Consumer is another BAM, it will write read events to this register. If the Consumer is the Software, it will prepare descriptors in the descriptor FIFO and update the DESC_FIFO_PEER_OFST value in this register.

If current BAM works as Consumer, opposite behavior is assumed.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:16 | P_BYTES_CONSUMED | This field is used only in the B2B mode.<br>It indicates the number of bits consumed by the Consumer.<br>Consumer sends this value to the Producer as a part of a read event, for the Producer to know how many bytes were consumed.<br>When working in System mode, this value should be set to zero.<br>BAM to BAM Producer writes zero in this value. |
| 15:0 | P_DESC_FIFO_PEER_OFST | This field indicates the Descriptor Fifo Offset Pointer of the Peer BAM (The BAM or the Software which creates descriptors).<br>For example when current BAM works as consumer for the current pipe, Producer BAM (or the software) updates this value to let the current pipe know about the new descriptors added in the Descriptor Fifo. |

### 0x00897828+ QDSS_NDPBAM_BAM_BAM_P_EVNT_GEN_TRSHLDn, n=[0..30]

**Address Formula:** `0x00897828 + 4096*n`
**Type:** RW
**Clock:** bam_clk
**Reset State:** 0x00000000

This register configures the threshold value for Read/Write event generation by the BAM towards another BAM. When aBAM pushes/pops this number of bytes to/from the pipe an event to the other BAM will be generated. A counter summing up the bytes pushed/popped is reset when event is issued, thus restarting count for the threshold.

Events are also issued after End Of Transfer received from the peripheral (Producer case), non regarding whether the pushed bytes count has reached the threshold or not.

This register is non relevant in System Modes.

BAM_P_EVNT_GEN_TRSHLDn, n=[0..30]

| :--- | :--- | :--- |

### SNOC_TPRB3_SPROF_MAINCTL

* **Address:** `0x00584C08`
* **Type:** RW
* **Reset State:** `0x00000000`

Register MainCtl contains probe global control bits. The register has seven bit fields:

| Bits | Name | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 7 | FILTBYTEALWAYSCHAINABLEEN | RW | When set to 0, Filter Byte / ByteEn Cnt will be connected to all statistics counters where odd Stat count are not chainable. When set to 1, Filter Byte / ByteEn Cnt will be connected only to chainable stat counter (even stat counter). |
| 6 | INTRUSIVEMODE | R | When set to 1, register field IntrusiveMode enables trace operation in Intrusive flow-control mode. When set to 0, the register enables trace operation in Overflow flow-control mode |
| 5 | STATCONDDUMP | RW | When set, register field StatCondDump enables the dump of a statistics frame to the range of counter values set for registers StatAlarmMin, StatAlarmMax, and AlarmMode. This field also renders register StatAlarmStatus inoperative. When parameter statisticsCounterAlarm is set to False, the StatCondDump register bit is reserved. |
| 4 | ALARMEN | RW | When set, register field AlarmEn enables the probe to collect alarm-related information. When the register field bit is null, both TraceAlarm and StatAlarm outputs are driven to 0. |
| 3 | STATEN | RW | When set to 1, register field StatEn enables statistics profiling. The probe sends statistics results to the output for signal ObsTx. All statistics counters are cleared when the StatEn bit goes from 0 to 1. When set to 0, counters are disabled. |
<!-- page 2979 -->

### SNOC_TPRB3_SPROF_MAINCTL (continued)

| Bits | Name | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 2 | PAYLOADEN | RW | Register field PayloadEn, when set to 1, enables traces to contain headers and payload. When set to 0, only headers are reported. |
| 1 | TRACEEN | RW | Register field TraceEn enables the probe to send filtered packets (Trace) on the ObsTx observation output. |
| 0 | ERREN | RW | Register field ErrEn enables the probe to send on the ObsTx output any packet with Error status, independently of filtering mechanisms, thus constituting a simple supplementary global filter. |

### SNOC_TPRB3_SPROF_STATPERIOD

* **Address:** `0x00584C24`
* **Type:** RW
* **Reset State:** `0x00000000`

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 4:0 | STATPERIOD | Register StatPeriod is a 5-bit register that sets a period, within a range of 2-8 megacycles, during which statistics are collected before being dumped automatically. Setting the register effectively enables automatic mode operation for statistics collection. Note: The configured period is also used for statistics alarm generation. The period is calculated with the formula: N_Cycle = 2\*\*min(23,StatPeriod). When register StatPeriod is set to its default value 0, automatic dump mode is disabled, and register StatGo is activated for manual mode operation. Note: When parameter nStatisticsCounter is set to 0, statistics collection is disabled, with the consequence that all statistics collection registers, including StatPeriod, are reserved. |
<!-- page 2980 -->

## SNOC_MSS_QOS_PRIORITY (0x00587008)

**Type:** RW

**Reset State:** 0x00000000

Priority register.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 3:2 | P1 | In Regulator mode, defines the HIGH hurry level. In Fixed/Limiter mode, defines the Urgency level for READ transactions. |
| 1:0 | P0 | In Regulator mode, defines the LOW hurry level. In Fixed/Limiter mode, defines the Urgency level for WRITE transactions. |

## SNOC_MSS_QOS_MODE (0x0058700C)

**Type:** RW

**Reset State:** 0x00000000

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1:0 | MODE | Functional Mode: 0=Fixed, 1=Limiter, 2=Bypass, 3=Regulator. |

## SNOC_MSS_QOS_BANDWIDTH (0x00587010)

**Type:** RW

**Reset State:** 0x00000000
<!-- page 2996 -->
| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 15:0 | BANDWIDTH | Defines the bandwidth threshold in 1/256th-byte-per-cycle units. In other words, the desired rate in MBps is divided by frequency in MHz of the NIU, and then multiplied by 256. |

## SNOC_MSS_QOS_SATURATION (0x00587014)

**Type:** RW

**Reset State:** 0x00000000

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 9:0 | SATURATION | Defines the size of the bandwidth counter, that is, the measurement window, in 16-byte units. In other words, the desired number of bytes divided by 16. |

## SNOC_MSS_QOS_EXTCONTROL (0x00587018)

**Type:** RW

**Reset State:** 0x00000000

External inputs control.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 2 | INTCLKEN | Replace the External reference by the local clock. |
| 1 | EXTTHREN | ExtThr input controls Low/High priority instead of bandwidth threshold. |
| 0 | SOCKETQOSEN | Combines the Socket QoS with Regulator QoS. |

# 15 Top Level Mode Multiplexing

## 15.1 TLMM_MPU1132_16_M22L12_AHB

## 15.2 TLMM_CSR

TLMM control and status

### 15.2.1 TLMM_CSR

TLMM control and status

### 0x01000000 + 0x1000 * n TLMM_GPIO_CFGn, n=[0..121]

**Type:** RW

**Clock:** GCC_TLMM_AHB_CLK

**Reset State:** 0x00000001

The GPIO_CFG[n] controls the GPIO Output Enable, Drive strength, Pull and Alternate Function for GPIO[n]. The default PULL can vary for different GPIOs and can be found in the pinout spreadsheet. The default drive setting for all GPIOs is '000' (2 mA).

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 10 | GPIO_HIHYS_EN | Controls the hihys_en for GPIO[n] |
| 9 | GPIO_OE | Controls the OE for GPIO[n] when in GPIO mode. |
<!-- page 3013 -->

### TLMM_GPIO_CFGn (continued)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 8:6 | DRV_STRENGTH | Controls the GPIO pad drive strength. This applies regardless of the FUNC_SEL field selection.<br>0x0: DRV_2_MA (Sets the drive strength to 2mA. When in RFFE mode, sets output cap to 5-26 pF)<br>0x1: DRV_4_MA (Sets the drive strength to 4mA. When in RFFE mode, sets output cap to 27-45 pF)<br>0x2: DRV_6_MA (Sets the drive strength to 6mA. When in RFFE mode, sets output cap to 46-60 pF)<br>0x3: DRV_8_MA (Sets the drive strength to 8mA. When in RFFE mode, sets output cap to 61-79 pF)<br>0x4: DRV_10_MA (Sets the drive strength to 10mA. When in RFFE mode, it is a don't care)<br>0x5: DRV_12_MA (Sets the drive strength to 12mA. When in RFFE mode, it is a don't care)<br>0x6: DRV_14_MA (Sets the drive strength to 14mA. When in RFFE mode, it is a don't care)<br>0x7: DRV_16_MA (Sets the drive strength to 16mA. When in RFFE mode, it is a don't care) |
| 5:2 | FUNC_SEL | Many of the GPIO pads have one or more functional hardware interfaces behind them. This field controls how the pad is used. Set this to the appropriate value for the function desired. |
| 1:0 | GPIO_PULL | The pad can be configured to employ an internal weak pull up, pull down, or keeper function. This applies regardless of the FUNC_SEL field selection.<br>0x0: NO_PULL (Disables all pull)<br>0x1: PULL_DOWN (Weak Pull-down)<br>0x2: KEEPER (Weak Keeper)<br>0x3: PULL_UP (Weak Pull-Up) |

### 0x01000004 + 0x1000 * n TLMM_GPIO_IN_OUTn, n=[0..121]

**Type:** RW

**Clock:** GCC_TLMM_AHB_CLK

**Reset State:** 0x00000000

The GPIO_IN_OUT[n] controls the Out and In on the GPIO[n]. The GPIO_IN bit is read-only.

| Bits | Name | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1 | GPIO_OUT | RW | Controls the value of the GPIO Output |
| 0 | GPIO_IN | R | Allows you to read the Input value of the GPIO |
<!-- page 3014 -->

### 0x01000008 + 0x1000 * n TLMM_GPIO_INTR_CFGn, n=[0..121]

**Type:** RW

**Clock:** GCC_TLMM_AHB_CLK

**Reset State:** 0x000000E2

The GPIO_INTR_CFGn controls the summary and direct interrupt settings for GPIO[n]. Additional settings for direct connect interrupts can be found in the DIR_CONN_INTR_CFGn_* registers.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 8 | DIR_CONN_EN | This bit tells the TLMM that GPIO[n] is being used as a Direct Connect Interrupt.<br>0x1: ENABLE (Enable the GPIO as direct connect interrupt)<br>0x0: DISABLE (Disable the GPIO as direct connect interrupt) |
| 7:5 | TARGET_PROC | This field determines which processor a summary interrupt from GPIO[n] should get routed to.<br>0x0: WCSS (Route the GPIO[n] signal to WCSS summary interrupt)<br>0x1: SENSORS (Route the GPIO[n] signal to SENSORS summary interrupt)<br>0x2: Reserved<br>0x3: RPM (Route the GPIO[n] signal to RPM summary interrupt)<br>0x4: APSS (Route the GPIO[n] signal to APSS summary interrupt)<br>0x5: MSS (Route the GPIO[n] signal to MSS summary interrupt)<br>0x6: TZ (Route the GPIO[n] signal to TZ summary interrupt)<br>0x7: NONE (Don't route to any processor subsystem. Default) |
| 4 | INTR_RAW_STATUS_EN | This enables the RAW status for the summary interrupt on this GPIO. This is a power saving mechanism. Leave this disabled unless it is needed.<br>0x1: ENABLE<br>0x0: DISABLE |
| 3:2 | INTR_DECT_CTL | Controls the Edge or Level Detection of the Interrupt Controller<br>0x0: LEVEL (Level sensitive. INTR_POL_CTL should be set to '1' for active-high, '0' for active-low)<br>0x1: POS_EDGE (Positive-edge sensitive. INTR_POL_CTL should be '1')<br>0x2: NEG_EDGE (Negative-edge sensitive INTR_POL_CTL should be '1')<br>0x3: DUAL_EDGE (Sensitive to both edges. INTR_POL_CTL is a don't care for this case) |
| 1 | INTR_POL_CTL | Controls the Polarity Detection of the Interrupt Controller. Polarity 1 corresponds to active high and Polarity 0 corresponds to active low.<br>0x1: POLARITY_1 (Active-high)<br>0x0: POLARITY_0 (Active-low) |
<!-- page 3015 -->

### TLMM_GPIO_INTR_CFGn (continued)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 0 | INTR_ENABLE | Controls if this GPIO generates a summary interrupt.<br>0x1: ENABLE<br>0x0: DISABLE |

### 0x0100000C + 0x1000 * n TLMM_GPIO_INTR_STATUSn, n=[0..121]

**Type:** RW

**Clock:** GCC_TLMM_AHB_CLK

**Reset State:** 0x00000000

The GPIO_INTR_STATUS[n] indicates the status of the summary interrupt for GPIO[n].

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 0 | INTR_STATUS | When read it returns the status for the interrupt on GPIO[n]. When written with a 1 in this position, it sets the interrupt for GPIO[n]. When it is written with a 0, it clears the interrupt |

### 0x01100000 TLMM_CLK_GATE_EN

**Type:** RW

**Clock:** GCC_TLMM_AHB_CLK

**Reset State:** 0x00000000

This register can enable the clock gating in the TLMM. By default, the clock gating is disabled.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 2 | AHB_HCLK_EN | Enables the Clock Gating on the AHB Clock.<br>0x1: ENABLE<br>0x0: DISABLE |
| 1 | SUMMARY_INTR_EN | Enables the Clock Gating on the Summary Interrupt Demets.<br>0x1: ENABLE<br>0x0: DISABLE |
| 0 | CRIF_READ_EN | Enables the Clock Gating on the Read Data Register on the CRIF interface.<br>0x1: ENABLE<br>0x0: DISABLE |
<!-- page 3016 -->

### 0x01100004 TLMM_IE_CTRL_DISABLE

**Type:** RW

**Clock:** GCC_TLMM_AHB_CLK

**Reset State:** 0x00000001

This register can enable/disable control of the pad input enable within the TLMM. By default the IE control is disabled. When disabled, the IE for all GPIOs is always high and the input path is always enabled. When IE_CTRL is enabled, the input path can enabled/disabled based on the direction of the function that is configured for the GPIO. This register only affects GPIOs. Some loopback tests require the IE to always be high. As such, this bit is required functionality for certain test modes.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 0 | IE_CTRL_DISABLE | Enables control of the pad IE within TLMM. When disabled, the IE is tied high.<br>0x1: DISABLE<br>0x0: ENABLE |

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |

| 0 | START_BIT | Always set '1' |

### 0x01108000 TLMM_RFFE_CTL

* **Type**: RW
* **Clock**: GCC_TLMM_AHB_CLK
* **Reset State**: 0x00000000

This register controls the RFFE sr_ctl_en/sen_en TLMM outputs. Its purpose is to control the clock and data pads for RFFE on GPIO. It is used to enable/disable slew rate control for the RFFE pads. When used for RFFE, slew rate control must be enabled by setting the SR_CTL_EN bits must be set to '01'. When used for other purposes, slew rate control should be disabled. When disabled, the pad behaves in a similar manner to a regular GPIO pad. The default value is to keep the slew rate control disabled.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 29 | RFFE5_DATA_SEN_EN | Reserved |
| 28:27 | RFFE5_DATA_SR_CTL_EN | Select whether slew rate control is enabled/disabled. Set to '01' for RFFE mode |
| 26 | RFFE5_CLK_SEN_EN | Reserved |
| 25:24 | RFFE5_CLK_SR_CTL_EN | Select whether slew rate control is enabled/disabled. Set to '01' for RFFE mode |
| 23 | RFFE4_DATA_SEN_EN | Reserved |

### TLMM_GPIO_OUT_CLR_0

**Address:** `0x01200020`
**Type:** W
**Clock:** `GCC_TLMM_AHB_CLK`
**Reset State:** `0x00000000`

This register can be used to clear the output values of GPIO[31:0]. Once the CLR bit is written to '1', the output of the corresponding GPIO is cleared to '0'. The CLR bit then automatically returns to '0' so that it can be used again. This register is designed for bit-bang or fast configuration of multiple output bits and alleviates the need for a read-->modify-->write operation.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:0 | GPIO_OUT_CLR | Clear bits for GPIO[31:0] output values. |

### LPASS_LPAIF_I2S_CTLa (0x07709000 + 0x1000 * a, a=[0..3]) (continued)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31 | RESET | 0x0: DISABLE<br>0x1: ENABLE |
| 22 | EN_LONG_RATE | Allow for frame size to be longer than I2S sample bit width, BIT_WIDTH<br>0x0: DISABLE<br>0x1: ENABLE |
| 21:16 | LONG_RATE | Used as WS rate when EN_LONG_RATE=1 |
| 15 | LOOPBACK | SW: RW, HW: R<br>Loopback control bit.<br>0x0: DISABLE (DISABLE)<br>0x1: ENABLE (ENABLE (only applicable to a=1=codec_mic, a=2=mi2s, & a=4=sec mic. If ENABLE is set for a=1, codec speaker is looped back to both wires of codec mic. For a=2, mi2s is looped back on itself. For a=4 sec speaker is looped backed to sec mic)) |
| 14 | SPKR_EN | SW: RW, HW: R<br>Enable for the speaker direction operation (out of the MSM). I2S interface will start transmitting serial data when enabled and trying to access a read DMA channel. Set the enable after the other control bits (speaker related, bit_width, ws_src) are configured. Disable before changing the other bits.<br>0x0: DISABLE (DISABLE)<br>0x1: ENABLE (ENABLE) |
| 13:10 | SPKR_MODE | SW: RW, HW: R<br>Controls which I2S lines are used (if supported by HW) and multichannel operation<br>0x0: NONE (NONE)<br>0x1: SD0 (SD0 (data sent to SD0 only- stereo or mono))<br>0x2: SD1 (SD1 (data sent to SD1 only- stereo or mono))<br>0x3: SD2 (SD2 (data sent to SD2 only- stereo or mono))<br>0x4: SD3 (SD3 (data sent to SD3 only- stereo or mono))<br>0x5: QUAD01 (QUAD01 (SD0 & SD1 = quad channel mode))<br>0x6: QUAD23 (QUAD23 (SD2 & SD3 = quad channel mode))<br>0x7: ENUM_6CH (6CH (SD0, SD1 & SD2 = 6 channel mode))<br>0x8: ENUM_8CH (8CH (SD0, SD1, SD2 & SD3 = 8 channel mode)) |
| 9 | SPKR_MONO | SW: RW, HW: R<br>In mono mode, the speaker path of I2S (out of MSM) will take each mono sample from memory and transmit it during both the right and left portions of the word select. Only applicable when a single I2S line is used in SPKR_MODE.<br>0x0: STEREO (STEREO)<br>0x1: MONO (MONO) |

### LPASS_LPAIF_I2S_CTLa (0x07709000 + 0x1000 * a, a=[0..3]) (continued)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 8 | MIC_EN | SW: RW, HW: R<br>Enable for the microphone direction operation (into the MSM). I2S interface will start capturing data when enabled and trying to access a write DMA channel. Set the enable after the other control bits (mic related, bit_width, ws_src) are configured. Disable before changing the other bits.<br>0x0: DISABLE (DISABLE)<br>0x1: ENABLE (ENABLE) |
| 7:4 | MIC_MODE | SW: RW, HW: R<br>Controls which I2S lines are used (if supported by HW) and multichannel operation<br>0x0: NONE (NONE)<br>0x1: SD0 (SD0 (data taken from SD0 only- stereo or mono))<br>0x2: SD1 (SD1 (data taken from SD1 only- stereo or mono))<br>0x3: SD2 (SD2 (data taken from SD2 only- stereo or mono))<br>0x4: SD3 (SD3 (data taken from SD3 only- stereo or mono))<br>0x5: QUAD01 (QUAD01 (SD0 & SD1 = quad channel mode))<br>0x6: QUAD23 (QUAD23 (SD2 & SD3 = quad channel mode))<br>0x7: ENUM_6CH (6CH (SD0, SD1 & SD2 = 6 channel mode))<br>0x8: ENUM_8CH (8CH (SD0, SD1, SD2 & SD3 = 8 channel mode)) |
| 3 | MIC_MONO | SW: RW, HW: R<br>Controls whether only the left word is stored in memory (mono) or the left and right words are stored (stereo). In mono mode, the data in the right portion of WS is ignored. Only applicable when a single I2S line is used in MIC_MODE.<br>0x0: STEREO (STEREO)<br>0x1: MONO (MONO) |
| 2 | WS_SRC | SW: RW, HW: R<br>Controls the source of the word select, internally generated or taken from outside. Does not affect the clock. Master/Slave bit clock mode is controlled in LPASS clk_ctl.<br>0x0: INT (INT (master mode))<br>0x1: EXT (EXT (slave mode)) |
| 1:0 | BIT_WIDTH | SW: RW, HW: R<br>Controls the bit width of the I2S samples<br>0x0: ENUM_16 (16)<br>0x1: ENUM_24 (24)<br>0x2: ENUM_32 (32)<br>0x3: ENUM_25 (25) |

### 0x0771C034 + 0x20*n LPASS_CDC_RXn_B6_CTL, n=[1..3]

**Type:** RW  
**Clock:** csr_wr_clk  
**Reset State:** 0x00000000  

Specifies the enable signals for the Gain multiplier (Volume controller). This register should be updated only once per 5 mclk cycles for well-defined operation.

| Bits | Name | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |

### 0x0771C038 + 0x20*n LPASS_CDC_RXn_VOL_CTL_B1_CTL, n=[1..3]

**Type:** RW  
**Clock:** csr_wr_clk  
**Reset State:** 0x00000000  

RX Timeout value for gain multipliers.  
At 48KHz sampling rate (Fs), the maximum timeout is 1.37s ((256*TIMER_VAL+255)/Fs)  
- 11111111 => (256*255+255)/48k = 1.365s; (256*255+255)/8k = 8.19s  
- 10000000 => (256*128+255)/48k = 0.69s; (256*128+255)/8k = 4.13s  
- 01000000 => (256*64+255)/48k = 0.347s; (256*64+255)/8k = 2.08s  
- 00000000 => Immediate gain update without timer expiration and zero crossing detection. SW control mode.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 7:0 | TIMER | Specifies the Volume Controller timeout period in Fs cycles. |

At 48KHz sampling rate (Fs), the maximum timeout is 1.37s ((256*TIMER_VAL+255)/Fs)
* `11111111` => (256*255+255)/48k = 1.365s; (256*255+255)/8k = 8.19s

* **Reset State:** `0x00000000`

| 7 | BYPASS | Set (1) to disable automatic pointer incrementing<br>0x0: AUTOINC<br>0x1: BYPASS |
<!-- page 3075 -->

### LPASS_CDC_IIRn_COEF_B1_CTL (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---------- |
| 6:0 | ADDR | Pointer to internal register bank to store the Sidetone IIR filter coefficients. This register auto increments every time `CDC_IIRn_COEF_B2_CTL` is written.<br>The maximum allowed value is 0x18. Any value above this will corrupt the coefficient bank. Data is LSB first. IIR co-efficients are 30-bits long, the co-efficients are written in a bank of registers 1-byte at a time. Since only 30 bits are needed, the top 2 MSB bits of every 4th byte is dropped in the design.<br>0x0: BIQ_STG0_COEFF_B0<br>0x4: BIQ_STG0_COEFF_B1<br>0x8: BIQ_STG0_COEFF_B2<br>0xC: BIQ_STG0_COEFF_A1<br>0x10: BIQ_STG0_COEFF_A2<br>0x14: BIQ_STG1_COEFF_B0<br>0x18: BIQ_STG1_COEFF_B1<br>0x1C: BIQ_STG1_COEFF_B2<br>0x20: BIQ_STG1_COEFF_A1<br>0x24: BIQ_STG1_COEFF_A2<br>0x28: BIQ_STG2_COEFF_B0<br>0x2C: BIQ_STG2_COEFF_B1<br>0x30: BIQ_STG2_COEFF_B2<br>0x34: BIQ_STG2_COEFF_A1<br>0x38: BIQ_STG2_COEFF_A2<br>0x3C: BIQ_STG3_COEFF_B0<br>0x40: BIQ_STG3_COEFF_B1<br>0x44: BIQ_STG3_COEFF_B2<br>0x48: BIQ_STG3_COEFF_A1<br>0x4C: BIQ_STG3_COEFF_A2<br>0x50: BIQ_STG4_COEFF_B0<br>0x54: BIQ_STG4_COEFF_B1<br>0x58: BIQ_STG4_COEFF_B2<br>0x5C: BIQ_STG4_COEFF_A1<br>0x60: BIQ_STG4_COEFF_A2 |

### 0x0771C260+0x20*n LPASS_CDC_TXn_VOL_CTL_TIMER, n=[1..2]

* **Type**: RW
* **Clock**: `csr_wr_clk`
* **Reset State**: `0x00000000`

TX Timeout value for gain multipliers.

At 48KHz sampling rate (Fs), the maximum timeout is 1.37s ((256*TIMER_VAL+255)/Fs)

* `11111111` => (256*255+255)/48k = 1.365s; (256*255+255)/8k = 8.19s
* `10000000` => (256*128+255)/48k = 0.69s; (256*128+255)/8k = 4.13s
* `01000000` => (256*64+255)/48k = 0.347s; (256*64+255)/8k = 2.08s
* `00000000` => Immediate gain update without timer expiration and zero crossing detection. SW control mode.
<!-- page 3084 -->

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 7:0 | PGA_TIMER | Specifies the Volume Controller timeout period in Fs cycles. |

### 0x0771C264+0x20*n LPASS_CDC_TXn_VOL_CTL_GAIN, n=[1..2]

* **Type**: RW
* **Clock**: `csr_wr_clk`
* **Reset State**: `0x00000000`

TX Channel Gain. The gain is approximate to +/- 0.3dB.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 7:0 | PGA_GAIN | Specifies the Volume Controller gain. The value is a twos complement number. |

### 0x0771C268+0x20*n LPASS_CDC_TXn_VOL_CTL_CFG, n=[1..2]

* **Type**: RW
* **Clock**: `csr_wr_clk`
* **Reset State**: `0x00000000`

Specifies the enable signals for the Gain multiplier (Volume controller). This register should be updated only once per 5 mclk cycles for well-defined operation.

| Bits | Name | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 3 | GAIN_UPD_STATUS | R | Specifies if the gain update has been completed. Automatically resets to IN_PROCESS when gain is updated. When the gain has been applied, changes state to COMPLETE. Read only bit.<br>0x0: IN_PROCESS<br>0x1: COMPLETE |
| 2 | MODE | RW | Specifies the mode in which gain is updated.<br>0x0: AUTOMATIC<br>0x1: MANUAL |
| 1 | HALF_DB | RW | Specifies the addition of a half db to the original gain. When set(1) and If the actual gain is 1, a gain of 1.5dB is applied. When set(1) and If the actual gain is -1, a gain of -0.5dB is applied.<br>0x0: DISABLE<br>0x1: ENABLE |
<!-- page 3085 -->

| Bits | Name | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 0 | MUTE_EN | RW | Specifies if the output of the volume controller needs to be muted.<br>0x0: DISABLE<br>0x1: ENABLE |

### 0x0771C26C+0x20*n LPASS_CDC_TXn_MUX_CTL, n=[1..2]

* **Type**: RW
* **Clock**: `csr_wr_clk`
* **Reset State**: `0x00000000`

Specifies the control signals for Multiplixer inputs in TX path.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |

| 3 | HPF_BP_SEL | Specifies if the high pass controller needs to be bypassed or not.<br>0x0: NO_BYPASS<br>0x1: BYPASS |
| 2:1 | RESERVED | Reserved |
| 0 | ADC_DMIC_SEL | Specifies ADCMIC source selection path in CIC filter.<br>0x0: ADC<br>0x1: DMIC |

### 0x01A011E0 MDSS_MDP_QOS_REMAPPER_CLASS_0
- **Type**: RW
- **Reset State**: 0x000000E4

QoS remapper to translate health level to priority levels on the bus

Class 0 is used by the real time clients in the system (i.e. ViG/RGB/DMA pipes in line mode)

Class 1 is used by the non-real time clients in the system (i.e. DMA pipes in block mode)

WB modules are completely SW configurable and dont rely on watermarks.

Therefore they do NOT go through the remapper

double buffered: NO

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 7:6 | REQPRIORITY_3 | Remapping ID for priority 3 onto the client port |
| 5:4 | REQPRIORITY_2 | Remapping ID for priority 0 onto the client port |
| 3:2 | REQPRIORITY_1 | Remapping ID for priority 1 onto the client port |
| 1:0 | REQPRIORITY_0 | Remapping ID for priority 0 onto the client port |

### 0x01A011EC MDSS_MDP_UPPER_NEWROI_PRIOR_TO_START
- **Type**: RW
- **Reset State**: 0x00000001

The newroi prior to start is used to flush out incorrect states and such between frames. The newroi is sent prior to the start signals from the PMU's. This field is for the PMU's in the upper pipeline only - there exists a separate register for the lower pipeline (LOWER_NEWROI_PRIOR_TO_START)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 0 | ENABLE | Enable the mode to send out newroi prior to start |

### 0x01A012E0 MDSS_MDP_VIDEO_INTF_UNDERFLOW_CTL

**Type:** RW  
**Reset State:** 0x00001111  
**Double Buffered:** NO  

VIDEO_INTF_UNDERFLOW_CTRL register controls the auto recovery mechanism on underflow case. Register reprogramming is not allowed when each video interface is running.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 4 | INTF_1_ERR_RECOVERY_EN | Enable auto recovery during underflow case in interface 1 if NEWROI_PRIOR_TO_START is disabled.<br>0x0 : Disable. SW is required to apply SW reset when underflow interrupt occurs<br>0x1 : Enable. No SW reset is required. Underflow interrupt is generated after auto recovery is finished |

### 0x01A013E0 MDSS_MDP_QOS_REMAPPER_LOWER_CLASS_0

* **Type**: RW
* **Reset State**: 0x000000E4
* **Description**: QoS remapper to translate health level to priority levels on the bus.
  Class 0 is used by the real time clients in the system (i.e. ViG/RGB/DMA pipes in line mode).
  Class 1 is used by the non-real time clients in the system (i.e. DMA pipes in block mode).
  WB modules are completely SW configurable and dont rely on watermarks. Therefore they do NOT go through the remapper.
* **Double Buffered**: NO

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 7:6 | REQPRIORITY_3 | Remapping ID for priority 3 onto the client port |
| 5:4 | REQPRIORITY_2 | Remapping ID for priority 0 onto the client port |
<!-- page 3144 -->
### MDSS_MDP_QOS_REMAPPER_LOWER_CLASS_0 (Continued)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 3:2 | REQPRIORITY_1 | Remapping ID for priority 1 onto the client port |
| 1:0 | REQPRIORITY_0 | Remapping ID for priority 0 onto the client port |

| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 8 | INTF_2_TIM_GEN_SYNC_MODE | Control synchronization mode for timing generator in interface 2<br>0x0 : No sync mode<br>0x1 : Use INTF_1's enable signal for interface 2 |
| 4 | INTF_1_TIM_GEN_SYNC_MODE | Control synchronization mode for timing generator in interface 1<br>0x0 : No SW trigger change<br>0x1 : Use INTF_2's enable signal for interface 1 |

### 0x01A013F8 MDSS_MDP_LOWER_NEWROI_PRIOR_TO_START

* **Type**: RW
* **Reset State**: 0x00000001
* **Description**: The newroi prior to start is used to flush out incorrect states and such between frames. The newroi is sent prior to the start signals from the PMU's. This field is for the PMU's in the lower pipeline only - there exists a separate register for the upper pipeline (UPPER_NEWROI_PRIOR_TO_START)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 0 | ENABLE | Enable the mode to send out newroi prior to start |

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1:0 | INTF_1_SW_RESET_MASK | Control mask for intf_1 (DSI0)<br>0x0 : Resets for both video and command modes<br>0x1 : Reset for video mode only<br>0x2 : Reset for command mode only<br>0x3 : No resets to both video and command |

### MDSS_MDP_CTL_0_TOP

**Address:** `0x01A02014`
**Type:** RW
**Reset State:** `0x00001F00`

Operation Mode Configuration for the Pipeline
The purpose of the register is to define the complete data path of this operation and that includes all the way to the interfaces such as DSI/HDMI/eDP.

> [!NOTE]
> Changing of the data path dynamically is NOT supported and requires stopping that data path, reconfiguring the connections, and restarting the datapath.
<!-- page 3157 -->

### MDSS_MDP_CTL_0_TOP (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 17 | MODE_SEL | Interface Mode of the destination interface<br>Needed to distinguish interfaces such as DSI that can be either mode<br>DSI can also interleave streams of different types (i.e. command and video) to a single core<br>0x0: Video Mode<br>0x1: Command Mode1 |
| 16:15 | STREAM_SEL | Stream Identification<br>Used For Interleaving of Command Streams<br>This field is a dont care for video mode streams<br>0x0: Stream 0<br>0x1: Stream 1<br>0x2: Stream 2 |
| 7:4 | OUT_SEL | Output Ping-Pong Interface Connection to external display interface<br>0x0: No connection from Ping-Pong buffers to output interfaces<br>0x1: Interface 0<br>0x2: Interface 1<br>0x3: Interface 2<br>0x4: Interface 3 |
| 3:0 | MEM_SEL | Memory Output Connection<br>0x0: NO memory output selected<br>0x1: Memory BLOCK mode output selected for rotation 0<br>0x2: Memory BLOCK mode output selected for rotation 1<br>0x3: Memory LINE mode output selected for rotation 0<br>0x4: Memory LINE mode output selected for rotation 1<br>0x5: Memory LINE mode output selected for linear memory writeback |

### MDSS_MDP_CTL_0_FLUSH

**Address:** `0x01A02018`
**Type:** RW
**Reset State:** `0x00000000`

Register Flush register
The flush register is used to indicate a pipe/layermixers registers are all programmed, and are safe to update to the back copy of the double buffered registers.
<!-- page 3158 -->

### MDSS_MDP_CTL_0_FLUSH (cont.)

Each pipes/layermixers flush mask bit will be used only when the associated pipe/layermixer is running at active refresh pull mode, e.g., direct out going to LCDC/HDMI/DSI Video.

In such operation mode, the associated pipe/layermixers double buffered registers back copies are updated with the new values at the vsync boundary only when the flush mask bit has already been written a 1.

Each flush mask bit would also returned a 0 once the back copies are updated.

Before the back copies are updated, the associate mask bit would returned a 1 if it has been previously written a 1.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 30 | TIMING_1 | Timing Interface 1 are ready for flush |
| 17 | CTL | Control Pipe register is ready for flush<br>This applies to upper pipe ONLY to change the adding/removal of layers |
| 16 | WB | Write Back registers are ready for flush |
| 15 | DSPP_2 | DSPP2 registers are ready for flush |
| 14 | DSPP_1 | DSPP1 registers are ready for flush |
| 13 | DSPP_0 | DSPP0 registers are ready for flush |
| 12 | DMA_1 | DMA_1 registers are ready for flush |
| 11 | DMA_0 | DMA_0 registers are ready for flush |
| 10 | LAYER_MIXER_4 | Layer Mixer4 registers are ready for flush<br>This includes the cursor registers stored in the layer mixer register space |
| 9 | LAYER_MIXER_3 | Layer Mixer3 registers are ready for flush<br>This includes the cursor registers stored in the layer mixer register space |
| 8 | LAYER_MIXER_2 | Layer Mixer2 registers are ready for flush<br>This includes the cursor registers stored in the layer mixer register space |
| 7 | LAYER_MIXER_1 | Layer Mixer1 registers are ready for flush<br>This includes the cursor registers stored in the layer mixer register space |
| 6 | LAYER_MIXER_0 | Layer Mixer0 registers are ready for flush<br>This includes the cursor registers stored in the layer mixer register space |
| 5 | RGB_2 | RGB2 registers are ready for flush |
| 4 | RGB_1 | RGB1 registers are ready for flush |
| 3 | RGB_0 | RGB0 registers are ready for flush |
<!-- page 3159 -->

### MDSS_MDP_CTL_0_FLUSH (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 2 | VIG_2 | VIG2 registers are ready for flush |
| 1 | VIG_1 | VIG1 registers are ready for flush |
| 0 | VIG_0 | VIG0 registers are ready for flush |

### MDSS_MDP_CTL_0_CTL_START

**Address:** `0x01A0201C`
**Type:** W
**Reset State:** `0x00000000`

Overlay Processor Start Signal for the given Control Operation

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 0 | START | A write to this register will kick off operation for the given operation control and activate all layers |

### MDSS_MDP_CTL_0_SW_RESET

**Address:** `0x01A02030`
**Type:** RW
**Reset State:** `0x00000000`

Software Reset of the given control operation

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 0 | RESET | Writing to this bit will trigger a soft reset for the described data path<br>This register is self-clearing and will return 0x1 if soft reset sequence is not complete<br>Upon completion, this will return 0x0<br>Note that this will soft reset the peripheral display interfaces that are described in this path<br>i.e. if driving intf_0 it will reset the pixel clock domain of intf_0 as well |

### MDSS_MDP_CTL_0_SW_RESET_OVERRIDE

**Address:** `0x01A02034`
**Type:** RW
**Reset State:** `0x00000000`
<!-- page 3160 -->

### MDSS_MDP_CTL_0_SW_RESET_OVERRIDE (cont.)

Software Reset Override of the given control operation

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 0 | RESET | Writing to this bit will assert reset for the described data path<br>This value contained in this register will be forced onto the datapath<br>It will reset the state machines within the scheduler as well for the given datapath<br>To use this register sequence, SW shall write a value of 0x1 to this register to assert reset<br>Once SW wants to de-assert reset, SW shall write a value of 0x0<br>SW will need to ensure the duration of the value 0x1 is long enough to ensure the path is clean and all memory reads are complete<br>The datapath will not be triggered if this bit is asserted |

## MDSS_MDP_CTL_1_TOP

* **Address:** `0x01A02214`
* **Type:** `RW`
* **Reset State:** `0x00001F00`
* **Description:** Operation Mode Configuration for the Pipeline. The purpose of the register is to define the complete data path of this operation and that includes all the way to the interfaces such as DSI/HDMI/eDP. Changing of the data path dynamically is NOT supported and requires stopping that data path, reconfiguring the connections, and restarting the datapath.


<!-- page 3171 -->

### MDSS_MDP_CTL_1_TOP (Continued)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 17 | MODE_SEL | Interface Mode of the destination interface<br>Needed to distinguish interfaces such as DSI that can be either mode.<br>DSI can also interleave streams of different types (i.e. command and video) to a single core.<br>0x0: Video Mode<br>0x1: Command Mode 1 |
| 16:15 | STREAM_SEL | Stream Identification<br>Used For Interleaving of Command Streams<br>This field is a dont care for video mode streams.<br>0x0: Stream 0<br>0x1: Stream 1<br>0x2: Stream 2 |
| 7:4 | OUT_SEL | Output Ping-Pong Interface Connection to external display interface<br>0x0: No connection from Ping-Pong buffers to output interfaces<br>0x1: Interface 0<br>0x2: Interface 1<br>0x3: Interface 2<br>0x4: Interface 3 |
| 3:0 | MEM_SEL | Memory Output Connection<br>0x0: NO memory output selected<br>0x1: Memory BLOCK mode output selected for rotation 0<br>0x2: Memory BLOCK mode output selected for rotation 1<br>0x3: Memory LINE mode output selected for rotation 0<br>0x4: Memory LINE mode output selected for rotation 1<br>0x5: Memory LINE mode output selected for linear memory writeback |

## 0x01A02218 MDSS_MDP_CTL_1_FLUSH

**Type:** RW  
**Reset State:** 0x00000000  

Register Flush register

The flush register is used to indicate a pipe/layermixers registers are all programmed, and are safe to update to the back copy of the double buffered registers.
<!-- page 3172 -->

Each pipes/layermixers flush mask bit will be used only when the associated pipe/layermixer is running at active refresh pull mode, e.g., direct out going to LCDC/HDMI/DSI Video.

In such operation mode, the associated pipe/layermixers double buffered registers back copies are updated with the new values at the vsync boundary only when the flush mask bit has already been written a 1.

Each flush mask bit would also returned a 0 once the back copies are updated.

Before the back copies are updated, the associate mask bit would returned a 1 if it has been previously written a 1.

| 9 | LAYER_MIXER_3 | Layer Mixer3 registers are ready for flush<br>This includes the cursor registers stored in the layer mixer register space |
| 8 | LAYER_MIXER_2 | Layer Mixer2 registers are ready for flush<br>This includes the cursor registers stored in the layer mixer register space |

| 6 | LAYER_MIXER_0 | Layer Mixer0 registers are ready for flush<br>This includes the cursor registers stored in the layer mixer register space |

| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 0 | START | A write to this register will kick off operation for the given operation control and activate all layers |

## 0x01A02230 MDSS_MDP_CTL_1_SW_RESET

**Type:** RW  
**Reset State:** 0x00000000  

Software Reset of the given control operation

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 0 | RESET | Writing to this bit will trigger a soft reset for the described data path.<br>This register is self-clearing and will return 0x1 if soft reset sequence is not complete.<br>Upon completion, this will return 0x0.<br>Note that this will soft reset the peripheral display interfaces that are described in this path.<br>i.e. if driving intf_0 it will reset the pixel clock domain of intf_0 as well |

## 0x01A02234 MDSS_MDP_CTL_1_SW_RESET_OVERRIDE

**Type:** RW  
**Reset State:** 0x00000000  
<!-- page 3174 -->

### MDSS_MDP_CTL_1_SW_RESET_OVERRIDE (Continued)

Software Reset Override of the given control operation

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 0 | RESET | Writing to this bit will assert reset for the described data path.<br>This value contained in this register will be forced onto the datapath.<br>It will reset the state machines within the scheduler as well for the given datapath.<br>To use this register sequence, SW shall write a value of 0x1 to this register to assert reset.<br>Once SW wants to de-assert reset, SW shall write a value of 0x0.<br>SW will need to ensure the duration of the value 0x1 is long enough to ensure the path is clean and all memory reads are complete.<br>The datapath will not be triggered if this bit is asserted |

### MDSS_MDP_CTL_2_TOP

**Address**: `0x01A02414`
**Type**: RW
**Reset State**: `0x00001F00`

Operation Mode Configuration for the Pipeline

The purpose of the register is to define the complete data path of this operation and that includes all the way to the interfaces such as DSI/HDMI/eDP

Changing of the data path dynamically is NOT supported and requires stopping that data path, reconfiguring the connections, and restarting the datapath
<!-- page 3185 -->
### MDSS_MDP_CTL_2_TOP (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 17 | MODE_SEL | Interface Mode of the destination interface<br>Needed to distinguish interfaces such as DSI that can be either mode<br>DSI can also interleave streams of different types (i.e. command and video) to a single core<br>0x0: Video Mode<br>0x1: Command Mode1 |
| 16:15 | STREAM_SEL | Stream Identification<br>Used For Interleaving of Command Streams<br>This field is a dont care for video mode streams<br>0x0: Stream 0<br>0x1: Stream 1<br>0x2: Stream 2 |
| 7:4 | OUT_SEL | Output Ping-Pong Interface Connection to external display interface<br>0x0: No connection from Ping-Pong buffers to output interfaces<br>0x1: Interface 0<br>0x2: Interface 1<br>0x3: Interface 2<br>0x4: Interface 3 |
| 3:0 | MEM_SEL | Memory Output Connection<br>0x0: NO memory output selected<br>0x1: Memory BLOCK mode output selected for rotation 0<br>0x2: Memory BLOCK mode output selected for rotation 1<br>0x3: Memory LINE mode output selected for rotation 0<br>0x4: Memory LINE mode output selected for rotation 1<br>0x5: Memory LINE mode output selected for linear memory writeback |

### MDSS_MDP_CTL_2_FLUSH

**Address**: `0x01A02418`
**Type**: RW
**Reset State**: `0x00000000`

Register Flush register

The flush register is used to indicate a pipe/layermixers registers are all programmed, and are safe to update to the back copy of the double buffered registers.
<!-- page 3186 -->
### MDSS_MDP_CTL_2_FLUSH (cont.)

Each pipes/layermixers flush mask bit will be used only when the associated pipe/layermixer is running at active refresh pull mode, e.g., direct out going to LCDC/HDMI/DSI Video.

In such operation mode, the associated pipe/layermixers double buffered registers back copies are updated with the new values at the vsync boundary only when the flush mask bit has already been written a 1.

Each flush mask bit would also returned a 0 once the back copies are updated.

Before the back copies are updated, the associate mask bit would returned a 1 if it has been previously written a 1.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 30 | TIMING_1 | Timing Interface 1 are ready for flush |
| 17 | CTL | Control Pipe register is ready for flush<br>This applies to upper pipe ONLY to change the adding/removal of layers |
| 16 | WB | Write Back registers are ready for flush |
| 15 | DSPP_2 | DSPP2 registers are ready for flush |
| 14 | DSPP_1 | DSPP1 registers are ready for flush |
| 13 | DSPP_0 | DSPP0 registers are ready for flush |
| 12 | DMA_1 | DMA_1 registers are ready for flush |
| 11 | DMA_0 | DMA_0 registers are ready for flush |
| 10 | LAYER_MIXER_4 | Layer Mixer4 registers are ready for flush<br>This includes the cursor registers stored in the layer mixer register space |
| 9 | LAYER_MIXER_3 | Layer Mixer3 registers are ready for flush<br>This includes the cursor registers stored in the layer mixer register space |
| 8 | LAYER_MIXER_2 | Layer Mixer2 registers are ready for flush<br>This includes the cursor registers stored in the layer mixer register space |
| 7 | LAYER_MIXER_1 | Layer Mixer1 registers are ready for flush<br>This includes the cursor registers stored in the layer mixer register space |
| 6 | LAYER_MIXER_0 | Layer Mixer0 registers are ready for flush<br>This includes the cursor registers stored in the layer mixer register space |
| 5 | RGB_2 | RGB2 registers are ready for flush |
| 4 | RGB_1 | RGB1 registers are ready for flush |
| 3 | RGB_0 | RGB0 registers are ready for flush |
<!-- page 3187 -->
### MDSS_MDP_CTL_2_FLUSH (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 2 | VIG_2 | VIG2 registers are ready for flush |
| 1 | VIG_1 | VIG1 registers are ready for flush |

### MDSS_MDP_CTL_2_SW_RESET

**Address**: `0x01A02430`
**Type**: RW
**Reset State**: `0x00000000`

Software Reset of the given control operation

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 0 | RESET | Writing to this bit will trigger a soft reset for the described data path<br>This register is self-clearing and will return 0x1 if soft reset sequence is not complete<br>Upon completion, this will return 0x0<br>Note that this will soft reset the peripheral display interfaces that are described in this path<br>i.e. if driving intf_0 it will reset the pixel clock domain of intf_0 as well |

### MDSS_MDP_CTL_2_SW_RESET_OVERRIDE

**Address**: `0x01A02434`
**Type**: RW
**Reset State**: `0x00000000`
<!-- page 3188 -->
### MDSS_MDP_CTL_2_SW_RESET_OVERRIDE (cont.)

Software Reset Override of the given control operation

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 0 | RESET | Writing to this bit will assert reset for the described data path<br>This value contained in this register will be forced onto the datapath<br>It will reset the state machines within the scheduler as well for the given datapath<br>To use this register sequence, SW shall write a value of 0x1 to this register to assert reset<br>Once SW wants to de-assert reset, SW shall write a value of 0x0<br>SW will need to ensure the duration of the value 0x1 is long enough to ensure the path is clean and all memory reads are complete<br>The datapath will not be triggered if this bit is asserted |

## MDSS_MDP_CTL_3_TOP

* **Address:** `0x01A02614`
* **Type:** `RW`
* **Reset State:** `0x00001F00`

Operation Mode Configuration for the Pipeline.
The purpose of the register is to define the complete data path of this operation and that includes all the way to the interfaces such as DSI/HDMI/eDP.
Changing of the data path dynamically is NOT supported and requires stopping that data path, reconfiguring the connections, and restarting the datapath.
<!-- page 3199 -->
## MDSS_MDP_CTL_3_TOP (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 17 | MODE_SEL | Interface Mode of the destination interface<br>Needed to distinguish interfaces such as DSI that can be either mode<br>DSI can also interleave streams of different types (i.e. command and video) to a single core<br>0x0: Video Mode<br>0x1: Command Mode1 |
| 16:15 | STREAM_SEL | Stream Identification<br>Used For Interleaving of Command Streams<br>This field is a dont care for video mode streams<br>0x0: Stream 0<br>0x1: Stream 1<br>0x2: Stream 2 |
| 7:4 | OUT_SEL | Output Ping-Pong Interface Connection to external display interface<br>0x0: No connection from Ping-Pong buffers to output interfaces<br>0x1: Interface 0<br>0x2: Interface 1<br>0x3: Interface 2<br>0x4: Interface 3 |
| 3:0 | MEM_SEL | Memory Output Connection<br>0x0: NO memory output selected<br>0x1: Memory BLOCK mode output selected for rotation 0<br>0x2: Memory BLOCK mode output selected for rotation 1<br>0x3: Memory LINE mode output selected for rotation 0<br>0x4: Memory LINE mode output selected for rotation 1<br>0x5: Memory LINE mode output selected for linear memory writeback |

## MDSS_MDP_CTL_3_FLUSH

* **Address:** `0x01A02618`
* **Type:** `RW`
* **Reset State:** `0x00000000`

Register Flush register.
The flush register is used to indicate a pipe/layermixers registers are all programmed, and are safe to update to the back copy of the double buffered registers.
<!-- page 3200 -->
Each pipes/layermixers flush mask bit will be used only when the associated pipe/layermixer is running at active refresh pull mode, e.g., direct out going to LCDC/HDMI/DSI Video.

In such operation mode, the associated pipe/layermixers double buffered registers back copies are updated with the new values at the vsync boundary only when the flush mask bit has already been written a 1.
Each flush mask bit would also returned a 0 once the back copies are updated.

Before the back copies are updated, the associate mask bit would returned a 1 if it has been previously written a 1.

| 9 | LAYER_MIXER_3 | Layer Mixer3 registers are ready for flush<br>This includes the cursor registers stored in the layer mixer register space |
| 8 | LAYER_MIXER_2 | Layer Mixer2 registers are ready for flush<br>This includes the cursor registers stored in the layer mixer register space |

### MDSS_MDP_CTL_3_CTL_START (0x01A0261C)

* **Type**: W
* **Reset State**: 0x00000000

Overlay Processor Start Signal for the given Control Operation

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 0 | START | A write to this register will kick off operation for the given operation control and activate all layers |

### MDSS_MDP_CTL_3_SW_RESET (0x01A02630)

* **Type**: RW
* **Reset State**: 0x00000000

Software Reset of the given control operation

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 0 | RESET | Writing to this bit will trigger a soft reset for the described data path. This register is self-clearing and will return 0x1 if soft reset sequence is not complete. Upon completion, this will return 0x0. Note that this will soft reset the peripheral display interfaces that are described in this path. i.e. if driving intf_0 it will reset the pixel clock domain of intf_0 as well. |

### MDSS_MDP_CTL_3_SW_RESET_OVERRIDE (0x01A02634)

* **Type**: RW
* **Reset State**: 0x00000000
<!-- page 3202 -->

### MDSS_MDP_CTL_3_SW_RESET_OVERRIDE (cont.)

Software Reset Override of the given control operation

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 0 | RESET | Writing to this bit will assert reset for the described data path. The value contained in this register will be forced onto the datapath. It will reset the state machines within the scheduler as well for the given datapath. To use this register sequence, SW shall write a value of 0x1 to this register to assert reset. Once SW wants to de-assert reset, SW shall write a value of 0x0. SW will need to ensure the duration of the value 0x1 is long enough to ensure the path is clean and all memory reads are complete. The datapath will not be triggered if this bit is asserted. |

### MDSS_MDP_CTL_4_TOP

**Address**: `0x01A02814`
**Type**: `RW`
**Reset State**: `0x00001F00`

**Description**:
Operation Mode Configuration for the Pipeline.

The purpose of the register is to define the complete data path of this operation and that includes all the way to the interfaces such as DSI/HDMI/eDP.

Changing of the data path dynamically is NOT supported and requires stopping that data path, reconfiguring the connections, and restarting the datapath.
<!-- page 3213 -->
### MDSS_MDP_CTL_4_TOP (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 17 | MODE_SEL | Interface Mode of the destination interface<br>Needed to distinguish interfaces such as DSI that can be either mode<br>DSI can also interleave streams of different types (i.e. command and video) to a single core<br>0x0: Video Mode<br>0x1: Command Mode 1 |
| 16:15 | STREAM_SEL | Stream Identification<br>Used For Interleaving of Command Streams<br>This field is a dont care for video mode streams<br>0x0: Stream 0<br>0x1: Stream 1<br>0x2: Stream 2 |
| 7:4 | OUT_SEL | Output Ping-Pong Interface Connection to external display interface<br>0x0: No connection from Ping-Pong buffers to output interfaces<br>0x1: Interface 0<br>0x2: Interface 1<br>0x3: Interface 2<br>0x4: Interface 3 |
| 3:0 | MEM_SEL | Memory Output Connection<br>0x0: NO memory output selected<br>0x1: Memory BLOCK mode output selected for rotation 0<br>0x2: Memory BLOCK mode output selected for rotation 1<br>0x3: Memory LINE mode output selected for rotation 0<br>0x4: Memory LINE mode output selected for rotation 1<br>0x5: Memory LINE mode output selected for linear memory writeback |

### MDSS_MDP_CTL_4_FLUSH

**Address**: `0x01A02818`
**Type**: `RW`
**Reset State**: `0x00000000`

**Description**:
Register Flush register

The flush register is used to indicate a pipe/layermixers registers are all programmed, and are safe to update to the back copy of the double buffered registers.
<!-- page 3214 -->
### MDSS_MDP_CTL_4_FLUSH (cont.)

Each pipes/layermixers flush mask bit will be used only when the associated pipe/layermixer is running at active refresh pull mode, e.g., direct out going to LCDC/HDMI/DSI Video.

In such operation mode, the associated pipe/layermixers double buffered registers back copies are updated with the new values at the vsync boundary only when the flush mask bit has already been written a 1.
Each flush mask bit would also returned a 0 once the back copies are updated.

Before the back copies are updated, the associate mask bit would returned a 1 if it has been previously written a 1.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 30 | TIMING_1 | Timing Interface 1 are ready for flush |
| 17 | CTL | Control Pipe register is ready for flush<br>This applies to upper pipe ONLY to change the adding/removal of layers |
| 16 | WB | Write Back registers are ready for flush |
| 15 | DSPP_2 | DSPP2 registers are ready for flush |
| 14 | DSPP_1 | DSPP1 registers are ready for flush |
| 13 | DSPP_0 | DSPP0 registers are ready for flush |
| 12 | DMA_1 | DMA_1 registers are ready for flush |
| 11 | DMA_0 | DMA_0 registers are ready for flush |
| 10 | LAYER_MIXER_4 | Layer Mixer4 registers are ready for flush<br>This includes the cursor registers stored in the layer mixer register space |
| 9 | LAYER_MIXER_3 | Layer Mixer3 registers are ready for flush<br>This includes the cursor registers stored in the layer mixer register space |
| 8 | LAYER_MIXER_2 | Layer Mixer2 registers are ready for flush<br>This includes the cursor registers stored in the layer mixer register space |
| 7 | LAYER_MIXER_1 | Layer Mixer1 registers are ready for flush<br>This includes the cursor registers stored in the layer mixer register space |
| 6 | LAYER_MIXER_0 | Layer Mixer0 registers are ready for flush<br>This includes the cursor registers stored in the layer mixer register space |
| 5 | RGB_2 | RGB2 registers are ready for flush |
| 4 | RGB_1 | RGB1 registers are ready for flush |
| 3 | RGB_0 | RGB0 registers are ready for flush |
<!-- page 3215 -->
### MDSS_MDP_CTL_4_FLUSH (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 2 | VIG_2 | VIG2 registers are ready for flush |
| 1 | VIG_1 | VIG1 registers are ready for flush |
| 0 | VIG_0 | VIG0 registers are ready for flush |

### MDSS_MDP_CTL_4_SW_RESET

**Address**: `0x01A02830`
**Type**: `RW`
**Reset State**: `0x00000000`

**Description**:
Software Reset of the given control operation

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 0 | RESET | Writing to this bit will trigger a soft reset for the described data path<br>This register is self-clearing and will return 0x1 if soft reset sequence is not complete<br>Upon completion, this will return 0x0<br>Note that this will soft reset the peripheral display interfaces that are described in this path<br>i.e. if driving intf_0 it will reset the pixel clock domain of intf_0 as well |

### MDSS_MDP_CTL_4_SW_RESET_OVERRIDE

**Address**: `0x01A02834`
**Type**: `RW`
**Reset State**: `0x00000000`
<!-- page 3216 -->
### MDSS_MDP_CTL_4_SW_RESET_OVERRIDE (cont.)

Software Reset Override of the given control operation

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 0 | RESET | Writing to this bit will assert reset for the described data path<br>This value contained in this register will be forced onto the datapath<br>It will reset the state machines within the scheduler as well for the given datapath<br>To use this register sequence, SW shall write a value of 0x1 to this register to assert reset<br>Once SW wants to de-assert reset, SW shall write a value of 0x0<br>SW will need to ensure the duration of the value 0x1 is long enough to ensure the path is clean and all memory reads are complete<br>The datapath will not be triggered if this bit is asserted |

### 0x01A052F0 MDSS_MDP_VP_0_VIG_0_PA_LUTV

**Type:** RW
**Reset State:** 0x00000000
**Description:** PA LUTV data. Auto-incremented by hardware or by software. 256 entries are available for reading.
**Double Buffered:** NO. Hardware maintains 2 copies

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 17 | VALUE_UPDATEN | Software issue a write to the LUT<br>0: VALUE will be written to RAM at INDEX if INDEX_UPDATE=1 or at INDEX+1 if INDEX_UPDATE=0<br>1: VALUE will not be written to RAM, this setting is appropriate for example when INDEX needs to be updated for read |
| 16 | INDEX_UPDATE | Software issue an index update<br>0: No index update by software<br>1: Update LUT index to value specified by INDEX |
| 15:8 | INDEX | VALUE is stored in this INDEX of the HIST_LUTn, next write will be stored to the next higher INDEX |
| 7:0 | VALUE | Value read depends on the LUT select and which one is available for reading by software<br>The read sequence should always begin with WR INDEX_UPDATE=1, INDEX=\<rptr start location\><br>subsequent RD will start from the start location and every read will auto-increment the rptr |
