### 0x01A05050 MDSS_MDP_VP_0_VIG_0_SSPP_REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_0

**Type:** RW
**Reset State:** 0x00000040

FIFO watermark to aid in generation of mdpREQPRIORITY
<!-- page 3252 -->

### MDSS_MDP_VP_0_VIG_0_SSPP_REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_0 (cont.)

The watermark here refers to the # of 128-entries available in the Shared Memory Pool

The value programmed here should be aware of the amount programmed in the Shared Memory Pool.

So a value of 0 indicates completely FULL (i.e. there are no more entries available in the SMP)

A value of 100 indicates 100 entries in the Shared Memory Pool (each entry being 128-bit entries)

This is the lowestmost FIFO depth and should not be programmed higher than REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_1 or REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_2

An example programming would set the following:
* REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_0 : 50 (meaning 50 entries free to be written into SMP - least room available)
* REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_1 : 100 (meaning 100 entries free to be written into SMP - middle ground room available)
* REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_2 : 150 (meaning 150 entries free to be written into SMP - most room available)

* mdpREQPRIORITY = 11 (highest priority request) when above all 3 watermark levels (i.e. lots of space available in SMP)
* mdpREQPRIORITY = 10 above FIFO_0 and FIFO_1 but below FIFO_2
* mdpREQPRIORITY = 01 above FIFO_0 but below FIFO_1 and FIFO_2
* mdpREQPRIORITY = 00 (lowest priority request) when below all 3 watermark levels (i.e. not a lot of space available in SMP so its good)

**double buffered:** YES

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 15:0 | WATERMARK | Watermark Level for FIFO_0 |

### 0x01A05054 MDSS_MDP_VP_0_VIG_0_SSPP_REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_1

**Type:** RW
**Reset State:** 0x00000080

FIFO watermark to aid in generation of mdpREQPRIORITY

The watermark here refers to the # of 128-entries available in the Shared Memory Pool

The value programmed here should be aware of the amount programmed in the Shared Memory Pool.

So a value of 0 indicates completely FULL (i.e. there are no more entries available in the SMP)
<!-- page 3253 -->

### MDSS_MDP_VP_0_VIG_0_SSPP_REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_1 (cont.)

A value of 100 indicates 100 entries in the Shared Memory Pool (each entry being 128-bit entries)

This is the middle FIFO depth and should not be programmed higher than REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_2 or lower than REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_0

An example programming would set the following:
* REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_0 : 50 (meaning 50 entries free to be written into SMP - least room available)
* REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_1 : 100 (meaning 100 entries free to be written into SMP - middle ground room available)
* REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_2 : 150 (meaning 150 entries free to be written into SMP - most room available)

* mdpREQPRIORITY = 11 (highest priority request) when above all 3 watermark levels (i.e. lots of space available in SMP)
* mdpREQPRIORITY = 10 above FIFO_0 and FIFO_1 but below FIFO_2
* mdpREQPRIORITY = 01 above FIFO_0 but below FIFO_1 and FIFO_2
* mdpREQPRIORITY = 00 (lowest priority request) when below all 3 watermark levels (i.e. not a lot of space available in SMP so its good)

**double buffered:** YES

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 15:0 | WATERMARK | Watermark Level for FIFO_1 |

### 0x01A05058 MDSS_MDP_VP_0_VIG_0_SSPP_REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_2

**Type:** RW
**Reset State:** 0x000000C0

FIFO watermark to aid in generation of mdpREQPRIORITY

The watermark here refers to the # of 128-entries available in the Shared Memory Pool

The value programmed here should be aware of the amount programmed in the Shared Memory Pool.

So a value of 0 indicates completely FULL (i.e. there are no more entries available in the SMP)

A value of 100 indicates 100 entries in the Shared Memory Pool (each entry being 128-bit entries)

This is the highest FIFO depth and should not be programmed lower than REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_0 or REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_1
<!-- page 3254 -->

### MDSS_MDP_VP_0_VIG_0_SSPP_REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_2 (cont.)

An example programming would set the following:
* REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_0 : 50 (meaning 50 entries free to be written into SMP - least room available)
* REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_1 : 100 (meaning 100 entries free to be written into SMP - middle ground room available)
* REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_2 : 150 (meaning 150 entries free to be written into SMP - most room available)

* mdpREQPRIORITY = 11 (highest priority request) when above all 3 watermark levels (i.e. lots of space available in SMP)
* mdpREQPRIORITY = 10 above FIFO_0 and FIFO_1 but below FIFO_2
* mdpREQPRIORITY = 01 above FIFO_0 but below FIFO_1 and FIFO_2
* mdpREQPRIORITY = 00 (lowest priority request) when below all 3 watermark levels (i.e. not a lot of space available in SMP so its good)

**double buffered:** YES

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 15:0 | WATERMARK | Watermark Level for FIFO_2 |

### 0x01A05070 MDSS_MDP_VP_0_VIG_0_SSPP_SRC_ADDR_SW_STATUS

**Type:** RW
**Reset State:** 0x00000000

Security Status of the source buffer plane

This is programmed by SW to indicate if the buffer is NON-SECURE or SECURE

This information will be presented to VBIF per transaction and reflected as part of the memory transaction

**double buffered:** YES
<!-- page 3255 -->

### MDSS_MDP_VP_0_VIG_0_SSPP_SRC_ADDR_SW_STATUS (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 3 | SRC3_ADDR_CP | This is the secure status bit for source plane 3 (if used)<br>If the format doesnt fetch from that plane then this value is ignored<br>Memory transactions will not complete if this status doesnt corespond to system programming in the rest of the path to memory<br>SW should program SRC0_ADDR_CP, SRC1_ADDR_CP, SRC2_ADDR_CP, SRC3_ADDR_CP to the same value<br>0x0: Non Content Protected Buffer State<br>0x1: Content Protected Buffer State |
| 2 | SRC2_ADDR_CP | This is the secure status bit for source plane 2 (if used)<br>If the format doesnt fetch from that plane then this value is ignored<br>Memory transactions will not complete if this status doesnt corespond to system programming in the rest of the path to memory<br>SW should program SRC0_ADDR_CP, SRC1_ADDR_CP, SRC2_ADDR_CP, SRC3_ADDR_CP to the same value<br>0x0: Non Content Protected Buffer State<br>0x1: Content Protected Buffer State |
| 1 | SRC1_ADDR_CP | This is the secure status bit for source plane 1 (if used)<br>If the format doesnt fetch from that plane then this value is ignored<br>Memory transactions will not complete if this status doesnt corespond to system programming in the rest of the path to memory<br>SW should program SRC0_ADDR_CP, SRC1_ADDR_CP, SRC2_ADDR_CP, SRC3_ADDR_CP to the same value<br>0x0: Non Content Protected Buffer State<br>0x1: Content Protected Buffer State |
| 0 | SRC0_ADDR_CP | This is the secure status bit for source plane 0 (if used)<br>If the format doesnt fetch from that plane then this value is ignored<br>Memory transactions will not complete if this status doesnt corespond to system programming in the rest of the path to memory<br>SW should program SRC0_ADDR_CP, SRC1_ADDR_CP, SRC2_ADDR_CP, SRC3_ADDR_CP to the same value<br>0x0: Non Content Protected Buffer State<br>0x1: Content Protected Buffer State |

### 0x01A050B4 MDSS_MDP_VP_0_VIG_0_SSPP_DECIMATION_CONFIG

**Type:** RW
**Reset State:** 0x00000000

Decimation Configuration

Note that there is no decimation on DMA pipe which means no decimation in line mode on DMA or block mode

**double buffered:** YES

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 11:8 | HORZ_S | Horizontal Configuration for decimation; required to support downscaling greater than 1/4<br>S refers to the number of pixels skipped.<br>The algorithm is always the following: read 1 pixel skip S pixels<br>The algorithm is applied to ALL components.<br>Decimation only supports the following values. All other values will result in undefined behaviour<br>The decimation block will provide coarse scaling and should be used in conjunction with qseed2 to support all scaling ratios.<br>0x0: No decimation is performed<br>0x1: Read 1 pixel drop 1 pixel. Used to decimate by 2 horizontally<br>0x3: Read 1 pixel drop 3 pixels. Used to decimate by 4 horizontally<br>0x7: Read 1 pixel drop 7 pixels. Used to decimate by 8 horizontally<br>0xF: Read 1 pixel drop 15 pixels. Used to decimate by 16 horizontally |
<!-- page 3258 -->

### MDSS_MDP_VP_0_VIG_0_SSPP_DECIMATION_CONFIG (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 3:0 | VERT_S | Vertical Configuration for decimation; required to support downscaling greater than 1/4<br>S refers to the number of lines skipped.<br>The algorithm is always the following: read 1 line skip S lines<br>The algorithm is applied to ALL components.<br>Decimation only supports the following values. All other values will result in undefined behaviour<br>The decimation block will provide coarse scaling and should be used in conjunction with qseed2 to support all scaling ratios.<br>0x0: No decimation is performed<br>0x1: Read 1 line drop 1 line. Used to decimate by 2 horizontally<br>0x3: Read 1 line drop 3 lines. Used to decimate by 4 horizontally<br>0x7: Read 1 line drop 7 lines. Used to decimate by 8 horizontally<br>0xF: Read 1 line drop 15 lines. Used to decimate by 16 horizontally |

## 0x01A072F0 MDSS_MDP_VP_0_VIG_1_PA_LUTV

**Type:** RW  
**Reset State:** 0x00000000

PA LUTV data

Auto-incremented by hardware or by software

256 entries are available for reading  
double buffered: NO. Hardware maintains 2 copies

### MDSS_MDP_VP_0_VIG_1_PA_LUTV

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 17 | VALUE_UPDATEN | Software issue an write to the LUT<br>0: VALUE will be written to RAM at INDEX if INDEX_UPDATE=1 or at INDEX+1 if INDEX_UPDATE=0<br>1: VALUE will not be written to RAM, this setting is appropriate for example when INDEX needs to be updated for read |
| 16 | INDEX_UPDATE | Software issue an index update<br>0: No index update by software<br>1: Update LUT index to value specified by INDEX |
| 15:8 | INDEX | VALUE is stored in this INDEX of the HIST_LUTn, next write will be stored to the next higher INDEX |
| 7:0 | VALUE | Value read depends on the LUT select and which one is available for reading by software<br>The read sequence should always begin with WR INDEX_UPDATE=1, INDEX=\&lt;rptr start location\&gt;<br>subsequent RD will start from the start location and every read will auto-increment the rptr |
<!-- page 3282 -->

### MDSS_MDP_VP_0_VIG_1_SSPP_REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_0

* **Address:** `0x01A07050`
* **Type:** RW
* **Reset State:** `0x00000040`

FIFO watermark to aid in generation of mdpREQPRIORITY.
The watermark here refers to the # of 128-entries available in the Shared Memory Pool.

The value programmed here should be aware of the amount programmed in the Shared Memory Pool.

So a value of 0 indicates completely FULL (i.e. there are no more entries available in the SMP)

A value of 100 indicates 100 entries in the Shared Memory Pool (each entry being 128-bit entries)

This is the lowestmost FIFO depth and should not be programmed higher than REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_1 or REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_2.

An example programming would set the following:
* REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_0 : 50 (meaning 50 entries free to be written into SMP - least room available)
* REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_1 : 100 (meaning 100 entries free to be written into SMP - middle ground room available)
* REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_2 : 150 (meaning 150 entries free to be written into SMP - most room available)

* mdpREQPRIORITY = 11 (highest priority request) when above all 3 watermark levels (i.e. lots of space available in SMP)
* mdpREQPRIORITY = 10 above FIFO_0 and FIFO_1 but below FIFO_2
* mdpREQPRIORITY = 01 above FIFO_0 but below FIFO_1 and FIFO_2
* mdpREQPRIORITY = 00 (lowest priority request) when below all 3 watermark levels (i.e. not a lot of space available in SMP so its good)

* **double buffered:** YES
<!-- page 3302 -->

### MDSS_MDP_VP_0_VIG_1_SSPP_REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_0 (continued)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 15:0 | WATERMARK | Watermark Level for FIFO_0 |

### MDSS_MDP_VP_0_VIG_1_SSPP_SRC_ADDR_SW_STATUS

* **Address:** `0x01A07070`
* **Type:** RW
* **Reset State:** `0x00000000`

Security Status of the source buffer plane.
This is programmed by SW to indicate if the buffer is NON-SECURE or SECURE.
This information will be presented to VBIF per transaction and reflected as part of the memory transaction.

* **double buffered:** YES

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 3 | SRC3_ADDR_CP | This is the secure status bit for source plane 3 (if used).<br>If the format doesn't fetch from that plane then this value is ignored.<br>Memory transactions will not complete if this status doesn't correspond to system programming in the rest of the path to memory.<br>SW should program SRC0_ADDR_CP, SRC1_ADDR_CP, SRC2_ADDR_CP, SRC3_ADDR_CP to the same value.<br>0x0: Non Content Protected Buffer State<br>0x1: Content Protected Buffer State |
| 2 | SRC2_ADDR_CP | This is the secure status bit for source plane 2 (if used).<br>If the format doesn't fetch from that plane then this value is ignored.<br>Memory transactions will not complete if this status doesn't correspond to system programming in the rest of the path to memory.<br>SW should program SRC0_ADDR_CP, SRC1_ADDR_CP, SRC2_ADDR_CP, SRC3_ADDR_CP to the same value.<br>0x0: Non Content Protected Buffer State<br>0x1: Content Protected Buffer State |
| 1 | SRC1_ADDR_CP | This is the secure status bit for source plane 1 (if used).<br>If the format doesn't fetch from that plane then this value is ignored.<br>Memory transactions will not complete if this status doesn't correspond to system programming in the rest of the path to memory.<br>SW should program SRC0_ADDR_CP, SRC1_ADDR_CP, SRC2_ADDR_CP, SRC3_ADDR_CP to the same value.<br>0x0: Non Content Protected Buffer State<br>0x1: Content Protected Buffer State |

### MDSS_MDP_VP_0_VIG_1_SSPP_DECIMATION_CONFIG

* **Address:** `0x01A070B4`
* **Type:** RW
* **Reset State:** `0x00000000`

Decimation Configuration.
Note that there is no decimation on DMA pipe which means no decimation in line mode on DMA or block mode.

* **double buffered:** YES
<!-- page 3307 -->

### MDSS_MDP_VP_0_VIG_1_SSPP_DECIMATION_CONFIG (continued)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 11:8 | HORZ_S | Horizontal Configuration for decimation; required to support downscaling greater than 1/4.<br>S refers to the number of pixels skipped.<br>The algorithm is always the following: read 1 pixel skip S pixels. The algorithm is applied to ALL components.<br>Decimation only supports the following values. All other values will result in undefined behaviour.<br>The decimation block will provide coarse scaling and should be used in conjunction with qseed2 to support all scaling ratios.<br>0x0: No decimation is performed<br>0x1: Read 1 pixel drop 1 pixel. Used to decimate by 2 horizontally<br>0x3: Read 1 pixel drop 3 pixels. Used to decimate by 4 horizontally<br>0x7: Read 1 pixel drop 7 pixels. Used to decimate by 8 horizontally<br>0xF: Read 1 pixel drop 15 pixels. Used to decimate by 16 horizontally |
| 3:0 | VERT_S | Vertical Configuration for decimation; required to support downscaling greater than 1/4.<br>S refers to the number of lines skipped.<br>The algorithm is always the following: read 1 line skip S lines. The algorithm is applied to ALL components.<br>Decimation only supports the following values. All other values will result in undefined behaviour.<br>The decimation block will provide coarse scaling and should be used in conjunction with qseed2 to support all scaling ratios.<br>0x0: No decimation is performed<br>0x1: Read 1 line drop 1 line. Used to decimate by 2 horizontally [sic]<br>0x3: Read 1 line drop 3 lines. Used to decimate by 4 horizontally [sic]<br>0x7: Read 1 line drop 7 lines. Used to decimate by 8 horizontally [sic]<br>0xF: Read 1 line drop 15 lines. Used to decimate by 16 horizontally [sic] |

## Register: MDSS_MDP_VP_0_VIG_2_OP_MODE

**Address**: `0x01A09200`
**Type**: RW
**Reset State**: `0x00040000`
**Double Buffered**: YES (when: On frame boundaries (vsync or SW trigger))

Virtual Pipeline operation mode

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 28 | PA_CONT_MASK | 0x0: Disable HSIC adj on CONTRAST<br>0x1: Enable HSIC adj on CONTRAST |
| 27 | PA_VAL_MASK | 0x0: Disable HSIC adj on VALUE<br>0x1: Enable HSIC adj on VALUE |
| 26 | PA_SAT_MASK | 0x0: Disable HSIC adj on SATURATION<br>0x1: Enable HSIC adj on SATURATION |
| 25 | PA_HUE_MASK | 0x0: Disable HSIC adj on HUE<br>0x1: Enable HSIC adj on HUE |
| 19 | CSC_DST_DATA_FORMAT | Destination Data Format<br>0x0: RGB<br>0x1: YCbCr |
| 18 | CSC_SRC_DATA_FORMAT | Source Data Format<br>0x0: RGB<br>0x1: YCbCr |
<!-- page 3316 -->

### MDSS_MDP_VP_0_VIG_2_OP_MODE (continued)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 17 | CSC_1_EN | Enables the color matrix conversion 1<br>0x0: Bypass<br>0x1: Enabled |
| 10 | PA_LUTV_EN | Histogram Enhancement Lookup Table enable |
| 8 | HIST_EN | Histogram Enable<br>0x0: Disabled<br>0x1: Enabled |
| 7 | PA_MEM_COL_SKY_MASK | 0x0: Disable Sky adjustment<br>0x1: Enable Sky adjustment |
| 6 | PA_MEM_COL_FOL_MASK | 0x0: Disable Foliage adjustment<br>0x1: Enable Foliage adjustment |
| 5 | PA_MEM_COL_SKIN_MASK | 0x0: Disable Skin adjustment<br>0x1: Enable Skin adjustment |
| 4 | PA_EN | Enable Picture Adjustment<br>0x0: Disabled<br>0x1: Enabled |
| 3 | PA_MEM_PROTECT_ENABLE | 0: global hsv adjustment is independent of memory color<br>1: global hsv adjustment is active if the pixel is not already processed by memory color<br>contrast adjustment in global adjustment is always independent of memory color regardless |
| 2 | PA_SAT_ZERO_EXP_ENABLE | 0: if PA_SAT_ADJ < -32, clamp PA_SAT_ADJ to 0<br>1: if PA_SAT_ADJ < -64, clamp PA_SAT_ADJ to 0 |

### 0x01A092F0 MDSS_MDP_VP_0_VIG_2_PA_LUTV

- **Type**: RW
- **Reset State**: 0x00000000
- **Description**: PA LUTV data. Auto-incremented by hardware or by software. 256 entries are available for reading
- **Double Buffered**: NO. Hardware maintains 2 copies


<!-- page 3331 -->
### MDSS_MDP_VP_0_VIG_2_PA_LUTV (continued)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 17 | VALUE_UPDATEN | Software issue an write to the LUT<br>0: VALUE will be written to RAM at INDEX if INDEX_UPDATE=1 or at INDEX+1 if INDEX_UPDATE=0<br>1: VALUE will not be written to RAM, this setting is appropriate for example when INDEX needs to be updated for read |
| 16 | INDEX_UPDATE | Software issue an index update<br>0: No index update by software<br>1: Update LUT index to value specified by INDEX |
| 15:8 | INDEX | VALUE is stored in this INDEX of the HIST_LUTn, next write will be stored to the next higher INDEX |
| 7:0 | VALUE | Value read depends on the LUT select and which one is available for reading by software<br>The read sequence should always begin with<br>WR INDEX_UPDATE=1, INDEX=\<rptr start location\><br>subsequent RD will start from the start location and every read will auto-increment the rptr |

## MDSS_MDP_VP_0_VIG_2_SSPP_REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_0

**Address:** `0x01A09050`
**Type:** RW
**Reset State:** `0x00000040`

FIFO watermark to aid in generation of mdpREQPRIORITY
The watermark here refers to the # of 128-entries available in the Shared Memory Pool
The value programmed here should be aware of the amount programmed in the Shared Memory Pool.
So a value of 0 indicates completely FULL (i.e. there are no more entries available in the SMP)
A value of 100 indicates 100 entries in the Shared Memory Pool (each entry being 128-bit entries)


<!-- page 3351 -->

This is the lowestmost FIFO depth and should not be programmed higher than REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_1 or REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_2

An example programming would set the following:
* REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_0 : 50 (meaning 50 entries free to be written into SMP - least room available)
* REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_1 : 100 (meaning 100 entries free to be written into SMP - middle ground room available)
* REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_2 : 150 (meaning 150 entries free to be written into SMP - most room available)

* mdpREQPRIORITY = 11 (highest priority request) when above all 3 watermark levels (i.e. lots of space available in SMP)
* mdpREQPRIORITY = 10 above FIFO_0 and FIFO_1 but below FIFO_2
* mdpREQPRIORITY = 01 above FIFO_0 but below FIFO_1 and FIFO_2
* mdpREQPRIORITY = 00 (lowest priority request) when below all 3 watermark levels (i.e. not a lot of space available in SMP so its good)

double buffered: YES

### MDSS_MDP_VP_0_VIG_2_SSPP_REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_0

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 15:0 | WATERMARK | Watermark Level for FIFO_0 |

- **Type**: RW

This information will be presented to VBIF per transaction and reflected as part of the memory transaction

### 0x01A090B4 MDSS_MDP_VP_0_VIG_2_SSPP_DECIMATION_CONFIG

- **Type**: RW
- **Reset State**: 0x00000000

Decimation Configuration

Note that there is no decimation on DMA pipe which means no decimation in line mode on DMA or block mode

double buffered: YES

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 11:8 | HORZ_S | Horizontal Configuration for decimation; required to support downscaling greater than 1/4<br>S refers to the number of pixels skipped.<br>The algorithm is always the following: read 1 pixel skip S pixels<br>The algorithm is applied to ALL components.<br>Decimation only supports the following values. All other values will result in undefined behaviour<br>The decimation block will provide coarse scaling and should be used in conjunction with qseed2 to support all scaling ratios.<br>0x0: No decimation is performed<br>0x1: Read 1 pixel drop 1 pixel. Used to decimate by 2 horizontally<br>0x3: Read 1 pixel drop 3 pixels. Used to decimate by 4 horizontally<br>0x7: Read 1 pixel drop 7 pixels. Used to decimate by 8 horizontally<br>0xF: Read 1 pixel drop 15 pixels. Used to decimate by 16 horizontally |
| 3:0 | VERT_S | Vertical Configuration for decimation; required to support downscaling greater than 1/4<br>S refers to the number of lines skipped.<br>The algorithm is always the following: read 1 line skip S lines<br>The algorithm is applied to ALL components.<br>Decimation only supports the following values. All other values will result in undefined behaviour<br>The decimation block will provide coarse scaling and should be used in conjunction with qseed2 to support all scaling ratios.<br>0x0: No decimation is performed<br>0x1: Read 1 line drop 1 line. Used to decimate by 2 horizontally<br>0x3: Read 1 line drop 3 lines. Used to decimate by 4 horizontally<br>0x7: Read 1 line drop 7 lines. Used to decimate by 8 horizontally<br>0xF: Read 1 line drop 15 lines. Used to decimate by 16 horizontally |
<!-- page 3357 -->

### MDSS_MDP_VP_0_RGB_0_SSPP_SRC_FORMAT (continued)

* **When:** On frame boundaries (vsync or SW trigger)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:30 | FRAME_FORMAT | Frame format<br>In the current revision, there is no support for tiled formats<br>0x0: Linear, no tile<br>0x1: Tiled, 4x4 |
| 25:23 | SRC_CHROMA_SAMP | Source Chroma Sampling<br>0x0: RGB/YUV 4:4:4<br>0x1: 4:2:2 - H2V1<br>0x2: 4:2:2 - H1V2<br>0x3: 4:2:0 - N2V1<br>0x4: 4:2:0 - N1V2 |
| 22 | SOLID_FILL | Fetch feeds the lower pipeline with the CONSTANT_COLOR register as its output value.<br>NOTHING is fetched<br>Note that in order to use this feature then Interleaved FETCH_PLANES must be set as well and no chroma sub-sampling enabled |
| 21 | VC1_REDUCE | VC1 range reduction enable for YUV sources<br>The reduce range is set by separate register VC1_RANGE |
| 20:19 | FETCH_PLANES | Determines the number of planes to fetch<br>0x0: Interleaved<br>0x1: Planar<br>0x2: Pseudo-planar |
| 18 | UNPACK_ALIGN | 0x0: TO LSB<br>0x1: TO MSB |
| 17 | UNPACK_TIGHT | 0x0: Loose<br>0x1: Tight |
| 13:12 | UNPACK_COUNT | Valid unpacking pattern count<br>0x0 = 1 component<br>0x1 = 2 components<br>...<br>0x3 = 4 components<br>Unpacking applies to interleaved plane (chroma plane in pseudo-planar |
| 11 | ROT90 | Source image is to be rotated 90 degrees |
| 10:9 | SRC_BPP | Effective source byte per pixel<br>0x0: 1 byte<br>0x1: 2 bytes<br>0x2: 3 bytes<br>0x3: 4 bytes<br>This is used ONLY when unpacking the interleaved plane |

| 5:4 | SRCC2 | Number of bits for component 2 (R/Cr)<br>0x0: 4 bits<br>0x1: 5 bits<br>0x2: 6 bits<br>0x3: 8 bits |

### MDSS_MDP_VP_0_RGB_0_SSPP_REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_0
**Address:** `0x01A15050`  
**Type:** `RW`  
**Reset State:** `0x00000040`  

FIFO watermark to aid in generation of mdpREQPRIORITY
<!-- page 3375 -->
### MDSS_MDP_VP_0_RGB_0_SSPP_REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_0 (cont.)

The watermark here refers to the # of 128-entries available in the Shared Memory Pool.
The value programmed here should be aware of the amount programmed in the Shared Memory Pool.

So a value of 0 indicates completely FULL (i.e. there are no more entries available in the SMP).
A value of 100 indicates 100 entries in the Shared Memory Pool (each entry being 128-bit entries).
This is the lowestmost FIFO depth and should not be programmed higher than `REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_1` or `REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_2`.

An example programming would set the following:
* `REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_0` : 50 (meaning 50 entries free to be written into SMP - least room available)
* `REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_1` : 100 (meaning 100 entries free to be written into SMP - middle ground room available)
* `REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_2` : 150 (meaning 150 entries free to be written into SMP - most room available)

* `mdpREQPRIORITY` = 11 (highest priority request) when above all 3 watermark levels (i.e. lots of space available in SMP)
* `mdpREQPRIORITY` = 10 above FIFO_0 and FIFO_1 but below FIFO_2
* `mdpREQPRIORITY` = 01 above FIFO_0 but below FIFO_1 and FIFO_2
* `mdpREQPRIORITY` = 00 (lowest priority request) when below all 3 watermark levels (i.e. not a lot of space available in SMP so its good)

**Double Buffered:** YES

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 15:0 | WATERMARK | Watermark Level for FIFO_0 |

---

| 1 | SRC1_ADDR_CP | Secure status bit for source plane 1 (if used).<br>If the format doesn't fetch from that plane then this value is ignored.<br>Memory transactions will not complete if this status doesn't correspond to system programming in the rest of the path to memory.<br>SW should program SRC0_ADDR_CP, SRC1_ADDR_CP, SRC2_ADDR_CP, SRC3_ADDR_CP to the same value.<br>0x0: Non Content Protected Buffer State<br>0x1: Content Protected Buffer State |

### 0x01A17050 MDSS_MDP_VP_0_RGB_1_SSPP_REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_0

* **Type**: RW
* **Reset State**: 0x00000040
* **Double Buffered**: YES

FIFO watermark to aid in generation of mdpREQPRIORITY

The watermark here refers to the # of 128-entries available in the Shared Memory Pool

The value programmed here should be aware of the amount programmed in the Shared Memory Pool.

So a value of 0 indicates completely FULL (i.e. there are no more entries available in the SMP)

A value of 100 indicates 100 entries in the Shared Memory Pool (each entry being 128-bit entries)

This is the lowestmost FIFO depth and should not be programmed higher than REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_1 or REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_2

An example programming would set the following:
* **REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_0** : 50 (meaning 50 entries free to be written into SMP - least room available)
* **REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_1** : 100 (meaning 100 entries free to be written into SMP - middle ground room available)
* **REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_2** : 150 (meaning 150 entries free to be written into SMP - most room available)

Priority levels:
* **mdpREQPRIORITY = 11** (highest priority request) when above all 3 watermark levels (i.e. lots of space available in SMP)
* **mdpREQPRIORITY = 10** above FIFO_0 and FIFO_1 but below FIFO_2
* **mdpREQPRIORITY = 01** above FIFO_0 but below FIFO_1 and FIFO_2
* **mdpREQPRIORITY = 00** (lowest priority request) when below all 3 watermark levels (i.e. not a lot of space available in SMP so its good)
<!-- page 3400 -->

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 15:0 | WATERMARK | Watermark Level for FIFO_0 |

| 1 | SRC1_ADDR_CP | This is the secure status bit for source plane 1 (if used)<br>If the format doesn't fetch from that plane then this value is ignored<br>Memory transactions will not complete if this status doesn't correspond to system programming in the rest of the path to memory<br>SW should program SRC0_ADDR_CP, SRC1_ADDR_CP, SRC2_ADDR_CP, SRC3_ADDR_CP to the same value<br>0x0: Non Content Protected Buffer State<br>0x1: Content Protected Buffer State |

**Address:** `0x01A170B4`
**Type:** RW
**Reset State:** `0x00000000`
**Double Buffered:** YES

Decimation Configuration

Note that there is no decimation on DMA pipe which means no decimation in line mode on DMA or block mode
<!-- page 3405 -->

### MDSS_MDP_VP_0_RGB_1_SSPP_DECIMATION_CONFIG (continued)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 11:8 | HORZ_S | Horizontal Configuration for decimation; required to support downscaling greater than 1/4<br>S refers to the number of pixels skipped.<br>The algorithm is always the following: read 1 pixel skip S pixels<br>The algorithm is applied to ALL components.<br>Decimation only supports the following values. All other values will result in undefined behaviour<br>The decimation block will provide coarse scaling and should be used in conjunction with qseed2 to support all scaling ratios.<br>0x0: No decimation is performed<br>0x1: Read 1 pixel drop 1 pixel. Used to decimate by 2 horizontally<br>0x3: Read 1 pixel drop 3 pixels. Used to decimate by 4 horizontally<br>0x7: Read 1 pixel drop 7 pixels. Used to decimate by 8 horizontally<br>0xF: Read 1 pixel drop 15 pixels. Used to decimate by 16 horizontally |
| 3:0 | VERT_S | Vertical Configuration for decimation; required to support downscaling greater than 1/4<br>S refers to the number of lines skipped.<br>The algorithm is always the following: read 1 line skip S lines<br>The algorithm is applied to ALL components.<br>Decimation only supports the following values. All other values will result in undefined behaviour<br>The decimation block will provide coarse scaling and should be used in conjunction with qseed2 to support all scaling ratios.<br>0x0: No decimation is performed<br>0x1: Read 1 line drop 1 line. Used to decimate by 2 horizontally<br>0x3: Read 1 line drop 3 lines. Used to decimate by 4 horizontally<br>0x7: Read 1 line drop 7 lines. Used to decimate by 8 horizontally<br>0xF: Read 1 line drop 15 lines. Used to decimate by 16 horizontally |

### MDSS_MDP_VP_0_RGB_2_SSPP_SRC_FORMAT (continued)

**When:** On frame boundaries (vsync or SW trigger)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:30 | FRAME_FORMAT | Frame format<br>In the current revision, there is no support for tiled formats<br>0x0: Linear, no tile<br>0x1: Tiled, 4x4 |
| 25:23 | SRC_CHROMA_SAMP | Source Chroma Sampling<br>0x0: RGB/YUV 4:4:4<br>0x1: 4:2:2 - H2V1<br>0x2: 4:2:2 - H1V2<br>0x3: 4:2:0 - N2V1<br>0x4: 4:2:0 - N1V2 |
| 22 | SOLID_FILL | Fetch feeds the lower pipeline with the CONSTANT_COLOR register as its output value.<br>NOTHING is fetched<br>Note that in order to use this feature then Interleaved FETCH_PLANES must be set as well and no chroma sub-sampling enabled |
| 21 | VC1_REDUCE | VC1 range reduction enable for YUV sources<br>The reduce range is set by separate register VC1_RANGE |
| 20:19 | FETCH_PLANES | Determines the number of planes to fetch<br>0x0: Interleaved<br>0x1: Planar<br>0x2: Pseudo-planar |
| 18 | UNPACK_ALIGN | 0x0: TO LSB<br>0x1: TO MSB |
| 17 | UNPACK_TIGHT | 0x0: Loose<br>0x1: Tight |
| 13:12 | UNPACK_COUNT | Valid unpacking pattern count<br>0x0 = 1 component<br>0x1 = 2 components<br>...<br>0x3 = 4 components<br>Unpacking applies to interleaved plane (chroma plane in pseudo-planar |
| 11 | ROT90 | Source image is to be rotated 90 degrees |
| 10:9 | SRC_BPP | Effective source byte per pixel<br>0x0: 1 byte<br>0x1: 2 bytes<br>0x2: 3 bytes<br>0x3: 4 bytes<br>This is used ONLY when unpacking the interleaved plane |

| 7:6 | SRCC3 | Number of bits for component 3 (Alpha)<br>0x0: 1 bits<br>0x1: 4 bits<br>0x2: 6 bits<br>0x3: 8 bits |
| 5:4 | SRCC2 | Number of bits for component 2 (R/Cr)<br>0x0: 4 bits<br>0x1: 5 bits<br>0x2: 6 bits<br>0x3: 8 bits |
| 3:2 | SRCC1 | Number of bits for component 1 (B/Cb)<br>0x0: 4 bits<br>0x1: 5 bits<br>0x2: 6 bits<br>0x3: 8 bits |
| 1:0 | SRCC0 | Number of bits for component 0 (G/Luma)<br>0x0: 4 bits<br>0x1: 5 bits<br>0x2: 6 bits<br>0x3: 8 bits |

### 0x01A19050 MDSS_MDP_VP_0_RGB_2_SSPP_REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_0

* **Type**: RW
* **Reset State**: 0x00000040
* **Description**: FIFO watermark to aid in generation of mdpREQPRIORITY
<!-- page 3424 -->

### MDSS_MDP_VP_0_RGB_2_SSPP_REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_0 (cont.)

* **Double buffered**: YES

The watermark here refers to the # of 128-entries available in the Shared Memory Pool.
The value programmed here should be aware of the amount programmed in the Shared Memory Pool.
So a value of 0 indicates completely FULL (i.e. there are no more entries available in the SMP).
A value of 100 indicates 100 entries in the Shared Memory Pool (each entry being 128-bit entries).
This is the lowestmost FIFO depth and should not be programmed higher than REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_1 or REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_2.

An example programming would set the following:
* `REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_0` : 50 (meaning 50 entries free to be written into SMP - least room available)
* `REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_1` : 100 (meaning 100 entries free to be written into SMP - middle ground room available)
* `REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_2` : 150 (meaning 150 entries free to be written into SMP - most room available)

Priority levels:
* `mdpREQPRIORITY = 11` (highest priority request) when above all 3 watermark levels (i.e. lots of space available in SMP)
* `mdpREQPRIORITY = 10` above FIFO_0 and FIFO_1 but below FIFO_2
* `mdpREQPRIORITY = 01` above FIFO_0 but below FIFO_1 and FIFO_2
* `mdpREQPRIORITY = 00` (lowest priority request) when below all 3 watermark levels (i.e. not a lot of space available in SMP so its good)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 15:0 | WATERMARK | Watermark Level for FIFO_0 |

* `mdpREQPRIORITY = 10` above FIFO_0 and FIFO_1 but below FIFO_2
* `mdpREQPRIORITY = 01` above FIFO_0 but below FIFO_1 and FIFO_2
* `mdpREQPRIORITY = 00` (lowest priority request) when below all 3 watermark levels (i.e. not a lot of space available in SMP so its good)

| Bits | Name | Description |

| 15:0 | WATERMARK | Watermark Level for FIFO_1 |

| 2 | SRC2_ADDR_CP | This is the secure status bit for source plane 2 (if used). | 1 | SRC1_ADDR_CP | This is the secure status bit for source plane 1 (if used). If the format doesn't fetch from that plane then this value is ignored.<br>Memory transactions will not complete if this status doesn't correspond to system programming in the rest of the path to memory.<br>SW should program SRC0_ADDR_CP, SRC1_ADDR_CP, SRC2_ADDR_CP, SRC3_ADDR_CP to the same value.<br>0x0: Non Content Protected Buffer State<br>0x1: Content Protected Buffer State |
| 0 | SRC0_ADDR_CP | This is the secure status bit for source plane 0 (if used). ## 17.17.7.9 MDSS_MDP_VP_0_LAYER_0
### Layer Mixer hardware register description

### 17.17.7.9.1 MDSS_MDP_VP_0_LAYER_0_LAYER
### LAYER
Layer Mixer hardware register description

### Register: MDSS_MDP_VP_0_LAYER_0_OP_MODE
* **Address**: `0x01A45000`
* **Type**: `RW`
* **Reset State**: `0x00000000`
* **Double Buffered**: `YES`
* **When**: On frame boundaries (vsync or SW trigger)

**Description**: LayerMixer Operation Control

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 4 | BLEND3_COLOR3_OUT | Selects which source to drive on color3 component output for stage3 blend. <br>0x0: BG Layer Color3 <br>0x1: FG Layer Color3 |
<!-- page 3439 -->

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 3 | BLEND2_COLOR3_OUT | Selects which source to drive on color3 component output for stage2 blend. <br>0x0: BG Layer Color3 <br>0x1: FG Layer Color3 |
| 2 | BLEND1_COLOR3_OUT | Selects which source to drive on color3 component output for stage1 blend. <br>0x0: BG Layer Color3 <br>0x1: FG Layer Color3 |
| 1 | BLEND0_COLOR3_OUT | Selects which source to drive on color3 component output for stage0 blend. <br>0x0: BG Layer Color3 <br>0x1: FG Layer Color3 |
| 0 | GC_LUT_EN | 0x0: Disabled - mapped linearly from 12-bit to 8-bit <br>0x1: Enabled |

### Register: MDSS_MDP_VP_0_LAYER_0_OUT_SIZE
* **Address**: `0x01A45004`
* **Type**: `RW`
* **Reset State**: `0x00000000`
* **Double Buffered**: `YES`
* **When**: On frame boundaries (vsync or SW trigger)

**Description**: LayerMixer Output Size

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:16 | DST_H | Destination Output Height |
| 15:0 | DST_W | Destination Output Width. <br>The exact supported size depends on the width of line buffers allocated for MDP. |

### Register: MDSS_MDP_VP_0_LAYER_0_BORDER_COLOR_0
* **Address**: `0x01A45008`
* **Type**: `RW`
* **Reset State**: `0x00000000`
* **Double Buffered**: `YES`

**Description**: LayerMixer Border Color Register
<!-- page 3440 -->

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 27:16 | COLOR1 | Color1 in 12-bit format |
| 11:0 | COLOR0 | Color0 in 12-bit format |

### Register: MDSS_MDP_VP_0_LAYER_0_BORDER_COLOR_1
* **Address**: `0x01A45010`
* **Type**: `RW`
* **Reset State**: `0x00000000`
* **Double Buffered**: `YES`

**Description**: LayerMixer Border Color Register

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |

| 11:0 | COLOR2 | Color2 in 12-bit format |

### Register: MDSS_MDP_VP_0_LAYER_0_BLEND0_OP
* **Address**: `0x01A45020`
* **Type**: `RW`
* **Reset State**: `0x00000000`
* **Double Buffered**: `YES`
* **When**: On frame boundaries (vsync or SW trigger)

**Description**: LayerMixer Blend0 Operation Control

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 13 | BG_TRANSP_EN | BG transparency enabled |
| 12 | BG_INV_MOD_ALPHA | Ability to select between alpha and inverse alpha right after the alpha modulation. <br>0x0: Alpha <br>0x1: Inverse Alpha |
| 11 | BG_MOD_ALPHA | Modulate BG Alpha |

| :--- | :--- | :--- |

| 5 | FG_TRANSP_EN | FG transparency enabled |

### MDSS_MDP_VP_0_LAYER_0_CURSOR_FETCH_CONFIG
**Address:** `0x01A45204`
* **Type:** RW
* **Reset State:** `0x00000087`

Cursor Client Fetch Configuration per Virtual Pipeline
This register must NOT be altered during operation and MDP must be idle when changing values

* **Double Buffered:** NO

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 17:16 | TILE_SIZE | Tile Size for processing of BLOCK formats<br>Note that this only applies to blocks that operate in block mode which is limited to DMA source pipe. This setting has no effect for all other source pipes (ViG/RGB)<br>0x0: 128x128<br>0x1: 64x64<br>0x2: 32x32 |
| 12 | ADDR_SYNC_MODE | Boundary on which fetch address synchronizes.<br>Setting this field to line forces the address updates on the next line which performs the software requested feature of updating on hsync.<br>Note that updating on line boundaries will likely result in tearing on the panel since hardware is fetching from new memory buffer.<br>0x0: frame (default)<br>0x1: line |
<!-- page 3467 -->

### MDSS_MDP_VP_0_LAYER_0_CURSOR_FETCH_CONFIG (continued)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 9:8 | MAL | Describes the Minimum Access Length for the source pipeline.<br>This value should align with the DRAM's expected transaction alignment unit.<br>This setting forces the source fetch pipe to be aligned to DRAM and implement re-alignment for maximum efficiency<br>0x0: 128b alignment (default)<br>0x1: 256b alignment<br>0x2: 512b alignment |
| 7:4 | MAX_BURST_SIZE | Maximum burst beat size.<br>Hardware fetch engines operate on 128-bit bus<br>Possible values:<br>0x8: burst of 8<br>0x4: burst of 4<br>0x2: burst of 2 |
| 3:0 | REQ_DEPTH_LIMIT | Pending request limit, default max value of 0x7 means maximum pending requests allowed in the design<br>Anything less limits the bus requests to that number + 1. |

### MDSS_MDP_VP_0_LAYER_0_CURSOR_REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_0
**Address:** `0x01A45220`
* **Type:** RW
* **Reset State:** `0x00000008`
* **Double Buffered:** YES

FIFO watermark to aid in generation of mdpREQPRIORITY
The watermark here refers to the dedicated cursor fetch memory.
The value programmed here should be aware of the amount of dedicated cursor fetch memory.
So a value of 0 indicates completely FULL (i.e. there are no more entries available in the dedicated memory)
A value of 100 indicates 100 entries in the Shared Memory Pool (each entry being 128-bit entries)
This is the lowestmost FIFO depth and should not be programmed higher than REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_1 or REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_2

An example programming would set the following:
* REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_0 : 0x08 (meaning 0x08 entries free to be written into dedicated cursor fetch memory - least room available)
* REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_1 : 0x10 (meaning 0x10 entries free to be written into dedicated cursor fetch memory - middle ground room available)
* REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_2 : 0x20 (meaning 0x20 entries free to be written into dedicated cursor fetch memory - most room available)

* mdpREQPRIORITY = 11 (highest priority request) when above all 3 watermark levels (i.e. lots of space available in dedicated cursor fetch memory)
* mdpREQPRIORITY = 10 above FIFO_0 and FIFO_1 but below FIFO_2
* mdpREQPRIORITY = 01 above FIFO_0 but below FIFO_1 and FIFO_2
* mdpREQPRIORITY = 00 (lowest priority request) when below all 3 watermark levels (i.e. not a lot of space available in dedicated cursor fetch memory so its good)
<!-- page 3469 -->

### MDSS_MDP_VP_0_LAYER_0_CURSOR_REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_0 (continued)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 15:0 | WATERMARK | Watermark Level for FIFO_0 |

### 0x01A46204 MDSS_MDP_VP_0_LAYER_1_CURSOR_FETCH_CONFIG

* **Type**: RW
* **Reset State**: 0x00000087
* **Double Buffered**: NO

Cursor Client Fetch Configuration per Virtual Pipeline

This register must NOT be altered during operation and MDP must be idle when changing values
<!-- page 3500 -->

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 17:16 | TILE_SIZE | Tile Size for processing of BLOCK formats<br>Note that this only applies to blocks that operate in block mode which is limited to DMA source pipe. This setting has no effect for all other source pipes (ViG/RGB)<br>0x0: 128x128<br>0x1: 64x64<br>0x2: 32x32 |
| 12 | ADDR_SYNC_MODE | Boundary on which fetch address synchronizes.<br>Setting this field to line forces the address updates on the next line which performs the software requested feature of updating on hsync.<br>Note that updating on line boundaries will likely result in tearing on the panel since hardware is fetching from new memory buffer.<br>0x0: frame (default)<br>0x1: line |
| 9:8 | MAL | Describes the Minimum Access Length for the source pipeline.<br>This value should align with the DRAM's expected transaction alignment unit.<br>This setting forces the source fetch pipe to be aligned to DRAM and implement re-alignment for maximum efficiency<br>0x0: 128b alignment (default)<br>0x1: 256b alignment<br>0x2: 512b alignment |
| 7:4 | MAX_BURST_SIZE | Maximum burst beat size.<br>Hardware fetch engines operate on 128-bit bus<br>Possible values:<br>0x8: burst of 8<br>0x4: burst of 4<br>0x2: burst of 2 |
| 3:0 | REQ_DEPTH_LIMIT | Pending request limit, default max value of 0x7 means maximum pending requests allowed in the design<br>Anything less limits the bus requests to that number + 1. |

## Register: MDSS_MDP_VP_0_LAYER_1_CURSOR_REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_0

* **Address**: `0x01A46220`
* **Type**: `RW`
* **Reset State**: `0x00000008`

FIFO watermark to aid in generation of mdpREQPRIORITY

The watermark here refers to the dedicated cursor fetch memory.

The value programmed here should be aware of the amount of dedicated cursor fetch memory.

So a value of 0 indicates completely FULL (i.e. there are no more entries available in the dedicated memory)

A value of 100 indicates 100 entries in the Shared Memory Pool (each entry being 128-bit entries)

This is the lowestmost FIFO depth and should not be programmed higher than REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_1 or REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_2

An example programming would set the following:
<!-- page 3502 -->

* **Double Buffered**: YES

* REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_0 : 0x08 (meaning 0x08 entries free to be written into dedicated cursor fetch memory - least room available)
* REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_1 : 0x10 (meaning 0x10 entries free to be written into dedicated cursor fetch memory - middle ground room available)
* REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_2 : 0x20 (meaning 0x20 entries free to be written into dedicated cursor fetch memory - most room available)
* mdpREQPRIORITY = 11 (highest priority request) when above all 3 watermark levels (i.e. lots of space available in dedicated cursor fetch memory)
* mdpREQPRIORITY = 10 above FIFO_0 and FIFO_1 but below FIFO_2
* mdpREQPRIORITY = 01 above FIFO_0 but below FIFO_1 and FIFO_2
* mdpREQPRIORITY = 00 (lowest priority request) when below all 3 watermark levels (i.e. not a lot of space available in dedicated cursor fetch memory so its good)

### MDSS_MDP_VP_0_LAYER_1_CURSOR_REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_0 Bits

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 15:0 | WATERMARK | Watermark Level for FIFO_0 |

LayerMixer Operation Control

### MDSS_MDP_VP_0_LAYER_2_OP_MODE Bits

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 4 | BLEND3_COLOR3_OUT | Selects which source to drive on color3 component output for stage3 blend<br>0x0: BG Layer Color3<br>0x1: FG Layer Color3 |
| 3 | BLEND2_COLOR3_OUT | Selects which source to drive on color3 component output for stage2 blend<br>0x0: BG Layer Color3<br>0x1: FG Layer Color3 |
| 2 | BLEND1_COLOR3_OUT | Selects which source to drive on color3 component output for stage1 blend<br>0x0: BG Layer Color3<br>0x1: FG Layer Color3 |
| 1 | BLEND0_COLOR3_OUT | Selects which source to drive on color3 component output for stage0 blend<br>0x0: BG Layer Color3<br>0x1: FG Layer Color3 |
| 0 | GC_LUT_EN | 0x0: Disabled - mapped linearly from 12-bit to 8-bit<br>0x1: Enabled |

### 0x01A47204 MDSS_MDP_VP_0_LAYER_2_CURSOR_FETCH_CONFIG

* **Type**: RW

Cursor Client Fetch Configuration per Virtual Pipeline double buffered: NO

<!-- page 3533 -->

#### MDSS_MDP_VP_0_LAYER_2_CURSOR_FETCH_CONFIG (Continued)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 17:16 | TILE_SIZE | Tile Size for processing of BLOCK formats. Note that this only applies to blocks that operate in block mode which is limited to DMA source pipe. This setting has no effect for all other source pipes (ViG/RGB).<br>0x0: 128x128<br>0x1: 64x64<br>0x2: 32x32 |
| 12 | ADDR_SYNC_MODE | Boundary on which fetch address synchronizes. Setting this field to line forces the address updates on the next line which performs the software requested feature of updating on hsync. Note that updating on line boundaries will likely result in tearing on the panel since hardware is fetching from new memory buffer.<br>0x0: frame (default)<br>0x1: line |
| 9:8 | MAL | Describes the Minimum Access Length for the source pipeline. This value should align with the DRAM's expected transaction alignment unit. This setting forces the source fetch pipe to be aligned to DRAM and implement re-alignment for maximum efficiency.<br>0x0: 128b alignment (default)<br>0x1: 256b alignment<br>0x2: 512b alignment |
| 7:4 | MAX_BURST_SIZE | Maximum burst beat size. Hardware fetch engines operate on 128-bit bus. Possible values:<br>0x8: burst of 8<br>0x4: burst of 4<br>0x2: burst of 2 |
| 3:0 | REQ_DEPTH_LIMIT | Pending request limit, default max value of 0x7 means maximum pending requests allowed in the design. Anything less limits the bus requests to that number + 1. |

### 0x01A47220 MDSS_MDP_VP_0_LAYER_2_CURSOR_REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_0

* **Type**: RW
* **Reset State**: 0x00000008

FIFO watermark to aid in generation of mdpREQPRIORITY

The watermark here refers to the dedicated cursor fetch memory.

The value programmed here should be aware of the amount of dedicated cursor fetch memory.

So a value of 0 indicates completely FULL (i.e. there are no more entries available in the dedicated memory)

A value of 100 indicates 100 entries in the Shared Memory Pool (each entry being 128-bit entries)

This is the lowestmost FIFO depth and should not be programmed higher than REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_1 or REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_2

An example programming would set the following:
<!-- page 3535 -->

#### MDSS_MDP_VP_0_LAYER_2_CURSOR_REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_0 (Continued)

Example programming:
* REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_0 : 0x08 (meaning 0x08 entries free to be written into dedicated cursor fetch memory - least room available)
* REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_1 : 0x10 (meaning 0x10 entries free to be written into dedicated cursor fetch memory - middle ground room available)
* REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_2 : 0x20 (meaning 0x20 entries free to be written into dedicated cursor fetch memory - most room available)

* mdpREQPRIORITY = 11 (highest priority request) when above all 3 watermark levels (i.e. lots of space available in dedicated cursor fetch memory)
* mdpREQPRIORITY = 10 above FIFO_0 and FIFO_1 but below FIFO_2
* mdpREQPRIORITY = 01 above FIFO_0 but below FIFO_1 and FIFO_2
* mdpREQPRIORITY = 00 (lowest priority request) when below all 3 watermark levels (i.e. not a lot of space available in dedicated cursor fetch memory so its good)

double buffered: YES

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 15:0 | WATERMARK | Watermark Level for FIFO_0 |

### 0x01A48000 MDSS_MDP_VP_0_LAYER_3_OP_MODE

* **Type**: RW

when: On frame boundaries (vsync or SW trigger)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 4 | BLEND3_COLOR3_OUT | Selects which source to drive on color3 component output for stage3 blend.<br>0x0: BG Layer Color3<br>0x1: FG Layer Color3 |
| 3 | BLEND2_COLOR3_OUT | Selects which source to drive on color3 component output for stage2 blend.<br>0x0: BG Layer Color3<br>0x1: FG Layer Color3 |
| 2 | BLEND1_COLOR3_OUT | Selects which source to drive on color3 component output for stage1 blend.<br>0x0: BG Layer Color3<br>0x1: FG Layer Color3 |
| 1 | BLEND0_COLOR3_OUT | Selects which source to drive on color3 component output for stage0 blend.<br>0x0: BG Layer Color3<br>0x1: FG Layer Color3 |
| 0 | GC_LUT_EN | 0x0: Disabled - mapped linearly from 12-bit to 8-bit<br>0x1: Enabled |

### 0x01A48204 MDSS_MDP_VP_0_LAYER_3_CURSOR_FETCH_CONFIG

**Type:** RW

**Reset State:** 0x00000087

Cursor Client Fetch Configuration per Virtual Pipeline

double buffered: NO

This register must NOT be altered during operation and MDP must be idle when changing values
<!-- page 3566 -->

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 17:16 | TILE_SIZE | Tile Size for processing of BLOCK formats<br/>Note that this only applies to blocks that operate in block mode which is limited to DMA source pipe. This setting has no effect for all other source pipes (ViG/RGB)<br/>0x0: 128x128<br/>0x1: 64x64<br/>0x2: 32x32 |
| 12 | ADDR_SYNC_MODE | Boundary on which fetch address synchronizes.<br/>Setting this field to line forces the address updates on the next line which performs the software requested feature of updating on hsync.<br/>Note that updating on line boundaries will likely result in tearing on the panel since hardware is fetching from new memory buffer.<br/>0x0: frame (default)<br/>0x1: line |
| 9:8 | MAL | Describes the Minimum Access Length for the source pipeline.<br/>This value should align with the DRAM's expected transaction alignment unit.<br/>This setting forces the source fetch pipe to be aligned to DRAM and implement re-alignment for maximum efficiency<br/>0x0: 128b alignment (default)<br/>0x1: 256b alignment<br/>0x2: 512b alignment |
| 7:4 | MAX_BURST_SIZE | Maximum burst beat size.<br/>Hardware fetch engines operate on 128-bit bus<br/>Possible values:<br/>0x8: burst of 8<br/>0x4: burst of 4<br/>0x2: burst of 2 |
| 3:0 | REQ_DEPTH_LIMIT | Pending request limit, default max value of 0x7 means maximum pending requests allowed in the design<br/>Anything less limits the bus requests to that number + 1. |

### 0x01A48220 MDSS_MDP_VP_0_LAYER_3_CURSOR_REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_0

**Type:** RW

**Reset State:** 0x00000008

FIFO watermark to aid in generation of mdpREQPRIORITY

The watermark here refers to the dedicated cursor fetch memory.

The value programmed here should be aware of the amount of dedicated cursor fetch memory.

So a value of 0 indicates completely FULL (i.e. there are no more entries available in the dedicated memory)

A value of 100 indicates 100 entries in the Shared Memory Pool (each entry being 128-bit entries)

This is the lowestmost FIFO depth and should not be programmed higher than REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_1 or REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_2

An example programming would set the following:
<!-- page 3568 -->

REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_0 : 0x08 (meaning 0x08 entries free to be written into dedicated cursor fetch memory - least room available)

REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_1 : 0x10 (meaning 0x10 entries free to be written into dedicated cursor fetch memory - middle ground room available)

REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_2 : 0x20 (meaning 0x20 entries free to be written into dedicated cursor fetch memory - most room available)

mdpREQPRIORITY = 11 (highest priority request) when above all 3 watermark levels (i.e. lots of space available in dedicated cursor fetch memory)

mdpREQPRIORITY = 10 above FIFO_0 and FIFO_1 but below FIFO_2

mdpREQPRIORITY = 01 above FIFO_0 but below FIFO_1 and FIFO_2

mdpREQPRIORITY = 00 (lowest priority request) when below all 3 watermark levels (i.e. not a lot of space available in dedicated cursor fetch memory so its good)

double buffered: YES

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 15:0 | WATERMARK | Watermark Level for FIFO_0 |

#### 0x01A49000 MDSS_MDP_VP_0_LAYER_4_OP_MODE

* **Type**: RW
* **Reset State**: 0x00000000
* **Description**: LayerMixer Operation Control
* **Double buffered**: YES
* **When**: On frame boundaries (vsync or SW trigger)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 4 | BLEND3_COLOR3_OUT | Selects which source to drive on color3 component output for stage3 blend<br>0x0: BG Layer Color3<br>0x1: FG Layer Color3 |
| 3 | BLEND2_COLOR3_OUT | Selects which source to drive on color3 component output for stage2 blend<br>0x0: BG Layer Color3<br>0x1: FG Layer Color3 |
| 2 | BLEND1_COLOR3_OUT | Selects which source to drive on color3 component output for stage1 blend<br>0x0: BG Layer Color3<br>0x1: FG Layer Color3 |
| 1 | BLEND0_COLOR3_OUT | Selects which source to drive on color3 component output for stage0 blend<br>0x0: BG Layer Color3<br>0x1: FG Layer Color3 |
| 0 | GC_LUT_EN | 0x0: Disabled - mapped linearly from 12-bit to 8-bit<br>0x1: Enabled |

### 0x01A49204 MDSS_MDP_VP_0_LAYER_4_CURSOR_FETCH_CONFIG

**Type:** RW  
**Reset State:** 0x00000087  

Cursor Client Fetch Configuration per Virtual Pipeline

double buffered: NO

This register must NOT be altered during operation and MDP must be idle when changing values
<!-- page 3599 -->

### MDSS_MDP_VP_0_LAYER_4_CURSOR_FETCH_CONFIG

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 17:16 | TILE_SIZE | Tile Size for processing of BLOCK formats<br>Note that this only applies to blocks that operate in block mode which is limited to DMA source pipe. This setting has no effect for all other source pipes (ViG/RGB)<br>0x0: 128x128<br>0x1: 64x64<br>0x2: 32x32 |
| 12 | ADDR_SYNC_MODE | Boundary on which fetch address synchronizes.<br>Setting this field to line forces the address updates on the next line which performs the software requested feature of updating on hsync.<br>Note that updating on line boundaries will likely result in tearing on the panel since hardware is fetching from new memory buffer.<br>0x0: frame (default)<br>0x1: line |
| 9:8 | MAL | Describes the Minimum Access Length for the source pipeline.<br>This value should align with the DRAM's expected transaction alignment unit.<br>This setting forces the source fetch pipe to be aligned to DRAM and implement re-alignment for maximum efficiency<br>0x0: 128b alignment (default)<br>0x1: 256b alignment<br>0x2: 512b alignment |
| 7:4 | MAX_BURST_SIZE | Maximum burst beat size.<br>Hardware fetch engines operate on 128-bit bus<br>Possible values:<br>0x8: burst of 8<br>0x4: burst of 4<br>0x2: burst of 2 |
| 3:0 | REQ_DEPTH_LIMIT | Pending request limit, default max value of 0x7 means maximum pending requests allowed in the design<br>Anything less limits the bus requests to that number + 1. |

### 0x01A49220 MDSS_MDP_VP_0_LAYER_4_CURSOR_REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_0

**Type:** RW  
**Reset State:** 0x00000008  

FIFO watermark to aid in generation of mdpREQPRIORITY

The watermark here refers to the dedicated cursor fetch memory.

The value programmed here should be aware of the amount of dedicated cursor fetch memory.

So a value of 0 indicates completely FULL (i.e. there are no more entries available in the dedicated memory)

A value of 100 indicates 100 entries in the Shared Memory Pool (each entry being 128-bit entries)

This is the lowestmost FIFO depth and should not be programmed higher than REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_1 or REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_2

An example programming would set the following:




<!-- page 3601 -->

REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_0 : 0x08 (meaning 0x08 entries free to be written into dedicated cursor fetch memory - least room available)

REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_1 : 0x10 (meaning 0x10 entries free to be written into dedicated cursor fetch memory - middle ground room available)

REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_2 : 0x20 (meaning 0x20 entries free to be written into dedicated cursor fetch memory - most room available)

mdpREQPRIORITY = 11 (highest priority request) when above all 3 watermark levels (i.e. lots of space available in dedicated cursor fetch memory)

mdpREQPRIORITY = 10 above FIFO_0 and FIFO_1 but below FIFO_2

mdpREQPRIORITY = 01 above FIFO_0 but below FIFO_1 and FIFO_2

mdpREQPRIORITY = 00 (lowest priority request) when below all 3 watermark levels (i.e. not a lot of space available in dedicated cursor fetch memory so its good)

double buffered: YES

### MDSS_MDP_VP_0_LAYER_4_CURSOR_REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_0

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 15:0 | WATERMARK | Watermark Level for FIFO_0 |

| 31 | SIX_ZONE_VAL_MASK | 0x0: Disable six zone adj on VAL<br>0x1: Enable six zone adj on VAL |
| 30 | SIX_ZONE_SAT_MASK | 0x0: Disable six zone adj on SAT<br>0x1: Enable six zone adj on SAT |
| 29 | SIX_ZONE_HUE_MASK | 0x0: Disable six zone adj on HUE<br>0x1: Enable six zone adj on HUE |
| 28 | PA_CONT_MASK | 0x0: Disable HSIC adj on CONTRAST<br>0x1: Enable HSIC adj on CONTRAST |
| 27 | PA_VAL_MASK | 0x0: Disable HSIC adj on VALUE<br>0x1: Enable HSIC adj on VALUE |
| 26 | PA_SAT_MASK | 0x0: Disable HSIC adj on SATURATION<br>0x1: Enable HSIC adj on SATURATION |
| 25 | PA_HUE_MASK | 0x0: Disable HSIC adj on HUE<br>0x1: Enable HSIC adj on HUE |
| 22 | GC_LUT_EN | 0x0: Disabled - mapped linearly from 12-bit to 8-bit<br>0x1: Enabled |
| 20 | PA_EN | Picture Adjustment enable<br>0x0: DISABLED<br>0x1: ENABLED |
| 19 | PA_LUTV_EN | Histogram Enhancement Lookup Table enable |

### 0x01A55210 MDSS_MDP_VP_0_DSPP_0_HIST_COLLECT_CTL

except for LOCK

| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 0 | LOCK | 0: SW and HW swap their access on the 2 histogramg tables;<br>HW collects on a new table on the new frame, while SW accesses the histogram of the last frame on the table just swapped out by HW<br>1: current table will be overwritten for new collection on the next frame, the other table remains untouched for SW to continue to access |

### 0x01A55230 MDSS_MDP_VP_0_DSPP_0_PA_LUTV

**Type**: RW
**Reset State**: 0x00000000

PA LUTV data

Auto-incremented by hardware

256 entries are available for reading
double buffered: NO

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 17 | VALUE_UPDATEN | Software issue an write to the LUT<br>0: VALUE will be written to RAM at INDEX if INDEX_UPDATE=1 or at INDEX+1 if INDEX_UPDATE=0<br>1: VALUE will not be written to RAM, this setting is appropriate for example when INDEX needs to be updated for read |
| 16 | INDEX_UPDATE | Software issue an index update<br>0: No index update by software<br>1: Update LUT index to value specified by INDEX |
| 15:8 | INDEX | VALUE is stored in this INDEX of the PA_LUTV, next write will be stored to the next higher INDEX |
| 7:0 | VALUE | Value read depends on the LUT select and which one is available for reading by software<br>The read sequence to the LUT should always begin with WR INDEX_UPDATE=1, INDEX=&lt;rptr start location&gt;<br>subsequent RD will start from the start location and every read will auto-increment the rptr |

## 17.17.7.15 MDSS_MDP_VP_0_DSPP_1
DSPP hardware register description

### 17.17.7.15.1 MDSS_MDP_VP_0_DSPP_1_DSPP
DSPP hardware register description
<!-- page 3628 -->

### MDSS_MDP_VP_0_DSPP_1_OP_MODE (0x01A57000)
* **Type:** RW
* **Reset State:** 0x00000000
* **Double buffered:** Yes (On frame boundaries (vsync or SW trigger))

DSPP Operation Control

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31 | SIX_ZONE_VAL_MASK | 0x0: Disable six zone adj on VAL<br>0x1: Enable six zone adj on VAL |
| 30 | SIX_ZONE_SAT_MASK | 0x0: Disable six zone adj on SAT<br>0x1: Enable six zone adj on SAT |
| 29 | SIX_ZONE_HUE_MASK | 0x0: Disable six zone adj on HUE<br>0x1: Enable six zone adj on HUE |
| 28 | PA_CONT_MASK | 0x0: Disable HSIC adj on CONTRAST<br>0x1: Enable HSIC adj on CONTRAST |
| 27 | PA_VAL_MASK | 0x0: Disable HSIC adj on VALUE<br>0x1: Enable HSIC adj on VALUE |
| 26 | PA_SAT_MASK | 0x0: Disable HSIC adj on SATURATION<br>0x1: Enable HSIC adj on SATURATION |
| 25 | PA_HUE_MASK | 0x0: Disable HSIC adj on HUE<br>0x1: Enable HSIC adj on HUE |
| 22 | GC_LUT_EN | 0x0: Disabled - mapped linearly from 12-bit to 8-bit<br>0x1: Enabled |
| 20 | PA_EN | Picture Adjustment enable<br>0x0: DISABLED<br>0x1: ENABLED |
| 19 | PA_LUTV_EN | Histogram Enhancement Lookup Table enable |
| 16 | HIST_EN | Histogram Enable |
| 8 | DST_DITHER_EN | Destination Dither enable<br>0x0: DISABLED<br>0x1: ENABLED |
| 7 | PA_MEM_COL_SKY_MASK | 0x0: Disable Sky adjustment<br>0x1: Enable Sky adjustment |
| 6 | PA_MEM_COL_FOL_MASK | 0x0: Disable Foliage adjustment<br>0x1: Enable Foliage adjustment |
<!-- page 3629 -->

#### MDSS_MDP_VP_0_DSPP_1_OP_MODE (Continuation from page 3628)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 5 | PA_MEM_COL_SKIN_MASK | 0x0: Disable Skin adjustment<br>0x1: Enable Skin adjustment |
| 4 | PCC_EN | Panel Color Correction enable<br>0x0: DISABLED<br>0x1: ENABLED |
| 2 | PA_MEM_PROTECT_ENABLE | 0: global hsv adjustment is independent of memor color<br>1: global hsv adjustment is active if the pixel is not already processed by memory color<br>contrast adjustment in global adjustment is always independ of memory color regardless |
| 1 | PA_SAT_ZERO_EXP_ENABLE | 0: if PA_SAT_ADJ < -32, clamp PA_SAT_ADJ to 0<br>1: if PA_SAT_ADJ < -64, clamp PA_SAT_ADJ to 0 |
| 0 | IGC_LUT_EN | Inverse Gamma Correction LUT enable<br>0x0: DISABLED<br>0x1: ENABLED |

### MDSS_MDP_VP_0_DSPP_1_PA_LUTV

**Address:** `0x01A57230`
**Type:** RW
**Reset State:** `0x00000000`
**Double Buffered:** NO

PA LUTV data  
Auto-incremented by hardware  
256 entries are available for reading  

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 17 | VALUE_UPDATEN | Software issue an write to the LUT<br>0: VALUE will be written to RAM at INDEX if INDEX_UPDATE=1 or at INDEX+1 if INDEX_UPDATE=0<br>1: VALUE will not be written to RAM, this setting is appropriate for example when INDEX needs to be updated for read |
| 16 | INDEX_UPDATE | Software issue an index update<br>0: No index update by software<br>1: Update LUT index to value specified by INDEX |
| 15:8 | INDEX | VALUE is stored in this INDEX of the PA_LUTV, next write will be stored to the next higher INDEX |
| 7:0 | VALUE | Value read depends on the LUT select and which one is available for reading by software<br>The read sequence to the LUT should always begin with WR INDEX_UPDATE=1, INDEX=\<rptr start location\><br>subsequent RD will start from the start location and every read will auto-increment the rptr |

---

### 0x01A59000 MDSS_MDP_VP_0_DSPP_2_OP_MODE

- **Type**: RW
- **Reset State**: 0x00000000
- **double buffered**: YES
- **when**: On frame boundaries (vsync or SW trigger)

DSPP Operation Control
<!-- page 3652 -->

#### MDSS_MDP_VP_0_DSPP_2_OP_MODE (continued)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31 | SIX_ZONE_VAL_MASK | 0x0: Disable six zone adj on VAL<br>0x1: Enable six zone adj on VAL |
| 30 | SIX_ZONE_SAT_MASK | 0x0: Disable six zone adj on SAT<br>0x1: Enable six zone adj on SAT |
| 29 | SIX_ZONE_HUE_MASK | 0x0: Disable six zone adj on HUE<br>0x1: Enable six zone adj on HUE |
| 28 | PA_CONT_MASK | 0x0: Disable HSIC adj on CONTRAST<br>0x1: Enable HSIC adj on CONTRAST |
| 27 | PA_VAL_MASK | 0x0: Disable HSIC adj on VALUE<br>0x1: Enable HSIC adj on VALUE |
| 26 | PA_SAT_MASK | 0x0: Disable HSIC adj on SATURATION<br>0x1: Enable HSIC adj on SATURATION |
| 25 | PA_HUE_MASK | 0x0: Disable HSIC adj on HUE<br>0x1: Enable HSIC adj on HUE |
| 22 | GC_LUT_EN | 0x0: Disabled - mapped linearly from 12-bit to 8-bit<br>0x1: Enabled |
| 20 | PA_EN | Picture Adjustment enable<br>0x0: DISABLED<br>0x1: ENABLED |
| 19 | PA_LUTV_EN | Histogram Enhancement Lookup Table enable |
| 16 | HIST_EN | Histogram Enable |
| 8 | DST_DITHER_EN | Destination Dither enable<br>0x0: DISABLED<br>0x1: ENABLED |
| 7 | PA_MEM_COL_SKY_MASK | 0x0: Disable Sky adjustment<br>0x1: Enable Sky adjustment |
| 6 | PA_MEM_COL_FOL_MASK | 0x0: Disable Foliage adjustment<br>0x1: Enable Foliage adjustment |
| 5 | PA_MEM_COL_SKIN_MASK | 0x0: Disable Skin adjustment<br>0x1: Enable Skin adjustment |
| 4 | PCC_EN | Panel Color Correction enable<br>0x0: DISABLED<br>0x1: ENABLED |
| 2 | PA_MEM_PROTECT_ENABLE | 0: global hsv adjustment is independent of memor color<br>1: global hsv adjustment is active if the pixel is not already processed by memory color<br>contrast adjustment in global adjustment is always independ of memory color regardless |
<!-- page 3653 -->

#### MDSS_MDP_VP_0_DSPP_2_OP_MODE (continued)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1 | PA_SAT_ZERO_EXP_ENABLE | 0: if PA_SAT_ADJ < -32, clamp PA_SAT_ADJ to 0<br>1: if PA_SAT_ADJ < -64, clamp PA_SAT_ADJ to 0 |
| 0 | IGC_LUT_EN | Inverse Gamma Correction LUT enable<br>0x0: DISABLED<br>0x1: ENABLED |

### 0x01A59230 MDSS_MDP_VP_0_DSPP_2_PA_LUTV

**Type**: RW
**Reset State**: 0x00000000

PA LUTV data

Auto-incremented by hardware

256 entries are available for reading

double buffered: NO

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---------- |
| 17 | VALUE_UPDATEN | Software issue an write to the LUT<br>0: VALUE will be written to RAM at INDEX if INDEX_UPDATE=1 or at INDEX+1 if INDEX_UPDATE=0<br>1: VALUE will not be written to RAM, this setting is appropriate for example when INDEX needs to be updated for read |
<!-- page 3662 -->

### MDSS_MDP_VP_0_DSPP_2_PA_LUTV (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---------- |
| 16 | INDEX_UPDATE | Software issue an index update<br>0: No index update by software<br>1: Update LUT index to value specified by INDEX |
| 15:8 | INDEX | VALUE is stored in this INDEX of the PA_LUTV, next write will be stored to the next higher INDEX |
| 7:0 | VALUE | Value read depends on the LUT select and which one is available for reading by software<br>The read sequence to the LUT should always begin with WR INDEX_UPDATE=1, INDEX=\<rptr start location\><br>subsequent RD will start from the start location and every read will auto-increment the rptr |

### 0x01A59248 MDSS_MDP_VP_0_DSPP_2_SIX_ZONE_ADJ_CURVE_P0

**Type**: RW
**Reset State**: 0x00000000

Six Zone Adjust Curve Part 0
double buffered: No

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---------- |
| 26 | INDEX_UPDATE | Set this to 1 to point current LUT location to INDEX.<br>The LUT location is autoincremented on every value write or read when there is no INDEX_UPDATE<br>Before every series of read, there must be an INDEX_UPDATE |
| 25 | VALUE_UPDATEN | Set this to 0 to enable VALUE to be written to the current location of the LUT |
| 24:16 | INDEX | Index to one of the 384 location of the LUT |
| 11:0 | HUE | S12, recommand to be within exclusive range x2800 and x1800 (i.e. -360 to +360 exclusive)<br>circularly clipped otherwise<br>On write: Value to be updated to one of the 384 entry LUT<br>On read : Value read out from LUT location pointed by INDEX |

### 0x01A65000 MDSS_MDP_WB_0_DST_FORMAT

- **Type**: RW
- **Reset State**: 0x00000000
- **Double Buffered**: No

Memory Write Back Output Format

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:30 | FRAME_FORMAT | FRAME_FORMAT<br>In the current revision, there is no support for tiled formats<br>0x0: Linear, no tile |
| 29:26 | DST_CHROMA_SITE | Destination Chroma Site<br>0x0: A (cosite for YUV422)<br>0x1: B (offsite for YUV422)<br>0x2: C (N/A for YUV422)<br>0x3: D (N/A for YUV422)<br>0x4: E (N/A for YUV422)<br>0x5: F (N/A for YUV422)<br>0x6: G (N/A for YUV422)<br>0x7: H (N/A for YUV422)<br>0x8: I (N/A for YUV422) |
<!-- page 3676 -->

### MDSS_MDP_WB_0_DST_FORMAT (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 25:23 | DST_CHROMA_SAMP | Chroma Sampling<br>0x0: RGB/4:4:4<br>0x1: 4:2:2 - H2V1<br>0x2: 4:2:2 - H1V2<br>0x3: 4:2:0 - N2V1<br>0x4: 4:2:0 - N1V2 |
| 22 | DST_DITHER_EN | Destination Dither Enable |
| 20:19 | WRITE_PLANES | Number of planes<br>0x0: Interleaved<br>0x1: Planar<br>0x2: Pseudo-planar |
| 18 | PACK_ALIGN | 0x0: LSB<br>0x1: MSB |
| 17 | PACK_TIGHT | 0x0: Loose<br>0x1: Tight |
| 14 | DST_ALPHA_X | 0x0: Use alpha value from pipe<br>0x1: Use alpha value from register |
| 13:12 | PACK_COUNT | Valid packing elements count<br>0x0 = 1 element<br>0x1 = 2 elements<br>0x2 = 3 elements<br>0x3 = 4 elements |
| 10:9 | DST_BPP | Effective byte per pixel<br>0x0: 1 byte<br>0x1: 2 bytes<br>0x2: 3 bytes<br>0x3: 4 bytes |
| 8 | DSTC3_EN | 0x1: Destination has alpha |
| 7:6 | DSTC3_OUT | Number of bits for component 3 output<br>0x0: 1 bit<br>0x1: 4 bits<br>0x2: 6 bits<br>0x3: 8 bits |
| 5:4 | DSTC2_OUT | Number of bits for component 2 output<br>0x0: 4 bits<br>0x1: 5 bits<br>0x2: 6 bits<br>0x3: 8 bits |
<!-- page 3677 -->

### MDSS_MDP_WB_0_DST_FORMAT (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |

| 1:0 | DSTC0_OUT | Number of bits for component 0 output<br>0x0: 4 bits<br>0x1: 5 bits<br>0x2: 6 bits<br>0x3: 8 bits |

### 0x01A652B0 MDSS_MDP_WB_0_DST_ADDR_SW_STATUS

* **Type**: RW
* **Reset State**: 0x00000000
* **Double Buffered**: NO

Security Status of the destination buffer plane.

This provides a SW override to the hardware calculated content protection sent to VBIF.
This value is logically OR'ed with the source content protection produced by hardware.

This information will be presented to VBIF per transaction and reflected as part of the memory transaction.
Note that the VBIF context banks need to be properly programmed for the output to be successful.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 0 | DST_ADDR_CP | This is the secure status bit for destination plane 0 (if used). Memory transactions will not complete if this status doesn't correspond to system programming in the rest of the path to memory.<br>0x0: Content Protected Buffer State<br>0x1: Non Content Protected Buffer State |

---

| 29:26 | DST_CHROMA_SITE | Destination Chroma Site<br>0x0: A (cosite for YUV422)<br>0x1: B (offsite for YUV422)<br>0x2: C (N/A for YUV422)<br>0x3: D (N/A for YUV422)<br>0x4: E (N/A for YUV422)<br>0x5: F (N/A for YUV422)<br>0x6: G (N/A for YUV422)<br>0x7: H (N/A for YUV422)<br>0x8: I (N/A for YUV422) |
| 25:23 | DST_CHROMA_SAMP | Chroma Sampling<br>0x0: RGB/4:4:4<br>0x1: 4:2:2 - H2V1<br>0x2: 4:2:2 - H1V2<br>0x3: 4:2:0 - N2V1<br>0x4: 4:2:0 - N1V2 |
| 22 | DST_DITHER_EN | Destination Dither Enable |

### MDSS_MDP_WB_1_DST_ADDR_SW_STATUS

**Address:** 0x01A65AB0
**Type:** RW
**Reset State:** 0x00000000

Security Status of the destination buffer plane

This provides a SW override to the hardware calculated content protection sent to VBIF

This value is logically ORed with the source content protection produced by hardware

This information will be presented to VBIF per transaction and reflected as part of the memory transaction

Note that the VBIF context banks need to be properly programmed for the output to be successful

double buffered: NO

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 0 | DST_ADDR_CP | This is the secure status bit for destination plane 0 (if used)<br>Memory transactions will not complete if this status doesn't correspond to system programming in the rest of the path to memory<br>0x0: Content Protected Buffer State<br>0x1: Non Content Protected Buffer State |

### 0x01A662B0 MDSS_MDP_WB_2_DST_ADDR_SW_STATUS

* **Type**: RW
* **Reset State**: 0x00000000
* **Description**: Security Status of the destination buffer plane. This provides a SW override to the hardware calculated content protection sent to VBIF. This value is logically ORed with the source content protection produced by hardware. This information will be presented to VBIF per transaction and reflected as part of the memory transaction. Note that the VBIF context banks need to be properly programmed for the output to be successful.
* **Double Buffered**: NO

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 0 | DST_ADDR_CP | This is the secure status bit for destination plane 0 (if used). Memory transactions will not complete if this status doesn't correspond to system programming in the rest of the path to memory.<br>0x0: Content Protected Buffer State<br>0x1: Non Content Protected Buffer State |

* **Type**: RW
* **Reset State**: 0x00000000
* **Description**: Memory Write Back Output Format

<!-- page 3726 -->

### MDSS_MDP_WB_3_DST_FORMAT (Continuation)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:30 | FRAME_FORMAT | In the current revision, there is no support for tiled formats.<br>0x0: Linear, no tile |
| 29:26 | DST_CHROMA_SITE | Destination Chroma Site<br>0x0: A (cosite for YUV422)<br>0x1: B (offsite for YUV422)<br>0x2: C (N/A for YUV422)<br>0x3: D (N/A for YUV422)<br>0x4: E (N/A for YUV422)<br>0x5: F (N/A for YUV422)<br>0x6: G (N/A for YUV422)<br>0x7: H (N/A for YUV422)<br>0x8: I (N/A for YUV422) |
| 25:23 | DST_CHROMA_SAMP | Chroma Sampling<br>0x0: RGB/4:4:4<br>0x1: 4:2:2 - H2V1<br>0x2: 4:2:2 - H1V2<br>0x3: 4:2:0 - N2V1<br>0x4: 4:2:0 - N1V2 |
| 22 | DST_DITHER_EN | Destination Dither Enable |
| 20:19 | WRITE_PLANES | Number of planes<br>0x0: Interleaved<br>0x1: Planar<br>0x2: Pseudo-planar |
| 18 | PACK_ALIGN | 0x0: LSB<br>0x1: MSB |
| 17 | PACK_TIGHT | 0x0: Loose<br>0x1: Tight |
| 14 | DST_ALPHA_X | 0x0: Use alpha value from pipe<br>0x1: Use alpha value from register |
| 13:12 | PACK_COUNT | Valid packing elements count<br>0x0 = 1 element<br>0x1 = 2 elements<br>0x2 = 3 elements<br>0x3 = 4 elements |
| 10:9 | DST_BPP | Effective byte per pixel<br>0x0: 1 byte<br>0x1: 2 bytes<br>0x2: 3 bytes<br>0x3: 4 bytes |
| 8 | DSTC3_EN | 0x1: Destination has alpha |
<!-- page 3727 -->

### MDSS_MDP_WB_3_DST_FORMAT (Continuation 2)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |

| 5:4 | DSTC2_OUT | Number of bits for component 2 output<br>0x0: 4 bits<br>0x1: 5 bits<br>0x2: 6 bits<br>0x3: 8 bits |

| 1:0 | DSTC0_OUT | Number of bits for component 0 output<br>0x0: 4 bits<br>0x1: 5 bits<br>0x2: 6 bits<br>0x3: 8 bits |

### 0x01A66AB0 MDSS_MDP_WB_3_DST_ADDR_SW_STATUS

**Type:** RW
**Reset State:** 0x00000000
**Double buffered:** NO

Security Status of the destination buffer plane

This provides a SW override to the hardware calculated content protection sent to VBIF

This value is logically or ed with the source content protection produced by hardware

This information will be presented to VBIF per transaction and reflected as part of the memory transaction

Note that the VBIF context banks need to be properly programmed for the output to be successful

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 0 | DST_ADDR_CP | This is the secure status bit for destination plane 0 (if used)<br>Memory transactions will not complete if this status doesn't correspond to system programming in the rest of the path to memory<br>0x0: Content Protected Buffer State<br>0x1: Non Content Protected Buffer State |

### 0x01A67000 MDSS_MDP_WB_4_DST_FORMAT

**Type:** RW
**Reset State:** 0x00000000
**Double buffered:** NO

Memory Write Back Output Format
<!-- page 3743 -->
| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:30 | FRAME_FORMAT | FRAME_FORMAT<br>In the current revision, there is no support for tiled formats<br>0x0: Linear, no tile |
| 29:26 | DST_CHROMA_SITE | Destination Chroma Site<br>0x0: A (cosite for YUV422)<br>0x1: B (offsite for YUV422)<br>0x2: C (N/A for YUV422)<br>0x3: D (N/A for YUV422)<br>0x4: E (N/A for YUV422)<br>0x5: F (N/A for YUV422)<br>0x6: G (N/A for YUV422)<br>0x7: H (N/A for YUV422)<br>0x8: I (N/A for YUV422) |
| 25:23 | DST_CHROMA_SAMP | Chroma Sampling<br>0x0: RGB/4:4:4<br>0x1: 4:2:2 - H2V1<br>0x2: 4:2:2 - H1V2<br>0x3: 4:2:0 - N2V1<br>0x4: 4:2:0 - N1V2 |
| 22 | DST_DITHER_EN | Destination Dither Enable |
| 20:19 | WRITE_PLANES | Number of planes<br>0x0: Interleaved<br>0x1: Planar<br>0x2: Pseudo-planar |
| 18 | PACK_ALIGN | 0x0: LSB<br>0x1: MSB |
| 17 | PACK_TIGHT | 0x0: Loose<br>0x1: Tight |
| 14 | DST_ALPHA_X | 0x0: Use alpha value from pipe<br>0x1: Use alpha value from register |
| 13:12 | PACK_COUNT | Valid packing elements count<br>0x0 = 1 element<br>0x1 = 2 elements<br>0x2 = 3 elements<br>0x3 = 4 elements |
| 10:9 | DST_BPP | Effective byte per pixel<br>0x0: 1 byte<br>0x1: 2 bytes<br>0x2: 3 bytes<br>0x3: 4 bytes |
| 8 | DSTC3_EN | 0x1: Destination has alpha |
<!-- page 3744 -->
| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 7:6 | DSTC3_OUT | Number of bits for component 3 output<br>0x0: 1 bit<br>0x1: 4 bits<br>0x2: 6 bits<br>0x3: 8 bits |
| 5:4 | DSTC2_OUT | Number of bits for component 2 output<br>0x0: 4 bits<br>0x1: 5 bits<br>0x2: 6 bits<br>0x3: 8 bits |
| 3:2 | DSTC1_OUT | Number of bits for component 1 output<br>0x0: 4 bits<br>0x1: 5 bits<br>0x2: 6 bits<br>0x3: 8 bits |
| 1:0 | DSTC0_OUT | Number of bits for component 0 output<br>0x0: 4 bits<br>0x1: 5 bits<br>0x2: 6 bits<br>0x3: 8 bits |
