### 0x01A672B0 MDSS_MDP_WB_4_DST_ADDR_SW_STATUS

* **Type**: RW
* **Reset State**: 0x00000000

Security Status of the destination buffer plane

This provides a SW override to the hardware calculated content protection sent to VBIF

This value is logically or ed with the source content protection produced by hardware

 This information will be presented to VBIF per transaction and reflected as part of the memory
transaction

Note that the VBIF context banks need to be properly programmed for the output to be successful

double buffered: NO

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 0 | DST_ADDR_CP | This is the secure status bit for destination plane 0 (if used)<br>Memory transactions will not complete if this status doesnt<br>corespond to system programming in the rest of the path to<br>memory<br>0x0: Content Protected Buffer State<br>0x1: Non Content Protected Buffer State |

| Bits | Name | Description |

| 29 | ACTIVE_H_EN | Active H Enable |
| 28 | VSYNC_INTERRUPT_MODE | vsync interrupt generation mode<br>0 = generate an interrupt every vsync<br>1 = generate an interrupt every 2 fields (applicable to interlace<br>mode) |

### MDSS_MDP_INTF_0_INTF_CONFIG (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Description |

| 23 | DSI_VIDEO_STOP_MODE | This bit controls how video mode stream is stopped when DSI dynamic refresh is triggered. It is not applicable for non-DSI interface.<br>0x0: disable timing engine when DSI sets the video stop signal;<br>0x1: halt timing engine counters when DSI sets the video stop signal |
| 21 | CHROMA_DWN_SAMPLE_H_MTHD | Horizontal Chroma Down Sample method<br>0x0: non-pixel dropping<br>0x1: pixel dropping |
| 20 | CHROMA_DWN_SAMPLE_EN | Chroma Down Sample enable for YUV444<br>0x0: Disabled<br>0x1: Enabled |
| 18 | CSC_DST_DATA_FORMAT | Destination Data Format<br>0x0: RGB<br>0x1: YCbCr |
| 17 | CSC_SRC_DATA_FORMAT | Source Data Format<br>0x0: RGB<br>0x1: YCbCr |
| 16 | CSC_EN | Enables the color matrix conversion<br>0x0: Bypass<br>0x1: Enabled |
| 13:11 | NIBBLE_SWAP_EN | Enable nibble swapping within each pixel byte<br>NIBBLE_SWAP_EN[0]: 0 = no swapping for pixel_data [7:0]; 1 = enable swapping of pixel_data[3:0] with pixel_data[7:4]<br>NIBBLE_SWAP_EN[1] = 0 = no swapping for pixel_data [15:8]; 1 = enable swapping of pixel_data[11:8] with pixel_data[15:12]<br>NIBBLE_SWAP_EN[2] = 0 = no swapping for pixel_data [23:16]; 1 = enable swapping of pixel_data[19:16] with pixel_data[23:20] |
| 10 | PACK_ALIGN | 0x0: LSB<br>0x1: MSB |
| 9:8 | PACK_422 | 0x0: Y2Cr1Y1Cb1<br>0x1: Cr1Y2Cb1Y1<br>0x2: Y2Cb1Y1Cr1<br>0x3: Cb1Y2Cr1Y1 |
| 6:4 | OUT_MODE | 0x0: YCbCr or RGB4444 seperate syncs 24-bit interface<br>0x1: RSVD<br>0x2: YCbCr 422 seperate syncs 16-bit interface |
| 2 | INTERLACE_INIT_SEL | 0x0: start with even field<br>0x1: start with odd field |

| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:0 | DISPLAY_START_Y | Display Y Start<br>Defines the time period between the field0 start of vsync pulse and the first displayed line position in pixel clocks<br>display_start_y = v_back_porch * hcycle<br>where hcycle = horizontal_back_porch + horizontal_active + horizontal_front_porch<br>For eDP control the value programmed into this register differs slightly and should be programmed to the first active pixel and not the first pixel on that line!<br>In particular, the programming for eDP should be:<br>display_start_y = (v_back_porch * hcycle) + horizontal_back_porch |

### MDSS_MDP_INTF_0_VIDEO_MISR_CTRL (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31 | RUN_MODE | RW | This register defines the operation mode for the MISR<br>0x0: Single run mode meaning it stops after the programmable number of frames. (i.e. legacy mode prior to MDP5 1.5.0)<br>0x1: Free running mode meaning it updates the misr signature every programmable number of frames and continues to run while MISR_ENABLE is set to 0x1 |
| 27:24 | INPUT_SEL | RW | This field allows the selected input to propagate to the MISR in the event that multiple inputs want to share the same physcial MISR<br>For example, the video interface might want to MISR on active pixel data only or active+timing information as well<br>This field would select which input is sent to the MISR |
| 10 | STATUS_CLEAR | W | This is a write only register that doesn't have any effect prior to MDP5 1.5.0 since there was no logic associated with it<br>Write 0x1: Clears the MISR_STATUS register<br>Write 0x0: Has no effect on the the MISR_STATUS register |
| 9 | STATUS | R | Read only register<br>Set to 0x1 when misr signature has been updated |
| 8 | ENABLE | RW | MISR enable which starts/ends calculation of MISR on the next vsync/trigger event<br>This essentially double buffers the enable so that the misr doesn't start/end immediately but rather at a defined time<br>The MISR calculation would run until the end of programmed number of frames |
| 7:0 | FRAME_COUNT | RW | Number of frames to run before capturing |

### 0x01A6B800 MDSS_MDP_INTF_1_TIMING_ENGINE_EN

**Type:** RW  
**Reset State:** 0x00000000  
**Double Buffered:** YES  
**When:** On frame boundaries  

Display Interface Timing Engine Enable register

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1 | OSYNC_LOCK | |
| 0 | EN | Display Interface enable<br>Should be the LAST register programmed for the interface<br>Be sure to program ALL timing registers and setting up of the display pipeline BEFORE enabling this register<br>Upon disabling of this bit, hardware will stop driving the interface at the NEXT vsync boundary<br>A VSYNC interrupt WILL be generated but a VSYNC will NOT be generated on the interface |

### 0x01A6B804 MDSS_MDP_INTF_1_INTF_CONFIG

**Type:** RW  
**Reset State:** 0x00040000  

Display Interface Configuration register.
<!-- page 3779 -->

### MDSS_MDP_INTF_1_INTF_CONFIG (cont.)

*Note: The configuration register ONLY applies to INTF_4 which transmits to MHL.*

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31 | PROG_FETCH_START_EN | Programmable Fetch feature enable bit<br>0: programmable line counter disabled - default value to be backward compatible<br>1: programmable line counter enabled |
| 30 | ACTIVE_V_EN | Active V Enable |
| 29 | ACTIVE_H_EN | Active H Enable |
| 28 | VSYNC_INTERRUPT_MODE | vsync interrupt generation mode<br>0 = generate an interrupt every vsync<br>1 = generate an interrupt every 2 fields (applicable to interlace mode) |
| 27:24 | REPEAT_PIXEL_MODE | Pixel repeat mode<br>0x1 = repeat each pixel 2 times<br>0x2 = repeat each pixel 3 times<br>...<br>15 = repeat pixel 16 times |
| 23 | DSI_VIDEO_STOP_MODE | This bit controls how video mode stream is stopped when DSI dynamic refresh is triggered. It is not applicable for non-DSI interface.<br>0x0: disable timing engine when DSI sets the video stop signal;<br>0x1: halt timing engine counters when DSI sets the video stop signal |
| 21 | CHROMA_DWN_SAMPLE_H_MTHD | Horizontal Chroma Down Sample method<br>0x0: non-pixel dropping<br>0x1: pixel dropping |
| 20 | CHROMA_DWN_SAMPLE_EN | Chroma Down Sample enable for YUV444<br>0x0: Disabled<br>0x1: Enabled |
| 18 | CSC_DST_DATA_FORMAT | Destination Data Format<br>0x0: RGB<br>0x1: YCbCr |
| 17 | CSC_SRC_DATA_FORMAT | Source Data Format<br>0x0: RGB<br>0x1: YCbCr |
| 16 | CSC_EN | Enables the color matrix conversion<br>0x0: Bypass<br>0x1: Enabled |
<!-- page 3780 -->

### MDSS_MDP_INTF_1_INTF_CONFIG (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 13:11 | NIBBLE_SWAP_EN | Enable nibble swapping within each pixel byte<br>NIBBLE_SWAP_EN[0]: 0 = no swapping for pixel_data [7:0]; 1 = enable swapping of pixel_data[3:0] with pixel_data[7:4]<br>NIBBLE_SWAP_EN[1] = 0 = no swapping for pixel_data [15:8]; 1 = enable swapping of pixel_data[11:8] with pixel_data[15:12]<br>NIBBLE_SWAP_EN[2] = 0 = no swapping for pixel_data [23:16]; 1 = enable swapping of pixel_data[19:16] with pixel_data[23:20] |
| 10 | PACK_ALIGN | 0x0: LSB<br>0x1: MSB |
| 9:8 | PACK_422 | 0x0: Y2Cr1Y1Cb1<br>0x1: Cr1Y2Cb1Y1<br>0x2: Y2Cb1Y1Cr1<br>0x3: Cb1Y2Cr1Y1 |
| 6:4 | OUT_MODE | 0x0: YCbCr or RGB4444 seperate syncs 24-bit interface<br>0x1: RSVD<br>0x2: YCbCr 422 seperate syncs 16-bit interface |
| 2 | INTERLACE_INIT_SEL | 0x0: start with even field<br>0x1: start with odd field |
| 1 | REPEAT_PIXEL | 0x0: Do NOT repeat<br>0x1: Repeat |
| 0 | INTERLACE_MODE | double buffered: YES<br>0x0: Progressive Out<br>0x1: Interlace out |

### 0x01A6B81C MDSS_MDP_INTF_1_DISPLAY_V_START_F0

**Type:** RW  
**Reset State:** 0x00000000  
**Description:** Display Interface Vertical Active Start Control for field 0  
**Double Buffered:** YES  

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:0 | DISPLAY_START_Y | Display Y Start<br>Defines the time period between the field0 start of vsync pulse and the first displayed line position in pixel clocks<br>display_start_y = v_back_porch * hcycle<br>where hcycle = hotizontal_back_porch + horizontal_active + horizontal_front_porch<br>For eDP control the value programmed into this register differs slightly and should be programmed to the first active pixel and not the first pixel on that line!<br>In particular, the programming for eDP should be:<br>display_start_y = (v_back_porch * hcycle) + horizontal_back_porch |

| 8 | ENABLE | RW | MISR enable which starts/ends calculation of MISR on the next vsync/trigger event<br>This essentially double buffers the enable so that the misr doesn't start/end immediately but rather at a defined time<br>The MISR calculation would run until the end of programmed number of frames |

### 0x01A6C004 MDSS_MDP_INTF_2_INTF_CONFIG

* **Type**: RW
* **Reset State**: 0x00040000

Display Interface Configuration register.
<!-- page 3797 -->

Note that the configuration register ONLY applies to INTF_4 which transmits to MHL

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31 | PROG_FETCH_START_EN | Programmable Fetch feature enable bit<br>0: programmable line counter disabled - default value to be backward compatible<br>1: programmable line counter enabled |
| 30 | ACTIVE_V_EN | Active V Enable |
| 29 | ACTIVE_H_EN | Active H Enable |
| 28 | VSYNC_INTERRUPT_MODE | vsync interrupt generation mode<br>0 = generate an interrupt every vsync<br>1 = generate an interrupt every 2 fields (applicable to interlace mode) |
| 27:24 | REPEAT_PIXEL_MODE | Pixel repeat mode<br>0x1 = repeat each pixel 2 times<br>0x2 = repeat each pixel 3 times<br>...<br>15 = repeat pixel 16 times |
| 23 | DSI_VIDEO_STOP_MODE | This bit controls how video mode stream is stopped when DSI dynamic refresh is triggered. It is not applicable for non-DSI interface.<br>0x0: disable timing engine when DSI sets the video stop signal;<br>0x1: halt timing engine counters when DSI sets the video stop signal |
| 21 | CHROMA_DWN_SAMPLE_H_MTHD | Horizontal Chroma Down Sample method<br>0x0: non-pixel dropping<br>0x1: pixel dropping |
| 20 | CHROMA_DWN_SAMPLE_EN | Chroma Down Sample enable for YUV444<br>0x0: Disabled<br>0x1: Enabled |
| 18 | CSC_DST_DATA_FORMAT | Destination Data Format<br>0x0: RGB<br>0x1: YCbCr |
| 17 | CSC_SRC_DATA_FORMAT | Source Data Format<br>0x0: RGB<br>0x1: YCbCr |
| 16 | CSC_EN | Enables the color matrix conversion<br>0x0: Bypass<br>0x1: Enabled |
<!-- page 3798 -->

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 13:11 | NIBBLE_SWAP_EN | Enable nibble swapping within each pixel byte<br>NIBBLE_SWAP_EN[0]: 0 = no swapping for pixel_data [7:0]; 1 = enable swapping of pixel_data[3:0] with pixel_data[7:4]<br>NIBBLE_SWAP_EN[1] = 0 = no swapping for pixel_data [15:8]; 1 = enable swapping of pixel_data[11:8] with pixel_data[15:12]<br>NIBBLE_SWAP_EN[2] = 0 = no swapping for pixel_data [23:16]; 1 = enable swapping of pixel_data[19:16] with pixel_data[23:20] |
| 10 | PACK_ALIGN | 0x0: LSB<br>0x1:MSB |
| 9:8 | PACK_422 | 0x0: Y2Cr1Y1Cb1<br>0x1: Cr1Y2Cb1Y1<br>0x2: Y2Cb1Y1Cr1<br>0x3: Cb1Y2Cr1Y1 |
| 6:4 | OUT_MODE | 0x0: YCbCr or RGB4444 seperate syncs 24-bit interface<br>0x1: RSVD<br>0x2: YCbCr 422 seperate syncs 16-bit interface |
| 2 | INTERLACE_INIT_SEL | 0x0: start with even field<br>0x1: start with odd field |
| 1 | REPEAT_PIXEL | 0x0: Do NOT repeat<br>0x1: Repeat |
| 0 | INTERLACE_MODE | double buffered: YES<br>0x0: Progressive Out<br>0x1: Interlace out |

| 31:0 | DISPLAY_START_Y | Display Y Start<br>Defines the time period between the field0 start of vsync pulse and the first displayed line position in pixel clocks<br>display_start_y = v_back_porch * hcycle<br>where hcycle = horizontal_back_porch + horizontal_active + horizontal_front_porch<br>For eDP control the value programmed into this register differs slightly and should be programmed to the first active pixel and not the first pixel on that line!<br>In particular, the programming for eDP should be:<br>display_start_y = (v_back_porch * hcycle) + horizontal_back_porch |

| Bits | Name | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31 | RUN_MODE | RW | This register defines the operation mode for the MISR<br>0x0: Single run mode meaning it stops after the programmable number of frames (i.e. legacy mode prior to MDP5 1.5.0).<br>0x1: Free running mode meaning it updates the misr signature every programmable number of frames and continues to run while MISR_ENABLE is set to 0x1 |
| 27:24 | INPUT_SEL | RW | This field allows the selected input to propagate to the MISR in the event that multiple inputs want to share the same physcial MISR.<br>For example, the video interface might want to MISR on active pixel data only or active+timing information as well. This field would select which input is sent to the MISR |
| 10 | STATUS_CLEAR | W | This is a write only register that doesn't have any effect prior to MDP5 1.5.0 since there was no logic associated with it.<br>Write 0x1: Clears the MISR_STATUS register.<br>Write 0x0: Has no effect on the the MISR_STATUS register. |
| 9 | STATUS | R | Read only register.<br>Set to 0x1 when misr signature has been updated |
| 8 | ENABLE | RW | MISR enable which starts/ends calculation of MISR on the next vsync/trigger event.<br>This essentially double buffers the enable so that the misr doesn't start/end immediately but rather at a defined time.<br>The MISR calculation would run until the end of programmed number of frames |
| 7:0 | FRAME_COUNT | RW | Number of frames to run before capturing |

INTF

Display Interface hardware register description

### MDSS_MDP_INTF_3_TIMING_ENGINE_EN (0x01A6C800)

* **Type:** RW
* **Reset State:** 0x00000000
* **Double Buffered:** YES
* **When:** On frame boundaries

Display Interface Timing Engine Enable register

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1 | OSYNC_LOCK | |
| 0 | EN | Display Interface enable.<br>Should be the LAST register programmed for the interface.<br>Be sure to program ALL timing registers and setting up of the display pipeline BEFORE enabling this register.<br>Upon disabling of this bit, hardware will stop driving the interface at the NEXT vsync boundary.<br>A VSYNC interrupt WILL be generated but a VSYNC will NOT be generated on the interface |

### MDSS_MDP_INTF_3_INTF_CONFIG (0x01A6C804)

* **Type:** RW
* **Reset State:** 0x00040000

Display Interface Configuration register.
<!-- page 3815 -->

### MDSS_MDP_INTF_3_INTF_CONFIG (continued)

Note that the configuration register ONLY applies to INTF_4 which transmits to MHL

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31 | PROG_FETCH_START_EN | Programmable Fetch feature enable bit<br>0: programmable line counter disabled - default value to be backward compatible<br>1: programmable line counter enabled |
| 30 | ACTIVE_V_EN | Active V Enable |
| 29 | ACTIVE_H_EN | Active H Enable |
| 28 | VSYNC_INTERRUPT_MODE | vsync interrupt generation mode<br>0 = generate an interrupt every vsync<br>1 = generate an interrupt every 2 fields (applicable to interlace mode) |
| 27:24 | REPEAT_PIXEL_MODE | Pixel repeat mode<br>0x1 = repeat each pixel 2 times<br>0x2 = repeat each pixel 3 times<br>...<br>15 = repeat pixel 16 times |
| 23 | DSI_VIDEO_STOP_MODE | This bit controls how video mode stream is stopped when DSI dynamic refresh is triggered. It is not applicable for non-DSI interface.<br>0x0: disable timing engine when DSI sets the video stop signal;<br>0x1: halt timing engine counters when DSI sets the video stop signal |
| 21 | CHROMA_DWN_SAMPLE_H_MTHD | Horizontal Chroma Down Sample method<br>0x0: non-pixel dropping<br>0x1: pixel dropping |
| 20 | CHROMA_DWN_SAMPLE_EN | Chroma Down Sample enable for YUV444<br>0x0: Disabled<br>0x1: Enabled |
| 18 | CSC_DST_DATA_FORMAT | Destination Data Format<br>0x0: RGB<br>0x1: YCbCr |
| 17 | CSC_SRC_DATA_FORMAT | Source Data Format<br>0x0: RGB<br>0x1: YCbCr |
| 16 | CSC_EN | Enables the color matrix conversion<br>0x0: Bypass<br>0x1: Enabled |

| Bits | Name | Description |

(i.e. legacy mode prior to MDP5 1.5.0)<br>0x1: Free running mode meaning it updates the misr signature every programmable number of frames and continues to run while MISR_ENABLE is set to 0x1 |

| 9 | STATUS | R | Read only register<br>Set to 0x1 when misr signature has been updated |
| 8 | ENABLE | RW | MISR enable which starts/ends calculation of MISR on the next vsync/trigger event<br>This essentially double buffers the enable so that the misr doesn't start/end immediately but rather at a defined time<br>The MISR calculation would run until the end of programmed number of frames |
| 7:0 | FRAME_COUNT | RW | Number of frames to run before capturing |

#### 0x01A79000 MDSS_MDP_AADC_0_APICAL_CORE_BYPASS

**Type:** RW
**Reset State:** 0x00000101

Apical bypass and SW reset control

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 23:16 | APICAL_CORE_RESERVED_23_16 | RESERVED for future use. |
| 8 | APICAL_CORE_SW_RESET_EN | Enable SW reset control capability for Apical Iridix core - SHOULD always be set to 1'b1; (active high, default 0).<br>This ensures that when ares and apical_core_sw_reset are ORed together, the in/out conversion blocks reset first to block propagation of any potential hazards out of the apical wrapper; also clocks to the apical core are stopped preventing internal hazards. |
<!-- page 3850 -->

### MDSS_MDP_AADC_0_APICAL_CORE_BYPASS (continued)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 0 | APICAL_CORE_BYPASS | 0x0: Pass pixel data through Apical core - Apical processing is enabled via APICAL_IRIDIX_CONTROL_0.IRIDIX_ENABLE<br>0x1: Bypass Apical core entirely - this will also clock gate the core (default)<br><br>Double-buffered: Yes |

#### 0x01A79004 MDSS_MDP_AADC_0_APICAL_CONTROL_REG0

**Type:** RW
**Reset State:** 0x00000003
**double buffered:** Yes

The Data format port specifies the input data format so that the iridix core can process the different input data formats.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 7:2 | CONTROL_REG0_RESERVED_7_2 | Reserved - Should be zero, except for bit 3 which is hardcoded as 1b. |
| 1:0 | DATA_FORMAT | Data Format Select<br>0x0: YCbCr Color space 4:2:2 format, interleaved (Cb-Y-Cr-Y)<br>0x1: YCbCr Color space 4:2:2 format, parallel<br>0x2: YCbCr Color 4:4:4 format<br>0x3: RGB Color space |

#### 0x01A79008 MDSS_MDP_AADC_0_APICAL_CONTROL_REG1

**Type:** RW
**Reset State:** 0x00000000
**double buffered:** Yes

Synchronization Format Register.


<!-- page 3851 -->

### MDSS_MDP_AADC_0_APICAL_CONTROL_REG1 (continued)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 7 | AUTO_SIZE | Auto Size Register<br>0x0: Auto_Size off. The Iridix core will use Frame_Width, Frame_Height ports values<br>0x1: Auto_Size on. The Iridix core will calculate the frame geometry based on the active line and field signals. The size of current frame will be used for the estimation of the next frame. The Frame size will be updated when the Field signal toggles. |
| 6:0 | CONTROL_REG1_RESERVED_6_0 | Reserved, should be set to 0x00. |

### 0x01A79010 MDSS_MDP_AADC_0_APICAL_IRIDIX_CONTROL_0

**Type:** RW
**Reset State:** 0x00000006
**Double buffered:** Yes

Iridix Control Register 0

<!-- page 3852 -->

### MDSS_MDP_AADC_0_APICAL_IRIDIX_CONTROL_0 (continued)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 4 | IRIDIX_COLOR_CORRECTION | Color Correction/Control - Enabling this processing will result in more accurate colors processing. The color correction algorithm is required on gamma corrected sources. It reduces the saturation in dark areas when they are being amplified, and saturates bright parts when they get darker.<br>0x0: Disable color correction<br>0x1: Enable color correction |
| 3 | IRIDIX_LOCAL_CONTRAST_2D | Local contrast (2D)<br>0x0: Memory interfaces for 2D processing used<br>0x1: Memory interfaces for 2D processing bypassed, 2D processing disabled. This selection overrides LC0, LC1 settings.<br>Note: If 2D Local contrast is not implemented then the bit[3] should be one. |
| 2:1 | IRIDIX_LOCAL_CONTRAST | Local Contrast Control - This is a supplementary module preserving local contrast in small areas. Depending on custom implementation LC module can be implemented differently and may have different settings.<br>1D Case :<br>0x0: disabled;<br>0x1: LC enabled, kernel 1x3 used<br>0x2: LC enabled, kernel 1x3 used<br>0x3: LC enabled, kernel 1x5 used<br><br>2D Case :<br>0x0: disabled;<br>0x1: LC enabled, kernel 1x3 used<br>0x2: LC enabled, kernel 3x3 used<br>0x3: LC enabled, kernel 3x5 used |
| 0 | IRIDIX_ENABLE | iridix Enable - This bit turns iridix processing ON and OFF. When iridix is OFF, the video data passes to the output without any changes. Disabling iridix® using this bit is equivalent to setting the Strength parameter to 0. Many internal modules run in idle mode when this bit is 0. The Latency Delays between the input and the output signals are the same in both ON and OFF modes.<br>0x0: Disable iridix processing<br>0x1: Enable iridix processing |

### 0x01A7901C MDSS_MDP_AADC_0_APICAL_VARIANCE

**Type:** RW
**Reset State:** 0x00000041
**Double buffered:** Yes

Affects the sensitivity of the transform to different areas of the image, and can be increased in order to emphasize small regions (e.g. faces).

If this parameter is set to zero, the sensitivity to the small areas is maximal. The transform becomes more local.

When the parameter is set to 0xFF the transform deemphasizes small local details, and transform becomes more global e.g. the sky at the top of the frame can affect flowers at the bottom of the frame.

Default value is 36h but it depends on custom implementation.

Setting variance to zero will progressively increase the spatial sensitivity of the algorithm but it can lead to artificial-looking images in some cases.
<!-- page 3854 -->

### MDSS_MDP_AADC_0_APICAL_VARIANCE (continued)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 7:4 | VARIANCE_INTENSITY | Sets the degree of sensitivity in the luminance domain. Maximum Variance is 0xF, and minimum Variance is 0x0. |
| 3:0 | VARIANCE_SPACE | Sets the degree of spatial sensitivity of the algorithm. As this parameter is made smaller, the algorithm focuses on smaller regions within the image. Maximum Variance is 0xF, and minimum Variance is 0x0 |

### 0x01A79020 MDSS_MDP_AADC_0_APICAL_IRIDIX_DITHER

**Type:** RW
**Reset State:** 0x00000000
**Double buffered:** Yes

Iridix Dither Register: When the number of color gradations of a display device is small (for example 6 bit per color) pixel dithering can make gradients look smoother.

There can be a situation when iridix output signal is 12 bits but the signal needs to be compressed into 8 bits.

The best way for this is to use dithering of least significant bits and then truncate these bits. The dithering can be performed by iridix Processor. However, the truncation needs to be done by a hardware designer outside iridix.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 7:3 | IRIDIX_DITHER_RESERVED_7_3 | Reserved - Not used for now. |
| 2:0 | DITHER | Strength of Dithering.<br>0x0: No dithering<br>0x1: One least significant bit of the output signal is dithered<br>0x2: Two bits are dithered<br>0x3: Three bits are dithered<br>0x4: Four bits are dithered<br>Others: Four bits are dithered |

### 0x01A79024 MDSS_MDP_AADC_0_APICAL_DITEHR_CONTROL

**Type:** RW
**Reset State:** 0x00000000
<!-- page 3855 -->

### MDSS_MDP_AADC_0_APICAL_DITEHR_CONTROL (continued)

Spatial Perceptual Model Dither: This module provides a 4-bit dither via a spatial perceptual model. There is no temporal dependence of the dither pattern, therefore eliminating the possibility of flicker. Note that temporal dither is available via the port iridix_dither.

**Double buffered:** Yes

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 7:4 | DITHER_CONTROL_RESERVED_7_4 | Reserved - Should be Zero. |
| 3:2 | DITHER_AMOUNT | Strength of Dithering.<br>0x0: Dither 1 bit<br>0x1: Dither 2 bit<br>0x2: Dither 3 bit<br>0x3: Dither 4 bit |
| 1 | DITHER_SHIFT_MODE | Shift Mode:<br>0x0: Output is MSB aligned<br>0x1: Output is LSB aligned |
| 0 | DITHER_ENABLE_DITHER | Enable Dither: Enables the dither module.<br>0: Disable dither module<br>1: Enable dither module |

Maximum limit is 0xF, when the value is 0x0 there is no limit. |

### MDSS_MDP_AADC_0_APICAL_LIMIT_AMPL (continued)

### 0x01A7902C MDSS_MDP_AADC_0_APICAL_SLOPE

**Type:** RW
**Reset State:** 0x00003C80
**Double buffered:** Yes

Slope Min and Max Limit used to restrict the slope of the tone-curve generated by Iridix.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 15:8 | SLOPE_MAX | Slope Max Limit - Slope Max Limit is used to restrict the slope of the tone-curve generated by iridix.<br>When Slope Max Limit parameter is set to 0xFF, the tone curve slope, generated by iridix is not limited (maximum slope 15).<br>When this value is set to 00 iridix will not generate the tone-curve with slope greater than 16/15 (48°).<br>Intermediate values of Slope Limit are linear interpolation between minimum and maximum values. Recommended Slope Max Limit range is 20h-60h.<br>For noisy images less value should be used. See Chapter 4 for more explanation. |
| 7:0 | SLOPE_MIN | Slope Min Limit - Slope Min Limit is used to restrict the slope of the tone-curve generated by iridix.<br>When Slope Min Limit parameter is set to 0x00, the tone curve slope, generated by iridix is not limited.<br>When this value is set to FF iridix will not generate the tone-curve with slope less than 3/4.<br>Intermediate values of Slope Limit are linear interpolation between minimum and maximum values. Recommended Slope Min Limit range is 00h-C0h. See Chapter 4 for more explanation. |

### 0x01A79030 MDSS_MDP_AADC_0_APICAL_BW_LEVEL

**Type:** RW
**Reset State:** 0x03FF0000

Black and White Level of the Iridix IP.
<!-- page 3857 -->

### MDSS_MDP_AADC_0_APICAL_BW_LEVEL (continued)

The least significant bits [dw-1:0] are used; higher bits [15:dw] are unused. dw is the component data width. dw=8 for MDSS.

**Double buffered:** Yes

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 25:16 | WHITE_LEVEL | White Level - The value stored in White Level Port will be used as white level for iridix processing in all unsigned data channels. Data above White level will not be processed and stay unchanged.<br>Note:<br>1. For 12 bit variant minimum White Level is constrained as: White Level - Black Level > 1024.<br>2. For 10 bit variant minimum White Level is constrained as: White Level - Black Level > 256. |
| 9:0 | BLACK_LEVEL | Black Level - The value stored in Black Level Port will be used as zero level for iridix processing in all unsigned data channels. Data below Black level will not be processed and stay unchanged.<br>Note:<br>1. For 12 bit variant maximum Black Level is constrained as: White Level - Black Level > 1024.<br>2. For 10 bit variant maximum Black Level is constrained as: White Level - Black Level > 256. |

### Register: `MDSS_MDP_AADC_0_APICAL_CALIBRATION_AB`
- **Address**: `0x01A790CC`
- **Type**: `RW`
- **Reset State**: `0x005F006E`
- **Double Buffered**: No

Screen calibration parameter

Four calibration parameters control the overall adaptation of displayed content to ambient light and backlight level.
They represent a combination of physical and perceptual factors which influence the apparent contrast of imagery as the user's eyes adapt to changing viewing conditions.
<!-- page 3873 -->

### Register: `MDSS_MDP_AADC_0_APICAL_CALIBRATION_AB` (Continuation)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---------- |
| 31:16 | CALIBRATION_B | This parameter controls the adaptation of content to the screen brightness. As backlight is reduced in the presence of ambient light, shadow detail is progressively lost below the minimum grey level of the display. When calibrated correctly, this parameter ensures that image content remains viewable at all backlight levels. |
| 15:0 | CALIBRATION_A | This parameter is related to the reflectivity of the screen. The more reflective the screen, the greater is the loss of shadow detail as ambient light level increases. It is the objective of the Assertive Display core to maintain the same level of shadow detail which pertains in very low light, up to ambient light levels typical of outdoor viewing. When calibrated correctly, this parameter ensures that image content is neither lost nor over-enhanced leading to preservation of the viewing experience. |

### Register: `MDSS_MDP_AADC_0_APICAL_CALIBRATION_CD`
- **Address**: `0x01A790D0`
- **Type**: `RW`
- **Reset State**: `0x00000013`
- **Double Buffered**: No

Screen calibration parameter

Four calibration parameters control the overall adaptation of displayed content to ambient light and backlight level.
They represent a combination of physical and perceptual factors which influence the apparent contrast of imagery as the user's eyes adapt to changing viewing conditions.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---------- |
| 31:16 | CALIBRATION_D | Typical movie, image and gaming content is 8-bit and encoded with a gamma curve which results in a dynamic range of around 1000:1. Most large displays have an effective contrast ratio larger than this under ideal viewing conditions (full backlight, low ambient light). However, many portable displays cannot reproduce such contrast ratios even under ideal conditions. When calibrated correctly, this parameter increases the effective contrast ratio of low contrast displays to match that of typical content. |
<!-- page 3874 -->

### Register: `MDSS_MDP_AADC_0_APICAL_CALIBRATION_CD` (Continuation)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---------- |
| 15:0 | CALIBRATION_C | This parameter controls the adaptation of content to overcome the limitations of the human eye sensitivity at very low light. Decreasing screen brightness in total darkness causes loss of image detail in shadow regions, especially on small displays, as the eyes are unable to adapt sufficiently. When calibrated correctly, this parameter enables restoration of such details. |

### Register: `MDSS_MDP_AADC_0_APICAL_FILTER`
- **Address**: `0x01A790F4`
- **Type**: `RW`
- **Reset State**: `0x000606CA`
- **Double Buffered**: No

Filter values for the input ambient_light

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---------- |
| 23:16 | FILTER_B | This value sets the ambient light-independent component of the stability threshold, below which deviations in photosensor measurements do not lead to a response by the backlight. Larger values result in greater stability to changes in photosensor measurements. This component of the threshold becomes increasingly influential as average ambient light decreases. |
| 15:0 | FILTER_A | FilterA Settings:<br>- **[11:9]**: Sets the recursion depth of the temporal filter used to smooth out rapid changes in detected ambient light. The larger this parameter, the greater the recursion depth, and the more slowly the backlight responds to changes in ambient light.<br>- **[8:6]**: Sets the ambient light-dependent component of the stability threshold, below which deviations in photosensor measurements do not lead to a response by the backlight. Larger values result in greater stability to changes in photosensor measurements. This component of the threshold becomes increasingly influential as average ambient light increases.<br>- **[5:3]**: Sets the rate at which backlight responds to changes in photosensor measurements, within the stability range established by the values in bits [8:6] and filter_b.<br>- **[2:0]**: Sets the asymmetry between the rate of decrease of backlight compared to the rate of increase of backlight. A value of 0 implies symmetric response, while increasing this value leads to a faster increase in backlight compared to decrease. |

### Register: `MDSS_MDP_AADC_0_APICAL_CONFIG_BUFFER`
- **Address**: `0x01A790F8`
- **Type**: `RW`
- **Reset State**: `0x00000003`
- **Double Buffered**: No

Double buffering control for Video Pipeline Configuration Parameters

Together with config_buffer_global real time input for iridix core, which is driven by vp_db_update, these control the double buffering of the video pipeline configuration parameters inside Iridix core.
<!-- page 3878 -->

### Register: `MDSS_MDP_AADC_0_APICAL_CONFIG_BUFFER` (Continuation)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---------- |
| 1:0 | CONFIG_BUFFER_MODE | config_buffer_mode = 0 (dec) (Pass through): Allows the input configuration ports to pass through to the registers within the core. The internal configuration registers are updated as soon as the ports are changed.<br>config_buffer_mode = 1 (dec) (Block Access): Stops the internal configuration registers from being updated even when the input port values change. The previous register values are held till the next update is allowed.<br>config_buffer_mode = 2 (dec) (Update on VBI): Allows the internal configuration registers only to be updated during the vertical blanking interval (VBI). This ensures that the configuration is never updated during an active frame.<br>config_buffer_mode = 3 (dec) (External): This method is based on the config_buffer_global signal and updates the internal configuration registers when the config_buffer_global signal is asserted. This signal can be generated externally by user logic. |

### 0x01A79148 MDSS_MDP_AADC_0_APICAL_START_CALC

* **Type**: RW
* **Reset State**: `0x00000000`
<!-- page 3886 -->

* **Double Buffered**: No
* **Description**: Start calculator pulse.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 0 | START_CALC | Start calculation register. <br>Start-Done Protocol of non-Video Pipeline Parameters: <br>Double buffering is not required for the Assertive Display core parameters. Instead a simple start-done protocol is used. The external host will update the parameters and then transition the start_calc input from 0 to 1. <br>After a rising edge is detected on this input, the Assertive Display core's calculator will use the input parameters to calculate the backlight and iridix module strength and the optimum backlight. <br>When the results are available the calc_done status flag is asserted about 500 clock cycles after this edge. In a typical use case this calc_done flag can be used as an interrupt to start the next parameter update cycle. <br>The calc_done flag is held high until the next start_calc rising edge arrives. |

In a typical use case this calc_done flag can be used as an interrupt to start the next parameter update cycle. <br>The calc_done flag is held high until the next start_calc rising edge arrives. |

| 23:16 | APICAL_CORE_RESERVED_23_16 | RESERVED for future use. |
| 8 | APICAL_CORE_SW_RESET_EN | Enable SW reset control capability for Apical Iridix core - SHOULD always be set to 1'b1; (active high, default 0). <br>This ensures that when ares and apical_core_sw_reset are ORed together, the in/out conversion blocks reset first to block propagation of any potential hazards out of the apical wrapper; also clocks to the apical core are stopped preventing internal hazards. |
| 0 | APICAL_CORE_BYPASS | 0x0 : Pass pixel data through Apical core - Apical processing is enabled via APICAL_IRIDIX_CONTROL_0.IRIDIX_ENABLE <br>0x1 : Bypass Apical core entirely - this will also clock gate the core (default) <br>Double-buffered: Yes |

The Iridix core will calculate the frame geometry based on the active line and field signals. The size of current frame will be used for the estimation of the next frame. The Frame size will be updated when the Field signal toggles. |

### 0x01A79810 MDSS_MDP_AADC_1_APICAL_IRIDIX_CONTROL_0

* **Type**: RW
* **Reset State**: `0x00000006`
* **Double Buffered**: Yes

Iridix Control Register 0

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 7:5 | IRIDIX_CONTROL_0_RESERVED_7_5 | Reserved - Should be zero. |
| 4 | IRIDIX_COLOR_CORRECTION | Color Correction/Control - Enabling this processing will result in more accurate colors processing. <br>The color correction algorithm is required on gamma corrected sources. It reduces the saturation in dark areas when they are being amplified, and saturates bright parts when they get darker. <br>0x0: Disable color correction <br>0x1: Enable color correction |
| 3 | IRIDIX_LOCAL_CONTRAST_2D | Local contrast (2D) <br>0x0: Memory interfaces for 2D processing used <br>0x1: Memory interfaces for 2D processing bypassed, 2D processing disabled. This selection overrides LC0, LC1 settings. <br>Note: If 2D Local contrast is not implemented then the bit[3] should be one. |


<!-- page 3891 -->

### MDSS_MDP_AADC_1_APICAL_IRIDIX_CONTROL_0 (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 2:1 | IRIDIX_LOCAL_CONTRAST | Local Contrast Control - This is a supplementary module preserving local contrast in small areas.<br>Depending on custom implementation LC module can be implemented differently and may have different settings.<br>1D Case :<br>0x0: disabled;<br>0x1: LC enabled, kernel 1x3 used<br>0x2: LC enabled, kernel 1x3 used<br>0x3: LC enabled, kernel 1x5 used<br><br>2D Case :<br>0x0: disabled;<br>0x1: LC enabled, kernel 1x3 used<br>0x2: LC enabled, kernel 3x3 used<br>0x3: LC enabled, kernel 3x5 used |
| 0 | IRIDIX_ENABLE | iridix Enable - This bit turns iridix processing ON and OFF. When iridix is OFF, the video data passes to the output without any changes.<br>Disabling iridix®using this bit is equivalent to setting the Strength parameter to 0. Many internal modules run in idle mode when this bit is 0.<br>The Latency Delays between the input and the output signals are the same in both ON and OFF modes.<br>0x0: Disable iridix processing<br>0x1: Enable iridix processing |

### MDSS_MDP_AADC_1_APICAL_VARIANCE

**Address:** `0x01A7981C`
**Type:** `RW`
**Reset State:** `0x00000041`
**Double Buffered:** Yes

Affects the sensitivity of the transform to different areas of the image, and can be increased in order to emphasize small regions (e.g. faces).

If this parameter is set to zero, the sensitivity to the small areas is maximal. The transform becomes more local.

When the parameter is set to 0xFF the transform deemphasizes small local details, and transform becomes more global e.g. the sky at the top of the frame can affect flowers at the bottom of the frame.

Default value is 36h but it depends on custom implementation.
Setting variance to zero will progressively increase the spatial sensitivity of the algorithm but it can lead to artificial-looking images in some cases.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 7:4 | VARIANCE_INTENSITY | Sets the degree of sensitivity in the luminance domain. Maximum Variance is 0xF, and minimum Variance is 0x0. |
| 3:0 | VARIANCE_SPACE | Sets the degree of spatial sensitivity of the algorithm. As this parameter is made smaller, the algorithm focuses on smaller regions within the image. Maximum Variance is 0xF, and minimum Variance is 0x0 |
<!-- page 3893 -->

### MDSS_MDP_AADC_1_APICAL_IRIDIX_DITHER

**Address:** `0x01A79820`
**Type:** `RW`
**Reset State:** `0x00000000`
**Double Buffered:** Yes

Iridix Dither Register: When the number of color gradations of a display device is small (for example 6 bit per color) pixel dithering can make gradients look smoother.

There can be a situation when iridix output signal is 12 bits but the signal needs to be compressed into 8 bits.

The best way for this is to use dithering of least significant bits and then truncate these bits. The dithering can be performed by iridix Processor.

However, the truncation needs to be done by a hardware designer outside iridix.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 7:3 | IRIDIX_DITHER_RESERVE_D_7_3 | Reserved - Not used for now. |
| 2:0 | DITHER | Strength of Dithering.<br>0x0: No dithering<br>0x1: One least significant bit of the output signal is dithered<br>0x2: Two bits are dithered<br>0x3: Three bits are dithered<br>0x4: Four bits are dithered<br>Others: Four bits are dithered |

### MDSS_MDP_AADC_1_APICAL_DITEHR_CONTROL

**Address:** `0x01A79824`
**Type:** `RW`
**Reset State:** `0x00000000`
**Double Buffered:** Yes

Spatial Preceptual Model Dither

This module provides a 4-bit dither via a spatial perceptual model.

There is no temporal dependence of the dither pattern, therefore eliminating the possibility of flicker.

Note that temporal dither is available via the port iridix_dither.
<!-- page 3894 -->

### MDSS_MDP_AADC_1_APICAL_DITEHR_CONTROL (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 7:4 | DITHER_CONTROL_RESERVED_7_4 | Reserved - Should be Zero. |
| 3:2 | DITHER_AMOUNT | Strength of Dithering.<br>0x0: Dither 1 bit<br>0x1: Dither 2 bit<br>0x2: Dither 3 bit<br>0x3: Dither 4 bit |
| 1 | DITHER_SHIFT_MODE | Shift Mode:<br>0x0: Output is MSB aligned<br>0x1: Output is LSB aligned |
| 0 | DITHER_ENABLE_DITHER | Enable Dither: Enables the dither module.<br>0: Disable dither module<br>1: Enable dither module |

### MDSS_MDP_AADC_1_APICAL_LIMIT_AMPL

**Address:** `0x01A79828`
**Type:** `RW`
**Reset State:** `0x000000F0`
**Double Buffered:** Yes

Two parameters used to restrict the luminance space in which Iridix can adaptively generate tone curves for each pixel.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 7:4 | BRIGHT_AMP_LIMIT | Bright amplification limit - The resultant tone curve cannot be lower than bright amplification limit line controlled by the bright amplification limit parameter.<br>See Apical TRM Chapter 4 for more explanation. Maximum limit is 0xF, when the value is 0x0 there is no limit. |
| 3:0 | DARK_AMP_LIMIT | Dark amplification limit - The resultant tone curve cannot be higher than dark amplification limit line controlled by the dark amplification limit parameter.<br>See Apical TRM Chapter 4 for more explanation. Maximum limit is 0xF, when the value is 0x0 there is no limit. |
<!-- page 3895 -->

### MDSS_MDP_AADC_1_APICAL_SLOPE

**Address:** `0x01A7982C`
**Type:** `RW`
**Reset State:** `0x00003C80`
**Double Buffered:** Yes

Slope Min and Max Limit used to restrict the slope of the tone-curve generated by Iridix.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 15:8 | SLOPE_MAX | Slope Max Limit - Slope Max Limit is used to restrict the slope of the tone-curve generated by iridix.<br>When Slope Max Limit parameter is set to 0xFF, the tone curve slope, generated by iridix is not limited (maximum slope 15).<br>When this value is set to 00 iridix will not generate the tone-curve with slope greater than 16/15 (48°).<br>Intermediate values of Slope Limit are linear interpolation between minimum and maximum values. Recommended Slope Max Limit range is 20h-60h.<br>For noisy images less value should be used. See Chapter 4 for more explanation. |
| 7:0 | SLOPE_MIN | Slope Min Limit - Slope Min Limit is used to restrict the slope of the tone-curve generated by iridix.<br>When Slope Min Limit parameter is set to 0x00, the tone curve slope, generated by iridix is not limited.<br>When this value is set to FF iridix will not generate the tone-curve with slope less than 3/4.<br>Intermediate values of Slope Limit are linear interpolation between minimum and maximum values.<br>Recommended Slope Min Limit range is 00h-C0h. See Chapter 4 for more explanation. |

### MDSS_MDP_AADC_1_APICAL_BW_LEVEL

**Address:** `0x01A79830`
**Type:** `RW`
**Reset State:** `0x03FF0000`
**Double Buffered:** Yes

Black and White Level of the Iridix IP.

The least significant bits [dw-1:0] are used; higher bits [15:dw] are unused. dw is the component data width. dw=8 for MDSS.

### MDSS_MDP_AADC_1_APICAL_BW_LEVEL (cont.)

For 12 bit variant minimum White Level is constrained as: White Level - Black Level > 1024.<br>2. For 10 bit variant minimum White Level is constrained as: White Level - Black Level > 256. |
| 9:0 | BLACK_LEVEL | Black Level - The value stored in Black Level Port will be used as zero level for iridix processing in all unsigned data channels.<br>Data below Black level will not be processed and stay unchanged.<br>Note: 1. For 12 bit variant maximum Black Level is constrained as: White Level - Black Level > 1024.<br>2. For 10 bit variant maximum Black Level is constrained as: White Level - Black Level > 256 |

### 0x01A798CC MDSS_MDP_AADC_1_APICAL_CALIBRATION_AB

**Type:** RW

**Reset State:** 0x005F006E

Screen calibration parameter

Four calibration parameters control the overall adaptation of displayed content to ambient light and backlight level.
They represent a combination of physical and perceptual factors which influence the apparent contrast of imagery as the user's eyes adapt to changing viewing conditions.

**double buffered:** No
<!-- page 3912 -->

### MDSS_MDP_AADC_1_APICAL_CALIBRATION_AB (continued)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:16 | CALIBRATION_B | This parameter controls the adaptation of content to the screen brightness. As backlight is reduced in the presence of ambient light, shadow detail is progressively lost below the minimum grey level of the display. When calibrated correctly, this parameter ensures that image content remains viewable at all backlight levels. |
| 15:0 | CALIBRATION_A | This parameter is related to the reflectivity of the screen. The more reflective the screen, the greater is the loss of shadow detail as ambient light level increases. It is the objective of the Assertive Display core to maintain the same level of shadow detail which pertains in very low light, up to ambient light levels typical of outdoor viewing. When calibrated correctly, this parameter ensures that image content is neither lost nor over-enhanced leading to preservation of the viewing experience. |

### 0x01A798D0 MDSS_MDP_AADC_1_APICAL_CALIBRATION_CD

**Type:** RW

**Reset State:** 0x00000013

Screen calibration parameter

Four calibration parameters control the overall adaptation of displayed content to ambient light and backlight level.
They represent a combination of physical and perceptual factors which influence the apparent contrast of imagery as the user's eyes adapt to changing viewing conditions.

**double buffered:** No

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:16 | CALIBRATION_D | Typical movie, image and gaming content is 8-bit and encoded with a gamma curve which results in a dynamic range of around 1000:1. Most large displays have an effective contrast ratio larger than this under ideal viewing conditions (full backlight, low ambient light). However, many portable displays cannot reproduce such contrast ratios even under ideal conditions. When calibrated correctly, this parameter increases the effective contrast ratio of low contrast displays to match that of typical content. |
<!-- page 3913 -->

### MDSS_MDP_AADC_1_APICAL_CALIBRATION_CD (continued)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 15:0 | CALIBRATION_C | This parameter controls the adaptation of content to overcome the limitations of the human eye sensitivity at very low light. Decreasing screen brightness in total darkness causes loss of image detail in shadow regions, especially on small displays, as the eyes are unable to adapt sufficiently. When calibrated correctly, this parameter enables restoration of such details. |

### 0x01A798F4 MDSS_MDP_AADC_1_APICAL_FILTER

**Type:** RW

**Reset State:** 0x000606CA

Filter values for the input ambient_light

**double buffered:** No

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 23:16 | FILTER_B | This value sets the ambient light-independent component of the stability threshold, below which deviations in photosensor measurements do not lead to a response by the backlight. Larger values result in greater stability to changes in photosensor measurements. This component of the threshold becomes increasingly influential as average ambient light decreases. |
| 15:0 | FILTER_A | FilterA Settings:<br>**[11:9]**: Sets the recursion depth of the temporal filter used to smooth out rapid changes in detected ambient light. The larger this parameter, the greater the recursion depth, and the more slowly the backlight responds to changes in ambient light.<br>**[8:6]**: Sets the ambient light-dependent component of the stability threshold, below which deviations in photosensor measurements do not lead to a response by the backlight. Larger values result in greater stability to changes in photosensor measurements. This component of the threshold becomes increasingly influential as average ambient light increases.<br>**[5:3]**: Sets the rate at which backlight responds to changes in photosensor measurements, within the stability range established by the values in bits [8:6] and filter_b.<br>**[2:0]**: Sets the asymmetry between the rate of decrease of backlight compared to the rate of increase of backlight. A value of 0 implies symmetric response, while increasing this value leads to a faster increase in backlight compared to decrease. |

### 0x01A798F8 MDSS_MDP_AADC_1_APICAL_CONFIG_BUFFER

**Type:** RW

**Reset State:** 0x00000003

Double buffering control for Video Pipeline Configuration Parameters

Together with config_buffer_global real time input for iridix core, which is driven by vp_db_update, these control the double buffering of the video pipeline configuration parameters inside Iridix core.

**double buffered:** No
<!-- page 3917 -->

### MDSS_MDP_AADC_1_APICAL_CONFIG_BUFFER (continued)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1:0 | CONFIG_BUFFER_MODE | **config_buffer_mode = 0 (dec) (Pass through)**: Allows the input configuration ports to pass through to the registers within the core. The internal configuration registers are updated as soon as the ports are changed.<br>**config_buffer_mode = 1 (dec) (Block Access)**: Stops the internal configuration registers from being updated even when the input port values change. The previous register values are held till the next update is allowed.<br>**config_buffer_mode = 2 (dec) (Update on VBI)**: Allows the internal configuration registers only to be updated during the vertical blanking interval (VBI). This ensures that the configuration is never updated during an active frame.<br>**config_buffer_mode = 3 (dec) (External)**: This method is based on the config_buffer_global signal and updates the internal configuration registers when the config_buffer_global signal is asserted. This signal can be generated externally by user logic. |

### MDSS_MDP_AADC_1_APICAL_START_CALC

**Address:** `0x01A79948`
**Type:** RW
**Reset State:** `0x00000000`
<!-- page 3925 -->

Start calculator pulse.
double buffered: NO

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 0 | START_CALC | Start calculation register<br>Start-Done Protocol of non-Video Pipeline Parameters:<br>Double buffering is not required for the Assertive Display core parameters. Instead a simple start-done protocol is used. The external host will update the parameters and then transition the start_calc input from 0 to 1.<br>After a rising edge is detected on this input, the Assertive Display core's calculator will use the input parameters to calculate the backlight and iridix module strength and the optimum backlight.<br>When the results are available the calc_done status flag is asserted about 500 clock cycles after this edge. In a typical use case this calc_done flag can be used as an interrupt to start the next parameter update cycle.<br>The calc_done flag is held high until the next start_calc rising edge arrives. |

## 17.18 MDSS_DSI_0

Basic description of the dsi controller block

### 17.18.1 MDSS_DSI_0_DSI

DSI

### MDSS_DSI_0_CTRL

**Address:** `0x01A98004`
**Type:** RW
**Reset State:** `0x00000000`

DSI Control Register provides general control to the protocol, lane management and PHY layers

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 30 | NEW_INTERLEAVE_MODE_EN | unused (Enable new interleave mode with H/W arbitration between long commands and BLLP periods.) |
| 29:28 | PACKET_BYTE_MSB_LSB_FLIP | Swap the bit ordering of each byte of a packet<br>0: no swap (bit 0 is lsb, bit 7 is msb)<br>1: swap each byte of payload (bit 0 is msb, bit 7 is lsb)<br>2: swap each byte of packet (bit 0 is msb, bit 7 is lsb) |
| 26 | RESERVED | Reserved |
| 24 | CRC_CHK_EN | Enable CRC verification of the received packets |
| 20 | ECC_CHK_EN | Enable ECC verification of the received packets |
| 8 | CLKLN_EN | Enable clock lane of the PHY |
| 7 | DLN3_EN | Enable data lane 3 of the PHY |
| 6 | DLN2_EN | Enable data lane 2 of the PHY |
| 5 | DLN1_EN | Enable data lane 1 of the PHY |
| 4 | DLN0_EN | Enable data lane 0 of the PHY |
| 2 | CMD_MODE_EN | Enable the Command Mode Engine. |
| 1 | VIDEO_MODE_EN | Enable the Video Mode Engine. |
| 0 | DSI_EN | Enable the DSI controller. |
<!-- page 3928 -->

### MDSS_DSI_0_STATUS

**Address:** `0x01A98008`
**Type:** RW
**Reset State:** `0x00000000`

DSI Status Register provides status of the DSI controller

| Bits | Name | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31 | INTERLEAVE_OP_CONTENTION_CLR | W | writing a 1 to this field will clear this bit |
| 31 | INTERLEAVE_OP_CONTENTION | R | The controller generates command mode packets and video mode packets at the same time (i.e.: the command mode packets are longer than one BLLP period) |
| 6 | PHY_RESET_BUSY | R | DSI interface is busy sending the panel reset through the link |
| 5 | GENERIC_TRIGGER_BUSY | R | DSI interface is busy sending the generic trigger through the link |
| 4 | BTA_BUSY | R | DSI interface is busy waiting for read response, acknowledge or tearing effect signal from the peripheral |
| 3 | VIDEO_MODE_ENGINE_BUSY | R | Video Mode Engine is busy sending data from display engine |
| 2 | CMD_MODE_MDP_BUSY | R | Command Mode Engine is busy sending data from display engine |
| 1 | CMD_MODE_DMA_BUSY | R | Command Mode Engine is busy sending data from memory or reading data from the display panel |
| 0 | CMD_MODE_ENGINE_BUSY | R | Command Mode Engine Busy |

### MDSS_DSI_0_VIDEO_MODE_CTRL

**Address:** `0x01A98010`
**Type:** RW
**Reset State:** `0x00008000`

DSI Video Mode Engine Control Register


<!-- page 3931 -->

### MDSS_DSI_0_VIDEO_MODE_CTRL

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31 | LAST_LINE_INTERLEAVE_EN | Allow command mode operation interleaved on last line of video stream<br>0: disable<br>1: enable |
| 28 | PULSE_MODE_OPT | Select pulse mode option<br>0: no HSA and HE following VS/VE packet<br>1: send HSA and HE following VS/VE packet |
| 24 | HFP_PWR_MODE | Select power mode during the HFP period<br>0: send blanking packets in High Speed mode<br>1: low power stop mode (LP-11) |
| 20 | HBP_PWR_MODE | Select power mode during the HBP period<br>0: send blanking packets in High Speed mode<br>1: low power stop mode (LP-11) |
| 16 | HSA_PWR_MODE | Select power mode during the HSA period<br>0: send blanking packets in High Speed mode<br>1: low power stop mode (LP-11) |
| 15 | EOF_BLLP_PWR_MODE | Select power mode for the BLLP of the last line of a frame<br>0: send blanking packets during BLLP in high speed mode and block Command Mode packets<br>1: low power stop mode (LP-11) or let Command Mode Engine send packets in HS or LP mode |
| 12 | BLLP_PWR_MODE | DSI Power Mode for packets sent during BLLP period<br>0: send blanking packets during BLLP in high speed mode and block Command Mode packets<br>1: low power stop mode (LP-11) or let Command Mode Engine send packets in HS or LP mode |
| 9:8 | TRAFFIC_MODE | DSI video mode traffic sequence<br>0: non-burst mode with sync pulses<br>1: non-burst mode with sync start events<br>2: burst mode |
| 5:4 | DST_FORMAT | Pixel format. If there is interleaved Command Mode pixel packets (generated from MDP), the pixel depth of the Command Mode pixel packet should be greater or equal to the pixel depth of the Video mode pixel packet.<br>0: RGB565<br>1: RGB666 (packed)<br>2: RGB666 (loosely packed)<br>3: RGB888 |
| 1:0 | VC | Virtual channel identifier |

### MDSS_DSI_0_VIDEO_MODE_DATA_CTRL (0x01A98020)

**Type:** RW
**Reset State:** 0x00000000

DSI Video Mode Data Control Register

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 14:12 | RGB_SWAP | Swaps the R, G, and B channels of the dst pixels. This field should be used when different R,G, and B orderings are required. For example, if RGB_SWAP = 1 , RGB565 will become RBG556. |
| 8 | B_SEL | Bit Swaps the B Channel of the dst pixel. This field is used to reverse the ordering of the bits that is outputed for the color red. For example, for RGB888 color format, if the red component is 10000000 then if this field is enabled, 00000001 is output. |
| 4 | G_SEL | Bit Swaps the G Channel of the dst pixel. This field is used to reverse the ordering of the bits that is outputed for the color red. For example, for RGB888 color format, if the red component is 10000000 then if this field is enabled, 00000001 is output. |
| 0 | R_SEL | Bit Swaps the R Channel of the dst pixel. This field is used to reverse the ordering of the bits that is outputed for the color red. For example, for RGB888 color format, if the red component is 10000000 then if this field is enabled, 00000001 is output. |

| Bits | Name | Description |

| 15 | STREAM1_DST_FORMAT_SEL | Pixel format selection for stream 1. If MDP sends two streams to DSI and these streams have different output formats, then the pixel clock must be set according to the smallest pixel depth between the two. Otherwise, underflow may occur. Ex.: If stream0 is in RGB888 and stream1 is in RGB565, then pixel clock must be greater than dsiclk/2.<br>0: DST_FORMAT (same as stream0)<br>1: DST_FORMAT1 |

This field is used to reverse the ordering of the bits that is outputed for the color red. For example, for RGB888 color format, if the red component is 10000000 then if this field is enabled, 00000001 is output. |
| 12 | B_SEL | Bit Swaps the B Channel of the dst pixel. This field is used to reverse the ordering of the bits that is outputed for the color red. For example, for RGB888 color format, if the red component is 10000000 then if this field is enabled, 00000001 is output. |
| 9 | G_SEL1 | Bit Swaps the G Channel of the dst pixel for stream 1 (if STREAM1_DST_FORMAT_SEL = 1, otherwise bit swap for stream1 is defined by G_SEL). ### 0x01A98084 MDSS_DSI_0_TRIG_CTRL

* **Type**: RW

* **Description**: DSI Trigger Control Register. When DSI is enabled and CRTC1 or 2 is used for other non-DSI panels, the display engine path trigger must be set to manual internal, otherwise the CRTC will be stalled.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31 | TE_SEL | Select TE path<br>0: Tearing effect (external trigger) returns from data link<br>1: Tearing effect (external trigger) returns from a dedicated pin |
| 28 | COMMAND_MODE_DMA_MDP_ORDER | This bit field indicates whether DMA or MDP path will win the arbitration if both requests the link at the same time<br>0: DMA has higher priority than display processor<br>1: Display processor has higher priority than DMA |
| 24 | COMMAND_MODE_MDP_REQ_ORDER | If PHY TE is required for one of the MDP stream while the other stream is ready to transmit, this field determines which will win the arbitration<br>0: Command Mode MDP PHY TE request has higher priority than Command Mode MDP data transmission request<br>1: Command Mode MDP Data transmission request has higher priority than Command Mode MDP PHY TE request |
| 12 | BLOCK_DMA_WITHIN_FRAME | If Command Mode DMA operation is triggered in the middle of a frame of the stream selected by COMMAND_MODE_DMA_STREAM_SEL, delay the operation until end of frame, otherwise service the dma operation right away |

| :--- | :--- | :--- |

(The stream to be triggered is selected by COMMAND_MODE_DMA_STREAM_SEL)<br>0: none<br>1: reserved0<br>2: TE<br>3: reserved1<br>4: sw trigger<br>5: reserved2<br>6: sw trigger and TE<br>7: reserved3 |

### 0x01A98114 MDSS_DSI_0_IOBIST_CTRL

**Type:** RW  
**Reset State:** 0x00000000  

DSI IOBIST Control Register
<!-- page 3964 -->
### MDSS_DSI_0_IOBIST_CTRL (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:0 | DSI_IOBIST_CTRL | This register has 2 modes of operation: command and timing mode. All configuration fields should be written first, then enable (bit 0) should be set to 1 next and start (bit 5) is set to 1 last.<br><br>**COMMAND MODE** (bit 15 = 0)<br>- **bit 0**: DSI IOBIST ENABLE. Active high;<br>- **bit 5**: IOBIST start. Active high;<br>- **bit 6**: Select power mode for data transfer.<br>  - 0 = high speed (HS)<br>  - 1 = low power (LP)<br>- **bit 7**: Data pattern mode.<br>  - 0 = Use data pattern word<br>  - 1 = PRBS pattern.<br>- **bit 10:8**: multiple of finite random run (N): if bit 12 is finite, the finite run is 256 x (N+1) runs for HS PRBS and user data, or 16 x (N+1) for LP PRBS<br>- **bit 12**: Infinite run.<br>  - 0 = infinite<br>  - 1 = 256 x (N+1) runs of HS PRBS, 16 x (N+1) runs of LP PRBS, 256 x (N+1) runs of HS user data, or 8 runs of LP user data.<br>- **bit 14:13**: DSIBIST_DSIPHY_LANE_SWAP, select which lane is used as lane0 for LPDT:<br>  - 0 = DLN0<br>  - 1 = DLN1<br>  - 2 = DLN2<br>  - 3 = DLN3<br>- **bit 15**: Select instruction type.<br>  - 0 = command mode<br>  - 1 = DSI timing control mode.<br>- **bit 23:16**: data pattern byte (used when bit 7 is set to 0)<br>- *other bits*: reserved<br><br>**TIMING MODE** (bit 15 = 1)<br>- **bit 0**: DSI IOBIST ENABLE. Active high;<br>- **bit 5**: IOBIST start. Active high;<br>- **bit 15**: Select instruction type.<br>  - 0 = command mode<br>  - 1 = DSI timing control mode.<br>  *(If you write one DSI timing data with the select instruction type == 1, you have to change the select instruction type from 1 to 0 for timing data latch control.)*<br>- **bit 23:16**: DSI timing data;<br>- **bit 28:24**: DSI timing register selection:<br>  - 0x10 = DSI_T_CLK_PRE (data width[5:0])<br>  - 0x11 = DSI_T_CLK_POST (data width[5:0]) |

### MDSS_DSI_0_COMMAND_MODE_MDP_IDLE_CTRL

**Address:** `0x01A98194`
**Type:** RW
**Reset State:** `0x00000000`

**Idle insertion between Command MDP packets**

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 14:12 | EN | Enable idle insertion between Command Mode MDP packets:<br>0: disable<br>1: insert idle for stream0<br>2: insert idle for stream1<br>3: insertion idle for both streams |
| 9:0 | LENGTH | Number of dsiclk cycles of idle time to insert between Command Mode MDP packets. This idle counter is added in the application layer. To ensure the DSI link will go into stopstate between Command Mode MDP packets, the LENGTH must be long enough to cover the time the link takes to switch between High Speed mode to Low Power mode (LP11). |

### MDSS_DSI_0_COMMAND_MODE_MDP_CTRL2

**Address:** `0x01A981B8`
**Type:** RW
**Reset State:** `0x00000006`

**Command Mode MDP Control2**

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 16 | BURST_MODE | Enable frame transfer in one burst:<br>0: a frame can be transferred in multiple High Speed data bursts<br>1: enable frame transfer in one High Speed data burst if there is no gaps between lines from MDP |
<!-- page 3972 -->

### MDSS_DSI_0_COMMAND_MODE_MDP_CTRL2 (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 14:12 | INPUT_RGB_SWAP | Swaps the R, G, and B channels of the input command mode pixels from MDP. This field should be used when different R, G, and B orderings are required. |
| 10:8 | RGB_SWAP2 | Swaps the R, G, and B channels of the dst pixels. This field should be used when different R, G, and B orderings are required. For example, if RGB_SWAP = 1, RGB565 will become RBG556. |
| 7 | BYTE_MSB_LSB_FLIP2 | Swap the bit ordering of each byte of the dst pixel (this is done after the RGB swap and R/G/B_SEL).<br>0: bit 0 is lsb, bit 7 is msb<br>1: bit 0 is msb, bit 7 is lsb |
| 6 | B_SEL2 | Bit Swaps the B Channel of the dst pixel. This field is used to reverse the ordering of the bits that is outputted for the color red. For example, for RGB888 color format, if the red component is 10000000 then if this field is enabled, 00000001 is output. |
| 5 | G_SEL2 | Bit Swaps the G Channel of the dst pixel. This field is used to reverse the ordering of the bits that is outputted for the color red. For example, for RGB888 color format, if the red component is 10000000 then if this field is enabled, 00000001 is output. |
| 4 | R_SEL2 | Bit Swaps the R Channel of the dst pixel. This field is used to reverse the ordering of the bits that is outputted for the color red. For example, for RGB888 color format, if the red component is 10000000 then if this field is enabled, 00000001 is output. |
| 3:0 | DST_FORMAT2 | Pixel format for stream 2:<br>0 = RGB111<br>1 = reserved<br>2 = reserved<br>3 = RGB332 (data_src_width must be in multiple of 2 pixels)<br>4 = RGB444 (data_src_width must be in multiple of 2 pixels)<br>5 = reserved<br>6 = RGB565<br>7 = RGB666<br>8 = RGB888<br>others = reserved |

| 7 | HALT_REQ_C7 | HALT request and internal SW-reset for Client I/F 7 . |
| 6 | HALT_REQ_C6 | HALT request and internal SW-reset for Client I/F 6 . |
| 5 | HALT_REQ_C5 | HALT request and internal SW-reset for Client I/F 5 . |

### 0x07824000 SDC1_SDCC_MCI_POWER

**Type:** RW
**Clock:** same rate as HCLK
**Reset State:** 0x00000000

(ARM name: MCIPower). This register must be updated to the MCLK domain so subsequent writes to this register will be ignored until 3 MCLK and 3 HCLK have passed. SW should wait until bit 0 (MCLK_REG_WR_ACTIVE) of MCI_STATUS2 register is 0, after writing to MCI_POWER register and before accessing this register again.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 11 | DML_SW_RST_WAIT_IDLE_DIS | If this bit is set, then SW_RST_REQ procedure before BAM_TRANS_RESET is not executed automatically. |
| 10 | SW_RST_WAIT_IDLE_DIS | If this bit is set, then SW_RST_REQ procedure is not executed automatically. |
| 9 | SW_RST_REQ | Before executing SW_RST or SW_RST_CONFIG, this bit should be set and SW needs to polls on it until it's being cleared. The bit is cleared after AXI master has finished processing the outstanding transactions and it's in IDLE state. |
| 8 | SW_RST_CONFIG | SW reset bit for the core without resetting configuration registers (MCI_POWER, MCI_CLK, MCI_INT_MASKn). In that case, SW will be able to reset the internal state machines, data path, etc. and it will be able to proceed to next transaction without reconfiguring the SDCC registers. |
| 7 | SW_RST | SW reset bit for the core. The impact of this reset bit will be similar to the impact of the reset from SW register in CLK_CTRL bloCK. All SW registers and all internal logic is reset. |

### 0x0782400C SDC1_SDCC_MCI_CMD

**Type:** RW
**Clock:** same rate as HCLK
**Reset State:** 0x00000000

(ARM name: MMCCommand) CPSM: Command Path State Machine. This register must be updated to the MCLK domain so subsequent writes to this register will be ignored until 3 MCLK and 3 HCLK have passed. SW should wait until bit 0 (MCLK_REG_WR_ACTIVE) of MCI_STATUS2 register is 0, after writing to MCI_POWER register and before accessing this register again.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 17 | AUTO_CMD21 | If set (1), CPSM sends CMD21 automatically before sending CMD17 or CMD18. This sequence is needed for CDR auto-calibration of cm_dll_sdc4. CMD21 is supported in eMMC4.5 Spec. |


<!-- page 4071 -->
### SDC1_SDCC_MCI_CMD (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 16 | AUTO_CMD19 | If set (1), CPSM sends CMD19 automatically before sending CMD17 or CMD18. This sequence is needed for CDR auto-calibration of cm_dll_sdc4. CMD19 is supported in SD3.0 Spec. |
| 15 | CCS_DISABLE | If set (1), CPSM sends Command_Completion_Signal (CCS) disable sequence to the external CE-ATA device. |
| 14 | CCS_ENABLE | If set (1), CPSM waits for CCS from external card CE-ATA device. |
| 13 | MCIABORT | Signals the next command will be an abort (stop) command. This bit always read as (0) due to the hardware implementation. See a related note in next field |
| 12 | DAT_CMD | If set (1) indicates that this is a Command with Data. Note - MCIABORT and DAT_CMD bits don't have any effect on the CPSM. They are used to signal the SDIO Interrupt state machine that a Multi Block (examples: CMD18, CMD25, CMD53, etc. The rule is that each command with data must set this bit) data transaction is taking place. The DAT_CMD bit signals the start of the data transaction while the MCIABORT bit signals the end. For a pure SD Memory card, these bits are a "don't care" and should be set to zero by convention. However, some software drivers may chose to manipulate the bits in order to maintain compatibility with Combo cards and/or pure SDIO cards. |
| 11 | PROG_ENA | If set (1), PROG_DONE status bit will be asserted when busy is de-asserted. This bit is to be used with a stop or status command after a block write is performed. Does not effect CPSM. |
| 10 | ENABLE | The action of writing to this register (MCI_CMD) with this bit set (1), triggers CPSM to leave the Idle State. |
| 9 | PENDING | If set (1), CPSM waits for 'CmdPend' from the DPSM before it starts sending a command. This bit is designed to be used with SD CMD18 (READ_MULTIPLE_BLOCK) and SD CMD25 (WRITE_MULTIPLE_BLOCK) which must be terminated with a SD CMD12 (STOP_TRANSMISSION). After CMD18 or CMD25 is sent, the DPSM is enabled to send or receive data of amount MCI_DATA_LENGTH. After the DPSM finishes the transferring the data, it sends "CmdPend" to the CPSM and goes idle. When the CPSM receives this signal, it sends the currently loaded command which software would normally establish as CMD12. |
| 8 | INTERRUPT | If set (1), CPSM disables command timer and waits for interrupt request (Card Response). The START, CMD_INDEX, ARGUMENT, and CRC are a total of 48 bits in length. If the INTERRUPT bit is zero, the CPSM will wait (63-47) 16 MCLK ticks for a response before going back to IDLE. If the INTERRUPT bit is set, the CPSM will wait indefinitely for a card response. |
<!-- page 4072 -->

| 6 | RESPONSE | If set (1), CPSM waits for a response subject to INTERRUPT above. |
| 5:0 | CMD_INDEX | Command index. |

### SDC1_SDCC_MCI_STATUS
**Address:** 0x07824034
**Type:** R
**Clock:** same rate as HCLK
**Reset State:** 0x000C0000
*(ARM name: MCIStatus)*

This register may need exclusion for QCSR POR Test for bits 25 and 22.

**Static[30:26], [24:23] and [10:0]**
These remain asserted until they are cleared by writing to the appropriate bit in the Clear Register (see MCI_CLEAR).

**XCIS**
The means used to send the SDIO external-card-interrupt-signal (XCIS) to the SDCC depends on the transfer mode: 1-bit, 4-bit, or 8-bit. Under 1 bit transfer mode, the XCIS has a dedicated physical connection to the SDCC. Hence once it is asserted, it remain at a high level. Under 4 and 8 bit transfe modes, the XCIS is time multiplexed with physical connection data bit 1. The XCIS is recognized as valid during specific time slots on data bit 1 by the SDCC. How this 'recognition' takes places shows up as different behaviors on SDIO_INTR_OPER, SDIO_INTR, and the actual interrupt sent to the ARM through MCI_INT_MASKn.

**Special[25]**
The SDIO_INTR_OPER indicator reflects the true state of XCIS as it would be observed inside the external SDIO card. As such, there is no bit 25 in MCI_CLEAR. The only way to clear SDIO_INTR_OPER is to clear the appropriate bit in the external card Common Card Control Registers (CCCR). Like 'static' above and 'dynamic' below, bit 25 in MCI_INT_MASKn controls actually sending this indicator value to the ARM. This indicator of XCIS is used for normal SDCC operation.

**Special[22]**
The SDIO_INTR indicator reflects that there has been a low-to-high transition on the connection as explained under XCIS above. This indicator is cleared via bit 22 of MCI_CLEAR but any low-to-high transition on the connection will set this indicator again. Further note that this indicator is not routed through the MCI_INT_MASKn to the ARM. For bit 22, the raw value of the connection is routed through the MCI_INT_MASKn to the ARM. As this raw connection is not aware of
<!-- page 4076 -->
### SDC1_SDCC_MCI_STATUS (cont.)
*specific time slots, the signal sent to the ARM generally toggles in an unpredictable fashion. This is generally not useful during normal SDCC operation. However, for wake-up with clocks off, the raw connection is desirable.*

**Dynamic[21:11]**
These change state depending on the state of the underlying logic (for example, FIFO full and empty flags are asserted and de-asserted as data while written to the FIFO).

| 29 | BOOT_TIMEOUT | Data wasn't received within the valid time (according to MCI_CCS_TIMER) from the start of boot operation. |
| 28 | BOOT_ACK_ERR | Acknowledge pattern wasn't received correctly or not within the valid time (according to MCI_ACK_TIMER) from the start of boot operation. |

### SDC1_SDCC_MCI_FIFO_COUNT
**Address:** 0x07824044
**Type:** R
**Clock:** same rate as HCLK
**Reset State:** 0x00000000
*The SDCC core operates in two clock domains MCLK and HCLK. The CPSM and DPSM operate in MCLK domain and MciFifoDmaCtl (FIFO/DMA Controller) operates in HCLK domain. The MCI_FIFO_COUNT is a counter of FIFO Controller that monitors how many words of data are still needed to be transferred through the FIFO. At the beginning of data transaction the MCI_FIFO_COUNT counter will be loaded with the (MCI_DATA_LENGTH / 4) value and then will count down during the data transaction until it reach zero. This register is only useful for debug purposes and should not be used for normal operation since it does not reflect data which may or may not be in the pipeline.*

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 23:0 | DATA_COUNT | Remaining data. |
<!-- page 4080 -->

| 3 | EARLY_ASSERT_CMD_LINE | If set to '1' then the CMD line is asserted by HW when all the data was received on the SD bus. (Orig name: EARLY_ASSERT_CMD_LINE and E) |
| 2 | BOOT_ACK_EN | If set to '1' then Host waits for acknowledge pattern after initiating the boot operation. |
| 1 | BOOT_EN | When this bit is asserted, the boot operation is initiated in both of the modes. |
| 0 | BOOT_MODE | If set to '1' then CMD line is low during the boot operation. If boot_mode = '0', then CMD0 with the argument 0xFFFFFFFA is sent. |

### SDC1_SDCC_MCI_EMULATION_DLY_LINE
**Address:** 0x07824054
**Type:** RW
**Clock:** same rate as HCLK
**Reset State:** 0x00000000
*The register is responsible for handling DCM which is used in emulation supports 256 values of shift intervals so 8 bits are required (0:255). Bits [31:30] are used for emulation purposes only.*

*The procedure for activating the DCM is:*


<!-- page 4081 -->
1. Setting bit 28 - DCM_RESET.
2. Clearing bit 28 - DCM_RESET.
3. Waiting until bit 29 DCM_LOCKED is high.
4. Writing a new phase in SD_CLK_DLY_CTRL field and setting the DCM_START bit (bit 30).

The clock's placement was executed by the DCM when DCM_DONE is asserted.

### SDC1_SDCC_MCI_EMULATION_DLY_LINE (Continuation)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31 | DCM_DONE | The shift process was finished in DCM and CMD19 can be sent towards the card. This is a read-only bit. |
| 30 | DCM_START | A new value of SD_CLK_DLY_CTRL is ready. Clears the DCM_DONE bit. |
| 29 | DCM_LOCKED | Reading the status of the LOCKED DCM's output which indicates that the output clock is ready for use. |
| 28 | DCM_RESET | Driving reset to DCM. |
| 7:0 | SD_CLK_DLY_CTRL | Input to DCM block in FPGA (8 bits). Controlling the change of the delay interval. The value's range may be 0-255 in DCM block. |

## SDC1_SDCC_MCI_FIFOn (0x07824080 + 0x4 * n, n=[0..15])

### Bitfields
| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:0 | DATA | FIFO data. This register is aliased to 16 words, 0x080 - 0xBC. In SDCC3, an access to the FIFO was executed with 16 words so 16 addresses were defined. However, in SDCC5 only 8 words are used in each burst so only 8 addresses from the range should be used.<br>When writing to the external SD_Card, writes to the data path FIFO.<br>When reading from the external SD_Card, reads from the data path FIFO. |

## SDC1_SDCC_MCI_PWRCTL_STATUS_REG (0x078240DC)

- **Type**: R
- **Clock**: PCLK
- **Reset State**: `0x00000000`
<!-- page 4090 -->
### SDC1_SDCC_MCI_PWRCTL_STATUS_REG (Continuation)

HC Spec Defines power and IO voltage switch bits. The information is sent by a dedicated interrupt to the QCT SW driver for handling the power and voltage tasks with PMIC. The different tasks are defined in this register

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 3 | IO_HIGH_V | SDCC driver orders that the I/O signaling level be switched to 3.0v. This interrupt is triggered when SDCC driver writes '0' to offset 03Eh in HC register (bit 3) or when SW reset for all is handled and last supported voltage was 1.8V. This logic is enabled when SWITCHABLE_SIGNALING_VOLTAGE=true |
| 2 | IO_LOW_V | SDCC driver orders that the I/O signaling level be switched to 1.8v. This interrupt is triggered when SDCC driver writes '1' to offset 03Eh in HC register (bit 3). This logic is enabled when SWITCHABLE_SIGNALING_VOLTAGE=true |
| 1 | BUS_ON | SDCC driver orders that the SD bus power be switched on. This interrupt is triggered when SDCC driver writes '1' to offset 029h in HC register (bit 0). |
| 0 | BUS_OFF | SDCC driver orders that the SD bus power be switched off. This interrupt is triggered when SDCC driver writes '0' to offset 029h in HC register(bit 0) or when SW reset for all is handled. |
