### 0x078240E8 SDC1_SDCC_MCI_PWRCTL_CTL_REG

**Type:** RW
**Clock:** PCLK
**Reset State:** 0x00000000

HC Spec Defines power and IO voltage switch bits. The information is sent by a dedicated interrupt to the QCT SW driver for handling the power and voltage tasks with PMIC and then the QCT SW driver needs to report success or fail to this register.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 9 | HC_CARD_STATE_STABLE | This bit is driving CARD_STATE_STABLE bit in Present State Register |
| 8 | RST_NOT_WAIT_PWRCTL_REG | RST process doesn't need to wait for accessing to MCI_PWRCTL_CTL_REG register |
| 7:6 | HC_WRITE_PROTECT_PAD | Value 0 inversion of HC_WRITE_PROTECT is connected to bit 19 in Present State Register.<br>Value 1 input from PAD is used.<br>Value 2 inversion of input from PAD is used |
| 5 | CARD_DETECT_PIN_LEVEL | This bit reflects the inverse value of the SDCD# pin. Debouncing is not performed on this bit. This bit may be valid when Card State Stable is set to 1, but it is not guaranteed because of propagation delay. Use of this bit is limited to testing since it must be debounced by software.<br>value 1: card present<br>value 0: no card present |
| 4 | HC_WRITE_PROTECT | This bit allows to disable the writing.<br>value 0: write enabled<br>value 1: write protected |
| 3 | IO_SIG_SWITCH_FAIL | Host controller clears this bit when it fires either I/O Low V interrupt or I/O High V interrupt. SDCC power control software writes '1' to indicate the signal switch has failed. |
<!-- page 4092 -->
### SDC1_SDCC_MCI_PWRCTL_CTL_REG (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 2 | IO_SIG_SWITCH_SUCCESS | Host controller clears this bit when it fires either I/O Low V interrupt or I/O High V interrupt. SDCC power control software writes '1' to indicate the signal switch has completed successfully. |
| 1 | BUS_ON_OFF_FAIL | Host controller clears this bit when it fires either Bus ON interrupt or Bus OFF interrupt. SDCC power control software writes '1' to indicate the requested operation has failed. |
| 0 | BUS_ON_OFF_SUCCESS | Host controller clears this bit when it fires either Bus ON interrupt or Bus OFF interrupt. SDCC power control software writes '1' to indicate the requested operation has completed successfully. |

### 0x07824140 SDC1_SDCC_CSR_CDC_CTLR_CFG0

**Type:** RW
**Clock:** HCLK
**Reset State:** 0x00000000

The CSR_CDC_CTLR_CFG0 register configures the following:

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 25 | STAGGER_CAL_ENA | 1'b1: Stagger calibration of write and read CDCs once after the other to reduce peak voltage drop.<br>1'b0: Both write and read CDCs calibrated simultaneously<br>This bit is introduced on the x2 core, so not present on x0 and x1 versions of DIM/PHY. |
| 24 | TRACKING_CAL_ENA | 1'b1: Relationship between subunits and oscillator count is learnt and used for tracking calibration.<br>1'b0: Periodic calibration triggers cause full recalibration |
<!-- page 4098 -->
### SDC1_SDCC_CSR_CDC_CTLR_CFG0 (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 23:20 | OSC_COUNT_ERR_TOLERANCE | Magnitude of the difference between oscillator count and target count when the algorithm assumes convergence and stops further search. |
| 19 | TRACK_CALIB_MODE | 1'b0: Tracking calibration uses previous Target_count value.<br>1'b1 Accurate mode: Target_count is recomputed at the start of tracking calibration |
| 18 | FULL_DELAY | 1'b0: unitstep and subunit caps are from calibration or SW settings<br>1'b1: All unit step and subunit caps are selected for the delay arrays. |
| 17 | HW_AUTOCAL_ENA | 1'b1: Enables periodic auto calibration<br>1'b0: Periodic calibration is disabled |
| 16 | SW_TRIG_FULL_CALIB | A low to high transition on this register bit triggers the CDC calibration statemachine to initiate full calibration of the standby delay array. Also resets tracking mode for the delay arrays. |
| 13:12 | OSC_PRE_DIV | The factor by which the raw oscillator frequency is divided before being given to the counting logic.<br>2'b00 Divide by 1<br>2'b01 Divide by 2<br>2'b10 Divide by 4<br>2'b11 Divide by 8 |
| 10:0 | TMUX_CHAR | Cchar is a characterized constant equal to the ratio of output mux offset delay to average unit step delay. This register is programmed by multiplying the constant with 1024 and rounding to the nearest integer. E.g. if Cchar = 0.67, RO(0.67 * 1024) = 686, hence program TMUX_CHAR = 11'h2AE |

Configuration bits for e.MMC5.0 DDR200 mode

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |

### SDC1_SDCC_DDR200_CFG (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 8:7 | CDC_TRAFFIC_SEL | Selecting the method of cdc_traffic's assertions: Value 0 (default) - auto calibration with stand by feature. Value 1 - SW calibration before any transaction. Value 2 - automatic calibration with HW assertion of cdc_traffic. |
| 6 | START_CDC_TRAFFIC | This bit starts the cdc traffic assertion after calibration done is received. |
| 5 | CRC_TOKEN_SAMPL_FALL_EDGE | If set, the start bit of incoming CRC token in DDR200 mode is sampled in falling edge. If this bit is cleared (default) then the start bit is detected in rising edge |
| 4 | DATIN_SAMPL_FALL_EDGE | If set, the start bit of incoming data in DDR200 mode is sampled in falling edge. If this bit is cleared (default) then the start bit is detected in rising edge |
| 3 | CDC_T4_TEST_OUT_SEL | controls the mux between dll test_out and CDC test out. Default value is 0 (dll is chosen). When set - CDC test_out is chosen. |
| 2 | CMDIN_EDGE_SEL | Select sampling edge of CMD input when CMDIN_RCLK_EN is 1: 0 (default) - falling edge of RCLK, 1 - rising edge of RCLK |
| 1 | CMDIN_RCLK_EN | Enable CMD input sampling with RCLK: 0 (default) - CMD input is sampled by SD DLL output clock, 1 - CMD input is sampled by delayed RCLK |
| 0 | CDC_T4_DLY_SEL | Select block for RCLK delay: 0 (default) - use CM_DLL_SDC4 |

### 0x07824400+0x4*n SDC1_SDCC_MCI_FIFO_ALTn, n=[0..255]
* **Type:** RW
* **Clock:** same rate as HCLK
* **Reset State:** 0x00000000

Alternative register to MCI_FIFO (0x80-0xBC). The SW can use this register range (0x400-0x7FC) for accessing all the RAM range (1024 bytes) in FIFO mode. The advantage is that any byte in the RAM can be accessed without repeating the same address

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:0 | DATA | WORD is written or received to/from the RAM in FIFO mode |

### 0x07824A00 SDC1_SDCC_HC_REG_DLL_CONFIG

* **Type**: RW
* **Clock**: same rate as HCLK
* **Reset State**: 0x60006400

This register configures the DLL's inputs.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31 | SDC4_DIS_DOUT | When this bit equals to '0', the data which comes out from the dll is valid. When it equals to '1' this data isn't valid. The inversion of this bit is connected to dll's input - dll_en_dout |
| 30 | DLL_RST | Setting this bit to 1 resets cm_dll_sdc4. cm_dll_sdc4 should be reset every time the MCLK frequency is changed. |
| 29 | PDN | Power Down<br>Value 0 - analog blocks are enabled<br>Value 1 - analog blocks are powered down (default) |
| 28 | CK_INTP_SEL | Selects interpolator output |
| 27 | CK_INTP_EN | Enable clock interpolation for finer resolution |
| 26:24 | MCLK_FREQ | Frequency of MCLK<br>Value 000 - 100 - 112 (MHz)<br>Value 001 - 112 - 125<br>Value 010 - 125 - 137<br>Value 011 - 137 - 150<br>Value 100 - 150 - 162<br>Value 101 - 162 - 175<br>Value 110 - 175 - 187<br>Value 111 - 187 - 200 |
<!-- page 4134 -->

### 0x07824A00 SDC1_SDCC_HC_REG_DLL_CONFIG (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 23:20 | CDR_SELEXT | CDR phase select (gray coded)<br>Value 0000 - phase 0<br>Value 0001 - phase 1<br>Value 0011 - phase 2<br>Value 0010 - phase 3<br>Value 0110 - phase 4<br>Value 0111 - phase 5<br>Value 0101 - phase 6<br>Value 0100 - phase 7<br>Value 1100 - phase 8<br>Value 1101 - phase 9<br>Value 1111 - phase 10<br>Value 1110 - phase 11<br>Value 1010 - phase 12<br>Value 1011 - phase 13<br>Value 1001 - phase 14<br>Value 1000 - phase 15 |
| 19 | CDR_EXT_EN | Enable external control of cdr phase select |
| 18 | CK_OUT_EN | Enable output clock (default value is '1') |
| 17 | CDR_EN | Enable CDR function |
| 16 | DLL_EN | Enable DLL function |
| 15:14 | CDR_UPD_RATE | CDR update rate, low pass filtering window of CDR<br>Max update rate:<br>Value 00 - 0.5 MCLK frequency<br>Value 01 - 0.25 MCLK Frequency (default)<br>Value 10 - 0.125 MCLK frequency<br>Value 11 - 1/16 MCLK Frequency |
| 13:12 | DLL_UPD_RATE | DLL update rate<br>Value 00 - sdc4_mclk/10<br>Value 01 - sdc4_mclk/20<br>Value 10 - sdc4_mclk/40 (default)<br>Value 11 - sdc4_mclk/80 |
| 11:10 | DLL_PHASE_DET | DLL phase detector low pass average window<br>Value 00 - 2 cycles<br>Value 01 - 4 cycles (default)<br>Value 10 - 8 cycles<br>Value 11 - 16 cycles |
| 9 | CDR_ALGORITHM_SEL | CDR algorithm select<br>Value 0 - Edge (default)<br>Value 1 - Level |

* **Type**: RW

| Bits | Name | Description |

| 31:22 | HC_AUTO_CMD_COUNTER | This counter will determine the time between two auto commands transmissions |
| 21:19 | HC_SELECT_IN | Selecting the SD controller's mode. Equivalent to SELECT_IN field in MCI_CLK |

### 0x07824A0C SDC1_SDCC_HC_VENDOR_SPECIFIC_FUNC (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 13 | HC_SW_SDC4_CMD19 | The input of cm_dll_sdc4 - sdc4_cmd19 can be driven by SW if AUTO_CMD19 (bit 16 in MCI_CMD) feature is not used.<br>Value 1 - sdc4_cmd19 is driven by SW<br>Value 0 (default) - sdc4_cmd19 is driven by HW |
| 12 | HC_INVERT_OUT | value: 0 data and cmd are driven by falling edge<br>value 1: data and cmd are driven by rising edge. |
| 11 | HC_INVERT_OUT_EN | value 1: HC_INVERT_OUT is driven by bit 12 of HC_VENDOR_SPECIFIC_FUNC (HC_INVERT_OUT)<br>value 0: HC_INVERT_OUT is driven by HST_CTL1_HS_EN . |

Desired delay cannot be realized even when all unit-steps are selected.<br>3'b100: Unit-step underflow<br>3'b101: Unit-step overflow: Overflow during coarse calibration. ### SDC1_SDCC_HC_VENDOR_SPECIFIC_PWRCTL_STATUS_REG

**Address:** `0x07824AA0`

HC Spec Defines power and IO voltage switch bits. The information is sent by a dedicated interrupt to the QCT SW driver for handling the power and voltage tasks with PMIC. The different tasks are defined in this register

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 3 | IO_HIGH_V | SDCC driver orders that the I/O signaling level be switched to 3.0v. This interrupt is triggered when SDCC driver writes '0' to offset 03Eh in HC register (bit 3) or when SW reset for all is handled and last supported voltage was 1.8V. This logic is enabled when SWITCHABLE_SIGNALING_VOLTAGE=true |

| 1 | BUS_ON | SDCC driver orders that the SD bus power be switched on. This interrupt is triggered when SDCC driver writes '1' to offset 029h in HC register (bit 0). |
| 0 | BUS_OFF | SDCC driver orders that the SD bus power be switched off. This interrupt is triggered when SDCC driver writes '0' to offset 029h in HC register(bit 0) or when SW reset for all is handled. |

### SDC1_SDCC_HC_VENDOR_SPECIFIC_PWRCTL_CTL_REG

**Address:** `0x07824AAC`  
**Type:** RW  
**Clock:** PCLK  
**Reset State:** `0x00000000`  

HC Spec Defines power and IO voltage switch bits. The information is sent by a dedicated interrupt to the QCT SW driver for handling the power and voltage tasks with PMIC and then the QCT SW driver needs to report success or fail to this register

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 9 | HC_CARD_STATE_STABLE | This bit is driving CARD_STATE_STABLE bit in Present State Register |
| 8 | RST_NOT_WAIT_PWRCTL_REG | RST process doesn't need to wait for accessing to MCI_PWRCTL_CTL_REG register |
| 7:6 | HC_WRITE_PROTECT_PAD | Value 0: inversion of HC_WRITE_PROTECT is connected to bit 19 in Present State Register.<br>Value 1: input from PAD is used.<br>Value 2: inversion of input from PAD is used |
| 5 | CARD_DETECT_PIN_LEVEL | This bit reflects the inverse value of the SDCD# pin. Debouncing is not performed on this bit. This bit may be valid when Card State Stable is set to 1, but it is not guaranteed because of propagation delay. Use of this bit is limited to testing since it must be debounced by software.<br>value 1: card present<br>value 0: no card present |
| 4 | HC_WRITE_PROTECT | This bit allows to disable the writing.<br>value 0: write enabled<br>value 1: write protected |
| 3 | IO_SIG_SWITCH_FAIL | Host controller clears this bit when it fires either I/O Low V interrupt or I/O High V interrupt. SDCC power control software writes '1' to indicate the signal switch has failed. |
| 2 | IO_SIG_SWITCH_SUCCESS | Host controller clears this bit when it fires either I/O Low V interrupt or I/O High V interrupt. SDCC power control software writes '1' to indicate the signal switch has completed successfully. |
| 1 | BUS_ON_OFF_FAIL | Host controller clears this bit when it fires either Bus ON interrupt or Bus OFF interrupt. SDCC power control software writes '1' to indicate the requested operation has failed. |
<!-- page 4160 -->
### SDC1_SDCC_HC_VENDOR_SPECIFIC_PWRCTL_CTL_REG (continued)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 0 | BUS_ON_OFF_SUCCESS | Host controller clears this bit when it fires either Bus ON interrupt or Bus OFF interrupt. SDCC power control software writes '1' to indicate the requested operation has completed successfully. |

# 19 SDC2

## 19.1 SDC2_SDCC_SDCC5

### 0x07864000 SDC2_SDCC_MCI_POWER

**Type:** RW  
**Clock:** same rate as HCLK  
**Reset State:** 0x00000000  

(ARM name: MCIPower). This register must be updated to the MCLK domain so subsequent writes to this register will be ignored until 3 MCLK and 3 HCLK have passed. SW should wait until bit 0 (MCLK_REG_WR_ACTIVE) of MCI_STATUS2 register is 0, after writing to MCI_POWER register and before accessing this register again.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---------- |
| 11 | DML_SW_RST_WAIT_IDLE_DIS | If this bit is set, then SW_RST_REQ procedure before BAM_TRANS_RESET is not executed automatically. |
| 10 | SW_RST_WAIT_IDLE_DIS | If this bit is set, then SW_RST_REQ procedure is not executed automatically. |
| 9 | SW_RST_REQ | Before executing SW_RST or SW_RST_CONFIG, this bit should be set and SW needs to polls on it until it's being cleared. The bit is cleared after AXI master has finished processing the outstanding transactions and it's in IDLE state. |
| 8 | SW_RST_CONFIG | SW reset bit for the core without resetting configuration registers (MCI_POWER, MCI_CLK, MCI_INT_MASKn). In that case, SW will be able to reset the internal state machines, data path, etc. and it will be able to proceed to next transaction without reconfiguring the SDCC registers. |
| 7 | SW_RST | SW reset bit for the core. The impact of this reset bit will be similar to the impact of the reset from SW register in CLK_CTRL bloCK. All SW registers and all internal logic is reset. |
<!-- page 4163 -->

### SDC2_SDCC_MCI_POWER (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---------- |
| 6 | OPEN_DRAIN | MCICMD Output Control. This bit is reserved for the use mentioned in the Description but it is not tested. The open drain mode is preserved such that when enabled, the command output is driven low when the logic is low and undriven (so that the pull up can pull high) when the logic is high. Whether this gets used in the system is up to SW/system but the HW does support this mode. |
| 0 | CONTROL | This register is used to control the operation of the memory controller. <br>value 0: power-off<br>value 1: power-on |

### 0x07864004 SDC2_SDCC_MCI_CLK

**Type:** RW  
**Clock:** same rate as HCLK  
**Reset State:** 0x01008000  

(ARM name: MCIClock). This register must be updated to the MCLK domain so subsequent writes to this register will be ignored until 3 MCLK and 3 HCLK have passed. SW should wait until bit 0 (MCLK_REG_WR_ACTIVE) of MCI_STATUS2 register is 0, after writing to MCI_POWER register and before accessing this register again.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---------- |
| 31 | PWRSAVE_DLL | When this bit is set, DLL will get clock during transactions but not in idle. When this bit is cleared, DLL will get clock all the time so sdc4_dll_lock won't be de-asserted |
| 30 | SDIO_TRANS | When this bit is set in SDIO transaction, START_BIT_ERR status bit won't be raised. The reason is that interrupt period which is de-asserted only after the RX command can cause to wrong START_BIT_ERR detection. The START_BIT_ERR bit won't appear in MCI_STATUS when SDIO_TRANS is set |
| 29 | HCLK_IDLE_GATING | Additional CGC for HCLK was added, which gates the HCLK for status bits. If this bit is set then HCLK is gated for these registers during IDLE |
| 28 | MCLK_IDLE_GATING | Additional CGC for MCLK was added, which gates the MCLK for status bits. If this bit is set then MCLK is gated for these registers during IDLE |
| 27 | INT_MCLK_ON | An internal CGC is located in MCLK domain. SW can enable the internal clock at IDLE time by writing '1' to this bit. If the bit is cleared, then the clock is gated at IDLE time |
<!-- page 4164 -->

### SDC2_SDCC_MCI_CLK (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---------- |
| 26 | SDCC_CLK_EXT_EN | Value 0 (default) - sdcc_clkout is driven via the clock pad and external clock can't be used for testing the cm_dll_sdc4.<br>Value 1- External clock can be used as a test clock. |
| 25 | RX_FLOW_TIMING | Configuration bit which selects the cycle which RxFlowControl will be asserted when UHS mode is used<br>Value 0 (default) - RxFlowControl is asserted one clock before the end bit is received in DPSM (NextBlkTCnt in DPSM equals to 1).<br>Value 1 - RxFlowControl is asserted two clocks before the end bit is received in DPSM (NextBlkTCnt in DPSM equals to 2). |
| 24:23 | SDC4_MCLK_SEL | Selects the sdc4_mclk - input clock of cm_dll_sdc4<br>Value 1 - feedback clock from CLK pad<br>Value 2 (default) - free running MCLK (gated between the transactions)<br>Value 3 - free running MCLK divided by 2 |
| 22 | CLK_INV | When set(1), the input clock which is inserted into the input macros is inverted. |
| 21 | IO_PAD_PWR_SWITCH | Indication to Pad that power has to be switched from 3.3V to 1.8V. |
| 20 | CLK_FB_DLY_SEL | Selects the source of feedback clock used by the controller.<br>Value 1 - output of cm_dll_sdc4 is used as feedback clock<br>Value 0 - feedback clock from CLK pad is used |
| 19:18 | SD_DEV_SEL | Select the active device if more than one device are connected in shared bus mode. (range: '00' - '11'). |
| 17 | HCLKON_SW_EN | SW enable of AHB clock request of SDCC5.<br>value 0: HW clock request mechanism is used<br>value 1: clock request signal is always high |
| 16:14 | SELECT_IN | Select to latch data and command coming in:<br>value 000: on the falling edge of internal MCLK.<br>value 001: on the rising edge of internal MCLK.<br>value 010: using feedback clock (default).<br>value 011: DDR mode.<br>value 100: UHS mode - MCLK is used internally.<br>value 101: UHS mode - divided frequency (MCLK/2) is used internally.<br>value 110: e.MMC5.0 DDR200 mode. |
| 13 | INVERT_OUT | Clear (0) to change data and command going out on the falling edge.<br>Set (1) to change data and command going out on the rising edge. |
| 12 | FLOW_ENA | Enable flow control:<br>value 0: disable (default)<br>value 1: enable |
<!-- page 4165 -->

### SDC2_SDCC_MCI_CLK (cont.)

### 0x0786400C SDC2_SDCC_MCI_CMD

**Type:** RW  
**Clock:** same rate as HCLK  
**Reset State:** 0x00000000  

(ARM name: MMCCommand) CPSM: Command Path State Machine. This register must be updated to the MCLK domain so subsequent writes to this register will be ignored until 3 MCLK and 3 HCLK have passed. SW should wait until bit 0 (MCLK_REG_WR_ACTIVE) of MCI_STATUS2 register is 0, after writing to MCI_POWER register and before accessing this register again.
<!-- page 4166 -->

### SDC2_SDCC_MCI_CMD (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---------- |
| 17 | AUTO_CMD21 | If set (1), CPSM sends CMD21 automatically before sending CMD17 or CMD18. This sequence is needed for CDR auto-calibration of cm_dll_sdc4. CMD21 is supported in eMMC4.5 Spec. |
| 16 | AUTO_CMD19 | If set (1), CPSM sends CMD19 automatically before sending CMD17 or CMD18. This sequence is needed for CDR auto-calibration of cm_dll_sdc4. CMD19 is supported in SD3.0 Spec. |
| 15 | CCS_DISABLE | If set (1), CPSM sends Command_Completion_Signal (CCS) disable sequence to the external CE-ATA device. |
| 14 | CCS_ENABLE | If set (1), CPSM waits for CCS from external card CE-ATA device. |
| 13 | MCIABORT | Signals the next command will be an abort (stop) command. This bit always read as (0) due to the hardware implementation. See a related note in next field |
| 12 | DAT_CMD | If set (1) indicates that this is a Command with Data. Note - MCIABORT and DAT_CMD bits don't have any effect on the CPSM. They are used to signal the SDIO Interrupt state machine that a Multi Block (examples: CMD18, CMD25, CMD53, etc. The rule is that each command with data must set this bit) data transaction is taking place. The DAT_CMD bit signals the start of the data transaction while the MCIABORT bit signals the end. For a pure SD Memory card, these bits are a "don't care" and should be set to zero by convention. However, some software drivers may chose to manipulate the bits in order to maintain compatibility with Combo cards and/or pure SDIO cards. |
| 11 | PROG_ENA | If set (1), PROG_DONE status bit will be asserted when busy is de-asserted. This bit is to be used with a stop or status command after a block write is performed. Does not effect CPSM. |
| 10 | ENABLE | The action of writing to this register (MCI_CMD) with this bit set (1), triggers CPSM to leave the Idle State. |
| 9 | PENDING | If set (1), CPSM waits for 'CmdPend' from the DPSM before it starts sending a command. This bit is designed to be used with SD CMD18 (READ_MULTIPLE_BLOCK) and SD CMD25 (WRITE_MULTIPLE_BLOCK) which must be terminated with a SD CMD12 (STOP_TRANSMISSION).<br>After CMD18 or CMD25 is sent, the DPSM is enabled to send or receive data of amount MCI_DATA_LENGTH. After the DPSM finishes the transferring the data, it sends "CmdPend" to the CPSM and goes idle. When the CPSM receives this signal, it sends the currently loaded command which software would normally establish as CMD12. |
<!-- page 4167 -->

If the INTERRUPT bit is zero, the CPSM will wait (63-47) 16 MCLK ticks for a response before going back to IDLE. If the INTERRUPT bit is set, the CPSM will wait indefinitely for a card response. |
| 7 | LONGRSP | If set (1), receives a 136-bit long response. |
| 6 | RESPONSE | If set (1), CPSM waits for a response subject to INTERRUPT above. |

### 0x07864034 SDC2_SDCC_MCI_STATUS

**Type:** R  
**Clock:** same rate as HCLK  
**Reset State:** 0x000C0000  

(ARM name: MCIStatus)  

This register may need exclusion for QCSR POR Test for bits 25 and 22.  
Static[30:26], [24:23] and [10:0]  
These remain asserted until they are cleared by writing to the appropriate bit in the Clear Register (see MCI_CLEAR)  

**XCIS**  
The means used to send the SDIO external-card-interrupt-signal (XCIS) to the SDCC depends on the transfer mode: 1-bit, 4-bit, or 8-bit. Under 1 bit transfer mode, the XCIS has a dedicated physical connection to the SDCC. Hence once it is asserted, it remain at a high level. Under 4 and 8 bit transfe modes, the XCIS is time multiplexed with physical connection data bit 1. The XCIS is recognized as valid during specific time slots on data bit 1 by the SDCC. How this 'recognition' takes places shows up as different behaviors on SDIO_INTR_OPER, SDIO_INTR, and the actual interrupt sent to the ARM through MCI_INT_MASKn.

**Special[25]**  
The SDIO_INTR_OPER indicator reflects the true state of XCIS as it would be observed inside the external SDIO card. As such, there is no bit 25 in MCI_CLEAR. The only way to clear SDIO_INTR_OPER is to clear the appropriate bit in the external card Common Card Control Registers (CCCR). Like 'static' above and 'dynamic' below, bit 25 in MCI_INT_MASKn controls


<!-- page 4171 -->
                   actually sending this indicator value to the ARM. This indicator of XCIS is used for normal SDCC
                   operation.

                   Special[22]

                   The SDIO_INTR indicator reflects that there has been a low-to-high transition on the connection
                   as explained under XCIS above. This indicator is cleared via bit 22 of MCI_CLEAR but any low-
                   to-high transition on the connection will set this indicator again. Further note that this indicator is
                   not routed through the MCI_INT_MASKn to the ARM. For bit 22, the raw value of the connection
                   is routed through the MCI_INT_MASKn to the ARM. As this raw connection is not aware of
                   specific time slots, the signal sent to the ARM generally toggles in an unpredictable fashion. This
                   is generally not useful during normal SDCC operation. However, for wake-up with clocks off, the
                   raw connection is desirable.

                   Dynamic[21:11]

                   These change state depending on the state of the underlying logic (for example, FIFO full and
                   empty flags are asserted and de-asserted as data while written to the FIFO).

### SDC2_SDCC_MCI_FIFO_COUNT

**Address:** `0x07864044`
**Type:** `R`
**Clock:** `same rate as HCLK`
**Reset State:** `0x00000000`

The SDCC core operates in two clock domains MCLK and HCLK. The CPSM and DPSM operate in MCLK domain and MciFifoDmaCtl (FIFO/DMA Controller) operates in HCLK domain. The MCI_FIFO_COUNT is a counter of FIFO Controller that monitors how many words of data are still needed to be transferred through the FIFO. At the beginning of data transaction the MCI_FIFO_COUNT counter will be loaded with the (MCI_DATA_LENGTH / 4) value and then
<!-- page 4175 -->
will count down during the data transaction until it reach zero. This register is only useful for debug purposes and should not be used for normal operation since it does not reflect data which may or may not be in the pipeline.

### SDC2_SDCC_MCI_EMULATION_DLY_LINE

**Address:** `0x07864054`
**Type:** `RW`
**Clock:** `same rate as HCLK`
**Reset State:** `0x00000000`

The register is responsible for handling DCM which is used in emulation supports 256 values of shift intervals so 8 bits are required (0:255). Bits [31:30] are used for emulation purposes only.

The procedure for activating the DCM is:

1. Setting bit 28 - DCM_RESET.
2. Clearing bit 28 - DCM_RESET.
3. Waiting until bit 29 DCM_LOCKED is high.
4. Writing a new phase in SD_CLK_DLY_CTRL field and setting the DCM_START bit (bit 30).

The clock's placement was executed by the DCM when DCM_DONE is asserted.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31 | DCM_DONE | The shift process was finished in DCM and CMD19 can be sent towards the card. This is a read-only bit. |
| 30 | DCM_START | A new value of SD_CLK_DLY_CTRL is ready. Clears the DCM_DONE bit. |
| 29 | DCM_LOCKED | Reading the status of the LOCKED DCM's output which indicates that the output clock is ready for use. |
| 28 | DCM_RESET | Driving reset to DCM. |
| 7:0 | SD_CLK_DLY_CTRL | Input to DCM block in FPGA (8 bits). Controlling the change of the delay interval. The value's range may be 0-255 in DCM block. |

| Bits | Name | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 21 | PROGDONE_WO_CMD_RESP | RW | '0' (Default): we wait for cmd response end to detect progdone (legacy behavior). '1': we start looking for progdone without waiting for cmd response end but after 10 cycles from end bit of command |

| 13 | FF_CLK_SW_RST_DIS | RW | Disabling the SW reset in FF clock domain |
| 12 | IO_MACRO_SW_RST_PERIOD | R | When moving to DDR mode, reset period is generated for dividers. There is possibility to read from this bit if this period was finished |
| 11 | CLOCK_AFTER_EOB_DIS | RW | Disabling the 8 cycles after the CRC token when TxFlowControl is asserted before the end of the block |
| 10 | ADMA_INT_DATA | RW | If this bit is set, then the ADMA interrupt is set when the data was already transferred. If this bit is cleared, then the ADMA interrupt is set when the requests related to the descriptors were finished on address channel before the data itself is processed |
| 9 | BAM_CLK_EN_ACT | RW | If this bit is set, then bam_clk is gated when hc mode is enabled |
| 8 | ADMA_HPROT_DIS | R | If cleared then HPROT is changed in last burst of write transaction if block_count_en is 1, otherwise it will be for each end of descriptor. Not applicable for Gandalf - AXI Noc |
| 7 | ADMA_NON_WRD_ALIGN_DIS | R | If set the fix for non word aligned transfers in ADMA is disabled. Not applicable for Gandalf - AXI Noc |

**Type:** RW
**Clock:** same rate as HCLK
**Reset State:** 0x00000000

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:0 | DATA | FIFO data. This register is aliased to 16 words, 0x080 - 0xBC. In SDCC3, an access to the FIFO was executed with 16 words so 16 addresses were defined. However, in SDCC5 only 8 words are used in each burst so only 8 addresses from the range should be used. <br>When writing to the external SD_Card, writes to the data path FIFO.<br>When reading from the external SD_Card, reads from the data path FIFO. |

### 0x078640DC SDC2_SDCC_MCI_PWRCTL_STATUS_REG

**Type:** R
**Clock:** PCLK
**Reset State:** 0x00000000

HC Spec Defines power and IO voltage switch bits. The information is sent by a dedicated interrupt to the QCT SW driver for handling the power and voltage tasks with PMIC. The different tasks are defined in this register

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 3 | IO_HIGH_V | SDCC driver orders that the I/O signaling level be switched to 3.0v. This interrupt is triggered when SDCC driver writes '0' to offset 03Eh in HC register (bit 3) or when SW reset for all is handled and last supported voltage was 1.8V. This logic is enabled when SWITCHABLE_SIGNALING_VOLTAGE=true |
| 2 | IO_LOW_V | SDCC driver orders that the I/O signaling level be switched to 1.8v. This interrupt is triggered when SDCC driver writes '1' to offset 03Eh in HC register (bit 3). This logic is enabled when SWITCHABLE_SIGNALING_VOLTAGE=true |
| 1 | BUS_ON | SDCC driver orders that the SD bus power be switched on. This interrupt is triggered when SDCC driver writes '1' to offset 029h in HC register (bit 0). |
| 0 | BUS_OFF | SDCC driver orders that the SD bus power be switched off. This interrupt is triggered when SDCC driver writes '0' to offset 029h in HC register(bit 0) or when SW reset for all is handled. |

### 0x078640E8 SDC2_SDCC_MCI_PWRCTL_CTL_REG

**Type:** RW
**Clock:** PCLK
**Reset State:** 0x00000000

HC Spec Defines power and IO voltage switch bits. The information is sent by a dedicated interrupt to the QCT SW driver for handling the power and voltage tasks with PMIC and then the QCT SW driver needs to report success or fail to this register

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 9 | HC_CARD_STATE_STABLE | This bit is driving CARD_STATE_STABLE bit in Present State Register |
| 8 | RST_NOT_WAIT_PWRCTL_REG | RST process doesn't need to wait for accessing to MCI_PWRCTL_CTL_REG register |
| 7:6 | HC_WRITE_PROTECT_PAD | Value 0 inversion of HC_WRITE_PROTECT is connected to bit 19 in Present State Register.<br>Value 1 input from PAD is used.<br>Value 2 inversion of input from PAD is used |
| 5 | CARD_DETECT_PIN_LEVEL | This bit reflects the inverse value of the SDCD# pin. Debouncing is not performed on this bit. This bit may be valid when Card State Stable is set to 1, but it is not guaranteed because of propagation delay. Use of this bit is limited to testing since it must be debounced by software.<br>value 1: card present<br>value 0: no card present |
<!-- page 4187 -->

### SDC2_SDCC_MCI_PWRCTL_CTL_REG (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 4 | HC_WRITE_PROTECT | This bit allows to disable the writing.<br>value 0: write enabled<br>value 1: write protected |
| 3 | IO_SIG_SWITCH_FAIL | Host controller clears this bit when it fires either I/O Low V interrupt or I/O High V interrupt. SDCC power control software writes '1' to indicate the signal switch has failed. |
| 2 | IO_SIG_SWITCH_SUCCESS | Host controller clears this bit when it fires either I/O Low V interrupt or I/O High V interrupt. SDCC power control software writes '1' to indicate the signal switch has completed successfully. |
| 1 | BUS_ON_OFF_FAIL | Host controller clears this bit when it fires either Bus ON interrupt or Bus OFF interrupt. SDCC power control software writes '1' to indicate the requested operation has failed. |
| 0 | BUS_ON_OFF_SUCCESS | Host controller clears this bit when it fires either Bus ON interrupt or Bus OFF interrupt. SDCC power control software writes '1' to indicate the requested operation has completed successfully. |

| 18 | FULL_DELAY | 1'b0: unitstep and subunit caps are from calibration or SW settings<br>1'b1: All unit step and subunit caps are selected for the delay arrays. |
| 17 | HW_AUTOCAL_ENA | 1'b1: Enables periodic auto calibration<br>1'b0: Periodic calibration is disabled |

| 10:0 | TMUX_CHAR | Cchar is a characterized constant equal to the ratio of output mux offset delay to average unit step delay. This register is programmed by multiplying the constant with 1024 and rounding to the nearest integer. E.g. if Cchar = 0.67, RO(0.67 * 1024) = 686, hence program TMUX_CHAR = 11'h2AE |

Alternative register to MCI_FIFO (0x80-0xBC). The SW can use this register range (0x400-0x7FC) for accessing all the RAM range (1024 bytes) in FIFO mode. The advantage is that any byte in the RAM can be accessed without repeating the same address

### 0x07864A00 SDC2_SDCC_HC_REG_DLL_CONFIG

* **Type:** RW

| 27 | CK_INTP_EN | Enable clock interpolation for finer resolution |

| 19 | CDR_EXT_EN | Enable external control of cdr phase select |
| 18 | CK_OUT_EN | Enable output clock (default value is '1') |
| 17 | CDR_EN | Enable CDR function |
| 16 | DLL_EN | Enable DLL function |
| 15:14 | CDR_UPD_RATE | CDR update rate, low pass filtering window of CDR<br>Max update rate:<br>Value 00 - 0.5 MCLK frequency<br>Value 01 - 0.25 MCLK Frequency (default)<br>Value 10 - 0.125 MCLK frequency<br>Value 11 - 1/16 MCLK Frequency |
| 13:12 | DLL_UPD_RATE | DLL update rate<br>Value 00 - sdc4_mclk/10<br>Value 01 - sdc4_mclk/20<br>Value 10 - sdc4_mclk/40 (default)<br>Value 11 - sdc4_mclk/80 |

## SDC2_SDCC_HC_VENDOR_SPECIFIC_FUNC2

* **Address:** `0x07864A10`
* **Type:** RW
* **Clock:** same rate as HCLK
* **Reset State:** `0xF88218A8`

| Bits | Name | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31 | QSB_AXI_ABURST | RW | Driving QSB AXI output |
| 30:28 | NUM_OUTSTANDING_DATA | RW | Configuring the number of outstanding transactions for the data. The descriptors accesses have more one outstanding request |
| 27 | PROCEED_AXI_AFTER_ERR | RW | When error occurs on AXI master the traffic can continue or terminate.<br>If this bit is set then the traffic continues and more requests are transmitted on the address channel |
| 26 | QSB_AXI_AFULL_CALC | RW | If this bit is set, then afull isn't '0' constantly but can be equal to '1' if all the beats have 8 bytes on the strobe lines |
| 25 | ONE_MID_SUPPORT | RW | If this bit is set, then only 1 MID is used for descriptors and data |
| 24:22 | RESERVED | RW | Reserved |
| 21 | HC_SW_RST_REQ | RW | Before executing HC_SW_RST_FOR_ALL or HC_SW_RST_FOR_DAT this bit can be set and SW needs to polls on it until it's being cleared.<br>The bit is cleared after AXI master (QMB) has finished processing the outstanding transactions and it's in IDLE state. This bit can be useful for HPI feature. |
| 20 | HC_SW_RST_WAIT_IDLE_DIS | RW | When this bit is cleared, the HC_SW_RST is executed only after the AXI master (QMB) is in IDLE state. This bit can be used for HPI feature instead of polling on HC_SW_RST_REQ bit. This bit should be cleared for SW reset from unknown states. |
| 19 | SDCC5_HALT_REQ | R | Reading SDCC5_HALT_REQ input |
| 18 | SDCC5_HALT_ACK | R | Reading SDCC5_HALT_ACK output |
| 17 | SDCC5_M_IDLE | R | Reading SDCC5_M_IDLE output |
| 16 | SDCC5_HALT_ACK_SW_EN | RW | Enabling the SW value for SDCC5_HALT_ACK |
| 15 | SDCC5_HALT_ACK_SW | RW | Driving SDCC5_HALT_ACK from SW and not by HW |
| 14 | SDCC5_M_IDLE_DIS | RW | If this bit is set, then sdcc5_m_idle will be tied low |
| 13 | QSB_AXI_INTERLEAVING_EN | RW | If the bit is set, then the controller can support interleaving between two bursts from the Noc. This option is disabled by default because Noc doesn't support interleaving but only re-ordering |
| 12 | RESERVED | RW | Reserved |

## SDC2_SDCC_HC_VENDOR_SPECIFIC_CSR_CDC_CTLR_CFG0

* **Address:** `0x07864A30`
* **Type:** RW
* **Clock:** HCLK
* **Reset State:** `0x00000000`

The HC_VENDOR_SPECIFIC_CSR_CDC_CTLR_CFG0 register configures the following:

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 25 | STAGGER_CAL_ENA | 1'b1: Stagger calibration of write and read CDCs once after the other to reduce peak voltage drop.<br>1'b0: Both write and read CDCs calibrated simultaneously<br>This bit is introduced on the x2 core, so not present on x0 and x1 versions of DIM/PHY. |
| 24 | TRACKING_CAL_ENA | 1'b1: Relationship between subunits and oscillator count is learnt and used for tracking calibration.<br>1'b0: Periodic calibration triggers cause full recalibration |
<!-- page 4238 -->

### SDC2_SDCC_HC_VENDOR_SPECIFIC_CSR_CDC_CTLR_CFG0 (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 23:20 | OSC_COUNT_ERR_TOLERANCE | Magnitude of the difference between oscillator count and target count when the algorithm assumes convergence and stops further search. |
| 19 | TRACK_CALIB_MODE | 1'b0: Tracking calibration uses previous Target_count value.<br>1'b1 Accurate mode: Target_count is recomputed at the start of tracking calibration |
| 18 | FULL_DELAY | 1'b0: unitstep and subunit caps are from calibration or SW settings<br>1'b1: All unit step and subunit caps are selected for the delay arrays. |
| 17 | HW_AUTOCAL_ENA | 1'b1: Enables periodic auto calibration<br>1'b0: Periodic calibration is disabled |
| 16 | SW_TRIG_FULL_CALIB | A low to high transition on this register bit triggers the CDC calibration statemachine to initiate full calibration of the standby delay array. Also resets tracking mode for the delay arrays. |
| 13:12 | OSC_PRE_DIV | The factor by which the raw oscillator frequency is divided before being given to the counting logic.<br>2'b00: Divide by 1<br>2'b01: Divide by 2<br>2'b10: Divide by 4<br>2'b11: Divide by 8 |
| 10:0 | TMUX_CHAR | Cchar is a characterized constant equal to the ratio of output mux offset delay to average unit step delay. This register is programmed by multiplying the constant with 1024 and rounding to the nearest integer. E.g. if Cchar = 0.67, RO(0.67 * 1024) = 686, hence program TMUX_CHAR = 11'h2AE |

Hardware waits for explicit acknowledgement of delay array switch from CDC.<br>Others: Explicit acknowledgement mode is disabled and the counter is used |
| 18:16 | DEL_MODE_DELAY | Number of reference clock cycles between putting a newly calibrated delay array in delay mode to selecting it as the active delay array. The minimum allowed value is 1 |

| 2:0 | MULTIPLIER_DELAY | Number of reference clock cycles allowed for arithmetic multiplication operations. The minimum allowed value is 1 |

HC Spec Defines power and IO voltage switch bits. The information is sent by a dedicated interrupt to the QCT SW driver for handling the power and voltage tasks with PMIC. The different tasks are defined in this register.

| Bits | Name | Description |

| 3 | IO_HIGH_V | SDCC driver orders that the I/O signaling level be switched to 3.0v. This interrupt is triggered when SDCC driver writes '0' to offset 03Eh in HC register (bit 3) or when SW reset for all is handled and last supported voltage was 1.8V. | 0 | BUS_OFF | SDCC driver orders that the SD bus power be switched off. This interrupt is triggered when SDCC driver writes '0' to offset 029h in HC register(bit 0) or when SW reset for all is handled. |

| Properties | Value |

HC Spec Defines power and IO voltage switch bits. The information is sent by a dedicated interrupt to the QCT SW driver for handling the power and voltage tasks with PMIC and then the QCT SW driver needs to report success or fail to this register.

**SDC2_SDCC_HC_VENDOR_SPECIFIC_PWRCTL_CTL_REG Bits**

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 9 | HC_CARD_STATE_STABLE | This bit is driving CARD_STATE_STABLE bit in Present State Register |
| 8 | RST_NOT_WAIT_PWRCTL_REG | RST process doesn't need to wait for accessing to MCI_PWRCTL_CTL_REG register |
| 7:6 | HC_WRITE_PROTECT_PAD | Value 0: inversion of HC_WRITE_PROTECT is connected to bit 19 in Present State Register.<br>Value 1: input from PAD is used.<br>Value 2: inversion of input from PAD is used. |
| 5 | CARD_DETECT_PIN_LEVEL | This bit reflects the inverse value of the SDCD# pin. Debouncing is not performed on this bit. This bit may be valid when Card State Stable is set to 1, but it is not guaranteed because of propagation delay. Use of this bit is limited to testing since it must be debounced by software.<br>value 1: card present<br>value 0: no card present |
| 4 | HC_WRITE_PROTECT | This bit allows to disable the writing.<br>value 0: write enabled<br>value 1: write protected |
| 3 | IO_SIG_SWITCH_FAIL | Host controller clears this bit when it fires either I/O Low V interrupt or I/O High V interrupt. SDCC power control software writes '1' to indicate the signal switch has failed. |
<!-- page 4254 -->
### SDC2_SDCC_HC_VENDOR_SPECIFIC_PWRCTL_CTL_REG (Continued)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 2 | IO_SIG_SWITCH_SUCCESS | Host controller clears this bit when it fires either I/O Low V interrupt or I/O High V interrupt. SDCC power control software writes '1' to indicate the signal switch has completed successfully. |
| 1 | BUS_ON_OFF_FAIL | Host controller clears this bit when it fires either Bus ON interrupt or Bus OFF interrupt. SDCC power control software writes '1' to indicate the requested operation has failed. |
| 0 | BUS_ON_OFF_SUCCESS | Host controller clears this bit when it fires either Bus ON interrupt or Bus OFF interrupt. SDCC power control software writes '1' to indicate the requested operation has completed successfully. |

### 20.1.1 BLSP1_BLSP_BAM_BAM_BAM

### 0x07884000 BLSP1_BLSP_BAM_BAM_BAM_CTRL

| Properties | Value |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Type** | RW |
| **Clock** | bam_clk |
| **Reset State** | 0x00020000 |

BAM Control register allows global controls for the BAM.

**BLSP1_BLSP_BAM_BAM_BAM_CTRL Bits**

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 20 | BAM_MESS_ONLY_CANCEL_WB | When active (1) - BAM will DROP former descriptor write-backing and Interrupt firing when former descriptor has been closed (accumulated=acknowledged) and ack_on_success with EOT and size 0 arrived (messaging only).<br>When legacy mode is used (0) - This said a case then the former descriptor has been closed (accumulated=acknowledged) and ack_on_success with EOT and size 0 arrived (messaging only). In this case the FIFO-pointer has been already advanced before the ack_on_success arrives and therefore we do write-back to former descriptor and fire interrupt.<br>1'b1 - Drop WB and Interrupt<br>1'b0 - legacy. |
| 19 | CACHE_MISS_ERR_RESP_EN | When set to '1', upon local ahb access results with cache miss, the bam_ndp will not stall the bus, and finish the access with error response.<br>This bit is relevant for BAM_NDP only. |
<!-- page 4257 -->
### BLSP1_BLSP_BAM_BAM_BAM_CTRL (Continued)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 18:17 | LOCAL_CLK_GATING | These Bits enables power saving by using a local clock gating cell.<br>Bit 17:<br>1'b1 - CGC is on, so that the clock is controlled by the HW - this is the reset value.<br>1'b0 - CGC is off so that the clock is free running<br>Bit 18:<br>Reserved bit for future improvements. |
| 16 | IBC_DISABLE | This Bit enables power saving by disabling the inactivity clock timer/counter. This is useful when:<br>1) The BAM is Enabled but idling for long periods.<br>2) The BAM is Enabled and running but the inactivity timers/counters are not required by the SW for operating the BAM.<br>When the BAM is Disabled, it automatically shuts down those timers to save power.<br>1'b1 - Enable Power Saving Mode<br>1'b0 - Disable Power Saving Mode |
| 15 | BAM_CACHED_DESC_STORE | This Bit enables storage of a cached Descriptor into RAM when doing Context Switch and loading it back when returning to this pipe. This is relevant for System Modes Only.<br>BAM to BAM Consumer mode doesn't have this option.<br>Enabling this makes the Context Switch process slightly longer but reduces AHB Descriptor Fetch time later on. It also reduces the number of descriptor fetches done by the BAM if BAM is treating more than 2 pipes.<br>1'b1 - Enabled<br>1'b0 - Disabled<br>Available in BAM only |
| 14:13 | BAM_DESC_CACHE_SEL | This Selector chooses which Descriptor Caching mode will be used. This is relevant for System Producer or Consumer modes only.<br>2'b00 - Cache when current descriptor has less than 64 bytes left.<br>2'b01 - Cache when current descriptor has less than 128 bytes left.<br>2'b10 - Immediate Auto cache - cache will happen whenever there are no descriptors cached. This might cause unnecessary descriptors reads when switching between more than 2 pipes. It is the most effective when each pipe processes more bytes than there are in an average descriptor (small descriptors, big block size), or when working with 2 or less pipes.<br>2'b11 - Cache when descriptor is needed only. This results in 1 descriptor present in cache at most.<br>Available in BAM only |
| 11:5 | RESERVED | Reserved |
<!-- page 4258 -->
### BLSP1_BLSP_BAM_BAM_BAM_CTRL (Continued)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 4 | BAM_EN_ACCUM | When Enabled, BAM will accumulate data written by the peripheral in Direct Mode into INCR8 Bursts.<br>This is an optimization feature for Producer Direct Mode cases.<br>1'b1 - Enabled<br>1'b0 - Disabled<br>Available in BAM only |
| 1 | BAM_EN | After reset the BAM wakes up in Disabled Mode.<br>While Disabled, BAM operates in Legacy mode (all the transfers from the peripheral go around the BAM as if it doesn't exist)<br>Software Enables this bit to allow BAM operation.<br>This bit doesn't affect the PIPE enable bit in BAM_P_CTRL register.<br>The only possibility to Disable the BAM after it has been enabled is by Hardware or Software reset.<br>1'b1 - Enabled<br>1'b0 - Disabled |
| 0 | BAM_SW_RST | This will reset the BAM & all Pipes. Software may use this to reset the BAM. As long as the bit remains high the BAM remains in reset state.<br>Software should clear this bit<br>1'b1 - Reset state<br>1'b0 - Normal state |

## BLSP1_BLSP_BAM_BAM_BAM_CNFG_BITS

**Address:** `0x0788407C`
**Type:** RW
**Clock:** `bam_clk`
**Reset State:** `0x00000000`

This Register holds the BAM configuration bits for bug fixes. It is highly recommended to follow the directions for each bit and set it accordingly.
<!-- page 4262 -->
### BLSP1_BLSP_BAM_BAM_BAM_CNFG_BITS (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31 | AOS_OVERFLOW_PRVNT | This bit enables overflow prevention when Sideband block accumulates ack_on_success updates from peripherals to values higher than 0x7fff.<br>'1' - enable ack-on_success overflow prevention. If current ack_on_success update causes overflow accept_ack_on_success_toggle will not approve the update until SB accumulator is cleared.<br>'0' - disable ack-on_success overflow prevention.<br>Available in BAM-NDP only.<br>Default value is '0' (Legacy).<br>Recommended value is '1'. |
| 30 | MULTIPLE_EVENTS_DESC_AVAIL_EN | This is an enable bit for supporting multiple events received by a Producer BAM2BAM and makes BAM-NDP to notify a correct desc_cache_avail bus.<br>It fixed CR: QCTDD00209370. |
| 29 | MULTIPLE_EVENTS_SIZE_EN | This is an enable bit for supporting multiple events received by a Producer BAM2BAM and makes BAM-NDP delivering correct descriptor sizes on local_ahb bit.<br>It fixed CR: QCTDD00209379. |
| 28 | BAM_ZLT_W_CD_SUPPORT | Recommended value: 1<br>Enables support of ZLT (i.e. a zero-sized descriptor) before a command-descriptor.<br>Specifically it supports a case on a pipe without any data-descriptors but with ZLT descriptors and Command-descriptors only.<br>This allows putting NWD bit in the ZLT descriptor (instead of in the CMD) which results in better performance than using the NWD in the command-descriptor.<br>Available in BAM-Lite Only. |
| 27 | BAM_CD_ENABLE | Recommended value: 1<br>Enables the command descriptor feature. |
| 26 | BAM_AU_ACCUMED | Recommended value: 1<br>This bit fixes a bug in the Ack Update state machine, where an overflow happened while counting descriptors and reaching more than 64kB of calculated sizes.<br>1'b1 - Enable Fix<br>1'b0 - Disable<br>Available in BAM/BAM-NDP only |
<!-- page 4263 -->
### BLSP1_BLSP_BAM_BAM_BAM_CNFG_BITS (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 25 | BAM_PSM_P_HD_DATA | Recommended value: 1<br>This bit allows pipe state machine to ignore retransmission requests if a pipe has just been initialized and process those as a regular fetch request. (consumer modes only).<br>When this bit disabled, BAM could fetch descriptors for a pipe which was reset and no descriptors were added yet, if a retransmission request followed after the reset.<br>1'b1 - Enable Fix<br>1'b0 - Disable<br>Available in BAM only |
| 24 | BAM_REG_P_EN | Recommended value: 1<br>This bit fixes the pipe configuration signals mux for the current active pipe in 2 pipes BAM.<br>When disabled, internal state machines might get into enabled states while the pipe is disabled. This would typically happen after pipe reset.<br>1'b1 - Enable<br>1'b0 - Disable<br>Available in BAM/BAM-NDP only |
| 23 | BAM_WB_DSC_AVL_P_RST | Recommended value: 1<br>This bit allows the Writeback state machine to reset the vector indicating there are available descriptors when a pipe reset occurs.<br>If disabled, BAM might fetch descriptors after resetting and reconfiguring a pipe, even though no Event (descriptors) was provided.<br>1'b1 - Enable<br>1'b0 - Disable<br>Available in BAM only |
| 22 | BAM_WB_RETR_SVPNT | Recommended value: 1<br>This bit fixes a bug where a pipe which was reset, still stored its retransmission savepoint, but into the illegal's pipe address space, thus hurting the last pipe of the BAM if the BAM had a total 4, 8 or 16 pipes.<br>This is relevant for Producer to System modes only.<br>(CR-0000151585)<br>1'b1 - Enabled<br>1'b0 - Disable<br>Available in BAM/BAM-NDP only |
| 21 | BAM_WB_CSW_ACK_IDL | Recommended value: 1<br>This bit allows the Writeback state machine to switch into idle state prior to visiting disabled state. This is needed when context switching from mode X to another pipe of mode X is well. This is required to fix a bug in the 2 pipes BAM.<br>1'b1 - Enable<br>1'b0 - Disable<br>Available in BAM/BAM-NDP only |
<!-- page 4264 -->
### BLSP1_BLSP_BAM_BAM_BAM_CNFG_BITS (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 20 | BAM_WB_BLK_CSW | Recommended value: 1<br>When Enabled, this bit does not allow context switch to happen in the Writeback state machine until it has created a descriptor. This is relevant when the descriptor fifo is becoming full and there's no space to create a descriptor, while another pipe is context switching. This might result in the descriptor not to be created ever, if it was the last one for that pipe.<br>Relevant for Producer BAM-to-BAM mode only.<br>1'b1 - Enable<br>1'b0 - Disable<br>Available in BAM only |
| 19 | BAM_WB_P_RES | Recommended value: 1<br>This bit allows to reset all internal registers of the Writeback state machine when performing pipe reset.<br>1'b1 - Enable<br>1'b0 - Disable<br>Available in BAM only |
| 18 | BAM_SI_P_RES | Recommended value: 1<br>This bit allows to reset all internal registers of the Sideband Inform state machine when performing pipe reset.<br>1'b1 - Enable<br>1'b0 - Disable<br>Available in BAM only |
| 17 | BAM_AU_P_RES | Recommended value: 1<br>This bit allows to reset all internal registers of the Ack Update state machine when performing pipe reset.<br>1'b1 - Enable<br>1'b0 - Disable<br>Available in BAM only |
| 16 | BAM_PSM_P_RES | Recommended value: 1<br>This bit allows to reset all internal registers of the Pipe state machine when performing pipe reset.<br>1'b1 - Enable<br>1'b0 - Disable<br>Available in BAM only |
| 15 | BAM_PSM_CSW_REQ | Recommended value: 1<br>This bit forces the context switch request from pipe state machine to RAM controller not to last longer than the slave requested. (2 Pipes BAM bug fix).<br>1'b1 - Enable<br>1'b0 - Disable<br>Available in BAM only |
<!-- page 4265 -->
### BLSP1_BLSP_BAM_BAM_BAM_CNFG_BITS (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 14 | BAM_SB_CLK_REQ | Recommended value: 1<br>This bit allows the clock request from the sideband block to propagate into the BAM's common clock request.<br>1'b1 - Propagate Sideband Clock Request<br>1'b0 - Disable<br>Available in BAM only |
| 13 | BAM_IBC_DISABLE | Recommended value: 1<br>This bit helps to save power by allowing the BAM to keep the inactivity base counter in reset when BAM is disabled or when SW configures IBC_DISABLE bit high. Irrelevant field for BAM-NDP.<br>1'b1 - Enable Power Saving<br>1'b0 - Disable Power Saving |
| 12 | BAM_NO_EXT_P_RST | Recommended value: 1<br>This bit allows the BAM / BAM Lite to ignore the externally connected blocks (eDML) when doing pipe reset.<br>The BAM, once instructed to pipe reset, first thing lets the externally connected block know a reset is needed. Then it waits for the externally connected block to Acknowledge it is ready for the pipe reset (meaning it doesnt push any data for the reseted pipe) and then the BAM Lite completes the pipe reset operation internally.<br>When disabled, the BAM doesnt require any Acknowledge from the external block to perform pipe reset.<br>1'b1 - Enable external block pipe reset<br>1'b0 - Disable - ignore external block pipe reset |
| 11 | BAM_FULL_PIPE | Recommended value: 0<br>This enables the BAM support for a BAM to BAM Producer which insists to write to a full pipe. When 0, BAM might issue data overflow if producers write to a full pipe. When 1 BAM will not allow this and lower HReady when peripheral tries to do so. Once space is freed in the pipe, Hready will rise and the flow will continue.<br>1'b1 - Enable<br>1'b0 - Disable<br>Available in BAM only |
| 3 | RESERVED | Reserved |
| 2 | BAM_PIPE_CNFG | Recommended value: 1<br>Pipe SM upgrade for writing EOT bit to the previous descriptor. It's invoked only when EOB arrives in the end of a descriptor. It is highly recommended to set this bit high. Leaving it low might cause incorrect Pipe Bytes Free value reported to peripheral in rare cases.<br>1'b1 - Enable<br>1'b0 - Disable<br>Available in BAM only |
| 1:0 | RESERVED | Reserved |

## BLSP1_BLSP_BAM_BAM_BAM_REVISION

**Address:** `0x07885000`
**Type:** R
**Clock:** `bam_clk`
**Reset State:** Undefined

This Register holds a hard coded revision number of the BAM RTL. This corresponds to the BAM target number in the IMS. Also additional BAM settings are reflected here.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:24 | INACTIV_TMR_BASE | This indicates the width of the inactivity timers base counter. |
| 23 | CMD_DESC_EN | This indicates BAM has Command Descriptor feature enabled in HW. |
| 22:21 | DESC_CACHE_DEPTH | This field indicates the Per-Pipe-Descriptor-Cache. Could be 1-4:<br>2'b00 - Descriptor Cache Depth of 1.<br>2'b01 - Descriptor Cache Depth of 2.<br>2'b10 - Descriptor Cache Depth of 3.<br>2'b11 - Descriptor Cache Depth of 4.<br>Valid only for BAM_NDP. |
| 20 | NUM_INACTIV_TMRS | This bit is checked only if INACTIV_TMRS_EXST = 1. This bit indicates how many inactivity timers are implemented according to value of INACTIVITY_TIMERS_SUPPORTED generic:<br>1'b1 - One timer for global BAM activity (INACTIVITY_TIMERS_SUPPORTED = 1)<br>1'b0 - MAX_PIPES timers for each pipe activity (INACTIVITY_TIMERS_SUPPORTED = 2) |
| 19 | INACTIV_TMRS_EXST | This indicates BAM has inactivity timers.<br>1'b1 - Timers available (INACTIVITY_TIMERS_SUPPORTED = 1 or 2)<br>1'b0 - No timers available (INACTIVITY_TIMERS_SUPPORTED = 0) |
| 18 | HIGH_FREQUENCY_BAM | This indicates BAM has Double Sampling on the Ack On Success interface.<br>1'b1 - Ack On Success double sampled<br>1'b0 - No double sampling of Ack On Success |
| 17 | BAM_HAS_NO_BYPASS | This field indicates BAM has no bypass on the AHB Data bus, from the Peripheral AHB Master to the fabric. When Bypass is available, it is the default routing when BAM is disabled.<br>1'b1 - No Bypass<br>1'b0 - Bypass Exists |
| 16 | RESERVED | Reserved |
| 15 | RESERVED | Reserved |
<!-- page 4267 -->
### BLSP1_BLSP_BAM_BAM_BAM_REVISION (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 14 | AXI_ACTIVE | This field indicates BAM_NDP uses internal AXI bridge on the master port. |
| 13:12 | CE_BUFFER_SIZE | This field indicates the size (in Data words) of the buffer which stores the command elements. Each command element includes 4 words.<br>2'b00 - 4 Words (one command element).<br>2'b10 - 8 Words (2 command elements).<br>2'b11 - 16 Words (4 command elements).<br>Valid Only if CMD_DESC_EN = 1'b1. |
| 11:8 | NUM_EES | This indicates the Number of Interrupt Lines (Execution Environments) supported by the BAM.<br>When 1 EE is supported, only the BAM_IRQ_SRCS*_EE0 registers exist.<br>When 4 EEs are supported, all BAM_IRQ_SRCS*_EEn registers exist for n=[0..3]. |
| 7:0 | RESERVED | Reserved |

* **Reset State:** `0x00000000`

This Register holds the BAM Trusted configurations.
This register cannot be reset by any SW reset. Only HW reset applies. When using a non-secured BAM, it is reset by the BAM HW Reset.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 12:8 | RESERVED | Reserved |
| 7:3 | BAM_P_SUP_GROUP | Super-Group is the upper division of the pipes compared to the pipe-group division.<br>When any pipe locks or unlocks the BAM, all the pipes which are in a different super-group will NOT be affected. Only the pipes within the same super-group of the locker are affected.<br>Usually pipes which belongs to different peripherals which share the same BAM, would be in a different super-groups |

The BAM interrupt will fire to the EE # set at BAM_P_TRUST_REGn registers.<br>The number of supported EEs is reflect in the NUM_EES field in the BAM_REVISION register.<br>3'b000 - EE0<br>3'b001 - EE1<br>3'b010 - EE2<br>3'b011 - EE3<br>3'b100 - EE4<br>3'b101 - EE5<br>3'b110 - EE6<br>3'b111 - EE7 |

### BLSP1_BLSP_BAM_BAM_BAM_IRQ_SRCS_EEn, n=[0..7]

* **Address:** `0x07887000 + 4096 * n`
* **Type:** R
* **Clock:** `bam_clk`
* **Reset State:** `0x00000000`

This Interrupt Status Register provides a single interrupt bit per each pipe in the BAM and a single bit for the BAM (not pipe related) interrupt. This register is read only and provides fast indication for the software to decide which pipe triggered the interrupt. After checking this register, SW reads the BAM_P_IRQ_STTSn register for the pipe interrupt reason and BAM_IRQ_STTS for the BAM interrupt reason.

This register has an alias - BAM_IRQ_SRCS register.

Registers with n=[1..7] exist only when the BAM supports multiple EEs (NUM_EES field in the BAM_REVISION register).

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31 | BAM_IRQ | BAM Global interrupt |
| 30:0 | P_IRQ | An interrupt bfit per each pipe in the BAM. |

### BLSP1_BLSP_BAM_BAM_BAM_IRQ_SRCS_MSK_EEn, n=[0..7]

* **Address:** `0x07887004 + 4096 * n`
* **Type:** RW
* **Clock:** `bam_clk`
* **Reset State:** `0x00000000`
<!-- page 4273 -->
### BLSP1_BLSP_BAM_BAM_BAM_IRQ_SRCS_MSK_EEn (cont.)

Interrupt Sources Mask register allows to mask the interrupts by their source, whether BAM or a specific pipe.

This register has an alias - BAM_IRQ_SRCS_MSK register.

Registers with n=[1..7] exist only when the BAM supports multiple EEs (NUM_EES field in the BAM_REVISION register).

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31 | BAM_IRQ_MSK | BAM Global Interrupt Mask<br>0x1: ENABLE_BAM_INTERRUPT (Enable BAM interrupt)<br>0x0: DISABLE_BAM_INTERRUPT (Disable BAM interrupt) |
| 30:0 | P_IRQ_MSK | An Interrupt Mask bit per each pipe in the BAM.<br>0x1: ENABLE_PIPE_INTERRUPT (Enable Pipe interrupt)<br>0x0: DISABLE_PIPE_INTERRUPT (Disable Pipe interrupt) |

* **Reset State:** `0x00000000`

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31 | BAM_IRQ_UNMASKED | BAM Global Interrupt after Mask |
| 30:0 | P_IRQ_UNMASKED | An Interrupt bit per each pipe in the BAM, after Mask |

The reset value written above is true only if EE>0. For BAM_PIPE_ATTR_EE0 the default value is: Bits [MAX_PIPES-1:0] = 1 , Bits [31: MAX_PIPES] = 0 .

### BLSP1_BLSP_BAM_BAM_BAM_P_CTRLn, n=[0..30]

* **Address:** `0x07897000 + 4096 * n`
* **Type:** RW
* **Clock:** `bam_clk`
* **Reset State:** `0x00000000`

Pipe Control register provides various controls for the pipe.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 20:16 | P_LOCK_GROUP | Pipe's lock group.<br>Upon a lock request on this pipe, all pipes related to different pipe group and different EE (see PIPE_TRUST_REG) will be locked. |
<!-- page 4276 -->
### BLSP1_BLSP_BAM_BAM_BAM_P_CTRLn (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 11 | P_WRITE_NWD | BAM-Lite feature.<br>Applicabale to BAM2BAM producer pipes only.<br>When this bit is set for producer B2B pipe, NWD bit (bit number 28 in the second word of descriptor) will be written with EOT into the generated descriptor for the consumer usage.<br>This bit is not applicable in pipes belong to a Peripheral which uses messaging_only (e.g. USB2). |
| 10:9 | P_PREFETCH_LIMIT | Bam Lite feature<br>Selects the number of bytes to be prefetched by the Bam Lite, once a peripheral requests to read data from a pipe.<br>This feature is relevant for Consumer modes only.<br>2'b00 - 32 bytes at most (INCR8)<br>2'b01 - 16 bytes at most (INCR4)<br>2'b10 - 4 bytes at most (SINGLE)<br>Available in BAM-Lite only |
| 8:7 | P_AUTO_EOB_SEL | Bam Lite feature.<br>Selects the number of bytes to be processed before creating End Of Block indication internally by the BAM. See P_AUTO_EOB.<br>Descriptors generated by this feature (bam to bam producer mode) will always be of the chosen size, unless an End Of Transfer, causes a smaller descriptor to be created.<br>2'b00 - 512 Bytes<br>2'b01 - 256 Bytes<br>2'b10 - 128 Bytes<br>2'b11 - 64 Bytes<br>Available in BAM-Lite only |
| 6 | P_AUTO_EOB | BAM Lite feature.<br>When Enabled, the BAM Lite will ignore any incoming End Of Block indications from the peripheral (if any). Instead, the BAM Lite will generate it's own End Of Block indications internally, every P_AUTO_EOB_SEL bytes.<br>This feature is relevant for Producer Bam 2 Bam modes only.<br>It is a must for peripherals which are not able to produce End Of Block indications.<br>1'b1 - Enable<br>1'b0 - Disable<br>Available in BAM-Lite only |
| 5 | P_SYS_MODE | This bit sets the pipe to work in System Mode, where the Software is the second side of the pipe.<br>1'b1 - System mode.<br>1'b0 - BAM to BAM mode. |
<!-- page 4277 -->
### BLSP1_BLSP_BAM_BAM_BAM_P_CTRLn (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 4 | P_SYS_STRM | Streaming Enable. Relevant to System Producer BAM mode only. When enabled, BAM will not close descriptors with End Of Transfer notifications received from peripheral, but continue writing the data to the same descriptor.<br>1'b1 - Enable Streaming Mode<br>1'b0 - None-Streaming Mode.<br>This field is NOT supported in BAM-NDP (i.e. no streaming mode in NDP). |
| 3 | P_DIRECTION | This bit denotes pipe direction.<br>1'b1 - The pipe can be written (producer mode)<br>1'b0 - The pipe can be read (consumer mode) |
| 1 | P_EN | 1'b1 - Enable Pipe<br>1'b0 - Disable Pipe |

### BLSP1_BLSP_BAM_BAM_BAM_P_RSTn, n=[0..30]

* **Address:** `0x07897004 + 4096 * n`
* **Type:** W
* **Clock:** `bam_clk`
* **Reset State:** `0x00000000`

Pipe Reset register provides Pipe Reset ability. Software needs to write 1 to this register to make the Pipe Reset. Writing 0 to this register will finish the Pipe Reset. Writing zero is needed prior to Peripheral reconfiguration for the same pipe.

Note: Software can invoke pipe reset only after it make sure that the pipe is 'quiet'.
('quiet' - No data transaction or command-descriptor is active at the time.)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 0 | P_SW_RST | This resets the pipe and it's registers, (Both Flip-Flops and RAM). Software can invoke pipe reset only after it make sure that the pipe is 'quiet'.<br>1'b1 - Reset<br>1'b0 - Do Nothing |

### BLSP1_BLSP_BAM_BAM_BAM_P_HALTn, n=[0..30]

* **Address:** `0x07897008 + 4096 * n`
* **Type:** RW
* **Clock:** `bam_clk`
* **Reset State:** `0x00000000`
<!-- page 4278 -->
### BLSP1_BLSP_BAM_BAM_BAM_P_HALTn (cont.)

Pipe Halt register Enables/Disables the Halt Sequence. Refer to the Software Procedures chapter for the Halt Sequence Procedure.

This is a self-modifying register.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1 | P_PROD_HALTED | This bit is used to inform the Consumer about the Producer being in Halt mode now. This is a part of the Halt procedure. See the Software Procedures chapter.<br>1'b1 - Sets this bit to 1<br>1'b0 - Does Nothing<br>This bit will be cleared by the HW. |
| 0 | P_HALT | When Enabled, the Pipe will enter Halt Mode.<br>1'b1 - Enable Halt<br>1'b0 - Disable Halt<br>For B2B Producer pipes, this bit is self modifying. It doesn't need the SW to clear it. See the Software Procedure chapter for the detailed flow. |

### BLSP1_BLSP_BAM_BAM_BAM_P_IRQ_STTSn, n=[0..30]

* **Address:** `0x07897010 + 4096 * n`
* **Type:** R

### BLSP1_BLSP_BAM_BAM_BAM_P_TIMER_CTRLn

**Address:** `0x07897020 + 4096 * n`, where `n=[0..30]`
**Type:** RW
**Clock:** `bam_clk`
**Reset State:** `0x00000000`

This register sets various controls and the threshold of the inactivity for interrupt triggering after long idle time.
The resolution of the pipe inactivity timers are in units set by a common counter. This common counter is controlled by a PARAMETER value of the BAM, and uses a separate clock, the `inactivity_timers_clk`. This clock can be slower than the `bam_clk`. The intent of the design is to use the `sleep_clk`, which is an always on 32kHz clock. This allows the `bam_clk` to be turned-off, while the base counter keeps counting. The width of this counter, as well of the rollover value are set using BAM PARAMETER. These values, taking the `inactivity_timers_clk` frequency define the pulse frequency that the base counter gives, and the threshold value can be calculated and set to interrupt after a specific time, regardless of the `bam_clk` frequency, and independent of clock power save features of the `bam_clk`. The timers continue counting even if the clock is turned off due to BAM dynamic hardware clock request voting.

The timer configuration is based on the `inactivity_timers_clk` period and the `INACTIVITY_TIMER_WIDTH` parameter constant. These parameters should be taken into account when setting this register. For example: for `inactivity_timer_clk` period of 1us and parameter is 3 and `P_TIMER_THRSHLD` is 10 will indicate the 2^3 * 1us * 10 which is 80us of inactivity in a pipe before sending an interrupt.

The general formula is: 2^INACTIVITY_TIMER_WIDTH * clock_period * P_TIMER_TRSHLD.
<!-- page 4282 -->

#### BLSP1_BLSP_BAM_BAM_BAM_P_TIMER_CTRLn (Continued)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31 | P_TIMER_RST | To begin using the inactivity timer the SW should write the threshold and write 1 to this bit. writing the value 0 will hold the timer reset until value 1 is written again. Then the timer will start down counting from the P_TIMER_THRESOLD value<br>1'b1 - Active<br>1'b0 - Reset |
| 30 | P_TIMER_RUN | Will be used along with P_TIMER_MODE<br>Not implemented at this time. Set to zero(0) |
| 29 | P_TIMER_MODE | Not implemented at this time. Set to zero(0) |
| 15:0 | P_TIMER_TRSHLD | Inactivity timer threshold for interrupt generation. |

### BLSP1_BLSP_BAM_BAM_BAM_P_SW_OFSTSn

**Address:** `0x07897800 + 4096 * n`, where `n=[0..30]`
**Type:** RW
**Clock:** `bam_clk`
**Reset State:** `0x00000000`

This register denotes the pointer Offset of the first Not Acknowledged Descriptor. Meaning all Descriptors prior to this one have been processed by the BAM. This register is only used by the Software. After receiving an interrupt, software reads this register in order to know what descriptors has been processed.
When the BAM works as Producer, Software will usually read this value after Descriptor Processed Interrupt or after the End of Transfer Interrupt.

> [!NOTE]
> Although being Writable, Software should never write to this register.

> [!NOTE]
> When using 2 pipes BAM, REVISION 0x03, this registers is Read Only.

Then the SW can read this value to know how many Bytes were written to the current descriptor if it was not closed down.<br>This is useful for Streaming mode.<br>This Field is NOT available in BAM-NDP |
| 15:0 | SW_DESC_OFST | Descriptor FIFO offset. |

## 20.2 BLSP1_BLSP_UART0_UART_DM

### BLSP1_BLSP_UART0_UART_DM_MR1

* **Address:** `0x078AF000`
* **Type:** RW
* **Clock:** `AHB_CLK`
* **Reset State:** `0x00000000`

The UART_DM_MR1 register is the UART mode register #1. It is used, along with UART_DM_MR2, to configure the operational mode of the UART.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:8 | AUTO_RFR_LEVEL1 | These bits are used, along with field AUTO_RFR_LEVEL0 to program the level in the receive FIFO at which the Ready-For-Receive signal (RFR_N) toggles, if programmed to do so (see RX_RDY_CTL field of this register).<br>When RX-FIFO level is greater than the value in fields AUTO_RFR_LEVEL1 and AUTO_RFR_LEVEL0 , signal will indicate Not-Ready (RFR_N high). Otherwise signal will indicate Ready RFR_N low.<br>Configured value should be higher/equal than RFWR value, otherwise the watermark will never be reached.<br>Value of this register is in words and can be programmed from 1 to 2^RAM_ADDR_WIDTH.<br>- Only RAM_ADDR_WIDTH +1:8 bits of this field are generated. |
| 7 | RX_RDY_CTL | Setting (1) this bit enables the automatic ready-for-receiving (RFR_N) control for the receiver. RFR_N is turned off, or set (1), when a valid start bit is received and the RX channel FIFO is at the level programmed in bits [31:8,5:0] of this register. When the FIFO level falls back to the programmed level, the RFR_N signal is turned on, or clear (0). When this feature is off, the RFR_N signal can be used by normal signal port bit manipulation (see UART_DM_CR register). |
| 6 | CTS_CTL | When this bit is set(1), the transmitter checks the CTS_N input to determine whether to begin transmission of a new character. If CTS_N is low, the character is sent. Otherwise the transmitter continues marking until CTS_N goes low, then the next character is transmitted. A change on CTS_N during the transmission of a character has no effect on that character.<br>When this bit is clear(0), the CTS_N input for the channel has no effect on the transmitter. |
| 5:0 | AUTO_RFR_LEVEL0 | See the description of field AUTO_RFR_LEVEL1. |
<!-- page 4296 -->

### BLSP1_BLSP_UART0_UART_DM_MR2

* **Address:** `0x078AF004`
* **Type:** RW
* **Clock:** `AHB_CLK`
* **Reset State:** `0x00000000`

See description of UART_DM_MR1 register.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 10 | RFR_CTS_LOOPBACK | Enables internal loopback between RFR_N of RX channel and CTS_N of TX channel if set. For this feature to be enabled, data loopback must also be enabled (LOOPBACK bit of this register). |
| 9 | RX_ERROR_CHAR_OFF | When this bit is set, characters received with parity or framing errors get discarded and not moved to the RX channel. Otherwise they enter RX channel as any valid character. |
| 8 | RX_BREAK_ZERO_CHAR_OFF | When this bit is set, the zero character received at rx_break event get discarded and not moved to the RX channel. Otherwise it enters RX-channel as any valid character. |
| 7 | LOOPBACK | When set - data output of transmitter is fed back to the data input of the receiver, i.e. TX-pin is connected to RX-pin. Might be used with flow-control loopback (RFR_CTS_LOOPBACK bit above). |
| 6 | ERROR_MODE | This bit controls the operation of the two status register bits for the RX channel (parity or framing error and received break, see UART_DM_SR register).<br>- When clear (0), the UART operates in character mode and the status bits apply only to the last character received.<br>- When set (1), the UART operates in block mode and both bits are sticky, i.e. they go high once an error/break-event is detected and go low only after reset error status command is issued (see UART_DM_CR register). |
| 5:4 | BITS_PER_CHAR | These bits determine how many data bits are transmitted or received per character, not including the start, stop, and parity bits.<br>0x0: ENUM_5_BITS (5 bits)<br>0x1: ENUM_6_BITS (6 bits)<br>0x2: ENUM_7_BITS (7 bits)<br>0x3: ENUM_8_BITS (8 bits) |
| 3:2 | STOP_BIT_LEN | This field programs the duration of the stop bit that is appended to each transmitted character. The stop bit duration can be 9/16, 1, 1+ 9/16, and 2 bit times. The receiver only samples the stop bit once, regardless of the programmed stop bit length. This configuration only applies to UART/IrDA interfaces, for SIM interface see SIM_STOP_BIT_LEN field of UART_DM_SIM_CFG register.<br>0x0: ENUM_0_563 (0.563 (9/16) bit times)<br>0x1: ENUM_1_000_BIT_TIME (1.000 bit time)<br>0x2: ENUM_1_563 (1.563 (1+9/16) bit times)<br>0x3: ENUM_2_000_BIT_TIMES (2.000 bit times) |
<!-- page 4297 -->

### BLSP1_BLSP_UART0_UART_DM_MR2 (continued)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1:0 | PARITY_MODE | These bits determine which parity mode is used. The user can select between odd, even, space, or no parity.<br>0x0: NO_PARITY (no parity - last data-bit is followed by a stop-bit)<br>0x1: ODD_PARITY (odd parity - parity-bit ensures number of ones in data-bits+parity-bit is odd)<br>0x2: EVEN_PARITY (even parity - parity-bit ensures number of ones in data-bits+parity-bit is even)<br>0x3: SPACE_PARITY (space parity - parity is always '0') |

---

### BLSP1_BLSP_UART0_UART_DM_IPR

* **Address:** `0x078AF018`
* **Type:** RW
* **Clock:** `AHB_CLK`
* **Reset State:** `0xFFFFFF9F`

The UART_DM_IPR register is the UART interrupt programming register.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:7 | STALE_TIMEOUT_MSB | The stale character time-out duration field contains a number from 1 to 2^30 -1. This number determines how many character times must elapse before a stale event is generated. This character time is defined as 10 times the bit rate. It is reset whenever a data bit is received. Never set this fields to 0 while RX channel is operational. Do not re-configure while an RX-transfer is active.<br>Note the discontinuity in the bit assignments. |
| 6 | SAMPLE_DATA | Currently not in use.<br>Setting (1) to this bit enables the sample data mode. In this mode start bit is sampled along with the data of the UART character.<br>Works only in 'Packet mode' (See the CR register, CHANNEL_COMMAND bit for more information). |
| 5 | RESERVED | Reserved. |
| 4:0 | STALE_TIMEOUT_LSB | This bitfield is the LSbits of the STALE_TIMEOUT bitfield. |
<!-- page 4299 -->

### BLSP1_BLSP_UART0_UART_DM_TFWR

* **Address:** `0x078AF01C`
* **Type:** RW
* **Clock:** `AHB_CLK`
* **Reset State:** `0x00000000`

The UART_DM_TFWR register is the UART transmit FIFO watermark register.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:0 | TFW | These bits contain a number, between 0 and 2^RAM_ADDR_WIDTH - 1, that determines the level of the transmit (TX) FIFO at which space_avail_req signal is asserted in BAM mode or TXLEV interrupt is asserted in non-BAM mode. The signal/interrupt is asserted when the FIFO level (number of TX words in the FIFO) is less than or equal to the value in TFWR. Notice that the value is in words. See UART_DM_ISR register for TXLEV interrupt description.<br>- Only RAM_ADDR_WIDTH -1:0 bits are generated. |

---

### BLSP1_BLSP_UART0_UART_DM_RFWR

* **Address:** `0x078AF020`
* **Type:** RW
* **Clock:** `AHB_CLK`
* **Reset State:** `Undefined`

The UART_DM_RFWR register is the UART receive FIFO watermark register.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:0 | RFW | These bits contain a number, between 0 and 2^RAM_ADDR_WIDTH - 1, that determines the level of the receive (RX) FIFO at which data_avail_req signal is asserted in BAM mode or RXLEV interrupt is asserted in non-BAM mode. The signal/interrupt is asserted when the FIFO level (number of words in the RX FIFO) is greater than the value in RFWR. Configured value should be lower/equal than AUTO_RFR_LEVEL value, otherwise the watermark will never be reached. Notice that the value is in words. See UART_DM_ISR register for TXLEV interrupt description<br>- Only RAM_ADDR_WIDTH -1:0 bits are generated. |
<!-- page 4300 -->

| Bits | Name | Description |

### BLSP1_BLSP_UART0_UART_DM_DMRX

* **Address:** `0x078AF034`
* **Type:** RW
* **Clock:** `AHB_CLK`
* **Reset State:** `0x00000000`

Initializes RX transfer and configures maximal length in bytes of the transfer.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 24:0 | RX_DM_CRCI_CHARS | A write to RX_DM_CRCI_CHARS initializes RX transfer in SW (FIFO) mode, with written value configuring the maximal length in bytes of the transfer. In BAM-mode, only the value held in this register impacts the data-flow and not the write-event. A write-value of 0 is not valid.<br>Read of UART_DM_DMRX register is returns the number of characters that were received since the end of the last RX transfer.<br>To read back the last value written to this register use UART_DM_DMRX_DBG register.<br>Refer to UART_DM_BCR register description for additional constraints on the value to be written to this register. |
