### USB2_HSIC_USB_OTG_HS_BAM_BAM_BAM_P_SW_OFSTSn

**Address:** `0x078D7800 + 4096 * n, n=[0..30]`

**Type:** RW
**Clock:** `bam_clk`
**Reset State:** `0x00000000`

This register denotes the pointer Offset of the first Not Acknowledged Descriptor. Meaning all Descriptors prior to this one have been processed by the BAM. This register is only used by the Software. After receiving an interrupt, software reads this register in order to know what descriptors has been processed.

When the BAM works as Producer, Software will usually read this value after Descriptor Processed Interrupt or after the End of Transfer Interrupt.

> [!NOTE]
> When using 2 pipes BAM, REVISION 0x03, this registers is Read Only.

### USB2_HSIC_USB_OTG_HS_BAM_BAM_BAM_P_EVNT_REGn

**Address:** `0x078D7818 + 4096 * n, n=[0..30]`

**Type:** RW
**Clock:** `bam_clk`
**Reset State:** `0x00000000`

This Register is where Read/Write events are sent to. If current BAM works as Producer, it will receive Read events into this register from the Consumer. If the Consumer is another BAM, it will...
<!-- page 4619 -->

### USB2_HSIC_USB_OTG_HS_BAM_BAM_BAM_P_EVNT_REGn (cont.)

...write read events to this register. If the Consumer is the Software, it will prepare descriptors in the descriptor FIFO and update the DESC_FIFO_PEER_OFST value in this register.

If current BAM works as Consumer, opposite behavior is assumed.

BAM_P_EVNT_REGn, n=[0..30]

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:16 | P_BYTES_CONSUMED | This field is used only in the B2B mode. It indicates the number of bits consumed by the Consumer. Consumer sends this value to the Producer as a part of a read event, for the Producer to know how many bytes were consumed. When working in System mode, this value should be set to zero. BAM to BAM Producer writes zero in this value. |
| 15:0 | P_DESC_FIFO_PEER_OFST | This field indicates the Descriptor Fifo Offset Pointer of the Peer BAM (The BAM or the Software which creates descriptors). For example when current BAM works as consumer for the current pipe, Producer BAM (or the software) updates this value to let the current pipe know about the new descriptors added in the Descriptor Fifo. |

### USB2_HSIC_USB_OTG_HS_BAM_BAM_BAM_P_EVNT_GEN_TRSHLDn

**Address:** `0x078D7828 + 4096 * n, n=[0..30]`

**Type:** RW
**Clock:** `bam_clk`
**Reset State:** `0x00000000`

This register configures the threshold value for Read/Write event generation by the BAM towards another BAM. When a BAM pushes/pops this number of bytes to/from the pipe an event to the...


<!-- page 4621 -->
Other BAM will be generated. A counter summing up the bytes pushed/popped is reset when event is issued, thus restarting count for the threshold.

Events are also issued after End Of Transfer received from the peripheral (Producer case), regardless of whether the pushed bytes count has reached the threshold or not.

This register is not relevant in System Modes.

| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 15:0 | P_TRSHLD | Threshold value. The maximum allowed value is 32kByte. |

# PDM

`WEB_TCXO4` includes three PDMs and one MND_clock_devider, which are controlled using the following registers. They are clocked with `HCLK`.

### PDM_WEB_TCXO4_TCXO_PDM0_TOP_CTL
**Address:** `0x00068000`
**Type:** RW
**Clock:** HCLK
**Reset State:** 0x00000000

Top level control register of PDM0 used for OE, Output polarity control and clock enable of PDM0.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 2 | TCXO4_CLK_DISABLE | Set (1) this bit to disable the TCXO4 clock, and Clear (0) the bit to enable the TXCO4 clock. PDM0 |
| 1 | PDM0_POLARITY | This bit defines the polarity of PDM0. Set (1) this bit to invert the sense of the PDM0 output, meaning that the PDM value will indicate the number of 0's in every $2^{16}$ cycles. Clearing (0) this bit will keep the PDM in its native polarity, meaning that the PDM value will indicate the number of 1's in every $2^{16}$ cycles. |
| 0 | PDM0_OE | |

---

### PDM_WEB_TCXO4_PDM0_CTL
**Address:** `0x00068004`
**Type:** RW
**Clock:** HCLK
**Reset State:** 0x00008000

The `PDM0_CTL` register is the pulse density modulation register number 0. This register determines the density of pulses on the PDM0 pin.
<!-- page 4629 -->
**PDM_WEB_TCXO4_PDM0_CTL** (continued)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 15:0 | PDM0_DAT | The `PDM0_DAT`, after inverting the MSbit (1's complement), determines the number of 1's in $2^{16}$ TCXO4 cycles for PDM0. When the `PDM0_POLARITY` is set (1), the output sense is inverted. |

---

### PDM_WEB_TCXO4_TCXO_PDM1_TOP_CTL
**Address:** `0x00069000`
**Type:** RW
**Clock:** HCLK
**Reset State:** 0x00000000

Top level control register of PDM1 used for OE, Output polarity control and clock enable of PDM1.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 2 | TCXO4_CLK_DISABLE1 | Set (1) this bit to disable the TCXO4 clock, and Clear (0) the bit to enable the TXCO4 clock. PDM1 |
| 1 | PDM1_POLARITY | This bit defines the polarity of PDM1. Set (1) this bit to invert the sense of the PDM1 output, meaning that the PDM value will indicate the number of 0's in every $2^{16}$ cycles. Clearing (0) this bit will keep the PDM in its native polarity, meaning that the PDM value will indicate the number of 1's in every $2^{16}$ cycles. |
| 0 | PDM1_OE | |

---

**Address:** `0x00069004`
**Type:** RW
**Clock:** HCLK
**Reset State:** 0x00000080

The `PDM1_CTL` register is the pulse density modulation register number 1. This register determines the density of pulses on the PDM1 pin.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 7:0 | PDM1_DAT | The `PDM1_DAT`, after inverting the MSbit (1's complement), determines the number of 1's in $2^8$ TCXO4 cycles for PDM1. When the `PDM1_POLARITY` is set (1), the output sense is inverted. |
<!-- page 4630 -->

**Type:** RW
**Clock:** HCLK

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |

| 1 | PDM2_POLARITY | This bit defines the polarity of PDM2. Set (1) this bit to invert the sense of the PDM2 output, meaning that the PDM value will indicate the number of 0's in every $2^{16}$ cycles. Clearing (0) this bit will keep the PDM in its native polarity, meaning that the PDM value will indicate the number of 1's in every $2^{16}$ cycles. |

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 15:0 | PDM2_DAT | The `PDM2_DAT`, after inverting the MSbit (1's complement), determines the number of 1's in $2^{16}$ PDM2_clk cycles for PDM2. When the `PDM2_POLARITY` is set (1), the output sense is inverted. |

---

### PDM_WEB_TCXO4_GP_MN_CLK_MDIV
**Address:** `0x0006B000`
**Type:** RW
**Clock:** HCLK
**Reset State:** 0x00000000

The `GP_MN_CLK_MDIV` register is the MDIV specification register for the GP M/N clock. For all GP_MN registers, this signal is generated by dividing the frequency of the TCXO signal by an M/N counter. M, N and D have the following specifications and constraints:


<!-- page 4631 -->

* The maximum value of M is 511.
* The maximum value of N is 8191.
* N > 2M.
* The value of M cannot exceed the value of N.
* N and M cannot have any common divider else than 1.
* D is allowed to be between M and N-M => (M < D < N-M).

### PDM_WEB_TCXO4_GP_MN_CLK_MDIV (continued)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 8:0 | GP_M_VALUE | This register defines the value of M for the M/N counter, which generates the GP_MN signal. |

---

### 0x0006B004 PDM_WEB_TCXO4_GP_MN_CLK_NDIV

**Type:** RW
**Clock:** HCLK
**Reset State:** 0x00000000

The GP_MN_CLK_NDIV register is the NDIV specification register for the GP M/N clock.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 12:0 | GP_N_VALUE | This register defines the value (-(N-M)), using 1's complement value of N minus M for the M/N counter, which generates the GP_MN signal. |

---

### 0x0006B008 PDM_WEB_TCXO4_GP_MN_CLK_DUTY

**Type:** RW
**Clock:** HCLK
**Reset State:** 0x00000000

The GP_MN_CLK_DUTY register is the duty cycle specification register for the GP M/N clock.
<!-- page 4632 -->

| Bits | Name | Description |

### 0x00022004 PRNG_PRNG_STATUS

**Type:** R
**Reset State:** 0x00000000

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:10 | RESERVED | |
| 9:8 | CURRENT_OPERATION | 0x0: IDLE (IDLE)<br>0x1: GENERATE (GENERATE)<br>0x2: INSTANTIATE (INSTANTIATE)<br>0x3: RESEED (RESEED) |
| 7 | GENERATE_REQUIRED | Indicates that a generate is, or soon will be occurring. This occurs when the generate counter != 0. This is only valid when the PRNG is enabled (PRNG_EN = 1) |
| 6 | RESEED_REQUIRED | Indicates that a reseed operation is, or soon will be occurring. This occurs when the reseed counter = reseed freq. This is only valid when the PRNG is enabled (PRNG_EN = 1) |
| 5 | INSTANTIATE_REQUIRED | Indicates that an instantiate operation or soon will be occurring. This occurs when the instantiate counter = 0. This is only valid when the PRNG is enabled (PRNG_EN = 1) |
<!-- page 4634 -->

### PRNG_PRNG_STATUS (cont.)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 4 | RING_OSC3_HEALTHY | Indicates that ring oscillator 3 is healthy. Only valid when RING_OSC3_CFG is set to one of the feedback settings (not valid when set to one of the FORCE inputs). When set to one of the FORCE inputs, this is reset to 0. |
| 3 | RING_OSC2_HEALTHY | Indicates that ring oscillator 2 is healthy. Only valid when RING_OSC2_CFG is set to one of the feedback settings (not valid when set to one of the FORCE inputs). When set to one of the FORCE inputs, this is reset to 0. |
| 2 | RING_OSC1_HEALTHY | Indicates that ring oscillator 1 is healthy. Only valid when RING_OSC1_CFG is set to one of the feedback settings (not valid when set to one of the FORCE inputs). When set to one of the FORCE inputs, this is reset to 0. |
| 1 | RING_OSC0_HEALTHY | Indicates that ring oscillator 0 is healthy. Only valid when RING_OSC0_CFG is set to one of the feedback settings (not valid when set to one of the FORCE inputs). When set to one of the FORCE inputs, this is reset to 0. |
| 0 | DATA_AVAIL | Indicates that data is available on the PRNG_DATA_OUT FIFO. |

### PRNG_PRNG_CONFIG (cont.)

Ring oscillators and the LFSR will still operate as per PRNG_LFSR_CFG, however when this is 0, the PRNG when the PRNG is disabled it will return to the IDLE state once its current operation has been completed, with the current operation possibly requiring space to be created in the output fifo for data that must be generated in the completion of the current operation. This space can be created by reading from the PRNG_DATA_OUT register.<br>0x0: DISABLED (disabled)<br>0x1: ENABLED (enabled) |

# 25 Qualcomm Debug Subsystem Wrapper

## 25.1 CXATBFUNNEL_32W2SP

The Funnel is used when there is more than one trace source.

### 25.1.1 QDSS_WRAPPER_ATB_FUN2X1_CXATBFUNNEL_32W2SP

The Funnel is used when there is more than one trace source.

#### 0x00868000 QDSS_WRAPPER_ATB_FUN2X1_CTRL_REG

**Type:** RW
**Reset State:** 0x00000300

The Funnel Control Register enables the slave ports and defines the hold time of the slave ports. Hold time refers to the number of transactions that are output on the funnel master port from the same slave while that slave port atvalidsx is HIGH. Hold time does not refer to clock cycles in this context.
<!-- page 4663 -->

#### Continuation of: 0x00868000 QDSS_WRAPPER_ATB_FUN2X1_CTRL_REG

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 11:8 | HT | The formatting scheme can easily become inefficient if fast switching occurs, so, where possible, this must be minimized. If a source has nothing to transmit, then another source is selected irrespective of the minimum number of transactions. <br>The maximum value that can be entered is 0xE and this equates to 15 cycles. <br>0xF is reserved. <br>0x0: HOLD_TIME_1 (1 transactions hold time) <br>0x1: HOLD_TIME_2 (2 transactions hold time) <br>0x2: HOLD_TIME_3 (3 transactions hold time) <br>0x3: HOLD_TIME_4 (4 transactions hold time) <br>0x4: HOLD_TIME_5 (5 transactions hold time) <br>0x5: HOLD_TIME_6 (6 transactions hold time) <br>0x6: HOLD_TIME_7 (7 transactions hold time) <br>0x7: HOLD_TIME_8 (8 transactions hold time) <br>0x8: HOLD_TIME_9 (9 transactions hold time) <br>0x9: HOLD_TIME_10 (10 transactions hold time) <br>0xA: HOLD_TIME_11 (11 transactions hold time) <br>0xB: HOLD_TIME_12 (12 transactions hold time) <br>0xC: HOLD_TIME_13 (13 transactions hold time) <br>0xD: HOLD_TIME_14 (14 transactions hold time) <br>0xE: HOLD_TIME_15 (15 transactions hold time) |
| 1 | ENS1 | Setting this bit enables this input, or slave, port. If the bit is not set then this has the effect of excluding the port from the priority selection scheme. The reset value is all clear, that is, all ports disabled. <br>0x1: ENABLE (Slave port enabled) <br>0x0: DISABLE (Slave port disabled) |
| 0 | ENS0 | Setting this bit enables this input, or slave, port. If the bit is not set then this has the effect of excluding the port from the priority selection scheme. The reset value is all clear, that is, all ports disabled. <br>0x1: ENABLE (Slave port enabled) <br>0x0: DISABLE (Slave port disabled) |

#### 0x00868004 QDSS_WRAPPER_ATB_FUN2X1_PRIORITY_CTRL_REG

**Type:** RW
**Reset State:** 0x00000000

The Priority Control Register defines the order in which inputs are selected. Each 3-bit field represents a priority for each particular slave interface. Location 0 has the priority value for the first slave port. Location 1 is the priority value for the second slave port, Location 2 is the third, down to location 7, which has the priority value of the eighth slave port. Values represent the priority value for each port number. If you want to give highest priority to a particular slave port,
<!-- page 4664 -->

#### Continuation of: 0x00868004 QDSS_WRAPPER_ATB_FUN2X1_PRIORITY_CTRL_REG

... the corresponding port must be programmed with the lowest value. Typically this is likely to be a port that has more important data or that has a small FIFO and is therefore likely to overflow.

If you want to give lowest priority to a particular slave port, the corresponding slave port must be programmed with the highest value. Typically this is likely to be a device that has a large FIFO that is less likely to overflow or a source that has information that is of lower importance.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 5:3 | PRIPORT1 | Priority value of the 2nd port. <br>0x0: PRORITY_LEVEL_0 (This value represents the highest priority.) <br>0x1: PRORITY_LEVEL_1 (2nd highest priority) <br>0x2: PRORITY_LEVEL_2 (3rd highest priority) <br>0x3: PRORITY_LEVEL_3 (4th highest priority) <br>0x4: PRORITY_LEVEL_4 (5th highest priority) <br>0x5: PRORITY_LEVEL_5 (6th highest priority) <br>0x6: PRORITY_LEVEL_6 (7th highest priority) <br>0x7: PRORITY_LEVEL_7 (This value represents the lowest priority.) |
| 2:0 | PRIPORT0 | Priority value of the first slave port. The value written into this location is the value that you want to assign the first slave port. <br>0x0: PRORITY_LEVEL_0 (This value represents the highest priority.) <br>0x1: PRORITY_LEVEL_1 (2nd highest priority) <br>0x2: PRORITY_LEVEL_2 (3rd highest priority) <br>0x3: PRORITY_LEVEL_3 (4th highest priority) <br>0x4: PRORITY_LEVEL_4 (5th highest priority) <br>0x5: PRORITY_LEVEL_5 (6th highest priority) <br>0x6: PRORITY_LEVEL_6 (7th highest priority) <br>0x7: PRORITY_LEVEL_7 (This value represents the lowest priority.) |

#### 0x00868F00 QDSS_WRAPPER_ATB_FUN2X1_ITCTRL

**Type:** RW
**Reset State:** 0x00000000

This register is used to enable topology detection. For more information see the CoreSight Architecture Specification. This register enables the component to switch from a functional mode, the default behavior, to integration mode where the inputs and outputs of the component can be directly controlled for the purpose of integration testing and topology solving.

> [!NOTE]
> When a device has been in integration mode, it might not function with the original behavior. After performing integration or topology detection, you must reset the system to ensure correct behavior of CoreSight and other connected system components that are affected by the integration or topology detection.
<!-- page 4665 -->

#### Continuation of: 0x00868F00 QDSS_WRAPPER_ATB_FUN2X1_ITCTRL

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |

#### 0x00868FB4 QDSS_WRAPPER_ATB_FUN2X1_LOCKSTATUS

**Type:** R
**Reset State:** 0x00000003

This indicates the status of the Lock control mechanism. This lock prevents accidental writes by code under debug. This register must always be present although there might not be any lock-access control mechanism. The lock mechanism, where present and locked, must block write accesses to any control register, except the Lock Access Register. For most components this covers all registers except for the Lock Access Register 0xFB0.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |

| 1 | LOCKGRANT | Returns the current status of the Lock. <br>0x0: ACCESS_PERMITTED (Write access is allowed to this device) <br>0x1: DEVICE_LOCKED (Write access to the component is blocked. All writes to control registers are ignored. Reads are permitted) |
| 0 | LOCKEXIST | Indicates that a lock control mechanism exists for this device. <br>0x0: LOCK_NOT_PRESENT (No lock control mechanism exists, writes to the Lock Access register (0xFB0) will be ignored) <br>0x1: LOCK_PRESENT (Lock control mechanism is present) |

## 25.2 CXATBFUNNEL_32W8SP

The Funnel is used when there is more than one trace source.

### 25.2.1 QDSS_WRAPPER_ATB_FUN8X1_CXATBFUNNEL_32W8SP

### QDSS_WRAPPER_ATB_FUN8X1_CTRL_REG

**Address:** `0x00869000`  
**Type:** RW  
**Reset State:** `0x00000300`  

The Funnel Control Register enables the slave ports and defines the hold time of the slave ports. Hold time refers to the number of transactions that are output on the funnel master port from the same slave while that slave port atvalidsx is HIGH. Hold time does not refer to clock cycles in this context

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 11:8 | HT | The formatting scheme can easily become inefficient if fast switching occurs, so, where possible, this must be minimized. If a source has nothing to transmit, then another source is selected irrespective of the minimum number of transactions.<br>The maximum value that can be entered is 0xE and this equates to 15 cycles.<br>0xF is reserved.<br>0x0: HOLD_TIME_1 (1 transactions hold time)<br>0x1: HOLD_TIME_2 (2 transactions hold time)<br>0x2: HOLD_TIME_3 (3 transactions hold time)<br>0x3: HOLD_TIME_4 (4 transactions hold time)<br>0x4: HOLD_TIME_5 (5 transactions hold time)<br>0x5: HOLD_TIME_6 (6 transactions hold time)<br>0x6: HOLD_TIME_7 (7 transactions hold time)<br>0x7: HOLD_TIME_8 (8 transactions hold time)<br>0x8: HOLD_TIME_9 (9 transactions hold time)<br>0x9: HOLD_TIME_10 (10 transactions hold time)<br>0xA: HOLD_TIME_11 (11 transactions hold time)<br>0xB: HOLD_TIME_12 (12 transactions hold time)<br>0xC: HOLD_TIME_13 (13 transactions hold time)<br>0xD: HOLD_TIME_14 (14 transactions hold time)<br>0xE: HOLD_TIME_15 (15 transactions hold time) |

### QDSS_WRAPPER_ATB_FUN8X1_PRIORITY_CTRL_REG

**Address:** `0x00869004`  
**Type:** RW  
**Reset State:** `0x00000000`  

The Priority Control Register defines the order in which inputs are selected. Each 3-bit field represents a priority for each particular slave interface. Location 0 has the priority value for the first slave port. Location 1 is the priority value for the second slave port, Location 2 is the third, down to location 7, which has the priority value of the eighth slave port. Values represent the priority value for each port number. If you want to give highest priority to a particular slave port, the corresponding port must be programmed with the lowest value. Typically this is likely to be a port that has more important data or that has a small FIFO and is therefore likely to overflow.

If you want to give lowest priority to a particular slave port, the corresponding slave port must be programmed with the highest value. Typically this is likely to be a device that has a large FIFO that is less likely to overflow or a source that has information that is of lower importance.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 23:21 | PRIPORT7 | Priority value of the eighth port. The value written into this location is the value that you want to assign the eighth slave port. If a priority value has been entered for multiple different slave ports then the arbitration logic selects the lowest port number of them.<br>0x0: PRORITY_LEVEL_0 (This value represents the highest priority.)<br>0x1: PRORITY_LEVEL_1 (2nd highest priority)<br>0x2: PRORITY_LEVEL_2 (3rd highest priority)<br>0x3: PRORITY_LEVEL_3 (4th highest priority)<br>0x4: PRORITY_LEVEL_4 (5th highest priority)<br>0x5: PRORITY_LEVEL_5 (6th highest priority)<br>0x6: PRORITY_LEVEL_6 (7th highest priority)<br>0x7: PRORITY_LEVEL_7 (This value represents the lowest priority.) |

### QDSS_WRAPPER_ATB_FUN8X1_ITCTRL

**Address:** `0x00869F00`  
**Type:** RW  
**Reset State:** `0x00000000`  

This register is used to enable topology detection. For more information see the CoreSight Architecture Specification. This register enables the component to switch from a functional mode, the default behavior, to integration mode where the inputs and outputs of the component can be directly controlled for the purpose of integration testing and topology solving

*Note:*
<!-- page 4678 -->

### QDSS_WRAPPER_ATB_FUN8X1_ITCTRL (continued)

*Note:* When a device has been in integration mode, it might not function with the original behavior. After performing integration or topology detection, you must reset the system to ensure correct behavior of CoreSight and other connected system components that are affected by the integration or topology detection.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 0 | INTEGRATION_MODE | Allows the component to switch from functional mode to integration mode or back. If no integration functionality is implemented, this register must read as zero.<br>0x1: INTEGRATION_MODE (Enable integration mode)<br>0x0: FUNCTIONAL_MODE (Disable integration mode) |

An invalid write will have the affect of removing write access.<br>0xC5ACCE55: UNLOCK (Unlock the protection register to enable write access)<br>0xDEADBEEF: LOCK (invalid write value to enable the protection register and block write access) |

### QDSS_WRAPPER_ATB_FUN8X1_LOCKSTATUS

**Address:** `0x00869FB4`  
**Type:** R  
**Reset State:** `0x00000003`  

This indicates the status of the Lock control mechanism. This lock prevents accidental writes by code under debug. This register must always be present although there might not be any lock-access control mechanism. The lock mechanism, where present and locked, must block write accesses to any control register, except the Lock Access Register. For most components this covers all registers except for the Lock Access Register 0xFB0

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 2 | LOCKTYPE | Indicates if the Lock Access Register (0xFB0) is implemented as 8-bit or 32-bit<br>0x0: ENUM_32_BIT (This component implements a 32-bit Lock Access Register) |
<!-- page 4680 -->

### QDSS_WRAPPER_ATB_FUN8X1_LOCKSTATUS (continued)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1 | LOCKGRANT | Returns the current status of the Lock<br>0x0: ACCESS_PERMITTED (Write access is allowed to this device)<br>0x1: DEVICE_LOCKED (Write access to the component is blocked. All writes to control registers are ignored. Reads are permitted) |
| 0 | LOCKEXIST | Indicates that a lock control mechanism exists for this device<br>0x0: LOCK_NOT_PRESENT (No lock control mechanism exists, writes to the Lock Access register (0xFB0) will be ignored)<br>0x1: LOCK_PRESENT (Lock control mechanism is present) |

### QDSS_WRAPPER_ATB_FUN8X1_AUTHSTATUS

**Address:** `0x00869FB8`  
**Type:** R  
**Reset State:** `0x00000000`  

Reports the required security level and current status of those enables. Where functionality changes on a given security level then this change in status must be reported in this register

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 7:6 | SNID | Indicates the security level for secure non-invasive debug<br>0x0: ENUM_2_B00 (Functionality not implemented or controlled elsewhere) |
| 5:4 | SID | Indicates the security level for secure invasive debug<br>0x0: ENUM_2_B00 (Functionality not implemented or controlled elsewhere) |
| 3:2 | NSNID | Indicates the security level for non-secure non-invasive debug<br>0x0: ENUM_2_B00 (Functionality not implemented or controlled elsewhere) |
| 1:0 | NSID | Indicates the security level for non-secure invasive debug<br>0x0: ENUM_2_B00 (Functionality not implemented or controlled elsewhere) |

### 0x00869FE8 QDSS_WRAPPER_ATB_FUN8X1_PERIPHID2

**Type:** R
**Reset State:** 0x0000002B

Part of the set of Peripheral Identification registers. Contains part of the designer identity and the product revision.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 7:4 | REVISION | The Revision field is an incremental value starting at 0x0 for the first design of this component. This only increases by 1 for both major and minor revisions and is simply used as a look-up to establish the exact major/minor revision.<br>0x2: R2P0 (This device is at r2p0) |
| 3 | JEDEC | Always set. Indicates that a JEDEC assigned value is used<br>0x1: JEDEC_IDENTITY (The designer ID is specified by JEDEC (http://www.jedec.org)) |

<!-- page 4683 -->
### 0x00869FEC QDSS_WRAPPER_ATB_FUN8X1_PERIPHID3

**Type:** R
**Reset State:** 0x00000000

Part of the set of Peripheral Identification registers. Contains the RevAnd and Customer Modified fields.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 7:4 | REVAND | This field indicates minor errata fixes specific to this design, for example metal fixes after implementation. In most cases this field is zero. It is recommended that component designers ensure this field can be changed by a metal fix if required, for example by driving it from registers that reset to zero.<br>0x0: NO_MODS (Indicates that there have been no metal fixes to this component) |
| 3:0 | CUSTOMER_MODIFIED | Where the component is reusable IP, this value indicates if the customer has modified the behavior of the component. In most cases this field is zero.<br>0x0: NO_MODS (Indicates that there have been no modifications made) |

### 0x00869FD0 QDSS_WRAPPER_ATB_FUN8X1_PERIPHID4

**Type:** R
**Reset State:** 0x00000004

Part of the set of Peripheral Identification registers. Contains part of the designer identity and the memory footprint indicator.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 7:4 | FOURKB_COUNT | This is a 4-bit value that indicates the total contiguous size of the memory window used by this component in powers of 2 from the standard 4KB. If a component only requires the standard 4KB then this should read as 0x0, 4KB only, for 8KB set to 0x1, 16KB == 0x2, 32KB == 0x3, and so on.<br>0x0: ENUM_4KB (Indicates that the device only occupies 4kB of memory) |
| 3:0 | JEP106_CONT | JEDEC continuation code indicating the designer of the component (along with the identity code)<br>0x4: ARM_JEP106_CONTINUATION_CODE (Indicates that ARM's JEDEC identity code is on the 5th bank) |
